(32’) CLOSE! Rooney whips the delivery towards the penalty spot where an unmarked Carrick looks to connect. However, he cannot quite stretch far enough to get the vital touch and Federici gratefully gathers.
(31’) United are awarded a free-kick after Rashford was bundled over by Surman, who had just got the wrong side of the teenager. This is a good opportunity for the hosts...
(29’) The Cherries are just unable to enjoy a lengthy spell with the ball at the moment. When they do, United are instantly closing them down and eager to win it back as soon as possible.
(27’) Bournemouth are still struggling to gain a foothold in this contest, but they can afford to be very pleased with their efforts this season. Howe's men are set to finish at least 16th which, while just two places above the relegation zone, would have been instantly accepted had you offered them that scenario at the start of their maiden Premier League campaign.
(25’) It is set to be a season of Premier League lows for United this term. They have won just 18 league games - one less than two seasons earlier - while managing just 46 goals, which is 12 less than their lowest tally of 58 in the 2004/05 campaign.
(23’) A patient build-up from United sees Martial scoop the ball into the area for Borthwick-Jackson to run onto. Elphick is well-positioned, though, and the Bournemouth skipper makes an important intervention.
(21’) Old Trafford is fairly quiet this evening with United having nothing to play for other than guaranteeing fifth place. Manchester City's draw with Swansea City on Sunday means that only a victory by 19 goals or more this evening would see them secure Champions League football in fourth place.
(19’) Valencia shows great vision and precision to play a neat through ball for Lingard to run onto in behind Daniels. The Bournemouth left-back does well, though, as he makes up vital ground before producing a perfectly timed challenge.
(17’) Bournemouth now have the opportunity to establish a foothold in this game as they are awarded a free-kick on the near touchline after Pugh was fouled. They should just try to find their rhythm here and get a feel for the ball.
(15’) United continue to zip the ball around the field and maintain possession. They need to make the most of it, though, and start asking questions of their opponents in dangerous areas.
(13’) Both the form and history books suggest that Bournemouth have a job on their hands in attack this evening. They have never scored at Old Trafford where United have only conceded eight all season - fewer than any other team on home soil - while only Petr Cech has kept more clean sheets than De Gea in the Premier League this term.
(11’) Bournemouth are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment. United are dominating in possession, but the Cherries are holding their own in defence so far.
(9’) Ironically, this is Rooney's lowest scoring season at Manchester United with just seven goals to his name. He needs to score a hat-trick this evening to ensure that his record of reaching double figures in each of his Premier League campaigns at Old Trafford continues.
(7’) Rooney is settling nicely into the holding midfield role. He is dictating the majority of his side's play so far and, given the impressive form of Harry Kane and Jamie Vardy this season, you feel that his best bet for a place in England's starting line-up at Euro 2016 would be in that position.
(5’) United have enjoyed the stronger start of the two sides in possession. In fact, only Arsenal, Manchester City and Chelsea have completed more passes in this season's Premier League.
(3’) Despite just four days separating tonight from the FA Cup Final, Van Gaal has named a fairly strong starting 11 this evening. It appears that he is trying to build momentum among his key players rather than resting them.

HERE THEY COME! The players are making their way out onto the field and kick-off is just moments away...

(48’) The last time Norwich did the double over United was during the 1989-90 season and you feel that repeating that feat here would go a long way towards securing their Premier League status.
(46’) KICK-OFF! Mr Pawson blows his whistle and United get the ball rolling once more.

(45’) Mr Pawson blows his whistle and brings the first half to an end.

That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.

(88’) Foster is happy to take his time over a goal-kick, with the home fans whistling the England international goalkeeper to get a move on. Berahino is picked out by a long pass forward, but the youngster can only carry possession into the box before rifling a low shot straight at Boruc.

(84’) Bournemouth are pushing on to try and complete a late comeback. Foster is forced into action once again, but a powerful effort shoots straight down the goalkeeper's throat. (80’) Rondon is almost realised by a quick pass in behind, but Francis covers across to make a timely interception. Bournemouth's right-back has been one of their only solid performers on the field, with the Cherries really struggling to muster something up from nowhere.
(78’) Narrowly over 10 minutes remain in this contest, with Bournemouth looking to be ending things with a whimper. King breaks forward to try and inspire his teammates into something, but a cross-cum-shot from the Norway international flashes ahead of both Grabban and Wilson but wide of the far upright.
(76’) Berahino drives to the right byline, but can only cut back a cross. It results in Rondon slamming a shot goalwards, but Boruc makes an easy save. West Brom are running down the clock with sluggish pushes forward, but only Berahino is providing any kind of directness.
--- 74’ Substitution Howe makes his final change, with Ritchie replacing Stanislas for the dying stages. ---
--- 74’ Substitution Berahino replaces Gardner, with the young Englishman having a quarter of an hour to freshen up the attack. ---
(74’) Rondon is the target of a long cross in from McClean, with the ex-Sunderland winger's delivery finding the forehead of his teammate. The ex-Zenit striker cranes his neck to angle a header goalwards, but the ball sails high and wide of the target.
(72’) Less than 20 minutes remain at Dean Court, with West Brom having no interest in getting forward. The visitors are sat on the edge of their penalty area, inviting the Cherries to keep going forward relentlessly. Rondon is relatively isolated, with Pulis clearly happy for his men to close out a narrow away victory.
--- 70’ Yellow card Arter goes into the book for a very late challenge on Fletcher, with the Irishman having absolutely no complaints at all there. It was high and late, and probably should have been red. ---
(69’) The introductions of King and Wilson have breathed new life into the Cherries, with both offering pace and sharp movement in the dying stages of this contest. The pair have 20 minutes to make a notable difference, with West Brom suddenly coming under a lot more dangerous pressure.
(67’) Frustrations are rising for the home side, with players moaning among themselves about the odd poor pass. Gardner is the target of a long, searching pass from the visitors, but Boruc is able to defuse the danger easily. Bournemouth respond, with Wilson pivoting and firing wide of the far post!
(65’) Foster is forced into a relatively easy save inside his right-hand post, after a dipping free-kick attempt from Stanislas. West Brom go down the other end, with Dawson whipping in a cross from out wide, but Rondon can only guide a looping header high and wide of the target.
(63’) King immediately causes problems after driving infield from the right, but sees a shot blocked, before the same Bournemouth man manages to win a free-kick on the periphery of the penalty area after being brought down untidily.
--- 62’ Yellow card Initally, the referee books Evans for a foul on King, but realises his mistake and flashes his card at the real offender, Yacob. ---
--- 61’ Substitution After an afternoon of poor deliveries, Gradel is hooked off for King. ---
--- 60’ Substitution Wilson comes into the fray for the hosts for Afobe, with the former raring to get back into action after long-term injury problems. ---

(58’) Bournemouth take a corner short, with Stanislas involved in taking the set-piece short. The former Burnley man plays a neat one-two, before unleashing a swerving shot from the edge of the penalty box. Foster is forced to cling onto a neat save at his near post.
(56’) The opening 10 minutes of the second half haven't seen much in the way of entertainment, with this contest threatening to peter out. West Brom's away fans are having a great time and making plenty of noise, but the atmosphere off the pitch isn't really inspiring anything positive off it.
(54’) The hosts continue to retain the ball, but there's no quality in the final third from the Cherries. West Brom are defending deep, with Bournemouth bashing their head against a brick wall. Frustrating times for Howe, with Foster having a very easy afternoon in the visiting net.
(52’) Rondon is picked out by a long pass, but the Venezuelan striker's touch lets him down terribly. The ball just can't seem to stick to the West Brom striker. Foster is on hand to claim yet another cross, this time from the right-hand side, with Grabban unable to get there first. Afobe didn't even look interested at all.
(50’) Gradel jinks infield from the right-hand side, with the ex-Saint Etienne winger clipping a cross into the penalty area. Foster is very quick off his line to claim yet again, with the ex-Watford shot-stopper having everything under control at present. The Ivorian takes a corner moments later, but Rondon makes a defensive header.
(48’) Bournemouth will be trying to come back into this contest as quickly as possible, with the second half starting as the first ended. Plenty of possession for the hosts, but still no end product. Leko continues to be a thorn in the hosts' side, with the 17-year-old full of bright running.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at Dean Court! West Brom could be closing in on an away win, something that their travelling support haven't seen all too often this season, while Bournemouth will want to give their home fans something to shout about at the end of a positive campaign.
HALF-TIME! West Brom go into the interval with a 1-0 lead, given to them by Rondon, as Tony Pulis' men find themselves halfway to a rare away Premier League win. Gardner could have doubled the Baggies' advantage, but a penalty double-save from Boruc kept the visitors at bay. Bournemouth have been lacklustre and need to create more to get back into this one.
(45’) Wide of the post from Afobe! A looping cross is deflected high into the air, with the ex-Arsenal striker setting himself for an overhead kick. With McAuley putting him under pressure, the Englishman can only hack a hurried effort beyond the right-hand post.

Leko and Rondon combine down the right-hand side, with Daniels forced to concede a corner against the 17-year-old. McAuley is dragged to the ground at the back post, however, with Elphick giving away a spot-kick.
(38’) The Cherries threaten down the right-hand side once again, but choose to open play back out wide to the opposite flank. The hosts are probing for an opening and are prepared to take their time, with Howe's principals definitely not being sacrificed. Leko is felled by Gradel, with there a little bit of afters from the latter. Moments later, Evans goes down and requires treatment.
(36’) Arter sends a looping pass looking for Grabban, but Foster races off his line to make an easy catch ahead of the ex-Norwich striker. The former Manchester United goalkeeper hasn't had a great deal to do, other than smother a poorly angled shot from Gradel. Bournemouth continue to hold onto the ball, but create very little indeed.
(34’) Gardner curls a free-kick delivery into the box, but Francis heads half-clear, before the same Bournemouth defender is required moments later to deny Rondon. (32’) Less than a quarter of an hour remains in the first half, with Bournemouth needing a goal from somewhere to try and inspire a response from both their players and fans alike. West Brom calm things down with some steady possession, before a hopeful and looping cross from Dawson is easily cleared by Cook.

The opening half an hour has been low on clear-cut chances, with Bournemouth held to taking shots from range. West Brom are sat back and defending well, with Fletcher and Yacob shielding their central defenders well.
(28’) Good save from Boruc! Gardner shoots from 25 yards out, after being Arter all ends up with a neat touch. The ball zips off the turf and looks to creep into the bottom corner, but the ex-Celtic goalkeeper sprawls low to his right in order to make a smart stop. The resulting corner comes to absolutely nothing, due to a poor delivery.
(26’) The hosts threaten once again, with Arter lining up an effort. The Irishman takes aim from the best part of 30 yards, but places a swerving effort some way wide of the near post. The Cherries are trying to kick on since conceding, but they are yet to really get Afobe and Grabban into the game regularly.
(24’) The referee has a word with Arter, with the Republic of Ireland international pushing McAuley to the ground! The Bournemouth midfielder was reacting angrily to a full-bodied challenge from his opponent, but there can't be any excuses for that. The official opts to keep his cards in his pocket for now.
(22’) Bournemouth whip in a deep free-kick delivery from the right flank, but Stanislas' ball is terrible and the trajectory of it results in Foster watching it sail over his crossbar and wide. Rondon uses his strength brilliantly to muscle his way into the opposition penalty area, but Cook recovers well to deny the Baggies' goalscorer.
(20’) Foster is given some time to remove a beachball from the field of play, with that showing the atmosphere of this fixture. Both fans are enjoying their afternoon in the sun, if nothing else. Bournemouth will want to get back into this one, however, as every place they finish higher in the table will mean more prize money for their club.
(18’) Despite only having one real chance, West Brom find themselves ahead, with their fans cheering a very rare potential away win. Bournemouth win a corner on the right-hand side, but it is cleared behind for a second, but the successive delivery is also wasted. Howe's men don't seem to have any urgency at all, with the tempo not kicking up a gear.

Newcastle earn a point in their battle against the drop, but the news from the Stadium of Light is not good for the Magpies. Sunderland have beaten Chelsea 3-2 and as a result move out of the bottom three. The Black Cats can relegate Newcastle and Norwich on Wednesday if they beat Everton. Rafael Benitez and his men will be hugely deflated by their efforts today. They lacked the clinical edge in front of goal as Jack Colback and Aleksandar Mitrovic both missed sitters, which could mean that the club are playing Championship football next season. Villa did their part today, they were decent with the ball and did their defensive duties manfully, if not for a couple of let-offs from the Newcastle duo. The protests rage on at the club as supporters threw beach balls and paraded banners around the stadium, but hopefully they will be able to end their campaign in the Premier League with a small bit of pride.

Swansea visit London this afternoon knowing that their status in England's top-flight has been secured, mainly due to the upturn in form since the appointment of Francesco Guidolin. The Swans are currently down in 13th with 43 points taken from 36 matches, and are coming off a superb win against Liverpool last week when they ran out 3-1 winners against Jurgen Klopp's outfit, with a double from Jordan Ayew and a goal from Jack Cork sealing the three points.
The last game to ever take place at the Boleyn Ground will be this midweek when the Hammers take on Manchester United, but any sentiment will need to wait until after full-time as are there is only one place between the sides in the league. The hosts could be celebrating European football as well as one of England's most famous football grounds, though, as the bubbles float out on to the pitch for the last time.

They still have a very slight chance of getting into the Champions League, also, as they are currently placed in sixth, just five points away from the last qualification place. Europa League entry seems more likely, but there is still all to play for even at this stage of the season.
The tears are sure to start flowing this afternoon for Hammers fans as their team plays its last every 3pm Premier League kick-off at their famous Boleyn Ground in Upton Park. The field has been the home of West Ham for 112 years since its construction in 1904, but with residency in the 2012 Olympic Stadium up for grabs, the capital club find themselves moving into a new home from the start of next season,

Ranieri's men cap off their final home match of the season in clinical fashion, the only way they know how. Vardy opened the scoring early on, with King adding yet another feel good story with his strike shortly after to double the Foxes' lead. With all due respect to Everton, they'll play second fiddle this afternoon. Win, lose, or draw, there’s no spoiling Leicester’s party. The Toffees have nothing to play for themselves, and support will likely be lacking given the cost of being in attendance. If any Everton fans find themselves without a ticket, they can be had for a measly £500 in the away supporter’s section – which is actually a bit of a deal given how much the Leicester locals are being made to pay. If the allure of the Premier League trophy being lifted isn’t enough to tempt the Merseysiders, perhaps the vocals of one Mr. Andrea Bocelli will tickle their fancy.
Lost in all the noise, and taking a back seat to the occasion, is the fact there’s still a game to be played today! Leicester say they want to win their final home match, and while the sentiments are probably true, it’s going to be tough for them today. They have come off a booze-filled week of celebrations, where football was furthest from their mind as could be. Even without the week of distractions, it becomes a lot harder to find a source of motivation when the job is done.
The stories surrounding the Foxes improbable success have been beaten to death, and deservedly so. The 5,000-1 odds given at the start of the season to Leicester to win the title makes them the biggest sporting underdog to ever pay out. It’s a fairytale that will stick with surveyors of the sport around the world, becoming a story which promises to be passed on from generation to generation. You’ll be telling your grandkids about this one down the road: “kid, let me tell you a story... about one of the most unlikely triumphs the world has ever seen.” And we all were lucky enough to witness it. It hardly matters where your allegiances lie - we can all appreciate the incredible nature of Leicester's meteoric rise to the top.
They are deserving because they found what no one else could. Neither Tottenham, Arsenal nor the Manchester clubs could find what Leicester did - consistency. From the first day of the season when they trounced Sunderland 4-2 at this same venue, spearheaded by folklore legends Jamie Vardy and Riyad Mahrez, the Foxes stuck to Ranieri's plan and played it out time and time again with ruthless efficiency. There was no formula for stopping them. With Kasper Schmeichel in goal, the resurrection of Wes Morgan and Robert Huth in defence, N'Golo Kante and Danny Drinkwater as unlikely marshals in midfield, Shinji Okazaki's outstanding work rate up top, Jamie Vardy's pace and clinical finishing, and Riyad Mahrez's player of the year contributions in attack, Leicester found the winning formula and never strayed.
The sentiments throughout the season were very much consistent. It was a great story, but one no one truly thought would carry out to the end of the campaign. It was, and remains hard to fathom what was happening in Leicester when they reached the summit earlier in 2016. Well, it's happened - and it's fair to say there’s no one more deserving. They will be presented with the trophy after full-time at the King Power Stadium, giving them the chance to celebrate in front of their own fans before a final-day trip to the previous holders, Chelsea. Tickets are being advertised anywhere between £1,500 to £8,000, but it’s nothing a measly £10 bet back in August on the Foxes to win the title wouldn’t cover.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Leicester City's championship party at the King Power Stadium, as they play host to Everton. Claudio Ranieri's side clinched the Premier League title on Monday, with Tottenham playing to a draw with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. The Foxes didn't get to win it in front of their fans, but they can share it with them this afternoon - a party that promises to go long through the night as their week of celebrations culminate into one memorable day in Leicestershire.

Well, that’s all we’ve got time for this afternoon. As always, it has been a pleasure to bring you the action from the Premier League! Until next time, thank you and goodbye!
On the other hand, it is proving to be a fantastic end to the season for Southampton, who are well in the running for a place in next season’ Europa League, though they have played one more game than West Ham have.
Tottenham’s inability to hang onto the lead is what cost them their title challenge in the last two games, and their soft underbelly was again exposed today as - after they took an early lead through Heung-Min Son - a brace from Steven Davis secured the points for Ronald Koeman’s side. They are still all-but guaranteed a place in the top three of the Premier League, but should Arsenal win later this afternoon, Pochettino’s men may well have to go into the last game of the campaign against Newcastle United needing a victory to guarantee second spot.
FULL TIME! It’s all over at White Hart Lane, where Tottenham have failed to win for the third-game running as Southampton came from a goal behind to better the team of their former manager 2-1. It moves Southampton up into sixth, with the Saints matching last season’s level points total in the process. For the hosts, it opens the door for their rivals Arsenal to move level on points with them should they beat Manchester City this afternoon.

As for Watford, their season has stagnated somewhat, with a run of just two victories from their last eight Premier League fixtures - combined with an FA Cup semi-final defeat to Crystal Palace at Wembley - casting doubt on Quique Sanchez Flores' future, with reports suggesting he will leave at the end of the season. He has been tipped to be on the shortlist for what appears to be the soon-to-be vacant Everton job, with his compatriot Roberto Martinez seemingly fighting a losing battle to retain his job, while there is also said to be interest from his former club Valencia. However, Flores’ focus will be entirely on Watford’s final few games of the season. Having already staved off any threat of relegation by making it to 44 points, just four behind 10th-placed Stoke City, they could still feasibly mark their return to the top-flight with a top-flight finish.
Though Klopp’s style and philosophy looks to be finally taking shape on Merseyside, it must be said that the German has found it rather easier to implement his high-intensity pressing play in European competition than he has domestically. The Reds were beaten convincingly by Swansea City last time out, and were bettered 3-0 by Watford in the reverse fixture at Vicarage Road earlier in this campaign - their biggest defeat against a newly promoted side since 1993. However, they have suffered just one defeat in their last 11 Premier League matches at home, and with just Chelsea left to visit Anfield in 2015/16, the hosts - who still have a slim chance of qualifying for next season’s Europa League via the league - will be looking to end their domestic season on a high note.

This match was billed as a title decider whe the fixture list was first released, but with both of these sides disappointing hugely in the league, it has taken on a much less glamorous, but still significant connotation. Arsenal haven't lost in their last five games against City, with the Manchester club's last win against the Gunners coming in a 6-3 thriller in December 2013.
Arsenal were handed a boost by Tottenham's 2-1 loss at home to Southampton earlier in the day, meaning that they still have a chance of finishing in second place. A win will take them level on points with their London rivals, but behind on goal difference, taking that battle down  to the final day. Three points here will also ensure Arsene Wenger's men of third place and a guaranteed spot in the Champions League group stages.
Manuel Pellegrini takes charge of his final home game as City manager. With Arsenal three points ahead and Manchester United only a point behind in fifth, he knows that a win is vital to edge into the final automatic Champions League qualification spot. Even a draw won't be the worst result, given that they trail the Gunners by only one strike in goal difference - the tie-breaker if they finish level on points.

The game started off in frantic fashion, with Tom Cleverley giving the hosts the lead before Marc Pugh drew Bournemouth level. The second half was an even contest but, in the end, Everton just did enough to edge it courtesy of Baines’ strike - his first in open play in over three years - and bring to an end their awful run of form. However, it is unlikely that the three points will relieve any of the pressure on Roberto Martinez, who takes his side to champions-elect Leicester City next week before they face relegation-battling Sunderland and Norwich in the final two games of the campaign. As for Eddie Howe’s side, it is their third straight defeat, and although they can consider themselves safe from the drop, he will be looking for them to bounce back and end what has been a fine season on a high note.
FULL-TIME! It’s all over at Goodison Park, where Everton have beaten Bournemouth 2-1 thanks to Leighton Baines’ superb strike midway through the second half. It was a hard-fought victory for the hosts who, after suffering a humiliating defeat in the Merseyside derby and slumping out of the FA Cup, have managed to claim what is only their fifth home triumph of the Premier League campaign.

(90’) The fourth official has indicated a minimum of four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game. Can Everton finally hold onto a lead and avoid conceding a late goal to secure their first Premier League win in seven games?

HALF TIME! So, we’ve reached the interval at Goodison Park, where it is Everton 1-1 Bournemouth. The game started off in a flurry of activity as, just two minutes after falling behind to Tom Cleverley’s strike, the visitors were level courtesy of Mark Pugh’s ninth-minute effort. It has been a rather tepid affair since then, with the depth of feeling towards Everton’s current predicament being highlighted by a plane soaring in the skies overhead with a clear message to Roberto Martinez that fans feel he has outstayed his welcome at the club. The Spaniard will certainly need a big performance from his players in the second half…

If there was ever a sign that a fanbase has turned, largely en mass, against the manager, then this is it.

(40’) STAT FLASH – If Everton fail to win this afternoon, it will extend their winless streak in the Premier League to eight matches. The last time they failed to claim a single victory over a run of eight fixtures was under Walter Smith in 1999.
(38’) CHANCE! That’s a smart bit of goalkeeping by Boruc, who came off his line swiftly to prevent Barkley sliding a finish into the back of the net after he had raced onto the end of Niasse’s perfectly weighted through ball.

(22’) STAT FLASH – Everton have never lost against Bournemouth in the five matches they have played in all completions (W4 D1), with those fixtures having averaged four goals per game.

A touching moment now, as applause rings out in tribute as the families of the 96 victims of the Hillsborough disaster who, after 27 years, have this week finally seen some semblance of justice served for the deaths of their family members, make their way out onto the pitch. For all the rivalries between Everton and Liverpool, the blue side of Merseyside has never faltered in sticking by their neighbours, showing that the city will always be united as one.
The teams are out onto the pitch now, and going through the typical pre-match niceties. It is the fist-ever league meeting between the two sides at Goodison. The reverse fixture back in November finished 3-3 in dramatic fashion, with Stanislas’ last-gasp header cancelling out Ross Barkley’s stoppage-time strike. Martinez’s side did, however, inflict some revenge on the Cherries in February, when they claimed a 2-0 victory at the Vitality Stadium in the fifth round of the FA Cup.
It will certainly be interesting to soak in the atmosphere from Goodison Park this afternoon. The discontent amongst the Everton faithful has been steadily growing over the course of the campaign, and though Martinez has claimed he “feels the pain” of the supporters, that has done nothing to quell the fans’ desire to see the Spaniard relieved of his duties. If the hosts fail to get a positive result today, there may well be little other choice for Bill Kenwright and the Everton board members, including new majority shareholder Fahrad Moshiri - who supposedly met in the week to discuss Martinez’s future at the club - than to make the change that seems to be required.

Everton’s home form has been terrible this season - the Toffees have lost eight of their Premier League games at Goodison Park - and Eddie Howe’s Bournemouth have also had a similar issue, with their performances and results on the road often better than those at the Vitality Stadium. The visitors slumped to their fourth defeat in five games, and a second on the bounce, with a 4-1 loss to Chelsea on the south coast last weekend, and will be looking to bounce back with a strong display today. A victory would see them leapfrog Everton and potentially move up to 11th, should results elsewhere go their way.
Any hope of Everton salvaging something from what has been another disappointing season were ended last week as Anthony Martial’s last-gasp strike at Wembley ensured that it was Manchester United who progressed to the FA Cup final, not the Toffees. Roberto Martinez’s side have not won since March 12, and their winless streak in the league now stretches back seven games. The Spaniard has insisted that he is not worrying about his position and is purely focusing on a strong end to the campaign, but if he fails to deliver anything but with the majority of fans now disillusioned with the former Wigan manager’s style of play and refusal or inability to sure-up the Toffees’ defence, it does appear he is living on borrowed time.

Speaking of Crystal Palace, the Eagles are soaring following their FA Cup semi-final success last weekend and there’s no question they will have one eye on the final over the remaining three weeks of the season. While they aren’t mathematically safe in the Premier League, it would take an incredibly unlucky string of results to see them finish in the bottom three – and as a result, their season will hinge on the May 21st clash with Manchester United at Wembley, as they chase their first success in the competition.
Besides, Newcastle have bigger fish to fry. The Magpies are fighting for their lives in the Premier League, though they’re just a point back of Sunderland who play away to Stoke this afternoon. The Black Cats have a game in hand, but three points today would give Rafa Benitez’s side a great chance of avoiding the drop – defeat would leave them hanging by a thread, and while Palace certainly won’t lay down, Pardew still undeniably has a special place in his heart for Newcastle and would hate to be the man to send them down.
These Geordies are educated football fans and they realise all the good work Pardew did while at St. James’ Park, which included a fifth-place finish in 2011/12, booking their ticket to the Europa League. He made it clear this week that he still has a great relationship with some of the players there, and he was beloved by fans up until the bitter end, so it would be a bit of a surprise to see him jeered as Palace make their way out of the tunnel.
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Alan Pardew’s return to St. James’ Park as Newcastle aim to keep their Premier League status afloat when they play host to Crystal Palace. Today marks the first time the 54-year-old returns to Tyneside since leaving the Toon Army after more than four years in charge of the club. Despite a tumultuous end to his tenure during his final month in charge, Pardew was a great manager for Newcastle – who likely wouldn’t be in this predicament had he stayed in charge – and because of that he figures to receive a warm welcome ahead of kick-off.

Things are rather more straightforward for Sunderland. This is the fifth league match in a row in which Allardyce has named the exact same starting XI. The visitors' side boasts plenty of steel in the middle, with Lee Cattermole, Yann M'Vila and Jan Kirchhoff, while their front trio of Jermain Defoe, Khazri and Fabio Borini possesses a good combination of pace, power and work rate.
The home side have made significant changes to the side which was on the end of a 4-0 thumping at Manchester City a week ago - five alterations, to be precise. In goal Haugaard comes in for Given, while at the back both Marc Muniesa and Philipp Wollscheid drop to the bench, with Erik Pieters and Charlie Adam coming in for them. The other two to come back into the side are Xherdan Shaqiri and Peter Crouch (making only his third league start of the season). Joselu and Mame Biram Diouf drop to an attack-minded bench, which also contains Jon Walters and Bojan.
Sunderland's position is rather more desperate than Stoke's as they battle away towards the bottom, hoping to hold on to the 17th spot they currently occupy. Their form of late has certainly helped ease the tension a little, losing only once in their last seven games and picking up three clean sheets in four outings. However, they've still only managed one victory since the end of February. One major bonus for them has been the form of January signing Lamine Kone, who attracted special praise from his manager in the week. In fact, Sam Allardyce claims it was his best January transfer window ever, with Wahbi Khazri also catching the eye since his switch from Bordeaux.
There is little left to play for this season from Stoke's perspective, with Mark Hughes' men comfortably safe from the drop in tenth place but a little too far off to challenge for a European spot. That in itself looked a real possibility until not too long ago, but three defeats on the spin in the league have seen them fall nine points behind sixth-placed West Ham United. Nevertheless, their coach will be desperate to stop the rot and potentially finish above one of his former clubs in Chelsea, whom they are level with on 47 points. Perhaps he also has one eye on impressing a prospective new employer - the former Manchester United star has been strongly linked with a switch to Everton, should Roberto Martinez get the boot.

As for Norwich, they may currently sit at the opposite end of the table but their job is exactly the same as Arsenal’s. Sunderland’s draw last weekend was enough to move them out of the relegation zone, sending the Canaries down in their place, and the Black Cats now sit one point in front thanks to today's narrow 1-1 draw away to Stoke City. After winning back-to-back games against West Bromwich Albion and Newcastle United, Alex Neil’s men head to the Emirates with two defeats from their previous two clashes, leaving them in desperate need of all three points today. Despite the Gunners’ current struggles, it’s not going to be easy, and Norwich’s run-in looks just as difficult, with games against Manchester United, Watford and Everton still to play before the end of the campaign. Their poor away form hasn’t helped, and they currently have just one win from their last eight league clashes played away from Carrow Road. During that time they have managed to find the back of the net just twice, with scoring goals proving to be a real problem for them. Strikers Dieumerci Mbokani and Cameron Jerome have both looked poor in front of goal, with the former scoring just once in his last 11 appearances whilst the latter hasn’t hit the back of the net at all this year. If Norwich are to have any hope of pulling off a much-needed win today, their forward line will have to be in top form.
Another disappointing season has left many Arsenal fans feeling frustrated at both the board and Arsene Wenger, the latter of whom once again finds himself faced with questions about his future at the club. Two supporters’ groups are planning to stage protests during today’s game, and it could end up having an impact on a side that desperately need to pick up all three points this afternoon. Last weekend’s frustrating goalless draw away to Sunderland resulted in the Gunners dropping down to fourth place, still on course to qualify for the Champions League for yet another season but worryingly close to Manchester United, who have won four of their last five Premier League games and sit five points behind the North London club. In contrast, Arsenal have won just twice in that time, leaving them in real danger of finishing behind in-form Manchester City. The two teams are currently tied on 64 points, meaning that Arsene Wenger’s only priority now is to win the remaining three games of the season in an attempt to guide his side to a third-place finish for the second consecutive campaign, but with a trip to the Etihad scheduled for eight days’ time, the battle looks set to go down to the wire.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Arsenal and Norwich City at the Emirates Stadium.

The referee brings things to a close, with Swansea running out comfortable 3-1 winners to confirm their status as a Premier League club for another year. Apart from a 15 minute spell which included a slight Liverpool improvement, the home side were far superior, dominating playing with way more hunger than their visitors. Klopp's men were guilty of so many individual errors and some didn't look overly interested. They'll need to raise their game massively on Thursday.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
(90’) Shouts of "ole" are coming from the Swansea fans now, as they casually knock the ball around with victory almost secured.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution A late change now, as Britton gets a standing ovation and is replaced by Fulton. ---
(90’) There will be four minutes added on here.
(88’) Good play by Swansea! Sigurdsson gets the ball inside from Routledge and gets a shot away from 25 yards, sending it just past the post. Ayew was unmarked just to his left, though, and he lets the Iceland star know about that in no uncertain terms.
(86’) Can Swansea make this even more comfortable? Liverpool haven't really offered anything since Ayew's second goal and the hosts and still getting plenty of men forward.
(84’) Good effort from Sigurdsson, as the midfielder charges forward after picking up the ball in the left channel and goes for goal from 30 yards, but Ward makes the stop.
(82’) Things look like they are starting to peter out a little here. Swansea remain on the front foot, though, generally dictating possession.
--- 80’ Substitution Another Liverpool change now. Ibe, who has been utterly anonymous, makes way and is replaced by Brannagan. ---
(79’) LIVERPOOL SURVIVE! The resulting corner is clipped into the area and appears to strike the hand of Sturridge, but the referee ignores the protests. The ball then drops kindly for Rangel, but his emphatic strike goes agonisingly wide of the top-right corner.
--- 77’ Yellow card Another booking, this time for Skrtel as he cynically blocks off Routledge out wide. The resulting free-kick is swiftly knocked behind for a corner. ---
--- 76’ Red card! RED CARD! Swansea clear the Liverpool corner and Naughton pounces, knocking the ball over Smith and drawing a clumsy tackle. Roger East trudges over and shows the young left-back a second yellow card and a subsequent red. ---
--- 74’ Yellow card Cynical from Rangel, as he is beaten for pace by Ojo so he opts to pull him back and bring him down. Out comes the yellow card. ---
--- 73’ Substitution Here comes a Swansea switch, as Naughton comes on for Montero, who has been excellent. ---
(71’) More pressure from the home side, as Ayew robs Ojo and races forward up the right. Eventually Routledge attempts to cross but his delivery is blocked by Smith.
(69’) Brilliant response by Swansea. They had been quite poor since the break, sitting back and allowing Liverpool a lifeline, but as soon as the visitors appeared to claw their way back into it they hit them with a suckerpunch.
--- 67’ Goal! GOAL!!!! SWANSEA REPLY INSTANTLY! Montero causes havoc on the left and digs a cross into the centre. Ojo can't get a clearance in and finds himself outmuscled by Ayew, who then squeezes the ball inside the left-hand post. ---
--- 65’ Assist A good delivery from the corner by Ojo, as he drops it right in the centre and lays it on a plate for Benteke. ---
--- 65’ Goal! GOAL!!!! LIVERPOOL PULL ONE BACK! After a pause for Fabianski to get medical attention, Ojo's corner delivery is decent and Benteke manages to lose Sigurdsson, heading into the bottom-right corner. Game on! ---
(63’) Better from the visitors, as Clyne gets forward from right-back and plays a good give-and-go with Sturridge, but Rangel sees out the danger and collides with Fabianski in the process. Corner to Liverpool.
(61’) Liverpool may be seeing more of the ball, but it is all so slow and lacking invention. They've no creativity in the final third, with Ibe being kept quiet and the service to Benteke really poor.
(59’) More moaning from Benteke, as the Belgian again feels as though he is fouled at the corner, but in truth most of the players in the area were tussling with each other.
(58’) SWANSEA SURVIVE! Ojo clips a decent delivery into the area and Benteke claims for a penalty following a nudge from Rangel, with Britton rather nonchalantly knocking the ball just past the post. That wasn't far from going in!
(57’) Clyne takes the corner but the delivey is poor, not getting past the first man, with Routledge heading clear. What a waste.
(56’) Good defending from Rangel, as the experienced right-back tracks Ojo and then blocks the winger's attempted cross. Liverpool win a corner, though.
(54’) Liverpool are seeing a bit more of the ball at the start of the second half, but Lovren almost gifts Swansea a great chances as his pass to Smith is well underhit. Routledge races on to it but then slips, much to the relief of the visitors.
(52’) This is a problem for Swansea. Ayew appeared to take a bit of a kick from Lovren and he has gone down. Liverpool eventually put the ball out of play to allow him to get medical attention.
(50’) Another misplaced pass from Liverpool, as Sturridge drops deep to collect the ball and then slices it straight out of play.
(48’) Klopp will be hoping that the introduction of Lucas in place of Chirivella adds a little more stability in midfield. That was their biggest problem in the first half.
--- 46’ Substitution And the second change sees Lucas come in for Chirivella, who endured a tough Premier League debut. ---
--- 46’ Substitution We are back under way for the second half. Liverpool have made changes at the break, with Benteke replacing Coutinho as the first. ---
The referee brings the first half to a close, seemingly putting Liverpool out of their misery. The much-changed visitors have been extremely poor so far today, with Swansea running them ragged at times. They may have two goals thanks to Ayew and the brilliant Cork, but in truth it could quite easily have been four were it not for the efforts of Ward between the posts. Expect changes from Klopp at the break.
(45’) HALF-TIME!
(45’) Well, that won't cause too many problems for Swansea! Sturridge steps up to the free-kick and skews it horribly wide of the mark. That was pretty terrible.
(44’) Maybe one last chance here before the break for Liverpool, as Coutinho tricks his way past Britton about 25 yards from goal and forces a foul from the midfielder.
(43’) Things are petering out a little here ahead of half-time, with Swansea sitting back a little more, inviting Liverpool forward. The atmosphere has gone very quiet.
--- 41’ Yellow card Clever turn from Stewart, as his first-touch sees him completely beat Cork, who leaves a leg in and rather cynically brings him down. Out comes the yellow card again. ---
--- 39’ Yellow card Montero is causing all sorts of problems today. The rapid Ecuadorian cuts in from the left and surges past Clyne. The full-back keeps at his task but ultimately trips the winger from behind and gets booked. ---
(37’) JUST WIDE! Sturridge latches on to a pass played in behind Amat from Ojo and show great craft to produce a chipped effort from outside the area. His attempt has Fabianski scrambling, but luckily for the goalkeeper the ball bounces just past the post.
(35’) Swansea have been exceptional so far. Liverpool may well have an inexperienced side out, but you can only beat team in front of you and the home side are making light work of them at the moment.
--- 33’ Goal! GOAL!!! WHAT A STRIKE! Swansea double their lead and in some style! Cork outmuscles Coutinho in the middle and then strides forward. Space opens up on the edge of the area and the former Southampton man casually caresses a fine finish into the top-right corner from 25 yards. ---
(31’) Another Swansea chance! Chirivella is robbed by Montero in midfield and the Ecuadorian quickly gets the ball back again from Ayew. He races towards goal and gets a shot away, forcing a good stop from Ward.
(30’) Coutinho clips the corner delivery into the area and Skrtel manages to get a touch to it, but it is comfortably shepherded out by Swansea.
(29’) Corner for Liverpool now, as Sturridge gets on to a Coutinho pass into the area and Williams comes across to see out the danger.
(28’) WHAT A MISS! Sigurdsson flashes a fine cross into the area from the free-kick and Amat is left with a simple finish from four yards out, but he somehow heads it over!
--- 27’ Yellow card Poor defending from Smith, as the youngster finds Routledge in behind him and he is forced to tug him back. Out comes the yellow card. ---
(26’) BIG SAVE! Brilliant play by Swansea. Montero picks out an intricate pass into the area for the advancing Taylor. The left-back latches on to it and cuts a decent ball back into the danger zone. Sigurdsson smashes it goalwards but Ward makes a crucial save.
(24’) Another good move from the away side. Clyne's cross is easily headed out, but Chirivella pounces. The Spaniard finds Coutinho, who in turn picks out Ibe. The winger beats Britton and gets the ball on to his left foot, shooting from 25 yards and forcing a straightforward save from Fabianski.
(22’) NO PENALTY! Liverpool are straight back on the front foot Coutinho dribbles his way into the area and gets past one tackle, before seemingly beating Amat and getting brought down. There was clear contact but no penalty given.
--- 20’ Goal! GOAL!!! SWANSEA TAKE THE LEAD! Sigurdsson clips a fine corner delivery into the danger zone and Ayew rises to meet it, heading it past Ward after losing his man. ---
(20’) LIVERPOOL SURVIVE! Brillant counter from the home side, as Montero finds Cork in the centre and they charge forward. The midfielder picks out Routledge in a central position and his first touch is a clever flick into the path of Ayew. The Ghana star looks destined to net but Lovren makes a crucial block. Corner.
--- 20’ Assist Assist Gylfi Þór Sigurðsson ---
(19’) The initial free-kick doesn't cause Liverpool too much bother, but the visitors don't clear their lines very well and Swansea remain on the front foot. Cork manages to get just inside the area, he shifts on to his right foot and then tries a clever flick to feed the overlapping Montero, but it is just cut out.
(17’) Free-kick now to Swansea, as Ayew receives a ball into feet and Skrtel barges into him from behind. This is a decent position to create something, with Sigurdsson standing over it about 35 yards from goal.
(15’) ANOTHER CHANCE! Swansea are ramping up the pressure here. Another individual error, this time from Sturridge, and the hosts burst forward quickly. Montero jinks past a couple of challenges and then feeds Ayew. He rides Lovren's challenge and then smashes goalwards after the ball sat up nicely for him, but he slices a wild effort well over.
(13’) LIVERPOOL ESCAPE! Britton plays a good ball into Ayew on the edge of the area and he knocks it down for Sigurdsson. The Iceland star hits it first-time and forces a stop from Ward. The visitors then mess things up again as Coutinho is caught in possession in a dangerous area, but Smith sees out the danger by knocking a cross out of play.
(11’) More good play by the visitors on the left flank. This time it is Ibe doing the damage, squeezing a cross into the danger zone and Sturridge manages to steer it towards goal, but it goes wide.
(10’) Good play by Ojo, as the winger pops up in the middle, glides across the pitch and feeds Smith. The left-back does well to get a low cross into the area, but it is easily cleared by Amat.
(9’) The referee is forced into giving his first lecture to a Liverpool player, as Smith goes in hard on Routledge out wide. The left-back insists he got the ball, but it was a pretty wild tackle.
(7’) Liverpool try to play their way through Swansea, as Sturridge and Coutinho link up, but Williams steps out brilliantly and tackles the England international.
(5’) It's Swansea dictating the early play here, as they get the ball forward quickly, but this time it falls apart when Britton clips the ball into the final third for Ayew, only for it to sail harmlessly through to Ward.
(3’) The first genuine attack of the match sees Swansea rob Liverpool of possession in the centre, as Cork cuts out a misplaced pass from Chirivella. They work it forward quickly and Montero clips it into the area. Ayew brings it down and tries to get a shot away but it is well blocked.
(1’) Off we go! Liverpool get us started in Wales.
The players are now out on the pitch ahead of kick-off, with a minute's applause for the 96 who died in the Hillsborough disaster following the recent verdict and justice handed out 27 years on.
It is certainly an inexperienced side Klopp has chosen today, evidence of his focus really being on the Europa League and the prize of Champions League qualification for the victors. Their opponents today don't have to make such wholesale changes, though they have very little left to play for this season, as they sit on 40 points, that fabled benchmark for Premier League survival. They've had a pretty unspectacular season, however, and consecutive defeats in their last two games which have seen them concede seven times without reply will likely have their coach Francesco Guidolin after an improvement today. And considering how unfamiliar this Liverpool side is, you'd expect them to give it a good go.
Daniel Ward comes in for Simon Mignolet between the posts, while at left-back Brad Smith gets his second start of the season. The deep midfield duo will be Kevin Stewart and Spanish 18-year-old Pedro Chirivella, a highly rated Premier League debutant. Seyi Ojo will be one of the three supporting the returning Daniel Sturrdige, with Jordon Ibe and Philippe Coutinho also in the side. Their main man today will likely be playing with something of a point to prove, having been left out of the team in Spain on Thursday.
It will come as little surprise to most to see a host of changes in the Liverpool side today. Jurgen Klopp's men's exertions in the Europa League on Thursday see them still with a great chance of winning the competition after losing just 1-0 in Villarreal, with the return leg next week. Their coach clearly has his sights fixed firmly on the Europa League and has made a total of eight changes to his team for today, with several youngsters getting a run out.
Liverpool subs: Mignolet, Lucas, Brannagan, Teixeira, Lallana, Benteke.
Liverpool starting XI (4-2-3-1): Ward; Clyne, Lovren, Skrtel, Smith; Chirivella, Stewart; Ibe, Coutinho, Ojo; Sturridge.
Swansea subs: Nordfeldt, Naughton, Fernandez, Ki, Fulton, Barrow, Gomis.
TEAM NEWS: Swansea City starting XI (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Rangel, Amat, Williams, Taylor; Britton, Cork; Routledge, Sigurdsson, Montero; Ayew.
Hello and welcome to the LIVE coverage of the Premier League clash between Swansea City and Liverpool. I will be describing all of the action for you today, as these two sides go head-to-head at the Liberty Stadium, with the visitors hoping to keep the pressure on West Ham United and Manchester United.

Despite their best efforts, Leicester's wait for the Premier League title goes on after being held to what was, under the circumstances, a good point. After going behind so early it looked as if they may be on course for a rare defeat, but they fought back valiantly and caused plenty of problems for United during a second half in which both sides were battling hard for that all-important second goal. In the end, neither could find it, meaning that Claudio Ranieri's men must now wait for the league crown until at least tomorrow, when a win for Chelsea against Tottenham Hotspur would confirm their victory.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-1 LEICESTER CITY
(90’) United try to push forward on one last attack as they fling ball after ball into the Leicester penalty area, but no matter what they do they just can't seem to turn their possession into a chance on goal. The visitors are eventually able to clear the danger before Ulloa is brought crashing to the ground by Blind, resulting in a free-kick for the Foxes that will surely be the last action of the game.
(90’) Fantastic goalkeeping by Schmeichel! Valencia charges down the right flank before sending a lovely through-ball into the path of Martial, but it's just about cut out by Huth before it can find the Frenchman. The defender's sliced clearance rolls over to the edge of the Leicester penalty area, however, but the Danish goalkeeper charges out and cuts out the danger with a vital sliding interception before Depay can get a shot away.
(90’) It's all United at the moment as they continually push forward in search of what would surely be the winner, but they just can't seem to find a way through the blue shirts camped in front of them. Leicester have every single player camped behind the ball and are doing incredibly well to keep the hosts at bay.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be four minutes of added time.
(88’) After spending what feels like an age eyeing up his target, Rooney eventually steps up and whips a curling shot towards goal that Schmeichel does well to punch away from danger. United quickly win themselves another free-kick that Depay fires into the wall in front of him, but Rooney is there to try and test the Danish goalkeeper with a long-range shot that is well saved once again.
--- 87’ Substitution Leicester quickly throw on King to replace Mahrez as they look to hold on to what would be a big point under the circumstances. But will they manage to do so? ---
--- 86’ Red card! RED CARD! Leicester will have to play the final few minutes of the game with 10 men after Drinkwater receives his second yellow card of the game. Depay, who has made a big impact since coming on to the pitch, once again causes problems with his pace before being dragged to the ground by the midfielder just a few inches outside of the box, leaving the referee with no choice but to award a free-kick to the hosts before showing the Englishman a red card. The United players are arguing that the contact actually happened inside the penalty area, and the replays seem to indicate that it may well have done. ---
(84’) Depay breaks down the left wing on a marauding run before being tripped over from behind by Mahrez, leaving the referee with no choice but to award a free-kick to United. Rooney steps up and fires a looping cross into the middle of the box, but Schmeichel is there to cut out the danger with a strong catch under very little pressure from red shirts.
--- 82’ Substitution Rashford receives a rousing round of applause from the United fans as he's replaced by Depay for the final eight minutes of the game. Can the Dutchman help the hosts find what would surely be a winning goal? ---
(81’) And now Mata goes close! Rooney picks up the ball just outside of the United penalty area before sending a lovely through-ball into the path of Valencia. The Ecuadorian sprints into the right-hand side of the penalty area before sending a lovely cross over to the Spaniard, who is just about to meet the ball in the air but can't direct his headed effort on target.
(80’) What a chance for Ulloa! A determined United attacking move breaks down, allowing Leicester to fly forward on a great counter-attack thanks to good play by Albrighton. Mahrez sprints down the right wing and cuts inside before teeing up the Argentine with a chipped cross, but the striker ends up scuffing his volleyed shot up into the air and on to the head of Rooney, who then nods the ball into the hands of De Gea.
(78’) Smalling hits the post! Rooney darts around just outside of the penalty area before chipping a great cross over to the far post, where it finds the centre-back. He rises high and meets the ball well before sending a bouncing header towards goal, but it ends up smashing off the outside of the woodwork after missing the fingertips of Schmeichel by the narrowest of margins.
--- 77’ Substitution Leicester have made their second substitution of the game, with Albrighton coming on to replace Schlupp. ---
(76’) Another interception by Morgan! Martial is starting to cause plenty of problems down the left wing, where his pace and skill is giving Leicester real problems. This time he darts past two blue shirts before whipping a low cross-cum-shot towards the six-yard box, but the big centre-back is there to stick out a foot to send the ball away from danger and out to the opposite flank.
--- 75’ Substitution Fellaini makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Herrera for the final quarter of an hour of the game. ---
(74’) Great block by Morgan! Once again, Rojo finds himself in plenty of space deep down the left flank before cutting inside and finding Martial. The Frenchman takes a great first touch before trying to unleash a low shot from just inside the penalty area, but the Leicester captain is there to cut out the danger with a vital block.
(73’) It doesn't quite seem to be working for United, who are seeing plenty of the ball in advanced positions but are finding it difficult to do much with it. This time it's Rojo who quickly breaks down the left flank and gets himself into a good area before swinging a cross into the middle of the box, but there's nobody there to meet it and it's dealt with by Fuchs as a result.
(71’) Lovely play by Mahrez! Leicester break forward on a blisteringly quick counter-attack through Mahrez, who twists and turns on the edge of the United penalty area before unleashing a looping 20-yard shot. It looks as if it's going to find the roof of the net, but De Gea does well to parry the strike away from goal with a two-fisted save.
(69’) Mata battles his way down the right wing before Schlupp pokes the ball out for a corner. Blind steps up and curls a great cross straight on to the head of Fellaini, who once again is easily able to beat his marker in the air before sending a bullet header marginally wide of the Leicester goal. Both sides are finding plenty of joy from set-pieces, which will be a cause for concern for both managers.
--- 67’ Substitution Leicester have made their first change of the afternoon, with Okazaki making way for Gray. ---
--- 66’ Yellow card Once again, Mahrez causes plenty of problems for United as he tries to break down the left flank, but he's clattered into by Rooney and wins his side a free-kick near to the halfway line. The United captain isn't at all happy with the decision and reacts angrily to the linesman nearest to him, and as a result he becomes the latest player to be shown a yellow card. ---
(64’) Mahrez weaves down the right wing on a great run before being clumsily tripped over by Martial, resulting in a free-kick for Leicester in a very advantageous position. Drinkwater steps up and whips in a wonderful cross that finds the head of Ulloa, but the Argentine's effort ends up fizzing just wide of the far post. He's been causing plenty of problems for the hosts since the start of the second half, and Blind is really struggling to deal with him in the air.
--- 62’ Substitution United have decided to make their first substitution of the afternoon, with Mata coming on to replace Lingard. ---
(60’) Chance for Rooney! Kante loses the ball on the edge of the Leicester penalty area, allowing United to pick up possession in a dangerous position before Valencia whips a low cross into the box. It's just about dealt with by the visitors before the ball rolls out to the hosts' captain, but his attempted chipped shot is completely overhit and comfortably sails over the top of the crossbar and out for a goal-kick.
--- 58’ Yellow card The referee's yellow card is out once again, and this time it's Drinkwater who's the culprit, as he cynically pulls back Rashford as the youngster tries to sprint down the left wing and leaves the man in charge with no choice but to reach for his pocket. ---
--- 57’ Yellow card Carrick loses the ball in the middle of the pitch and immediately flies in to Schlupp to try and retrieve it, but he ends up catching the Ghanaian and sends him crashing to the ground before becoming the latest player to receive a yellow card. ---
(56’) Schlupp trips Martial to the ground as the two battle for the ball down the right wing, resulting in a free-kick for United. It's taken short and worked over to Lingard, who then tries to play a quick one-two with Rashford on the edge of the box, but the striker's looping pass is easily cut out by Drinkwater before it can find the young winger.
(55’) Leicester have started the second half really well and are firmly on the front foot as they continue to put United's back line under an incredible amount of pressure. A lofted pass is flung forward and finds Okazaki on the edge of the box, and the striker does well to nod it down to Ulloa. The Argentine immediately unleashes a thumping, first-time shot, but it takes a deflection off the foot of Blind that sends it out for a corner. Once again, the set-piece finds Ulloa in a dangerous position, but his header fails to trouble De Gea and flies several yards wide of the far post.
--- 53’ Yellow card A heavy touch from Lingard sends the ball straight to Drinkwater, who then tries to kick-start a quick Leicester counter-attack. The visitors initially move the ball around well before Schlupp tries to sprint down the left wing, but his run is broughto to an end by the United youngster, who receives a yellow card as a result. ---
(52’) Two good chances for Leicester! Mahrez and Simpson link up well midway down the right wing before the latter takes advantage of poor defending from Rojo to penetrate the penalty area. He then tries to tee up Okazaki with a deft pass towards the edge of the six-yard box, but the ball ends up taking a slight knick of Carrick which sends it rolling out for a corner. The set-piece is sent straight on to the head of Ulloa, but the Argentine's effort ends up looping over the top of the crossbar.
(50’) Schlupp twists and turns on the left wing before firing a very dangerous cross into the heart of the United penalty area. Okazaki does well to rise high and almost meets the ball ahead of Smalling, but the centre-back beats him to it before earning his side a free-kick after receiving a push from the Japanese striker.
(48’) Chance for Martial! Fellaini does well to chest down a throw-in on the left-hand side of the Leicester penalty area before spinning and finding the French forward, who then quickly penetrates the box before curling a shot past Schmeichel but just over the top of the crossbar.
(47’) Leicester quickly push forward down the left wing before earning themselves a corner, which Fuchs swings straight on to the head of Morgan. Once again, the defender beats his marker with ease before sending a bouncing header towards goal, but De Gea is just about able to cut out the danger before Ulloa can get a foot on the ball just a yard or so off the line.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
What a first half that was! Both sides are really going for it and impressing whenever they push forward, so it's no wonder that the tie is still on a knife-edge as we head into the half-time break. United got the perfect start when Martial latched on to a Valencia cross before slotting the ball under Schmeichel, but Leicester showed great grit and determination to fight back and equalise through Morgan, who took advantage of poor defending to beat De Gea. Since then, the two teams have been fighting tooth and nail to find a way back in front, but with 45 minutes left to play, this game could still go either way.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-1 LEICESTER CITY
(45’) It's all United at the moment as they continue to put Leicester under plenty of pressure. Martial and Rooney work the ball around well just outside of the box before Lingard and Valencia play a lovely one-two between themselves deep down the right wing. The young Englishman then chips a deft cross into the heart of the penalty area, but, not for the first time today, there's nobody there to meet it and it can only find a blue shirt.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
(43’) And now it's United that are on the front foot! Ball after ball is flung into the Leicester penalty area but the visitors are just about able to deal with the initial danger, with a 20-yard strike from Rooney being closed down well by Drinkwater. Valencia then picks up the ball on the right wing before cutting inside and firing a low shot towards goal, but this time it's Huth who sticks out a foot to stop the effort from testing Schmeichel.
(41’) It's all Leicester at the moment as they desperately push forward in search of a second goal. Ulloa, who has been largely quiet thus far but is now coming to life, breaks towards the edge of the penalty area before teeing up Drinkwater, but the midfielder's low shot is deflected out of play for a corner. The set-piece once again finds Morgan, who easily beats Rojo in the middle of the box, but this time the defender's header ends up clearing the top of the crossbar by quite some distance.
(39’) It's all going on inside the United penalty area! First, Schlupp cuts inside from the left wing before forcing De Gea into making a last-gasp, flapping save with a curling cross-cum-shot that causes the Spaniard plenty of problems. The ball then bounces out to Mahrez, who immediately goes down after clashing with Rojo, but the referee isn't at all interested in his protestations and waves for play to go on.
(37’) Simpson charges down the right flank before teeing up Mahrez, who takes a couple of quick touches before curling a wonderful cross into the heart of the penalty area. Ulloa makes a great run into the box and does well to meet the ball ahead of Smalling, but he's unable to direct his headed effort towards goal and it ends up looping several yards over the top of the crossbar.
(35’) Rojo does well to out-muscle Mahrez in the middle of the pitch before dispossessing the Algerian and kick-starting a United counter-attack. The hosts work the ball forward quickly before Lingard battles furiously with Fuchs on the right-hand side of the penalty area, but the Austrian comes out on top before having to concede a corner. The set-piece is curled to the far post, where it finds Fellaini, but the Belgian is unable to get enough power behind his effort and it's easily stopped by Schmeichel as a result.
(33’) United come back at Leicester once again and continue finding joy down the left wing. Rashford cuts into the penalty area and weaves his way towards goal before unleashing a low cross-cum-shot, but it ends up deflecting off the foot of Morgan before Schmeichel does well to stop the ball from rolling out of play for a corner.
(31’) Big call by the referee! Simpson picks up the ball on the halfway line and completely mishits an attempted pass over to Drinkwater. It's easily cut out by Lingard, who then sprints towards the Leicester penalty area whilst battling with the right-back, but the latter is just about able to come out on top before Schmeichel rushes out to clear the danger. The young United winger goes down on the edge of the box and screams for a free-kick, but the referee isn't at all interested and allows play to go on.
(29’) Vital block by Valencia! Ulloa muscles his way inside from the right wing before teeing up Mahrez, who then weaves his way towards the edge of the penalty area before finding Schlupp. The Ghanaian takes two quick touches and then fires a thumping low shot that the Ecuadorian does well to send over the top of the crossbar with an outstretched foot.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this evening…
As for Chelsea, the impressive Premier League unbeaten run that they embarked on in the immediate aftermath of Guus Hiddink’s return was finally brought to an end by Swansea City at the start of last month, and it was immediately followed by a comfortable 3-0 victory for Manchester City at Stamford Bridge. As a result, the Blues head into tonight’s game in danger of losing back-to-back home league clashes for the first time since November 2011. A season to forget for the West London club means that it has already been confirmed that they will be finishing outside of the top six for the first time since 1996, but they will still no doubt be motivated to put in a strong performance against their rivals, if only to stop them from being the team to pick up the Premier League title that they so impressively won last season. Asmir Begovic and Eden Hazard both said as much in the buildup to tonight’s encounter, with Mousa Dembele hitting back at his Belgium teammate by claiming that he is “envious of Tottenham’s success” because Chelsea “failed to rise to the occasion” this season. As a result, tonight’s clash is expected to be an incredibly feisty one, with both sides desperately wanting to come away as victors.
It’s now or never for Tottenham, whose chances of winning the Premier League title are slim but still a possibility if they are able to win all of their remaining three games. Anything but all three points in any of those clashes will automatically hand the crown to league leaders Leicester, so tonight’s London derby is one that has had an extra amount of spice added to it. Last week’s 1-1 draw at home to West Bromwich Albion was a thoroughly disappointing one, but there is no denying that Mauricio Pochettino’s men have been in fine form throughout the season and head to Stamford Bridge with a great chance of finally getting one over their rivals, who have consistently frustrated the North London club over the past two and a half decades. Tottenham haven’t won in West London since 1990, a 25-game run in which they’ve been on the losing end 17 times, whilst they haven’t managed to score a single goal in their previous three games on this ground. However, not only will they be buoyed by the seven-game domestic unbeaten run that they currently find themselves on, but they have also lost just one of their last 10 London derbies, with that defeat coming against West Ham United exactly two months ago.

(29’) This is better from Everton at the minute, with Martinez’s side having seen the majority of the possession in the last five minutes or so. This is definitely promising for the visitors.
(27’) SO CLOSE! Barkley again gets forward to the edge of Palace’s area, managing to lay a pass off into the general direction of Kone. The former Wigan striker meets it on the run, powering a first-time strike goalwards. It beats Hennessey all-ends-up, but whistles just over the crossbar.
(25’) After that brief period of goalmouth action, the game has settled back into its somewhat lackadaisical rhythm now, with both sides seemingly unwilling to stretch themselves too far in order to get the opening goal.
(22’) Chances at both ends! This game has finally sparked into life, now! First, Lukaku drives forward into space from the right wing, but his eventual pass - which was aimed for Kone - is a poor one and Delaney intercepts. Palace launch a swift counter-attack, with Zaha jinking his way into the area, but his resulting effort is hit high over the crossbar.
(20’) GREAT SAVE! That’s a fine stop from Hennessey, who reacts instinctively to kick away a close-range volley from Coleman after the Republic of Ireland full-back had latched onto Baines’ looping cross at the back post. Better from Everton!
(19’) Good goalkeeping from Hennessey, as the Palace shot-stopper comes off his line at pace to gather the ball under pressure from Lukaku, who Barry’s raking pass was aimed at. (16’) There is no doubting who has started the better in this match, with Palace dominating both possession and territory. Everton have barely threatened, with Barkley’s half-chance their only notable foray into the opposition’s half so far.
(14’) Solid defending from Baines and Lennon down on Everton’s left flank, as the former Tottenham man gets back to cover for his teammate - who had initially done well to prevent Bolasie making headway into the penalty area - and win a foul off of Puncheon.
(12’) More pressure now from Palace, as Cabaye is fouled by Barry out on the right, presenting the home side with another opportunity to test Everton’s shaky back-line... However, Puncheon's delivery is a poor one, and Robles is able to collect it.
(9’) A free-kick now for Palace on the half-way line, which Cabaye floats into the box, but to no avail on this occasion. Palace have already lumped several looping crosses into Everton’s area so far, and that is no surprise, considering the visitors’ tendency to concede from crosses.
(9’) Almost! Sharp play from the visitors, as they finally manage to lodge a foray forward. Lukaku does well to hold up the play before turning the ball onto Barkley, who twists and turns his way into the area, only to see his eventual shot charged down by Delaney.
(7’) CHANCE! Another sloppy bit of play, this time from Barkley, allows Palace to counter quickly. Zaha drives goalwards before feeding Gayle with a crisp pass, but Stones gets across swiftly to prevent the pacy forward getting a clean shot on goal, and his effort skews wide.
(5’) Dreadful! That’s so sloppy from Kone! The Ivorian did well initially to skip his way out of danger and away from Cabaye, only to then concede possession straight to Bolasie. The winger tries his luck with a low strike from the edge of the area, but Robles gets down well to make the save. That's a lucky escape for the visitors, who have come under some pressure here in the opening five minutes.
(3’) Early appeals from the Palace faithful now, as Gayle goes down in the box under pressure from Funes-Mori. It was never a foul, however, though the hosts will be boosted with how easy they carved through Everton’s defence as, a moment later, Lennon has to recover sharply to prevent Bolasie’s cross finding a teammate.

We’re just moments away from kick-off now, as the teams make their way out onto the field. Unusually, it is not a full house at Selhurst Park, and the Palace fans are, as always, in full voice.

Top-scorer Romelu Lukaku has netted in each of his last three Premier League appearances against the Eagles, and he was the player who rescued a point for the Toffees when they played host to Palace in December, levelling late on after Scott Dann had nodded the visitors ahead at Goodison.

The Toffees’ saving-grace so far has been their away form, with the 1-1 draw with Watford last time out having arrested a worrying run of three-straight Premier League defeats. Saturday’s stalemate at Vicarage Road has been deemed typical of Everton’s campaign, however. Alan Pardew’s side finally managed their first league victory of 2016 with a 1-0 win over Norwich City on Saturday, courtesy of Jason Puncheon’s second-half strike. Prior to that victory, which lifts the south-London side 10 points clear of the relegation zone, Palace had lost all but three of their Premier League fixtures since the turn of the year, with a season that started with so much promise having swiftly turned sour. With five games left to play after tonight’s clash, Pardew will be looking for his team to show the quality they showed in the opening third of the season, and secure at least a mid-table finish. (90’) You could hear a pin drop in the Etihad at the moment as the crowd slowly awaits the final whistle. This result certainly stands City well in their pursuit to maintain their position in the top four, as well as building confidence for their upcoming European duties.
(90’) City are just going throw the motions in these latter stages. Four minutes of added time is the order of the day and the home side don't have too many moments remaining before turning their attentions to toppling the almighty Real Madrid in the Champions League. Such an exciting fixture!

(86’) The Etihad fans rise off their seats in applause as Yaya Toure manages to shake off whatever knock he received to enter back into the action. Even if he is okay, should he not be taken off for the last five minutes just to be sure? City have the game wrapped up, after all.
(84’) Some worrying scenes for City at the moment as Toure is currently in a lot of pain after going down under the late challenge from Cameron.
