All the stats point to United potentially spoiling the Boleyn Ground leaving party here tonight. They have lost none of their last 14 league matches against the Hammers, and in Wayne Rooney they have a player who has scored 11 goals in 15 games in this fixture, while also being the record scorer of opposition goals at Upton Park with seven. The last match between the two outfits took place a month ago in the quarter-final replay of the FA Cup, and on that occasion Van Gaal's charges progressed with a narrow 2-1 win thanks to goals from Marcus Rashford and Marouane Fellaini.
Due to the Manchester United coach arrival late at the stadium kick-off has been DELAYED by 45 minutes.
In the second half of the season, Louis van Gaal has came under increased scrutiny as United boss, with the currently unemployed Jose Mourinho being touted for the managerial role at the Red Devils from some sources. Champions League football is seen as a must for a club the size of United, and if they are to gain entry to the tournament, they would ideally have to come out of tonight's match with a win in order to heap pressure on Man City in the top-four race.
The Hammers have enjoyed a fabulous season under the tutelage of the Croatian boss, but will be disappointed that their own slight ambition of making it into the top four is now gone after that damaging loss at the weekend. They still harbour hopes of gracing their new Olympic Stadium home with European football next campaign, though, so entry into the Europa League remains a real target for their two remaining league matches.
Indeed, sentimentality will need to wait until the full-time whistle, as West Ham would love to derail United's chance of going ahead of Manchester City in the race to claim the last remaining Champions League place. However, Slaven Bilic will be demanding a much better performance from his side than what he witnessed on Saturday afternoon, as the Londoners were embarrassed at home in a 4-1 loss to Swansea.
After 112 years, one of the world's most famous football arenas, the Boleyn Ground at Upton Park, will finally close the doors to its tenants, West Ham, who will be moving to the Olympic Stadium for the start of the next Premier League season. It is sure to be a fairly emotional night for Hammers fans, but there can be no room for complacency on the pitch as they face a Manchester United side full of motivation.

Norwich will miss out on the new lucrative television deal that comes into play next season and the club will have a lot of decisions to make over the summer to prepare for life in the second tier. The truth is that they have simply not been good enough in the second half of the campaign, taking just 14 points from their last 18 games, which has cost them their place in the Premier League. Alex Neil looks still to be the right man to lead the club, and the Canaries can look no further than the example of Burnley on how to bounce back immediately. Disappointment for now, but there could be hope for the future at Carrow Road.
Sunderland's 3-0 victory over Everton tonight means that Norwich are heading back down to the Championship after just one season in the Premier League. They held up their end of the bargain with a strong performance tonight to hammer Watford 4-2. Nathan Redmond was impressive with two assists and a goal, while Dieumerci Mbokani netted a brace with two good finishes. Craig Cathcart helplessly put the ball into his own net in the first half on a night where Watford were not at it all, despite the best efforts of Troy Deeney. He was excellent with a goal and laying on a perfect pass for Odion Ighalo to score, but it wasn't enough for his team.

Watford are playing a significant role in the relegation battle by playing the Canaries and Sunderland in the final week. The Hornets were tipped to struggle at the start of the season, but Quique Sanchez Flores has performed well to keep his side in the Premier League. Questions marks remain over whether the Spaniard will remain at Vicarage Road for next season, and his side will be determined to make a point that he should remain in his post with two victories to cap off a successful term.
Home form is crucial to all sides in the lower half of the Premier League, but Norwich have struggled to make Carrow Road the foundation to build their bid for survival around. They have recorded only five wins at home this term, including one in their last eight fixtures. That will have to change to stave off yet another plummet into the second tier.
Norwich were in a decent position at the turn of the year, indeed they were eight points clear of Sunderland after taking 20 points from their opening 19 games of the season. Had they continued that run of form they would have all but secured their top-flight status. However, in their last 17 matches Neil's men have claimed just 11 points, a worrying statistic for the Scot and Norwich supporters.
Goals have been the main issue for Neil's men in the second half of the season. They have found the net just 14 times in their last 17 matches, including blanks in their last four games. Seven of those strikes came in two games, which has highlighted their inconsistency in front of goal. Cameron Jerome, Steven Naismith, Patrick Bamford and Dieumerci Mbokani have to find a way to supply goals in the final two matches of the campaign to save their side from the Championship.
The task at hand for the Canaries could be a difficult prospect as the club have lost their last four matches on the spin in the Premier League, which has left them four points adrift of safety. The problems emerged in a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month that killed the mometum built courtesy of wins over West Brom and Newcastle. Their defeat to Sunderland looks to be the game that has put them in jeopardy, having sent the Black Cats on a charge for safety. They will have to put all of their problems aside tonight and battle their way to the three points.
It's a simple formula for Alex Neil's men tonight. They have to beat Watford and hope that Sunderland are unable to take all three points from their match against Everton at the Stadium of Light, which would send the battle for survival into the final day of the season.

A huge win for Sunderland in their bid to escape the drop for the fourth season on the spin. They were clinical when they needed to be in the final third, and were resilient at the back with numerous important last-ditch challenges. Sam Allardyce will be elated with his side's performance, although they remain in the bottom three, one point behind Norwich. The Black Cats do have a game in hand over their rivals and with five matches remaining in the campaign, it is anyone's guess who will be condemned to life in the Championship. The Canaries will be devastated by this defeat as a victory would have all-but secured their top-flight status, but now face the prospect of sending the battle into the final weeks of the season. One interested party will have been Newcastle United, who would have probably been down had the Canaries won, but are now back in the fight ahead of their clash against Swansea this afternoon. What an ending to the season we have in prospect.

Marcus Rashford's fourth league goal keeps the Red Devils' top-four hopes alive, while officially bringing an end to the Villans' 28-year run in the Premier League. (71’) STAT: Aston Villa have scored just five goals in their last 12 Premier League games on the road.

(45’) There will be just one minute added on at the end of this first half.

(34’) That goal has done a whole lot to liven up the crowd at Old Trafford, while it will be equally curious to see how Villa respond. In games past they've simply caved in after conceding the first goal, but with the Premier League status on the line, can they produce a different response today?

(19’) STAT: Manchester United have 12 fewer points and 20 less goals than they did at this same stage last season.

(9’) STAT: Aston Villa have won none of their last 12 Barclays Premier League meetings with Manchester United (D3, L9).

Whilst it has been nowhere near as bad as Chelsea’s, City’s Premier League campaign has also been a disappointing one, as several poor results have resulted in them dropping 15 points behind league leaders Leicester, ending their chances of treating Pellegrini to another league title in his final season at the Etihad Stadium. Nonetheless, a wonderful result against Paris Saint-Germain during the week means that they will now feature in the semi-finals of the Champions League for the first time in their history, a huge result for a club that have too often struggled on the European stage. Connected to this have been positive performances in the league, as they seem to have recovered from a poor month-long period of form that started at the beginning of February and are now in with a chance of winning their third consecutive league game for the first time since the middle of September. However, like their opponents today, the Citizens have consistently struggled when playing against sides in the upper echelons of the table. They are yet to play Arsenal for a second time, however, but their inability to pick up points against the big boys is arguably what has hurt them the most this season. As a result, a win here today is imperative if they are to qualify for the Champions League and remain in front of Manchester United, who are fast-approaching and now sit one point behind their rivals thanks to today’s win against Aston Villa.
With just six games left to play, Chelsea’s aim remains to finish a thoroughly disappointing season on as much of a high as possible. Despite performing far better under the watchful eye of Guus Hiddink, the reigning champions still look far from their best and, as a result, head into today’s big clash in 10th place, 13 points behind their opponents and 12 away from a Europa League qualifying spot. The positive impact that their interim manager has made after replacing Jose Mourinho in December was clear to see throughout an impressive three and a half month unbeaten run in the league, but that was finally brought to an end last weekend by Swansea City, who took advantage of a lacklustre performance by the Blues to beat them 1-0 in South Wales. Despite the disappointment of that defeat, today’s hosts nonetheless boast the eighth-best recent form in the Premier League thanks to the 11 points that they have gained from their last six domestic clashes, but they have largely struggled against sides that are positioned near the top of the table. In league meetings against Leicester City, Tottenham Hotspur, Arsenal and Manchester City, they have only managed to win against the Gunners, whilst their last league clash against this afternoon’s opponents ended in a comfortable 3-0 win for Manuel Pellegrini’s men. However, Chelsea did easily see off a young City side in a 5-1 thrashing in the FA Cup two months ago, and they will be looking to perform in a similar manner today as they aim to firmly banish painful early-season memories with a strong end to a frustrating campaign.

(84’) Rose tries to get in on the act for the visitors by launching an ambitious effort, but he scuffs his strike well wide of the target.
--- 82’ Assist Eriksen carves Stoke apart with a run down the left and picks out his team-mate with a lofted pass on to the penalty spot. ---
--- 82’ Goal! GOALLLL!! Alli does score his second goal of the night, atoning for his horror miss earlier in the half. The England man produces an excellent finish on the volley to steer Eriksen's pinpoint cross into the bottom corner. He has had another impressive outing to bolster his ever-growing reputation. ---
(80’) Slight stoppage in play as Arnautovic hits the deck after an altercation with Lamela. The Austrian clutches his face after coming into contact with the Tottenham's man arm. Not sure if there was any intent from the Argentine, but it was unnecessary.
--- 79’ Yellow card Adam goes into the book for taking out Lamela down the right as the Argentine tried to break past him. ---
(77’) Space opens up for Alderweireld 25 yards from goal and he is urged to shoot by the Tottenham fans behind the goal, but he skews his strike well wide of the target.
--- 76’ Substitution Stoke make their second change of the night as Whelan is replaced by Adam. ---
(74’) Spurs have been outstanding throughout the contest, matching their performance from the final 20 minutes against Manchester United. Their passing has been sublime all evening, while they have also been solid as a rock at the back. Their fans are singing "Leicester City we're coming for you", well Claudio Ranieri's side may just be looking ove their shoulders with a little bit of apprehension now.
--- 71’ Assist Lamela shows his selflessness by passing the ball to an unmarked Kane to apply the finish into an open goal. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOAL!! Game over as Kane notches his second goal of the game with a simple tap-in. Spurs hit the home side on the counter and the Stoke defence dissolved into nothing which allowed Lamela to break forward before sliding the ball to his team-mate to apply the finish into the empty net. Magical football from the visitors, and that will make Alli feel a whole lot better about his miss. ---
(69’) WHAT A MISS! Alli should put the game to bed as he breaks in behind the Stoke defence and rounds Given. He has the whole net to hit from the right inside channel, but smashes his effort off the post. He falls to the ground in disbelief, while Pochettino hammers the turf in the technical area in frustration.
--- 67’ Assist Eriksen produces a moment of magic to look off the Stoke defence before guiding an arcing ball over the centre-backs into space to release his team-mate. Super stuff from the Dane. ---
--- 67’ Goal! GOAL!! Spurs take a huge stride towards victory this evening as Alli latches on to pinpoint pass from Eriksen to get in between Shawcross and Wollscheid. The 20-year-old displays total composure by lifting the ball over Given into the net. A sublime goal from the visitors. ---
(66’) Joselu wastes an opportunity from a decent position after latching on to a loose ball on the edge of the area, sending his right-footed strike well over the bar.
(65’) The Austrian's delivery from the set-piece is poor and the visitors are able to clear the danger with relative ease.
(64’) Stoke have the chance to threaten in the final third as Affellay is brought down by Eriksen. Arnautovic stands over the ball waiting to take the free-kick.
(62’) After their burst early in the half, Stoke have offered very little in the final third. They have not been able to get a foot on the ball and attempt to bring Bojan or Arnautovic into the game due to the quality of Tottenham's pressing.
--- 61’ Yellow card Imbula becomes the first man to go into the book this evening for pulling back Dier. ---
(58’) Kane runs at the Stoke defence for the umpteenth time in the match, and puts the ball on his left foot to strike. However, he scuffs his effort well wide of the target.
(56’) CHANCE! Lamela is denied by a fine block by Shawcross at his near post following another flowing attack by Spurs. Kane released the run of Walker down the flank and the right-back sent another low cross into the danger area. Lamela gathered at the back post and hammered a strike towards the net, but Shawcross was one of several red and white shirts to converge on the ball.
(53’) CHANCE! Tottenham break with pace down the right as Walker sends a ball low across the face of goal, which is cleared only as far as Eriksen on the edge of the box. The Dane slides a pass into the feet of Alli, but the midfielder can only send his first-time strike over the bar. Another wasted opportunity from the visitors.
(49’) PENALTY SHOUT!  Kane threads a sublime through ball for the run of Rose behind the Stoke defence. The full-back takes the ball in stride and attempts to round Given, but he loses his footing under pressure from Cameron. All eyes look to Swarbrick, but the referee waves play on.
(48’) CHANCE! Affellay latches on to another poor clearance from the Tottenham defence and drives an effort at goal on the half-volley, but his strike goes just wide of the target.
(47’) Affellay pounces on a loose ball outside the penalty area and fires an effort on the volley, but he can only send his strike well over the bar.
--- 46’ Substitution Shaqiri is forced off with an injury and replaced by Joselu. ---
(46’) We're back underway at the Britannia Stadium.
The players are making their way back out on to the pitch for the second-half.
Tottenham are on course to cut Leicester's lead at the top of the Premier League to five points thanks to Harry Kane's ninth-minute strike. It could have been better for the visitors had Christian Eriksen been able to find the net with his effort late in the half, but he could only smash his shot on to the bar. That could well be a crucial moment in the match as well as the title race should Spurs not go on to win the game. Mauricio Pochettino will be delighted with his side's display so far as they have cut the Stoke defence open at will, but have lacked the clinical edge to add further goals. Should they find their form in the second-half, Spurs should be able to close out the win. The Potters have been poor at the back, showing of a lack of positional discipline. Marko Arnautovic has offered some threat in the final third, but it has not been enough to trouble Hugo Lloris. Mark Hughes will want to see a lot more from his team in the second period.
HALF-TIME: Stoke 0-1 Tottenham
(45’) Referee Swarbrick brings an end to the first half at the Britannia Stadium.
(45’) There will be one minute of added time.
(45’) CHANCE! Alli releases the run of Kane down the right inside channel following clever moment from the frontman. He lines up a strike with his right foot, but he can only scuff his shot wide of the post, much to the delight of the home crowd.
(43’) CHANCE! Alli breaks into the final third this time and tries to turn Wollscheid to strike an effort at goal. However, the German gets enough on the midfielder's left-footed strike to deflect it away from goal. Spurs try to keep the attack alive, but the Potters are resilient enough to hold them at bay.
(42’) OFF THE BAR! Eriksen misses a huge opportunity to double his side's lead as he crashes his one-on-one effort off the bar. A sublime flick from Alli released him through on goal with Given, but he took a poor first touch and could only drive his strike on to the frame. Big let-off for the home side.
(40’) Shaqiri sends a curled ball over the top of the Spurs defence and Arnautovic has the pace on Alderweireld. The winger tries an ambitious strike with his right foot, but he gets very little of the ball and his scuffed effort is cleared out by Lloris. The Austrian would have been better suited waiting for support there.
(36’) Walker wastes a good opportunity to pressure the Stoke goal as Alli sends him down the right flank. The defender has Lamela and Kane to hit in the box, but he can only send his low ball into the waiting arms of Given.
(34’) CHANCE! Dembele comes close to adding a second goal for Spurs, but his left-footed strike from the edge of the box sails narrowly over the bar. The opportunity came from a low cross from Kane, and the Potters failed to effectively clear their lines before Dembele drove on the ball from 20 yards, but failed to his the target.
(31’) Tottenham break down the left and Kane knocks the ball past Whelan, but then gets clatter by the Republic of Ireland international. The referee awards a free-kick, but opts against booking the midfielder. Looked a cynical challenge from Whelan and he may have been a tad fortunate to escape a yellow card.
(29’) The Potters continue to put pressure on the Spurs goal as Shaqiri sends a low ball into the box, which travels through the legs of two players to land at Bojan's feet. However, the Spaniard wastes his opening by blazing his strike over the bar.
(27’) CHANCE! Imbula shows off his strength to hold off Dier and play the ball into Arnautovic. The Austrian uses a clever piece of skill to beat Vertonghen and then strike with power towards goal, but Lloris beats his effort away with ease. Promising signs for Stoke over the past few minutes.
(25’) Dembele loses the ball deep in his own half, and Affellay sends his pass out to the right for Cameron. The full-back lifts a dangerous cross towards the back post, and it forces Vertonghen into action to head behind with Bojan lurking behind him.
(22’) Spurs break with menace down the right as Walker has plenty of space to raid into. The right-back tries to thread his pass into Kane, but the ball is blocked into the path of Alli on the flank. He tries an effort on the volley, but can only send his strike well over the bar.
(20’) Stoke are struggling to click in the final third in the early stages of this match. Imbula tries an ambitious ball over the top of the Spurs backline, but his effort travels behind for a goal-kick as Bojan did not appear to have realised his intent.
(18’) A couple of tricky moments for Wollscheid as Alli closes him down and blocks his attempted clearance, fortunately for the defender the ball bounced kindly to Shawcross. However, seconds later when trying to pick out Muniesa down the flank the German lifts his pass into the stands.
(17’) Alli appears to be okay after the tackle, it might have just been a stinger that he had to run off. You can breathe again Spurs and England fans.
(15’) Worrying moment for Spurs and England fans as Alli comes up a little worse for wear following a challenge from Shawcross. The tackle was fair by the Stoke defender, but he just caught Alli's ankle on the follow through.
(14’) Better from Stoke as Muniesa raids into the final third and sends a low pass into the feet of Arnautovic. The winger turns Alderweireld, but the Belgian blocks his strike at goal out for a corner.
(12’) Kane knocks the ball into the path of Alli on the edge of the box. The midfielder shifts the ball on to his right foot to strike with power, but Cameron gets his body in the way to divert the strike over the bar. Tottenham in complete command at the moment.
--- 9’ Assist A simple lay-off from Dembele does the trick for Spurs as Kane did the rest with a fine finish. ---
--- 9’ Goal! GOAL!!  A fantastic strike from Kane hands Tottenham the lead. The England man collected the ball out wide on the left and he was allowed to cut back inside on his right foot. With space and time Kane curled his effort beyond the reach of Given into the bottom corner.  Super goal from the 22-year-old. ---
(8’) Rose goes down on the left under the challenge of Cameron, giving Lamela another opportunity to send the ball into the box. However, the Argentine's cross goes over the head of Vertonghen and the Potters clear.
(6’) SAVE! Given shows that he hasn't lost his touch as he denies Kane with his legs after the striker had peeled off Shawcross in the box. Lamela picked out his team-mate with an incisive through-ball, but the forward just couldn't take the ball in stride. He was forced to hack his effort towards goal with his left foot, but Given was there to make the block.
(4’) Shawcross sends a long ball over the top of the Spurs defence for the run of Bojan. Alderweireld tracks the run of the forward, and is forced to knock the ball out for a throw on the stretch with the Spaniard lurking.
(3’) The delivery from Lamela does not have the power to trouble the Stoke backline and Muniesa clears the ball to safety.
(3’) Lamela tries to thread a pass into the feet of Alli on the edge of the box, but he gets brought down by Whelan. The Argentine has a chance to whip the ball into the box for the first time this evening.
(1’) We're underway at the Britannia Stadium.
Referee watch: Today's men in the middle is Neil Swarbrick after Kevin Friend stood down from the fixture last week.
The players are making their way out on to the pitch so we should be underway shortly.
Pochettino has spoken with Sky Sports ahead of kick-off, stating that his side need to take advantage of Leicester's slight stumble against West Ham: "The gap is big but it's a great opportunity for us. We must win today if we want to fight for the title."
Spurs are unchanged from their victory over United last week. Harry Kane as per usual leads the attack for the North London outfit, looking to add to his 22 Premier League goals this season. Christian Eriksen, Lamela and Alli will play close in behind the England forward, with the former MK Dons man making runs beyond Kane. Mousa Dembele and Eric Dier will sit in front of the back four, which was boosted by the return of Jan Vertonghen against the Red Devils. He and his compatriot Alderweireld will aim to continue their solid partnership this season, with Kyle Walker and Danny Rose with them in the full-back positions.
Stoke have made four changes to their lineup from their 4-1 defeat to Liverpool. Shay Given comes into the team to replace Jakob Haugaard, making his Premier League debut for the Potters. Geoff Cameron, Marc Muniesa and Marko Arnautovic all come back into the fold as Phil Bardsley, Erik Pieters and Peter Crouch drop out of the side. Bojan Krkic leads the line for Hughes's men, supported by Xherdan Shaqiri, Ibrahim Affellay and Arnautovic, while Glenn Whelan and Giannelli Imbula anchor the midfield. Ryan Shawcross and Philipp Wollscheid operate in the heart of the defence in front of Given.
Tottenham subs: Vorm, Davies, Trippier, Wimmer, Mason, Chadli, Son.
Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Walker, Alderweireld, Vertonghen, Rose; Dier, Dembele; Lamela, Eriksen, Alli; Kane.
Stoke subs: Haugaard, Bardsley, Ireland, Joselu, Adam, Diouf, Crouch.
Stoke City (4-2-3-1): Given; Cameron, Shawcross, Wollscheid, Muniesa; Whelan, Imbula; Shaqiri, Afellay, Arnautovic; Bojan.
The teams have been announced and we'll start with the home side.
Stoke were on the receiving end of a 4-1 drubbing courtesy of Liverpool in their last outing. The Potters have displayed potency in the final third in recent weeks, scoring in their last eight matches, although worryingly for Hughes his team have kept just one clean sheet in their last 11 games. That record will have to improve if the club want to make a late assault on the top six.
Spurs come into the fixture fresh of their 3-0 victory over Manchester United. Pochettino's men struggled to break down the Red Devils in the opening 70 minutes before Dele Alli broke the deadlock, and from that point onwards Tottenham were rampant as Toby Alderweireld and Erik Lamela added further strikes. The Argentine will be hopeful that his side are in a similar vein of form this evening.
Stoke have still got plenty to play for this evening, with the prospect of challenging for a place in Europe still on their agenda. The Potters currently reside in ninth place in the Premier League, but a win today will pull them within six points of Manchester United in sixth. Mark Hughes's men are a stubborn outfit and will make life extremely difficult for Spurs at the Brit, so we could well be in for a dogged contest.
It's a huge evening for Tottenham as Mauricio Pochettino and his men will know that a win will bring them to within five points of Leicester City in the battle for the Premier League title. The Foxes scored an equaliser right at the death to earn a point against West Ham United, but Spurs will be hopeful that further pressure will be enough to help them reel in Claudio Ranieri's side.
Good evening and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Stoke City and Tottenham Hotspur at the Britannia Stadium.

FULL TIME! What a game! West Ham and Arsenal share the spoils in the afternoon's early kick-off, with the hosts battling back from 2-0 down to make a contest of it. Goals from Ozil and Alexis started the ball rolling, before a hat-trick from Carroll made things interesting. A late equaliser from Koscielny tied things up once again, as both outfits take another tiny step towards securing European football next season. That's all we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Antonio picks up a late yellow card for a cynical tackle that halts a Gunners counter-attack. ---
(90’) Reid dives into yet another vital challenge, with Alexis being halted in his tracks as he attempts to lead a pacey break for the visitors. The central defender eventually gives away a foul, but the resulting set-piece delivery is claimed with ease by Adrian.
(90’) There are three minutes of stoppage time.
(88’) Payet is found on the edge of the box, with the Frenchman attempting to use the momentum of the pass into him! He curls his foot around the ball and looks to nestle it inside the top-right corner, but gets his angles all wrong! West Ham could still nick a late winner here.
(86’) Less than five minutes are on the clock here, with the home supporters urging their players towards what would be a vital three points in the chase for European football. Alexis slides a neat pass into Ozil, who attempts to find Giroud in the penalty area, but the ex-Montpellier man is robbed of possession before he can shoot.
(84’) Payet spreads play with a diagonal pass out to Cresswell, but the West Ham left-back takes a terrible touch. Arsenal respond with a break down the right, but Ogbonna scrambles away a near-post clearance. The hosts counter, but the aforementioned Frenchman is outmuscled on the periphery of the box by Gabriel.
(82’) West Ham break at pace down the right-hand side, but a throughball from Lanzini is far to heavy for Carroll to control! End-to-end stuff at the moment, with each failed attack leading to the opposition throwing caution to the wind entirely.
--- 81’ Substitution Walcott replaces Welbeck, with the former Saints wide man having less than 10 minutes to have an impact. ---
(80’) We are into the final 10 minutes in this early kick-off, with this game poised to have a potential grandstand finish. Ozil and Giroud combine inside the penalty area, before a pass is flicked into Alexis. The Chilean forward goes down claiming a foul, but the referee isn't interested at all!
(78’) Payet curls in a corner delivery from the right-hand side, which Carroll meets in the air! The goalscorer finds Reid at the back post with a flick, but the New Zealand international can only scuff a half-volley into the side netting!
(76’) Bilic is gesticulating wildly on the sideline, with the Croatian coach kicking every ball as West Ham press on for a winner. Cresswell lines up a long-range strike from the best part of 25 yards out, but Ospina gets a firm wrist to the ball in order to push a save around the post.
(74’) Payet breaks down the left flank, before cutting back an unselfish pass! Lanzini and Carroll combine, but the latter gets the ball caught under his feet as he looks to return the ball to his Argentine teammate. The home supporters are baying for a fourth Hammers goal!
(72’) Less than 20 minutes remain at the Boleyn Ground, with this contest set to end up at any scoreline. It is end-to-end stuff, with both coaches making changes to really open up the game as a whole. Entertainment can be expected between now and the final whistle.
--- 70’ Assist Welbeck set back a neat pass for his teammate, but the finish from the French central defender wasn't to be sniffed at either. ---
--- 70’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! KOSCIELNY FIRES HOME THE EQUALISER! Arsenal keep the pressure on and slide into the penalty area on the right-hand side. A cross is scrambled across the six-yard box, with the French defender present in an advanced position to steer home a lovely finish! Adrian got a hand to it but couldn't keep it out! ---
--- 68’ Substitution El Nenny is sacrificed for the away side, with Giroud thrown into the fray to lead the line and search for an equaliser. ---
(68’) Ramsey does brilliantly to lift an improvised flick over the head of Ogbonna, before looking to fire a low drive inside the near post! Reid covers across, however, to concede a much-needed corner. Ine set-piece delivery falls to Monreal, who hammers a close-range effort goalwards, but Lanzini makes a vital block on the goalline with Adrian beaten!
(66’) Frustrations are rising somewhat for Arsenal, with the away side not getting the rub of the green in the second half. El Nenny is penalised for a jostling battle with Antonio, with both the Egyptian midfielder and Welbeck unable to hide their disbelief. Giroud is warming up for the Gunners.
(64’) Payet drives at pace down the left-hand side, before gliding infield. The France international stabs a low pass into the path of Emenike on the edge of the penalty area, but Koscielny gets in there first to hack a hurried clearance away from the danger area.
(62’) Antonio wins a corner from Monreal, with Arsenal taking the opportunity to replace Coquelin with the returning Ramsey. The Wales international should offer a little more energy and endeavour between the boxes. The set-piece is eventually taken and then cleared with ease.
--- 61’ Substitution Substitution Francis Coquelin Aaron Ramsey ---
(60’) West Ham keep the ball well, before foraying down the left-hand side, but Lanzini is unable to prevent it from going out of play for a goal-kick. Bilic's men have their lead and can now sit back a little, before the likes of Emenike and Antonio can cause problems at pace down the right-hand side on the break.
(58’) Carroll is picked out at the back post yet again, but this time can only guide a looping effort onto the roof of the net! The former Liverpool man is proving to be a real handful, especially when he drops onto Arsenal's fairly diminutive full-backs.
(56’) West Ham try to break away at pace, but Koscielny does really well to make a vital interception. Should Arsenal concede again, it would be easy to think that this could be game over. Wenger does, however, have plenty of options on his bench this afternoon.
(54’) Noble and Antonio are both warned for a poor pair of tackles on Iwobi, with West Ham really up for this contest now. Their home supporters are making plenty of noise, with momentum firmly with the Hammers. Monreal tries to whip a cross in from the left, but Reid heads clear with ease.
--- 52’ Assist Antonio does brilliantly to beat Monreal all ends up, before placing a lovely cross straight onto his teammate's forehead. ---
--- 52’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! CARROLL GRABS HIS HAT-TRICK! Bilic's men continue their turnaround in this game! Antonio is found in space down the right, before beating Monreal easily and whipping in a back-post cross! The Englishman peeled onto Bellerin, before rising highest to power home a great header! 3-2! ---
(50’) GOAL RULED OUT FOR WEST HAM! Carroll battles with Koscielny, with the ex-Newcastle striker able to hustle the Frenchman and force the loose ball to Payet. The ex-Lille midfielder slams home a close-range finish, but the referee pulls play back for a supposed foul on the Arsenal centre-back. Controversy!
(49’) West Ham claim for a penalty, with Bellerin getting the wrong side of Lanzini. It looked, however, as though the Spanish right-back simply lost his footing. Arsenal respond with an attack of their own, but a looping delivery from the right-hand side is dealt with by Antonio. Bright start to this second half.
(48’) There's a brief break in play, after Gabriel goes down heavily. Carroll, who is already on a yellow card, is accused of catching the former Villarreal defender in the face with a stray arm. The referee deems it accidental, rather than intentional, but the Englishman needs to be careful.
--- 46’ Substitution Tomkins is sacrificed for the home side, which will see Antonio revert to right-back. Emenike will be asked to stretch Arsenal with his pace on the right-hand side of the attack. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! West Ham have fought their way back to 2-2, but Bilic's men will now want to take their momentum into the second period. Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to bed in and weather a brief storm from an inspired and confident set of Hammers.
HALF-TIME! What a half at the Boleyn Ground! Ozil and Alexis put the away side two goals to the good, before the Hammers responded at the death. A quick-fire brace from Carroll has put Bilic's men back on level terms, with the second half poised to be a cracker.
--- 45’ +2 Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! CARROLL NETS ANOTHER! WEST HAM EQUALISE! Arsenal just can't clear their lines and the England international striker makes them pay! A corner is whipped in and half cleared by Ospina, before a second delivery is hung up to the back post. Gabriel can't clear, with his opponent turning home a powerful half-volley as a result! ---
(45’) We're into the first of two minutes of stoppage time.
--- 44’ Assist Cresswell whips a lovely ball in from deep, but Carroll still had a lot to do in order to beat Ospina! ---
--- 44’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! CARROLL MAKES IT 2-1! Hope for the hosts! The ex-Newcastle striker is picked out by a lovely cross from Cresswell, before powering a bullet header beyond a static Ospina! The Englishman got pace and direction on his finish, leaving the Arsenal goalkeeper with no chance! ---
(43’) Payet and Cresswell combine down the left-hand side, with the latter then looping a cross in towards the back post. Carroll rises highest to plant a header back across goal, but Ospina is on hand to claim the tame attempt. Bilic does not look like a happy man at present.
(41’) Arsenal threaten down the left-hand side yet again, with a dangerous cross flashing across the face of goal. Moments later, Welbeck almost manages to win a corner from Adrian, with the Spanish goalkeeper taking way too long on the ball as usual. His defenders won't be feeling too confident with giving their shot-stopper possession.
(39’) Good effort from Carroll! The Englishman is fed possession to feet, before swivelling smartly! A low, left-footed drive is saved well by a sprawling Ospina, with the Colombia international needing to quickly scramble to smother the rebound. That's the closest that West Ham have legally come!
(37’) Welbeck chases a loose ball down, before appearing to pull up ever so slighltly. The England international should be fine to run that off, however, as it was just a minute overstretch. Arsenal are in real control here, with the Hammers struggling to piece together dangerous build-up play with Carroll boisterously leading the line.
--- 35’ Assist Two assists for the young Nigerian, who continues to exude real confidence in his first few Premier League appearances. ---
--- 35’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! ALEXIS MAKES IT TWO! The Chile international has plenty of time and space in the penalty area to guide a neat finish beyond the gloves of Adrian! Iwobi lifts another dangerous throughball forward, which is polished off by the ex-Barcelona forward. ---
(34’) Antonio opens play out to the left-hand side, before a long diagonal pass is controlled well by Payet. The former Lille playmaker swings in an attempted cross, but Koscielny is on hand at the near post to deny his compatriot. The Gunners have defended fairly well thus far, it must be said.
(32’) Only a quarter of an hour remains in the first half in the capital city, with Wenger's men arguably creating the better chances. Antonio is forced to block a cross from Iwobi, with the Gunners earning themselves a corner as a result. As has been the case with a lot of set-piece scenarios in this contest, it is promptly wasted.
(30’) El Nenny sees a tame long-range shot gathered up by Adrian, before West Ham respond with a break. Payet manages to combine with Cresswell to earn his side a corner, but nothing comes of it once again. The Frenchman was able to nutmeg Coquelin beautifully in the build-up play, however.
(28’) Bilic's men are yet to really get out of second gear, with Payet in particularly not managing to create much. The France international has been frustrated by Bellerin, with Arsenal looking very comfortable defensively. A dangerous cross is whipped in from the left, but Monreal confidently controls and then clears.
(26’) The Gunners break forward at pace, with a throughball threatening to carve West Ham apart and set Welbeck in behind enemy lines. Reid comes across brilliantly, however, with the New Zealand international sliding in to make a timely interception. That could have been a big chance to make it 2-0 inside the opening half an hour.
(24’) A long throw is launched in from the right flank for West Ham, but a flicked header from Kouyate can only bobble harmlessly wide of Ospina's back post. Bilic's men are yet to force a save from the former Nice goalkeeper, who has been happily wandering around his penalty area.
(22’) Arsenal are enjoying more dangerous pressure at the moment, with their supporting trio behind Welbeck causing some problems. The latter hasn't had much service, nor created anything, but Iwobi is looking like a threat yet again. No fear is being shown by the young forward.
(20’) Adrian is forced to watch another dangerous pass wide of the target, with Arsenal lifting some inquisitive deliveries into the Hammers' penalty area. West Ham force a corner out of Gabriel moments later, however, but the ball in is cleared easily by the first man. Antonio keeps the pressure on, but Koscielny cuts out an eventual low delivery from the ex-Forest winger.
--- 18’ Assist Iwobi is involved in positive fashion yet again, with the Nigeria international playing a dangerous pass into his teammate. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! OZIL OPENS THE SCORING! The ex-Real Madrid midfielder benefits from a neat throughballl, which allows him to scamper into the penalty box. With Adrian coming out to close the angle, the Germany international holds his nerve and slides a low finish underneath the opposition shot-stopper. ---
(16’) Alexis lifts a diagonal cross into the box from the right flank, but the trajectory of the ball makes it simple for Adrian to claim. The Spanish goalkeeper immediately looks for Carroll, but Gabriel is on hand to beat the former Liverpool striker in the air. Cagey stuff at present at the Boleyn Ground.
(14’) OFFSIDE! West Ham have the ball in the back of the net, but it won't count! A back-post cross is turned goalwards by an acrobatic bicycle kick from Carroll, with Lanzini following the effort in! The Argentine forward nods a close-range header inside Ospina's left-hand upright, but the linesman's flag was already up to deny him.
(13’) West Ham settle into a slow and steady spell of possession, before a long ball forward from Adrian is headed back to Ospina by Gabriel. Arsenal threaten again, with Alexis drifting in from the right-hand side, but the Chile internationals sees a throughball intended for Iwobi cut out easily.

Since that rather fortuitous victory on the south coast, Villa have secured only two other league wins and come into this game having lost their last seven on the bounce, conceding 22 goals and scoring just twice in the process. Caretaker manager Eric Black will again be without the services of Gabriel Agbonlahor who was suspended by the club for disciplinary reasons last week and has now been struck down by a virus. Alan Hutton is ruled out by suspension having seen red in last weekend’s defeat against Chelsea, but fellow-defender Ciaran Clark has recovered from a calf strain and starts. The Irishman is joined in the run-on side by 20-year-old midfielder Jordan Lyden who makes his first ever Premier League start, while Scott Sinclair partners Jordan Ayew up front.
Bournemouth, meanwhile, are currently 11 points above the drop zone and victory in the Midlands this afternoon would go a long way towards securing a second season in the top flight. Manager Eddie Howe has called for an improved performance from his charges in the wake of back-to-back defeats against Tottenham and Manchester City and the Dorset side will also be out for revenge having lost at home to Villa on the opening day of the season.
This could be a dark day for the home faithful as their apparently inevitable relegation will be confirmed if they fail to at least match Norwich’s result at Crystal Palace. Protests against club owner Randy Lerner are expected once again, but the man himself has already confirmed that he will not be in attendance.

A huge win for Crystal Palace this afternoon as they end their winless run in the Premier League thanks to Jason Puncheon's second-half strike. The Eagles are now 10 points clear of the relegation zone with six matches remaining in their campaign, which should all-but seal their place in the top-flight next season. Norwich will be bitterly disappointed to take nothing away from this fixture as the match was even for the majority of the contest. They remain four points clear of Sunderland ahead of their crucial clash against the Black Cats at Carrow Road next week.

However, Dann is unable to win the flick-on and it travels out for a goal-kick.
(13’) The Canaries are beginning to control the game in the middle of the park, much to the frustration of the home supporters inside Selhurst Park.
(11’) CHANCE! Norwich win a free-kick down the left flank and O'Neil sends the ball deep into the box. Hennessey tries to claim the ball under his crossbar, but can only fumble the ball. Klose is the nearest man to the ball and is unaware the keeper has made the error, which allows Palace to hack it away from the six-yard box. Another cross comes in from Jarvis, but again the Eagles clear.
(8’) Dann is okay to continue, and the match resumes with Norwich knocking the ball around in their own half. The injury temporarily knocks the game out of its early flow.
(7’) Norwich come forward again and Jarvis takes the ball down the right flank and then cuts back in on his left foot. Jarvis's strike is powerful, but Dann is brave and gets the block to prevent his shot from finding the target. The Palace defender is down, and looks to be in a bit of trouble as he is evaluated by the medical staff.
(5’) Brady is allowed to raid forward into the final third by the home side, and the Republic of Ireland man takes on the shot and misses the target. The Norwich man was afforded far too much space and time by the Eagles for Pardew's liking there.
(4’) UPDATE: Huge news for both of these teams in their battle against relegation. Shane Long has just put Southampton ahead against Newcastle at St Mary's Stadium. It would be very hard to see the Magpies come back from another defeat and survive this season.
(3’) Klose fails to clear the ball and Bolasie pounces to sprint down the right. The winger attempts to send a low ball across the face of goal, but Bennett is there to make the intervention at the near post. Nervy start from the Canaries.
(2’) Gayle collects a loose ball and feeds the run of Cabaye, who then sends his pass out wide to Souare. The left-back lacks quality with his delveries from the left as his first cross hits Wisdom and his seconds is cleared with ease.
(1’) A strong start to the game for the Eagles as Sako races down the left flank, but Jarvis does well to block his attempted cross into the box. Good intent from Palace in the opening seconds of the contest.
(1’) We're underway at Selhurst Park.
Five minutes to go until kick-off at Selhurst Park and the players have taken the pitch. Not long now before we're underway.
Neil has named an unchanged side from his team that triumped 3-2 over Newcastle last week. The Scot retains the same 4-4-1-1 formation that proved to be successful against the Magpies as Mbokani leads the line with support just in behind from Steven Naismith. Robbie Brady starts on the left wing as Jonny Howson and Gary O'Neil patrol the middle of the park, with Wes Hoolahan forced to settle for a place on the bench. Sebastien Bassong will also be a spectator from the sidelines alongside the midfielder as Klose and Ryan Bennett occupy the centre-back positions, with Andre Wisdom and Olsson in the full-back roles. Along with Hoolahan and Bassong, Neil can call on Nathan Redmond, Patrick Bamford and Cameron Jerome from the bench.
Palace have made two changes from their 2-2 draw against West Ham United last week. Wilfried Zaha and Joe Ledley drop out of the starting lineup and are replaced by Yohan Cabaye and Dwight Gayle. The Frenchman returns from injury and goes straight back into the side, while Gayle leads the line following his goalscoring performance against the Hammers last week. The back four remains the same as Scott Dann and Damien Delaney anchor the middle of the defence, with Joel Ward and Pape Souare operating in the full-back roles. Cabaye and Mile Jedinak are expected to sit in front of the back four, while Yannick Bolasie, Jason Puncheon and Bakary Sako will start behind the lone forward Gayle.
Subs: Rudd, Bassong, Jerome, Bamford, Hoolahan, Mulumbu, Redmond.
Norwich City (4-4-1-1): Ruddy; Wisdom, Bennett, Klose, Olsson; Jarvis, Howson, O'Neil, Brady; Naismith; Mbokani.
Subs: Speroni, Kelly, Ledley, Lee, Zaha, Campbell, Wickham.
Crystal Palace (4-2-3-1): Hennessey; Ward, Dann, Delaney, Souare; Jedinak, Cabaye; Puncheon, Sako, Bolasie; Gayle.
The team news has been announced and we'll start with the home side.
Norwich have been battling relegation since the opening months of the season, despite enjoying a bright opening month following their promotion back to the top-flight. The Canaries looked to be in trouble after going 10 matches without a victory, but their fortunes turned at The Hawthorns as Robbie Brady's second-half strike handed them a crucial three points. Neil's men then faced another huge test at home to Newcastle United last week in a true nerve-jangling fixture. Timm Klose put Norwich ahead only to be pegged back by Aleksandar Mitrovic, but Dieumerci Mbokani restored the Canaries' lead. A tense 10 minutes followed and the Magpies drew level as Mitrovic netted from the spot, but Martin Olsson fired home for the hosts in injury time to hand Norwich the victory, and with it a huge three points. That result could well be the difference come the end of the season. They have won back-to-back matches for the first time since the turn of the year, and Neil will know another win this afternoon may be enough to put the nail in the coffins of Sunderland and Newcastle.
Palace have put themselves in trouble this season after looking like challenging for a place in Europe at the mid-stage of the campaign. Alan Pardew's men have failed to win in the top-flight in their last 14 matches, taking just four points from a possible 42. As a result, the Eagles are 15th in the table and just seven points clear of the relegation zone. Pardew was touted for many of the top jobs by the press following his side's strong start to the campaign, but now finds himself under a lot of pressure to get the points that will secure Palace's place in the Premier League for next season. A win here today at Selhurst Park would go a long way into doing that.
We have a crunch match on our hands this afternoon as both teams find themselves embroiled in the relegation battle at the foot of the Premier League. The Eagles are seven points adrift of 18th-place Sunderland, and will feel that a win today may be enough to secure their top-flight status for next season. Meanwhile, Alex Neil's men are four points clear and will be desperate to cash in on their recent good form to pull further away from danger.
Good afternoon and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League clash between Crystal Palace and Norwich City at Selhurst Park.

FULL TIME! Southampton tie up a comfortable 3-1 win over Newcastle, with the visitors looking to be one of the favourites for the drop. Long, Pelle and Wanyama fired home the goals for the Saints, with Townsend giving brief hope to the Magpies with a wonderful strike late on. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Ward-Prowse lifts a free-kick into the box from deep, but Darlow comes out among traffic to punch clear of Van Dijk's head! Newcastle's travelling support continues to make noise, but they've really been let down by the majority of their personnel here this afternoon.
(90’) There are three minutes of stoppage time.
(88’) Shelvey tries to make things happen with a direct pass upfield, but Van Dijk takes control of the situation and cushions a backpass into Forster. Romeu and Pelle try to combine, but a low cross from the former is headed wide of the post by the latter - with the aid of what he thinks was a deflection.
(86’) Mane hangs a great cross up to the back post from the right byline, but Anita is present to nod a timely defensive clearance behind for a corner. Rodriguez was threatening to score with his first touch, but the Dutchman did his duty diligently. Moments later, Romeu shoots well wide from the edge of the box.
--- 84’ Substitution Tadic takes his leave, with Rodriguez coming into the game in order to make his first appearance in six months for the Saints. The ex-Burnley man gets a great reception. ---
(81’) We're into the final 10 minutes at St. Mary's, with Rodriguez warming up for the hosts. It appears that Southampton are happy to sit back and amble their way through the dying embers of this contest, with Newcastle failing to kick on since Townsend's strike.
(79’) Townsend sends a curling cross towards the back post, with De Jong unable to rise quite high enough to make telling contact! The flick from the Dutchman narrowly evades Mbemba, with Forster breathing a sigh of relief due to his defenders' lack of action.
--- 77’ Substitution Romeu replaces Clasie, with the former Stuttgart midfielder looking to settle the midfield third for the last 10 minutes or so. ---
(76’) Wanyama and Fonte combine to clear another cross from Sissoko, with the Frenchman really offering a strong outlet down this left-hand side. Southampton threaten with an immediate break, but a curling shot from Mane dips just high and wide of the top-left corner!
(74’) Sissoko is picked out on the left-hand side, before attempting to curl in a delivery from out wide. It is clear that Mitrovic is his target, but Forster reads his intentions and comes out to claim with ease. There's a brief stoppage in play, with Martina going down heavily after being accidentally trodden on.
(72’) Shelvey is trying to get on the ball and pull the strings, with Newcastle having more luck in the second half with their reshuffled full-backs. Southampton, however, look fairly solid. Van Dijk in particular has the total measure of Mitrovic, with Koeman's men not looking likely to throw their two-goal lead away.
--- 70’ Substitution Cisse is introduced for the final 20 minutes, with Benitez clearly hoping that Townsend's goal can be more than just a consolation. ---
(67’) Van Dijk and Mitrovic clash aerially, with the former going down holding his face. Neither the referee nor the Newcastle strike is impressed with the reaction of the Dutchman, as there wasn't anything in that at all.
--- 65’ Assist Anita slides a neat pass into his teammate, who promptly does the rest to give the visitors a glimmer of hope. ---
--- 65’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! WHAT A STRIKE FROM TOWNSEND! It is trademark stuff from the winger, who cuts infield dangerously from the right. He unleashes an absolute thunderbolt with his left foot, crashing a great finish into the top-left corner! Forster had no chance! 3-1! ---
(64’) Lascelles gives away yet another corner, as Newcastle's bright start to the second half is now long forgotten. Bertrand whips it in, but Darlow claims comfortably. Sissoko tries to lead a break for the Magpies, but Fonte does brilliantly to rob the France international of possession.
(62’) Tadic tries to lift a cross in from the left-hand side, but the Serbian is caught narrowly offside. Van Dijk continues to stride out of his back four and kick-start attacks, with the Saints clearly not in the mood to sit back and preserve their already healthy lead.
--- 60’ Substitution Long takes his leave after a bright hour, with Ward-Prowse being introduced into the midfield third for the final 30 minutes or so. ---
(58’) Townsend now lines up a shot after cutting infield from the right, with the England international forcing Forster into a smart stop! The goalkeeper turns the attempt around the post for a corner, but nothing comes of the set-piece for the visitors. Finally, Benitez's men are trying their luck, even if it is when they have a three-goal deficit.
(56’) Forster finally makes a save! Ayoze manages to line up a shot from the periphery of the penalty area, but can only place a bobbling effort too close to the goalkeeper. Southampton counter through Pelle, but Mbemba comes over brilliantly to make a last-ditch challenge!
--- 55’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! WANYAMA MAKES IT 3-0! The hosts take a short corner, which results in Mane scampering to the byline. Fonte tries his luck with a close-range shot, which is blocked, before the Kenyan midfielder follows up and rattles a low finish into the bottom corner! ---
(52’) The improvement from the away side has been shown by the Magpies picking up their first corner of the afternoon, but they waste it terribly. The tempo and urgency is better from Benitez's men, with Mitrovic actually getting some service in and around the penalty box.
(50’) Newcastle have seen more of the ball thus far, with Shelvey opening play out to Sissoko on the left-hand side. The ex-Toulouse midfielder drives down the wing, but an attempted cross from the Frenchman is hacked at awfully by Mitrovic.
(48’) Benitez has reshuffled his back four, with Lascelles coming in at centre-back. Anita is at right-back, due to Janmaat picking up an injury, while Sissoko slots in at left-back. The latter drives down the wing and cuts infield, before shooting wide of the near post.
--- 46’ Substitution Lascelles comes into the fray for the restart, with Taylor taking his leave due to injury. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Newcastle have had no fight or intensity thus far, with Benitez presumably having a lot to say in the half-time break. The Magpies have 45 minutes to change their fortunes.
HALF-TIME! Awful first half from Newcastle, who appear to be edging towards relegation and look doomed. Long and Pelle have netted the first two goals, with the visitors' defending being nothing less than abysmal. Benitez needs to inspire quite the comeback if the Magpies are even going to take a share of the spoils.
(45’) We're into the first of two minutes of first-half stoppage time.
(44’) Only a couple of minutes remain until the interval, with Benitez still roaming his technical area desperately. Southampton are in total control, with Van Dijk even coming up from the back to fire hopelessly wide from 30 yards out.
(42’) Southampton appeal for another penalty, with Long going down under pressure from Mbemba, but the referee isn't interested once again. A few minutes remain until the break, with Koeman's men looking for a third to wrap up this win.
--- 40’ Substitution Janmaat took a tumble in the build-up to the second goal of the afternoon, with the Netherlands international appearing to get his studs caught in the turf. De Jong is brought on in his place, with Sissoko reverting to right-back. ---
--- 38’ Assist After netting the opener, the former Hull City striker sets back a neat tee-up to ensure that Pelle can double the hosts' advantage. ---
--- 38’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! PELLE MAKES IT 2-0! Tadic drifts infield from the left-hand side, before slotting a pass into Long. The striker sets a ball back unselfishly to Pelle, who guides a lovely finish into the bottom-right corner with ease. That will ease any nerves that the Saints fans have, with Newcastle defending comically again. ---
(35’) Pelle is picked out by a looping cross, but the Italian striker can only flick a poor header some way wide of the target! The target man hasn't had much good service, but his pass into Long proved vital in the opening goal. Martina is nearly picked out by a diagonal moments later, but Darlow is quick off his line to smother.
(33’) Newcastle manage to win themselves a free-kick, but Shelvey takes it quickly and squanders possession irresponsibly. The away side continue to fritter away the ball and create nothing, with their back four the only players to enjoy having it with any regularity. Southampton are winning the midfield battle with ease.
(31’) Janmaat is the only defender to be heavily involved for the away side, though Mbemba dives into a neat challenge on Long to ensure that the goalscorer doesn't stretch the hosts' defensive line again. Darlow hasn't had many saves to make, but Southampton haven't had to be at their best to dominate this one.
(29’) Attack after attack keeps petering out in the midfield third for the away side, with Southampton having all of the meaningful possession and moves. Sissoko opens play out to the right, before Janmaat eventually delivers a cross from the byline, but Van Dijk heads clear under no pressure.
(27’) Tadic sees a shot blocked! The ex-Groningen man links up brilliantly with Mane, before the latter cuts back a neat pass from the right byline. The Serbia international sets himself, before switching the ball onto his left foot, but Janmaat makes a block just before his opponent could pull the trigger with any conviction.
(25’) Mitrovic has had absolutely no service thus far, with Newcastle having no staying power in the opposition half at all. Their coach is barking out instructions on the sideline, but his expression is that of a frustrated man. The away supporters won't be pleased with what they've seen, with the Saints pressing on for the second goal of the afternoon.
(23’) Southampton continue to create the more dangerous chances, with Townsend struggling to do anything when drifting in from the right. Benitez won't be pleased with how his side have started this game. Wanyama releases Long down the left-hand side, but the Republic of Ireland international chooses to shoot horrendously over the crossbar from range.
(21’) Long is able to win a free-kick in a dangerous position on the left-hand side, with Clasie swinging in a cross-cum-shot! The ex-Feyenoord midfielder's whipped ball curves just inches wide of the back post, with Darlow unable to get anywhere near it if it was on target.
(19’) Janmaat is forced into action yet again, with Van Dijk and Wanyama threatening to get on the end of a swirling free-kick delivery. The Dutchman willingly concedes a corner, with Clasie's resulting delivery unable to find anybody rising high at the back post.
(17’) Janmaat makes a timely block to deny Tadic, as the Serbia international looked to shoot on the turn at the edge of the Magpies' penalty area. The visitors are showing no real signs of life, with Ayoze's early strike the only indication that Newcastle might fight back against relegation with more than a whimper.
(15’) Koeman will be pleased with how the opening quarter of an hour has panned out, as the Saints were able to break the visitors' resilience fairly quickly. Now, the hosts can be more measured in their attacks and sit deep to invite pressure on. The likes of Tadic, Long and Mane can be real threats on the counter.
(13’) Taylor makes a mistake, with Shelvey putting a poor pass back into his teammate's path. The experienced centre-back strokes a mishit backpass to Darlow, who has to rush off his line and then hit Long with a crunching tackle. The former Hull man has really felt the full force of it, too.
(12’) Koeman's men allow for Newcastle to settle into a slow spell of possession, but Benitez's men aren't going anywhere fast. Long and Pelle are ensuring that the ball is fired into non-dangerous areas, before then forcing it to go all the way back to Darlow.
(10’) Townsend drifts in from the right, before an attempted throughball from the ex-Spurs man fails to find Wijnaldum. Newcastle just haven't got going yet at all, with the away side slumping into the same kind of performance that has seen them throw away points recently.
(8’) Mane fires wide! Tadic breaks down the left, before sending a great delivery dipping towards the back post. The Saints winger meets it on the volley, but a deflection takes the ball hurtling behind for a corner. The set-piece is half-cleared, before Pelle goes down in a heap, but the referee doesn't point to the spot.
(6’) Fonte makes a timely block for the home side, with Southampton then immediately breaking away. Pelle is the target of another direct pass, but this time the Italy international's touch lets him down and the opposition goalkeeper collects. Ayoze has been the only man to threaten for the Magpies thus far.
--- 4’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! LONG MAKES IT 1-0! Pelle manages to flick a pass on to the Irishman, who then scampers beyond Taylor with consummate ease! A low finish is slotted into the bottom-left corner, with Darlow left wondering what his defensive line were doing. ---
--- 4’ Assist Assist Graziano Pellè ---
(3’) First chance falls to the Saints! The hosts earn themselves an early corner, which is headed square back cross goal by Van Dijk. Pelle meets the rebound, but the ex-Feyenoord striker can only guide a tame aerial attempt into the gloves of Darlow.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at St. Mary's! Newcastle desperately need a win today, otherwise the visitors could see themselves being cut adrift in the relegation battle. Southampton, meanwhile, will want to add a frustrating run of form.
Substitutes: Woodman, De Jong, Lascelles, Dummett, Tiote, Obertan, Cisse.
Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Darlow; Janmaat, Taylor, Mbemba, Anita; Sissoko, Shelvey; Townsend, Wijnaldum, Perez; Mitrovic.
Substitutes: Stekelenburg, Soares, Romeu, Austin, Yoshida, Ward-Prowse, Rodriguez.
The teams are in at St Mary's, here are the two line-ups, starting with Southampton (4-2-3-1): Forster; Martina, Fonte, Van Dijk, Bertrand; Clasie, Wanyama; Long, Mane, Tadic; Pelle.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Newcastle's long trip down south to face Southampton, as Rafa Benitez's men search for the much-needed points that will guide them away from the drop. As it stands, the Magpies occupy the penultimate place in the Premier League, with Ronald Koeman's men still in seventh despite an indifferent run of recent form.

They've done it! The referee blows his whistle for the final time and confirms that all three points will be going to Swansea thanks to an excellent performance from the South Wales side. Throughout, they caused plenty of problems for Chelsea on the break and looked incredibly solid at the back, where they sat deep and defended resolutely to constantly frustrate the reigning champions. The Blues' front line found very little join against the hosts, with Fernandez and Williams both putting in brilliant displays in the middle of a well-organised and compact back four. The victory all but guarantees the Swans' place in next season's Premier League, as they have now reached the all-important 40-point mark, and in some style.
FULL-TIME: SWANSEA CITY 1-0 CHELSEA
(90’) With little over a minute left to play, it looks as if time has run out for Chelsea. The visitors now look bereft of ideas when pushing forward and are struggling to turn their possession into chances on goal, which has resulted in the intensity of their attacking moves subsiding substantially. As a result, Swansea are now patiently passing the ball around as they aim to run down the clock and pick up three huge points.
(90’) A Chelsea attacking move breaks down, allowing Gomis to break forward on a counter-attack. He decides not to go for the corner and instead flies towards the visitors' penalty area before poking the ball back to Naughton, whose first-time shot from the edge of the box deflects off the foot of Ivanovic and into the hands of Begovic at the near post.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be five minutes of added time.
(88’) Blue shirts are piling into the Swansea half of the pitch, but they just can't seem to find a way through the Swansea defenders. The hosts now have every available body camped deep inside their own half of the pitch, and the visitors are becoming increasingly frustrated as a result. Chelsea are now just a few minutes away from seeing their excellent unbeaten run come to an end...
(86’) Falcao goes close! Traore drops deep and picks up the ball in a pocket of space midway inside the Swansea half of the pitch. He takes a quick touch and spins quickly before teeing up the Colombian striker with a lovely through-ball, but the forward's shot has the sting taken out of it by a vital block by Williams and ends up flying straight into the hands of Fabianski in the middle of the goal.
--- 84’ Substitution The Swansea fans serenade Montero with a standing ovation as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Naughton in an understandably defensive change by Guidolin. ---
(82’) Chelsea are continuing to throw as many bodies forward as possible as they desperately search for a late equaliser. Azpilicueta charges down the right flank before curling a dangerous cross into the middle of the Swansea box, but Fabregas is beaten to the ball by Williams before Routledge ends up clearing the danger fully with a thumping volley from the byline.
(80’) Great defending by Mikel! A lofted pass forward bounces over Ivanovic and into the path of Gomis, who does well to get goalside of the Serbian. He brings the ball down before muscling his way towards the Chelsea penalty area, but just as he's about to penetrate the box he's dispossessed by a vital tackle by the Nigerian, who then calmly clears the danger under pressure.
--- 79’ Yellow card Oscar twists and turns as he tries to make his way down the left wing, but Fer is there to bring the Brazilian crashing to the ground with a poor sliding challenge that results in a yellow card for the Dutchman. ---
--- 77’ Substitution Falcao will feature for the last 13 minutes after replacing Loftus-Cheek. Hiddink has decided that now is the time for his side to throw everything at the hosts. ---
--- 76’ Yellow card Yellow card Ashley Williams ---
--- 76’ Yellow card Yellow card Francesc Fàbregas i Soler ---
(76’) What a chance for Montero! Sigurdsson skips down the right wing on an excellent run before cutting inside and beating Mikel far too easily. After flying past the Nigerian he chips a lovely cross into the middle of the box, where the Ecuadorian winger is completely unmarked, but he's unable to get behind the ball well enough and ends up sending his close-range header looping just over the top of the crossbar. What a great opportunity that was to make it 2-0!
--- 75’ Substitution Gomis comes on to replace Paloschi for the final 15 minutes of the game. Can he find the all-important second goal for Swansea? ---
(73’) It's all Chelsea at the moment as they continue to try and find a way through Swansea's resolute and well-organised back line. The hosts are now sitting deep inside their own half of the pitch as they try to hold on to their one-goal lead, and it's making life incredibly difficult for the visitors, who have increased the tempo over the past few minutes and are pushing plenty of bodies forward.
--- 71’ Yellow card And now Pedro is shown a yellow card for diving after trying to win a free-kick just outside of the Swansea penalty area. There was very little contact between the Spaniard and Cork, and that is obviously why the referee decided to reach into his pocket. ---
--- 70’ Yellow card Pedro charges through the middle of the pitch and looks set to cause problems for the Swansea back line, but before he's able to do so he's brought crashing to the ground by Paloschi, who flies into the back fo the Spaniard and brings him down with a hefty challenge that earns him a yellow card. ---
(69’) Chelsea keep coming back at Swansea, but they just can't seem to break down the hosts' determined back line. Kenedy, who has made a good impact since coming off the substitutes' bench, finds himself in a pocket of space deep down the left flank before firing a cross off the outside of his boot and towards the near post, but there's nobody there to meet it and, as a result, the ball sails comfortably into the hands of Fabianski.
--- 67’ Substitution Ayew receives a rousing applause from the Swansea fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Routledge. ---
(66’) Pedro, who is operating more centrally after starting the game out wide, twists and turns on the edge of the Swansea penalty area before drifting out to the left and firing a cross off Rangel and out for a corner. The resulting set-piece is flung into a dangerous position in the middle of the penalty area, but Fabianski is there to make sure that the ball is pushed out of the box and away from danger.
--- 64’ Substitution Chelsea have decided to make their first change of the afternoon, with Traore coming on to replace Pato. ---
(62’) What a ball by Rahman! The left-back gets himself into a great position deep down the wing before swinging a dangerous cross into the heart of the Swansea penalty area, but Pato is unable to reach it in time and, as a result, can't take advantage of what would have been the perfect opportunity to fire in an equaliser.
(60’) Almost a costly mistake by Ivanovic! The Serbian sends a terrible pass across the edge of his own penalty area, resulting in the ball finding Sigurdsson in a very dangerous position. The Icelandic midfielder quickly fires a shot towards goal, but it bounces off Mikel and out to Ayew. The Ghanaian then tries to test Begovic with a similar strike, but his isn't hit at all well and ends up rolling comfortably wide of the near post.
(58’) A lofted pass from Cork flies over to the right wing, where it finds Paloschi in a good position. The striker brings the ball down well and is initially able to skip past Ivanovic, but the Serbian is able to recover quickly and eventually dispossesses the Italian before poking a pass back to Begovic.
(56’) Great save by Begovic! Montero beats Kenedy with ease on the left wing before curling a wonderful cross into the heart of the penalty area, where Rahman is just about able to cut out the danger before the ball can find Sigurdsson. He clearance bounces straight out to Cork, however, and the midfielder immediately unleashes a rocket of a shot that the Bosnian goalkeeper does well to push away with an excellent diving stop.
(54’) Chance for Paloschi! Once again, Sigurdsson and Montero link up beautifully on the edge of the penalty area before the latter pokes a great pass into the path of the Italian striker. He charges forward and tries to meet the ball but is beaten to it by Begovic, who then reacts angrily after claiming that the former Chievo forward had stuck a foot into his chest in the follow-up.
(52’) Pato scores, but it's ruled out! Fabregas picks up the ball in a pocket of space in the middle of the pitch and immediately fires a wonderful lofted pass over the top of the Swansea back line and into the path of the striker, who brings it down well before poking a shot under Fabianski and into the back of the net, but just as he does the linesman's flag is raised for a handball against the Brazilian, much to his disbelief.
(50’) An attempted Chelsea counter-attack is brought to a premature end by Cork, who sticks a foot in and dispossesses Fabregas before sending the ball over to Sigurdsson. The Icelander plays a lovely one-two with Montero before the Ecuadorian unleashes a curling strike from the edge of the penalty area, but it fails to beat Ivanovic and ends looping into the hands of Begovic.
(48’) Chelsea immediately push forward on a determined attack before Loftus-Cheek fires a low strike off the leg of Williams and out for a corner. The set-piece is dealt with well by the Swansea captain, resulting in a second, but this time the cross is flung straight into the hands of Fabianski in the middle of the penalty area.
--- 46’ Substitution Chelsea have made one substitution during the break, with Miazga, who struggling during the first half, making way for Kenedy. ---
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half.
It's been an excellent opening 45 minutes for Swansea, who have comfortably been the better of the two sides and, as a result, head into the half-time break with a well-deserved one-goal lead. They have looked incredibly dangerous on the counter, with Montero being their most creative player inside the final third. The Ecuadorian has caused plenty of problems for Azpilicueta and, when cutting inside, Miazga, resulting in both picking up yellow cards whilst trying to deal with the winger's pace and skill. At the other end of the pitch, Chelsea have barely tested Fabianski, who has had a comfortable afternoon thus far due to the visitors' struggles in front of goal.
HALF-TIME: SWANSEA CITY 1-0 CHELSEA
(45’) Golden opportunity for Pato! An absolutely excellent lofted pass from Fabregas flies over the top of the Swansea back line before finding Oscar, who is completely unmarked in front of goal. He brings the ball down wonderfully before spinning and poking the ball back to the striker, but, under pressure from two white shirts, he ends up firing his first-time strike several yards wide of the near post. He really should have buried that chance!
