Chelsea have enjoyed a similar renaissance under the watchful eye of Guus Hiddink, who has dramatically improved the team’s performances after replacing Jose Mourinho in December. As a result, the Blues now sit in 10th place in the table, just nine points behind fifth-place Manchester United after embarking on an excellent 15-game unbeaten run in the Premier League. Whilst their chances of qualifying for a European competition are slim, to say the least, poor performances from the sides in front of them could result in the reigning champions being able to make a late push up the table in search of a top-five finish that would be warmly received by Antonio Conte, who the club recently confirmed will be taking over from Hiddink before the start of next season. With seven wins and eight draws from their last 15 domestic games and last weekend’s comfortable 4-0 thrashing of Aston Villa under their belts, Chelsea will be no doubt be feeling confident ahead of this afternoon’s clash, one that proved to be the beginning of the end for Mourinho when the two sides met at Stamford Bridge on the opening day of the season.
When Francesco Guidolin was confirmed as the new Swansea manager in January, his side sat just one point clear of the relegation zone with only one victory from their previous 11 league games. Since then, the Swans have achieved a remarkable turnaround under the experienced Italian, who has guided the South Wales side up the table and into 15th place, where they now lie 10 points clear of the dreaded drop zone and look almost certain to be playing Premier League football once again next season. Under his tutelage, they have lost just three of their last 10 domestic clashes, and they head into this afternoon’s contest with three wins from five games, their best run of form this campaign. Today’s hosts have shown great fight and determination in their bid to avoid dropping down to the Championship, and that was on show last weekend when they came from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 against Stoke City thanks to goals from Alberto Paloschi and Gylfi Sigurdsson, the latter of whom has played an incredibly important role in their change of fortune. The all-important 40-point mark now sits just three points away, and another win today would be enough to see them achieve their target and all but guarantee their place in the top tier of English football for a sixth consecutive season.

(82’) INCHES AWAY! Nasri looks a player renewed! He makes a terrific individual run into attack, breaking into the area before cutting onto his right and curling a shot just beyond the top corner with Foster rooted to his spot.
--- 80’ Substitution West Brom bring on 16-year-old Jonathan Leko, who made his Premier League debut in stoppage time last week at Sunderland. He gets his first real chance to make an impact with the first team here, replacing Sessegnon. ---
(78’) Aguero has played such a great part in this match, and has undoubtedly been City's best player, but it's becoming apparent that he can't play a full 90 minutes. Fatigue is clearly becoming an issue for him, struggling to get on the end of these searching balls forward, allowing the Baggies to consistently win back possession.
(76’) All of a sudden it's becoming a bit uncomfortable for City as they attempt to see this lead through to the final whistle. A victory would take them four-points clear of Manchester United for fourth place, who play at White Hart Lane tomorrow afternoon.
(74’) BERAHINO MISSES A SITTER! It's a mess in every aspect, as Gardner's straightforward cross causes City's defence far too much of a problem, as they allow it to run through for Berahino, but he misses the target with the goal at his mercy! The linesman made a mistake as well as he should have put his flag up for offside! I'm not sure what was worse there, the finish, the defending or the missed offside.
(72’) STAT: Manchester City have won each of their last eight Premier League games against West Brom.
(70’) CLOSE! Good response produced by the Baggies, as Gardner and Berahino link-up on the break. The substitute rolls a return pass through for the striker, but he can't quite sort his footing as he stabs an effort wide of the far post!
(68’) City have a spring in their step now, while finding more space to operate in on the front foot as the visitors are forced to throw more bodies forward in search of an equaliser. That's exactly what the doctor ordered for the hosts.
--- 66’ Goal! A STORYBOOK RETURN FOR NASRI! City have their first lead of the evening and it's no coincidence who was at the heart of it! De Bruyne makes a sensational jaunt into attack, before rolling the ball through for Navas. The Spaniars lays it off for Aguero, whose initial shot it blocked before showing great awareness to set-up Nasri who has a simple finish at the near post. ---
(64’) Manchester City have firmly parked themselves in the attacking half now as West Brom start to drop deeper with the added quality brought into this City side. The hosts have changed their shape a bit as well, with Aguero acting as the lone striker in front of an attacking trio of Navas, De Bruyne and Nasri, with Toure and Fernando just behind them.
(62’) STAT: City have won 50 per cent (1.8 pts/game) of their Premier League matches to feature Kevin De Bruyne since the Belgium international's debut last September and only 27 per cent (1.0 pts/game) without him in the side.
--- 60’ Substitution The second swap brings with it the return of Yaya Toure from injury, replacing Delph. ---
--- 60’ Substitution On comes the cavalry for Manchester City. The first substitution in a double change sees Kevin de Bruyne replace Bony. ---
(58’) NO PENALTY SAYS MIKE JONES! That's extremely careless from Mangala who leaps into the back of Sandro, toppling the midfield over from behind and preventing him from getting on the end of Sessegnon's cross. That's a legitimate shout from the Baggies, but the decision goes against them!
(56’) TERRIFIC STRIKE! It's a chance out of absolutely nothing for the hosts! Aguero cuts into the centre and from about 35-yards out he cannons an effort at goal, forcing Foster to dive across to his right and knock the ball to safety!
(54’) Bony has been a virtual passenger in this match, though the entirety of the blame shouldn't be placed on his shoulders. He's not the type of striker who will consistently create his own chances, and service has been very poor thus far. City need to start playing some balls in to him through the air.
(52’) The width City had going forward was one thing they really had going for them in the first half, but they've come out of the gate far too narrow in their approach. Kolarov has drifted into a central position, in an already clogged midfield, which is making life very easy on the Baggies in defence.
(50’) STAT: West Brom have conceded three times in each of their past five Premier League contests against Manchester City.
(48’) Timid start to the second half from both teams. It's all bit lethargic at the moment as the sides struggle to keep their legs. Motivation could understandably be a bit of an issue for the Baggies, but there's no reason for City to lose their focus as they're in the midst of a tight battle for a top-four finish.
(46’) Here we go again!
Stephane Sessegnon gave West Brom a shock lead after six minutes, but he went on to concede a penalty shortly after, which Sergio Aguero was able to convert to pull City level. That's where we stand after 45 minutes at the end of a very even first half of play at the Etihad, leaving the match perfectly poised for the final 45 minutes.
(45’) HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 1-1 WEST BROM.
(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Approaching the half-time whistle now and it's anyone's guess as to which way this game will go. West Brom have been dominated by City in recent years but that is far from the case today, and they're showing signs of spoiling the hosts' bid for a top-four finish.
(41’) McClean is causing Zabaleta all sorts of problems on the break. The City right-back is being exploited for his lack of pace and that has to be a concern for Pellegrini. The winger sees a cross blocked by the arm of Zabaleta and appeals for a penalty, but he was never going to get that call as the contact was unavoidable.
(39’) The rain continues to come down here and it's clearly having an impact on City's ability to build on the ground in attack. Kolarov has provided the bulk of their creativity on the front foot, and with all due respect to the lively left-back, that's not going to cut it for the hosts.
(37’) STAT: Manchester City have shipped just one goal in their last four Premier League games after conceding a total of eight in their three fixtures before that.
(35’) This has been a much better showing from West Brom in attack, a side who have failed to muster a shot on target in seven Premier League games this season, the most of any club in a single season since 2003/04. They certainly don't appear toothless this evening, but that could perhaps be more of a comment on City's frailties in defence.
--- 33’ Yellow card That's a bad one from the substitute! Gardner has a chance from a free-kick in a similar position to the one he scored against Leicester, but his effort is blocked by a team-mate inside the area. In a frantic pursuit to win the ball back, he gets his studs high up and catches Navas, which will prompt Mike Jones to issue the midfielder a yellow card. ---
(31’) The atmosphere at the Etihad resembles that of a wake as opposed to a football match. It's incredibly subdued, with the cagey nature of the match lulling these fans to sleep. They'll have to be much more vocal when PSG come to town on Tuesday, regardless of the flow of the match.
(29’) Decent effort! The Baggies are packing a greater punch on the counter than they have shown in recent weeks. Berahino produces a lovely flick to tee up Gardner for a strike atop the area, but the substitute drags his effort just beyond the far post!
(27’) The tempo has slowed significantly after a rampant first 20 minutes. City are enjoying the bulk of possession, but the Baggies remain compact in midfield as they keep the hosts to the periphery.
(25’) Kolarov has been a focal point in this match, finding himself heavily involved in the play at both ends in this first half. The left-back gets forward again, this time in a more central position, as he takes a pass from Aguero and tries his luck from distance - but his effort blazes just over the bar.
(23’) STAT: City have conceded first six times this season at home in the Premier League, and only once did they rescue points, in a 6-1 drubbing of Newcastle.
--- 21’ Substitution The Baggies make their first change, which should prompt a reshuffling in attack as Craig Garnder comes on for the injured Rondon. The substitute will move into the number 10 role, with Berahino now leading the line. ---
--- 19’ Goal! AGUERO CONVERTS FROM THE SPOT! Foster guesses right, but there's just too much pace behind the striker's excellently placed penalty as City have restored parity at the Etihad. ---
(18’) PENALTY TO MANCHESTER CITY! Mike Jones is back in the good books of these fans as he does very well to play the advantage and let City's attack continue. Kolarov gets into the area and Sessegnon takes him to ground, with the referee immediately pointing to the spot.
(16’) The atmosphere is surprisingly subdued at the Etihad. The start hasn't been ideal for the Citizens, but they need the backing of these fans to get back into the game, and the supporters should be showing their appreciation following their side's strong showing in Paris.
(14’) Rondon has picked up a knock, something he has been battling for the last five minutes or so, and it doesn't look like he'll play much more of a part in this match. He's labouring on for now, but Craig Gardner is warming up on the touchline as Pulis appears ready to pull the trigger on a change.
(12’) City very much back on the front foot as they win their sixth corner of the match, and third in quick succession. Nasri and Kolarov provide the deliveries, but they're hardly packing the quality that is required, as West Brom don't struggle much in dealing with it.
(10’) City will argue that Mike Jone's interruption in midfield has led to the Baggies opener, but they only have themselves to blame. They still had plenty of bodies back in defence and a number of opportunities to deal with the threat. Kolarov should have got a block on the shot, while Hart had to do better to react to it.
(8’) STAT: West Brom have registered seven 1-0 wins this season - the joint-highest figure in the division alongside leaders Leicester.
--- 6’ Assist Great running and an ever better pick out from McClean who picks up the assist. ---
--- 6’ Goal! WEST BROM LEAD AMIDST CONTROVERSY! Mike Jones gets in the way of Samir Nasri, which brings an end to City's attack and allows the visitors to break. McClean makes strides down the left and picks out an excellent cross for Sessegnon, who brings the ball down admirably before sending an emphatic strike past Hart at the near post from a difficult angle. The keeper was rooted to his spot, but he really shouldn't be beaten from there. ---
(3’) The match is wonderfully stretched in the opening minutes, with City especially lively as they commit their full-backs forward on the overlap. The conditions will make for a nervy evening for the two keepers, who will have to be very sharp in dealing with balls into the box from the wider areas.
(1’) Underway in Manchester!
The players come out of the tunnel to a very wet pitch at the Etihad. The rain has been pouring down steadily today, with it picking up drastically over the last hour or so, though it has slowed a bit over the last 10 minutes. It's still coming down nonetheless, and we'll see what sort of effect it has on the match.
Just two changes for the Baggies following their draw at the Stadium of Light, and they are positive ones from Tony Pulis who is trying to get his side back amongst the goals. Stephane Sessegnon and James McClean are brought in to man the flanks in support of Saido Berahino and Salomon Rondon, with Claudio Yacob and Craig Gardner giving way. Darren Fletcher drops into a deeper role in midfield to make room, partnering ex-Tottenham man Sandro.
Manuel Pellegrini has rotated his squad ahead of their crucial Champions League quarter-final second leg at home to PSG on Tuesday. Bacary Sagna, Gael Clichy, Fernandinho, David Silva and Kevin de Bruyne are all awarded a rest after featuring in their draw in Paris on Wednesday, while Vincent Kompany, Raheem Sterling and Yaya Toure remain injured, though the latter is available as a substitute. Pablo Zabaleta and Aleksandr Kolarov come in as the two wing-backs, while Fabian Delph, who featured as a substitute midweek, is handed a start. Samir Nasri makes his first start in nearly seven months, providing support along with Jesus Navas on the flank for the strike duo of Sergio Aguero and Wilfried Bony.

West Brom have struggled of late to get amongst the goals, and with their Premier League status secured for next season, motivation could start to become a factor. They have found the back of the net just once since a 2-2 draw with Leicester at the King Power on the first of March, and they won’t fancy their chances this afternoon given their recent struggles against this City side.
Hello and welcome to live coverage from the Etihad as Manchester City try hold on to fourth place when they play host to West Brom. Kevin de Bruyne’s return has sparked the Citizens, who looked like their old selves in a 4-0 demolition of Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium a week ago. They followed it up in the Champions League with an impressive 2-2 draw in Paris – De Bruyne amongst the goals – leaving them poised for a potential semi-final berth should they take care of business in the return leg on Tuesday. This is something of an ideal match for Manuel Pellegrini’s side as, with the Baggies struggling to find their form, it shouldn’t take too much focus away from their looming clash with PSG.

Full time at the Stadium of Light. Leicester's march towards the Barclays Premier League championship is showing no signs of halting as they record another narrow win, this time 2-0 away to Sunderland. Claudio Ranier's men were no means at their best, but thanks to a double rom Jamie Vardy, they go 10 points clear of Tottenham in second, who play against Manchester United in an hour or so. Thanks for joining us, see you next time. Can anybody stop the Foxes?
--- 90’ +5 Assist Good contribution off the bench from Gray, who hits a ball into space in behind the defence for Vardy. ---
--- 90’ +5 Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLL FOR LEICESTER! THAT SEALS IT! Even though the game is nearly finished, Vardy refuses to give the Sunderland defenders any time on the ball and eventually wins possession before running through on goal, rounding the keeper, and passing into the empty net! Two-nil! Unbelievable! ---
(90’) MANNONE SAVES SUNDERLAND AGAIN! With the home side striving to get the equaliser, the Foxes charge forward with a meaningful counterattack through Amartey. The substitute goes one-on-one with the Italian, who eventually comes out on top after a great save down to the right! Still 1-0!
(90’) SAVE BY MANNONE! Leicester trick Sunderland into a false sense of security with their patient passing, only to pounce with a pacey counter through Drinkwater. Vardy eventually sees the ball inside the area to direct a low shot at goal, but the Sunderland keeper does well to dive across goal to make the potentially vital block!
(89’) Five minutes of added time is the order of the day at the Stadium of Light, and Leicester are doing fairly well to run down the clock with sustained possession near the corner flag inside the Sunderland half. The amount of time remaining catalyses a big cheer for the home fans, who realise they have been given a small lifeline to try and find the equaliser.
(87’) We are entering the latter stages of the match now and Sunderland are running out of time to try and stage a late comeback. Leicester, meanwhile, need to keep their concentration up to a high degree if they are to successfully go 10 points clear. What a result this would be!
--- 85’ Substitution Claudio Ranieri makes his last change of the match now and it is Marc Albrighton who leaves the pitch with five minutes to go. His replacement will be Daniel Amartey, who will provide slightly more defensive solidity than the former Aston Villa winger. ---
(83’) OH WHAT A MISS FROM JACK RODWELL! The substitute makes his way into the penalty area and luckily receives the ball to feet completely unmarked at the back post. He opens up his body to try and find the top corner with a strike, but ends up firing his attempt a yard over the bar from six yards out! The Sunderland fans, and Sam Allardyce, can't quite believe it!
--- 81’ Substitution Another change from Leicester here, which was actually set to take place just a few moments before the scored. Entering the action is Demarai Gray who is introduced in place of the disappointing Mahrez, who has struggled to showcase his immense talents today. ---
(80’) Fair play to the Stadium of Light faithful, as they are still right behind their team to try and catalyse a comeback. However, their encouragement halts ever-so-slightly as they witness Defoe nearly finding the corner flag with a strike on goal from 25 yards. Not the best from the former Tottenham striker, who isn't doing his old team many favours.
(78’) Kaboul receives a loose ball to feet around 30 yards out and intelligently finds Lens, who in turn teases a cross deep to the back post. Van Aanholt has a great chance to take the touch and get the shot away, but as Huth just gets the flick-on, he isn't ready for it and Leicester are gifted the goal kick.
--- 76’ Substitution Third and final change from the home side here and it sees the disappointing Fabio Borini leave the action to be replaced by Jeremain Lens, who can certainly pull something out of the hat on his day. He has just under 15 minutes to prove himself a Sunderland hero. ---
(74’) Leicester's game management will certainly be important in the last few minutes here as there isn't really any need for them to press ahead for more goals. Their clean-sheet record has been excellent in recent matches, and it will need to continue today if they are to go 10 points clear of Spurs before the London side face Manchester United.
(72’) Well, a situation here arguably sums up Sunderland's plight this season. Borini, who should have at least one already this afternoon, latches on to a cross into the area and looks poised to get the shot away, but only succeeds in hitting the ball off his own face with a half-volley. Comical, and disappointing.
(70’) Mahrez collects the ball to feet on the right channel and typically cuts in on his left foot before attempting to find a yard of space by opening up his bag of tricks in front of the defender. He gains a bit of space and goes for the curler into the bottom corner, but the strike takes a deflection on the way through which allows Mannone to make the comfortable stop.
--- 69’ Substitution It turns out it us a double-substitution for Sunderland as M'Vila also leaves the pitch, with Jack Rodwell being given a run out. ---
--- 68’ Substitution Sam Allardyce quickly reacts to going a goal behind and introduces a centre-forward coming on for a midfielder. Leaving the action is Wahbi Khazri, and his replacement will be Dame N'Doye, who will provide a physical presence up top alongside Defoe, as the Black Cats move to a 4-4-2 formation. ---
--- 66’ Assist Drinkwater displays two aspects of his game for the goal by battling to win the ball in the central area before finding Vardy with an outstanding diagonal pass. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLL FOR LEICESTER! THE FOXES MAKE THE BREAKTHROUGH! Drinkwater wins the ball brilliantly in midfield before popping a perfect pass in behind the Sunderland defence for Vardy, who utilises his electric pace to run forward before curling a lovely finish into the corner! One-nil! ---
(64’) In five out of the past six matches for Leicester, they have ran out winners with a very narrow 1-0 scoreline, and it looks like if they are to claim all three points today it will be through a similar performance and result. They are running out of time to find the opener, though!
--- 62’ Substitution First substitution of the match now and it comes from Claudio Ranieri. Leaving the action is Shinji Okazaki, who had a decent first half only to tail off as time went on, replaced by Leonardo Ulloa, which will likely see the visitors implement a more direct style of play with crosses into the box. ---
(60’) A third of the match to go now and we aren't really any closer to finding the opening goal of the match. It really is a brilliantly even contest so far, but it is meaning that neither side can maintain any kind of ascendancy going forward.
(58’) Yedlin, who is blessed with absolutely tremendous pace, displays it down the right wing with a powerful run before firing a cross into the danger area. Huth, ever the dominant force in the air, manages to clear though with an authoritative header.
(56’) Not a lot of quality on show at the moment as there are far too many long balls being speculatively fired up top. Plenty of desire and bravery out there, as you would expect, but there isn't a lot of creativity to give the fans something to cheer about.
(54’) Vardy breaks in behind the Sunderland defence on the right flank and subsequently chips a teasing pass into the box for the onrushing Drinkwater, who looks poised to pull the trigger whilst through on goal. A combination of the retreating Kaboul and Mannone eventually defuse the situation for the home side though, with the goalkeeper collecting possession on the deck.
(52’) The intensity has just been increased a notch or two in the past couple of minutes, with the passing starting to get a lot more slick. Okazaki exchanges a one-two with Kante down the left touchline to receive the ball back in to space, but the resulting strike on goal is fired high and wide over the bar.
(50’) BORINI! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT?! Defoe breaks away down the left and has a strike on goal, which is blocked. Possession fortuitously drops to the former Roma striker, who drills a lovely half-volley aimed towards the top corner, only for it to just go the wrong side of the post by no more than a yard. Really unlucky!
(48’) A fairly low-tempo start to proceedings after the break, as both sides are really fearing being the ones to concede the opener. There have been a few speculative strikes on goal, but nothing that has tested either goalkeeper to a particularly high degree.
(46’) We are back under way at the Stadium of Light!
Half-time at the Stadium of Light. It has not been a game of the season contender so far in this Premier League clash as we enter the break at a 0-0 stalemate between Sunderland and Leicester. With so much on the line, it is no real surprise that nerves are playing a real part in proceedings, but it isn't exactly ideal for the viewing public. Second half to come, so some goals please!
(45’) Three minutes of added time have been allocated by the referee here, which will likely stem from that injury to Borini as there haven't exactly been a plethora of goals which have lead to stoppages. Schmeichel is on hand to save Leicester from going into the break a goal down as he gets down to stop Borini's deflected strike from the right of the box.
(43’) Kirchhoff, who usually features as a centre-back for the Black Cats, has been deployed in midfield today just in front of the back for and has done a really solid job so far. Mahrez in particular has not been allowed any room whatsoever to cut in on that cultured left foot, while Vardy has also been starved of space in which to operate.
(41’) A small break in play at the moment as Borini is currently down injured after a nasty clash of heads with Fuchs, in what is the latest chapter in the ongoing battle between that duo. The Italian has had his bell rung, but it appears he will be okay to continue after receiving some attention from the physios.
(39’) Khazri, who has been deployed down the left wing this afternoon by Allardyce, finally manages to see a bit more of possession in a more central area. He goes to cleverly click the ball into the path of Defoe to get the shot away, but Morgan sticks out a leg to make the block before catalysing a counterattack with a pass in to midfield.
(37’) The Sunderland fans are demanding a penalty kick here! Van Aanholt gallops down the left channel and eventually skips past a couple of challenges before reversing a cross low to the front post, but no striker from the hosts can get on the end of it due to Huth's interception on the floor. Inconclusive as to whether it struck the German's arm!
(35’) Good effort from Kaboul! Borini picks up the ball a yard or so in from the right touchline and finds a yard of space before swinging a teasing cross to the edge of the area. The former Spurs defender, who had made his way all the way up from the back, bullets a header at goal, but Schmeichel is on hand to see the attempt comfortably over the bar without incident.
(33’) There is some signs of frustration starting to creep in within the ranks of Leicester here, and this is no better summed up by Vardy, who bursts a gut to get on the end of a loose ball down the left wing, only to take a heavy touch to gift Sunderland back possession with a throw-in.
(31’) Mahrez, who has really struggled to get into the game so far, attempts to ignite his performance with a twisting and turning run deep down the right wing. Unfortunately for him, due to his successes this season he is now a targeted man within the Premier League, and finds himself outnumbered on this occasion.
--- 29’ Yellow card There is a fairly entertaining feud developing down the right wing between Borini and Fuchs. The Italian had previously been booked for a poor challenge on his opposition number, but is on the receiving end of a bad tackle on this occasion, which sees the Leicester left-back see yellow. ---
(27’) We are just beyond the midway point of the opening half now, and although it was mentioned at the start of the game that nerves didn't seem to be too noticeable, that theory has been shot down by the way the play has developed. (25’) Penalty shout for Leicester! Okazaki, who has probably been the most dangerous player on the pitch, runs in behind the Sunderland defence to latch on to a lofted pass, only to apparently be nudged on the hip by the right leg of the retreating Yedlin! The referee quickly waves off the appeals from the Foxes, but there definitely looked to be contact there!
(23’) Okazaki has popped up more and more on the right of the pitch in the past few minutes. He picks up possession this time before opening his stride up down the touchline, but only succeeds in earning a corner kick by firing a cross off the leg of Kaboul at the back post.

(19’) Van Aanholt shows some attacking ambition to burst forward down the left wing and hits the byline before reversing a cross into the box, but Huth manages to rise above Defoe to nod the danger away. Sunderland showing a little more in the final third now.
(17’) Vardy chases a seemingly lost cause down the left wing and picks up possession at the corner flag before flashing a cross into the penalty area. Mahrez is lingering on the edge of the box looking to pick up some scraps, but Sunderland clear fairly routinely.
(15’) There hasn't really been too much goalmouth action to speak of here at the Stadium of Light, with the aforementioned midfield battle being the most prominent factor within the game. Leicester's matches have been typically tight in recent matches, though, so not exactly a surprise we remain at 0-0.
(13’) Vardy drives forward deep down the middle and releases Okazaki into the left channel. The Japan international attempts to return the favour with a low pass into the six-yard box, but Kaboul is on hand to make the vital interception at the front post.
(11’) Sunderland are just starting to squeeze their way into contention here and look like they may be able to pose a threat on the counter. Defoe, typically, is playing on the shoulder of the last defender but will need to receive a little more support up top if he is to pose a threat inside the area.
(9’) There is certainly a really interesting midfield battle going on, with the typically combative Cattermole and Drinkwater having already butted heads a couple of times. (7’) The Foxes are just enjoying a little period of sustained possession on the edge of the Sunderland box with short, stabbed passes. (3’) It has been a very high-tempo start to proceedings here in this early Barclays Premier League clash. Sunderland may be down in a precarious position near the bottom of the table, but they are consistently picking up points, albeit through a series of draws. Their 0-0 stalemate against West Brom last weekend was their fourth draw in a row, but a win will be needed at some point if they are to overtake Norwich to leave the bottom three. Leicester's last match was a 1-0 win over Southampton, with Wes Morgan putting in a captain's performance to grab the only goal of the match for the win.
The last time Sunderland and Leicester faced each other in the league was back in August at the King Power in the opening fixture of the season. Ranieri, who was making his managerial debut for the Foxes, oversaw an entertaining 4-2 home win with goals from Marc Albrighton and Jamie Vardy, as well as a double from Riyad Mahrez sealing the maiden victory for the Italian. Who would have predicted at that moment just what kind of journey would be in store for Leicester after that win?
One thing seems like a certainty these days in the Premier League, and that is that Sunderland will be involved in a relegation scrap is some form or another. Gus Poyet and Paulo Di Canio have oversaw unlikely escapes in recent years, and it appears that veteran boss Sam Allardyce will need to pull something similar out of the hat to ensure survival this year. The Black Cats are currently down in 17th position, four points away from Norwich, but do have a game in hand over their relegation rivals after today's round of fixtures.
Leicester, meanwhile, continue their incredible fairytale by riding high at the top of the table with 69 points taken from 32 matches. The team news is in now from Villa Park, with the hosts making just the two changes from the line up that lost to Swansea City last time out. In come Micah Richards and Carlos Sanchez, with Ciaran Clark and Jordan Veretout dropping out, while Gabriel Agbonlahor has been suspended from the squad amidst an on-going investigation about a trip to Dubai where he was pictures smoking from a shisha pipe. Meanwhile, the major news for Chelsea is that both John Terry and Gary Cahill miss out through injury, meaning that the United States youngster Matt Miazga comes in to make his debut alongside Bratislav Ivanovic. The other two changes see Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Pedro replace Oscar and Willian respectively, with Baba Rahman filling the void at left-back with Cesar Azpilicueta having moved to the opposite flank.
Chelsea, on the other hand, have stalled somewhat in recent weeks after Guus Hiddink had overseen their mini-revival following a disastrous first half of the campaign. After crashing out of both the Champions League and FA Cup, they had to rely on a last-gasp Cesc Fabregas penalty to earn them a point against high-flying West Ham at Stamford Bridge last time out. The West London club sit in 10th place, three points behind ninth-placed Liverpool and nine adrift of the Manchester United in sixth, and while Europa League qualification is still a possibility, it seems highly likely that they will not be featuring in either of the European competitions in 2016/17.
Villa, who come into this fixture having lost their last six matches, can still, mathematically at least, beat the drop, though it seems almost certain that they will be playing their football in the Championship next season, and they are currently nine points adrift of 19th-placed Newcastle United, with a high possibility that the club could be relegated as early as next week. Caretaker boss Eric Black will take charge of the first team in the wake of Garde’s departure - at least until a more permanent replacement is appointed, with David Moyes and Nigel Pearson both highly-touted to take the helm.

(78’) Gradel feeds Pugh overlapping down the left-hand side, but the substitute is brought back by the linesman's flag! He strayed just offside due to his overenthusiasm. Even though a share of the spoils isn't on the cards for Bournemouth, you can't fault their continued effort.
(77’) Gradel dips in another free-kick, which is half-cleared by Fernando! Ritchie watches the rebound onto his boot, but can only blast a first-time volley well beyond the near post. The Cherries are trying to get a consolation goal, but Caballero has looked comfortable throughout.
(76’) Chance for Kolarov! The Serbia international is found in space by Aguero, with Boruc getting down neatly to make a save! The aforementioned Argentine picks up the rebound, but is tackled well as he attempts to shoot.
(75’) Nasri tries to cut back a neat pass to Kolarov, but the Frenchman's attempted ball is intercepted with ease. Bournemouth respond with a break, but Mangala outmuscles Grabban once again. Caballero has been a spectator, really, since the restart.
(73’) Gradel sends a looping free-kick delivery into the box from the left flank, but Francis can only leap up to head well wide of the upright! Howe is still roaming his technical area and giving instructions to his players, who have given a slightly better account of themselves in the second half.
(71’) Bournemouth sweep possession out to the right-hand side, with Ritchie looking to make things happen. The ex-Swindon man, however, is sent flying to the turf by Fernandinho. No yellow cards on show from the referee thus far.
(69’) Big chance for O'Kane! A dangerous cross is only half-cleared by Mangala, with the Irishman the quickest to react inside the penalty area! He looks to shoot from close-range, but fires wide under intense pressure from Otamendi.
--- 68’ Substitution Smith limps off, with Tommy Elphick brought into the game after a lengthy injury absence of his own. Francis pushes out to right-back, with Bournemouth's club captain deployed at the heart of the back four. ---
(67’) There are set to be a few changes from both sides, with Smith also appearing to be in some trouble for the home side. Howe doesn't have a ready-made replacement, which could lead to some reshuffling from the Cherries.
--- 66’ Substitution Silva takes his leave after a neat performance, with Nasri coming into the fray following an injury lay-off of around six months. ---
(65’) Pugh marauds his way to the byline, but a cut-back to O'Kane results in the Republic of Ireland man taking a tumble. Man City take their time with some low-tempo football, as Grabban slowly makes his way across to press. Bournemouth certainly aren't looking very bright or pro-active this afternoon.
(63’) Kolarov and Aguero combine, with the latter found in space in the opposition penalty area, but the linesman has his flag raised for offside. With less than half an hour left to play, Bournemouth aren't looking as though they will allow the visitors to rack up an embarrassing scoreline.
(61’) Zabaleta beats Pugh down the right-hand side, before dipping in a great cross from the byline that flashes across the face of goal! Aguero just can't quite get there. Gradel carries possession away on the break, before releasing Grabban, but Mangala covers across to marshal the former Norwich striker brilliantly.
(60’) Francis makes yet another block, following a poor cross from Navas. In the aftermath, Kolarov gives away a cheap free-kick. Bournemouth's fans are starting to find their voice a little more now, but a break-away goal from Man City would be bound to dampen the atmosphere once again.
(59’) Boruc flaps at a free-kick delivery from Silva, but just about manages to take the ball off the head of Fernandinho. The touch from the Polish goalkeeper results in conceding a corner, but Bournemouth are able to clear their lines at the set-piece well. O'Kane tries to lead a break for the hosts, but quickly loses out to Fernando.
--- 57’ Substitution De Bruyne comes off, after a presumably pre-planned hour, with the Belgian midfielder putting on a great performance on his return to first-team action. ---
(56’) Silva sets a pass out to the left, that invites Clichy to overlap, but the France international's cross is blocked well by Francis. Moments later, Aguero drives infield from the left, but the same Bournemouth central defender is on hand to defuse the danger.
(55’) Caballero and Clichy have a mix-up at the back post, after a neat delivery in from the left by Pugh. Gradel tries to press the Frenchman, who looks to control the ball rather than clear it, but the ex-Arsenal left-back holds his nerve and leathers a rushed clearance into touch.
(54’) Francis is the victim of a few handball claims, but the referee waves away the appeals from both Man City's players and fans. Moments later, Silva tries to curl a cross in towards Aguero from deep, but Boruc is able to claim inside his own box without a challenge.
(52’) The home side are getting a feel for possession in the early minutes of the second half, but Grabban is getting no service at all. Man City look comfortable when they're on the defensive, and very dangerous on the break. Navas drives down the right and zips in a low cross, but Francis hooks a near-post clearance to safety well.
(50’) Pugh tries to drive towards the edge of the penalty area, but Otamendi steps out well to outmuscle the substitute and defuse the danger. Bournemouth aren't put off, however, with the same player picked out by a searching long pass down the left, but this time Ritchie's release ball is too heavy to be controlled.
(48’) Aguero can only find the side netting with a low drive, with Boruc's net coming under fire in the early stages of the second half. Moments later, O'Kane is penalised for handball, but avoids a booking.
(47’) Important save from Boruc! De Bruyne shoots across goal with his right foot, forcing the former Celtic goalkeeper to get down smartly to make a good stop! Man City immediately threaten after the restart.
--- 46’ Substitution Pugh comes into the fray in place of King, which will see Ritchie figure in a central area for the second period too. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Bournemouth have a lot to do if they are to find the minimum of three goals required for a point here this afternoon, with Man City's personnel all hoping to get on the scoresheet before the final whistle.
HALF-TIME! Man City steamroll their way into the interval, with the Citizens having a 3-0 lead over Bournemouth. Goals from Fernando, De Bruyne and Aguero have Pellegrini's men in a fantastic position, with the away side looking revitalised after the international break. Howe has a lot to say in the dressing room, you would imagine!
(45’) De Bruyne guides a pass out to the right-hand side, with Navas then picking the same team-mate out on the edge of the box. As the former Chelsea man looks to shoot, Francis slides in to deny him brilliantly. There is one minute of stoppage time.
(43’) Only a few minutes remain in the first period, with Bournemouth needing a goal to try and inspire some confidence from both themselves and their supporters. De Bruyne scampers in behind enemy lines, but the Belgian midfielder is caught narrowly offside in the process.
(41’) Grabban looks to break down the right channel, but Mangala does well to outmuscle the Bournemouth striker. The final ball from the hosts has just not been there this afternoon, with only Smith and Daniels causing any problems at all. Ritchie shoots from the edge of the box, but Clichy makes a timely block.
(39’) Narrowly over five minutes remain in the first half, with Man City still looking for a fourth. Navas lets fly from around 25 yards out, but the ex-Sevilla winger balloons an utterly terrible effort high into the stands behind Boruc's goal. Everyone wants to get in on the act for the Citizens, with confidence coursing through their team.
(37’) Ritchie has the chance to open play out to the right-hand side dangerously, but the Scotland international takes a stray touch and Silva nips in to steal possession. Man City respond with patient play, before Aguero goes on a run that ends with him curling a left-footed effort well beyond the far post.
(35’) Bournemouth are building up a little bit of confidence, with Man City happy to sit back and take a brief breather. Silva and De Bruyne are sat right in, with the Citizens clearly happy to hold onto what they've got for now. Howe's men get themselves a feel of possession, but another dangerous cross, this time from Daniels, is flicked over the bar by Grabban.
(33’) Smith advances down the right-hand side, before being given all of the time in the world to deliver a cross. His diagonal ball picks out Grabban, who had peeled off Otamendi brilliantly, but the ex-Norwich striker could only guide a terrible headed attempt high and wide of the target! Wasteful stuff.
(31’) Half chance for the hosts! A long, hopeful ball from the right is flicked on by Cook, with King then unable to shoot on the half turn. Grabban also tries to flick a shot goalwards, but Fernando concedes a corner. The set-piece is taken short and then swung in, with Surman able to meet it from close range! Caballero gets down smartly to parry a powerful save away!
(29’) Bournemouth string together a lovely move that works the ball from left to right. Smith tries to break beyond Clichy, but Silva tracks the Englishman to ensure that the Cherries continue to be wholly frustrated. Caballero has had nothing to do.
(27’) Bournemouth will need to be careful not to allow this contest to get embarrassing, as Man City continue to push for their fourth first-half goal. Pellegrini's side have been undoubtedly in control for the last 15 minutes, with the hosts struggling to get their foot on the ball.
(25’) Man City win themselves a corner, but this time the set-piece results in nothing. Silva and Navas combine down the right moments later, before play is switched out to the opposite flank. Fernandinho takes aim from the best part of 25 yards, but the ex-Shakhtar midfielder can only crash a dipping attempt onto the crossbar! Close again!
(23’) Bournemouth are leaving Grabban up top on his own, with King dropping in on the right-hand side of midfield. Ritchie is functioning as more of a number 10, with Howe having realised that he may have been a little bold to opt for a 4-4-2. His usual 4-1-4-1 wouldn't have allowed for the space that has permitted Silva and De Bruyne to run the show.
(21’) The Cherries look to be in utter shock, with the hosts conceding a quickfire treble on home soil. The away fans are making all of the noise, as a stuttering Bournemouth outfit try and pull themselves together. Gradel marauds down the left, but then sees a poor cross easily cut out. Howe is trying to pull another player into the midfield battle at present.
--- 19’ Assist Navas manages to dig out a beautifully weighted cross from the right byline, but Aguero has no right to get above two Bournemouth defenders in order to turn it home! ---
--- 19’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! THREE FOR MAN CITY! Aguero grabs another! The visitors threaten down the right-hand side, with Navas then hanging up a neat cross from the byline. The ex-Atletico striker climbs well above Smith, before planting a looping header beyond Boruc and Daniels! ---
(18’) The away outfit are looking rejuvenated by the return of De Bruyne, with the former Wolfsburg man showing real chemistry with Silva in the early stages. King tries to play a quick give-and-go with Surman, but the Norway international is denied by Clichy as he attempts to foray down the left at pace.
(16’) The visitors get their foot on the ball for a while, with the home atmosphere going a little bit flat. Despite Bournemouth initially looking confident, the spring in their step has been quickly quashed by Pellegrini's men. Without Arter in the midfield battle, Man City are finding a lot of room to play in. De Bruyne lashes criminally wide from the edge of the box, after being found in acres of space.
(14’) Man City find themselves 2-0 up, despite not really exerting any real, concrete domination. De Bruyne and Silva have looked bright, but otherwise the away side have been quite quiet. Aguero tries to get in on the act with a long-range effort, but the Argentina international balloons the ball well over the crossbar!
--- 12’ Assist Silva shows lovely vision and technique to cushion back a well-weighted pass to his Belgian teammate. ---
--- 12’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! DE BRUYNE NETS ON HIS RETURN! Daniels gives possession away terribly, with Aguero and Silva then combining in beautiful fashion. The latter sets back a neat pass to his Belgian teammate, who guides a first-time finish into the back of the net! ---
(10’) De Bruyne tries his luck from range, but Boruc is easily able to watch the ball trickle into his clutches. The former Chelsea man is looking sharp, despite his two-month injury lay-off. Man City are looking rather bright when pushing on.
(9’) Despite this contest not previously having any half chances, Man City find themselves ahead. Given that Arsenal have already taken the lead against Watford, courtesy of Alexis Sanchez, with Citizens do need to put their foot on the gas. Gradel threatens down the left for the Cherries, but the Ivorian's dangerous delivery into the box skips off the turf and behind for a goal kick.
--- 7’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! FERNANDO GIVES THE AWAY SIDE THE LEAD! A corner is whipped in from the right by Navas, with a looping delivery finding its way towards the Brazilian following a deflection! Boruc is then caught out by a lovely, cushioned attempt from the ex-Porto man. ---
(6’) Silva glides forward, with the Spaniard finding Navas making tracks down the right. De Bruyne is picked out by the former moments later, with the ex-Wolfsburg midfielder linking up neatly with the Spain international thus far. Man City win themselves a corner for their trouble.
(5’) Clichy finds De Bruyne breaking down the left-hand side, but the latter's eventual cross from the byline is cut out by Francis. Bournemouth scamper forward in response, but a shot from King is dragged terribly wide of the left upright. A bright start on the coast!
(3’) Bournemouth launch a couple of interesting diagonals forward, with Zabaleta doing well at the back post to head a dangerous cross away from his man. Man City respond with a break, as Aguero and De Bruyne combine. The Belgium international tries to shoot from the edge of the box, but Gradel tracks back to intervene.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! Bournemouth will be high on confidence, despite their recent defeat to high flying Spurs, with Man City desperately scrambling to try and stop their league season from entirely capitulating. Champions League football is the aim for the away side.
Man City substitutes: Sagna, Nasri, Kolarov, Bony, Demichelis, Wright, Iheanacho.

TEAM NEWS: Willy Caballero deputises for the absent Joe Hart, with Eliaquim Mangala also featuring due to Vincent Kompany's recent injury woes. Pablo Zabaleta and Gael Clichy are preferred to Bacary Sagna and Aleksandar Kolarov, with fewer surprises further forward. Jesus Navas starts, with Raheem Sterling injured, while Kevin de Bruyne returns to competitive action.
TEAM NEWS: No big changes from the home side, with their back four remained settled and unchanged. Matt Ritchie starts on the right, after scoring for Scotland during the international break, with Max Gradel deployed on the other flank. Eunan O'Kane and Andrew Surman make up the central midfield two, as Howe opts for what appears to be a 4-4-2, meaning that Dan Gosling drops to the bench. Lewis Grabban and Josh King are the strike duo, with Benik Afobe absent this afternoon.
After four games unbeaten, Bournemouth came crashing back down to reality last time out, as they lost out 3-0 to title chasing Tottenham. Manuel Pellegrini, meanwhile, has a lot to do to inspire his charges back into form. Man City have won merely one of their last six top-flight fixtures, with that victory coming against the division's bottom club Aston Villa.
Hello and welcome to one of the Premier League's afternoon kick-offs, as Manchester City travel to face Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium. The visitors are four points off third-placed Arsenal's pace, with both West Ham and Manchester United breathing down the Citizens' necks. Eddie Howe's men, on the other hand, are closing in on the top half of the table, if they can keep their recent form rolling.

The Gunners open April with a commanding victory as they dominate from the start against the Hornets who lose a fourth straight in the league. Arsenal get goals from Sanchez, Iwobi, Bellerin and Walcott as they keep their slim title hopes alive. That's all for our live coverage from the Emirates, thanks for following along! Goodbye.
(90’) FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 4-0 WATFORD.
(90’) There will be three minutes added on at the end of this match.
--- 90’ Assist Campbell picks up the assist, serving the ball up on a platter for his fellow substitute. ---
--- 90’ Goal! WALCOTT MAKES IT FOUR! The pace of Campbell down the flank allows him to get beyond Nyom and pull it back into the centre for Walcott who taps it home. It was a lovely run to the near post from Walcott, and an exceptional early ball from Ozil to pick out Campbell. ---
(88’) HE HAS TO GO FOR GOAL! Amrabat does so well to float a delivery in towards the far post for Anya, who inexplicably opts to head it back into the centre for Deeney instead of trying to go for goal himself! Arsenal have it covered, and Gabriel prevents it from reaching the striker.
(86’) GOOD EFFORT! Guediora, who forced Ospina into a save from a free-kick just a minute ago, tries his luck again from distance and makes terrific contact with his effort, but it drifts just beyond the near post!
--- 84’ Yellow card Elneny picks up the first yellow card of the afternoon by a Gunners player as he drags down Deeney in midfield. The Hornets are showing a bit of life, but it's far too late for that now. ---
(83’) STAT: Arsenal had won the previous six meetings with Watford before a 1-2 defeat last month in the FA Cup quarter final.
(81’) With the result settled, Watford are enjoying more time on the ball than they have for the majority of the match. Still, they aren't nearly inquisitive enough in possession, with the Arsenal back-line remaining focused and organised as they try and hold on to the clean sheet.
--- 79’ Substitution The final change for the Gunners sees Alexis Sanchez, the scorer of their opening goal, give way. He is replaced by Joel Campbell for the remainder of the match. ---
(76’) The tempo has fizzled out drastically. Arsenal are hardly as keen on trying to add to their lead, while Watford are content on running the remaining time off the clock and getting on the next flight back home.
--- 74’ Substitution The Gunners make their second change as Theo Walcott comes on for Iwobi, who walks off to a standing ovation. ---
(73’) STAT: The Gunners have never lost twice at home to Watford in the same season. It is 28 years since they were beaten home and away by the Hornets across all competitions in a single campaign.
(71’) EXCELLENT SAVE! Deeney takes a pass in the area, using his big frame to turn past Gabriel and curl a shot towards the far post. It's well-struck by the forward, but Ospina is equal to the task, flying through the air to knock it behind!
--- 69’ Substitution The Hornets make their final change as Adlene Guedioura comes on for Abdi. ---
--- 69’ Substitution Olivier Giroud comes off the bench for Arsenal in place of Danny Welbeck. ---
(67’) It has been much of the same for the last couple of minutes. Arsenal have set themselves up so well in the Watford end, it's almost as if they're playing with an extra body. Meanwhile, Wenger is preparing a substitution.
(65’) The Gunners are shutting up shop. It looks like they're going to try and keep the ball in midfield and play keep-away for the last 25 minutes, with Watford showing little resistance of their own.
(63’) STAT: Watford have suffered three straight league defeats. They have won just two of their last 13 matches in the division, keeping two clean sheets in that period (W2, D3, L8).
--- 61’ Yellow card Nyom is subsequently booked for his foul on Ozil. ---
(60’) Frustration is starting to set in for Watford. They're having no success whatsoever trying to win the ball back and are struggling to keep the Gunners to the periphery. Nyom essentially kicks out at Ozil in real cynical fashion and he will have to ref to answer to for this one...
(58’) Watford are essentially chasing shadows in midfield. This is an afternoon for them to forget, coming up against an angry and determined Arsenal side. The Gunners continue to dominate possession and are showing no signs of slowing.
(56’) Arsenal show their first signs of complacency as Watson's free-kick isn't defended soundly by the Gunners. Deeney meet it with a header at the far post, sending it back in for Prodl, but his header is cleared off the line by Monreal!
(54’) TWO MORE FOR GOMES! The keeper is having such a busy afternoon! He's thrust into action to deny Ozil a strike from just outside the area, and Arsenal get right back at it following the save, with Sanchez's strike denied by the sprawling Hornets keeper!
(52’) STAT: Arsenal had scored just six goals in their last eight home games (all comps), averaging 25 shots for each goal scored. The Gunners have averaged nine shots faced for each goal conceded.
(50’) SHOULD BE FOUR! This is incredible from the Gunners! Another outstanding attack sees Sanchez pick out Iwobi inside the area. The forward uses the run of the Chilean to open up space for a shot, which he rattles off the underside of the bar, before Monreal knocks the rebound onto the roof of the net!
--- 48’ Goal! GAME OVER AT THE EMIRATES! Arsenal extend their lead to three! Sanchez heavily involved in the build-up again, as his cross is cleared only partially by Nyom, who sends it straight to Bellerin. The right-back sends a first-time effort at goal which deflects beyond a helpless Gomes. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Ighalo has had a difficult task up top, and he's grown frustrated after 45 minutes. Sensing this, Quique Sanchez Flores has opted to bring on Nordin Amrabat in his place for the second half. ---
(46’) Back underway in London!
A convincing first half comes to a close as Arsenal enjoy a two-goal lead into the interval thanks to goals from Alexis Sanchez and Alex Iwobi. The Gunners opened the scoring inside five minutes and never looked back, dominating from start to finish as they are headed for a winning start to April.
(45’) HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 2-0 WATFORD.
(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) This hasn't gone at all according to script for Watford in this first half, but Arsenal have put in an absolutely flawless performance. There's no fault to be found from this first-half showing, as it has been the ideal way for them to kick-off their final push.
--- 41’ Substitution Capoue has been playing down the left largely in this first half and has been in over his head. He's replaced by Ikechi Anya. ---
(40’) STAT: Arsenal has led at half-time in none of its last 10 matches in all competitions at the Emirates Stadium.
--- 38’ Assist It's a lovely pick out from Sanchez, who grabs an assist to go with his goal. ---
--- 38’ Goal! ARSENAL DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! It's another wonderfully worked goal, but it's almost too easy for them in the end as a result of Watford's negligent defending. Coquelin rolls Sanchez through on the right, and the Chilean picks out Iwobi who sends a first-time effort crashing into the back of the net. ---
(35’) Watford have to do a better job of making their limited time in possession count. Arsenal are going to enjoy the bulk of it throughout the match, as they did in their FA Cup defeat, but what the Hornets did so well on that day was make the most of their chances.
(33’) Play comes to a halt as Gabriel goes down in need of attendance, after taking the brunt of an inadvertent kick from Abdi. Play continued momentarily, and Deeney nearly slid Ighalo through into the area, but Bellerin was able to stretch his leg out and get just enough to knock it away.
(31’) CATHCART TO THE RESCUE AGAIN! The centre-half has been outstanding in the first half-hour, and there's no telling what the scoreline could be had it not been for his contributions. He's reading play brilliantly and taking up some excellent positions. His latest intervention denies Sanchez a simple tap-in, breaking up Welbeck's pull-back after a tidy one-two with Iwobi.
(29’) TERRIFIC GOALKEEPING! Ospina comes flying off his line as a ball over the top sends Ighalo through into the area, and the keeper arrives just ahead of the striker to knock it out of harm's way. The flag goes up late anyhow to indicate an offside call, but the replay shows that was the incorrect decision. It would have caused real controversy had Watford scored from that.
(27’) STAT: Watford have recovered just two points from losing positions in the Premier League this season, the fewest in the division.
(25’) The reason Arsenal are looking so dangerous on the front foot is that everyone is pulling their weight. Each member of the front four has been contributing, leaving Watford to guess which route the Gunners will take with each attack. A second goal may be enough to put this game to bed before half-time.
(23’) Smart save! The Guners win a free-kick from 25 yards out, which Sanchez is keen to take. The Chilean lines up a strike and tries to pick out the bottom corner at the near post, getting over the wall and down effectively, but Gomes reads it well in getting across to knock it behind.
(21’) Arsenal are relentless in their approach! They are often criticised for their inconsistencies under Wenger of late, but the good Gunners side seems to have shown up today. They're a joy to watch as they move the ball fluidly through the midfield. Ozil acts as provider on the latest foray, setting up Welbeck, but the striker's flick is blocked by Cathcart.
(19’) Watford manage their first attempt on target, with Watson getting down the right and whipping an inviting delivery into the box. It's a real tough task for Deeney to generate any power behind it, however, as Koscielny applies enough pressure, about 15 yards from goal.
(18’) STAT: Watford scored with their only two shots on target in that 2-1 victory at the Emirates Stadium.
(16’) INCHES WIDE! Another exceptional move down the right, with Sanchez heavily involved yet again, sees Welbeck's run picked out at the near post, but his first-time effort deflect just beyond the woodwork and into the side-netting!
(14’) OUTSTANDING SAVE! Gomes does so well to react to get a hand to Iwobi's impressive effort and knock it over the bar. Arsenal's approach play has been excellent thus far and Watford have been unable to slow them down.
(12’) Close to a second! Coquelin sprays a great ball forward for Sanchez, who skips into the final third before picking out Welbeck inside the area. The striker has a clean sight at goal, but Cathcart is just able to recover and do enough to take the sting out of the shot!
(10’) Watford seem to have weathered the early Arsenal storm, though they've already dug themselves a hole. They enjoy their first real spell in possession in the attacking half, with Watson keen to get on the ball as much as possible, but a fine tackle from Bellerin sends the ball behind off Ake for a goal-kick.
(8’) STAT: Arsenal have lost three competitive home games in a row. They haven’t lost four in a row on home turf since December 1959.
(6’) The noise level in the Emirates is off the charts, and the Sanchez goal is following by a touching tribute for the late David Rocastle. Watford are in over their heads at the moment, looking nothing like the side that won here just a few weeks ago.
--- 4’ Goal! GUNNERS LEAD INSIDE FIVE MINUTES! It's nothing less than they deserve, either, given how they've started. Iwobi is the provider this time, sending a teasing cross in for Sanchez. The Chilean sees his header stopped by Gomes, but is able to convert on the follow-up! ---
(3’) Impressive start from the Gunners who have yet to relenquish possession. They've firmly parked themselves in the Watford half, and a terrific cross in from Sanchez nearly sets up Welbeck for a free header, but Cathcart is able to get enough on his intervention to divert it away from the striker.

Sunderland will be determined to press for the win in the second half, with the news that Norwich hold a 1-0 half-time lead against Newcastle United. Should results remain the same the Canaries would be four points clear of the Black Cats. That could change Allardyce's approach in the second half, with perhaps a more advanced player replacing one of his midfield trio.
An entertaining first 45 minutes comes to an end at the Stadium of Light, although the match remains goalless. Sunderland have had the better of the opportunities, and considering their position in the league they should come out firing. Defoe has had a couple of half chances, while he also failed to make contact with a peach of a cross from Khazri, while Cattermole missed the best opportunity of the half for the Black Cats when he was denied by Foster. West Brom have been typical of their play under Pulis, solid at the back and looking to hit on the counter, although they have failed to test Mannone.

Sunderland's best opening of the game.

Quick note before kick-off. West Brom have given a spot on the bench to 16-year-old forward Jonathan Leko. Will he get a chance this afternoon?
The players are out on the pitch and we should be underway shortly at the Stadium of Light.
West Brom won the meeting between the sides earlier in the campaign thanks to a goal from Berahino. The game last season at the Stadium of Light ended in a goalless draw, although Sunderland did claim a 2-0 win in the 2013-14 season as part of their great escape with Borini and Jack Colback getting on the scoresheet.
West Brom have made two changes from their team that was beaten by Norwich at The Hawthorns. James Chester comes into the back four to replace Jonas Olsson, while Stephane Sessegnon misses out completely against his former club as Sandro replaces him in the middle of the park. Salomon Rondon and Saido Berahino lead the line this afternoon, while Craig Gardner, Darren Fletcher, Claudio Yacob and Sandro occupy the midfield, in what could be a diamond shape. Former Sunderland loanee Jonny Evans starts in the heart of the defence.
Sunderland have made one change to their side that drew 1-1 against Newcastle two weeks ago as Lee Cattermole comes into the lineup to replace Jack Rodwell. The move is surprising considering Allardyce was effusive in his praise of the midfielder during the week, but he has opted for the experience of Cattermole this afternoon who takes the captain's armband from Younes Kaboul. Jermain Defoe leads the line for the Black Cats looking to add to his 12 Premier League goals, while Fabio Borini and Wahbi Khazri operate on the flanks with a midfield trio of Jan Kirchhoff, Yann M'Vila and Cattermole.

Sunderland Subs: Pickford, Jones, Larsson, Rodwell, N'Doye, O'Shea, Toivonen.

The team news has been announced and we'll start with the home side.
The Baggies put in a poor display last time out in a 1-0 defeat to Norwich as Robbie Brady's 50th-minute goal was enough to hand the Canaries the victory at The Hawthorns. However, before the loss Pulis's men had gone on a run of five games without a defeat, including three wins over Everton, Crystal Palace and Manchester United. West Brom will be eyeing a return to form this afternoon.
West Brom are all but safe from the drop as they currently sit in 11th place on 39 points from their 30 matches. Tony Pulis has come in for criticism this season for his side's style of play, but it has at least kept the club in the Premier League. Fans of Aston Villa, Newcastle, Sunderland and Norwich would gladly swap situations with the Baggies at this stage of the campaign.
As a result, Sunderland will enter this match knowing that three points are a must, given their remaining home matches this season are against Leicester, Chelsea, Arsenal and Everton. Their problem has been keeping clean sheets as they have failed to hold a shutout since November a run which stretches 17 games in all competitions. Allardyce will be desperate to put that right today.
The Black Cats would have been frustrated by their draw in the Tyne-Wear derby against Newcastle last time out. Sunderland dominated the match for the opening hour, but they allowed the Magpies back into the contest and Aleksandr Mitrovic's header in the 81st minute earned the home side a vital point. It was the second time in as many matches that Allardyce's side had conceded a late goal, which could be costly come the end of the campaign.
It has been a long two weeks away from the action for both these sides following the international break. Sunderland return to action knowing that a victory is vital this afternoon to aid their battle against relegation. Sam Allardyce's men are 18th in the table, two points adrift of safety, although they do have a game in hand over Norwich City just outside the drop zone.
Hello and welcome to the live commentary of the Premier League match between Sunderland and West Brom at the Stadium of Light.

The referee blows his whistle for the final time and brings an end to a game that both sides will have felt they should have won. West Ham will feel hard done by after having to play with 10 men for the final 25 minutes, which severely disrupted the flow of their play and made life extremely difficult for them, whilst Palace will feel that they should have done better to make the hosts pay for Kouyate's rash challenge. From the 67th minute onwards the Eagles were all over the Hammers, but they could only find the back of the net once and, as a result, remain without a single win in 2016.

Palace sat in fifth place in the Premier League table on New Year’s Day thanks to a wonderful first half of the season, one that resulted in people seriously contemplating the idea that they may qualify for a European competition. However, since then it has been an absolute nightmare for Alan Pardew’s men, who have completely collapsed and, as a result, head to Upton Park with just four points and no wins from their last 13 games. This woeful run means that the Eagles’ dramatic slip down the table has left them dangerously close to the relegation zone, and with Sunderland unbeaten in five of their last six clashes, they could end up dropping into the bottom three if performances don’t soon improve. Their difficulties have come at both ends of the pitch, but it is up front where they have struggled the most. Since their last league victory in the middle of December, the South London side have found the back of the net just nine times, with almost a quarter of those being scored by defender Scott Dann. Connor Wickham showed much-needed sharpness when he scored four times in two games, but they were his first goals of the year and since then he has failed to capitalise on a good, albeit brief, run due to injury.
A five-game unbeaten streak comprising of three wins and two draws means that West Ham’s chances of achieving a top-four finish for the first time in exactly 20 years are alive and kicking heading into today’s London derby. A 2-2 draw away to Chelsea (which could have ended in a win for the Hammers if it wasn’t for a late penalty scored by Cesc Fabregas) before the international break has kept Slaven Bilic’s men in fifth place in the table, just one point behind fourth-place Manchester City, who will surely be feeling the pressure being put firmly on them by the East London side. After suffering a slight dip in form towards the end of last year that saw them go eight games without a win, they are now back to their best once again and have lost just twice in their last 17 Premier League games, a truly remarkable record and one that is second only to league leaders Leicester City. As a result, they will be confident about extending that run even further today as they take on a team that are struggling desperately near the foot of the table.

He has the pace to continue his run, rounding Schmeichel atop the area, but Simpson is around from the back with cover as he manages to get his body in front and make the crucial block! He saved a goal, but Mane has to be scoring there!
(29’) Southampton have a bit of a worry as Pelle goes down, clutching his back, after Simpson came clattering into him from behind. The striker has had his injury troubles in the past, so it's certainly something for Ronald Koeman to keep an eye on.
(27’) Had to be better! Mahrez twists and turns into space on the right before picking out Fuchs atop the area. The left-back opts not to hit it first-time, and winds up being caught in two minds in the end as a through-ball-cum-shot trickles harmlessly beyond the near post.
(25’) It really has been all Leicester in this first half, though Southampton have defended admirably. Fonte and Van Dijk have been especially strong at the back, but the visitors need to find ways to get on the ball for longer periods or the pressure may get to them sooner than later.
(23’) STAT: Southampton have scored an unrivalled 12 headed goals in the Premier League this season. Both their goals against Leicester in the reverse fixture were scored from set-pieces, though only one was a header.
(21’) Southampton get forward and win their first corner of the match as some no-nonsense defending from Morgan sees him head Pelle's cross behind. The ensuing delivery isn't dealt with straight away, allowing both Van Dijk and Fonte (ironically enough the two scorers for Southampton in the reverse fixture this season) to kick out at it, but Leicester do well to get bodies in front of them.
(19’) EXCELLENT BALL! It's a near identical attack from the Foxes, only this time it's Fuchs who springs Vardy down the left. The striker puts in some wonderfull dribbling, but he's too quick for his team-mate in the end as the ball into the middle arrives just a second before Okazaki.
(17’) Nearly through for Okazaki! Fuchs switches play smartly for Simpson, who sends a quick ball over the top for Mahrez. The Algerian finds an encouraging pocket of space on the right, before trying to thread a pass through for Okazaki, but Fonte tracks back to knock it to safety.
(15’) Southampton still have yet to manage an attack. Leicester are full of energy as they push forward with great consistency, forcing Saints to drop deeper than they would like in defence. Mane and Pelle have yet to be involved in the match, with Huth and Morgan having a walk in the park through the first third of this opening half.
(13’) Back-to-back set-pieces for the hosts. The corner is partially cleared, but only out for a throw. Soares lobs a long one into the area that runs all the way through for Morgan. The centre-half tries to control and volley an effort at goal, but again Fonte is on hand to knock it behind for another corner.
(11’) What an important piece of defending that was! Vardy with some determined running to get beyond Bertrand on the right edge of the area, keeping the ball in play at the byline and pulling it back for Okazaki at the near post, but Fonte does just enough to divert the forward's effort behind for a corner!
(9’) STAT: Leicester City have won only one of their last eight top-flight contests against Southampton (D4, L3).
(7’) Forster comes off his line smartly to pluck an Albrighton cross out of the air with Mahrez threatening to run onto it at the far post. The pressure stays on, and Vardy makes for an uncomfortable moment for Forster as he presses high up the pitch, forcing the England keeper to boot the ball out of play - the home support is absolutely loving this.
(5’) Excellent running from Albrighton! Southampton haven't been able to match the intensity level of Leicester in these early minutes, with the hosts clearly up for the occasion. Vardy pounces on an errant throw from the visitors, before laying off for Albrighton, and the winger makes an incredible run into the final third before Targett manages to usher the ball out for a throw.
(3’) Brilliant header! Mahrez wins the hosts the first corner of the match after an encouraging start, but the delivery into the area is poor. Okazaki does so well to contort his body and somehow flick a header into the danger area, but Fuchs' final effort drifts wide of the far post.
(1’) Leicester kick-off and we're underway at the King Power! The Foxes are attacking right to left in this first half.
The atmosphere is exceptional inside the King Power Stadium, and why wouldn't it be. The Foxes can move seven-points clear at the top of the table today, and to make matters even better - if that's at all possible - Leicester Chairman Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha has invited everyone in attendance today to celebrate his birthday with him, giving them all a free beer and a Krispy Kreme doughnut!
Ronald Koeman confirmed in his pre-match interview that he has reverted to a back three, with the likes of Cedric Soares and Matt Targett helping to provide width and control the wide areas where Leicester are so successful. Targett is tasked with containing the electrifying Mahrez, with the extra defender being thrust into the team today at the expense of winger Dusan Tadic. Soares is also back in the team after missing the Liverpool match, replacing Cuco Martina. The other two changes see Victor Wanyama return from suspension, forcing Oriol Romeu to the bench, while Shane Long has been deemed unfit after picking up a knock on international duty with the Republic of Ireland, which sees Sadio Mane get in from the start. He'll likely play in an advanced role, offering support for Graziano Pelle.
As usual, there's hardly a surprise in the Leicester team, with Claudio Ranieri putting out the same starting line-up he's used in 10 of the last 12 Premier League matches. Kasper Schmeichel was the only worry, but the keeper is fit despite suffering a minor injury while away on international duty with Denmark. Jamie Vardy, who scored twice in the reverse fixture at St. Mary's, partners Shinji Okazaki up top, with Riyad Mahrez and Marc Albrighton on the flanks. Danny Drinkwater and N'Golo Kante continue their partnership in midfield, with both players fresh off impressive showings with England and France respectively.
SUBS: Yoshida, Rodriguez, Tadic, Romeu, Ward-Prowse, Stekelenburg, Austin.

SUBS: King, Amartey, Gray, Ulloa, Dyer, Wasilewski, Schwarzer.
