Southampton still have plenty to play for themselves. They are within range of a European place, but have little margin for error given that they have played an extra game than the teams they’re left chasing. Ronald Koeman’s side have looked like world-beaters at times this season, and quite pedestrian at others, encapsulated by their dramatic comeback against Liverpool, erasing a 2-0 deficit to claim all three points in the final game before the international break. The question is, what Southampton team shows up today?
Hello and welcome to live coverage from the King Power Stadium as Leicester City try and take another massive step towards the title when they play host to Southampton. The Foxes received yet another boost yesterday as Tottenham were held at Anfield, meaning Claudio Ranieri’s side can extend their lead at the summit to seven points. Leicester hold their fate in their own hands and they’ve been playing like a team who doesn’t feel the pressure, despite the massive stakes. The attitude at the King Power is exactly where Ranieri wants it to be.

Full-time at Old Trafford. Not a match of the year contender by any means this afternoon, but Manchester United certainly won't mind as they earn the 1-0 win after a solitary strike from Anthony Martial, who once again provides the inspiration for the Red Devils. Champions League qualification is still a real possibility for Louis van Gaal's men, but still plenty of work to be done to overcome Manchester City in fourth place. Everton just want this season do be over and done with by the looks of it, with only the FA Cup providing any kind of excitement between now and May. Thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card Deserved yellow card for Lingard who stops an Everton counter with a foul. ---
(90’) FOUR minutes of added time have been allocated by the referee here which catalyses a chorus of nervous boos from the Old Trafford crowd. The hosts don't have too long to hold on now, but Everton may be buoyed by the fact that have been awarded a little extra time to try and equalise.
(89’) United are just professionally attempting to see out the remainder of the game here with a nice little period of sustained possession inside the Everton half. Indeed, the Toffees look dead on their feet out their now so it will take a monumental effort in the last portion of play if they are to claim a dramatic equaliser.
--- 87’ Substitution Another throw of the dice from Martinez here, who introduces January signing, Baye Niasse, in place of the ineffectual Ross Barkley. The Merseyside outfit are really turning up the heat on United here, but can they find that one elusive chance before the end of the 90 minutes?! ---
(86’) WHAT AN INTERCEPTION FROM VALENCIA! Coleman goes on a signature run down the right-hand side and eventually hits the byline before smashing a teasing cross along the six-yard box. Lukaku looks destined to find the back of the net with the tap-in, but is thwarted by the United substitute, who clears with a stunning slided block a couple of yards out!
(84’) Baines stands over a free kick deep down the right wing and it seems likely he will cross into the danger area. However, the left-back intelligently reverses a pass to the edge of the box where Cleverly smashes an attempt at goal, but the United backline defend superbly by dashing out as a unit to make the vital block before eventually clearing!
--- 82’ Substitution Confirmation of Blind having to leave the pitch here, as he is replaced by Antonio Valencia. Certainly a patched up Manchester United defence out there now, so perhaps Everton can take advantage by piling on the pressure in these latter stages. ---
(80’) Earlier on in the half, Blind went down clutching his hamstring, only to soldier on for another 20 minutes or so. The former Ajax man, who featured for the Netherlands over the international break, seems to have succumbed to the problem now though as he is once again looking to receive treatment from the physio. Unclear whether it is cramp or something a bit more sinister.
(78’) Joel receives a pass back from Jagielka and then sends a long diagonal up top Lukaku, who battles away with Blind trying to come out on top with the ball on the deck. In the end, the Dutchman, with some help from Schneiderlin, gets the better of the Everton striker, who once again vents his frustrations.
(76’) Lingard, who has been extremely quiet this afternoon, attempts to lift the pressure off his team-mates with a galloping run down the left channel before cutting inside. He manages to skip a couple of challenges, but is eventually dispossessed by Cleverley, who vigilantly tracked the run all of 30 yards from inside the home half.
(74’) Just over 15 minutes remaining at Old Trafford and Everton are running out of time to try and force a comeback here. On paper, United probably need the points more than their opponents today, who are down in 12th place with not a lot to play for, so the pressure that comes with that may start to crop up.
(72’) Martial barges his way into the penalty area from the left wing and looks poised to pull the trigger, only to decide against it to lay into the path of Herrera, who subsequently lifts a pass in behind the Everton defence. Rashford collects and attempts to reverse a low ball back inside towards the penalty spot, but Coleman is on hand to make the vital interception.
(70’) As we all know, one thing Manchester United can do pretty well is keep possession, and although this may have been a curse at 0-0, they can rest assured that they have the capabilities to see out the victory by simply keeping the ball. With Everton pressing for the equaliser, they might get a bit more room up top, too.
(68’) Barkley, despite showing a couple of glimpses of quality, really has not been in the game at all in this second period and appears to be suffering from a bit of a lack on confidence. The England international this time collects possession deep down the left wing and goes to find Lukaku inside the six-yard box, but the resulting cross actually goes out for a throw-in on the opposite side of the pitch.
(66’) United still need to guard against complacency this afternoon if they are to move within a point of Manchester City in the race for the top four. They have only conceded seven goals in the league at Old Trafford this season, which will certainly give them encouragement, but Everton still have the tools to hurt the hosts before full-time.
(64’) Everton don't really seem to have any answers for Man Utd's ascendancy here at the moment and appear to have went slightly stale in their attacking play. Their best bet for a goal in the first half was probably Deulofeu, but he has not went off so the impetus is with Lukaku to try and find some inspiration, but he needs better service into the box.
--- 62’ Substitution Roberto Martinez finally decides a change is required out there and withdraws Deulofeu, who had a bright first half but a pretty poor beginning to the second period, leave the action to be replaced by Kevin Mirallas. Let's see if the Belgian can make a positive impact for his side here. ---
--- 61’ Yellow card Chris Smalling picks up a yellow card here, and in pretty needless fashion as he hauls John Stones to the floor. ---
(60’) Much, much better stuff from Man Utd here as they have clearly been advised by Van Gaal to up the tempo of their passing a bit. It took a little while for the tactic to pay-off, but after an abject start to the half they have burst into life after scoring that opening goal.
--- 58’ Substitution Van Gaal responds quite quickly to going a goal ahead here and makes his second change of the match. Coming off his Carrick, who is indeed getting on in years now, and his replacement in the middle of midfield will be Ander Herrera, who enters the action to a cheer of applause from the Old Trafford faithful. ---
(56’) EVERTON HIT THE WOODWORK! The Toffees almost make the perfect response to going a goal behind as Baines whips a superb corner kick into the box for Jagielka, who rises high to bullet a header at goal which cannons off the top of the crossbar! So very unlucky, and the hosts survive.
--- 54’ Assist Immediate impact from Fosu-Mensah, as a marauding run down the right wing eventually sees the youngster tee up Martial to score. ---
--- 54’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLL FOR MANCHESTER UNITED! THE HOSTS BREAK THE DEADLOCK! Fosu-Mensah, who actually appears to have been deployed down the right rather than the left, exchanges a lovely one-two with Rashford before teasing a cross deep to the back post, where Martial is on hand to squeeze a strike past Joel! One-nil! ---
(52’) There is an air of discontent around Old Trafford at the moment as the United faithful once again are seemingly unhappy at the pragmatic approach to the game. Yes, Martial and Rashford can inject some pace up top, but for the most part the hosts have been lackadaisical in possession, which has been a real problem for them all season when playing at home.
(50’) Half-hearted penalty shout from Everton as possession breaks loose to the edge of the box which allows McCarthy to smash a powerful strike at goal. Schneiderlin charges the attempt down, and there are a few musing of a potential hand ball, but the referee is having none of it and quickly waves play on.
(48’) It will be interesting to see if Everton try and get the ball to Deulofeu as quick as they can now as the former Barcelona star is now up against the relatively untested Fosu-Mensah at left-back. If the Spaniard continues his form from the first half, then it could be a long afternoon for the United youngster, but the latter has impressed in his cameos so far this season.
--- 46’ Substitution Change to report at the break for Manchester United and it sees Marcos Rojo leave the action to be replaced by Timothy Fosu-Mensah. Unclear at this point whether the alteration is tactical or due to an injury for the Argentine. ---
(46’) We are back under way in this clash between Man Utd and Everton! Do we have a winner?
Half-time at Old Trafford. Defences have been on top so far in this Barclays Premier League clash between Manchester United and Everton, who go into the break at a 0-0 stalemate. The visitors have arguably been the better side and have had a good portion of possession, but Van Gaal's men still capable of posing a threat, particularly through Martial and Rashford. All to play for in the second period!
(43’) Martial has showed glimpses of his quality this afternoon with his dashes into space, but he has been slightly guilty of coming far too deep to receive possession, too. He can regularly be found near the centre circle trying to see more of the ball, but that area is where Schneiderlin and Carrick should be operating, with the Frenchman causing havoc in more advanced positions.
(41’) There is a bit of a lull in the game at the moment as both sides seem apprehensive about the possibility of conceding the opening goal so close to the break. It has certainly been an even game so if anyone was to score just now, the opposing team would probably have the right to feel aggrieved.
(39’) Just over five minutes remaining in the opening half at Old Trafford, and we aren't really any closer to finding the first goal through either team. Defences have definitely been on top so far, with Blind, Smalling, Jagielka, and Stones in particular impressing.
(37’) What a fantastic challenge that is from John Stones! United penetrate through the middle and leading the charge is Martial, who bursts into the penalty area before looking poised to get the shot away, but before he can, the England international comes in from behind to claw possession away at the last minute! That looked a certain goal, but the hosts are denied!
(35’) Everton have had the majority of the possession so far in the game, but we all know how much Van Gaal loves this aspect of the game, so United are just trying to reclaim a bit more dominance in the central area with short, stabbed passes to one another. Schneiderlin and Carrick typically involved.
(33’) Rojo has been pretty impressive with his attacking play so far and is certainly not lacking in his ambition to hit the byline. He does just that here only to cut back and pass inside to Martial, who skips past a couple of challenges effortlessly before going for a curled strike at goal, but unluckily for him, Everton defend well on the edge of the box to make the block.
(31’) Stones, who has been heavily criticised over the pass few weeks for allegedly taking too many chances at the back when in possession, looks to have a more cautious air about him this afternoon. Even with that, though, he very nearly allows Rashford to steal the ball in a dangerous area with a loose pass into midfield.
(29’) It is now the hosts' turn to heap some pressure on the opposition as Everton just move into slightly deeper positions to deal with United's ascendancy. Rashford and Martial are more often than not the targets of crosses and passes into the box, but Jagielka and Stones have defended relatively solid so far, particularly in their aerial duties.
(27’) Rashford has worked the channels pretty well so far, even with the majority of his runs coming on the left. The United youngster pops up on the right on this occasion though, and opens up his stride with a typically incisive run at the defender, which eventually sees him earn a corner kick off the foot of a Baines. The set-piece is sent into the box, but Martial's blocked header allows Coleman to clear.
(25’) OUTSTANDING goalkeeping from De Gea! Smalling poorly slips at the back which allows Lukaku to gain possession before driving towards goal with authority, but the Man Utd stopper spotted the danger as soon as his team-mate was bested, and quickly dashes out from his line to clear up the park before the Belgian can think about getting the shot away.
(23’) We are just beyond the midway point of the first half now and Roberto Martinez will certainly be more than happy with the display of his outfit so far. The Toffees have had United camped inside their own half for a sustained period now, but they will still need to be wary of the counter as the hosts have the pace of Martial and Rashford in particular in their attack.
(21’) Baines stands over a free kick around 25 yards out and steps up to hit a weak set-piece which cannons off the top of the Man Utd wall before going out for a corner kick. The Engishman is tasked with this dead ball, also, which he floats dangerously to the back post, but a few United players combine to usher possession out for a goal kick.
(19’) Both sides are yet to really find their feet in an attacking sense, as although there is a fairly decent intensity out on the pitch, there hasn't been too much penetration into the final third and into the respective opposition penalty areas. A lot of respect being shown to each other.
(17’) MARTIAL! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT?! The former Monaco attacker, who has been deployed down the left wing this afternoon, pops up in a more central area on this occasion around 35 yards out and unleashes a stinging strike at goal which JUST goes the wrong side of the post! Joel was rooted to the spot, but he breathes a sigh of relief in the end.
(15’) Even with the high-tempo beginning to the match, neither goalkeeper has been tested to any kind of high degree between the sticks, with most of the play featuring down the wings. Plenty of bodies roaming in the middle of the pitch, too, which means the creative players aren't being awarded too much space in which to operate and dictate play.
(13’) Impressive from Everton in the past few minutes, who are approaching the game with little fear. Martinez's men do indeed have an excellent record away from home in the league, and by the looks of things the confidence continues to flow when they are not playing at Goodison Park.
(11’) Barkley collects possession around 30 yards out and thinks about pulling the trigger before opting to pop a lovely diagonal pass out wide to Deulofeu. The former Barcelona winger then successfully takes on Rojo before bursting dangerously into the box, but before he can get the shot away he just takes a heavy touch which allows Man Utd to clear.
(9’) A cracking start to proceedings at Old Trafford, and it is clear from the opening stages that Man Utd fancy their chances down this left wing with Rojo, Martial, and Rashford combining. Everton, meanwhile, are trying to get Lukaku into the game a little more as it has been a relatively comfortable start for Smalling and Blind in the centre of defence.
(7’) Rojo once again powers up the left wing before popping a precise pass down the channel for Rashford, who confidently takes in possession before linking up impressively with Martial. The Frenchman finds a yard of space to whip a teasing cross to the back post, but Cleverley, at the second attempt, shakes off the attentions of Darmian to eventually clear the danger.
(5’) Blind is put under massive pressure down at the corner flag from Lennon, who does well to retrieve possession before playing inside to Lukaku. The Belgian looks to take the ball in to feet before attempting to get a strike away, but just can't quite take the pass in, which allows Smalling to vigilantly come across to make the interception.
(3’) Some worrying scenes for Everton early on here as McCarthy is currently down injured after taking a nasty blow to the ankle from Rojo, who attempts to clear the ball down the left wing for Martial. The Republic of Ireland international looks in quite a bit of pain as he leaves the pitch for treatment, but does so on his feet, which suggests he is okay to continue.

The players make their way to the pitch and we are almost ready for kick-off!
Before the match this afternoon, Old Trafford will unite in tribute to Manchester United and England legend, Bobby Charlton, who sees one of the stands named after him today. The World Cup winner trudges out on to the pitch to soak up the accolades and the atmosphere.

Everton are aiming to get back to winning ways after two poor losses at Goodison Park against West Ham and Arsenal in the league, but can take some heart from the fact that sandwiched between these two defeats came an excellent FA Cup quarter-final victory against Chelsea at home. The Toffees have been much better on their travels this year, having lost only one of their last 14 matches away from home.
Despite being down in sixth at the moment, Man Utd should have relatively high confidence following their previous league match before the international break. At the Etihad Stadium a couple of weeks ago, a solitary strike from teenage sensation, Marcus Rashford, sealed the 1-0 win for the Red Devils as they overcame Manchester City in the derby. However, this result did come on the back of two disappointing results against West Ham and West Brom, so they will be keen to insitigate a run of good form with another win today following the City victory.
The two managers this afternoon can't really be totally assured of their positions next season due to the aforementioned inconsistencies, but it is worth noting that the reasons for the criticisms actually come at opposite ends of the spectrum. The former Bayern Munich boss has been accused of adopting a slightly pragmatic approach to games, with plenty of 0-0 draws peppered within the results of Man United this year. Martinez, conversely, has received accolades for Everton's attacking prowess, but continues to be accused of lacking the defensive tactical know-how to compliment the goals being scored. This is further proved by the records of both teams this season, as United have scored just 38 goals while conceding 27, with the Merseyside outfit netting an impressive 51, only to ship 41.
Considering the lofty stature of both sides featuring today, it would be fair to say that it has been an inconsistent season to say the least for Man Utd and Everton. Under the tutelage of Louis van Gaal, the Red Devils currently find themselves down in sixth place with 50 points taken from 30 matches, which is four points from the coveted last Champions League qualification position. Roberto Martinez, meanwhile, has came under plenty of pressure for the performances of his charges this campaign, as the Toffees are down in 12th place, six points away from even breaking into the top half of the league table.
Good afternoon football fans! Welcome to LIVE coverage of the Barclays Premier League clash between Manchester United and Everton from Old Trafford.

Boos once again ring down on the Everton players as the referee blows his whistle for the final time, and it's no wonder why. Whilst they looked slightly better after Arsenal sat back in the second half, it was still a very disappointing performance by the Toffees, who looked far too open at the back and lacked the movement and intensity needed to find their way through a determined back line. The Gunners, on the other hand, did exactly what was required as they constantly found plenty of joy in the final third of the pitch thanks to the pace and skill at their disposal.
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-2 ARSENAL
(90’) Deuolofeu twists and turns down the right flank before curling a cross towards Lukaku, but it's sent too near to Ospina and the goalkeeper is easily able to beat the Belgian to the ball before cutting out the danger with a strong take at the near post.
(90’) What an opportunity for Giroud! Chambers out-muscles Jagielka in the middle of the pitch and charges towards the edge of the penalty area before teeing up the French striker. He takes a quick touch before blasting a fierce strike towards goal, but it's slightly mishit and flies into the side-netting.
(90’) Everton keep desperately push forward as they try to find a way back into the game, but nothing they are trying seems to be working. Ball after ball is flung into the Arsenal penalty area, but each one is well dealt with by the visitors' defence before Ospina is eventually able to grab hold of it on the edge of the six-yard box.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be five minutes of added time.
(88’) Chance for Lukaku! The big Belgian has been kept quiet by the Arsenal back line today, but he's finally able to test Ospina with a close-range header. He does well to out-muscle Koscielny before reaching a cross from Funes Mori, but his downward effort fails to trouble the Arsenal goalkeeper, who is easily able to stop it from finding the back of the net.
--- 86’ Substitution That will be Iwobi's last contribution to the game, as he makes way for Chambers for the final few minutes. ---
(85’) A half-hearted Everton attacking move breaks down, and Arsenal immediately fly forward on a blisteringly quick counter-attack. Iwobi does well to sprint towards the hosts' penalty area before trying to tee up Sanchez on the right-hand side of the box, but the youngster's pass is completely misplaced and misses the Chilean before rolling out for a throw-in on the right flank.
(83’) Giroud scores, but it's ruled out! Arsenal win themselves a corner on the left wing, and from it Sanchez curls a lovely cross into the heart of the penalty. It finds the French striker, who beats Joel to the ball before nodding it into the back of the net, but just as it does the referee's whistle is blown and Everton are awarded a free-kick for a push on Jagielka in the build-up.
(81’) Giroud rises high and does well to nod the ball into the path of Sanchez, who picks it up on the right-hand side of the penalty area before trying to cut the ball back to the Frenchman. However, just as he's about to reach the ball he's cynically tripped over by Funes Mori, but the referee doesn't spot the off-the-ball incident and allows play to go on, much to the frustration of the Arsenal striker.
(79’) The game has become slightly erratic over the past few minutes, and the two sides are finding it difficult to achieve any sort of rhythm with their passing. Coleman is constantly trying to charge down the right wing but is quickly finding himself closed down by Gibbs and Monreal, both of whom are doing well to contain him.
(77’) Giroud is quickly involved in the game after Iwobi does well to pick him out on the edge of the Everton penalty area, but the Frenchman is far too slow on the ball and he's swifly dispossessed by Jagielka before he can get a shot away.
--- 75’ Substitution Meanwhile, Giroud has come to take the place of Welbeck for the final quarter of an hour. ---
--- 74’ Substitution Ozil seems to have picked up a slight injury after having his ankle accidentally trodden on by Stones, and he hobbles off to be replaced by Gibbs. ---
--- 73’ Substitution Barkley makes his way off the pitch for Deulofeu in Everton's second change of the game. ---
(72’) Everton quickly come back again as they desperately push plenty of bodies deep into the Arsenal half of the pitch. Lennon, who has arguably been one of their best players this afternoon, twists and turns on the left wing before curling a cross towards Lukaku, but it's slightly overhit and flies a few yards over the head of the Belgian striker.
(71’) Thumping strike by Cleverley! A lovely cross-field pass from Barkley finds Lennon on the right-hand side of the penalty area, and the winger controls it well before cutting the ball back to the former Manchester United midfielder. He immediately unleashes a rocket of a shot towards the bottom left-hand corner of the net, but Gabriel is there to stop it from troubling Ospina.
(69’) What a chance for Jagielka! Everton win themselves a corner on the right wing, which is quickly curled into the middle of the penalty area. It finds the centre-back, who beats the hobbling figure of Ospina to the ball before sending his bullet header agonisingly wide of the near post.
(68’) After receiving medical attention for a few moments, Ospina eventually gets back to his feet and seems able to continue for the time being. However, he doesn't seem to be moving at all comfortably and may have to make way if he doesn't make a fully recovery soon.

In a similar way to Roberto Martinez, Arsene Wenger starts the weekend under pressure and well aware that his star-studded Gunners haven’t reached their potential this season. With Chelsea out of the race and Manchester City stuttering, the Premier League title was there for the taking, but a series of disappointing results has left Arsenal 11 points behind league leaders Leicester City and with little chance of clinching the crown. Add to that the disappointment of being knocked out of two competitions - the FA Cup and the Champions League - in less than a week and you can see why the French boss is sweating. It’s now imperative that they achieve at least a top three finish, but with Manchester City just one point behind and fifth-place West Ham United in good form, that could end slipping away from them as well unless they can turn around a disappointing few weeks, starting with a win here this afternoon.
It’s been a mixed season for Everton, who have dazzled and frustrated their fans in equal measure over the course of the last six months. Consistency has been hard to come by for the Toffees, resulting in them picking up impressive wins only to go and lose the momentum gained with poor defeats. As a result, they start the weekend in a disappointing 12th place, 13 points away from both the relegation zone and the top four and, based on how this campaign has panned out thus far, with little chance of finishing in either. This afternoon marks the start of a tough period for Roberto Martinez’s men, who after today travel to Manchester United before entertaining Southampton and Liverpool in quick succession. However, they will no doubt have been buoyed by last weekend’s FA Cup win against Chelsea in a game that saw star striker Romelu Lukaku find the back of the net not once but twice. The Belgian has been in impeccable form this season and has already broken the club record for the most goals scored in a single campaign. He is set to play an important role here today as he looks to improve his tally against Arsenal’s lacklustre defence.

West Brom and Norwich have already met twice this season – once in the Barclays Premier League and once in the League Cup. The Baggies won the league match 1-0 at Carrow Road, with Rondon getting the only goal of the game again, but this was after they had been knocked out of the Cup by Neil's charges, who cruised to a 3-0 win to progress in the competition. The last three league meetings between the sides have seen wins for the away team and the home team failing to score.
Norwich, meanwhile, are still very much embroiled in a relegation dogfight and currently find themselves down in 18th with 25 points taken from their opening 30 matches. They can certainly take some heart from their last outing, though, as they managed to shut out Manchester City to a 0-0 stalemate at Carrow Road, with defensive solidity giving manager Alex Neil cause for optimism for the run-in.
West Brom's last match was the aforementioned brilliant 1-0 win over the Red Devils last weekend, in which Salomon Rondon proved to be the hero with his strike in the 66th minute. Pulis will probably be more content with the rearguard action, though, as the Baggies defence put in a superb display to see themselves to a clean sheet and subsequent three points.
A few weeks back, it looked like today's match may indeed be a relegation scrap between the Baggies and the Canaries. However, Tony Pulis has worked his magic once again by leading West Brom to a series of outstanding results which has subsequently seen them shoot right up the table into 11th place. A disappointing FA Cup exit at the hands of Reading aside, they have picked up wins against Everton, Crystal Palace, and Manchester United, whilst also drawing 2-2 against league leader, Leicester.

Aston Villa had the rug pulled further from under them last weekend when they were brushed aside all too easily by Tottenham. Despite reality creeping in, their fans were in high spirits on Sunday. They stood and applauded their side, showing real class and appreciation for everything they have been given during their life in the Premier League. It’s quickly fading away, but it’s hard for supporters to be upset with the players. The work ethic or fighting spirit isn’t what’s lacking – they’re simply not a good enough team to string together results, and full credit has to be given to the fans for realising this as they stick with their Lions till the bitter end.
Hello and welcome to live coverage from the Liberty Stadium as Swansea City try to secure their Premier League status when they play host to an Aston Villa side hoping not to relinquish theirs. With eight points protecting the Swans from the bottom three, it would take something of an epic collapse for them to be considered relegation candidates – though losing to Aston Villa would certainly border on disastrous. Sunderland were the winners of the first half but Newcastle did wonderfully well to fight back in the second period as the visitors began to sit deep and tire. Townsend and Sissoko looked particularly dangerous, resulting in Mitrovic finally finding the back of the net after having a tough afternoon up until then. Tyne-Wear derbies have been happy occasions for Sunderland over the past few years, and they head into the 156th meeting between the two sides with recent history firmly on their side. Last October saw them comfortably beat their fierce rivals 3-0 to extend their derby winning streak to six games, and during that time they have scored a whopping 21 goals, with Newcastle managing just one in reply. It’s now almost four and a half years since the Magpies last beat the Black Cats, whilst their last derby victory at St. James’ Park - a 5-1 thrashing made possible by a Kevin Nolan hat-trick - came way back in October 2010.
They may head to St. James’ Park ahead of their fierce rivals in the Premier League table, but things look just as bleak for Sunderland, who once again find themselves inside the relegation zone after Norwich City’s big win against West Bromwich Albion yesterday. However, after suffering a difficult end to 2015, the Black Cats have performed better since the start of the year, and that has particularly been the case over the past month and a half. A decent run of form - which was made even better by last month’s 2-1 win at home to Manchester United - has resulted in Sam Allardyce’s side losing just one of their last five league games, only the second time they have done so all season. Nonetheless, inconsistency is still plaguing the former Newcastle manager’s side and, with just one from their last eight, wins are proving hard to come by. They still have to face Leicester, Arsenal, Stoke City and Chelsea before the end of the season, so clashes like today’s are absolute must-wins if they are to have any chance of pulling themselves out of the relegation zone.
Due to the precarious positions that the two sides currently find themselves in, today’s Tyne-Wear is arguably one of the biggest and most important in recent memory. Difficult seasons for Newcastle and Sunderland have left them languishing near the bottom of the table, and, with just nine games left to play, both are in real danger of being relegated. Just one point currently separates them heading into this afternoon’s huge clash, and it is the hosts who are in worst form as a result of a miserable five-week period. The Magpies are now without a single point in their last four Premier League games after last weekend’s 1-0 defeat against Leicester City in Rafa Benitez’s first game in charge, whilst just one of their last seven has ended in a victory. During that time they have conceded 15 goals, scoring just four in the process. Injuries have hit them hard and has left their back four looking nervous and shaky to say the least, and whilst they showed positive signs in last weekend’s loss against the league leaders, their new boss will be well aware that he has a lot of work to do if he is to save them from dropping down to the second tier.

Full-time at St. Mary's as the referee calls time on an absolute thriller. THREE-TWO!! ---

He probably should have scored!

Offside, though, and Southampton get the free-kick.

--- 48’ Yellow card Yellow card Emre Can ---

(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!

Philippe Coutinho opened the scoring for the Reds with an outstanding curler into the bottom corner before Daniel Sturridge doubled the advantage with an excellent finish into the bottom corner past Forster. The Saints need to sort themselves out, even though they arguably should have been awarded a penalty. Second period to come!
(44’) Two minutes of added time allocated by the referee which sounds about right as the game has pretty much been free-flowing. Liverpool will go into the break two goals to the good unless Southampton can make a late rally before going in for their half-time team talk.
(42’) Southampton have a real opportunity to get some quality into the penalty area now with a free-kick down the right channel. (40’) There is just a bit of a lull in the game at the moment as both sides struggle to keep possession effectively. Liverpool won't mind the formula to the game too much, as long as proceedings are scrappy then the less chance they have of allowing Southampton a route back into contention.
(38’) Under 10 minutes remaining in the first half now and the Saints should really be looking to claw a goal back before the break, as the longer the match goes on the more confident Liverpool will get due to their relatively healthy advantage. Indeed, Klopp's men continue to look dangerous so it would be a big ask for the hosts to shut them out further for the remainder of play.
(36’) Southampton just haven't been able to muster up any kind of ascendancy going forward, as Liverpool are winning the ball back so quickly in the midfield areas that no threat can be made from the hosts. Koeman will probably be looking at changes, either personnel or tactically, as we approach the break.
(34’) GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR LIVERPOOL! WAIT! NO! OFFSIDE! Allen latches on to a loose ball on the outside of the box and sends a well-taken half-volley low into the bottom corner. The visitors go away to celebrate for a few moments, but are left disappointed as they realise the linesman has his flag up, seemingly penalising Sakho for being ahead of the play. Good decision in the end.
(32’) When the line-ups were announced, it was assumed that Flanagan would be deployed at left-back as he has played in that position before. But it appears that Clyne is the man who has moved to the opposite flank, with the Liverpool captain bombing forward on the right touchline. He gets forward on this occasion to tease a neat cross to the back post, where Martina is forced into putting behind for a corner.
(30’) Speaking of the tutelage of the former Dortmund boss, it is clear for all to see that he likes his team to play a pressing game high up the park, and this has been no more noticeable than today, and perhaps recent win over Manchester City, as Southampton find themselves under massive pressure whenever on the ball at the back and in midfield.
(28’) Southampton really need to sort themselves out here as Liverpool look like they are capable of scoring any time they venture into the final third. The frontline of the Reds are displaying some outstanding link-up play at the moment, which is a testament to the improvement they have made under Jurgen Klopp recently.
(26’) BRILLIANT SAVE FROM FORSTER! Allen wins the ball superbly in midfield and catalyses a sweeping counterattack forward, with Lallana and then Sturridge involved in the build-up. --- 24’ Yellow card First yellow card of the match now and no real surprise that it goes to Lovren for a late tackle on Long, who has been a thorn in the side of the Liverpool defender since the start of play. He'll need to watch himself from now on as there is plenty of time left on the clock! ---

--- 22’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR LIVERPOOL! A QUICKFIRE DOUBLE FROM THE REDS! Origi makes his way through the middle with a marauding before laying into the path of Sturridge. (19’) The Reds haven't managed to put together a run of four consecutive league wins in nearly a year, but they have put themselves in a decent position to do so here with this early lead. A bit of a sucker punch for Southampton, who are still feeling aggrieved at the penalty kick that wasn't awarded.

--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAALLLLL FOR LIVERPOOL! PURE INSPIRATION FROM COUTINHO! The Brazilian receives the ball to feet deep down the left wing and typically cuts inside on his right foot before whipping an outstanding strike low into the bottom right corner! Superb finish! One-nil! ---

(14’) Liverpool camp Southampton in their own half with a decent period of sustained possession, but there isn't much penetration into the box and into the danger areas as of yet. Roberto Firmino is missing today due to injury, so the burden is with Coutinho to try and get in between the lines to link the play between midfield and attack.

The referee fails to point to the spot and the Saints fans explode with a chorus of boos!

The Anfield outfit have won four of their last six Premier League matches, averaging three goals per game in that run, but come up against a Southampton side who have been resurgent since the return of Fraser Forster between the sticks. Should the former Celtic stopper keep a clean sheet this afternoon, he will be the fourth quickest goalkeeper to reach 20 clean sheets in league history, after Petr Cech, Jose Reina, and Roy Carroll.
Southampton may have solid recent home form, but unfortunately for them this form doesn't translate into matches against the Reds. The sides have already faced each other twice this season, with the last league match ending 1-1 at Anfield, with Christian Benteke and Sadio Mane on target for their respective sides. However, it was the League Cup match at the start of December which hit the headlines as Klopp's men recorded an emphatic 6-1 win away at St. Mary's. Combine this with the fact that Liverpool have won their last two away league matches against the Saints 2-0 and 3-0, and it generates into a cause for concern for Koeman and his charges.
Today's match presents us with the opportunity to view two sides in relatively decent form. The Saints have lost only one of their last six home games, while Liverpool have been buoyed by back-to-back Premier League wins over Manchester City and Crystal Palace, with progression in the Europa League also confirmed after an aggregate win over arch rivals, Manchester United.
European football qualification is still on the agenda for both Ronald Koeman and Jurgen Klopp this season, with Southampton and Liverpool placed in 8th and 9th in the table respectively, both on exactly 44 points. Due to the similar positioning in the league, if aspirations of Europa League football or indeed Champions League football are to be met then matches like this will prove to be vital in the run-in.

The referee blows his whistle for the final time and brings an end to a game that has resulted in a relatively comfortable victory for United. City never seemed to turn up, resulting in them finding very little joy whenever they pushed forward. They lacked the intensity and desire needed to break down a well-organised an resolute Red Devils back line, one that stuck their task diligently and left their opponents with very little space to operate in. As a result, from Rashford's goal onwards it was an easy afternoon for Louis van Gaal's men, who know sit just one point behind their local rivals and keep alive their chances of qualifying for the Champions League.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
Whilst inconsistency is plaguing both clubs, City head into today’s clash with recent history on their side after dominating the Manchester derby over the past three years. Since December 2012, the Citizens have beaten their rivals on four of the last six occasions, with United winning just once during that time. Today’s hosts have also thoroughly enjoyed themselves on this ground in recent years, winning the last two meetings in a row and scoring five goals to their opponents’ one. They now have the opportunity to beat the Red Devils on their home ground for the third time in a row, something that hasn’t happened since 1995.
Just when it looks as if United have turned a corner, poor results bring them crashing back down to earth. Back-to-back league wins - their first since November - against Arsenal and Watford, coupled with comfortable cup victories against Shrewsbury Town and Midtjylland, filled fans with hope and signalled a possible change in fortune for the Red Devils, but since the win against the Hornets they have been hit by the inconsistency and lethargy that characterised their early season performances. As a result, they are now out of the Europa League and without a win in their last four consecutive games, with their last Premier League clash, a disappointing affair against West Bromwich Albion, ending 1-0 to the Baggies. Whilst they have two games in hand over the seventh-place side, Stoke City’s win yesterday means that they now trail Louis van Gaal’s men by just one point, meaning that a victory today is absolutely vital if they are to keep alive their hopes of qualifying for a European competition next season.
Disappointing campaigns for both Manchester clubs means that they are now fighting tooth and nail for a place in the Champions League next season, and with just four points separating the two sides, the victor of this afternoon’s clash will win more than just bragging rights. After having a difficult few weeks in which they have picked up just four points from a possible 15 - including losing three league games in a row for the first time since November 2008 - City’s now sit 15 points behind league leaders Leicester City, rendering their title chances all but over. Now, their sights must be firmly set on European qualification, and with in-form West Ham United just a point behind them, a win today is imperative if they are to keep the Hammers at bay and keep the pressure firmly on third-place Arsenal. A relatively comfortable goalless draw at home to Dynamo Kiev on Tuesday evening saw the Citizens through to the quarter-finals of the Champions League, but it came at a cost, as both Nicolas Otamendi and, most importantly, Vincent Kompany will miss out today after picking up injuries against the Ukrainian side. Manuel Pellegrini’s team have looked far better since the Belgian returned from injury little over a month ago, but his absence could cause problems for his side, who have looked defensively poor when he is not on the pitch.

Bournemouth, rather impressively for a promoted team, have lost just one of their last nine away league matches, winning four and drawing the other four in the process. Even with this good form, though, they will still be wary of the fact that in their previous match against Spurs at the Vitality Stadium in October, the capital-club ran out comprehensive 5-1 winners.
Tottenham's biggest goal threat this season has typically been Harry Kane, who has scored eight goals in his last nine league games, taking his tally to 19 in total for the campaign. Such a prolific centre-forward would certainly be desired by Bournemouth, as their top goalscorer this season is Callum Wilson, who has scored five goals but has been injured since September. However, the burden to find the net has been shared throughout the squad, as 13 separate players have scored in the Premier League this season for the Cherries.
Pochettino's charges may be riding high near the top of their domestic league, but they will need to display some mental strength in order to recover from their miserable exit from the Europa League during the week when they were outclassed in a 5-1 aggregate defeat to Borussia Dortmund. The Argentine boss fielded weakened sides for both legs in that tie, though, so it is fairly clear that his priorities lie with the league.
Spurs are currently second in the table with 58 points taken from 30 matches, which is eight points behind the Foxes in top position. Today's match is indeed their game in hand though, so they can close the gap on the league toppers if they can claim all three points against Bournemouth this afternoon. The Cherries, meanwhile, are loftily positioned in 13th place on 38 points, and can probably begin to breathe a sigh of relief, with their Premier League status basically sealed for next year.
If it wasn't for the impeccable resurgence of Leicester City from relegation candidates to potential champions this season, there would certainly be more headline room awarded to Mauricio Pochettino and Eddie Howe for the jobs they have did in their respective roles this year. For the first time in recent memory, Tottenham are still in with a shout of being crowned as league winners at this stage of the season, while Bournemouth, in their maiden Premier League adventure, have all but sealed their status in the top flight for next season, with plenty of games to spare.
