(90’) A major opportunity for Norwich now as we move into three minutes of added time, as Mbokani wins a free-kick - on the right this time - that O’Neil stands over…
(87’) TOP DEFENDING! A free-kick now for City that Silva drifts in to Iheanacho, whose flicked-header is cleared by Mbokani but only as far as Zabaleta, who drinks a cross back in. It eventually falls back to Iheanacho, but he cannot get a clean strike on goal and it rebounds out to Sterling. The winger looks set to pull the trigger, but Klose again gets across on the cover to make an excellent challenge.
--- 85’ Substitution A final change now then for City, as Bacary Sagna is replaced by the more attack-minded Pablo Zabaleta for the remaining five minutes plus stoppage time. ---
(84’) CHANCE! What a moment that could have been for Norwich! Kompany and Sagna make a mess of a clearance and the ball bounces back into the path of Mbokani. who drives into the box before selflessly teeing up Dorrans on the edge of the area. The former West Brom man tries his luck with a first-time effort, but he can only skew his chance wide of the mark!
(82’) Sloppy from Sterling, as he - for a reason known only to himself - stalls his run after Iheanacho had played a neat ball into his path. The England winger looked sharp when he first came on, but his effect has diminished as the half has wore on...
(79’) Good work from Mbokani, as he shows his experience by winning a free-kick off Kompany down on the left flank. Olsson lofts in the cross towards the area, where Norwich’c centre backs have moved up to, but the delivery is a tame one and City counter through Aguero. He looks to slide a throughball into the path of Iheanacho, wh had checked his run to stay onside, but O’Neil is well-positioned to cut it out.
--- 77’ Substitution A second change now for City, as Kelechi Iheanacho - who made his first start in the reverse fixture - replaces Jesus Navas. The Nigerian youngster has an impressive nine goals to his name in all competitions this term. ---
(76’) CLOSE! More good defending from Norwich, as Klose gets across to prevent Aguero latching onto a cross at the near post. You do feel that the visitors are just starting to find more gaps now, having been in the hosts’ half for much of the second period.
--- 74’ Yellow card Another booking now for Norwich, as Jonny Howson picks up a yellow card for a cyncial foul on Fernandinho, who had got the better of the former Leeds midfielder with a neat bit of footwork. ---
(73’) One thing that the change does allow Norwich to do is to be a bit more direct with their counter-attacks, as they now have two big targets to hit upfield rather than the more slender figure of Bamford. City are still dominating possession, but despite their poor defensive record, the hosts are remaining steadfast in their efforts to keep the visitors at bay.
(70’) It will be interesting to see how Norwich set up now following those changes. Both Jerome and Mbokani are natural front-men, though since the introduction of Sterling, Neil’s side have found themselves been pushed back deeper and deeper. It appears that the hosts will retain their 4-4-1-1 shape for the time-being, with Mbokani sitting in the position behind the main striker that Hoolahan was previously occupying.
--- 68’ Substitution And that change is actually a double one, as Norwich’s third and final substitution sees Patrick Bamford make way for Cameron Jerome. It has been an impressive full debut for the youngster, who was unfortunate not to give the hosts a lead with a truly superb strike in the first half. ---
--- 67’ Substitution A second game of the change now for the hosts, and it is certainly an attacking one from Neil, as he replaces Wes Hoolahan with Dieumerci Mbokani. ---
(65’) Almost! Silva drives a low effort on target from the resulting set-piece, which clatters off the wall and pin-balls around in the Norwich area, before Dorrans reacts to hook it clear deep into City’s territory. The hosts really are sitting deeper and deeper now!
(64’) Superb from Aguero! The diminutive striker does brilliantly to get the better of Klose and draw a foul right on the cusp of the area. The referee could have bene forgiven had he pointed to the spot, but he instead awards the free-kick, and rightly so...
(62’) CHANCE! Sterling’s first involvement in the game is to drive past O’Neil down the left and win a free-kick after being brought down by the former Middlesbrough and Portsmouth midfielder. Silva lofts in the cross, and although it is cleared at first City work the move back into the area with Fernandinho bursting into the area and teeing up Aguero, who attempts to get the better of Klose but is just unable to get his shot away.
(60’) Poor from Navas as he twice fails to get a decent cross into the area from a corner down on the right. Norwich counter swiftly, with Bamford managing to get the better of Kompany on this occasion, but he is soon sandwiched off of the ball by Fernando and Fernandinho, who had covered the gap vacated by their captain.
--- 59’ Substitution A change now for City, as their second-highest scorer Raheem Sterling enters the fray to add some more width and pace to the visitor’s so-far lacklustre attack. The former Liverpool winger replaces the rather ineffective Wilfried Bony. ---
(58’) Solid defending again from Klose, as the former Wolfsburg defender powers out to prevent Bony getting on the end of Fernandinho’s cross.
(56’) It’s certainly an open and flowing game at Carrow Road, though Jon Moss does have a decision to make after Otamendi - already on a booking - clatters clumsily into Dorrans. The Argentina defender escapes with just a word of caution, though you do feel had he not already been booked that the foul would have warranted a yellow card.
(54’) More pressure from City, but again they are unable to carve out any space in between Norwich’s stubborn defence and the home side are able to counter through Hoolahan. The Republic of Ireland international drives forward before laying it off to Bamford, but the Chelsea-loanee is quickly smothered by the excellent Kompany.
(51’) Wasteful! Navas dinks in the free-kick, but in all truth it was a poor one and Norwich clear it - though only as far as Aguero. He attempts to twist around his marker and jink into the penalty area, but he is well-marshalled by Dorrans and the hosts manage to stem the chance.
--- 50’ Yellow card A corner now at the other end after Hoolahan’s cross is deflected wide. However, the hosts camped make anything of it and City counter through Aguero, who makes a length-of-the-field run before being dragged down on the cusp of the Norwich area by O’Neil, who picks up a booking. ---
(48’) City have started the second half in a similar fashion to how they began the first - well in control with Silva dictating the tempo of their attacks. Navas does well to win a corner down the right which he then whips in to a dangerous area. Otamendi - whose only goal for City so far came in the win over Norwich at the Etihad - meets it on the run, but his header lands on the roof of the net.
(46’) Under way! We are back up and running at Carrow Road, with Manchester City who have won just two of their last 10 matches on the road - getting the second half started.
Despite City controlling over 70% of possession in the early stages, they could not muster a clear chance until just prior to the half-hour mark, when Aguero raced clear of Olsson and powered a low strike at goal that Ruddy reacted instinctively to parry wide. Norwich hauled themselves back into proceedings from then-on-in, however, and were almost rewarded for their efforts when Bamford’s stunning 30-yard strike rattled the crossbar. The hosts have been dealt a blow, though, with their top-scorer and star player Redmond having to be taken off due to an ankle injury.
HALF-TIME! That’s it for the opening 45 minutes at Carrow Road, where the score is still level at 0-0 between Norwich and Manchester City. The visitors dominated proceedings in the opening half-an-hour, but since then the hosts have had the better of the game, with Bamford going agonisingly close to giving them the lead with what would arguably have been a goal of the season contender on his first Premier League start...
(45’) CLOSE! Great play again from the hosts as Dorrans drives in from the right wing and attempts to curl an effort into the top-left corner, but it takes a slight deflection and sails out for a corner...
--- 45’ Substitution And that injury duly results in a substitution for the hosts, as Graham Dorrans, who himself has been out with an injury lately, comes on to replace his stricken teammate. There will be two additional minutes of stoppage time at the end of this half... ---
(44’) A real dilemma for Norwich now, as Redmond again goes down onto the turf with what looks to be a re-occurance of that ankle injury he picked up earlier. He will not be able to continue, which is a real blow for the hosts.
(42’) A brief rest-bite now for City, as Silva, Clichy and Fernandinho make some headway down the left wing and retain possession down by the corner flag. Silva eventually attempts to weave his way into the area, but can only concede a foul after O’Neil had managed to position himself between the Spaniard and the ball.
(40’) CROSSBAR!!! WHAT AN EFFORT FROM BAMFORD!! That is so unlucky for the Chelsea-loanee, who takes a lofted ball from deep under control before, with no other alternative, hammering a half-volleyed effort at goal from over 30 yards out. The strike dips and swerves and evades Hart, but rather than nestling into the back of the net, clatters off the woodwork. What a way to open up his Norwich - and Premier League - goalscoring account that would have been!
(38’) Again, City have Kompany to thank as their skipper twice makes superb blocks to prevent Redmond and then Jarvis getting their crosses into the box. Norwich have really upped their game in the last 10 minutes and the visitors have been unable to really get out of their own half. Can the hosts take advantage and get the goal their manager and supporters so desperately crave...
(36’) More patient play from the hosts, as they again look to make headway down the left flank through Olsson, who drives in an inviting low cross, but once more City’s captain Kompany reads the situation perfectly and gets across to make the block. Norwich are certainly well in this game now, though!
(33’) Redmond has made his way back into the fray now, and looks to be moving relatively freely as Norwich forge another well-worked move into City’s final third, but Bamford is just unable to latch onto O’Neil’s cross.
(31’) A pause in play now, as Redmond receives treatment for an apparent knock to his ankle. Neil looks concerned on the touchline, and rightly so, given the importance of the winger to his team. The hosts will be desperate for him to be fit to carry on.
(29’) GREAT SAVE! That’s a super stop from Ruddy, who gets down low to his right to get a big, strong hand to Aguero’s driven effort that was destined for the bottom-left corner of Norwich’s net. The Argentine has looked sharp in the early stages, but that was his first real sighter at goal.
(28’) Redmond drives in the free-kick to a dangerous area, but Hart comes out to command his area and gather it in before getting City’s counter-attack kick-started at pace. Aguero controls it excellently, but he is well-marshalled by the retreating O’Neil.
--- 26’ Yellow card Norwich have settled somewhat in recent minutes, and that has really lifted the crowd. Bamford drops deep into midfield and sets Martin off with a superb first-time pass. The hosts’ captain - making a club-record 120th Premier League appearance this afternoon - drives down the flank before combining with Redmond and being brought down by Otamendi, who duly goes into the book for his troubles. ---
(23’) Better from Norwich now, as they finally manage to sustain a brief period of play in City’s half. Howson and Hoolahan combine to set up Olsson for the cross down the left, and the former Blackburn Rovers full-back duly delivers a flat ball in, but Kompany is well-placed to cut out the danger ahead of Bamford, who was lingering on the shoulder of the Belgian.
(21’) ALMOST! Great play by City, who are starting to pick out the gaps in Norwich’s defence with ease. Fernandinho is the architect in this instance as he drifts a precise 40-yards pass to Clichy, who despite finding himself free in acres of space in the hosts’ penalty area, can only fire a tame cross into the side-netting.
(19’) It’s patient and precise play from the visitors at the moment, as they continue to dominate proceedings with over 70% of possession.  Navas and Silva link up down the right before the latter tees up Aguero, who twists and turns towards goal before drilling a low effort in from the edge of the area, but it trickles harmlessly wide of the upright.
(17’) STAT FLASH - There have been 40 goals scored in the last eight Premier League meetings between the two sides, and only Tottenham have prevented Norwich from scoring at Carrow Road this campaign.
(15’) CLOSE! Aguero tries his luck from the free-kick with a dipping strike that gets up and over the wall, but Ruddy is equal to it to prevent the effort nestling in the top-right corner.
(14’) Silva really is running the show at the minute for City, as he drops deep to pick up possession and spread a lofted throughball towards Aguero. Bennett gets there first, with the loose ball falling to O’Neil, who can only foul Fernandinho and give the visitors a free-kick 30 yards from goal...
--- 12’ Yellow card A retrospective yellow card then for Ryan Bennett, who really did dive in late on Silva in the build-up to that chance and can have no complaints. Fortunately for the visitors, the Spaniard is okay to continue. ---
(11’) Great defending! Bennet dives in heavily on Silva, who stays down injured after managing to prod the ball onto Bony. Referee Jon Moss waves play-on, with Bony driving an effort towards the target from range, but Klose gets across to make a timely interception and clear the danger.
(10’) Unlucky! Silva picks out the run of Aguero with a sublime pass but the Argentine - who has scored 10 goals in his last 10 appearances - had made his move just too early and is correctly flagged for offside.
(9’) Good play from Norwich at the other end, now, as Redmond picks up a pocket of space in the inside-right channel and slots a meat pass though to Martin, whose attempted cross is deflected wide for a corner. The aforementioned former Birmingham City winger powers in a flat delivery, which falls out to Olsson on the edge of the area, but he blazes his strike well over the crossbar.
(7’) CHANCE! City are starting to get on the ball now, with Silva naturally dictating the tempo from that advanced central midfield position. The former Valencia playmaker slides a throughball into the path of Navas, who drives to the byline before lofting a cross towards the back post which Martin can only help on to Aguero. The striker sets himself up before drilling an effort goalwards, but the Norwich skipper atones for his error with a decent block.
(5’) An interesting tactical change for City, as it appears that Aguero is taking up a berth slightly out to the left at the moment, with Silva slotting in behind Bony. The Argentine wins a free-kick off Martin, which is floated in to the centre of the area. Ruddy charges out to collect it, only to spill the ball under pressure from Kompany, but the hosts manage to claw it clear.
(3’) A rather scrappy opening two minutes then at Carrow Road, with Norwich attempting to move the ball quickly and directly from back-to-front. The last time these sides met - in the FA Cup third round in January - City won 3-0, while the reverse fixture at the Etihad finished 2-1 to the League Cup winners.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are under way at Carrow Road, with the hosts, attacking from left to right in the first half, getting proceedings up and running.
Kick off is just moments away now, and the teams are out onto the pitch at Carrow Road - which is packed to capacity for this game, which really is a huge moment in the respective campaigns of both these sides!
Norwich have conceded 12 goals in their last four games at Carrow Road, and you feel that their defence will have their work cut out for them today against the in-form Sergio Aguero - who took his tally for the season to 16 league goals with the double against Villa last time out. However, City have struggled for goals on the road so far this campaign, having netted just 13 times in total away from the Etihad.
Norwich’s issues have stemmed from their inability to hold onto leads. Their have been prime examples in recent weeks - against Liverpool and West Ham respectively - where Neil’s side have taken two-goal advantages but failed to go on and claim the three points. As for City, their problems can be traced back to their quite dreadful record against teams in the top eight of Premier League this season. They have won none of their 11 fixtures against the sides around them, and it is only their form from their 17 fixtures against the bottom 12 of the league (W15, D2, L0), that is keeping them within range of a real tilt on the title in the last 10 games of the season.
TEAM NEWS - Manchester City substitutes: Zabaleta, Sterling, Kolarov, Caballero, Demichelis, Iheanacho, Garcia.
TEAM NEWS - Manchester City (4-4-2): Hart; Sagna, Kompany, Otamendi, Clichy; Navas, Fernando, Fernandinho, Silva; Bony, Aguero.
TEAM NEWS - Norwich substitutes: Bassong, Mbokani, Jerome, Rudd, Dorrans, Mulumbu, Pinto.
TEAM NEWS - Norwich (4-4-1-1): Ruddy; Martin, Bennett, Klose, Olsson; Redmond, O’Neil, Howson, Jarvis; Hoolahan; Bamford.
The teams are in now from East Anglia. There is one change for the visitors, as Manuel Pellegrini drafts in Fernando for Yaya Toure, who is absent through injury. As for Norwich, who would escape the drop zone with a victory today, they make four changes in total to the line up that started in the defeat to Swansea City. Two of those are enforced, with Robbie Brady and Steven Naismith both injured, while Cameron Jerome and Ivo Pinto drop to the bench. Martin Olsson, Ryan Bennett, Matt Jarvis and Patrick Bamford making his first Premier League start for the club - coming into the side. Lets check on the full starting XIs.
On the other hand, Manuel Pellegrini's side - 10 points behind league-leaders Leicester City heading into this round of fixtures - bounced back from their lacklustre performance in the 3-0 defeat to Liverpool with a comprehensive 4-0 thumping of lowly Aston Villa last time out. Top-scorer Sergio Aguero netted a double in that rout at the Etihad, and the former Atletico Madrid forward will fancy his chances of getting on the score sheet once again today - given his excellent record of six goals in six games against Norwich.
The Canaries have been in terrible form as of late, with a run of eight defeats from their last nine league fixtures leaving them in 18th place. Alex Neill, however, has called for the Norwich faithful to stick firmly behind their struggling side - who have taken just one point from their last four games - as they look for what would be just their second victory over City in 14 attempts in the Premier League.
Hello and welcome, folks, to this LIVE coverage of what promises to be another enthralling Premier League encounter, as relegation-battling Norwich City take on fourth-placed Manchester City, who have not won back to back games in the top-flight since October last year. Stick right here to get all the action as it happens from Carrow Road.

Full time at the Vitality Stadium. Cheers of 'we are staying up' sound out among the Bournemouth fans as they celebrate an entertaining 3-2 win at home over Swansea. The Swans actually fought back from behind twice with goals from Barrow and Sigurdsson, but it was strikes from Max Gradel, Josh King, and the winner from Steve Cook which sealsed the vital three points for Eddie Howe's men. Thanks for joining us - see you next time!
(90’) Last two minutes now, and expect it to be attack versus defence for the remaining moments of play as Swansea go all-out to try and find this equaliser. After two wins on the bounce, it looks like Francesco Guidolin's charges are back to reality in their pursuit to avoid the drop.
(90’) FOUR minutes of added time is the order of the day which sounds about right due to the aforementioned reasons. Swansea are giving it a good go in these latter stages, but time is against them with every second that ticks down towards the final whistle!
(88’) Swansea can take heart from the fact that there may indeed by a decent period of added time allocated by the referee, as we have seen the goals flying in this afternoon as well as plenty of substitutions. Can they come back from behind for the third time this afternoon to make it 3-3?
(86’) Swansea have did brilliantly to get back into contention twice today with two equalisers, but that third goal from Bournemouth looks to have sucked all the confidence out of them. Even with their two brave fightbacks, it looks like they are going to leave the game empty handed this afternoon.
--- 84’ Substitution Last throw of the dice from the Swans now as they make their third substitution. Coming off is on-loan QPR man, Fer, and entering the action is South Korea international, Ki Sung-Yeung, who certainly has the pedigree to pull something out of the back to get an equaliser here. ---
(82’) OHHH SO UNLUCKY FROM LEWIS GRABBAN! The substitute has played at a high tempo since being introduced into the action, and attempts to get on the scoresheet with a glorious chip from 25 yards out which looks destined to loop over Fabianski into the net! The Poland international eventually does really well to tip over the bar, though!
--- 80’ Substitution Second switch from Alan Curtis now and it is a slightly surprising one as it is Barrow, who has been dangerous down that right wing today, make way for the oncoming Marvin Emnes. There must be some sort of injury there, as Barrow was probably Swansea's best bet for an equaliser! ---
--- 78’ Assist A cross of the highest order from Ritchie, who records an assist for his ball into the box for Cook. ---
--- 78’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR BOURNEMOUTH! THE HOME FANS ERUPT! Ritchie picks up the ball down the left wing after a short corner and proceeds to curl a beauty of a cross to the back post for Cook, who rises above everyone to bullet a perfect header into the top right corner! Three-two! It is raining goals in the Vitality! ---
--- 76’ Substitution Another change from Eddie Howe here and it is Gradel who leaves the action to a standing ovation from the Vitality Stadium faithful. He can finally put his injury troubles behind him after a shining performance this afternoon, and he will come off to be replaced by Marc Pugh. ---
(74’) O'Kane collects possession down the middle and sends a lovely diagonal out to the left wing for Gradel, but Fernandez is proactive in his defending and quickly comes out of his position to charge down at he Ivorian before intercepting to win the ball.
(72’) Bournemouth have just allowed that equaliser from Sigurdsson to just take the wind out of their sails a bit, as they were going forward fairly gung-ho up until that point. Slightly more conservative in their attacking now, but can still be a threat if they can manage to get possession into the feet of Gradel in particular, as he has been superb this afternoon.
(70’) Twenty minutes remaining here at the Vitality Stadium and it is anyone's game at the moment. However, it is Swansea who have looked the more dangerous outfit since changing their formation to 4-4-2 with Gomis playing up top alongside Paloschi. Bournemouth by no means out of contention for the win, though.
(68’) It was mentioned previously that both Bournemouth and Swansea can be fairly content with their Premier League standing at the moment considering their distance in points away from the relegation zone. However, a victory would do wonders going into the last portion of the season and certainly take plenty of pressure off.
--- 66’ Substitution Second alteration of the match from Eddie Howe now as he introduces one of his January signings in place of the other. Benik Afobe, who has disappointed today, is the man trudging off to the bench and entering the play is Lewis Grabban, who returned to Bournemouth from Norwich in the transfer window. ---
(64’) When Swansea equalised in the first half, they quickly went on the ascendancy and looked the better team for 10 minutes or so. The same formula seems to be happening here as the Swans are piling on the pressure since getting back on level terms with a succession of corner kicks.
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLLLL FOR SWANSEA! BACK ON LEVEL TERMS AGAIN! Gomis has an instant impact for the Swans as he holds play up strongly before sending a neat pass down the wing for Barrow, who hits the byline before curling a teasing cross into the box. The Iceland international collects with an assure touch before sending a superb finish into the top right corner! Two-two! Fabulous game! ---
--- 60’ Substitution First change of the match from Alan Curtis and this perhaps signals a change in formation, as Routledge is the man making way for Gomis to come on. A four-four-two with the Frenchman alongside Paloschi up top? ---
(58’) OHH THAT IS A REAL CHANCE FOR KING! Bournemouth's second goalscorer, who has already missed a sitter today despite finding the net eventually, passes up a great opportunity to double his tally as he latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the area, only to completely mis-kick his attempt. Swansea clear.
(56’) Ten minutes gone in the second period now and there aren't really many signs coming from Swansea that they are going to find the net anytime soon. It is entirely his fault due to the lack of service, but Paloschi has had desperately little impact on the game, and with Ayew still missing due to an ankle injury, Curtis may look for Bafetimbi Gomis to provide a spark up top.
(54’) Angel tries to take the game by the scruff of the neck with a marauding run down the right wing, before exchanging a one-two with Barrow. The Swansea right-back receives the ball back to feet and goes for goal from around 30 yards, but due to his goalscoring record, it isn't really a surprise that the strike goes well wide of the mark.
(52’) A lightning-quick opening to the proceedings here after the break, which is similar to the formula we seen at the beginning of the first half. We are witnessing end-to-end stuff from Bournemouth and Swansea, but the impetus is on the latter to try and find an equaliser as quickly as possible.
--- 50’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL FOR BOURNEMOUTH! THE HOSTS RECLAIM THE LEAD! King initially does brilliantly to win possession back for the Cherries before receiving the ball back from Gradel and rifling a fabulous strike in off the right-hand post! Fabianski should have done better, but the home side won't care! Two-one! ---
--- 50’ Assist A goal and an assist for Gradel tonight, with the latter being provided for King with neat pass. ---
(48’) A few weeks ago, this game would probably have been played with noticeable more nerves, but two consecutive wins on the bounce for both Bournemouth and Swansea have seem them move comfortably away from the relegation zone. As a result, the game is at a frenetic pace with both sides going for the win. Entertaining stuff!
--- 46’ Substitution A change to report at the break and it sees Dan Gosling, who was on a yellow card, leave the action to be replaced by Eunan O'Kane. ---
(46’) We are back under way at the Vitality Stadium!
Half-time at the Vitality Stadium. It has been a highly entertaining Barclays Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Swansea this afternoon, as we head into the break at 1-1. Max Gradel got the goalscoring ball rolling with a controlled finish into the corner, but the home side were ahead for just over a minute as the Swans responded through a lovely Max Gradel strike. Exciting second period in store!
(45’) Only one minute of added time has been allocated by the referee here as both Bournemouth and Swansea attempt to claim a lead before we reach the half-time break. A draw probably just a fair result as the managers put the finishing touches on their team talks.
(43’) OHHH SO CLOSE FOR ROUTLEDGE! Barrow is absolutely oozing confidence now after claiming his first Premier League goal, and once again takes on Daniels with a twisting and turning run before hitting the byline and reversing a fantastic cross back into the danger area. His team-mate just can't stop his stride in time to get a meaningful connection on a shot, though, which allows the Cherries to clear!
(41’) It was mentioned previously that all this game needed was a goal in order for the afternoon to ignite, and hasn't it just! Bournemouth were only ahead for just over a minute or so which is testament to the mentality of Swansea, who recognised they needed an instant response after going behind through Gradel. If anything, the Swans look the more likely team to find the need now!
--- 39’ Assist Neat assist from Fer as he finds the feet of Barrow down the wing with a precision pass. ---
--- 39’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR SWANSEA! INSTANT RESPONSE! Fer feeds the ball down to Barrow down the right wing, who cleverly jinks his way into the penalty area on to his left foot before fizzing a superb left-footed strike perfectly into the bottom corner! One-one! ---
--- 37’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR BOURNEMOUTH! A SPECIAL MOMENT FOR GRADEL! The former Saint-Etienne winger finds the net for the first time since coming back from his horrible cruciate injury as he latches on to a poor clearance from Fabianski to find the bottom corner with a controlled volley! One-nil! He runs over to hug Eddie Howe! ---
(35’) Swansea need to be doing a lot better to get Paloschi involved in the action more, as he is feeding off scraps from this Bournemouth defence. The Italian thrives of balls into the danger area, but is being forced to come out his comfort zone into deeper areas to try and affect the play.
--- 34’ Yellow card First yellow card of the match comes to Gosling, and deservedly so as he hauls Gradel to the deck. ---
(33’) Despite a couple of poor deliveries from corner kicks, Gradel has been very bright so far and Swansea seem to be struggling with his movement inside. This time, the Ivorian pops up in behind the opposition midfield and turns sharply before moving into the final third, looking to thread a pass through for King. Good defending in the end from Williams, who steps in to intercept.
(31’) After a pretty intense first portion of the match, the play has just hit a bit of a lull, which is fairly disappointing as it looked like we were in for an exciting afternoon. The match is still relatively entertaining, but it needs a goal just to catalyse the contest a little more.
(29’) Bournemouth have had a couple of free kick opportunities around the Swansea box so far, and the latest is to be taken by Ritchie down the right wing. The Scotland international steps up and whips a dangerous looking cross-cum-shot deep to the back post, which forces Fabianski to retreat back and tip over the bar. Unclear whether he was going for goal or not!
(27’) After a spell of domination from the Cherries, Swans break out on the counterattack, with Sigurdsson leading the charge forward. The former Tottenham attacking midfielder shifts the ball on to his left foot around 25 yards out before pulling the trigger with a low strike aimed at the bottom corner, but it ends up being dragged relatively harmlessly beyond the post.
(25’) Gradel stands over Bournemouth's first corner kick of the match and swings it deep to the back post for Francis, who once again rises high to keep the attack alive with a header back inside. Afobe attempts to get on the end of the loose ball to stab a close-range attempt at goal, but just can't stretch out enough to make a connection, which allows Fabianski to save.
(23’) We are just beyond the midway point of the first period here and considering how free-flowing the match has been, it is a big surprise we find ourselves still viewing a 0-0 stalemate. Plenty of chances being created though so hopefully it won't be too long before the deadlock is broken.
(21’) Bournemouth started the match the better out of the two teams, but Swansea have just grown in prominence as time has gone on, and look much more comfortable in possession, which is how they prefer it. Interesting clash of two footballing philosophies today, as the Cherries are slightly more dynamic in their attacking play compared to the patient build-up of the visitors.
(19’) Swansea are once again without head coach, Francesco Guidolin, this aftenoon who continues to be missing from the dugout due to his recovery from a chest infection. Alan Curtis takes charge of the Swans today, and it may indeed be a good luck charm for them as they have won the past two games without the former Udinese coach being in attendance!
(17’) PENALTY SHOUT FOR SWANSEA! Barrow manages to get in behind the Bournemouth defence with a penetrating run before going down under the challenge of the retreating Daniels, who makes the tackle outside the area before eventually sliding into the box! The referee, perhaps correctly, doesn't give the foul, but more a corner kick to the Swans.
(15’) It has been an absolutely breathless opening 15 minutes or so here at the Vitality and both Bournemouth and Swansea seem to be eager to shine in one of the only two 3pm Barclays Premier League kick-offs this afternoon. The only thing the game has been missing so far is a goal, as it has been highly entertaining!
(13’) SURMAN STRIKES OFF THE BAR! The Bournemouth man steps up to the subsequent free kick from the Gradel foul and clips a lovely set-piece up and over the wall, but it just doesn't dip enough in time and ends up cannoning off the top of the woodwork!
(12’) Free kick to Bournemouth in a very useful position here as Fernandez steps out of his defensive position to try and win the ball, only to succeed in clumsily bringing down Gradel around 25 yards out or so.
(11’) Ritchie pops up down the right touchline and cuts inside on his left foot before attempting to fizz a pass into the path of King at the front post, but Fabianski proactively comes off his line and takes the pressure off his defence to claim possession on the deck.
(9’) Bournemouth get a free kick a yard or so into their own half and it is clipped to the back post for Francis, who recycles back into the danger area with a cushioned header, which is then cleared. Ritchie meets the ball on the volley, but it doesn't go as close as Routledge's recent volleyed effort and goes high and wide away from goal.
(7’) Another great chance passed up by Bournemouth! Gradel is involved in the action positively for the hosts as he releases the oncoming Daniels down the left wing, who subsequently hits the byline before reversing a perfect cross to the back post. King meets it, but displays a poor lack of composure as he blazes over from 10 yards or so.
(5’) ROUTLEDGE! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT?! It has been an outstanding game so far in these early stages as we witness back and forth attacks from both sides. On this occasion, Sigurdsson's free kick is cleared to the edge of the box for the former QPR winger, who sends a spectacular volley aimed towards the top left corner, only to see it flash by the post.
(3’) JUST OVER FROM KING! Gradel, who has been impressive since returning from a long-term cruciate ligament injury recently, cuts in from the left wing and swings a deep cross to the back post for his team-mate, who rises above Taylor to bullet a header off the roof of the net. Unlucky in the end.

The last clash between Bournemouth and Swansea took place earlier this season in a highly entertaining 2-2 draw at the Liberty Stadium. In that Premier League clash back in November, the Cherries actually went 2-0 up through Josh King and Dan Gosling, but the home side rallied not long after and clawed two goals back, with Andre Ayew and Jonjo Shelvey getting on the scoresheet. A similarly entertaining game would be nice today!
Swansea, meanwhile, have been rejuvenated under the the tutelage of Francesco Guidolin, who took over from Garry Monk after a disappointing campaign for the Swans, who had been flirting with dropping into the relegation zone. They are not quite as safe as their opponents today as they are only two positions away from the bottom three, and the former Udinese boss has urged his charges this week to guard against complacency before safety is guaranteed. Last week's vital win over Norwich was preceded by a highly impressive 2-1 away victory over Arsenal at the Emirates.
Bournemouth are currently positioned 14th in the Premier League with 35 points taken from their opening 29 matches. In the past couple of weeks, the aforementioned wins came at home against Southampton in a 2-0 victory and at St. James' Park where they ran out impressive 3-1 victors against Newcastle. It will certainly encourage manager Eddie Howe that the goals seem to be being spread across the squad, too, as they had four different scorers in those games in the form of Benik Afobe, Josh King, Steve Cook, and Charlie Daniels.
A few weeks ago, it seemed likely that today's clash between Bournemouth and Swansea may have potential ramifications for both sides as they attempted to avoid the drop. However, since the start of March both outfits have recorded two consecutive league wins which has catapulted them 11 points and nine points respectively clear of the dropzone.

Graziano Pelle's first-half brace was enough to give Southampton their first win in four and lift them above Stoke to eighth in the Premier League. Marko Arnautovic pulled one back for the hosts after the break, but they were unable to find an equaliser despite dominating most of the play in the second half.
FULL-TIME: STOKE CITY 1-2 SOUTHAMPTON
(90’) There goes the final whistle and Southampton have the points!
(90’) We are into the final few seconds at the Britannia. Stoke are continuing to push for a dramatic equaliser, but it looks like Southampton will hold on for all three points.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Davis is the next player to have his name taken by the referee. ---
--- 90’ +2 Substitution The final throw of the dice from Hughes sees Jonathan Walters thrown on in place of Pieters. ---
--- 90’ +1 Red card! MANE IS SENT OFF! The Southampton substitute receives a straight red card for catching Pieters in the face with his head. It was a sickening collision and Mr. Mason sends him for an early bath. ---
(90’) Danger for Southampton! Crouch wins the header in the penalty area and the ball bounces, but the visitors manage to scramble it away to safety.
(88’) OFF THE BAR! Southampton are awarded a free-kick 25 yards from goal. Ward-Prowse sees his whipped effort crash against the crossbar with Butland beaten. That would have been game over.
(86’) Of course, Southampton will leapfrog Stoke into eighth place if they can hang on and move closer to sixth-place Manchester United. Koeman will be keen to get the Saints back into Europe after falling in the Play-Off round of this season's Europa League.
(84’) As we approach the last five minutes of this game, will Southampton end their three-match winless streak or will Stoke extend their unbeaten run to five games?
(82’) Stoke continue to get the ball in and around the Southampton area. They are still lacking that cutting edge in the final third, however, and need to find something from somewhere.
--- 80’ Substitution Koeman responds by opting for experience at the back. Maya Yoshida comes into the heart of defence to replace youngster Targett. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Hughes is opting for the extra man up front, as Whelan is the man to make way for Crouch on his 300th appearance for Stoke. ---
(77’) Hughes looks to the bench for fresh Stoke inspiration and Peter Crouch is stripped off ready to come on against his former club. Could he be the man to find an equaliser?
--- 75’ Substitution And that is Tadic's last action for today, as he goes off to be replaced by Sadio Mané. ---
(74’) PENALTY?! Tadic gets in behind Wollscheid and goes down under the challenge from Butland. The referee points for a goal-kick and the replay suggests that the Southampton man made a meal of that.
(73’) All of Stoke's build-up play has been brilliant during this second half, until they reach the final third. They have 17 minutes to find an equaliser and extend their unbeaten run to five matches.
(71’) Southampton are struggling to get out of their own half at the moment with Stoke very much in the ascendency. The visitors still look particularly dangerous on the counter attack, though, and should look to use that to their advantage.
--- 69’ Substitution Southampton make their first change of the afternoon, as Clasie makes way to be replaced by James Ward-Prowse. ---
(67’) The hosts have got so much purpose about their play. Cameron delicately lifts the ball forward for Imbula, who's poor touch sees it trickle behind for a goal kick. Nevertheless, the home fans remain in good voice.
(65’) WHAT A BLOCK! Some neat play from Stoke sees Afellay thread the ball through for Cameron to run onto. He plays it across the area for Diouf, who's shot takes a vital deflection off Van Dijk that directs the ball over the crossbar.
(64’) Afellay tries his luck from 35 yards and, even though his ambitious effort is high and wide of the target, the Stoke fans are definitely encouraged by their side.
(62’) The hosts embark on another swift counter attack as Diouf sends Afellay on his way. The Dutchman finds Arnautovic, who looks to play the return pass, but catches the ball wrong and sends it straight into the grateful arms of Forster.
(60’) As we hit the hour-mark, Stoke are looking the better of the two sides in this second half. They have got a lot more urgency about them and Southampton will be worried.
(58’) GOOD STOP! Arnautovic draws a good save out of Forster, as he holds off his marker before unleashing a powerful effort. There is plenty of venom in the shot, but it is straight at the Southampton keeper.
(56’) Stoke have got their tails up all of a sudden. Some good build-up play sees Imbula try his luck from distance and, although the shot is way off target, it is all positive signs for Hughes' men.
--- 55’ Yellow card Pieters goes into the book for a late challenge on the near touchline. That is his eighth yellow card of the season. ---
(54’) Remember, Arnautovic's goals have resulting in Stoke picking up an extra 12 points in this season's Premier League. The hosts will be hoping that can be the case again today.
--- 52’ Assist Afellay delivered an inviting low cross to the near post. ---
--- 52’ Goal! LIFELINE FOR STOKE!!! Arnautovic pulls one back! The Austrian grabs his 10th goal of the season as he cleverly flicks Afellay's low cross into the roof of the net. Stoke have lift-off! ---
(50’) Stoke have lost just one of their last six matches in the Premier League at the Britannia. They need to keep asking questions like that if they are to keep that run going.
(48’) Arnautovic whips the resulting free-kick deep into the box. The ball comes to Diouf, but he cannot get enough on it to beat Forster. The offside flag had been raised anyway, however.
--- 47’ Yellow card Clasie is shown the first yellow card of the game for a late challenge on Pieters. ---
(46’) KICK-OFF! The referee blows his whistle and Southampton get the ball rolling once more.
The players are back out on the field and the second half is about to get started.
Meanwhile, Hughes needs to get Stoke fired up for the second half. His side's possession was good, but they need to cause more problems for the Saints defence.
Graziano Pelle's double separates the sides at the break with Southampton very much on top during that first half. More of the same will be the message from Koeman at half-time.
HALF-TIME: STOKE 0-2 SOUTHAMPTON
(45’) The referee blows his whistle and brings the first half to a close.
(45’) WHAT A WASTE! Long runs the channels wonderfully once again to break away from the Stoke defence. He has a man over in Tadic, who has a certain opportunity to make it 3-0. Instead, he takes an extra touch to cut inside Shawcross and Stoke recover to make an important interception. Southampton should be home and dry!
(45’) Stoke have a free-kick right on the stroke of half-time after Targett fouls Afellay. What can the hosts do from this? Now would be the perfect time to pull one back.
(43’) Hughes and the home fans will be encouraged by Bojan, however. The Spaniard shows some neat skill to nutmeg Clasie on the edge of the area, before his shot is blocked by a Southampton body.
(41’) Wollscheid lets fly from 40 yards with an ambitious effort that epitomises the way the first half has panned out for Stoke. Things need to improve for them after the break.
(40’) Nothing came of the resulting free-kick but Ronald Koeman will be very pleased with his side during this first half. Hughes, on the other hand, can not get his players in for half-time quickly enough.
(38’) Arnautovic is clearly frustrated as he leaves his mark on Martina near the far touchline. The referee has a word with the Stoke man and Southampton have a free-kick in a good position.
(36’) Southampton are brimming with confidence at the moment. There is a real swagger about their play as we approach the latter stages of the first half and it is really good to watch.
(34’) Stoke look to hit back and are awarded a free-kick 30 yards from goal. Arnautovic tries his luck with a very ambitious effort that goes well wide of the target.
(33’) Pelle is now Southampton's top scorer this season with eight goals. It is the second time he has scored twice at the Britannia, having also repeated the feat in that League Cup tie last season.
--- 31’ Substitution Mark Hughes looks to the bench as he looks to spark Stoke back into life. Shaqiri is withdrawn despite not appearing to be injured as is replaced by Bojan. ---
--- 30’ Assist Tadic crisply linked up with Pelle on the corner of the penalty area. ---
--- 30’ Goal! PELLE MAKES IT TWO!!! He retains the ball on the near touchline after Martina's cross evades everyone in the penalty area. The Italian then plays a neat one-two with Tadic, before bending the ball beautifully beyond the reach of Butland. ---
(28’) The Austrian is involved in his side's attempt to launch a quick counter attack following a Southampton free-kick. Imbula looks to find the onrushing Pieters, but overhits his pass and it goes behind for a goal-kick.
(26’) Arnautovic is Stoke's top scorer this season with nine goals. Interestingly, without his strikes, the Potters would be 12 points worse off in the Premier League.
(24’) Shaqiri bursts into life and the edge of the area. He cleverly steps away from his marker before looking for Arnautovic with the cross, but it is just too high for the Austrian.
(22’) Southampton are looking for a return to form this afternoon. They have are without a win in their last three matches, while it took Van Dijk's stoppage-time equaliser against Sunderland to prevent a third consecutive defeat last weekend.
(20’) Long pops up in the pocket of space in between two Stoke defenders to receive Van Dijk's direct pass. He looks to help the ball out wide for Targett, but the linesman rightly raises the offside flag.
(18’) Martina is in need of some attention after slipping near his own penalty area. He is quickly back on the pitch, however, much to the annoyance of the home fans.
(16’) Southampton have looked very dangerous on the counter attack so far today. Stoke have been on top in terms of possession, but they look vulnerable to their opponents' quick breaks.
(14’) GOOD SAVE! Long is very good at running the channels and gets in behind the Stoke defence as he latches onto a neat through ball. He unleashes a powerful strike from a tight angle and only strong hands from Butland pushes it to safety.
(13’) Stoke are looking to respond to going behind. Afellay advances towards the Southampton area, but Davis makes up vital ground to intercept and snuff out the danger.
--- 11’ Assist Davis provided a very inviting delivery for Pelle to attack. ---
--- 11’ Goal! SOUTHAMPTON LEAD!!! There is no denying Pelle this time! From the resulting corner, the Italian gets in between three Stoke defender to glance home Davis' delivery. That is his seventh Premier League goal of the season. ---
(10’) GOOD SAVE! Long whips the ball in from the left flank and Pelle rises to meet it in the area. His header is destined for the top corner, but Butland springs to tip it over.
(8’) The Britannia respond as the hosts launch a dangerous attack. Pieters delivers a deep cross into the penalty area which falls kindly for Afellay, who's shot is blocked and cleared by Southampton.
(6’) Interestingly, Mason refereed the reverse fixture in November, which Stoke won 1-0. He also took charge of the League Cup tie in the Last 16 of the 2014/15 season, sending off Peter Crouch as Southampton won 3-2.
(4’) Stoke have a free-kick inside their own half. They look to switch the play but it is cleverly read by Davis, who drives forward before looking to thread the ball into Long. The hosts recover the situation, though.

Goals on either side of half-time from Harry Kane see Spurs move to within two points of leaders Leicester, dealing a massive blow to the Villans' hopes of survival. Remi Garde's side did provide a bit of a late shock as they struck the frame of the goal three times, but that aside it was one of the most comfortable victories you'll ever see in the Premier League.

(90’) There will be three minutes added on at the end of this match.
--- 90’ Substitution Chadli replaces Lamela as Pochettino tries to run a bit more clock off as Tottenham show a few signs of vulnerability. ---
(88’) VILLA MISS ANOTHER SITTER! Gestede gets on the end of a corner, which he flicks on towards the far post. Lescott arrives to meet it, with Lloris stranded, but he sends it off the post and behind! It's quite remarkable to think that this game could actually be level has Villa not missed two sitters!
--- 86’ Substitution Spurs make their second change as Alli is replaced by Ryan Mason. It's mop-up duty for the substitute here, but it could have been a very different role for him had Villa taken their latest chance. ---

(82’) STAT: This is Villa's 20th league defeat of the season, equalling their previous worst tally of Premier League defeats in a single season (set in both of the past two years). They still have eight matches remaining in the campaign, though.
(80’) Tottenham will move to within two points of Leicester with the win today, though the Foxes can restore the five-point gap when they host Newcastle tomorrow. Spurs take on Bournemouth next, but it gets tricky after that as they have dates at Anfield, home to Manchester United, at Stoke and away to Chelsea in the five matches that follow (a home date with West Brom being the other).
--- 78’ Substitution Spurs make their first change with a little over 10 minutes remaining. Eriksen gets a deserved breather as Tom Carroll comes on in his stead. ---
(76’) This is resembling what you would see on the training ground, as Spurs are afforded time and space to pass the ball around in the attacking half and break down this Villa defence. The visitors aren't too eager to add to their lead, though, or this could have been much worse for the hosts.
(74’) A Villa goal would make for an exciting finish, but that doesn't even appear a remote possibility at this point. There's such little quality in this Villa team right now and Remi Garde can do little about that. It's one of the most comfortable two-goal leads you will ever see.
(72’) STAT: Tottenham Hotspur have lost just one of their last 13 Premier League away games (W7, D5, L1)
--- 70’ Substitution Villa's second change sees Scott Sinclair replace Carles gil. Perhaps the ex-City winger can provide a bit of directness and pace in attack as Villa try to claw their way back into the game - or at lease make for a nervy ending. ---
(68’) Play stops, although based on the tempo over the last five minutes it's hardly much of a drop-off, as Rose requires a bit of attention from the medical staff. He seems to have aggravated his ankle, but it's not looking like enough to force him off, either.
(66’) Spurs have a midweek fixture against Dortmund looming at the Lane, and it will be very interesting to see how they approach it. They got it all wrong on Thursday, and have dug quite a hole, but you have to wonder if they will try and turn it around in London with a very winable home fixture against Bournemouth to follow.
(64’) Villa aren't showing any ability to get out of their own end and keep the ball for more than a few seconds. Spurs aren't even pressing that hard to win it back, it's just all very poor from Villa's perspective.
--- 62’ Substitution Aston Villa give a Premier League debut to 17-year-old forward Andre Green, who replaces Veretout. It's a clear sign of what Villa are playing for at the moment - the 2016/17 season. ---
(60’) STAT: Tottenham have conceded just 12 goals in 14 Premier League away games this season, but kept just three clean sheets.
(58’) THUNDEROUS STRIKE! Walker is sprung down the right as Ayew doesn't show any interest in tracking the run of the full-back. He actually stops running and puts his head down. Walker takes advantage of the time and space, sending a ferocious strike at goal, but Guzan is on hand to beat it away.
(56’) The tempo has slowed drastically and it has become quite dull as Tottenham pass the ball around without any urgency in midfield. Villa aren't showing any intent of chasing the ball down, but out of nowhere the fans get on their feet and applaud their side. It's a terrific show of appreciation.
(54’) It's shaping up to be a case of how many, for Tottenham, as Villa start to sit back and let Spurs come at them. There's no fight in this side anymore, as they clearly have accepted their fate. It's a shame to see their Premier League life end this way.
(52’) This is a horror scene on repeat for Villa. They fall behind and utterly crumble as a team. It's not a characteristic of a side destined for success, and we can see how that translates with their position in the Premier League table. You could hear a pin drop at the moment at Villa Park.
(50’) STAT: Aston Villa have not won in 35 games when they concede the first goal.
--- 48’ Assist Alli registers his second assist of the afternoon with that delivery. ---

(46’) Back underway at Villa Park!
Harry Kane's goal just minutes before the break has alleviated Tottenham's frustrations as Villa are finally broken down in Birmingham. It couldn't have come at a better time for Spurs, while the resolve of Remi Garde's side will be tested now in the second half. How will they respond to falling behind so close to the interval?

(41’) STAT: Tottenham's next away defeat in the Premier League will be their 200th - only Newcastle United (201) have lost more on the road before this weekend.

(29’) STAT: Aston Villa's 16-point tally after 29 games this season is the third lowest at this stage of a Premier League season, but Leicester City only had three points more (19) at this stage last term and finished 14th.

(19’) STAT: Spurs have lost none of their last eight trips to Villa Park in all competitions (W6, D2).

(13’) You can really get a sense of what this game means to both teams. Their reasoning for needing the points may differ, but it's importance is equally high. (9’) There's a real sense of determination in this Tottenham team today. They're dominating in possession and causing Villa all sorts of problems at the back. Aston Villa are headed down without so much as a whimper. They were indifferent and languid as Manchester City ran them out of town last weekend, but despite their precarious position at the bottom of the table – nine points from safety – Remi Garde remains curiously optimistic. The Frenchman cited Leicester City’s timely resurgence at this same stage last season as reason for Villa fans not to lose all hope, but their on-field performance has been far less reassuring. They’ve won three of their first 29 league fixtures, and need to better that figure over their remaining nine to have any hope of survival.
Pochettino’s decision to rest many of his first-team regulars for their trip to Dortmund midweek is the perfect example of the chauvinistic nature which exists in the Premier League today – a microcosm for the recent struggles of English sides in Europe. Spurs were more concerned with a fixture with lowly Aston Villa than a European clash with one of the Bundesliga’s elite, and they paid dearly for their negligence. Such is the reality with the talent teams face weekly in the Premier League, and all will be forgotten should they secure three points as is expected of them this afternoon, but does the cost outweighed the potential benefits?

Pardew as made a host of changes from that side which left the Emirates with a point. Seven alterations to be precise. Wayne Hennessey, Scott Dann, Joel Ward, Joe Ledley, Jason Puncheon, Bolasie and Conor Wickham all make way, with Julian Speroni, Martin Kelly, Adrian Mariappa, Lee Chung-yong, Wilfried Zaha, Bakary Sako and Emmanuel Adebayor earning starts. In fact, Speroni will be making his first league start of the season today.
Palace themselves secured a commendable point at Arsenal at the weekend, with Yannick Bolasie stealing a point nine minutes from time. That result left them nine points clear of the drop zone with four matches to go. Of course they are not completely out of danger, but they are just one point from the fabled 40 mark - another year in the top flight almost certainly beckons.
Van Gaal has made three changes from the side who just barely overcame Aston Villa 1-0 on Saturday, a result which ultimately relegated the Birmingham club. Despite controlling things for much of the game, United struggled to see the game out and almost conceded a late equaliser when Rudy Gestede smashed against the post. Marcos Rojo, Marouane Fellaini and Memphis Depay are the ones to drop to the bench, with Matteo Darmian, Jesse Lingard and Anthony Martial coming into their respective places.
Manchester City's 1-1 draw with Newcastle United on Tuesday has aided United's chances, while successive league draws for Arsenal has seen their bid falter, with Manuel Pellegrini's men actually going above them - at least until tomorrow - in the table. A win for the home side today will take them within a point of the Gunners - who will have a game in hand - and their bitter cross-city rivals a further point ahead. The omens are on their side too, with Palace losing on each of their last eight visits to Old Trafford.
United's season has more or less been a constant quest to claim Champions League football for next or, at least it certainly has been since Christmas. Louis van Gaal's men have been a disappointment and, other than the early weeks of the campaign, have never looked like getting anywhere near their first title since Sir Alex Ferguson retired. They head into today's match with a solid chance of sneaking into the top four, but they are running out of time.

If the club are prepared to back him in the upcoming transfer window, as they did back in January, then he may well be able to build his squad into more than just relegation candidates come next season.
FULL TIME! SUNDERLAND ARE STAYING UP! It’s all over at the Stadium of Light, where Sam Allardyce’s side have dispatched a lacklustre Everton 3-0, courtesy of goals from Patrick van Aanholt and Lamine Kone, securing their Premier League status for next season and, in the process, relegating Norwich, who have beaten Watford 4-2 at Carrow Road this evening, along with north-east rivals and Allardyce’s former club Newcastle. What a night for the Black Cats, who have ensured their place in the top flight for a 10th consecutive season with the most comfortable of victories.
(90’) CROSSBAR! WHAT A MISS BY LUKAKU! The Everton man was unmarked in the six-yard box, but he could only hammer a half volley against the woodwork. Moments later, Mirallas gets in behind Sunderland’s defence and lifts an effort over Mannone, but it inches just wide.

(90’) FREE HEADER! That is awful from Osman, who after picking up acres of space in the area, latches onto a well-taken corner from Mirallas, but the long-time Everton midfielder can only direct his header well wide of the target.

(89’) The game is simply winding down now. with Sunderland’s support in celebratory mood, and understandably so!

(69’) A series of chances now for the visitors, as they search to inject some semblance of respectability back into the scoreless. First, Kone has to react sharply to volley the ball clear off the line following a header from Barry, before Baines’ long-range strike is well held by Mannone.
(68’) CHANCE! That’s a poor header from Funes Mori! The free-kick from Baines was a good one, and the aforementioned Argentine does well to rise highest and meet it with a header. However, rather than direct his effort back across the goal, he nods it straight at Mannone, who tips it wide.

(63’) Finally, Everton manage to forge a foray forward into Sunderland’s half, which results in a free-kick on the left. Baines drifts in the cross, but it soars high over the heads of everyone in the area, and Barry has to trek out to the touchline in order to recover it.
(61’) Sunderland are rampant at the moment, and so they should be. Bar a near-miracle, you cannot see a way back into this game for Everton, who are simply inviting more and more pressure on themselves as it stands.
(58’) CHANCE! Sunderland should be 4-0 up! First, Baines rescues Everton with a fantastic tackle in the area before, from the next attack, Khazri beats the offside trap. --- 55’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!!! KONE MAKES IT 3-0!! Surely it is all over now!? Awful defending from Everton once more as, from the resulting corner, Robles parries Khazri’s cross into the back of McCarthy. (53’) Almost! That’s unfortunate for Sunderland, as Cattermole picks up possession in the middle of the park and immediately looks to set Defoe away with a precise throughball. (51’) STAT FLASH - The last time Sunderland lost in the Premier League after being 2-0 up at half-time was in April 2001 (v Spurs).
(49’) CLOSE! How did that not go in? Sunderland win a corner down the left, which Khazri curls in. The cross is a decent one, and Kirchoff gets on the end of it, but he fails to make a solid connection with his header and can only glance his effort wide.
(47’) CHANCE! An early opportunity for Everton, as Baines clips a floated cross to the back post from a free-kick on the right wing. Though on target, his header lacked power, and Mannone is able to get across and make a comfortable save.

However, if the result stays as it is at the Stadium of Light, then it the outcome at Carrow Road will be irrelevant, and both Norwich and Newcastle shall be relegated.
Everton started promisingly, but for all their possession they failed to muster a single effort on target as Sunderland began to edge their way back into the game, and the hosts duly took a deserved lead when, in the 38th minute, Van Aanholt curled a free-kick around the visitors’ poorly organised wall. However, Robles should have still made an easy save, but for some reason the Spaniard elected to move to his left, and the strike nestled into the back of the net. Allardyce’s side continued to press as their manager urged them to take advantage of the Toffees’ shaky defence, and they swiftly had their reward when Kone drilled in from close-range with a venomous volley.
HALF TIME! Well, that’s it for the first half at the Stadium of Light, where two strikes in the space of four minutes from Patrick van Aanholt and Lamine Kone have put Sunderland on the verge of Premier League survival!
(45’) What an end to the first half this has been for Sunderland, who are all in control now and, as it stands, staying up. There will be a minimum of two minutes stoppage time before half-time is called...
--- 42’ Assist Everton’s defending from that corner was a complete shambles, and Baines’ header was poor one. However, M’Vila did well to keep the attack alive, and is rewarded for his efforts with an assist. ---
--- 42’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAALLLLLLL!!! SUNDERLAND DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! What a strike that is to make it 2-0 to the hosts! Khazri whips in the resulting corner following Robles’ save, but a poor header from Baines allows M’Vila to nod the ball back into the area. It looks to be dropping in the six-yard box but, instead, Kone takes on the volley from over his shoulder and proceeds to thump the ball past the Everton goalkeeper and high into the roof of the net! Sunderland 2-0 Everton! ---
(41’) SAVE! Well, he may have been at fault for the opener, but Robles has made up slightly for that error with a superb stop to prevent Defoe, who had connected with Khazri’s free-kick, converting with a powerful header.
--- 38’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLL!!!!! SUNDERLAND TAKE THE LEAD! That is quite terrible goalkeeping from Robles, but the home fans do not care as they are sent into raptures as Van Aanholt curls a strike through the Everton wall. The visitors’ shot-stopper initially looked well-placed to make the save, but he inexplicably side-stepped to his left, allowing the shot to sail past him and into the back of the net! ---
(37’) Free-kick! A real opportunity now for Sunderland, as Funes Mori fouls Defoe 25 yards out from Everton’s goal, just right of centre. Van Aanholt and Khazri stand over the set-piece…
(35’) The game has taken a slight lull now, as Everton manage to get back on the ball for a spell and dictate the tempo. A slip from Funes Mori almost allows the hosts in, but Stones covers for his partner and crisply drills a pass into the feet of Barkley. Unfortunately for the visitors, the England man cannot sort his feet out quickly enough, and Kone is able to make the tackle.
(32’) STAT FLASH - Sunderland have netted just six goals in their last 10 Premier League home matches against Everton while, before joining the Black Cats, Defoe only scored three goals in 17 Premier League games against Everton.
(30’) Great work from Kaboul! That’s top defending from the experienced Frenchman who, after Lukaku had kick-started an Everton counter with a driving run into Sunderland’s half, gets across to nick possession ahead of Mirallas - proceeding to sprint out from the back and eventually winning a free-kick after been taken down unceremoniously by Barry.
(28’) Sunderland are starting to dominate territory somewhat now, with Everton now restricted to infrequent counter-attacks. From one of these breaks, Cleverley dinks an inviting pass over the top into the path of Mirallas, but the ball is just slightly overhit and Mannone is out quickly to intercept it.
(25’) News in now from other fixture that matters to the relegation scrap this evening, and it is that, after initially going a goal down early on, Norwich are now leading 2-1 in their fixture with Watford. It means, as it stands, the Canaries are dragging themselves to within two points of Sunderland and level with Newcastle.
(23’) WHAT AN EFFORT! That’s dreadful defending from Everton but, in equal measure, it would have been a spectacular solo goal from Kaboul had the centre-back netted with that strike. The defender found himself in space down the left, somehow weaving his way around Pennington and Stones before hammering a shot goalwards. Robles is beaten, but fortunately for the visitors the ball flashes across the face of goal.
(21’) One of the major complaints from Everton’s fans about Martinez’s style of play is the Spaniard’s obsession with retaining possession at all costs - sometimes to the detriment of his side, with his players all too often taking unnecessary risks in order to try and play the ball out from the back. However, Funes Mori did not gamble on this occasion as, in a foot-race with Defoe, he does well to hook the ball out of play and into the crowd.
(19’) CHANCE! Sunderland win a corner down on the right, which Khazri whips in, but the Toffees manage to claw it clear. However, the hosts quickly work it back into the former Bordeaux winger, who curls in an inviting cross which Kaboul meets, but the former Tottenham defender is unable to generate enough power on his header to trouble Robles.
(16’) The hosts are pressing out from defence, now, as the game starts to open up slightly following that positive start from the visitors. A long pass from Cleverley is latched onto by Lukaku, but Kone does well to clear the danger and kick-start a counter. Defoe swiftly takes over, looking to drive into the area, but Stones comes across to make a well-timed block.
(14’) RISKY! That’s woeful play from Funes Mori, who almost gifts Sunderland a goal as he plays an under-hit back pass towards Robles which Defoe almost pounces on. Fortunately for the Argentina defender, his goalkeeper gets him out of jail by making a timely clearance.
(12’) The crowd are becoming frustrated now, as Sunderland conceded more and more territory to Martinez’s side, who have seen 70 per-cent of the possession so far in this game. The counter looks on momentarily as Kirchoff dispossess McCarthy, but the German can only find a blue shirt with his resulting pass and the visitors are able to maintain their pressure.
(9’) CLOSE! That’s neat and tidy play from the visitors, who are getting into their stride a bit now. A smart pass from Baines picks out Barkley down the left, with the playmaker swiftly turning the ball back into Barry, who lofts a cross into the path of Pennington. The defender had made a good run into the Sunderland area, and did well to win the header above Van Aanholt, but his effort sails just wide.
(7’) Everton have done well so far just to take the sting out of the game, with the Merseysiders retaining possession well and thus preventing Sunderland being able to lodge any meaningful moves forward.
(5’) Sloppy play from both sides now, as Stones concedes possession to Cattermole, who almost immediately gives it back to Barkley. The England midfield looks to turn his man and drive goalwards, but he is swiftly scythed down by the aforementioned Sunderland midfielder, who is perhaps fortunate to escape a booking for his rather reckless challenge.
(3’) A bit of a tactical change it seems for Martinez, with youngster Pennington starting at right-back rather than Stones, who is lining-up alongside Funes Mori in the centre-back positions. It has been a positive start from the visitors, as Lukaku and Barkley combine before the latter slips a neat throughball into the path of Mirallas, but the Belgian had strayed offside and the move is halted abruptly.
(1’) KICK OFF! We’re underway at the Stadium of Light, with Everton getting proceedings up and running.
We’re just moments away from kick off now in this massive fixture, and the teams are making their way out onto the pitch now, in front of what is a full-house at the Stadium of Light. The referee this evening is Anthony Taylor.
Despite the poor form of their opposition, Sunderland manager Allardyce is taking nothing for granted, and has claimed in the build-up to this evening’s fixture that he expects a reaction from Martinez’s side. A strong start will be key for the hosts, especially if they are to capitalise on Everton’s well-documented defensive frailties. The Toffees’ have performed well on the road for much of this campaign, having lost just four of their 18 Premier League games away from Goodison.

As for Everton, Martinez makes three amendments in total from the aforementioned defeat against Leicester. At the back, Ramiro Funes Mori has returned from his three-match suspension to take the place of Bryan Oviedo, with John Stones switching over to right-back. In midfield, Gareth Barry has overcome injury to return alongside James McCarthy, with Oumar Niasse dropping out and Tom Cleverley pushing up to the left of an advanced midfield three. For his well-take consolation strike on Saturday, Belgium winger Kevin Mirallas is rewarded with a starting berth on the right - with Aaron Lennon on the bench. Romelu Lukaku, without a Premier League goal since March 5 and without a strike in any competition since his brace against Chelsea in the FA Cup quarter-finals, starts up top.

The 33-year-old, who also netted at Goodison in the aforementioned reverse fixture, again leads the line for the hosts this evening, with former Liverpool forward Fabio Borini and the talented but inconsistent Wahbi Khazri providing support from the wings. In midfield, former Bayern Munich man Jan Kirchoff continues to be deployed in a deep-lying role, sandwiched in between Lee Cattermole and Yann M’Vila while, at the back, Lamine Kone has overcome the knock that saw him substituted off at the weekend to continue his fledgling partnership with Younes Kabul.

The teams are in from Wearside. Without further ado, let’s check on the full line ups, starting off with the hosts who, unsurprisingly, are unchanged from the side that started the 3-2 victory over Chelsea - and the same starting XI that has featured in the last six fixtures.
So, for the evening at least, Newcastle fans are firmly in the Everton camp as they hope and pray Martinez can turn his side’s form around in time to allow the Magpies one last shot at Premier League survival. Fellow strugglers Norwich, who incidentally travel to Goodison Park on Sunday, are also playing this evening, as they take on Watford at home.
To say Roberto Martinez’s position as Everton manager is under threat would be an understatement. The Toffees, who slumped to a 3-1 defeat against newly-crowned champions Leicester City last time out, have claimed just one victory from their last nine Premier League fixtures, and were also dumped out of the FA Cup semi-finals by Anthony Martial’s last-gasp winner for Manchester United. The run - which also included a humiliating 4-0 defeat in the Merseyside derby - has led to large-scale disillusionment amongst much of the Everton faithful, and despite the club’s board having not issued a statement either way, it seems almost certain that they will look to replace the Spaniard at the end of the season. However, recent history is on the visitors’ side heading into tonight’s clash, with Sunderland having claimed just one home victory from their last 10 meetings with the Merseysiders at the Stadium of Light.
Sunderland sit in 17th heading into this fixture - their penultimate match of the campaign. Courtesy of their dramatic comeback victory over Chelsea last time out, Sam Allardyce’s side sit one point ahead of local rivals Newcastle United having played a game less, and four ahead of 19th-placed Norwich City. And though the Black Cats, who have only lost one of their last nine Premier League games, were hammered 6-2 in the reverse fixture back in November, they will be confident of sealing the points needed to secure survival against an out of form Everton.

Christian Benteke's 92nd minute equaliser helps the Reds avoid defeat in their final match of the season at Anfield, cancelling out Eden Hazard's first-half opener. It wasn't one of the more memorable nights on Merseyside as it so often is when these two face off, but Benteke was sure to provide a bit of drama as Liverpool extend their unbeaten run at home in the Premier League to eight games.

Tottenham have lost just one of their last seven Premier League games against the Gunners at White Hart Lane, while Wenger's men have scored exactly one goal in each of their last six league games away at Spurs and each of the last four trips to face their rivals. Arsenal can take some heart from the fact that they have actually already won at the Lane this season in the League Cup, but they haven't managed to win two games there in the one season in 30 years.
One very interesting question that is raised this afternoon is just who needs the victory more today, Tottenham or Arsenal? Pochettino's outfit are facing their best opportunity to go for the title in many a year and are further motivated by the prospect of finishing above their rivals, whereas Wenger continues come under increased scrutiny in his role as boss due to the recent dire performances, so will he fear for his job should his charges lose at White Hart Lane today?
The last clash between Tottenham and Arsenal was a typically tense and entertaining affair, taking place at the start of November at the Emirates. Spurs looked primed to claim derby glory when Harry Kane gave them the lead 32 minutes in, but their hearts were broken just 13 minutes from time when an unlikely hero popped up from the bench for the hosts in the form of Kieran Gibbs, who netted to ensure the points were shared at 1-1.
Gunners fans have a right to be worried as they are coming up against a Tottenham side who, up until midweek, were unbeaten in seven league matches. The impressive run for Spurs saw them shoot right up the table into second place, but accusations of anxiety came at them a few days ago when they passed up the opportunity to go top of the table when they went down to London rivals, West Ham, in a 1-0 loss at the Boleyn Ground.
Arsenal are by no means faltering compared to Spurs disastrously, though, as a win for them today would see them go level on points with Pochettino's outfit. Indeed, it is more their recent run of form which has catalysed a cause for concern amongst fans, as they have lost their last three matches in all competitions - against Barcelona in the Champions League, and two league defeats against a patched up Manchester United side and relegation candidates, Swansea. They have not lost four on the bounce in 14 years.
Since Arsene Wenger took charge of the Gunners in 1996, Tottenham have never finished above Arsenal in the Premier League and have more or less lived in the shadows of their city rivals. However, the signs are this season that this trend could soon be broken, as Spurs continue to impress under the tutelage of Mauricio Pochettino, who currently has his side placed in second behind surprise leaders, Leicester. Arsenal are three points behind in third.
Is the balance of power starting to shift in North London? Today's derby presents potentially the most crucial encounter between the two arch rivals in the Premier League era as it is not only bragging rights up for grabs, but desperately needed points as both outfits battle alongside Leicester and Manchester City to earn the spot as champions of England.
