The team sheets are in from Goodison, and there’s certainly some interesting news for Everton fans as Martinez attempts to amend their poor home form with a quite radical change. John Stones - who made his return to a action as a second-half substitute against Aston Villa following a spell out with injury, comes into the side in what looks to be a back three, with Gareth Barry, one of the Toffees’ stand-out performers this term, dropping down to the bench, where he is also joined by the returning Muhammed Besic following his injury lay-off. As for the visitors, their victory over Tottenham came at a price, with James Collins picking up a hamstring strain. He is replaced by youngster Reece Oxford in what is the only change by Bilic.
On the other hand, the Hammers have been in superb form as of late, with the fantastic, hard-fought win over Tottenham put them into a fantastic position to mount a serious charge on the top four in the final ten games of the campaign. Like their hosts, they have lost just twice since in the league since the turn of the year, though they have managed five victories opposed to Everton’s three. As mentioned, however, their form against the Toffees has left a lot to be desired - with the East London outfit having being beaten 22 times by the Merseysiders in the Premier League era - while their recent away form has seen them claim just one win from their last nine Premier League fixtures on the road.
After a tricky spell of form in the run around the festive period, the Toffees have turned it around somewhat since the turn of the year. Since their League Cup semi-final loss to Manchester City at the Etihad towards the end of January, Martinez has guided his side to five victories from six games in all competitions - scoring 14 goals and conceding just twice in the process. The sole defeat in that run, against West Brom in their last fixture at Goodison, stalled their momentum however, and it is what sees the Merseysiders - who have managed just a measly four Premier League victories from their last 16 home matches - in the bottom half heading into today’s game. All hope is not lost, though, as they sit just four points behind seventh-placed Stoke City, and they have won 10 and lost none of their last 15 top-flight meetings with West Ham.

The Frenchman breaks towards the edge of the penalty area before trying to find Sinclair with a low cross into the middle of the box, but Kompany, who has had little to deal with today, is there to comfortably cut out the danger.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(88’) Villa try to push forward on a rare foray into the City half of the pitch as they work their way down the right flank, but, understandably, there's no urgency in their attacking move and they are quickly dispossessed by the hosts' hard-working defence before they can cause their opponents any problems.
(86’) City almost make it 5-0! Clichy picks up the ball in acres of space on the left-hand side of the penalty area and immediately fires a great low cross over towards the far post. It flies past every yellow shirt inside the box but there are no blue shirts there to meet it either, much to the frustration of the Frenchman.
(84’) Navas is continuing to give Cissokho plenty of problems down the right wing, and the Frenchman doesn't seem to have learnt his lesson from earlier. As a result, the Spaniard is left in far too much space on the right-hand side of the penalty area and is able to fire a low cross into the box, but Guzan does well to cut out the danger at the near post.
(82’) Sagna, who has spent the vast majority of the game camped deep inside the Villa half of the pitch due to the visitors' attacking struggles, finds himself with the ball at his feet 30 yards away from goal after good play by Clichy on the left flank. The right-back immediately unleashes a rocket of a strike towards goal, but it's completely overhit and fails to trouble Guzan.
--- 80’ Substitution Meanwhile, Garde has brought on Sinclair to replace Ayew for Villa. ---
--- 80’ Substitution Toure receives a rousing round of applause from the City fans as he's replaced by Garcia in the hosts' final change of the game. ---
(78’) Once again, Navas cuts inside from the right flank and runs rings around Cissokho, who has really struggled against the Spaniard during the second half. He then cuts the ball back to Aguero, who is in a good position in front of goal, but the Argentine is quickly cut down by Gueye before he is able to unleash a shot.
(76’) City work the ball around well before setting up Iheanacho, who finds himself in a pocket of space outside of the Villa penalty area. He takes a quick touch before unleashing a thumping strike, but it ends up flying just over the top of the crossbar.
--- 74’ Substitution Veretout makes his way off to be replaced by Bacuna in Villa's second substitution. ---
--- 73’ Missed penalty MISS! Aguero has the perfect opportunity to wrap up his hat-trick, but he ends up firing a thumping low strike into the post and out to the right wing. Guzan had dived the right way as well, and he most likely would have saved the effort even if it was sent a yard or so to the left. ---
(72’) PENALTY! Ihenacho twists and turns inside the Villa box as he tries to beat Clark, and he skips past the centre-back with ease before being clumsily tripped to the ground, leaving the referee with no choice but to point to the spot. The visitors' nightmare refuses to end...
--- 70’ Substitution Meanwhile, Villa have made a change as well, with Gestede coming on to replace the ineffectual Agbonlahor. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Silva receives a standing ovation from the City fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Iheanacho. ---
(68’) What do Villa do now? That's the question that Garde must be asking himself as he watches his side get torn apart. City are continuing to push forward and are thoroughly enjoying themselves whenever they're able to get into advanced positions, which, at the moment, is all of the time. Things could end up getting even worse for the visitors if they're not careful...
--- 66’ Assist Navas did well to skip past Cissokho before firing his cross towards the back post, but there was little pace on the pass and it really should have been dealt with by the Villa defenders. However, they all fell asleep and made no attempt to get near the ball, making life incredibly easy for Sterling. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOAL! It's now 4-0! Navas cuts into the right-hand side of the Villa penalty area before cutting a low pass across the face of goal. It comfortably flies past every yellow shirt before finding Sterling at the back post, and, under no pressure whatsoever, the youngster is easily able to tap the ball into the back of the net from close range. This is turning into a nightmare for the visitors... ---
(65’) City work the ball around quickly inside the Villa penalty area, with Aguero, Silva and Sterling playing important roles in the move. The latter then cuts the ball back to Toure, who looks to shoot but is unable to do so due to the pressure put on him by a group of three players, who close him down quickly.
(63’) Chance for Sterling! The youngster is immediately involved in the action as he picks up the ball inside the left-hand side of the penalty area. He then unleashes a thumping strike towards the roof of the net, but Guzan does well to push it over the top of the crossbar with a great save.
--- 62’ Substitution Bony, who has had a difficult afternoon, makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Sterling for the final half an hour of the game. ---
--- 60’ Assist After a slightly quiet first half, Silva has burst into life and is now running riot inside the Villa half of the pitch. Both he and Aguero are exhibiting a wonderful understanding, and it's proving to be very difficult for the visitors' back line to deal with. ---
--- 60’ Goal! GOAL! Things have gone from bad to worse for Villa! Aguero and Silva combine wonderfully down the left flank, with the Spaniard teeing up the Argentine with a beautiful chip over Hutton and Richards, both of whom were caught ball-watching. The striker then darts into the penalty area before firing a low shot that flies past the outstretched arm of Guzan and into the bottom left-hand corner of the net to extend City's comfortable lead. ---
(58’) Navas breaks down the right flank and cuts inside before teeing up Aguero on the edge of the penalty area. The Argentine immediately unleashes a thumping, first-time volley, but Lescott dives in front of the striker to stop it from troubling Guzan.
(56’) A half-hearted City attacking move breaks down, and Villa immediately fly forward on a quick counter-attack down the left wing. Ayew does well to skip past Kompany, who is beaten far too easily, before cutting inside and heading towards the penalty area, but Otamendi stops the Ghanaian's run with an excellent sliding tackle.
(54’) City patiently pass the ball around deep inside the Villa half of the pitch before Silva tries to tee up Bony on the edge of the penalty area, but just as the Ivorian is about to make contact with it Gueye dives in front to cut out the danger at the vital moment.
(52’) It's been a miserable start to the second half for Villa, who defended so resolutely during the opening 45 minutes but now have a mountain to climb if they are to come away with anything. It looks as if it could get even more difficult for them, as City are continuing to fly forward in search of further goals.
--- 50’ Goal! GOAL! City have doubled their lead! Bony picks up the ball just outside of the Villa penalty area and quickly sends a lovely through-ball into the path of Aguero, who darts into the box but is beaten to the ball by Richards. However, he sends his sliding clearance straight into the thigh of the Argentine, and the ball then loops over the diving body of Guzan and into the back of the net. It's all gone wrong for the visitors! ---
--- 48’ Assist Silva did well to pick out Toure with his quick cut-back but the Villa defence should have done better in the build-up, as Cissokho was beaten far too easily by Aguero before the aforementioned Ivorian was left in too much space inside the penalty area, something that they didn't let happen during the first half. ---
--- 48’ Goal! GOAL! City have taken the lead! Villa are unable to fully clear the danger from the corner, and the hosts quickly come back once again. Aguero cuts inside from the right wing and beats Cissokho before cutting the ball back to Silva, who then quickly works it over to Toure. Camped on the penalty spot, the Ivorian is completely unmarked, and he's easily able to tap the ball off the leg of Richards and into the back of the net. ---
(47’) Navas flies past Cissokho on the right wing and heads towards the byline before looking to send a cross into the penalty area, but the Frenchman does wonderfully well to dart back and dispossess the Spaniard before poking the ball out for a corner.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
It's been an incredibly frustrating opening 45 minutes for the hosts, who have dominated possession deep inside their opponents' half of the pitch but have continually struggled to find a way past Villa's resolute and well-organised back line. The visitors have offered little going forward but have defended excellently, with Lescott putting in a particularly strong performance in the centre of defence to frustrate his former employers on several occasions. As a result, Aguero and Bony have found it very difficult to carve out chances on goal, with latter looking particularly rusty.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 ASTON VILLA
(45’) City come back once again as they desperately try to find a goal before half-time. Another long ball forward in fired into the Villa penalty area, where it finds Aguero in front of goal, but the striker is quickly put under pressure by Clark and ends up firing his close-range strike well wide of its intended target.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
--- 45’ Yellow card Bony and Aguero link up well deep inside the Villa half of the pitch before the latter is clipped on the ankle by the Frenchman, resulting in a yellow card for the midfielder and a free-kick for City. It's taken quickly and launched into the left-hand side of the penalty area, where it finds Kompany, but the captain is unable to pick a teammate with his header across goal. ---
(43’) Once again Navas fires a dangerous cross into the middle of the penalty area after doing well to beat Cissokho, but Lescott is there to cut out the danger with a vital interception. The former City defender has been in excellent form thus far and has arguably been their most important player.
(41’) City work the ball down the right wing before Navas tries to swing a cross into the Villa penalty area, but it's underhit and fails to beat Cissokho. The wing-back then cynically pushes the Spaniard to the ground and gives away a needless free-kick as a result. It's flung into the middle of the box, where there is a group of blue shirts waiting patiently, but Lescott beats them all to the ball and heads it away from danger.
(39’) Ayew and Kompany clash midway inside the Villa half of the pitch, and the referee awards a free-kick to City on the right wing. Toure swings a cross towards the edge of the penalty area, where it finds the head of Bony, but the striker's attempt on goal ends up looping straight into the hands of Guzan.
(37’) Hutton loses the ball in a dangerous position, allowing City to fly forward on a quick counter-attack down the left flank. Aguero cuts inside before sending the ball out to Fernandinho, who is in space on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The Brazilian then cuts a pass back to Bony, but it's sent slightly behind the Ivorian and, as a result, he's unable to get a decent shot away.
(35’) After a determined City attacking move breaks down, Villa immediately break away on a quick counter-attack through the middle of the pitch. They initially get forward well through Ayew, who then works the ball out to the left, but the visitors take far too long with the attack and allow the hosts to get plenty of bodies back to snuff out the danger with ease.
(33’) Another dangerous cross is flung into the Villa penalty area from the left flank, but this time it's Clark who thumps the ball out for a corner with a vital volleyed clearance. The resulting set-piece is curled right on to the head of Bony, but the striker's attempt on goal is poor and Guzan is able to watch the effort sail comfortably wide of the goal.
(31’) City work the ball from right to left as they try to penetrate the Villa penalty area. Clichy eventually finds himself in a pocket of space deep down the left flank and takes the opportunity to swing a cross into the box. It bounces off Otamendi before finding Aguero in front of goal, but, under pressure from three yellow shirts, he's unable to get a shot away and the ball ends up bouncing into the hands of Guzan.
(29’) The pace of the game has slowed down somewhat over the past few minutes, and City aren't looking quite as sharp as they were earlier in the clash. Villa are now enjoying their fair share of possession and are patiently passing the ball around as they try to find a way through the hosts' compact defensive line.
(27’) Hart is finally called into action! City are unable to get the ball away from their own penalty area as they're put under pressure by a determined attack from Villa. The visitors continue to press forward before the ball eventually bounces over to Ayew on the right-hand side of the box, but the Ghanaian's thumping strike is tipped round the near post by an excellent diving save by the hosts' goalkeeper.
(25’) Aguero goes close! The Argentine and Bony play beautiful one-touch football on the edge of the Villa penalty area as they work the ball between a sea of yellow shirts. The former Atletico Madrid man then fires a brilliant low shot that beats the outstretched arm of Guzan, but it ends up flying into the side-netting rather than the back of the net.
(23’) It just doesn't seem to be working for City, who, after starting so brightly, are starting to struggle to find joy inside the final third of the pitch. Villa have every available body camped behind the ball and, as a result, life has become incredibly difficult for the determined hosts.
(21’) It's all City at the moment as they keep pushing deep into the Villa half of the pitch. Silva weaves his way towards the edge of the penalty area before cutting the ball back to Toure, who is in a pocket of space 25 yards away from goal. The Ivorian then tries to beat Guzan with a thumping shot, but it's overhit and sails comfortably over the top of the crossbar.
(20’) Richards clatters into Silva and sends his former teammate crashing to the ground, resulting in a free-kick for City 30 yards away from goal. It's taken short and sent to Fernandinho, but the set-piece is poorly executed and the Brazilian's tame long-range strike ends up deflection off the wall of yellow shirts in front of him and out for a throw-in on the right wing.
(19’) Another chance for Aguero! The Argentine cuts inside from the left wing and plays a quick one-two with Toure on the edge of the Villa penalty area. The striker immediately unleashes a rocket of a strike with his first-time shot from just inside the box, but once again Guzan does wonderfully well to push it away from danger with an acrobatic diving save.
(17’) Aguero and Lescott battle for the ball inside the Villa penalty area before the latter nods it out for a corner, which, again, the visitors deal with well. City come back again quickly, however, and Sagna penetrates the left-hand side of the box, but he's unable to pick out a teammate with his attempted low cross.
(15’) What a golden opportunity for Bony! Aguero is left in far too much space on the left flank, allowing him to dart down the wing on a marauding run. He then curls a beautiful cross into the middle of the Villa box, where it finds the aforementioned Ivorian in front of goal, but he completely mishits his first-time shot and scuffs it comfortably wide of its intended target. He really should have done better with that chance!
(13’) City win themselves another corner, but once again Villa have enough bodies back to comfortably deal with the danger. They then break away on a blisteringly quick counter-attack down the right wing through Hutton, who, after running into a cul-de-sac of blue shirts, ends up spinning and teeing up Ayew. The Ghanaian then blasts a cross into the penalty area and towards Agbonlahor, but Hart is there to cut out the danger on the edge of the six-yard box.
(12’) What a save by Guzan! Lescott's tackle results in a corner that is curled into the heart of the Villa penalty area. It initially fails to trouble the visitors before the ball bounces over to Aguero at the far post, and he skips past Cissokho before unleashing a thumping strike. It looks set for the top left-hand corner of the net, but the American goalkeeper does wonderfully well to tip it over the top of the crossbar.
(11’) Excellent tackle by Lescott! Aguero embarks on a wonderful run as he weaves through a sea of Villa players before penetrating and looking to shoot, but just as he's about to he's dispossessed by a great interception by the former City centre-back, who timed that to perfection.
(9’) Richards almost becomes the first player to receive a yellow card, but the referee decides to give the former City defender a stern talking to instead. He had clattered into the back of Aguero with a poorly-timed sliding challenge that sent the striker flying, and he was very lucky not to get booked as a result.
(7’) Villa immediately break forward on a quick counter-attack through Hutton, who takes City by surprise with an excellent run down the right wing. He skips past both Aguero and Kompany with ease before heading into the right-hand side of the hosts' penalty area, but he has no one up there to support him and he ends up conceding a goal-kick after a clearance from Clichy deflects off his ankle and out of play.
(6’) Sagna breaks down the right flank before sending a lovely through-ball past Veretout and into the path of Bony. The striker meets it well next to the byline before Cissokho pokes the ball out for a corner, but the set-piece fails to trouble Villa and they are easily able to deal with the danger.
(4’) Bony loses the ball in the middle of the pitch, allowing Ayew to pick up possession before breaking forward. He's quickly shoved in the back by Kompany, and the referee decides to award Villa a free-kick near to the halfway line. It's flung up towards the edge of the City box, where it finds Agbonlahor, but the striker is unable to direct his header towards a teammate and it ends up bouncing over to Silva on the left wing.
(2’) After spending the opening two minutes sitting deep inside their own half of the pitch as City patiently pass the ball around, Villa are finally able to push forward on their first meaningful attack of the game. Veretout initially does well to skip down the left wing before trying to cut towards the penalty area, but Otamendi is there to cut out the danger with a well-timed interception.
(1’) And we're off! City get us underway, attacking from left to right.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, Villa boss Remi Garde has decided to make just one alteration to the side that featured in Tuesday’s defeat away to Everton, with Leandro Bacuna making way for Jordan Veretout in midfield.
Manuel Pellegrini has decided to make three changes to the City side that were beaten by Liverpool on Wednesday evening, with Bacary Sagna, Yaya Toure and Wilfried Bony coming into the starting line-up to replace Pablo Zabaleta, Fernando and Raheem Sterling, respectively.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
As for Villa, three straight defeats of their own - including a 6-0 thrashing at the hands of Liverpool - has left them languishing at the bottom of the table and with very little hope of pulling off what would surely be the greatest of escapes over the final two months of the season. The Birmingham-based club have struggled all campaign and are just about managing to hold on to their Premier League status by the skin of their teeth, but if results don’t improve soon then their drop to the second tier could be confirmed in little over a month’s time. Wins against fellow strugglers Crystal Palace and Norwich City were high points but positives have been hard to come by for Remi Garde’s men, who have picked up just three points from their last five games. This afternoon’s clash is set to be just as difficult as for them, as they must face a team that they have managed to beat just once in their last 11 league meetings, whilst the last encounter involving the two sides, January’s FA Cup fourth-round tie at Villa Park, ended in an easy 4-0 victory for City.
It’s been a strange 10-day period for City, one that has been characterised by euphoric highs and crushing lows in equal measure. Last weekend’s Capital One Cup final victory and a strong performance against Dynamo Kiev the previous week had brought feelings of excitement and confidence to the Etihad, but their poor form in the Premier League is a cause for concern that has left fans scratching their heads in frustration. Wednesday’s lacklustre performance against Liverpool resulted in an easy 3-0 win for the Reds, and with it extended the Citizens’ league losing run to three games, their worst since 2007. As a result, Manuel Pellegrini’s men will be well aware that their chances of winning the title are slim, to say the least, as 10 points currently separate them and high-flying Leicester City heading into today’s games. However, this afternoon’s clash against the division’s bottom side brings with it a great opportunity to bounce back with a convincing win, and it is one that last season’s runners-up desperately need to grab with both hands if they are to avoid slipping further down the table.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Manchester City and Aston Villa at the Etihad Stadium.

FULL TIME! Bournemouth edge their way to a 3-1 victory over Newcastle, with the hosts finding themselves submerged in the relegation mire. Goals from King and Daniels were enough for the visitors, with Taylor opening the scoring with an own goal. Ayoze made things interesting late on, but it's three more important points for the Cherries. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.

--- 89’ Yellow card Grabban picks up a late booking, with the Englishman definitely getting heavily involved since entering the field of play. ---
(88’) Just wide from Wijnaldum! The Netherlands international is fed in behind enemy lines by Ayoze, with a wicked deflection taking the ball just shy of the near post. Boruc was entirely wrongfooted. So nearly an equaliser.

Narrowly over five minutes are left on the clock, with time running out slightly for the Magpies. The Newcastle goalkeeper is asked to make another save moments later, with Pugh denied at the near post.
(82’) We're into the final 10 minutes now, with Bournemouth facing a nervy end to this contest. All that Newcastle need to do is keep probing for an opening, with any openings easily exploitable by the deep-lying presence of Shelvey.

(72’) We're into the final 20 minutes at St. James' Park, with Newcastle having a veritable mountain to climb now. Two goals is a big ask, considering that Boruc hasn't had any very tough stops to make. Howe's men can afford to sit back and pick their moments to get forward.
--- 70’ Assist Ritchie slides a neat pass into his teammate, but King contributes the finishing touches. ---

Bournemouth then counter, but a cross from King skids across the danger zone and clear.

(63’) Mitrovic turns on the edge of the penalty area, before unleashing an excellent effort! The ball swerves and dips just beyond the far post, with Boruc looking very worried indeed. Newcastle need more of the same if they are to turn this scoreline around.

Shelvey loses out on possession in a dangerous area, before King is denied by a smart block from Lascelles. The ex-Blackburn Rovers winger had driven into a dangerous area, but was well denied.
(48’) Newcastle get hold of the ball from the offer, with Sissoko fed down the right-hand side. The France international cuts a great pass towards the penalty spot, but Wijnaldum gets his feet in a tangle and the chance disappears. Bournemouth counter, but Gradel shoots well wide.

(46’) We are back underway in the second half! The Magpies are trailing, but there's plenty of time for the hosts to turn things around. First of all, however, they'll have to disrupt Bournemouth's calm and tidy use of possession.

The away side have had much more possession, but the Magpies have had a couple of late chances in the half. McClaren's boys need to come out firing after the interval.
(45’) We're into the first of two minutes of stoppage time.

Bournemouth keep their pressure on, with Afobe going down in the box under pressure from Colback. The referee rightly doesn't point to the spot.
(35’) King sprints down the right-hand side and looks to use his pace, but Lascellas has the legs to keep up and then slide in to dispossess the Norway international. The former Forest centre-back has looked confident during the opening half hour or so.
(33’) The Cherries are unafraid to go all the way back to their goalkeeper, with Bournemouth willing to take their time. Afobe is the target of a quick ball into feet, but the Englishman fails to take a sturdy first touch. Lascelles mops up the scraps.
--- 31’ Substitution Anita comes into the fray for the home side, with McClaren opting to make a technical change on the half-hour mark. Dummett jogs off prematurely. ---
(30’) Bournemouth threaten again almost instantly, but Elliot is quick off his line to gobble up a slightly heavy throughball. The away side now have something to defend, which suits their calm and patient possession brilliantly. Newcastle will have to keep chasing and working hard.
--- 28’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! TAYLOR PRODS HOME AN OWN GOAL! King looks to squeeze a cross in from the left-hand side, with the English defender drawn into trying to deflect a clearance away from danger. Instead, the ball skims off the Newcastle man, before sliding in between a wrongfooted Elliot and the near post! ---
(28’) Gradel goes down heavily after clashing with Janmaat, with the ex-Feyenoord defender getting a bit of a talking to. Bournemouth continue to enjoy the lion's share of possession, but Shelvey and Colback are providing a veritable shield in front of the Magpies' back four.
(27’) Ayoze is fed into a pocket of space by Wijnaldum, with the Spaniard immediately taking a touch out of his feet and driving towards goal. The Newcastle striker lets fly, but the ball dips some way wide of the top left-hand corner! The Magpies keep the pressure on, but a cross from Sissoko sizzles across the danger area.
(25’) Afobe breaks away down the right-hand side, but Janmaat covers across brilliantly to ensure that the Englishman isn't able to test Elliot! The Dutchman concedes a corner as a result, but the set-piece can only be flicked into the goalkeeper's awaiting arms by Cook.
(23’) Wide from Riviere! Janmaat cuts a great cross back towards the penalty spot, with the Netherlands international finding his French teammate. The ex-Monaco forward tries to guide a neat finish inside the far upright, but a deflection takes it narrowly wide! The resulting corner then narrowly avoids the same Newcastle man at the back post.
(21’) A cross from the left-hand side was flicked away by Janmaat, with Lascelles trying to take control in the Newcastle back four. Moments later, a diagonal is pinged into Afobe, but Elliot comes quickly off his line to claim above the former Wolves striker.
(19’) The away side look to break down the right-hand side, but Smith and Ritchie can only combine to the point where the offside flag is raised. Bournemouth are simply holding onto possession and pulling all the strings, with Newcastle sitting back and letting their opponents have the ball.
(17’) Riviere and Ayoze haven't had much of the ball at all, with the duo chasing shadows while trying to press Bournemouth's central defenders. Play is opened out to the left-hand side to Gradel, but rather than force the issue the Cherries are happy to keep possession and look backwards.
(15’) The opening quarter of an hour hasn't led to Newcastle getting hold of this game, with Bournemouth looking after the ball much better. The ball retention from the Cherries has been characteristic of the visitors' approach under Howe, with his charges looking like the home side.
(13’) This contest has been rather even thus far, with both sides keeping plenty of men behind the ball. Given that both coaches have opted to sit with two banks of four, it has been left up to both striking partnerships to create most of the danger. Ritchie gets a warning from the referee, after a late tackle on Colback.
(11’) Smith is forced into a very rushed clearance, with Bournemouth finally coming under a bit of pressure. Dummett and Janmaat haven't been able to support the attack too much, with the Cherries doing a good job of limiting Newcastle to non-threatening areas of the field.
(9’) Afobe takes aim at the back post, but the former Arsenal striker can only lean back and send a terrible effort some way over the crossbar! Newcastle are conceding all of the early chances, with Howe's men coming out of the blocks at real pace.
(7’) Gradel shoots from around 12 yards out, but the former St. Etienne winger is denied by his own player! Surman gets in the way, with the deflection taking the ball curling off target and to safety. Elliot was left flummoxed.
(5’) Gosling drives to the edge of the penalty area, before trying to unleash a powerful effort, but the ex-Newcastle midfielder sees his attempt charged down easily. The away side keep the pressure on, with Afobe cutting a delivery back from the byline, but Lascelles hacks a rushed clearance away.
(3’) Just wide from Shelvey! A loose ball falls kindly to the ex-Liverpool midfielder, who takes the opportunity to shoot from 25 yards out. His right-footed attempt sweeps wide of the left-hand post, however, with Boruc covering his angles as a precaution. Bournemouth head up the other end, but a cross-cum-shot is gobbled up by Elliot.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at St. James' Park! Newcastle need three points to lift themselves out of the drop zone, with Bournemouth hoping to continue their recent excellent away form. The form book dictates that this should be very competitive indeed.

Max Gradel starts on the left-hand side, with Matt Ritchie hoping to continue some good recent form on the opposite flank. The back four remains unchanged, with the away side hoping to keep things tight against a recently optimistic Newcastle.

Hello and welcome to Bournemouth's trip up north to face Newcastle, with both sides looking to pick up three points in order to battle against relegation. Eddie Howe's men are currently 12 points away from the danger zone, but the Magpies are truly in the mire. The hosts could move out of the bottom three with a win this afternoon, however.

That's all for our live coverage from St. Mary's, thanks for following along. Good bye!
Virgil van Dijk salvages a point for the 10-man Saints with his 93rd minute equaliser, cancelling out Jermain Defoe's late breakthrough, with Jose Fonte seeing red. It's a missed opportunity in the end for Sunderland, though they still pick up a valuable point over the teams fighting them for survival.
(90’) FULL-TIME: SOUTHAMPTON 1-1 SUNDERLAND.
--- 90’ +3 Assist Outstanding delivery from Tadic as well to pick out the centre-half inside the area! ---
--- 90’ +3 Goal! THEY'VE DONE IT! SOUTHAMPTON EQUALISE AT THE DEATH! It was coming! Sunderland drop so deep in defence which allows Saints space to work the ball around craftily in attack, and a delightful pick out from Tadic is finished off emphatically by Van Dijk! Big Sam is disgusted. ---
--- 90’ +1 Substitution John O'Shea comes on to help shut up shop for Sunderland, replacing Kirchhoff. There will be four minutes of stoppage time at St. Mary's. ---
(90’) MARTINA DENIED! Great interplay there from Saints inside the penalty area, before Martina is teed up for a shot. He takes it first-time, but Mannone gets over to make a crucial save!
(89’) DEFLECTED BEHIND! Southampton throwing the kitchen sink forward in an attempt to chase down an equaliser. Tadic's effort from atop the area appears menacing, but a deflection takes it just beyond the far post!
(87’) Sunderland fans making plenty of noise as they creep towards a massive three points. They will have their eyes on the scoreboard across the rest of England, and take note that both Newcastle and Norwich are losing this afternoon as well! It's turning into a dream afternoon for Big Sam's men.
--- 85’ Assist Excellent piece of determined play from Kone to record the assist. ---
--- 85’ Goal! HOW CRUCIAL IS THAT FOR SUNDERLAND? It's a massive goal in their quest for survival! Kone with some excellent work to win the ball and keep play alive inside the area before rolling a pass across for Defoe, and he pounces like any good striker would! The away fans are sent into rapture! ---
(84’) WHAT A RETURN THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN! Careless giveaway by Bertrand, which Borini pounces on before squaring for Larsson. It's a good look at goal for the substitute, but his effort rises over the bar!
--- 83’ Substitution Koeman's hand is forced as he has to bring on Maya Yoshida to restore the four-man back line. Sadio Mane gives way, but you would have liked to see someone else come off there. ---
(81’) IMPORTANT SAVE! Forster flies through the air to turn aside Van Aanholt's powerful free-kick! It was well-struck by the left-back, but needed to be just a bit further from the centre to beat the Southampton keeper.
--- 79’ Red card! SOUTHAMPTON DOWN TO 10 MEN! Opportunity knocks for Sunderland who will play the final 10 minutes a man up! Borini makes a determined run to get on the end of a through-ball, before being wrestled to the ground by Jose Fonte who was clearly the last defender - and Kevin Friend doesn't hesitate is showing red! ---
(78’) Mane has become a focal point in attack for Saints, desperately trying to provide the quality needed to get Southampton their goal. He acrobatically gets on the end of a long ball over the top and heads down for Pelle, but the striker's first-time effort is blocked by Kone.
--- 76’ Substitution It is Seb Larsson who is introduced, making his long-awaited return from injury. The Swede hasn't appeared since November. ---
(75’) Khazri goes down again and is clearly labouring here as his day appears set to come to an end. Allardyce readies his substitute, and it looks as though it's going to be Seb Larsson who replaces him.
(73’) Boos rain down as Khazri goes to ground and stays there, bringing the game to a halt, ending a good spell from Southampton. Play resumes moments later and the ex-Bordeaux man in the casualty of a lovely piece of dribbling by Mane, but the Saints attacker can't pick out his desired cross in the end.
(71’) STAT: The Black Cats have kept the joint-fewest clean sheets in the Premier League this season (3, along with Norwich City).
(69’) SUPERB BLOCK! Craft work down the right from the hosts before the ball gets sent across the area into the path of Pelle by Mane. The striker takes it down, but not in a timely manner, allowing Yedlin to get across and throw his body in front of the shot!
(67’) WHO'S THERE?! Romeu rises above his man at the far post to head Bertrand's corner back across the face of goal, but no one is on hand to get the vital touch! It was there to be had, but Southampton miss the chance to open the scoring!
--- 65’ Substitution James Ward-Prowse is also introduced, as expected, with Steven Davis the one to give way. ---
--- 65’ Substitution The first change sees Juanmi replace Jordy Clasie, which is a positive switch from Koeman as the Spaniard packs much more of an attacking punch. ---
(63’) Koeman is displeased with what he's see over the last five minutes or so and there's plenty of movement now on the Southampton bench. Juanmi has stripped down to his uniform and looks set to come on, in what could well be a double switch as Ward-Prowse scrambles to get ready.
(61’) Big Sam is very animated on the touchline. He's sending his players forward to really get after this Southampton defence. They won't exactly throw caution to the wind just yet, but expect them to start packing a few more bodies forward on the counter, which should also help open the game up.
--- 59’ Substitution Sensing the opportunity to snatch a vital three points in their quest to stave off relegation, Sam Allardyce has introduced a second striker in the form of Jermain Defoe. His arrival is met by a roar of approval from the Sunderland fans, while Dame N'Doye gives way. ---
(58’) Southampton continue to build the pressure but continue to lack the cutting edge in the final third. The openings are there, but they haven't been able to pick them out. Sunderland are doing well to threaten on the counter, as well, though Forster does well to turn aside Borini's latest effort.
(56’) The rain is really coming down here at St. Mary's, and it's turned to hail now in fact. These are less than ideal weather conditions for a passing team like Southampton, but it's hardly unprecedented on the south coast of England. It could just cause a few slips and frantic moments in defence, however, which will be something to keep an eye on.
(54’) STAT: Sunderland have 24 points after 28 games, their lowest tally at this stage of a season since 2005-06, when they had 10 points and were eventually relegated.
(52’) INCHES AWAY! That should inject a bit of life into the Sunderland team! Borini is teed up for a shot atop the area and he drives a venomous half-volley at goal that has Forster beaten, but grazes the top of the bar before landing on the roof of the net!
(50’) Sunderland have been restrained since the restart, taking a more cautious approach with Southampton in possession. Every point is so crucial for the Black Cats in their quest for survival, and while they will sense the chance is there to steal a win, they won't want to put the draw at risk in the process either.
(48’) Southampton get on the front foot directly following the restart. They win a pair of corners, mostly navigating down the left flank, with Bertrand prominent on the overlap. Neither set-piece amounts to much for the hosts, however, but it will serve as a bit of encouragement for them going forward.
(46’) Underway once again at St. Mary's!
The fact that neither side has conceded will be encouraging for the two managers, but they will sense the points are there for the taking and will want to see more going forward in the second half. Fortune favours the bold, and you would have to say there's a real opportunity to be had for the team willing to take a risk.
(45’) HALF-TIME: SOUTHAMPTON 0-0 SUNDERLAND.
(45’) Play has come to a complete halt as Rodwell requires a bit of attention for a knock he's picked up. The board goes up to indicate two added minutes.
(43’) How about that for strength? The towering figure that is Kirchhoff does so well to keep the ball and fend off a couple of challenges near the corner flag, before Clasie sends him to ground. It's a cheap foul conceded by the ex-Feyenoord man, but a good chance for Sunderland to make some noise before the interval. It comes to nothing, however, rather disappointingly in the end from Van Aanholt.
(41’) CLOSE AT THE OTHER END! Back and forth they go as the game starts to spring to life! Bertrand finds a nice pocket of space on the left and passes a ball into the centre which Romeu is allowed to walk in unmarked to meet atop the six-yard box. He redirects it at goal, but Mannone gets down to cover his ground and keep it out!
(39’) WIDE FROM RODWELL! Unmarked and on the volley, the midfielder meets Van Aanholt's splendid delivery from the left, but sends his effort beyond the far post! He's been waiting over a year for his last Premier League goal, and that should well have been it!
(37’) FREE HEADER! Davis manages a really sound delivery from a corner-kick to pick out the run of Van Dijk. The defender again rises above his marker to meet it, but sends his header straight at Mannone! Either side of the keeper and that's probably the opener.
(35’) Plenty of intent shown by both teams, but they're proving very wasteful in the final third. Quality and indecisiveness have plagued these two sides on the front foot, preventing a breakthrough from being had. The points are certainly there for the taking, however.
(33’) NEARLY THE OPENER! Indecision from Forster as he misjudges Khazri's free-kick, floated in from the left. The keeper gets his angles wrong and gets only the slightest of touches on the delivery before watching it rattle off the underside of the bar! It comes to Kirchhoff atop the area, but the midfielder can't find the target with his follow-up.
--- 31’ Yellow card Commentator's curse, I suppose. Just as Van Dijk gets praised, he gets caught for pace and slides in late to impede the run of N'Doye. Referee Kevin Friend has made it clear already that there's little margin for error, and the Dutchman is issued a yellow card. ---
(30’) Van Dijk is proving a real imposing figure in defence for Southampton. Sunderland are whipping some inviting balls into the area for Borini to attack, but the Dutch centre-half has marshalled the back line with great authority thus far - no different than he's done throughout the entirety of his time at St. Mary's.
(28’) STAT: Sunderland have faced more opposition shots on target than any other team in the Premier League this season (166).
(26’) OUTSTANDING GOALKEEPING! Great quality and patience from Saints in the build-up! Mane delivers a teasing cross in from the left, which Pelle knocks down into the path of Tadic. The Serbian sends a bouncing effort at goal, which appears to be looping over the keeper, but an instinctive save from Mannone turns it over the bar!
(24’) The sunshine has vanished behind the clouds and rain has begun to fall at St. Mary's. This game seems to be very much up for grabs, with the gap between the two teams in the table hardly appearing evident based on the opening 24 minutes. Southampton need to assert themselves better.
(22’) Sunderland are growing into the game admirably. They're showing good intent now and there's a wonderful directness to the play of Borini. The striker is doing plenty of north-south running, which has put a strain on the likes of Fonte and Van Dijk.
(20’) Southampton living dangerously at the back as a loose touch from Fonte sends the ball into the path of Khazi who starts a quick counter. The Portuguese defender does well to recover, however, sprinting back to put in a tidy tackle and send the ball running into the waiting arms of Forster.
(18’) STAT: Sunderland have gone 14 games without a clean sheet, the longest run of any team in the Premier League this season.
(16’) Squandered chance! Kaboul's wayward clearance falls straight into the path of Pelle, but the striker almost seems to be taken off guard by the good fortune. He can't sort out his footing and winds up stabbing a feeble effort at goal.
(14’) Southampton are being hemmed back in their own end as Sunderland manage their first period of concentrated pressure. The Black Cats win a corner, though nothing comes of it, but it's an encouraging period for Sam Allardyce's side after an ominous start.
(12’) Bertrand takes, but rather ambitiously opts to go for goal himself from a difficult angle, and winds up sending his effort crashing onto the roof of the net.
--- 11’ Yellow card Dreadful challenge by Khazri - one you would expect from a forward - as he takes out Mane on the edge of the area just a couple of yards from the end line. He goes into the book for that one, with Kevin Friend setting the early precedence in this match. ---
(10’) FIRST CHANCE! Bertrand delivers an inviting ball in from a corner which proves menacing for the Sunderland defence. Van Dijk hangs above his marker to meet it, but Mannone applies enough pressure to force his header wide of the mark.
--- 8’ Yellow card Ryan Bertrand sees his name in the referee's book after just eight minutes for a naive challenge into the feet of Khazri. It's a bit harsh on the left-back, who could have easily walked away with a warning from referee Kevin Friend. ---
(7’) STAT: Sunderland suffered their worst ever Barclays Premier League defeat in this fixture away at Southampton last season (0-8).
(5’) Southampton asking the only questions thus far, attempting to use their pace up top to their advantage against Kaboul. Mane has a real dynamism about him thus far, eager to give chase, but nothing has come from the attacker's energetic start up to this point.
(3’) Reticent start to proceedings in the south of England, with neither side showing much vigour in the early stages. Possession changes hands frequently, while Sunderland appear a bit cautious, with last season's 8-0 drubbing at this venue still fresh in their minds.
(1’) Sunderland, in their green away strip, get the match underway at St. Mary's!
John O’Shea hasn't quite recovered in time from a calf problem that forced him out in the first half of Tuesday’s draw, and is forced to begin today's match on the bench, with Younes Kaboul selected to partner Lamin Kone in defence. Lee Cattermole is out with a head injury he suffered late in the 2-2 draw against the Eagles.

SUNDERLAND (4-5-1): Mannone; Yedlin, Kone, Kaboul, Van Aanholt; N'Doye, M'Vila, Kirchhoff, Rodwell, Khazri; Borini.

CONFIRMED TEAM NEWS:
Sunderland salvaged a draw against reeling Crystal Palace on Tuesday, and while it was enough to pull the Black Cats out of the relegation zone, it didn’t do nearly enough to instill confidence in Wearside. Sam Allardyce’s side are notoriously worse on their travels than at the rowdy Stadium of Light, and will really have to lean on their home form over the coming months if they are to stave off relegation. Hello and welcome to live coverage from St. Mary’s as Southampton look to close the gap on the European places when they play host to a Sunderland side desperate to stay above the bottom three. The famous Staplewood feline – a black cat who has called St. Mary’s home in recent years – will get some companionship today as Sunderland pay a visit to Britannia Road. Ronald Koeman will be hoping it’s not a bad omen for Saints, who have dropped two in a row, their first league defeats since the second of January. The recent skid has seen Southampton drop six points back of the top six, putting added pressure on claiming maximum points against their struggling opponents this afternoon.

The referee brings things to a close, as Swansea seal a big win in their bid to avoid the drop. Sigurdsson's cool second-half finish was ultimately enough to secure back-to-back wins for Alan Curtis in the absence of the ill Francesco Guidolin, but Norwich continue to rot in serious trouble towards the bottom of the league. Their winless run is stretched even further as they look doomed for a desperate fight at the end of the season. No creativity, little fight, there was not much to be encourage by for the visitors, but the Swans' character shone through and the Welsh club took a big step to ensuring their safety this season.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card Rangel picks up a late booking for a cynical foul on Bamford, but the visitors are running out of time to capitalise on the resulting free-kick. ---
(90’) Swansea are being forced to withstand serious pressure here, but they have everyone back and behind the ball. Norwich are hacking the ball into the area rather aimlessly but the hosts are standing firm.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on here.
(90’) BAMFORD! The young Chelsea-owned striker does really well in the area, using his body and easing beyond Fernandez. He prods the ball towards the bottom-left corner, but Fabianski makes the save.
(88’) SWANSEA ESCAPE AGAIN! Norwich remain on the front foot, keeping the hosts penned into their area. Hoolahan does well, but sees his effort blocked. The ball loops up into the air and Routledge tries to smash it clear, but he only knocks it straight back into the middle of the box. Redmond sends it goalwards but misses the target by a matter of inches.
(87’) DESPERATE DEFENDING! Redmond does really well on the left, as he glides past Rangel with ease and then crosses from the byline. Bamford heads it back into the danger zone, but Williams throws himself in the way and clears initially.
(85’) GREAT SAVE! Sigurdsson produces a fine strike from the resulting free-kick, sending a powerful curling effort towards the top-left corner, only for Ruddy to tip it over the crossbar.
(84’) That's a wild challenge from Bennett. The centre-back, who has already been booked, is beaten by Gomis and then desperately tries to get back at him and steal the ball away, but only hauls the striker down. He's lucky to escape a second booking there.
--- 82’ Substitution Here comes a switch for Swansea now, as Gomis is brought on for Ayew, who has worked hard in attack today. ---
(80’) More really bright play from Barrow. The winger charges into the Norwich half, bursting past a couple of defenders and then gets into the area, evading the efforts of Klose. He cuts it back to Sigurdsson, who drops his shoulder, beats the German defender and crosses, but Ruddy takes care of it.
(78’) Almost great play by Hoolahan. The Irishman receives the ball from Martin on the left. His first touch sees the it bounce up a little, but he improvises and then drops a volleyed pass over the defence for Bamford, only for it to be a little ahead of the youngster.
(76’) Norwich have not made much use of Mbokani's physical attributes since his introduction. This time they loft a free-kick into the danger zone towards the Congolese striker, but he nods it straight out of play.
(74’) BARROW! The attacker has been a real threat since coming on. This time he runs at Martin, producing a couple of stepovers and then cutting inside before curling a delivery into the area. His effort bends round and almost creeps inside the left-hand post.
(72’) Better from the visitors. Norwich use the ball really well as they work it up the right and then into the area. Bamford cuts it back to Hoolahan, who then tees up the arriving Howson, but Williams gets back well to kill off the threat.
(70’) Norwich are quickly back on the front foot. Eventually Bamford exploits space on the left and forces his way past Fernandez and into the area. The Chelsea-owned forward tries hammering the ball across the face of goal, but Fabianski gets in the way.
(68’) Good play again from Barrow, as the striker darts up the right, comes inside and picks out a clever pass into the area for Sigurdsson. The midfielders gets a shot away but it is blocked right in front of him.
(66’) NORWICH ESCAPE! Mbokani almost immediately causes his manager to regret his introduction, as he is caught out trying to take the ball out from the back. Routledge then plays the ball low into the danger zone but Ayew can't get his feet around it.

--- 61’ Assist Excellent pass from Fer, as the Dutchman picks out Sigurdsson through a crowd of players and the midfielder provides a cool finish. ---

(60’) Decent play again from the hosts. Barrow has made a difference since coming on, and this time he appears on the right, before teeing up Ayew to his left. The Ghanaian tries to find the top-left corner but misses the target.
(59’) That's a chance! The ball is worked into the Norwich area and Sigurdsson manages to get a shot away. It smacks againts a defender and loops up into the air, heading for the back post. Barrow is the quickest to it but he knocks it well over from a tight angle.

They are adamant they should have another as Jerome appears to knock the ball out, but the referee believes it took a last touch of Barrow. The Swans then bring on former Norwich man Fer, replacing Britton. ---

(54’) Good play by Hoolahan, as he pops up out on the left and draws a foul from Rangel. That was a rash decision from the Spaniard.
(52’) Williams is in a bit of pain here, as the Swansea captain receives a blow to the face while trying to get on the end of a free-kick delivery. He appears to be capable of staying on though.

(49’) Fine play from the hosts, as they find themselves under pressure while trying to clear their lines. They pass the ball around calmly and quickly and bring it away in style. The fans show their appreciation.
(47’) Sigurdsson clips the free-kick into the danger zone, about 30 yards from goal. Klose is there to head clear, though, bringing an end to the threat.

One spectator of note attending today's game will be new Fifa president Gianni Infantino. The 45-year-old, elected as Sepp Blatter's successor last month, is in Wales for the 130th International Football Association Board annual meeting.
Norwich boss Neil does not have the luxury of being able to make six changes and strengthen his team in the process. No, the Canaries have made just two alterations to the XI which lost to Chelsea, with Ryan Bennett and Alex Tettey replaced by Steven Naismith and Gary O'Neil, respectively.
Curtis has made a total of six changes to the team which beat Arsenal, but those alterations have arguably made their team stronger today than it was at the Emirates. Federico Fernandez, Angel Rangel, Neil Taylor, Leon Britton, Gylfi Sigurdsson and Alberto Paloschi all return to the Swans' starting XI, giving the home side an early boost. Ki Sung-yeung misses out, however, having picked up an ankle knock on Wednesday.
Swansea will no doubt be encouraged by the win over Arsenal, but the Liberty Stadium has by no means been a fortress for them in recent times, with only two of their last 12 home games producing victories. Alan Curtis will be the man in charge of the Swans again today as Francesco Guidolin continues to recover from a chest infection and he will be eager to put the Norwich defence - the equal-worst in the divison with 53 goals conceded - under pressure right from the off.
Norwich put up a decent fight in their last outing but ultimately slumped to a 2-1 loss at home to a resurgent Chelsea. The defeat ensured their winless run continued, with their last victory coming at home to Southampton on January 2. The Canaries are in freefall heading into the final months of the season and they need to start picking up points quickly if they are to avoid the late, uncomfortable scramble. Preventing defeat today would certainly be a start, but Alex Neil will be desperate to come away from Wales with the spoils.
Today's clash at the Liberty Stadium represents an important duel between two clubs looking to avoid the drop this season. Both have struggled throughout the campaign and thus have found themselves drawn into the battle against the drop. Swansea's shock 2-1 defeat of Arsenal on Wednesday helped to open up a six-point gap between themselves and the last relegation spot, which curiously is occupied by today's visitors, but it will not count for much if they follow that up with a disappointing reverse at home.

--- 60’ Substitution Austin looks to have pulled something here, and the physios immediately tend to the striker, who won't be able to continue. Koeman is forced into his second change, introducing Pelle in his place. ---
