(56’) Bournemouth's nearest rivals in the table are Crystal Palace, three points ahead of them in 14th place at the start of play. The London club have found an equaliser against Sunderland, meaning that the Cherries will stay 15th if these scores hold.
(54’) Southampton are starting to dominate more of the ball, but they're really struggling to create opportunities from open play. Credit to Bournemouth, then, for applying that energy to the defensive end as well.
(52’) Like they did at the start of the first half, Bournemouth win a series of corners to start the second period, but they're well defended by the visitors once again. Not too much final-third action since the restart.
(50’) Southampton had two solid chances in the opening 20 minutes, but since then, they've never really been in this game. Koeman's early introduction of Davis and shift to a back four did little to change their fortunes.
(48’) Davis releases Cedric on the overlap down the right, but the full-back's cross can't find Long inside the area, with Francis rising highest to win the initial header. Not long after, there's a handball by the visitors in the box, and Bournemouth have a free-kick.
(46’) Off we go again.
Kevin Friend has been taken to hospital and is thankfully still conscious, but there will be a replacement fourth official, Dean Treleaven for the second half. We're about to get underway again.
The start of the second half has been delayed for around five minutes after that injury to Kevin Friend. Apparently, the fourth official hit his head on the dugout, and is currently receiving medical attention.
Mike Dean sensibly blows the whistle for half-time to send both teams down the tunnel, and giving an opportunity to make sure that Kevin Friend is able to continue. Bournemouth have a one-goal lead at the break, thanks to Cook's close-range strike. Southamption created a few chances, but were generally second best here. A lot to play for after the restart, so stay tuned.
(45’) The game has been stopped here just before half-time, with the officials having a word with the managers. It's a bit of a mystery here, but the word is that fourth official Kevin Friend has hit his head.
(45’) King appeals halfheartedly for a handball after Long tried to clear a corner, but the referee was never going to award that penalty, given that the striker knew absolutely nothing about it.
(43’) Excellent defending by Van Dijk, as King goes scampering down the left wing, and he's got Afobe in support. However, the Dutchman tracks the run of the striker, muscles him off the ball and shepherds it out of play for a goal-kick.
(41’) Only minutes to go until the half-time break now, and it looks like the home side will be taking this one-goal lead into the interval. Southampton have had the better chances, but Bournemouth have just looked hungrier.
(39’) It seems that Bournemouth are winning all of the 50-50 balls - including the crucial one by King that saw him fouled, leading to the free-kick that caused the opener. Great energy from them.
(37’) OVER THE BAR! Gradel cuts in from the flank and beats Cedric, getting the ball onto his favoured right foot. He then hammers one towards goal, but it doesn't stay down and sails over.
--- 35’ Substitution Looks like an early tactical substitution from Koeman here, as he withdraws Yoshida in order to introduce Davis. That will spell an end to the back three that Southampton started this game with, as they shift to a flat back four. ---
(33’) A crucial goal for Bournemouth, who were having no luck from open play, and were seeing their set-piece deliveries repelled. Will this force Southampton out of their shell more to get back into this?
--- 31’ Goal! BOURNEMOUTH HAVE THE LEAD! From a free-kick on the right side, Forster can't handle the delivery, and it falls to Cook, who reacts quicker than Van Dijk to convert with an acrobatic attempt! ---
(30’) Gradel squares up to Cedric down the left-hand side, and he keeps his balance on the dribble after he looked set to join the defender in falling to the turf. That frees him on the flank, but his delivery is met by the head of Van Dijk, who has been a rock for Southampton so far.
(29’) Ward-Prowse whips in a dangerous, in-swinging delivery into the mixer from a set-piece, but an important defensive header allows it to spring up to Boruc, who makes the catch at the back post.
(27’) Surman loses out on a defensive header, forcing Smith and Long into a chase for the ball towards the corner flag. The right-back goes down in a heap, and that convinces the referee that the Saints striker committed a foul.
(25’) Bournemouth win a free-kick in a great position just outside the area. Ritchie stands primed to shoot, and the ball is rolled into his path, but the wall manages to get the important block in.
(23’) Again the visitors cause panic inside the opposition penalty area. A long pass into the area forces Boruc off his line to grab the ball, and it's good that he kept a hold of that with Long lurking at the back post!
(21’) Not a whole lot happening out on the pitch at the moment in terms of goalmouth action. You get the feeling that Southampton are happy to keep surrendering possession and playing on the counter, as Bournemouth haven't created much from open play.
(19’) Looks like close to a full house here at the Vitality Stadium, and the atmosphere is reflective of the derby crowd. The home fans are watching their side generally boss this, but the visitors have fashioned the only two chances so far.
(17’) SHOULD HAVE DONE BETTER! Ward-Prowse delicately hoists a ball over the top of the defence for Mane to chase, but the attacker never keeps his composure, torpedoing his finish into the stands.
(15’) Southampton have only let in 11 league goals away from St. Mary's all season, a mark that no side in the top flight can better. Having said that, only two other teams have scored less than their 11 strikes on the road. Perhaps the 0-0 score is not a surprise at this early stage then.
(13’) Southampton try to get something going down the right-hand side, but Bournemouth are having none of it. Van Dijk gets frustrated and lashes one on goal from long range, but Surman gets his body in the way.
(11’) Bournemouth are starting to assert their authority over this game, producing a few eye-catching passages of play. The question is whether they can find that final killer ball to really carve open the opposition.
(9’) Gradel, the former Saint-Etienne man, tries to get the better of Van DIjk down the left-hand side, but his attempt at a cross is blocked, leading to another corner, the fifth for Bournemouth by my count. It's reached by the defence first once more though.
(7’) Yet another corner for the home side, but it's defended well by the visitors here, as has been the theme throughout the opening minutes. Good tempo to this match already, with both sides getting active in the final third.
(5’) The danger suddenly appears for Southampton, as Cedric makes a great overlapping run to the byline. Mane, who had drifted out to the right, gets the ball and feeds him with a lovely pass. The wing-back slides it into the centre for Austin, who slams it wide of the mark!
(3’) Early pressure from the home side as they win a corner which Ritchie swings into a dangerous area, but Fonte rises well to get his head to the ball.Good play down the flanks to get that set-piece in the first place.
(1’) Off we go!
Koeman has reacted to the Chelsea defeat with three changes to his team. In comes Sadio Mane to an advanced midfield role, while Maya Yoshida steps into the back three, with James Ward-Prowse in the centre of the park. Jordy Claise, Matt Targett and Steven Davis all take a seat on the bench.
Junior Stanislas has been replaced by Max Gradel in the only change by Howe from his team's goalless draw with Watford last time out. Joshua King leads the line for the home side, with Benik Afobe tucking in just behind. Harry Arter and Andrew Surman make up the midfield pairing.
Southampton subs: Claise, Davis, Tadic, Martina, Pelle, Stekelenburg, Targett.
Southampton (3-4-1-2): Forster; Van Dijk, Fonte, Yoshida; Cedric Soares, Ward-Prowse, Romeu, Bertrand; Mane; Long, Austin.
Bournemouth subs: Gosling, Elphick, Pugh, Federici, Distin, Murray, Grabban.
Bournemouth (4-4-1-1): Boruc; Smith, Francis, Cook, Daniels; Ritchie, Surman, Arter, Gradel; Afobe; King.
Southampton won the reverse match 2-0 at St. Mary's earlier in the season, which made it five straight victories over the Cherries - who themselves have taken all three points in only four of their last 17 attempts in this fixture. You have to go back all the way to 1958, and down to the old Third Division for the last time that Bournemouth managed a league win over the Saints.
Southampton, meanwhile, are hunting for a European spot. They were downed by a Chelsea comeback in a 2-1 reverse over the weekend, which saw them drop four points behind fifth-placed Manchester United. Ronald Koeman's team are in a three-way tie for the second-best defensive record in the Premier League, with 26 goals conceded from 27 matches.
Bournemouth haven't won in three games, but the poorer form of those below them has enabled the Cherries to establish a five-point cushion between themselves and the relegation zone. Survival in their first-ever Premier League campaign is looking a real possibility for Eddie Howe and his team.
Hello and welcome to our live commentary of the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Southampton. Eight league places and 11 points separate the sides tonight as we set the stage for a busy Tuesday of top-flight football. Stick with us for all the action.

The defeat leaves Villa bottom of the table, and they now trail Sunderland by eight points as a result of the Black Cats' hard-earned 2-2 draw at home to Crystal Palace. The Villans' next opponents are Manchester City, which is bound to be a tough game, whilst Everton, who now sit in ninth place thanks to today's win, must face West Ham United on the weekend.
Another game, another defeat for Villa, whose time in the Premier League is rapidly coming to an end. Once again they were let down by poor defending today, as time and time again they were carved open by Everton's quick counter-attacks. In truth, the visitors didn't play at their best and were there for the taking on a few occasions, particularly in the second half when they switched off slightly, but the hosts never looked good enough to punish their opponents on the rare occasions that they were able to penetrate the final third of the pitch with any purpose.
FULL-TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-3 EVERTON
(90’) Villa try to break forward on one last attack through Cissokho down the left wing, but Everton have plenty of bodies behind the ball and the Frenchman is unable to get forward quick enough before the referee blows his whistle for the final time, bringing an end to another dreadful evening for the hosts.
(90’) Funes Mori almost scores again! This time, Barkley's corner is curled into the heart of the penalty area, where it bounces off the thigh of Lukaku before falling at the feet of the Argentine defender. He immediately tries to poke a first-time shot past Guzan from point-blank range, but the goalkeeper is just about able to tip it away with a vital save.
(90’) Everton earn themselves a corner on the right wing, which is sent short and worked over to McCarthy. Once again, the Villa defenders completely fall asleep and leave the midfielder in far too much space, but he's eventually closed down as soon as he shoots and his thumping strike ends up deflecting out for another corner.
(90’) Villa work the ball around quickly deep inside the Everton half of the pitch before Gueye tries to tee up Gestede with a through-ball into the left-hand side of the penalty area, but it's poorly hit by the Senegalese midfielder and fails to find the striker before rolling harmlessly out of play for a goal-kick.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be five minutes of added time.
(89’) Great chance for Ayew! A looping cross from Cissokho flies over towards the edge of the Everton penalty area, where it finds Gestede. The big striker rises high and nods the ball back to the aforementioned Ghanaian, who is in a pocket of space just outside of the box, but his first-time half-volley is well saved by a good diving stop from Joel.
--- 88’ Substitution Mirallas receives a rousing round of applause from the away fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Niasse, who comes on to make his Premier League debut. ---
(87’) Lukaku brings the ball down wonderfully well midway inside the Villa penalty area before spinning and teeing up Mirallas on the left-hand side of the box. The Belgian attacking midfielder immediately unleashes a rocket of a volley, but Hutton is there to throw his body in front of the strike to send it bouncing out of play for a corner.
(86’) Gestede muscles his way into the right-hand side of the Everton penalty area and battles with Funes Mori before earning his side a corner. It's flung into the heart of the box and bounces towards Cissokho, but the defender mistimes his attempted header and completely misses the ball, much to the frustration of the home fans.
(84’) The ball pinballs around the Everton penalty area, with no player able to make decent contact with it. It eventually bounces out to the left flank, where it finds Cissokho, but the French full-back's scooped cross loops up into the air and down into the safe hands of Joel.
(82’) Villa swarm back into the Everton half of the pitch as they desperately try to find a second goal that would completely change the game and give them a real chance of pulling off an excellent comeback. However, every ball that is flung into the penalty area is dealt with well by the visitors, who are now firmly on the back foot and defending resolutely.
--- 81’ Substitution Oviedo seems to have picked up a slight injury, and he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Baines for the final 10 minutes. ---
--- 79’ Assist Veretout picked out Gestede wonderfully well, and it was one of the first times this evening that Villa have sent a decent cross into the box. The added aerial threat that the striker has brought since coming on has also resulted in the hosts looking more dangerous when pushing forward, but is it too little too late? ---
--- 79’ Goal! GOAL! Villa have found the back of the net! The hosts break down the right wing before Veretout swings a lovely cross into the heart of the penalty area. It finds Gestede, who rises high and beats both Stones and Jagielka to the ball before sending a bullet header past Joel and into the back of the net. Game on? ---
(78’) Villa are trying to up the intensity as they aim to find a way back into the game, but with 12 minutes to go and with them struggling so much in front of goal, surely it's too little too late? Everton are sitting deep and look determined to hold on to the clean sheet, which would be their third in their last four games.
(76’) It's all Everton at the moment as they comfortably hold on to possession inside their own half of the pitch. Villa can't get anywhere near the ball and, as a result, the home fans are getting increasingly frustrated with what they are seeing.
(74’) There was talk before the game about a mass walkout by Villa fans in the 74th minute, and a significant portion of them have indeed left the stadium. It's been a miserable night for the hosts, who have continually struggled against Everton and are still in danger of falling further behind in the final quarter of an hour.
--- 73’ Substitution Coleman makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Stones, who comes on to make his first appearance in over a month. ---
(72’) Ayew battles with Oviedo on the right-hand side of the Everton penalty area before forcing the Costa Rican into poking the ball out of play for a corner. It's whipped into the middle of the box, but it's sent far too near to Joel and the Spaniard is easily able to cut out the danger under very little pressure.
--- 71’ Substitution Veretout marks his 23rd birthday with a 20-minute appearance, as it's he who is brought on to replace Westwood, who seems to have picked up a slight injury. ---
(70’) Lennon embarks on a wonderful run down the right flank and cuts into the Villa penalty area before beating Clark, but the midfielder's chipped cross ends up deflecting off Cissokho and out for a corner. Barkley sends another dangerous ball into the box, where Jagielka nods it into the path of Lukaku, but the big Belgian ends up firing his half-volleyed strike a few yards over the top of the crossbar.
(68’) Ayew twists and turns as he tries to muscle his way down the right flank, but he's dispossessed by Oviedo just as he's about to beat the Costa Rican. Villa win themselves a throw-in, which is taken quickly before Hutton swings a cross into the middle of the penalty area, but, once again, his attempted pass is poorly hit and is easily dealt with by the Everton defence.
--- 66’ Substitution Agbonlahor, who has had an incredibly difficult evening, makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Gestede in Villa's first substitution of the game. ---
(64’) Villa fly forward once again, and this time it's Bacuna who penetrates the Everton penalty area on a great run. He heads towards the byline before trying to cut a pass back to Agbonlahor, but it's sent too far behind the striker and is easily cut out by Jagielka in the middle of the box.
(62’) Westwood almost pulls a goal back for Villa! A determined attack from the hosts results in two corners in quick succession. The second sees the ball bounce out to the edge of the Everton box, where it finds the aforementioned midfielder, but his first-time strike ends up flying just a yard or so wide of the near post. That was certainly one of the hosts' best chances to score.
--- 60’ Assist Funes Mori did wonderfully well to pick out Lukaku with such a great cross, but where were the Villa defenders? They completely fell asleep and left him all alone, which made life incredibly easy for the Argentine. ---
--- 60’ Goal! GOAL! Lukaku makes it 3-0! The resulting corner is initially dealt with by Villa, but the visitors come back quickly through Funes Mori. The defender is left in so much space on the right-hand side of the penalty area, where there are no players whatsoever, and he takes advantage of the poor defending by whipping a lovely low cross towards the edge of the six-yard box, where the Belgian striker taps the ball into the back of the net with the easiest of strikes. With it, he becomes the first Everton player to score 17 Premier League goals in a single season! ---
(59’) What a save by Guzan! Lennon is left in far too much space on the left wing, allowing him to skip into the box before chipping a cross towards the penalty spot. It finds Lukaku, who rises high and meets the ball wonderfully well before sending a bullet header towards the bottom left-hand corner of the net, but the Villa goalkeeper is there to tip it round the post with an excellent diving stop.
(57’) Coleman battles with Cissokho on the right-hand side of the Villa penalty area before the French defender pokes the ball out for another Everton corner. Barkley's cross from the set-piece is excellent and is sent into the middle of the box, but there are no white shirts there to meet it and, as a result, it's easily dealt with by Richards.
(55’) Everton work their way down the right flank on a quick counter-attack through Coleman. The full-back then spins and finds McCarthy, who tries to tee up Lennon with a deep cross, but it's completely overhit by the midfielder and sails over the head of the Englishman out for a throw-in. On plenty of occasions the visitors have done well to get forward, but time and time again they have let themselves down with poor passing inside the final third of the pitch.
(53’) Bacuna, who has arguably been one of Villa's most creative players thus far, picks up the ball in plenty of space midway inside the Everton half of the pitch. He immediately tries to tee up Hutton with a quick through-ball down the right wing, but it ends up missing the outstretched foot of the wing-back by the narrowest of margins before rolling out of play for a goal-kick.
(51’) McCarthy is clattered into by Westwood in the middle of the pitch, resulting in a free-kick for Everton just inside their own half of the pitch. It's taken short and the visitors try to work the ball down the right wing, but Coleman's run forward is quickly halted by Gueye, and, under pressure from the Senegalese midfielder, the Irishman is forced into spinning round and darting backwards.
(49’) Villa patiently pass the ball around as they try to find a way through the sea of white shirts camped in front of them, but they're unable to do so and are forced into working their way back into their own half of the pitch due to strong defending by the visitors.
(47’) Everton immediately fly down the right flank through Lennon, who then wins his side a corner. It's curled into the middle of the Villa penalty area by Barkley, where this time it's Jagielka who is left unmarked, but the ball ends up flying just a yard or so over the head of the centre-back.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
Boos ring around the stadium as the two sets of players make their way off the pitch, and it's no wonder why. It's been an incredibly difficult first half for Villa, who have looked bright on a few occasions when pushing forward but, overall, have struggled to find much joy at all. At the back they have been particularly poor, with both of Everton's goals resulting from abysmal marking inside the penalty area. Lukaku has seen little of the ball but time and time again both Mirallas and Lennon have punished the hosts with their pace, which has made life incredibly tough for the Villans' back five.
HALF-TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-2 EVERTON
(45’) Another attempt at a Villa attack comes to nothing, allowing Everton to get back on the ball once again. However, with so little time left to play they decide to patiently pass it around inside their own half of the pitch until the referee brings an end to what has been an excellent first half for the visitors.
(45’) Lescott goes close! Villa earn themselves a corner on the right wing after nervy defending by Everton, and it's half dealt with by the visitors before Bacuna swings in a deep cross. It finds the centre-back in space on the left-hand side of the penalty area, but his chipped cross-cum-shot ends up flying agonisingly wide of the far post and out for a goal-kick.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
--- 44’ Yellow card Everton sit deep and defend well against another determined Villa attacking move before trying to break away on a quick counter-attack. Coleman whips a lofted pass up to the halfway line, where it finds Lukaku, but the Belgian strikes Clark in the face whilst battling with the Irishman, leaving the referee with no choice but to show him a yellow card. ---
(43’) Another chance for Agbonlahor! This time a wonderful cross comes from Cissokho, who flies down the left flank and beats two players before curling a lovely ball towards the near post. The striker makes a great run towards the near post, but he ends up missing making contact by the narrowest of margins.
(42’) Again, Hutton impresses down the right wing before curling a cross into the heart of the Everton box. Agbonlahor rises high and looks set to meet the ball near to the penalty spot, but Funes Mori beats him to it before clearing the danger with a strong header.
(40’) With just five minutes left to play, Everton seem in no rush to push forward as they look to hold on to their two-goal lead. They are enjoying their fair share of possession in the middle of the pitch and are doing well to keep the ball as far away from Villa as possible, which has resulted in the hosts becoming incredibly frustrated.
(38’) Vital interception by Funes Mori! A looping cross from Hutton does well to find Agbonlahor, who then nods the ball towards goal. Westwood charges through the Everton defence in an attempt to latch on to it, but the Argentine centre-back is just about able to poke it away with a clearance at the last possible moment.
(36’) Jagielka and Bacuna both battle for the ball in the air before the centre-back is caught in the face by the Dutchman, leaving him in a heap on the floor. He initially looks to be badly hurt by the coming together but eventually gets back to his feet before receiving medical treatment for a few moments.
(34’) Almost a costly mistake by Guzan! Once again, Everton hit Villa on the counter, and it's Mirallas who proves to be the most dangerous of the visitors' players. He flies into the box before firing a low strike towards goal, and it's fumbled into the path of Lukaku. The striker's shot is saved but the ball then finds Oviedo, and the Costa Rican immediately beats the American goalkeeper before seeing his effort cleared off the line by Lescott.
(32’) Villa immediately try to break forward from the restart as Cissokho charges down the left wing, but the full-back brings a promising attacking move to a disappointing end when he fires a low shot straight into the hands of Joel at the near post instead of crossing the ball into the penalty area.
--- 30’ Goal! GOAL! Everton have doubled their lead! Villa swarm into the visitors' half of the pitch on yet another determined attacking move, but it breaks down and the Toffees take advantage of poor play by the hosts by flying forward on a quick counter-attack. Barkley charges through the middle of the pitch before sending a lovely pass out to Mirallas, who sprints into the left-hand side of the penalty area and cuts a pass back to Lennon. The former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder is completely unmarked, allowing him to tap the ball through the legs of Guzan and into the back of the net. ---
--- 30’ Assist Assist Kevin Mirallas ---
(28’) Chance for Bacuna! Villa have been playing so much better of the past few minutes as they continue to push forward. They work the ball around quickly before the Dutchman cuts inside from the left wing, and his thumping strike looks set for the top left-hand corner of the net but is acrobatically stopped by Joel.
--- 27’ Yellow card A Villa attack breaks down, and Everton try to quickly break away on one of their own down the left wing. They initially do so well thanks to good hold up play by Lukaku, but Bacuna brings it to an end with a cynical handball, for which he receives a yellow card. ---
(25’) Acrobatic stuff from Richards! The first corner is horribly fumbled by Joel, resulting in a second set-piece for Villa. It's curled out to the edge of the penalty area, where it finds the aforementioned centre-back, but his wonderful scissor-kick is stopped by another good diving save by Everton's Spanish goalkeeper.
(24’) It's end to end stuff! First, Mirallas charges down the left flank before whipping a low cross into the box, but it misses Lukaku and is cut out by Lescott. Villa immediately break away on a quick counter-attack down the left wing, with Cissokho getting forward well before trying to set up Ayew. Funes Mori is there to cut out the danger but can only send his attempted clearance out to Bacuna, who then quickly tees up Westwood, and the Englishman's thumping 20-yard strike is tipped round the post by a great diving save from Joel.
(22’) Agbonlahor goes close! Bacuna embarks on a great run through the centre of the pitch, where there's far too much space left by the Everton holding midfielders. He then threads a lovely pass past Jagielka and into the path of the aforementioned striker, whose poked shot deflects off the outstretched foot of Funes Mori before being parried away by Joel.
--- 20’ Yellow card Villa lose possession deep inside the Everton half of the pitch before Gueye brings down McCarthy with a poorly timed sliding challenge that results in a yellow card for the Senegalese midfielder. ---
(19’) The pace of the game has slowed down somewhat over the past few minutes, and it's now Villa who are controlling possession in the middle of the pitch. They initially work the ball around well before Westwood tries to swing in a cross from the right wing, but it's underhit and is easily dealt with by Funes Mori inside the Everton penalty area.
(17’) Barry muscles his way through the middle of the pitch and weaves his way through a sea of Villa players before sending the ball out to McCarthy on the right wing. The Irishman then plays a quick one-two with Mirallas before heading towards the edge of the penalty area, where he goes down under a challenge from Gueye. He immediately screams for a free-kick, but the referee shakes his head and tells him to get back to his feet.
(15’) Villa are finally able to push forward on their first real attack of the game, but a speculative shot from just outside of the penalty area by Ayew loops up into the air and towards the far post, where it's comfortably dealt with by Joel before the ball can be reached by Agbonlahor.
--- 13’ Yellow card Villa can't break out of their own half of the pitch, and Everton quickly come back once again before Mirallas is hacked down by Clark on the right flank, resulting in a yellow card for the Irishman and another free-kick for the visitors. The Belgian midfielder curls the set-piece into the box but can only find the hands of Guzan, resulting in a chorus of ironic cheers from the home fans. ---

(11’) After holding on to possession for what feels like an age, Coleman swings a looping cross into the middle of the Villa box. It looks set to find Lukaku, who is waiting patiently on the penaty spot, but Lescott is just about able to beat him to the ball before heading it away from danger.
(9’) Everton patiently pass the ball around deep inside the Villa half of the pitch as they comfortably work their way forward. That early goal has resulted in the atmosphere inside the stadium turning sour, and the home fans are already booing and hissing with anger.
(7’) A half-hearted Villa attacking move breaks down inside the Everton half of the pitch, allowing the visitors to immediately break forward on a quick counter-attack. They fly forward through a great run by Lennon before the midfielder tees up Lukaku, but the striker is quickly put under pressure by Lescott and is unable to get a shot away before being dispossessed by the centre-back.

A lovely pass from Oviedo flies through the middle of the pitch and finds Lukaku in far too much space on the edge of the Villa box, but his first-time strike is deflected out of play for a corner. The set-piece is curled into the heart of the penalty area by Mirallas and it finds Funes Mori completely unmarked, allowing the centre-back to beat Guzan with a thumping header from six yards out. ---
(3’) After a patient start to the game from both sides, a lofted pass is flung up towards the edge of the Everton penalty area, where Agbonlahor tries to get on the end of it. (1’) And we're off! Everton get us underway, attacking from right to left.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, Everton boss Roberto Martinez has made just one alteration to the side that featured in the aforementioned defeat against West Brom, with Tom Cleverley, who misses out through illness, making way for Kevin Mirallas.
Remi Garde has decided to make four changes to the Villa side that lost 2-1 away to Stoke City on the weekend, with the biggest talking point being the return of Brad Guzan, who makes his first league start since January 2nd. It won’t be easy, however, as Everton head to Birmingham with recent history firmly on their side. They have won five of the last seven meetings between the two sides, including a 4-0 demolition of Villa back in November, when Romelu Lukaku and Ross Barkley, who have arguably been their best performers this season, both bagged themselves two goals each. The duo have been slightly less prolific in recent weeks but will be hoping to get back to their best after enjoying a weekend off, meaning that they should head into tonight’s clash the fresher of the two teams. They certainly need the win, too, as their last league outing resulted in a disappointing 1-0 defeat at home to West Bromwich Albion, their second in four games. Last weekend brought with it the news that the Toffees have a new majority shareholder in Iranian businessman Farhad Moshiri, and manager Roberto Martinez has claimed that the new investment should help his side aim for Champions League football. However, an underwhelming season thus far has left them in a disappointing 12th place, so for now the aim is to end the campaign with as many positive results as possible, starting with tonight's encounter against a team that they will be confident about beating.
With eight points separating them and a spot outside the relegation zone, and with just 11 games left to save their season, it looks as if it’s all but over for Villa. After spending the last 26 years in the top tier, it’s almost certain that a thoroughly disappointing campaign will end in them being relegated for the first time since 1987, and they now have a tough game against Everton to contend with. The Villans have won just three times all season, and they head into tonight’s clash in the wake of back-to-back defeats, one of which was a miserable 6-0 thrashing against Liverpool on this very ground. Over the course of the season, Villa Park hasn’t been a particularly happy place for today’s hosts, who have lost seven of their 13 Premier League games played here, conceding 20 goals in the process. However, they have looked far better since Christmas, and as a result the aforementioned defeat against Jurgen Klopp’s Reds was their first since December 13th. Huge wins against Crystal Palace and Norwich City came at home in January and February, respectively, so they will be hoping that they can banish memories of their previous thumping and instead pick up another much-needed victory.

(39’) SAVE! It's the first time Ruddy has really been called into action and he responds well as he dives low to his left to keep out a bending free-kick from Fabregas. The Spaniard originally tried to pick out Cahill, who missed the ball.
--- 39’ Yellow card Bennett picks up a caution from the referee as he robustly brings down Hazard inside his own half. Chelsea now have a free-kick in a great position. ---
(37’) Another good chance for Chelsea to test Ruddy goes begging as Traore takes a heavy touch down the right flank. He cleverly skips in behind Brady but shows too much of the ball to the Norwich goalkeeper, who gobbles it up in the end.
--- 36’ Substitution Neil gets forced into making his first change of the game for Norwich as Tettey, who picked up a knock following a collision with Hazard, comes off for O'Neil. ---
(35’) CLOSE! Hazard latches onto a loose ball outside Norwich's penalty area and weighs up his options. Fabregas reads his attentions well as he runs in behind Brady, before he heads over the crossbar from a decent position.
(33’) Tettey heads off the pitch as Fabregas picks up the ball to take Chelsea's free-kick. The Spaniard shows good vision as he quickly lofts a good pass over the top of Klose towards Traore, but the ball carries too much weight and goes out of bounds.

(29’) WASTE! Tettey opts against hitting a shot on the half volley from distance as he creeps forward towards goal. With little else on, he tries to feed a pass through to Jerome instead but his attempt runs away from the striker and into Courtois' arms.
(27’) Fabregas releases a cracking pass to set Traore running down the right-hand side of the field. The forward dips infield, shifting the ball onto his stronger left foot in the process, before he drives a shot which deflects off Klose and goes away from goal.
(25’) Hoolahan comes short and receives possession from Pinto down the right flank. The Irishman wastes little time as he curls the ball into the penalty area, but Ivanovic shuts the door quickly with a good headed clearance.

(21’) Norwich have tightened up defensively since Kenedy's early strike found the back of the net. Neil will be delighted with the response his side have made, though they need to catch Chelsea cold while they're still looking to find their rhythm.
(19’) Redmond carries possession forward well for Norwich and gets his head up looking for options. Pinto offers himself down the right-hand side but he frustratingly strays into an offside position despite looking across the line.
(17’) CLOSE! Jerome comes to life in Chelsea's half as Hoolahan collects possession down the left flank. The striker does well to stay onside as he steams into the penalty area to head over the crossbar from close range, though he should do better.
(15’) Chelsea haven't put their foot down on the gas after taking the lead inside the first minute, giving away possession cheaply a few times in the process. Norwich are definitely on the front foot at the moment.
(13’) Hoolahan cuts infield from the left-hand side slightly as he looks to bend in a cross towards Jerome. However, Azpilicueta gets close to him quickly and makes a good tackle to cancel out Norwich's attack.
--- 13’ Yellow card Howson picks up the first booking of the game as he mistimes a challenge in the middle of the park. The former Leeds man was just a little too keen to seize back possession for his side. ---
(11’) Traore has impressed in the opening stages of this game through his quick feet down the right-hand side. He's releasing the ball crisply into the path of his forward-thinking team-mates, allowing markers little time to get near him.
(9’) Norwich couldn't have dreamed of making a worse start to this game but they've reacted well since, continuing to feed possession into good wide areas to stretch Chelsea's backline around.
(7’) CHANCE! Redmond shows great technique as he skips past several Chelsea players and into the penalty area. The angle to score is tight so he rolls the ball back to Howson instead, who curls a good shot from outside the box but it deflects off Jerome and goes away from goal.
(5’) It's been a really confident, bright start from Chelsea as they continue to knock possession around with consummate ease. Norwich have looked a threat since falling behind, though, and the match has become a little bit end-to-end early doors.
(3’) Norwich surge forward in hope of finding a quick equaliser as Hoolahan curls a cross in from the left-hand side. Jerome rushes towards the near post to try and get on the end of it, but Cahill gets there first and makes a good block.

Fabio Borini's first goal since Boxing Day salvages a point for the Black Cats, who deny the Eagles their first league win of 2016 despite Connor Wickham's second-half brace. In the end a draw is fair for both sides, neither of whom were convincing enough to top a thrilling contest at the Stadium of Light.
(90’) FULL-TIME: SUNDERLAND 2-2 CRYSTAL PALACE.
(90’) Into the second of four minutes of stoppage time and both teams are on in search of a winner. It's becoming increasingly stretched at the Stadium of Light with the three points up for grabs!
--- 90’ Assist Yedlin is rewarded for his hard work tonight with the assist on the equaliser, though Borini had all the work to do still when that pass came in. ---
--- 90’ Goal! BORINI HAS DONE IT! HE'S PULLED SUNDERLAND LEVEL! It's a sensational strike from the Italian from a seemingly impossible angle! From the right flank, on the edge of the box, he lashes a cross-cum-shot towards the far post and it smacks off the woodwork and in! It's a massive goal for the Black Cats! ---
(88’) Sunderland are lacking any real ideas in attack as the fans start to head to the exits. Barring a late miracle, it looks as though they're going to leave Wearside with nothing in advance of a tricky fixture at St. Mary's on Saturday. Crosses are flying in, but there's nothing of quality for Palace to have to defend.
(86’) STAT: The last three Premier League meetings between Crystal Palace and Sunderland have all ended as away wins.
--- 84’ Substitution A chorus of boos ring through the Stadium of Light as Connor Wickham is replaced for the final five minutes. Four goals in four days for the striker, whose brace has his former club in all sorts of hot water at the moment. Emmanuel Adebayor is on in his place. ---
(82’) Sunderland are starting to throw the kitchen sink at Palace as they go in search of an equaliser. This is hardly how Allardyce would have envisioned the final 10 minutes going at around the hour mark, but nothing this season has gone according to script for the Black Cats.
--- 80’ Substitution This is a nasty one! Cattermole is clattered into in the air and he's cut open dangerously! He's bleeding profusely from just above the eye, and with Sunderland eager to get the game going again, the substitute is replaced. Fabio Borini comes on for the final 10 minutes. ---
(79’) WASTED OPPORTUNITY! Khazri somehow weaves his way out of a tangled web in attack, and has N'Doye making a run to his right. He tries to pick out the pass that would send the forward clean through on goal, but puts too much weight behind it!
--- 77’ Substitution Little surprise here as Bolasie, who is making his first start since December, is replaced for the final 13 minutes. Bakary Sako comes on to make his return from injury. ---
(75’) STAT: No side has kept fewer clean sheets at home in the Premier League this season than Sunderland (2). They have not kept a clean sheet in 14 league matches (including today) and have conceded 27 goals in the process.
--- 73’ Substitution Yohan Cabaye has been far from his best tonight, and Pardew has taken notice. The Frenchman's unusually quiet showing comes to and end with Joe Ledley on to replace him. ---
(71’) This stadium has been stunned into silence. Sunderland now trail a match which they looked in complete control of 10 minutes ago, all thanks to a striker whom they let walk during the summer. It's an absolute nightmare for the Black Cats!
(69’) OUCH! Mannone feels the full force of Wickham's boot, bravely diving into a challenge as he takes a kick in the head for his troubles. We saw how hard the forward can strike the ball just second ago, so that certainly has to hurt the Sunderland keeper.
--- 67’ Goal! HE'S DONE IT AGAIN! Wickham unleashes a volley from in close, following Kone's inability to clear from a corner, and Palace have turned this around! The forward is back at the Stadium of Light to terrorize Sunderland - he's got two more and the Eagles are flirting with a first league win of 2016! ---
(65’) It hasn't been the best of second halves, but it's perfectly poised for the final 25 minutes. Three points are of the essence for both teams, and there's really no telling who - if anyone - will come out on top at the moment.
--- 64’ Substitution Lee Cattermole's introduction is met by a loud applause by the home fans. The Sunderland cult hero replaces Kirchhoff for the final 25 minutes. ---
(63’) STAT: Crystal Palace have not won any of their last 10 Premier League matches in which they trailed at half-time (D2, L8).
--- 61’ Assist Bolasie has been on the fringes for much of the match, but when he has got on the ball he's managed to create - and it's no different this time around as he's credited with the assist. ---
--- 61’ Goal! AN EMPHATIC STRIKE AND PALACE ARE LEVEL! Wickham revives the Eagles' hopes at his old stomping ground, taking a pass inside the area, cutting inside Kone and punishing the ball in at the far post! He struck that with all sorts of venom! ---
(60’) Pardew has to make a change. Their midfield trio has been void of life this evening. They've contributed next to nothing in terms of creativity, leaving Bolasie and Wickham starved of service. If they aren't interested in competing, they shouldn't be left out there.
(58’) Every glimmer of life for Palace is followed by a period of comfortable possession for Sunderland, as they suck the momentum away from the visitors. Pardew is screaming at his players to push higher up and make life more difficult on the hosts, but they seem uninterested at the moment.
(56’) Better from the visitors! They win the ball just inside the Sunderland end and break forward straight away. Zaha tries his luck from distance with a rather ambitious strike, which Kaboul is able to turn aside. The ex-Manchester United forward appeals for a handball and a penalty, but he was never going to get that decision.
(54’) Sunderland remain on the front foot, searching for the second goal that would surely put this game to bed. Palace have a sense of nervousness about them, dropping deeper in defence as the Black Cats are allowed all the time in the world to pass the ball around in the attacking half.
(52’) STAT: Sunderland have won six Premier League games so far this season; just one away from their whole season tally in 2014-15 (7).
(50’) The tempo hasn't picked up where it left off at the end of the first half, however. Palace have a bit of urgency about them, but it hasn't translated into a much needed boost in attacking quality. It's all been rather straightforward for Sunderland thus far at the back.
(48’) Palace start the half well, but it's Sunderland again who carve out the first chance. Khazri is proving a real spark in the final third, consistently picking out a decent final ball. He's involved again as N'Doye gets played into the area via the right channel, but his shot deflects behind for a corner.
(46’) Back underway at the Stadium of Light!
HALF-TME: SUNDERLAND 1-0 CRYSTAL PALACE. The Black Cats lead at the interval thanks to Dame N'Doye's first goal for the club. It was aided by a generous deflection off Dann, but it's no less than they deserve in the end. There's plenty still to play at the Stadium of Light, but Sunderland are on their way out of the bottom three as things stand.
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card Dann's tough first half continues as he goes into the book for a cynical challenge on Van Aanholt. He'll be relieved to see these opening 45 minutes come to an end. ---
(45’) There will be just one minute added on at the end of the first half.
(44’) STAT: Sunderland haven't won back-to-back games at the Stadium of Light since May 2014.
(42’) The visitors are lacking width in attack, surprisingly so, as Bolasie and Zaha struggle to navigate space on the flanks. Sunderland are doing an excellent job of defending, while consistently posing a threat on the counter - and they have this stadium buzzing!
(40’) Palace, who have conceded in every one of their eight Premier League games in 2016 so far, are in danger of falling two behind before the interval. They were three down at half-time at the Hawthorns on the weekend before nearly storming back in the second half, but they can't afford these slow starts to continue.
(38’) Sunderland very much in the ascendency in this match, buoyed by their opener. Another encouraging passage of play is led by Defoe, who gets on the end of the move as well, but his shot from in close is collected safely by Hennessey. Palace are venturing into dangerous territory here.
--- 36’ Goal! SUNDERLAND BREAK THROUGH AT THE STADIUM OF LIGHT! Defoe draws all sorts of attention atop the area, which allows him to slide a pass over to N'Doye in acres of space. The forward takes it first-time, trying to place it in at the far post, but it winds up taking a wicked deflection off Dann, leaving Hennessey wrong-footed. Palace's misery continues here in Wearside! ---
--- 36’ Assist Defoe picks up the assist - good vision and unselfish play from the striker who could well have had a shot himself. ---
(34’) STAT: Crystal Palace haven't won any of their last 10 Premier League games (D3, L7) and have collected the fewest points of any side in their last 10 PL matches (3).
(32’) Speculative from N'Doye! It's a bit disappointing in the end, actually, as the Senegal international drives forward on a break and tests his luck from close to 30-yards out, rolling a strike into the hands of Hennessey. He has Khazri making a good run to his right and would have been wise to try and pick him out.
(30’) OUTSTANDING SAVE! It's a masterful piece of goalkeeping from Vito Mannone, who reacts brilliantly to get a strong hand to Dann's headed effort following a Cabaye corner. That was a great header from the centre-half, who thought he had himself a goal the second he made contact.
--- 28’ Substitution Bit of a blow here for Sunderland, as their rock at the back in John O'Shea is unable to continue. He's a warrior, no doubt about it, but a sensible one at that. He goes to ground with a leg injury and knows almost straight away he can't continue, signalling over to the touchline for a change. Younes Kaboul replaces him. ---
(26’) Has to be better! Khazri drives forward and draws the attention of a couple defenders, before squaring for M'Vila. The midfielder hesitates for a moment to allow the run of N'Doye to come to fruition, which he picks out appropriately. The forward has a clean look at goal, but gets it all wrong in the end as he was always leaning back, lifting a strike well over the bar.
(24’) Past the midway point of the first half, and although there haven't been any goals to speak of, it has been a widely entertaining contest thus far. The pace remains altogether lively, while both teams have been keen to stretch the game and attack with pace. Surely the breakthrough isn't too far on the horizon.
(22’) Bolasie's presence is felt for the first time, holding the ball up well before picking out an admirable through-ball for Mutch. The midfielder finds himself on a bit of a tight angle as he tries to squeeze the ball in at the near post, but Mannone has it covered.
(20’) This match is taking on the feel of a cage fight! The tackles are flying in and there certainly isn't a shortage of passion out on the pitch. It's a massive game that both teams can't afford to lose, and these players are certainly up for the occasion.
--- 18’ Yellow card Rodwell is issued a caution for the cynical challenge - the first booking of the match. ---
(18’) It's all starting to kick-off! Yedlin is hacked down at one end, but Anthony Taylor doesn't go to his pocket. The ensuing free-kick is dealt with and leads to a Palace break, but Rodwell dangerously takes out Zaha from behind, which leads to a coming together near the halfway line! Tempers boiling over here, with Cabaye and Rodwell at the heart of it.
(16’) STAT: A whopping 15 of Crystal Palace's 29 goals this season have come from set-pieces.
(15’) PANIC! Palace pose a real threat from set-pieces and they show just why here, as a flat delivery is flicked on by Wickham towards the far post, where Delaney meets it. The defender is unable to beat Mannone from a tight angle, however, before Kirchhoff is able to scramble clear. O'Shea was all over Wickham there as the rebound came into the centre, but the referee didn't spot it.
(13’) GOOD HIT! The tempo is picking up again, as the teams exchange promising attacks. Rodwell gets on the end of a clever passage of play at the other end, before driving a strike at goal from 20-yards out. He makes wonderful contact, but it's too close to the centre as Hennessey manages to make the save.
(11’) DAZZLING FOOTWORK! That's truly exceptional from Zaha, who changes direction no fewer than five or six times on the flank to see him past two defenders and into the area. It's a brilliant bit of skill, but a slight deflection takes the sting out of the shot in the end as it runs safely into the hands of Mannone.
(9’) OVER FROM ZAHA! Jedinak and Cabaye combine in midfield, with the latter playing Zaha into the area. It looks for a second like it's going to fall kindly for the winger, but Van Aanholt does enough to put him off, forcing the shot well over the bar from a promising position.
(7’) STAT: Sunderland have conceded a league-high nine goals in the opening 15 minutes of matches.
(5’) Decent effort from the full-back! Van Aanholt, who has shown impressive attacking ability this season, makes another teasing run on the overlap which winds up resulting in a bit of panic for Hennessey. His cross-cum-shot has wicked bend behind it, but winds up swerving just a few feet wide of the far post, with the keeper scrambling to get across.
(3’) Encouraging stuff from Sunderland in the early stages, starting very aggressively as they look to challenge the Crystal Palace defence. They're showing great energy as well, but a few suspect passes have let them down in the final third.
(1’) Sunderland get the game underway, attacking left to right.

Hello and welcome to live coverage from the Stadium of Light as Sunderland attempt an escape from the bottom three when they play host to a Crystal Palace side hoping to avoid being dragged back into the relegation picture. The Black Cats are just a point from safety, while recent form suggests they are trending in the right direction. AND THAT'S IT! Swansea have taken a massive result that eases their relegation fears just a little, as they move provisionally six points clear of the drop zone. But even the tactics of the TV producers can't silence the deafening boos that have erupted in anger around this stadium. Arsenal have simply thrown it away, especially with Spurs and City losing on the night as well. Shockingly, after their draw yesterday, it's Leicester who are the big winners of midweek action. That's all the time we have, thanks for tuning in!
(90’) Arsenal win a free-kick on the right side. It was from this position and around this time that Ozil clipped in the winner fo Welbeck against Leicester, but it's not to be, as Fabianski punches clear.
(90’) WIDE OF THE POST! Welbeck attacks a cross from Walcott, but the latter angled it in with his weaker left foot and without any power, leaving the former with too much to do, and he can't convert.
(90’) Keep in mind that this will be the third straight time that Swansea have come to the Emirates and emerged with a result - and the second consecutive win for them. A massive three points is moments away for the Welsh club.
(90’) Halfhearted appeals for an Arsenal penalty as Ramsey goes crashing down in the area, and it did appear that Routledge came in a bit late on the Welshman. However, the next time the referee blows the whistle is to call a foul against Giroud. You can guess how the crowd took that one.
--- 90’ Substitution Late Swansea change as Ayew is withdrawn for Angel Rangel. ---
(88’) FREE HEADER...but comfortably held by Fabianski. From a corner, the ball was attacked by Walcott, but he simply did not generate any sort of power to trouble his former team-mate.
(86’) MASSIVE header fron Naughton, as Giroud led a queue of three Arsenal players racing onto Ozil's excellent ball towards the back post. However, the ex-Tottenham man makes it safe!
(84’) Bellerin, Ramsey and Ozil combine, with the German slipping a pass out to Monreal on the overlap out wide. However, the Spaniard's cross is well over the head of Giroud at the back post.
(82’) Swansea fans will be relieved to hear that relegation rivals Newcastle have gone a goal down to Stoke. For Arsenal, this score-line gets even more bitter with Tottenham and Man City both still trailing in their respective games.
(80’) The atmosphere inside this stadium is absolutely poisonous as we enter the closing stages. The fans have every right to be seething - this is simply unacceptable for a team that wants to be taken seriously as title challengers.
(78’) Giroud takes the ball on the turn inside the area, and decides to lay the ball off to Monreal, but the full-back's left-footed attempt is slid over the bar. There's just no confidence whenever Arsenal take a shot.

(76’) SAVED BY FABIANSKI! Ozil plays a corner to Giroud, but the Frenchman is at least 12 yards out at the near post, and tries to head it across to the opposite corner. There's not enough power on it though.

--- 74’ Goal! SWANSEA HAVE COMPLETED THE TURNAROUND! Sigurdsson whips in an absolute diamond of a delivery, and Williams arrives ahead of two defenders and the goalkeeper to bundle it home! ---
(72’) OFF THE CROSSBAR! The Gunners have a free-kick just on the outside of the area, but Alexis' effort takes a deflection and rebounds off the woodwork - the third time that the Gunners have hit it in this game!

(68’) SIGURDSSON CAN'T CONVERT! Arsenal fall asleep as Gabriel is bypassed on the right-hand side, before the substitute races past a planted Mertesacker, but lashes his finish across the face of goal, instead of into the far corner!

Naughton's cross on the overlap fails to find a team-mate, but the visitors keep the play alive and work it to Gomis on the opposite side, but the big striker fails to muster up another shooting chance.
