(42’) JUST WIDE! Payet has been superb so far this evening, and he cuts in from the left and onto his right foot. He attempts to curl a shot inside the far post, but a deflection completely wrongfoots Lloris and almost sess it sneak in on the opposite side!
--- 41’ Yellow card Both Tottenham centre-backs are now in the book, with Wimmer shown a yellow card for sending Emenike tumbling as he looked to latch onto a long ball. Had that been closer to goal it could have been a red for denying a goalscoring opportunity. ---
(40’) The referee gives Kouyate and Lamela a talking to following a coming together near the half-way line on the right-hand side of the pitch. The Senegalese was caught by a late challenge from the former Roma man, and as he got up to appeal to the referee he brushed the West Ham man's head with his knee. The defender got up and looked intent on confronting the Argentine, but his team-mates intervene and stop him in his tracks!
(38’) Payet is oozing confidence! A no-look pass from the Frenchman is meant to feed Emenike, but the Nigerian is beaten to the ball by Wimmer, who concedes a corner. It's taken short and this time the former Marseille man's delivery is too deep.
(36’) CHANCE! Payet cuts the ball back to Noble 20 yards out in a central position, but his effort is blocked by Alderweireld. The ricochet falls straight to the West Ham captain, who rolls possession on to Antonio on the right-hand side of the box. The goalscorer cuts inside but his left-footed effort, too, is kept out by a white shirt.
(34’) Mason appears to be struggling with injury and walks to the sidelines accompanied by a member of the Tottenham medical staff. However, within seconds of play restarting he jogs back onto the pitch and slots back into midfield.
(33’) West Ham probe down both the left and right flanks within the space of one minute, but neither attack proves fruitful. Noble tries to arrow a pass to the byline for the run of Kouyate, but it's overhit and the Senegalese has no chance of catching it.
(31’) Payet goes for goal from direct from the free-kick, but it lacks the requisite power to beat a goalkeeper of Lloris' stature from such a distance. The ball bounces in the box and is held comfortably by the Tottenham shot-stopper.
--- 30’ Yellow card Alderweireld is shown the game's first yellow card for a trip on Payet after the Frenchman skipped beyond him in a central position, 30 yards from goal. ---
(29’) Almost a nightmare moment for Lloris! Trippier's pass back towards him bobbles up and the Frenchman's first touch is heavy. Emenike is once again relentless in chasing possession and is narrowly beaten to it by the Tottenham goalkeeper! That was a lucky escape.
(28’) Much of the possession is now with Tottenham, who have enjoyed comfortably over 65 per cent of the ball so far this evening. Kane hasn't seen much of it, though, and the visitors are coming under pressure from long, counterattacking passes from West Ham.
(26’) Ogbonna bursts out from defence and lays a pass out to the left for Payet before surging into the box. The Frenchman throws a number of stepovers at Trippier in attempt to hold up the play before darting to the byline and drilling in a cross. However, the former Burnley right-back isn't fooled and makes an important interception which ricochets off the West Ham forward before going out for a goal-kick.
(24’) Tottenham are lacking fluidity in the final third, with Eriksen the latest player to send a stray pass into touch. If they continue to play in this manner it is unlikely they will pick up a seventh straight league victory, a feat they have not achieved since 1967.
(22’) Lanzini produces a brilliant moment of skill, controlling the ball on his chest with his back to goal before looping it over the head of an approaching defender and spinning in behind. However, he is tackled by the next Tottenham defender and his claims for a penalty are ignored by referee Andre Marriner.
(20’) Dier is caught in possession 25 yards from his own goal, but Obiang is unable to take advantage and feed Emenike. Tottenham mount a rapid counterattack but a poor pass from Chadli sees the ball roll out for a goal-kick. Another disappointing contribution from the Belgian winger.
(18’) Alderweireld clips a long ball over the top of the West Ham defence, looking to release Kane in behind. However, the striker, sporting a face mask once again this evening, was standing idle in an offside position when the Belgian hit his pass.
(16’) Lamela has indeed returned to the pitch, and with no sign of any bandaging, so the cut he sustained clearly couldn't have been too serious.
(15’) WHAT A SAVE! Noble pulls the trigger with a stinging 25-yard drive that looks set to fly into the top-right corner. Lloris leaps across his goal and gets two hands to the ball, parrying it behind for a corner! Great work from the Frenchman.
(14’) Lamela has to go off for treatment after a clash of heads with Cresswell has left him bleeding. He seems fine in himself, though, so should return to the action soon.
(13’) Antonio is playing rather deep at times, with West Ham appearing to have a three-man defence at points. Kouyate, Collins and Ogbonna are sitting back, allowing the goalscorer and Cresswell greater freedom on the wings.
(11’) West Ham have started brilliantly and will be hopeful of continuing their impressive recent form by holding onto this lead. Tottenham are yet to trouble Adrian in the opposition goal, with the Spaniard enjoying a relatively quiet night so far.
(9’) Tottenham have come from behind to claim 17 points in the Premier League this season, more than any other side. They're going to have to do so again this evening following Antonio's brilliant opener.
--- 7’ Assist Another display of Payet's brilliance from dead-ball situations, there. An exquisite delivery was headed home by Antonio, but Lanzini also deserves credit for chasing down Chadli's stray pass to earn the corner initially. ---
--- 7’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAL!!! ANTONIO IS ON TARGET AGAIN! The forward gets in front of Chadli with a run to the near post and connects with Payet's corner first. He powers a header towards the near post and, despite getting a hand to the effort, Lloris is unable to stop it hitting the back of the net! ---
(5’) Kouyate makes a brilliant defensive header, stopping Kane from connecting with a low, whipped cross by Eriksen from the right. The centre-back stuck close to the Tottenham striker and got plenty on his clearance to send it away from danger. It was a good move from the visitors to release the Dane down the wing beforehand.
(4’) West Ham are enjoying a large amount of possession in the early stages, with Tottenham already giving the ball away a couple of times inside their own half. The visitors are awarded a free-kick following an offside decision against Emenike, so Alderweireld opts to take it short and enable the visitors to get a series of touches.
(2’) Lamela shows his intentions to track back and help defend right from the off, but he cannot stop Cresswell wriggling away from Trippier and earning a free-kick near the corner flag. Payet whips the set-piece into the centre of the box but Lloris races off his line and finds a route through a host of bodies to punch it to safety.
(1’) We are underway at Upton Park!
We're just a few moments away from kick off in this London derby!
Harry Kane and Antonio could be the key players on either side tonight. The Tottenham striker has been involved in four goals in as many Premier League appearances against tonight's opponents, scoring three and assisting one, while the West Ham forward has netted four times and laid on one in his last five top-flight appearances at Upton Park.
TOTTENHAM SUBSTITUTES: Vorm, Onomah, Walker, Rose, Carroll, Alli, Son.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Trippier, Alderweireld, Wimmer, Davies; Dier, Mason; Chadli, Eriksen, Lamela; Kane.
WEST HAM SUBSTITUTES: Randolph, Henry, Dobson, Oxford, Song, Sakho, Carroll.
WEST HAM (4-3-3): Adrian; Collins, Kouyate, Ogbonna, Cresswell; Noble, Obiang, Lanzini; Antonio, Emenike, Payet.
TOTTENHAM TEAM NEWS: Dele Alli is the most notable absentee from the starting line-up for the visitors with an ankle problem consigning him to the bench - Ryan Mason has the task of filling the impressive young midfielder’s boots. Kieran Trippier and Ben Davies take up the full-back positions with Kyle Walker and Danny Rose on the bench, and the only other change sees Son Heung-min make way for Nacer Chadli.
WEST HAM TEAM NEWS: With Sam Byram suspended and Carl Jenkinson absent through injury, James Collins moves to right-back with Cheikhou Kouyate filling in at centre-back alongside Angelo Ogbonna. Pedro Obiang comes into midfield, but the front free of Michail Antonio, Emmanuel Emenike and Dmitri Payet is retained by Bilic.
West Ham, however, will be hoping for another three points in order to aid a potential bid for Champions League football next season. Slaven Bilic's team sit just four points adrift of Manchester City - who face Liverpool this evening - in fourth position, and, although Manuel Pellegrini's men have a game in hand, they will surely be harbouring hopes of breaking into the top four in the coming weeks.
Following Leicester City's 2-2 draw with West Brom last night, top spot is tantalisingly close for Tottenham. They've not led the top flight in the second half of a season since January 1985, so can they provide Pochettino with a 44th birthday to remember by moving ahead of the rest of the pack? Their advantage over Claudio Ranieri's team would only be on goal difference, though.
Hello and welcome to this evening's LIVE commentary as West Ham entertain Premier League title hopefuls Tottenham at Upton Park. Mauricio Pochettino's side can move to the summit of the top-flight with three points tonight, but to do it they will have to overcome a side that has lost just twice in its last 18 outings in all competitions.

Loud cheers and rousing applause rings around Anfield as the two sets of players make their way off the pitch, and it's certainly coming from the home fans after they witnessed an excellent display by their side. Liverpool were fantastic from start to finish, and they did everything right to punish a City team that just didn't turn up. Time and time again the visitors were picked apart by the hard-working hosts, who pressed brilliantly to constantly frustrate their opponents and disrupt their rhythm. As a result, Aguero spent the vast majority of the night as a spectator, whilst the majority of the action happened deep inside the Citizens' half of the pitch, where they struggled defensively.
FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 3-0 MANCHESTER CITY
(90’) Aguero tries to push forward on one last attacking move down the left flank, but he's completely isolated and eventually has the ball poked away from him by a well-timed tackle from Flanagan before the referee brings an end to City's misery with the final blow of his whistle.
(90’) What an excellent effort by Allen! Benteke brings down a lofted pass forward and out-muscles Otamendi before teeing up the Welshman, who immediately unleashes a thumping volley that flies over the head of Hart before narrowly missing the top of the crossbar. That would have been an excellent way to wrap up tonight's thrashing!
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(89’) Navas battles his way down the right flank before earning a corner after forcing Henderson into poking the ball out of play. It's flung by the aforementioned Spaniard into the heart of the penalty area, but it fails to find a black shirt and is easily dealt with by the hosts.
--- 87’ Substitution Milner, who has been excellent tonight, receives a rousing round of applause from the home fans as he's replaced by Ibe for the final few minutes of the game. ---
(85’) So close from Henderson! Once again, Kompany climbs all over Benteke and gives away a free-kick in a dangerous position, this time just a few yards outside of the City penalty area. The Liverpool captain steps up and unleashes a wonderful strike that curls round the wall and looks set for the bottom left-hand corner of the net, but it ends up flying marginally wide of the goal. What a goal that would have been!
(83’) What was that from Kompany?! The left-back breaks down the wing on a great run as City push forward on what looks as if it could be a dangerous counter-attack, but he ends up firing an awful cross-cum-shot miles away from Aguero and over the top of the crossbar, much to the annoyance of the Argentine striker.
(81’) Kompany and Benteke are involved in a wrestling match midway inside the City half of the pitch, and it's the latter who wins the free-kick after being dragged to the ground by his fellow Belgian. Liverpool decide to take the set-piece short and send the ball down the left flank, but they're unable to get a cross away before the visitors win back possession.
(79’) City, who look to have lost all belief and are now limping over the finish line, try to push forward down the right flank through Aguero, but the Argentine, who is arguably the only of the visitors' players who is still trying, is unable to find a way past Clyne and ends up fouling the makeshift left-back deep inside the Liverpool half of the pitch.
(77’) Liverpool are now largely sitting deep and defending their comfortable lead, but they're able to push forward on a well-worked attacking move. Once again, Lallana plays an important role in it before Allen tries to tee up Benteke with a quick through-ball, but it's slightly overhit and fails to find the Belgian before being cut out by Hart at the near post.
--- 75’ Substitution Firmino, who has been absolutely excellent all night, is replaced by Allen for the final quarter of an hour. ---
--- 74’ Substitution City have made their final alteration of the game, with Clichy making way for Kolarov. The Serbian should give them more of an attacking threat down the left wing as they desperately try to find a way back into the contest. ---
(72’) Toure's clearance results in a throw-in for City on the left wing, and they take it quickly before sending it over to Aguero. The Argentine then tries to tee up Bony with a deep cross over to the far post, but it's completely mishit and ends up flying harmlessly out of play for a goal-kick.
(71’) What an excellent tackle by Toure! Aguero, who has had a miserable game thus far, picks up the ball just outside of the Liverpool penalty area and quickly skips past Lovren before penetrating the box. He then heads towards goal before looking to shoot, but just as he's about to he's dispossessed by a wonderful interception by the Ivorian, who out-muscles the striker brilliantly.
--- 69’ Substitution Origi receives a standing ovation from the Liverpool fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Benteke for the final 20 minutes of the game. ---
--- 68’ Yellow card It's heating up on the pitch! Lallana and Navas have a coming together after the former out-muscles the latter whilst they battle for the ball near the halfway line, and it results in an angry response from the Spaniard, who receives a yellow card as a result. ---
(67’) The visitors come back once again, this time through Iheanacho on the left flank, but the young striker is unable to find a way past Flanagan, who blocks his path well, and eventually sends a looping cross straight into the hands of Mignolet in the middle of the Liverpool penalty area.
(65’) City are finally able to break out of their own half of the pitch and push forward on an attacking move, but they take far too long on the ball and are unable to find a way through the sea of red shirts camped in front of them. With a mountain to climb if they are to find a way back into the game, the visitors are going to have to start playing with far more urgency both on and off the ball.
(63’) Another chance for Milner! Lallana holds up the ball near to the byline inside the visitors' penalty area before teeing up Clyne, who immediately knocks the ball back to the former City man. He then weaves his way through a sea of black shirts before unleashing a thumping strike, but his effort ends up flying just wide of the near post.
(61’) City just can't break out of their own half of the pitch. They desperately try to break forward but, as has been the case all evening long, they are immediately put under an incredible amount of pressure by Liverpool, who are defending wonderfully in the middle of the pitch.
(59’) What a strike by Milner! Once again, an awful touch by Otamendi gifts possession to Liverpool, who take advantage of the centre-back's mistake. The aforementioned midfielder picks up the ball just outside of the box before unleashing a rocket of a shot from 25 yards out that Hart is just about able to tip over the top of the crossbar with a fingertip save.
--- 57’ Assist Once again, Lallana played a vital role in that goal. The Englishman has been excellent all game long and showed great vision to read the play well before teeing up Firmino perfectly. ---
--- 57’ Goal! GOAL! It's gone from bad to worse for City! A terrible touch by Otamendi sends the ball into the feet of Henderson, who then quickly sends a pass towards Origi. The striker holds the ball up well before teeing up Lallana, who breaks forward and sets up Firmino, and the Brazilian is then easily able to beat Hart with a side-footed shot from just inside the penalty area. ---
--- 55’ Substitution Pellegrini has decided to make another attacking change, with Fernandinho making way for Iheanacho. ---
(54’) Almost a good chance for Silva! Fernandinho and Aguero play a lovely one-two just outside of the Liverpool box before the latter tries to tee up the aforementioned Spaniard on the left-hand side of the penalty area, but his poked pass is sent slightly in front of the attacking midfielder and fails to find his feet before being cut out by Milner.
(53’) Liverpool come back once again and keep alive a positive attacking move thanks to good play by Origi and Lallana on the edge of the City box. Milner then tries to tee up the Belgian striker with a pass back into the penalty area, but it's poorly hit and is easily cut out by Fernando before it can find the youngster.
(51’) The Kop scream for a free-kick, but nothing is given! Liverpool patiently work their way down the left flank before Milner darts along the City penalty area. He tries to send a low cross into the box but is seemingly pushed to the ground by Kompany before he can do so, but the referee ignores the pleas for a foul and allows play to go on, much to the annoyance of the hosts.
(49’) Chance for Origi! Milner receives the ball in acres of space just outside of the City penalty area after Otamendi commits himself far too early, and the midfielder then pokes a quick pass into the path of the Belgian striker. He heads towards goal before unleashing a rocket of a low shot, but Hart is just about able to push the strike away from danger with a strong diving save.
(47’) Liverpool immediately break forward on a blisteringly quick attack from the start, with Origi doing well to penetrate the right-hand side of the City penalty area. The Belgian then tries to cut the ball back to Firmino, but it marginally misses the Brazilian before Zabaleta is able to cut out the danger at the far post.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
--- 46’ Substitution City have made one change during the half-time break, with Sterling, who made very little impact during the first period, making way for Bony. It looks as if the visitors are going to switch to a 4-4-2 formation. ---
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half.
It's been an excellent first half for Liverpool, who head into the break with a well-deserved two-goal lead after making life incredibly difficult for City. The hosts have continually pressed extremely hard, which has resulted in their opponents finding little joy when breaking forward. Navas and Silva have enjoyed a few good moments in front of goal, but overall it's been a tough 45 minutes for them, whilst, bar his late header, Aguero has seen very little of the ball. At the other end of the pitch the Reds have hit the visitors on the counter in very effective fashion, and the pace of Firmino and Lallana has constantly caused problems for the Citizens' struggling back four.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 MANCHESTER CITY
(45’) Vital stop by Milner! Silva tries to muscle his way down the left wing before being clumsily fouled by Firmino, resulting in a free-kick for City in a very dangerous position just outside of the Liverpool penalty area. The Spaniard sends a chipped cross into the middle of the box, where it finds Aguero in front of goal, but the Argentine's first-time header is saved by the chest of the aforementioned Englishman before it can find the bottom right-hand corner of the net.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
(44’) Clyne breaks down the left wing in space before poking a lovely pass into the path of Firmino. The Brazilian heads towards the byline and then cuts the ball back to Lallana, but just as the latter midfielder fires his first-time shot over the top of the crossbar the linesman's flag is raised for offside against the former Hoffenheim man.
(42’) City try to push forward from the restart but, as has been the case for the vast majority of the game thus far, it fails to result in a chance on goal due to great pressing by Liverpool. The hosts have done wonderfully well to continually frustrate their opponents, who have looked incredibly average so far this evening.
--- 40’ Assist Once again, it was great work by Liverpool to quickly break down the right wing, but Firmino was left in far too much space, as there were no City players tracking his run. As a result, it made life extremely easy for the Brazilian, and he punished the visitors accordingly. ---
--- 40’ Goal! GOAL! Liverpool have doubled their lead! Lallana holds up the ball well down the left wing and takes both Otamendi and Clichy out of the game before sending a back-heeled pass towards Firmino. The Brazilian picks up possession and charges towards the penalty area before sending a lovely ball over to Milner, who skips past Kompany and into the box before poking a low shot into the bottom of the net. It's all gone wrong for City, who now have a big job on their hands! ---
(38’) Navas does well to get down the right wing once again before launching a deep cross over towards Fernandinho, but it misses the head of the Brazilian by the narrowest of margins before bouncing out to the left flank. Liverpool then try to break away on a quick counter-attack through Origi, but the striker is unable to find a way past Otamendi, who does well to keep the Belgian youngster at bay deep inside the City half of the pitch.
(36’) Almost another chance for Liverpool! The hosts quickly win back the ball from the restart and immediately push forward on a quick counter-attack. Milner cuts inside from the right flank before launching a looping cross over towards Firmino, but the Brazilian is unable to meet the ball with an outstretched foot before the linesman's flag is raised for offside.
--- 34’ Assist Milner did well to pick out Lallana after seeing that he was free and in acres of space, but questions have to be asked of the City holding midfielders, both of whom were nowhere to be seen after completely falling asleep. ---
--- 34’ Goal! GOAL! What a wonderful strike by Lallana! Liverpool patiently pass the ball around inside the City half of the pitch under no pressure whatsoever from the visitors. Milner then cuts inside from the right wing before teeing up the former Southampton midfielder, who is in acres of space in the middle. He's able to jog forward, which he does, before unleashing a thumping low shot that flies past the outstretched hand of Hart and into the bottom left-hand corner of the net. ---
(32’) Again, City work the ball around really well but are let down by a poor final ball. Fernandinho muscles his way towards the edge of the penalty area and plays a nice one-two with Aguero before the Argentine tees up Silva, who then tries to poke a pass back to the striker. It's overhit, however, and rolls past its intended target before being cut out by Mignolet.
(30’) Fernandinho breaks into the left-hand side of the Liverpool penalty area before cutting the ball back to Silva, who is in a great position in front of the goal. He takes a quick touch before looking to shoot, but instead of doing so he tries to tee up Aguero near the penalty spot. The Spaniard's pass is the wrong decision, however, and it's well cut out by Milner before it can find the Argentine striker.
(28’) City patiently work their way down the left wing as they try to find their way past Henderson, Milner and Flanagan, all of whom are sitting deep in an attempt to frustrate Clichy and Sterling. The former Liverpool youngster then cuts inside before unleashing a speculative strike from 30 yards out, but it's poorly hit and Mignolet is able to watch it sail comfortably wide of the goal.
(26’) Can is left in acres of space midway inside the City half of the pitch, allowing him to pick up the ball under no pressure whatsoever before trying to pick out Flanagan with a 30-yard through-ball. The full-back makes a great run down the right wing in an attempt to latch on to the pass, but there's slightly too much power on it and he's unable to do so before it rolls out of play.
(24’) Almost a great opportunity for Aguero! Once again, Navas, who has arguably been the only effective City player thus far, breaks down the right-hand side of the pitch before firing a low cross through the legs of Clyne. His pass also beats the outstretched hand of Mignolet before flying over to the far post, but it ends up missing the Argentine by the narrowest of margins before going out for a goal-kick.
(22’) City are finally able to push forward on a dangerous attacking move thanks to good play by Navas on the right-hand side of the Liverpool penalty area. He holds up the ball well before teeing up Zabaleta, who charges towards the byline and fires a thumping cross towards the edge of the six-yard box. It looks set to find Aguero in front of goal, but Mignolet is just about able to tip it away from danger with a vital diving save.
(21’) A half-hearted attack down the right from Liverpool fails to result in a chance on goal due to a misunderstanding between Henderson and Flanagan, allowing City to pick up the ball near the halfway line. They try to break away on a quick counter through the middle of the pitch, but Silva is quickly closed down by Can and is dispossessed before he can pick out a teammate.
(19’) The resulting set-piece is flung into the middle of the box, where Hart is just about able to get a hand on the ball to send it away from the head of Origi. It then bounces out to Sterling, who quickly sends a thumping clearance out of play for a Liverpool throw-in midway inside the City half of the pitch.
(18’) City remain camped deep inside their own half of the pitch as they aim to keep at bay a determined Liverpool side. The hosts work the ball around well before Flanagan cuts inside and tees up Lallana, and the winger, who is left in far too much space on the right wing, is allowed to penetrate the penalty area before firing a chipped cross off Otamendi and out for a corner.
(16’) It's been an impressive opening 16 minutes for Liverpool, who have looked strong both on and off the ball. As a result, City have found it incredibly difficult to push forward, as the hosts are constantly pressing high up the pitch to put them under plenty of pressure.
(14’) Clyne twists and turns on the left-hand side of the City penalty area, but he's unable to find a way past Navas and Zabaleta, which forces him into spinning and playing the ball back to Can. The German then quickly chips a pass over the head of the aforementioned duo and towards Milner, who had made a swift dart into the box, but it's slightly overhit and the Englishman is unable to make contact with the ball before it bounces out of play for a goal-kick.
(12’) Sterling bursts down the left wing on a great run before being cynically barged to the ground by Flanagan, resulting in a free-kick for City in a dangerous position. The set-piece is curled into the heart of the penalty area, where it finds Fernandinho, but the Brazilian's header ends up bouncing comfortably wide of the goal.
(10’) Liverpool work the ball around well inside the City half of the pitch before Henderson tries to thread a through-ball into the path of Origi, who had made a good run forward, but the midfielder's attempted pass is completely overhit and can only find the hands of Hart in the middle of the goal.
(8’) Origi charges into the City half of the pitch as he tries to latch on to a bouncing ball forward, but Kompany is there to cut out the danger at the vital moment. The centre-back then tries to break away on a quick counter-attack, but Lallana ends up dragging him back by the shirt and the visitors are awarded a free-kick near the halfway line as a result.
(6’) Origi muscles his way through the middle of the pitch and heads towards the City penalty area before being tripped over by Otamendi, resulting in another free-kick for Liverpool in a dangerous position. Milner tries to pick out the Belgian with his ball into the box but Fernandinho is there to clear the danger before Lallana fires a follow-up cross out of play for a goal-kick.
(4’) Sterling has already been on the receiving end of two crunching challenges during the opening exchanges, and now he's cynically pushed in the back by Firmino as the two players battle down the right flank. He can expect plenty more of that during the course of the evening, as Liverpool seem to be purposefully targeting him, and it's no surprise why.
(3’) Liverpool come back once again through a marauding run from Lallana in the middle of the pitch, but his final touch is poor and sends the ball bouncing into the hands of Hart before he can tee up Origi inside the City penalty area.
(2’) Liverpool start the game in frantic fashion and quickly win possession on the right flank before Lallana is brought down by Clichy, resulting in a free-kick for the hosts in a dangerous position not far outside of the penalty area. It's flung into the middle of the box by Henderson but the cross is comfortably cut out by the aforementioned Frenchman.
(1’) And we're off! City get us underway, attacking from left to right.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off. The atmosphere inside the stadium is electric, with both sets of fans in fine voice.
Meanwhile, City boss Manuel Pellegrini has made three alterations to the side that featured on Sunday, with Joe Hart once again taking the place of Willy Caballero, the hero of the final, in goal. Joining him in making a return to the starting line-up are Pablo Zabaleta and Jesus Navas, who feature instead of Bacary Sagna and Yaya Toure, the latter of whom is injured.
Jurgen Klopp has decided to make five changes to the Liverpool side that lost in the Capital One Cup final, with the biggest talking point being the inclusion of Jon Flanagan, who takes the place of Alberto Moreno to make his first Premier League start since May 2014. Meanwhile, Kolo Toure, Dejan Lovren, Adam Lallana and Divock Origi also come into the starting line-up to replace Lucas Leiva, Mamadou Sakho, Philippe Coutinho and Daniel Sturridge.
Manchester City substitutes: Caballero, Sagna, Kolarov, Mangala, Demichelis, Iheanacho, Bony.
Manchester City XI (4-2-3-1): Hart; Zabaleta, Otamendi, Kompany, Clichy; Fernando, Fernandinho; Navas, Silva, Sterling; Aguero.
Liverpool substitutes: Ward, Moreno, Skrtel, Allen, Ibe, Coutinho, Benteke.
Liverpool XI (4-3-3): Mignolet; Clyne, Toure, Lovren, Flanagan; Milner, Can, Henderson; Lallana, Origi, Firmino.
There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up evening…
Tonight’s game brings together one side that are struggling at home and another that are finding it difficult to pick up points away, and it means that it could be a difficult evening for both of them. Liverpool are yet to win a single league game at Anfield this calendar year, whilst they have only managed to pick up 17 points in front of their own fans this season, the same amount as 19th-place Newcastle United. City, meanwhile, have won just five of their 12 Premier League away games this campaign. However, they are unbeaten in their last four - two of which ended in victories - and they will be hoping that they can continue that good run with another positive result this evening.
As for City, back-to-back defeats against high-flying Leicester City and Tottenham Hotspur have left them 10 points behind the Foxes in fourth place, although they have two games in hand over the league leaders and will be desperate to get back to winning ways this evening. Three of Sanchez Flores' changes have come at the back, with Jose Holebas, Seb Prodl and Allan Nyom all returning, while Almen Abdi is the other to come back into the side. Dropping out are Nathan Ake, former United youngster Craig Cathcart, Juan Carlos Paredes and Nordin Amrabat, respectively.
Watford coach Quique Sanchez Flores has no such injury problems to contend with, though, as his side continue to plug away in mid-table. The Spaniard has made four changes today, however, as his side prepare for their first visit to Old Trafford since January 2007, a 4-0 defeat. He will be hoping that his alterations will go some way to preventing another such hammering.
A major boost to United is the return of Anthony Martial. The France international has missed their last two games due to a hamstring problem and he comes in today for Jesse Lingard. Although they won both games without the former Monaco man, his presence on the wing will be a serious threat. Elsewhere, Memphis Depay keeps his place in the team after two excellent outings and he will be keen to continue his resurgence.
Once again Rashford starts as the focal point of United's attack and will be eager to continue his incredible start to life in the senior side, having scored twice in both of his two previous appearances. Guillermo Varela unsurprisingly retains his place at right-back following a hugely encouraging couple of weeks, particularly against Arsenal, while there is a first Premier League start at centre-back for Timothy Fosu-Mensah. The Netherlands youth international is highly rated at the club and looked good in his cameo at the weekend, but this time around he looks set to start at centre-back as opposed to left-back, where fit-again Marcos Rojo slots in.
Manchester United's spell of decimation by injury rumbles on as they are forced to name another youthful-looking first XI today for the visit of Watford, but Louis van Gaal's need to inject some unfamiliar faces into his team has seen the club play with extra freedom and energy in their last two matches, the hammering of Midtjylland and then the entertaining, Marcus Rashford-inspired 3-2 defeat of Arsenal on Sunday. If anything, United have actually been playing better in spite of the absence of a significant amount of experience and first-team regulars.

Hello and welcome to the live text commentary for the Premier League clash between Stoke City and Aston Villa. We'll be guiding you through all the action as it happens at the Britannia Stadium.

Well, that’s all from Vicarage Road this afternoon. It has been a pleasure to bring you all the action from today’s Premier League clash, though ultimately neither side could find that bit of quality to grab a goal. Until next time, thank you and goodbye!
The result sees Watford miss out on the opportunity to move within two points of the top six, and instead the Hornets slip down into 10th place. Bournemouth, meanwhile, remain in 15th, though they are now five points clear of the relegation zone - having brought their three-match losing streak to an end. The visitors would have won it if not for a string of fine saves from Gomes, though in the end a draw was most probably a fair reflection of this afternoon's encounter - the 100th between these two sides in league competitions.
FULL TIME! It’s all over at Vicarage Road, where it has finished 0-0 between Watford and Bournemouth. It was a scrappy and closely-fought contest, with neither side having the quality needed to carve out too many clear cut opportunities, though Gomes did make several good saves to keep the visitors at bay, while, at the other end, Ighalo somehow directed a free header wide of the target.
(90’) We’re into the first of three minutes added time at the end of this game now, as Gradel looks to carve out another opportunity for himself down the left, but this time the danger is sniffed out by Paredes.
(88’) GREAT SAVE! What a chance for Bournemouth, as Gradel twists and turns in the area before drilling an effort goalwards, but Gomes displays all of his athleticism to tip the strike on to the roof of the net!
--- 87’ Yellow card Well, after going so long without reaching for his cards, the referee seems to be going wild now, as he books Cathcart for a foul on Gradel - with the Wales defender having tugged on the shirt of the diminutive Ivory Coast winger. ---
--- 85’ Substitution A third and final substitution now for the visitors, as Matt Ritchie is replaced by Glenn Murray - who netted his maiden Bournemouth goal in the reverse fixture back in October. ---
--- 84’ Yellow card Abdi’s first action of the game is to win a free-kick deep in his own half, having got clear of Surman with a neat turn before being felled by the Bournemouth midfielder, who duly goes into the referee’s book. ---
--- 83’ Substitution A final roll of the dice now from Flores, as he introduces Almen Abdi in place of Nordin Amrabat, who once again has struggled to make a real impact for his new side. ---
--- 82’ Yellow card A second yellow card now in quick succession for Watford, as Behrami is penalised for a collision with Ritchie. Again, a booking does seem rather harsh considering how lenient the official has been in this match. ---
(80’) SAVE! Another chance for Bournemouth and once more it is poor finishing that prevents them from taking the lead! King does brilliantly down the right to square up Ake before dropping a cross into the six-yard box. Gradel leaps to meet it, but rather than heading it directly at goal he elects to nod it down into the ground, allowing Gomes to dive to his right and make the stop.
(78’) CHANCE! What an opportunity that was for Gosling! The resulting free-kick is delivered into the area, with Deeney’s loose touch falling to the former Everton man, who, with his first touch of the game, can only direct his close range effort straight down the throat of Boruc.
--- 77’ Yellow card A first yellow card of the game now, as Watson goes into the book for a late tackle on Gradel. The Watford midfielder may feel a touch hard done by, however, as Taylor has let several other similar fouls by other players go without such a punishment. ---
(76’) CHANCE! Watford take a quick free-kick deep in Bournemouth’s half, with Watson feeding Ighalo. The Hornets’ top-scorer twists and turns before getting his shot off, but he cannot keep the effort down and it sails over the bar.
--- 74’ Substitution A second change now for Bournemouth, and it is a rather defensive one as Dan Gosling replaces Benik Afobe. The former Wolves striker has struggled to make an impact this afternoon, and this change seems to signal that Howe would be happy to leave Vicarage Road with a point. ---
(72’) Watford have improved noticeably since the introduction of Suarez, though Bournemouth have managed to forge a spell of possession in recent moments, which eventually leads to Ighalo fouling Arter. Suriname goes short from the set-piece, with the visitors then spreading a sweeping pass out to the left wing, but King is unable to keep it in play under pressure from Paredes.
(69’) A free-kick now in a really dangerous position for Watford, right on the edge of Bournemouth’s area following a foul on Deeney by Francis. The hosts’ captain takes charge, after being teed up by Watson, but he shanks his strike wide. That’s a waste!
(67’) WHAT A MISS!!! How did Ighalo squander that!? Amrabat does brilliantly to get the better of Daniels and drive into the area before drinking a cross directly onto the head of Ighalo. The Nigerian has more than half of the goal to aim for, but somehow skews his effort and it sails high and wide over the crossbar.
(65’) A second foul in quick succession by Smith provides Watson with an opportunity to deliver a free-kick from the left flank. He duly puts in another curling cross, which rebounds out to Suarez on the edge of the area, but the ex-Atletico Madrid midfielder’s strike is blocked. The move is eventually worked back out wide to Watson, who again drops in a cross, but Ighalo is just unable to latch onto it and Boruc comes out to smother the danger.
(63’) More lenient officiating from Taylor, this time in the visitors’ favour as Smith dives in on Ake. The Chelsea-loanee makes little of the foul, which is good to see, and that perhaps sways the referee to not award the Bournemouth man with a booking.
(61’) HANDBALL??? That’s a real let off for Watford, as Ritchie’s resulting corner bounces up in the area and clearly strikes the arm of Behrami. The former Napoli man had plenty of time to react and move out of the way of the ball, but nevertheless referee Anthony Taylor decides that it was ball-to-hand.
(60’) WHAT A SAVE! That’s fantastic from Gomes, who gets across swiftly to parry Arter’s venomous, long-range strike wide of the woodwork. The chance followed a neat passage of play from Bournemouth, who seem to have stepped up their game in recent moments, with their possession now becoming more incisive and penetrating in forward areas.
--- 57’ Substitution A first substitution of the game now for the hosts, as Flores elects to replace Etienne Capoue with Mario Suárez - a January arrival from Fiorentina. ---
(56’) GREAT DEFENDING! That’s top class, last-ditch play from Britos, who gets across to make a timely interception and prevent Gradel, who had created some space for himself in the area, from powering a finish into the roof of the net from close range.
(54’) That Bournemouth chance sparks Watford into life somewhat, as Paredes gets around Daniels with a sublime piece of skill down on the near touchline. The Ecuadorian drops in a cross to Amrabat at the back post, but the Morocco striker completely misses his attempted volley.
(53’) CHANCE! King should have done better there! A rare sight of goal for Bournemouth, who for all their possession have created very little. Ritchie does superbly to jink his way down the right flank before driving in a pin-point cross. The aforementioned forward meets it on the volley, but he can only power his effort way off-target.
(51’) An error from Britos provides Bournemouth with an opportunity to get the ball into the box from a corner, but once more the delivery from Ritchie isn’t up to par and Watford are able to clear their lines with ease. This game is still lacking some real quality...
(50’) A free-kick now for Watford, which Watson drifts in. His delivery is a decent one on this occasion, but again Cook is well-placed to head it clear. The hosts regain possession and launch a throw-in into the feet of Ighalo, who looks to tee up Amrabat, but the Moroccan’s strike is blocked by Francis.
(48’) A stuttering start to this second half, which has began in similar fashion to how the first half ended. Bournemouth eventually manage to find enough space for Arter to clip a lofted pass into King, but the Norwegian is pulled back for a foul on Britos.
(46’) We are back up and running at Vicarage Park! No changes for either side at half-time, as Watford get the second half under way. Hopefully there is a much more quality in the second 45 minutes than there were in the first!
There is definitely work to do for both managers in their half-time team talks. Bournemouth have looked to exploit space down the flanks, with Smith and Daniels both being able to get forward at will, but the land product has been lacking in quality far too often. At the other end, Deeney and Amrabat have both been anonymous, and you feel that Flores may well look to change his system to a more traditional 4-4-2 - which brought them so much success earlier in the campaign - in order to stem the visitors’ attacks and provide more of a threat going forward.
HALF-TIME! That’s all for the first half at Vicarage Road, where, in all truth, it has been a dull affair so far. The start was lively enough, with Ighalo testing Boruc with a driven effort from the cusp of Bournemouth’s area. However, that has been all that either side have been able to muster, though the visitors have seen more of the possession.
(45’) Deeney gets lucky here, as he slides in late on Smith, who looks in real pain as he receives some treatment from the Bournemouth physio, but the Watford skipper avoids the booking, with Anthony Taylor having been in a rather lenient mood so far in this game.
(43’) Another poor corner from the former Wigan midfielder, whose cross is collected with ease by Boruc. That really is wasteful from the hosts.
(42’) An opportunity for Watford now as Capoue tees up Amrabat with a precise pass. The forward jinks infield, but his resulting cross is a poor one and Cook clears it for a corner. Watson again stands over it...
(40’) It has been all Bournemouth in the last 10 minutes or so, with the hosts unable to get out of their own half. Flores’ side do eventually regain possession thanks to a well-timed tackle from Watson, who in turn feeds Capoue. The former Tottenham man lofts a looping long ball into the path of Paredes, but Daniels does well to get back and win the throw-in for the visitors.
(38’) Yet another free-kick for the visitors now, as Daniels is brought down by Amrabat. Ritchie drops in a cross, which King - after nudging Britos out of the way - latches onto, but the Norwegian miscues his strike and it trickles out harmlessly for a goal kick to Watford.
(36’) Good work from King, who manages to evade the challenge of Ake and sprint towards the byline, but his touch is too heavy and Behrami manages to clear. The loose ball falls straight to Ritchie, but the Scotland winger’s cross-field pass to Daniels is a poor one and the move breaks down. Wasteful.
(33’) One area that Bournemouth are finding some joy in is out on the flanks. Watford’s midfield trio of Capoue, Watson and Behrami are saying very central, meaning there is plenty of space and opportunity for Smith and Daniels to get forward. The latter does so once more, and wins a free-kick off Paredes in a good position. Gradel whips in the cross, but Gomes claims it with ease.
(31’) It has, in all truth, being a rather scrappy affair so far at Vicarage Road, with both sides looking to get the ball down on the deck but having cancelled each other out somewhat, meaning that opportunities have been few and far between at either end.
(28’) UNLUCKY! Watford get lucky there, as, after Watson conceded possession in midfield, King slid a neat throughball into the path of Afobe. The former Arsenal striker looked to have timed his run perfectly, with the replay duly proving that he had, but the linesman raises his flag for offside.
(26’) Fortunate for Paredes, now, as the Watford full-back clatters into Daniels with a wild challenge. The Bournemouth full-back makes little of it, and the hosts escape without even conceding a free-kick, though another referee may easily have deemed that late lunge more serious and worthy of a booking.
(25’) Behrami is furious here, claiming that he had been hit in the face by the elbow of Smith. There was indeed a collision, but nothing that would have led to the Swiss midfielder tumbling to the turf in the way he did, and the referee duly signals for play to continue.
--- 23’ Substitution As expected, Stanislas has now limped off down the tunnel. The resulting substitute is Max Gradel, who has been out since August with a knee-ligament injury. ---
(21’) INJURY. Oh that is such bad luck for Stanislas, as the Bournemouth winger pulls up with a hamstring injury. He had found himself in acres of space down the left, but it’s quite obvious he won’t be able to carry on in this game.
(19’) Good work from Bournemouth, as the visitors work a swift counter-attack wide out to Smith, whose strike from range is blocked away for a corner by Britos. Ritchie again delivers a dipping cross into the six-yard box, but Cathcart rises highest to head it clear.
(18’) Huge appeals for handball from Watford as Afobe battles with Britos on the edge of the hosts' area. There is nothing doing for the officials, though, and Bournemouth win the throw-in. However, the move is brought to an end swiftly enough as Surman is pulled back for a foul on Amrabat, who had tracked back well to regain possession.
(16’) Watford win another corner from the resulting set-piece, but once more the delivery is a tad too powerful and Bournemouth are able to clear their lines. Daniels manages to pick up some space on the inside-left, but he is stewarded out of play expertly by Watson.
(14’) Bournemouth win a corner down the right which Ritchie curls in, but Gomes collects the delivery confidently. The Brazilian immediately kick-starts a counter-attack, with Ake feeding Deeney who in turn tees it up to Amrabat. the former Malaga forward tries his luck with a first-time strike, which is deflected wide by Smith.
(11’) A promising spell of possession now for the visitors, as Arter and Surman begin to get more involved in proceedings. Cook eventually switches a long pass out to Smith, who, after doing well to keep it in cuts inside and combines with Ritchie to set up the aforementioned Arter on the egde of the area, but the midfielder can only drag his low strike wide of the left-hand upright.
(9’) CLOSE! Paredes finds some space down the right wing and duly delivers a superb dipping cross into the area. Inghalo meets it one the edge of the six-yard box, but having had to halt his run slightly to execute the volley, the former Granada man is just unable to adjust his feet quickly enough to direct his effort on target.
(7’) Great defending from Cook, as the Bournemouth centre-half manages to hold off the run of Ighalo as the Watford forward raced onto a pass from deep by Capoue, following a brief spell of possession from the hosts. (5’) Watson, making his 50th Watford appearance this afternoon, curls in the resulting set-piece, but it is over-hit and the visitors forge a swift counter-charge, with Smith leading it. (3’) GOOD SAVE! A really open start to proceedings at Vicarage Road, as Ighalo leads a Watford counter-attack. The Nigerian brushes aside his markers with ease before powering an effort goalwards from the edge of Bournemouth’s area, but Boruc does well to parry the strike away for a corner.
(2’) Promising start from the visitors, as Arter - on his 200th appearance for Bournemouth - sliding a neat throughball in-behind to King. The former Blackburn winger attempts to feed Afobe with a low cross, but Britos gets across to make the clearance.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are under Bournemouth, donning their pink away strip and attacking from left to right in the first half, getting proceedings up and running.

The atmosphere is excellent, with plenty of Bournemouth supporters having also made their way up from the south coast to this town just north of the capital. It promises to be another entertaining and enthralling Premier League encounter...

It’s a full house at Anfield, and the atmosphere is crackling with anticipation as the sides prepare to make their way out onto the pitch. While Liverpool are behind only Leicester City and Tottenham in the Premier League form table, Everton find themselves in 19th place - with only relegated Aston Villa worse off in terms of results from the last six games. A victory for Liverpool this evening could see them rise as high as sixth, should West Ham be beaten by Watford at Upton Park. Meanwhile, a win for the visitors would see the Toffees leapfrog Chelsea and move into the top half of the table.
This is the 48th Merseyside derby in the Premier Leageu era. Liverpool have won 19 of those in total, with nine wins for Everton and 19 draws. The visitors have not won at Anfield since September 1999, though the last time they played here, Phil Jagielka's stoppage time wonderstrike salvaged a point.
So, despite both sides having huge games just on the horizon, there has certainly been no indication from the team selections that either manager is thinking about anything but this evening’s encounter, with both Klopp and Martinez fielding what could be viewed as their strongest possible starting XIs given the personnel currently at their disposal. For Liverpool, Sturridge is perhaps the surprise omission, though Orgi though it seems that the young Belgian is finally starting to like up to his potential. As for the visitors, who are themselves struggling with injuries to key players such as skipper Phil Jagielka and the aforementioned Coleman, Martinez, who has drawn four and lost one of his five Merseyside derbies in charge of Everton, has provided the likes of Kevin Mirallas and Bryan Oviedo to make a case for themselves starting at Wembley on Saturday.

The team news is in from Anfield, with both sides making a raft of changes from their respective fixtures at the weekend. For the hosts, Klopp makes nine hanges in total from the line-up that started in the 2-1 win over Bournemouth on Sunday, with only Lucas Leiva and Roberto Firmino retaining their places. As for the visitors, Martinez names a more recognised starting XI compared to the one that featured in the 1-1 draw with Southampton. Gareth Barry and James McCarthy return - the latter from suspension - to sit in central midfield, while Aaron Lennon, Ross Barkley and Romelu Lukaku replace Gerard Deulofeu, Leon Osman and Arouna Kone respectively. Seamus Coleman is injured, which means Bryan Oviedo steps across to right back, and Leighton Baines takes his usual left-back berth.
Everton, on the other hand, are seeing their season swiftly fade away after another disappointing run of form. Having taken just three points form their last 18 on offer in the league, they sit in 11th - three places and 10 points behind their most fierce rivals - and there is a real feeling of discontent amongst the Toffees’ support, directed mainly at Roberto Martinez, who finds himself under increased pressure. Their campaign rests entirely on Saturday’s FA Cup semi-final against Manchester United, with the cup runs - they also reached the last four of the League Cup only to lose out to eventual winners Manchester City - having provided the only real positives from what has been another underwhelming season. Even so, a victory this evening, in a fixture they have not claimed one victory from in the last 10 attempts, would at least hand the fans and players a much-needed confidence boost ahead of their trip to Wembley.
The reverse fixture at Goodison Park back in October proved to be the last as Liverpool manager for Brendan Rodgers, who was relieved of his position later the same day following a 1-1 draw - in which Romelu Lukaku’s equaliser cancelled out Danny Ings’ opener. Clop took over the following weak, and though his side have been inconsistent, they have managed to claim a runners-up medal in the League Cup, as well as a spot in the semi-finals of the Europa League courtesy of their fantastic, last-gasp victory over Klopp’s former employers Borussia Dortmund. The German is certainly not without experience when it comes to local rivalries, having been involved in many Revierderbys during his tenure at Signal Iduna Park, and he is sure to be relishing this test as he takes charge of his first all-Merseyside clash.

(85’) SO CLOSE!!! How did he miss!? What a chance that was for Arsenal, as Ozil finds his compatriot Mertesacker with a delightful cross. The centre-back, without a goal in two years, was unmarked and unchallenged, but somehow turned his glancing header wide of the upright.
--- 83’ Substitution And there is also another change for the hosts, as Danny Welbeck - who has been out for 10 months following a knee operation - comes on to make his first appearance of the season. He replaces Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain. ---
--- 82’ Substitution A third and final change now for Leicester, as the more defensive minded Andy King comes on to replace Marc Albrighton. ---
(81’) Top quality defending from Leicester! Arsenal are mounting some serious pressure now, but the visitors are standing firm as wave after wave of red and white shirts bombard their area. Can Ranieri’s 10 men hang onto this point?
(79’) CHANCE!!! That’s dreadful from Sanchez, who completely misses his kick after Walcott had found him in acres of space in the penalty area with a neat cut-back. The rebound almost finds its way through to Giroud, but Schemichel comes out swiftly to smother the ball.
(77’) Unlucky! Another great break from Leicester, once again lead by Vardy, who twists and turns his way into the area before laying it back to the supporting Kante. The midfielder elects to try his luck with a curling strike, but Cech has it covered as he watches it sail harmlessly wide.
(74’) CHANCE! What a miss from Ramsey! Morgan does well to prevent Giroud netting with an audacious bicycle kick, from which the rebound falls to the aforementioned midfielder. The former Cardiff man blasts his effort golawards, but he can only skew it wide of the left-hand post.
(72’) Some controversy now, as Ramsey bombards the referee claiming that he had been fouled by Drinkwater. The Leicester man had definitely won the ball, though his momentum did lead to a rather high challenge on the Welshman, but the official did not choose to go to his book.
--- 70’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLL!!! WALCOTT DRAGS ARSENAL LEVEL! Well, for all their hard work, Leicester’s defence is finally undone as the Arsenal substitute latches onto a knock-down from Giroud before dispatching a superb finish past Schmeichel. That was the hosts’ first attempt on target this afternoon! ---
--- 70’ Assist It was a neat assists from Giroud, who cushioned a header perfectly into Walcott, who duly made no mistake with a powerful finish into the far corner. ---
(69’) While Leicester’s job certainly has been made more difficult due to that sending off, their system, as it were, has not actually altered that much. Vardy is still sitting high upfield, meaning that Arsenal are having to leave at least two players back to deal with the pace of the striker.
(67’) Montreal appears to run the ball out of play down the left before hooking a cross back into the area which Morgan deflects wide, though the officials - despite the appeals of the Leicester players - deem that the Spain full-back had kept the ball in. Ozil delivers from the resulting corner, but Kante manages to hook it out of danger.
(65’) Almost an opportunity for Leicester! The forward elects to go for goal with a crisp early effort from 20 yards out, but Cech is equal to it. The England man may have been better off trying to hold the ball up there rather than going for glory.
--- 62’ Substitution And there is now a first change of the game for Arsenal, as Wenger elects to replace Francis Coquelin with Theo Walcott as the hosts search for an equaliser. ---
--- 61’ Substitution A second substitution now for Leicester, as Shinji Okazaki makes way for the former Birmingham City youngster Demarai Gray. ---
(60’) The game has transformed from a free-flowing affair into a scrappy encounter in the last 10 minutes or so - mainly due to the sending off and the resulting changes. Arsenal eventually manage to carve out an opportunity on the edge of Leicester’s area, but Ozil’s touch is heavy and Drinkwater gets it clear.
--- 58’ Substitution A first change of the game now for Leicester, as Riyad Mahrez - who can consider himself unlcuky not to have won a penalty less than 10 minutes ago - is replaced by the veteran defender Marcin Wasilewski. The Arsenal man gets away with it, but he can consider himself very lucky considering that he is already on a yellow card. ---
--- 57’ Yellow card A booking now for Kante, after he had brought down Ozil. Martin Atkinson at first seemed not to book the Frenchman, but after a pause to think - during which he was bombarded by Arsenal’s players - he elects to award the yellow card. ---
--- 54’ Red card! RED CARD! Well, what a huge decision this is from Martin Atkinson, as he chooses to give Simpson his marching orders after the former Manchester United defender had pulled on the shirt of Giroud. It really does seem an incredibly harsh decision, and Leicester will now have to hang on with 10 men for the rest of this game! ---
--- 52’ Yellow card A second booking now for Leicester, as Christian Fuchs gets a yellow card for a late lunge on Giroud, who had already played in Oxlade-Chamberlain, but the England winger could not apply the finish. ---
(51’) SURELY THAT’S A PENALTY!? Mahrez picks up possession and, for the first time this game, finally manages to drive at Monreal. He completely fools the Arsenal defender with a sublime bit of footwork before being caught by the full-back’s trailing leg, but the referee waives away the appeals for a second Leicester penalty.
--- 49’ Yellow card A first booking of the game now for Leicester, as Danny Simpson goes into the book for a foul on Sanchez. The hosts watse the free-kick, however, and Drinkwater manages to hook a fantastic pass into the path of Vardy, who harrasses Bellerin into conceding a throw-in deep in Arsenal's territory. Great work from the visitors! ---
(48’) Confirmation of that injury to Koscielny, now, with the Arsenal man having picked up a dead-leg in that collision with Kante in the build-up to Leicester’s penalty.
(47’) SO CLOSE! What a chance for Arsenal straight from the restart! Sanchez works his way down the left before sliding a pass into Giroud, who goes for goal with a sweeping first-time effort that Drinkwater blocks with an excellent sliding challenge. The rebound falls out to Ramsey, but the Wales midfielder drags his strike wide of the left-hand upright.
--- 46’ Substitution Second-half! Leicester get this fantastic game back under way at the Emirates. This is set to be a huge 45 minutes in the Premier League title race! Arsenal have been forced into a chnage at the interval, with the injured Laurent Koscielny being replaced by Calum Chambers. ---
Arsenal may well feel aggrieved that they were not awarded a free-kick in the build-up to the penalty incident, however, as Morgan had lent slightly upon the shoulders of Ozil to win a header. A foul would have seemed very harsh, though, and the hosts can only have themselves to blame for not defending the resulting counter-attack. Lots of work to do for Wenger in his half-time team talk!
It has been a superb display from Leicester, who soaked up the Arsenal pressure throughout before using their pace on the counter-attack to quite devastating effect. Kante has been particularly impressive, with the former Caen midfielder having dominated the centre of the park so far, and it was his industry and tenacity that set up Vardy to win the penalty - the visitors’ 10th spot-kick of the campaign.
HALF-TIME! What a first half for Leicester, who have taken the lead in the final moments of the opening 45 minutes courtesy of Vardy’s excellent penalty. Arsenal started brightly, but Ranieri’s side held their ground and in all truth created the more clear-cut chances, and are more than worthy of their lead.
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Another booking now for Arsenal - a third of the game for the hosts - as Ramsey picks up a yellow card for a hefty challenge on Okazaki. ---
--- 45’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!!! What a finish by Vardy, who sends Cech the wrong way with a venomoulsy-driven penalty into the bottom-right corner. Arsenal 0-1 Leicester!!! ---
--- 44’ Yellow card During the penalty incident, there was also a late lunge by Koscielny on Kante, and the Arsenal centre-back has duly recieved a yellow card for that foul. ---
(43’) PENALTY TO LEICESTER!!! WHAT A MOVE FROM THE VISITORS! Kante does superbly to beat Koscielny to the ball and poke a pass into the path of Vardy. The England striker stands up Monreal before jinking his way around the Spaniard, who can do nothing but take him down, with Martin Atkinson pointing straight to the spot!
(40’) Mahrez whips in the resulting set-piece from the right flank, which Huth rises highest to latch onto, but the powerful German centre-back cannot direct his effort on target and Arsenal escape unscathed.
(39’) WHAT AN EFFORT! Leicester again launch a swift counter-charge that results in Mahrez holding the ball up brilliantly. He plays it back to Drinkwater, who sweeps a first-time pass out to Kante on the left wing. The midfielder turns inside onto his right foot before looping a curling strike towards the top-right corner, but Cech recovers well to tip it away for the corner.
--- 36’ Yellow card A first yellow card of the game now, as Francis Coquelin goes into Martin Atkinson's book for a tactical foul on Mahrez. The Algerian winger had looked to speed away from the Arsenal midfielder, who could only bring him down with a desperate slide-tackle. ---
(34’) Another opportunity now for the hosts, as they win a corner out on the left. Ozil drifts in an out-swinging cross towards Koscielny, but the centre-back is unable to connect with his attempted header and Leicester clear the danger - momentarily at least.
(32’) DISALLOWED! That was close, but it is the correct call by the linesman! Bellerin forged some space down the right before cutting a neat reverse pass back into Ozil, who picked out the run of Giroud with a sublime cross. The Frenchman duly got on the end of it and powered a header past Schmeichel, but the officials had already brought the move back for offside. Unlucky!
(30’) That’s a superb tackle from Kante, who as always seems to have been everywhere in the opening half-an-hour of this fixture, as the uncapped Frenchmen gets in a timely challenge on his compatriot Giroud to keep Arsenal well-camped in their own territory. What a signing he has been for Leicester!
(29’) Excellent counter-attacking play once more from Leicester, who work a move down the left wing through Kante. The dynamic box-to-box midfielder jinks his way past Bellerin with ease before lofting a cross to Mahrez at the back post, but the skilful winger is eventually crowded out by Arsenal’s defenders.
(26’) Poor! That’s a bad miss from Giroud, who rises highest to meet the resulting corner. It is a free header for the ex-Montpellier striker, but he can only direct his effort over the crossbar from close range. Wasteful!
(25’) SUPERB DEFENDING! What a block that is from Morgan, as the Leicester captain gets across to prevent Sanchez’s goalbound effort troubling Schmeichel. The chance came down the right wing for Arsenal, with Oxlade-Chamberlain again utilising his pace to get the better of Fuchs.
(23’) Great pressing from Leicester, as Kante powers forward from midfield before teeing up Mahrez, but the Algerian is unable to get a cross into the area and Arsenal claw it clear. The visitors are really starting to grow into proceedings now after withstanding that glut of early pressure from the hosts.
(21’) CLOSE! Fuchs ventures forward down the left wing, but a sloppy touch results in Oxlade-Chamberlain stealing possession. The former Southampton midfielder drives into the penalty area before sliding a low cross into Giroud, but the France striker is unable to generate any power on his toe-poked effort, which trickles harmlessly through to Schmeichel.
(19’) Almost! That’s poor from Ozil, really, who had acres of space to run into behind Leicester’s defence, but the Germany playmaker had strayed offside and the chance goes begging.
(16’) GREAT GOALKEEPING! End to end play here at the Emirates, as Schmeichel does superbly to race out and prevent Ramsey getting in on goal. The resulting counter-attack sees Leicester race upfield through Albrighton, who lofts a precise cross to the back post. Vardy meets it with a header, but Cech gets down brilliantly to deny the England striker a 19th goal of the season.
(14’) OFFSIDE! Almost an opening for Leicester there! The visitors manage a rare foray forward which results in Fuchs dinking an inviting chip into the path of Okazaki. The Japan forward takes it down expertly, but is unable to apply the finishing touch. It wouldn’t have counted anyway, as the linesman's flag had already been raised.
(12’) It has been an extremely positive start from the hosts, who have looked to get on the front foot straight from kick-off, but Leicester are holding their ground so far. Koscielny switches things up for Arsenal, going long to Giroud, who takes the ball down on the edge of the visitors’ area before winning a corner. Oxlade-Chamberlain elects to go short from the set-piece this time, however, and Ranieri’s side are able to smother the danger once more.
(10’) Fantastic skill from Ozil, who does brilliantly to chase down a loose pass and back-heel a ball back into the path of Oxlade-Chamberlain. The England man drifts inside and attempts to dink in a cross which does appear to strike the arm of Kante, but the referee waives away the appeals for a penalty. A spot-kick certainly would have been harsh on that occasion.
(8’) Cool and composed defending from Koscielny, who takes a long ball from Morgan down on his chest expertly. The touch seems to have got away from him at first as Vardy looks to knick in and retrieve possession, but the former Lorient centre-back recovers swiftly to regain control and kick-start another attack.
(6’) The free-kick is a poor one from Ozil, but the ball does somehow find its way through into the feet of Giroud. The Frenchman manages to lay it off into the path of Sanchez, but the diminutive forward is unable to get his shot away before being swarmed by Leicester’s defenders.
(4’) Good pressure here from Arsenal, who are not allowing their visitors any time or space on the ball. They work a patient move out to the left wing, where Sanchez combines with Monreal before the Chilean is scythed down by Drinkwater, giving Arsenal a free-kick in a dangerous area...
(2’) CLOSE! An early chance for Arsenal, as Oxlade-Chamberlain makes inroads down the right flank and wins a corner. The set-piece is whipped in by the aforementioned England winger, and Sanchez rises to meet it at the back post, but his header back across goal sails just wide of the upright.
(1’) KICK-OFF! On the sound of Martin Atkinson’s whistle, Arsenal get proceedings up and running here at the Emirates! They will attack from left to right in the first half.
The teams are making their way out from the tunnel now, in front of what is a full house at the Emirates. It promises to be quite the encounter!
Wenger has heaped the praise upon Leicester in the build-up to this afternoon’s clash, admitting that the "football romantics" will all be behind the visitors and labelling Riyad Mahrez as having “dominated the Premier League". A key battle today is likely to be between Per Mertesacker and Jamie Vardy - with the German centre-back perhaps lacking the pace to be able to cope with the runs and energy of the Premier League’s leading scorer. At the other end, the goals seem to have dried up for Olivier Grioud in recent weeks, while Alexis Sanchez is yet to re-find his best form since returning from injury. However, the former Barcelona forward netted a hat-trick in the victory at the King Power, and has scored four goals in his three appearances against the Foxes in total.

The team news is in now from the Emirates. While Leicester’s matchday squad is entirely unchanged from their victory over Manchester City last weekend, Wenger has made two changes to the line-up that started against Bournemouth. In defence, Per Mertesacker replaces Gabriel Paulista, who is out with a hamstring injury, while, further forward, Francis Coquelin comes in for Mathieu Flamini, who drops to the bench. Another boost for the hosts is the return of Danny Welbeck, who is amongst the substitutes this afternoon. The England forward has not featured since last April due to a knee injury. Without further ado, let’s check on the confirmed starting XIs.
As for Leicester, their quite-brilliant story continued with a superb 3-1 victory over Manchester City last time out, with Robert Huth scoring twice either side of Riyad Mahrez’s spectacular solo effort to claim the spoils at the Etihad Stadium. The defeat to Arsenal back in September was their first of the campaign, and Ranieri’s men have been beaten just once since then - against Liverpool on Boxing Day. The Foxes have won four of their last five league fixtures, conceding just twice in that run, though they have been beaten by Arsenal in their previous eight meetings on the road. Can they continue their love affair with the Premier League this Valentine’s Day?
After a run of four games without a league victory, Arsenal finally returned to winning ways as they dispatched AFC Bournemouth 2-0 last time out, with Mesut Ozil and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain grabbing the goals at the Vitality Stadium. Wenger’s side come into this game knowing that a win will, at least temporarily, see them leapfrog above their north London rivals Tottenham into second place. And the omens are positive in that respect, with the Gunners - who triumphed 5-2 in the reverse fixture at the King Power Stadium back in September - having won 12 and lost none of their last 18 Premier League meetings with the Foxes.
Hello ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the LIVE coverage of this huge top-of-the-table Premier League clash between Arsenal and Leicester City. The league leaders come into today’s early kick-off with a five-point gap between themselves and Arsene Wenger’s side - who sit in third place, and Claudio Ranieri’s men will be looking to maintain this extraordinary campaign with another victory over a title-rival this afternoon. It promises to be a thrilling encounter, and we’ll be bringing you all the action as it happens from the Emirates Stadium!

Hello and welcome to live coverage of Liverpool's Premier League trip to face Aston Villa, as Jurgen Klopp's men try to remove the memory of being knocked out of the FA Cup during the week. (90’) OVER THE BAR DRAMATICALLY! Aguero does incredibly well to get to the byline and hook a cross into the back post. Otamendi looks primed to convert from there, but Lloris gets a palm on it, before Silva skies the rebound from in close! Two players are down injured after that and it may be enough to see Spurs over the line.
(90’) Kolarov whacks in a late cross which finds its way through to Otamendi, who seemed surprised that it arrived in his path so soon. He fails to make proper contact despite being in an unmarked position.
(90’) Kolarov wins a corner after an overlapping run, and his resulting delivery is flicked just beyond the path of Toure at the back post. Aguero keeps it alive, but can't make anything happen.
(90’) Lamela scampers forward on the break once again, but he opts against going straight for goal and instead takes it to the corner flag in a bid to waste time. That is not where City need the ball to be.
--- 89’ Substitution Kane is hauled off for Chadli. ---
(89’) Danger for Spurs for one second as Aguero gets the ball inside the area, but he doesn't execute the spin to face goal quick enough, and the defence forces him into an over-hit pass to Kolarov out on the flanks.
(87’) Spurs try to make something happen down the left flank, and the ball bobbles out to Kane on that side, who lashes a half-volley on goal that flies the wrong side of the near post!
(85’) This second half has been the tale of two substitutes, with Iheanacho bringing City level, before Lamela orchestrated what looks like the winner for the visitors. The hosts looked good before conceding - do they have time to create another chance?
--- 83’ Assist What an impact from Lamela, who drew three defenders to him with a wonderful run, and released the ball just as they collapsed around him. ---
--- 83’ Goal! ERIKSEN DEALS A HAMMER BLOW TO CITY! Lamela charges through the middle before picking outt he perfect through ball to the Dane, who gives himself the best birthday gift possible by sliding the ball past Hart! ---
(82’) The fans howl in disbelief as Aguero is called for an offside, halting what looked like a promising counter-attack. Replays show that the Argentine might have been level with the defensive line though!
--- 81’ Substitution Alli has been withdrawn for Lamela with nine minutes to go. ---
(80’) Tottenham's last nine Premier League goals have either been scored or assisted by Harry Kane or Dele Alli. The former did bury the penalty to open the scoring, but neither player has been an attacking factor from open play.
(78’) LLORIS CALLED INTO ACTION! Toure takes the initiative and unleashes a powerful effort that is touched by the goalkeeper! Spurs are rocking while City are rolling. Just over 10 minutes to go for someone to win this game!
--- 76’ Yellow card Carroll gets booked by the referee for time wasting. It's really heating up here and Spurs just need to calm things down, with City looking to cash in on the momentum of this game and feed off the crowd. ---
--- 75’ Substitution That assist will be Clichy's last contribution of the match, as he's replaced by Kolarov. ---
--- 74’ Assist Great overlapping run and low cross from Clichy after a lovely slide-rule pass from Silva to set the play in motion. ---
--- 74’ Goal! IHEANACHO TIES IT UP! The substitute makes the greatest impact possible as he arrives in the box to hammer home Clichy's cross! No chance for Lloris and it's right back into the fire! ---
(73’) The City fans don't like Rose after his role in the penalty, but their boos don't stop the full-back from getting a cross in from the left-hand side that just misses the head of a team-mate at the near post.
--- 72’ Substitution Son put in a lot of work tonight, but his shift is over as Carroll replaces him. ---
(72’) This game seems on the cusp of something special, with the fans fully invested and the title implications starting to sink in with time slowly edging away. It's been a more open encounter since the restart.
(70’) The fans are already on edge after what they felt was an unjust penalty call, and they're brought into a roar as Zabaleta flattens Kane with a challenge. The referee just has to calm things down here.
(68’) Son dribbles into the area and has Kompany for, well, company. The Belgian goes to the turf in an attempt to block the South Korean's shot, but he needn't have bothered as there was a handball by Son in the buildup which was spotted by the referee.
--- 66’ Substitution Iheanacho is thrown on in place of Fernando, in the first substitution of the game. ---
