(64’) How damaging will this result be for City if it holds? They have an abysmal record against the top six this season, failing to win a single game, and as things stand, will lose their second straight game against a fellow title contender at home.
(62’) Aguero gets the ball on the counter-attack, and runs right at Dier down the left. The rebound just falls to ofa behind Fernandinho, who was on the edge of the box waiting to profit.
(60’) Gripping stuff and a great response from City to going behind. That goal from Kane was the best thing that could have happened to this games in terms of the entertainment factor. The hosts have half an hour plus stoppage time to get themselves level.
(58’) CITY HIT THE CROSSBAR! Toure curls a lovely effort over the wall, but the woodwork comes to Tottenham's rescue! Lloris was right under it though, and he may have just chipped the tip of his fingernail to touch that one!
--- 56’ Yellow card Wimmer upends Silva outside the box, but the referee makes a mental note of the challenge and allows play to continue, where Toure curls an effort narrowly off target. Play is then pulled back for the free-kick, and Wimmer is booked. ---
(55’) City try to hit back right away, with a corner-kick met by Fernandinho, who loops a header over the top. What will the response from Manuel Pellegrini's men be? They've been in control of the ball since conceding.
--- 53’ Goal! KANE BURIES IT FROM THE SPOT! After 53 minutes of invisibility, the forward strokes the ball down the middle, with Hart diving out of the way to his right. Massive goal in the title race and the onus is now on City! ---

(50’) Signs that the second half may be a little more open than the opening period. Silva and Sterling appear to have switched flanks. Still a long way to go here at the Etihad.
(48’) MASSIVE CHANCE FOR CITY! Toure weighs up his options at the top of the box, and decides to clip one over the defensive line for Aguero, who is onside and completely unmarked, but lashes it over the bar. It wasn't the easiest opening, but he may well feel that he should have hit the target!
--- 46’ Yellow card Alli gets brought down by Kompany, who picks up a yellow card, the first one of the game for City. ---
(46’) Here we go again!
And that will do it for now from the Etihad, with matters left just as they started between Manchester City and Tottenham. No goals and very little in the way of chances in a match where defence has been the watchword. Eriksen probably had the best opportunity of the first period with a 20-yarder that was saved by Hart. Both teams seem more preoccupied with not making a mistake, which has contributed to the cagey feel of this one. There's a lot at stake in the second half though, so stay tuned!
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card Toure looks to scamper into space on the break, but is hacked down near the halfway line by Dier, who is called over by the referee and gets yellow card on the stroke of half-time. There's been a few challenges like that in this match, and the referee decides to punish one. ---
(45’) It looks like we're set for only one minute of stoppage time here.
(43’) Both sides look happy to see this one out to the interval, where the managers will have a chance to regroup their troops. Defensively, it's been nearly perfect from City and Spurs, but in attack, it's been anything but.
(41’) Rose sees a piledriver take a nick off a City player and go out for a corner, but an offensive foul on Alli halts the play in its tracks. It's been that sort of stop-start game, with the referee probably having a considerable mental note of players on their last warnings already.
(39’) A draw won't be the worst result for either team, but given that Arsenal pegged Leicester's lead back to two points earlier in the day, you get the sense that these sides can smell a massive opportunity to suffocate things at the Premier League summit.
(37’) Mark Clattenburg has been lenient in this match, in contrast to Martin Atkinson in the Arsenal-Leicester game, who made a bunch of huge calls which dictated that top-of-the-table clash. Kompany escapes with a lecture after bringing down Kane.
(35’) Dier smashes a speculative effort high over the bar. Just about 10 minutes plus stoppage time to go until the break now, and it's clear that this match is going to be close until the very end. It's been a grind-it-out sort of affair in the first period.

(31’) Decent period on the ball for Spurs, but their lack of ideas in the final third is evident. Kane has barely touched the ball so far. It's City's turn to frustrate the opposition as they keep bodies in formation at the back to protect Hart.

The referee is lenient once again, only punishing City with a foul.

Pochettino's men haven't managed much themselves in attack though.

City have a great recent record against Spurs, winning eight of their last 10 Premier League meetings, including five in a row at the Etihad. Games between these two tend to be high-scoring affairs, as their last nine encounters have produced 41 goals. However, Manuel Pellegrini's men have not beaten any team in the top six this season, and were thrashed 4-1 by Mauricio Pochettino's outfit in the reverse fixture at White Hart Lane.
Spurs, meanwhile are in a rich vein of form, unbeaten in their last nine games in the top flight - winning eight of those. Their only loss away from home this season came on the opening day against Manchester United. Since then, they've won six and drawn five on their travels. They're the league's best defensive side with only 19 goals conceded - four less than the next-best side Arsenal, and a victory here will take them ahead of their second-place London rivals on goal difference.
Manchester City are six points off the pace at the start of play, but can climb as high as third with a win, which will see them leapfrog Tottenham in the table. The Citizens have the best home record in the top flight, triumphing in nine of their 14 games while scoring 34 goals - although their last match at the Etihad was a damaging 3-1 reverse to Leicester a week ago.
Hello and welcome to our live commentary of the Premier League clash between title hopefuls Manchester City and Tottenham. Arsenal's dramatic win over Leicester City has breathed new life into the race for the trophy, and both teams will be looking for a win to keep things tight at the top of the table. Stick with us for all the action.

The referee blows his whistle for the final time, and Leicester have picked up arguably their biggest and best win of the season! They were excellent from start to finish, with their well-organised back four putting in a particularly strong shift as they did well to largely contain Aguero. The Argentine was finally able to find the back of the net late on but it was too little, too late, meaning that the Foxes move six points clear at the top of the table and are surely now one of the favourites to pick up the Premier League title.

Poor defending by Manchester City allowed Huth to tap the visitors into the lead with just two minutes on the clock, and from then onwards they've done wonderfully well to remain defensively disciplined. As expected, the hosts have dominated possession but they've done little with it, with Sterling, Silva and, in particular, Toure all struggling to find much space inside the final third of the pitch.

Despite heading into today’s game three points behind their opponents, Manchester City are arguably the favourites to leave with a much-needed win. It’s not been the smoothest of campaigns for Manuel Pellegrini’s side, who have looked excellent on several occasions only to follow up good performances with poor results. Tuesday evening’s 1-0 win away to Sunderland extended their domestic unbeaten run to seven games, whilst they currently boast the best home record in the Premier League this season with nine victories and 33 goals from 12 games. At the start of the campaign, nobody, not even Leicester’s faithful fans, could have predicted that the Foxes would find themselves at the top of the Premier League table come the start of February. It’s been an incredible five months for Claudio Ranieri’s side, who have consistently impressed throughout and, as a result, find themselves sitting three points clear of Manchester City heading into today’s clash. A wonderful 2-0 win against Liverpool on Tuesday has kept alive their dreams of picking up their first ever top-flight title, but they now have to contend with what are arguably the two most important games of their season. After today’s game they must take on fourth-place Arsenal in what is sure to be a thrilling encounter at the Emirates. Back-to-back wins against two fellow title challengers would surely silence the doubters once and for all, whilst also putting them firmly in the driving seat to pull off what would be an absolutely remarkable league triumph.

The resulting corner comes to nothing, before the same ex-Toulouse midfielder heads horrendously high and wide from the next attack.
(48’) Foster is called into action immediately, with the English goalkeeper fumbling a loose ball into the path of one of his own defenders. There's now a stoppage in play, with the physios called onto the field in order to treat McAuley. The experienced defender appears to have a muscle problem.
--- 47’ Yellow card Yellow card Gareth McAuley ---
--- 46’ Substitution Sandro is sacrificed for the visitors, with Berahino coming into the fray to support Sandro. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Pritchard replaces Gardner at the interval, with the Spurs loanee looking to make an impact on his debut. ---
HALF TIME! The hosts go into the break with a 1-0 advantage, courtesy of a neat finish from Mitrovic. It could have been two, but Tiote saw a goal correctly ruled offside for Foster's vision being impaired by a black and white shirt. Despite a poor start, the Baggies are still in with a chance of stealing a share of the spoils.
(44’) Newcastle might just be a little nervy after surrendering that clear-cut chance moments ago, with McClaren's men trying to retain possession and calmly edge their way towards a half-time advantage.
(42’) Huge chance wasted by the away side! The Baggies race down the right-hand side, before Gardner cuts back an inviting cross from the byline! McClean shapes to shoot dangerously, but the Irishman sees an attempt blocked in desperate fashion! Elliot escapes unscathed yet again.
(40’) We're into the final five minutes of the first half, with West Brom still unable to string together a silky passage of play. Sissoko is picked out overlapping down the right-hand side, but McAuley and Foster combine to do just enough to deny the Frenchman from bringing a throughball under his spell on the move.
(38’) Newcastle continue to press on and search for a second goal of the afternoon, with the Baggies still sat on the edge of their penalty box. Tiote shoots from range once again, but the Ivorian's attempt is blocked well. Moments later, Mitrovic tries to cut back a square ball from the right byline, but is penalised for handball.
(36’) Townsend tries to combine with Mitrovic and break down the left flank, but the latter is tackled firmly by Dawson. West Brom take the resulting throw-in and try to counter, but a loose throughball ends up at the feet of Elliot. The Newcastle goalkeeper hasn't been tested yet at all.
(34’) Narrowly over 10 minutes remain in the first half, with West Brom desperately needing to rally their troops before the break. Pulis' men have just been second best to absolutely everything thus far, with Anichebe positively anonymously while trying to lead the Baggies' line.
--- 32’ Assist Shelvey picks out the run of the Serbian striker, with the England international pulling the strings for the Magpies in this first half. ---
--- 32’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! MITROVIC OPENS THE SCORING AND THIS ONE COUNTS! The Serbia international is fed into the clear, with the ex-Anderlecht man able to bustle his way towards the penalty area! Foster comes out to meet him, but the Newcastle striker keeps his cool and slots a neat finish underneath the English shot-stopper! ---
(31’) OFFSIDE! Newcastle think that they have the lead, but Tiote has a goal ruled out! The Ivory Coast international takes aim from 25 yards out, with his swirling effort wrongfooting Foster! The ball nestles in the back of the net, but the linesman flags for an offside player unsighting the former Watford shot-stopper.
(30’) Another big chance for the Magpies! Sissoko breaks down the right-hand side at real pace, before fizzing a fantastic cross along the six-yard line! Unfortunately for the hosts, Mitrovic can't quite stretch enough to get there! McClaren throws a water bottle in frustration, as he knows that his side need to make the most of this spell of pressure.
(28’) Townsend bursts down the left-hand side, before swirling in a teasing cross, but Yacob gets up well to head clear! Newcastle keep their pressure on, but Sissoko is dispossessed on the edge of the penalty box. The ex-Toulouse midfielder just can't quite seem to provide a final ball.
(26’) Aarons and Gardner clash heads, after the former managed to get up nicely to flick a defensive intervention away from Newcastle's danger area. Fortunately, both players are quickly back to their feet and are fine to continue. West Brom are coming into this contest a little bit more now, with the hosts finally getting something of a foothold in the midfield battle.
(24’) Shelvey lets fly from around 25 yards out, with the ex-Swansea midfielder getting plenty of power behind his long-range attempt! It is straight down Foster's throat, however, with the England international holding onto the ball well. West Brom try to counter, but Janmaat comes across brilliantly to deny McClean.
(22’) The referee is still yet to go into his pocket, despite a few heavy challenges being thrown in during the opening half an hour. West Brom win a free-kick in a deep area, but a looping ball forward from Olsson zips off the turf and straight behind for a goal-kick. Pulis' men just haven't been able to generate any kind of danger.
(20’) Foster's penalty area is continuing to see the majority of the ball, with McClaren's side causing all kinds of problems. Sandro gets up well to head a looping cross away, conceding a corner in the process. Shelvey sends in a swirling delivery, but the opposition goalkeeper is quick off his line to claim well.
(18’) Sissoko goes on a driving run into the opposition penalty area, and is picked out nicely, but the France international is denied at the final hurdle by a sliding challenge from Foster! Newcastle are continuing to dominate, with the Magpies needing to make the most of their spell of heavy pressure.
(17’) Gardner goes down on the edge of the penalty area, with the ex-Sunderland midfielder winning a dangerous free-kick on the periphery of the box. Newcastle put together a sizeable wall, but a deflected strike from the aforementioned Englishman loops over the crossbar and out for a corner. The resulting set-piece delivery is curled in, but Taylor heads clear.
(16’) West Brom's back four get some brief respite, with the away outfit winning a throw in high on the right-hand side. Sandro, however, does brilliantly to break up play and kick start a counter! With Townsend making tracks down the left-hand side, Wijnaldum plays a heavy pass out of play by mistake! Almost a lightning break-away from the hosts!
(15’) Olsson is now asked to make a headed intervention deep within his own penalty area, with the Baggies really having their backs to the wall. West Brom just can't seem to escape their own half, with Anichebe forced to chase long and aimless passes forward. Townsend drifts in a cross from the left, which is squared by Sissoko, but Mitrovic sees a header blocked!
(13’) Janmaat goes down heavily off the field, with the Netherlands international looking to be in some discomfort. The hosts debate putting the ball out, but continue with their passage of play. They're not wanting to let up their early momentum at any cost. A dipping cross from the right is headed away by Dawson brilliantly.
(11’) Newcastle are continuing to call all of the shots, with McClaren's men laying siege to the West Brom penalty area. Pulis will be concerned with how deep his midfield are sitting, with the Baggies' negative starting line-up seeing Anichebe become very isolated. McClean tries to whip a cross in from the left, but Shelvey makes a timely interception.
(9’) Elliot finally gets called into action, but the hosts' goalkeeper punts a rushed clearance upfield. There's then a break in play, with Anichebe going down heavily. Berahino is sent out to warm up, despite the Englishman being linked with the Magpies during the January transfer window. It appears that the former Everton striker will be alright to try and continue, however.
(7’) The away side are camped on the edge of the penalty area, with Newcastle getting chance after chance! Townsend is found in space, with the former Spurs winger unleashing a powerful right-footed effort, but Foster dives to his left to make a strong save! The resulting corner is whipped in, before the ex-Man United goalkeeper spreads himself well to deny Mitrovic!
(5’) Janmaat breaks down the right-hand side, before cutting back a neat ball, but Fletcher slides in to intercept! The hosts keep their pressure on, but a couple of further blocks from Olsson keep Foster well protected. McClaren's men are definitely up for this one, with the home fans baying for Baggies blood.
(3’) Good block by Olsson! The Sweden international slides in to deny Wijnaldum, after the former PSV midfielder looked to swivel and shoot from close range! Newcastle come under scrutiny defensively moments later, but Aarons lashes away an uncompromising clearance. The Magpies are coming out of the blocks well!
(1’) We are underway in the first half! West Brom need to perk up from their terrible away form of late, with Newcastle sitting merely two points from 17th-placed Norwich and safety. The hosts need to keep picking up results on home soil.
West Brom substitutes: Rondon, Berahino, Sessegnon, Myhill, Pritchard, Pocognoli, Lambert.
West Brom starting line-up (4-5-1): Foster; Dawson, McAuley, Olsson, Chester; Gardner, Yacob, Fletcher, Sandro, McClean; Anichebe.
Newcastle substitutes: Barlaser, Williams, Saivet, Doumbia, Darlow, Gibson, Ayoze.
Newcastle starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Elliot; Janmaat, Taylor, Coloccini, Aarons; Shelvey, Tiote; Sissoko, Wijnaldum, Townsend; Mitrovic.
TEAM NEWS: Ben Foster continues to be preferred to Boaz Myhill in goal, with James Chester slotting in at left-back. Sandro will partner Claudio Yacob in defensive midfield, with Darren Fletcher also offering plenty of experience. Craig Gardner and James McClean can offer inventiveness in wide areas, with Victor Anichebe leading the line alone. Salomon Rondon, Saido Berahino and Stephane Sessegnon are among the substitues, along with new loan signing Alex Pritchard.
TEAM NEWS: Jamal Lascelles is absent due to suspension for the hosts, with Steven Taylor and Fabricio Coloccini making up the heart of the back four. Rolando Aarons gets a start at left-back, with Jonjo Shelvey offering some deep lying creativity. Andros Townsend features, but there's pressure on the ex-Spurs man to repay his chunky transfer fee.
The Magpies have won merely one of their last five competitive games, while Tony Pulis' men continue to be tough to beat. The visitors have drawn their last three matches in all competitions, but haven't won away in the English top flight since last October.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of West Brom's away visit to St. James' Park, as Newcastle look to pick up some vital points in the battle against relegation. Steve McClaren's men have invested some money on new personnel during the recent transfer window, but the imports have to now do their talking on the pitch.

Well, that’s all from me for today from the Britannia, where Everton have claimed a comfortable 3-0 victory over Stoke City to move into seventh-place in the Premier League.
As for Everton, they could have feasibly scored five or six goals this afternoon, if not for some superb goalkeeping from Jack Butland. Aaron Lennon, Romelu Lukaku and Ross Barkley were particularly impressive, while in spite of their well-documented defensive issues, Roberto Martinez’s side never looked in danger of conceding as they claimed a third-straight clean sheet and a third-consecutive 3-0 victory in the space of six days.
While Everton were fantastic, Stoke were extremely poor, and never got to grips with the pace and power of the visitors on the counter, while struggling to make any real impact at the other end. That is a third-straight 3-0 defeat for Mark Hughes’ side.
FULL-TIME! What a display from Everton, who have sealed a fantastic and comprehensive 3-0 victory over Stoke here at the Britannia, with first-half goals from Romelu Lukaku, Seamus Coleman and Aaron Lennon doing the damage for the visitors, who claim a second-succesive Premier League win for the first time this term.
(90’) UNLUCKY! More fabulous play from the visitors, as Kone drives in-filed from the left before thumping a pass into the feet of Mirallas, who fails to get his shot away from the edge of the six-yard box.
(90’) Good work from Joselu, who stands up a cross to the back post, but Robles - who is ebbing with confidence at the moment - makes the save.
(90’) Lovely play from the visitors results in Osman drilling a pass into the path of Mirallas. The winger gets away from Pieters with some nice footwork, but loses his footing at the last moment and the chance goes begging. Everton playing with some real swagger now, as they have done all game.
--- 90’ Substitution A third and final change of the game now from Everton, as James McCarthy is replaced by the veteran Leon Osman. ---
--- 87’ Substitution A second change now for Everton as Ross Barkley, who has been superb today, makes way for Kevin Mirallas - making his first appearance in three games after recovering from a knee tendon injury. ---
(86’) HIGH OVER! Mori’s mistake allows Butland’s long hoof up-field to feed Joselu. The former Werder Bremen forward fires a pass back into the feet of Ireland on the edge of the area, but the midfielder’s effort is a poor one and does not come close to troubling Robles.
(85’) For once, it is sloppy from Everton, as McCarthy plays a loss ball back towards his defence that Joselu pounces upon. The Spaniard finds Diouf, but his cross is blocked away by Jagielka, who has been excellent today.
(83’) There are plenty of empty seats here at the Britannia now, with the Stoke faithful appearing to have lost hope of turning this around. However, there is still work to do for Everton, who will be rueing that they are not further ahead at the moment.
(81’) Imbula, who despite struggling defensively has been neat and tidy going forward, slides a cute pass into the feet of Ireland, but his lofted cross is well cleared by Jagielka.
(78’) WHAT A MISS! Mori connects with a free-header from the resulting corner. The Argentine is unmarked at the back post, but somehow skews his header wide of the left-hand post. Everton could, and perhaps should, have had five or six goals at the Britannia this afternoon.
(77’) GREAT SAVE! Another gilt-edged chance for Everton, as Barkley plays in Kone with a quite sublime flick. The Ivorian bares down on goal, but cannot direct his effort past Butland.
--- 76’ Substitution And there is a final switch of the encounter for Stoke, as Joselu, who netted the third for Hughes’ side in December, is introduced in place of Marko Arnautovic. ---
--- 76’ Substitution A first change of the game now from Everton, as Romelu Lukaku - who has now netted 20 this season across all competitions - makes way for Arouna Kone, who makes his 50th appearance for the Toffees. ---
(73’) A real display of strength and power there from Lukaku, as the Everton front-man latches onto Cleverley’s long pass before easily shirking off the challenge of Muniesa. Everton are unable to make anything of the resulting throw-in, however.
(71’) TOP DEFENDING! McCarthy almost costs his side with a sloppy touch that falls to Ireland. The former Manchester City midfielder sets up Diouf, who - on the turn - drills an effort goalwards - but Mori makes a timely block on the slide.
(68’) CHANCE! Once more, Lukaku leads a superb counter-charge from the visitors. The Belgian powers into the box before flicking it off to Barkley, who drives around two Stoke defenders before finally getting his shot away, but Wollscheid is on hand to make the block.
(67’) GOOD SAVE! Stoke finally manage an effort on goal and it is a quality effort from Johnson. The former Liverpool man rasps a strike in on target from the edge of the area, but Robles is equal to it.
(65’) ALMOST!!! Another superb counter from Everton as Lukaku holds up play excellently before sweeping an outstanding pass out to Barkley. The midfielder can’t get a shot away and has to play it back to his striker, who lays it off to McCarthy. The Irishman goes for goal with a venomous strike, which whistles just inches wide of the left-hand upright.
(64’) SO CLOSE! How did that not go in!? Lennon does brilliantly to junk clear of two Stoke defenders and drive into the box. He tees up Lukaku, who gets his shot off at the second attempt, but Butalnd is well-placed to make the save. Everton looks deadly going forward!
--- 62’ Substitution The second substitution sees Xherdan Shaqiri make way for Peter Odemwingie. ---
--- 62’ Substitution There will be a double-change now for the hosts, the first if which sees Steven Ireland replace Ibrahim Afellay. ---
--- 59’ Yellow card A yellow card now for Mame Biram Diouf, who tracks Lennon all the way back to Stoke's by-line before sliding in recklessly, and duly picking up a booking. Barkley delivers the set-piece, but Wollscheid heads it away. ---
(58’) CROSSBAR!!! That is a fantastic stop from Butland, who got a vital touch to tip Lukaku’s point-blank header onto the woodwork after the Belgian had connected with Barkley’s whipped cross. What a chance!
(57’) A bit of quality there from Imbula, who feeds Arnautovic with a crisp throughball, but the Austrian’s first touch is a heavy one and the ball rolls out of play.
(56’) Wasteful! Everton are playing very narrow here, which is forcing Stoke to go wide when they attack. Once more, the hosts work it out to Pieters, advanced down the left flank, but his cross is a poor one and lands on the roof of the net.
(54’) Almost! Stoke work a swift move forward, which is eventually played out wide to Pieters. The Dutchman puts a superb cross into the box, but neither Diouf or Shaqiri can make contact with it and it sails out of play for an Everton goal-kick.
(53’) Appeals for a penalty from Everton after Coleman wins a free-kick down the right which Barkley delivers in. The cross is a poor one, but the Jagileka gets a better one in at the second attempt. Mori tries to get on the end of it, but he is barged into by Pieters, however, Andre Marriner correctly waives away the claims for a spot-kick.
(51’) A slight bit of controversy here as Robles - who has been instructed to speed up with his goal-kicks by the officials - lofts a swift ball up-field from an Everton free-kick. Lukaku, one-on-one with his marker, latches onto it, but Andre Marriner pulls the play back, to the annoyance of the visitors.
(49’) SO CLOSE!!! WHAT A MOVE FROM EVERTON! Barkley makes a tackle and charges forward from deep in his own territory. The England man powers in from the left before playing a superb one-two with Lukaku to get into the area. He could have gone down due to a tug on his shirt, but he stays up and blasts an effort goalwards, but it nestles into the side-netting. Unlucky!
(48’) CHANCE! That’s a great block from Oviedo, who recovers just in time to intercept Afellay’s drilled strike from an acute angle. The rebound almost falls into the path of Diouf, but Robles is out quickly to smother the danger.
(47’) A half-chance here, as for the first time in the match Shaqiri picks up space in-field, twisting and turning before drilling an effort goalwards, but the strike trickles wide.
(46’) Well, despite that quite awful first-half for Stoke, there are no changes for Stoke at the interval, and Everton, also unchanged, get the second half under way.
While credit must go to Martinez’s side for a resolute and clinical display, Stoke really only have themselves to blame for that terrible first-half. Typically exciting players such as Arnautovic and Shaqiri have failed to make an impact, while Imbula has struggled with the pace of the visitors’ midfield on the counter, and changes will almost certainly be imminent here for Hughes’ side. Everton’s defensive frailties have been well-documented as of late, but the hosts will still have to be at their very best to get anything from this fixture now.
HALF-TIME! What a nightmare opening 45 minutes that has been for Stoke, with Hughes' side trailing Everton 3-0. Lukaku opened the scoring with a well-taken penalty after Butland had brought down Cleverley, before Coleman doubled the advantage with a terrific header. Lennon then capped off a superb first-half display for the visitors with a neat finish after a calamitous error from Wollscheid.
(45’) One final chance for Stoke now, as Mori concedes a corner… Pieters lofts it in, finding Diouf at the back post, but his tame strike is collected by Robles, and Andre Marriner blows for half-time.
(45’) That’s wasteful! The real was on there for the visitors after Shaqiri’s sloppy pass. Barkley burst forward and found Lukaku, but the Belgian - despite holding it up well - was then unable to tee up the on-rushing Cleverley.
(45’) The rain is absolutely teeming down here, and Stoke are really struggling to break down Everton’s ranks. Diouf has been anonymous up top, while Arnautovic and Shaqiri have also found it difficult to make an impact. Bojan is on the bench, and it seems likely that the former Barcelona forward will be introduced sooner rather than later.
(45’) Due to those injuries to Everton’s midfielders, there will be five additional minutes at the end of the first half. However, many Stoke fans have already made their way from the stands for the interval. The hosts do win a corner down the left, but Lukaku gets back to head Shaqiri's delivery well clear.
(44’) CHANCE! Good play from Stoke, who carve through Everton’s defence with a neat move. Diouf does well to feed Arnautovic, but the Austria forward can only direct a tame effort into the hands of Robles.
--- 42’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLL!!! WHAT AN ERROR FROM WOLLSCHEID! The former Bayer Leverkusen man lofts a dreadful ball in-field which Lennon nips in to intercept. The former Tottenham winger drives clear of Muniesa, before sliding a precise finish past Butland. That's his third goal in three games. Everton have thumped Stoke in this first half! ---
(41’) Back to those injuries for Everton, and both Barry and McCarthy appear to be okay after their spells off the pitch, though Ross Barkley has now made his way to the touchline to receive treatment on a cut.
(39’) High and wide! Well it is a typically windy and rainy day in the Potteries, and the weather is something that Stoke new-boy Imbula will have to quickly get accustomed to. The powerful midfielder tries his luck from range, but his strike sails way off target.
(37’) Barry is back on now, and appears to be moving freely enough, though it is one that Everton will continue to monitor closer. The stoppages for the injuries have made this encounter rather scrappy in the last few minutes. Stoke lodge an attack down the right, but are unable to make any headway through a congested collection of blue shirts.
(35’) Well, that was a really innocuous injury to Barry, which seems to have been picked up in a collision with Diouf. He is receiving treatment on the touchline at the moment, though Leighton Baines does look to be preparing to come on.
(33’) McCarthy appears to be okay to continue for now, at least. But there is now another injury for Everton, and it is Gareth Barry who is down, grabbing hold of his wrist. The former Manchester City man looks in real pain here.
(31’) A real worry now for Everton, as James McCarthy has to receive treatment on an injury. The Republic of Ireland international has only just returned from injury, and really is a key figure in Martinez’s side.
--- 28’ Assist Everton rarely get goals from set-pieces these days, but Tom Cleverley's corner was a superb one into a dangerous area. The run of Coleman was smart and well-timed, and he made no mistake with his header. ---
--- 28’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!!! COLEMAN HEADS IT IN! It’s a great header from the Irishman, who gets ahead of his marker and nods in his first goal in almost a year with a fantastic finish into the far-right corner. Stoke 0-2 Everton! ---
(27’) Everton manage to relieve some pressure for a moment as Butland concedes a throw-in high up-field. Barry picks up possession and drives into the box, with Afellay making the challenge and knocking it out for a corner, which Cleverley stands over...
(26’) Nasty! A hefty collision here that has left Jagielka groggy. Shaqiri lifted a super cross to the back post, where Diouf was waiting, but the aforementioned Everton skipper does well to get in a headed clearance, receiving a knock to the head for his troubles. However, after a brief moment on the turf, he appears to be okay to carry on.
(24’) It has been a disciplined and tight display from Martinez’s side so far, though Mori is slightly sloppy on this occasion as he attempts to find Cleverley down the left, but only succeeds in drilling the ball out for a Stoke throw-in. The hosts look to get into the box through Johnson, but Jagielka gets across to hook it clear for the time being.
(22’) STAT FLASH: Stoke have won a league-low one point in games that they have conceded the first goal in this season (10 games, W0 D1 L9). Can they turn that record around today?
(20’) Stoke are down for 10 men at the moment, as Muniesa makes his way to the touchline to receive some treatment on a nasty gash to his cheek. Barkley looks to take advantage with a crisp pass in-behind the hosts’ defence, but Whelan does well to intercept.
(18’) Good defending from Oviedo there, who does well to nip in ahead of Diouf to prevent the striker getting on the end of Whelan’s chipped cross. Stoke are definitely looking dangerous down their right side, but Everton are withstanding the pressure so far.
(16’) Everton are sitting deep here, and look more than willing to play on the counter. And you cannot blame them, especially with the pace and power of Barkley, Lennon and Lukaku up top. Stoke are pressing high, but have been so far unable to carve out a real opportunity since Shaqiri’s cross in the opening few minutes.
(14’) It really was a superb piece of counter-attacking play from the visitors. Barkley - playing in front of England manager Roy Hodgson today - was at the heart of it, feeding Oviedo with a sublime back-heel, and the Everton full-back did well to spot the run of Cleverley, who fooled Butland with a fantastic first touch. Stoke, however, were carved open through the middle, with Imbula not sharp enough to spot the danger.
--- 11’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAALLL!!! Lukaku fires home from the spot! It's a cool and composed finish from the Belgian, who drills in his 16th of the season in the league - and first goal in the league since he netted a double against Stoke at Goodison. What a start for Everton! ---
(10’) PENALTY TO EVERTON!!! Well, the Toffees only got there first two penalties of the season last time out, and they have a third now! Barkley plays through Oviedo with a superb flick, and the Costa Rican slides a wonderful pass into the path of Cleverley, who is duly scythed down by Butland.
(9’) There seems to be plenty of space so far inc central areas when Everton attack, and that may be down to a slight miss-understanding between new-boy Imbula and Whelan. Stoke do manage to gain some possession and get down the right once more, with Oviedo conceding a corner. The hosts elect to go short before Shaqiri whips in a cross at the second attempt, but Robles collects to with ease.
(7’) CHANCE! Cleverley puts in a great delivery which Mori connects with. The Argentine directs his header on target, but Pieters is there to nod it off the line and out of play, but the officials award a goal-kick rather than another corner.
(6’) Strong play from Lukaku, who does well to hold off Pieters in a central area and win a free-kick. Everton elect to go short and break swiftly down the left flank. Oviedo attempts to drill in a cross, but Johnson is on hand to deflect it wide for a corner.
(5’) STAT FLASH: The Potters have failed to score in any of their last three Premier League games; they haven't gone four top-flight games in a row without scoring since March 1985 (when they went eight games without a goal).
(3’) A scrappy start to proceedings so far, as both sides look to try and cement some authority on proceedings. Stoke eventually manage to play in Shaqiri on the left, and the winger, who netted twice in the reverse fixture, puts in a dangerous cross, but Coleman is well-placed to head it clear.
(1’) KICK-OFF! The first-half is under way here at the Britannia, with Stoke getting proceedings up and running following the whistle of Andre Marriner.
Peter Crouch, on the bench once more for Stoke, would make his 400th Premier League appearance should he come on in this match, and would become the 25th different Englishman to reach this landmark. Starting up top for Stoke today is Mame Biram Diouf, who is making just his second start since October.
It was a seven-goal thriller that last times these two met at Goodison back in December, with Marco Arnautovic sealing a 4-3 victory for Stoke with a controversial last-gasp penalty. Hughes’ side have won just once since then, however, and sit only a point above Everton in 10th place. The Toffees played well against a lacklustre Newcastle side in mid-week, with Ross Barkley and Aaron Lennon particularly impressive. It is also interesting to note the strength in depth that both these squads have, with the hosts’ bench featuring the likes of Bojan Krkic and Joselu, while the visitors name Baines, Mirallas and Gerard Deulofeu amongst their substitutes. There is however no place for their new arrival Oumar Niasse, who has not yet received clearance to play.
TEAM NEWS - Everton substitutes: Stanek, Baines, Mirallas, Kone, Osman, Pienaar, Deulofeu.
TEAM NEWS - Everton (4-2-3-1): Robles; Coleman, Jagielka, Funes-Mori; Oviedo; McCarthy, Barry; Lennon, Barkley, Cleverley; Lukaku.
TEAM NEWS - Stoke substitutes: Bardsley, Ireland, Odemwingie, Joselu, Crouch, Bojan, Haugaard.
TEAM NEWS - Stoke (4-2-3-1): Butland; Johnson, Wollscheid, Muniesa, Pieters; Imbula, Whelan; Shaqiri, Afellay, Arnautovic; Diouf.
The teams are in from Stoke, and as mentioned previously Hughes hands a full debut to their record signing Imbula, who sits alongside stand-in captain Glenn Whelan in midfield. Ryan Shawcross and Geoff Cameron are both still absent through injury, but Philipp Wollscheid is fit to start after overcoming a knock picked up against Manchester United. As for the visitors, Martinez names an unchanged starting XI. That means there is still no place in the line-up for Leighton Baines, who is on the bench, though Romelu Lukaku has overcome a back injury to start today. John Stones and Tim Howard are both injured, while Kevin Mirallas does return to the squad. Let’s check on the full team sheets.
Like their hosts, Everton also slumped out of the League Cup in the semi-final stage with a 4-3 aggregate defeat to Manchester City. However, Martinez’s side have won both of their fixtures since that defeat at the Etihad Stadium - dispatching Carlisle United in the FA Cup before comfortably seeing off struggling Newcastle at Goodison Park. The Toffees have not managed to string two consecutive victories together in the Premier League so far this campaign, and will be hoping to break that duck against an out-of-form and injury-hit Stoke at the Britannia.
Stoke’s poor form continued in mid-week with a 3-0 defeat to Manchester United at Old Trafford. The full-back then swings a dangerous cross into the heart of the Watford box, where Kane is waiting near the penalty spot, but Britos is just about able to get a boot on the attempted pass to send it away from the Tottenham striker.
(17’) Dembele twists and turns on the left wing as he weaves his way past two Watford players. He then cuts the ball back to Eriksen, who spins and tries to pick out Lamela, but the Dane's pass is poor and is easily cut out by Watson.
(15’) Ake tries to break down the left wing but is clumsily fouled by Chadli, resulting in a free-kick for Watford midway inside the Tottenham half of the pitch. It's whipped in by Watson but is poorly hit and fails to beat the first man, who is camped on the edge of the box.
(13’) After spending the vast majority of the opening 13 minutes firmly on the back foot, Watford are finally able to push out of their own half of the pitch, but they're quickly put under an incredible amount of pressure by the Tottenham midfield, which forces them to send the ball back towards the halfway line.
(11’) Dembele does well to charge down the right wing before sending a cross off a black shirt and out for a corner. It's whipped in by Lamela and curls towards the head of Alderweireld, but just as the centre-back is about to make contact with the ball he's beaten to it by the imposing figure of Watson.
(9’) Once again, Tottenham break down the left flank, with Davies flying forward on a marauding run before trying to swing a cross into the middle of the penalty area. It's well hit but fails to pick out Kane and is instead cut out by Britos near the penalty spot.
(7’) Dembele is clumsily fouled by Jurado, resulting in a free-kick for Tottenham in a very dangerous position 25 yards away from the Watford goal. Eriksen steps up and unleashes a shot from the set-piece, but it's underhit by the Dane and fails to beat the wall of black shirts camped in front of him.
(5’) Tottenham push down the left flank before Nyom dispossesses Davies and sends the ball out of play for a corner. Eriksen curls the resulting set-piece into the heart of the penalty area, where Kane is waiting, but Gomes is there to clear the danger with a strong punch.
(3’) It's been a determined start to the game by Tottenham, who are looking bright on the ball and are aiming to try and put as much pressure on Watford as possible. However, the visitors look well-organised and, as a result, are dealing with everything that is being thrown at them.
(1’) And we're off!
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, Watford boss Quique Sanchez Flores has made five alterations to the side that featured in the aforementioned draw at home to Chelsea, with Juan Carlos Paredes, Sebastian Prodl, Jose Holebas, Valon Behrami and Troy Deeney making way for Allan Nyom, Miguel Britos, Nathan Ake, Almen Abdi and Mario Suarez, the latter of whom makes his first start for the Hornets since joining from Fiorentina.
Mauricio Pochettino has decided to make four changes to the Tottenham side that comfortably beat Norwich City on Tuesday, with Kieran Trippier, Ben Davies, Erik Lamela and Nacer Chadli coming into the starting line-up to replace Kyle Walker, Danny Rose, Heung-Min Son and Dele Alli, respectively.
Watford substitutes: Pantilimon, Prodl, Holebas, Anya, Behrami, Amrabat, Deeney.
Watford XI (4-5-1): Gomes; Nyom, Cathcart, Britos, Ake; Abdi, Suarez, Watson, Capoue, Jurado; Ighalo.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up afternoon…
An excellent first half of the campaign led to many tipping Watford to qualify for the Europa League in their first season back in the top flight, but a disappointing post-Christmas slump has made that an increasingly unlikely scenario unless they are able to quickly turn things around. In the seven league games leading up to the festive period the Hornets won five times, but since Boxing Day’s 2-2 draw away to Chelsea they have picked up just one victory, with four of those games all ending in defeats. However, they seem to have steadied the ship in recent weeks, with a 2-1 win against Newcastle United being followed by a 0-0 draw against the aforementioned Blues during the week. Quique Sanchez Flores will be hoping that his side can put in another strong performance against Tottenham today as they aim to keep alive their hopes of finishing the season in the top half of the table.
After suffering a slightly mixed start to the season, it’s been a wonderful two months for Tottenham, who are now not only firmly part of the race for a top-four finish but also find themselves battling with Arsenal, Manchester City and Leicester City for the Premier League title. Things have been particularly good for Spurs since the start of the year, and they head into this afternoon’s game with just one defeat in eight clashes, the last five of which have all ended in victories. They look equally strong at both ends of the pitch, even after the nasty knee injury suffered by Jan Vertonghen two weeks ago, with Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli and, most importantly, Harry Kane consistently impressing in front of goal. As a result, Mauricio Pochettino’s men have found the back of the net 14 times in the last three weeks, setting them up nicely for a game against a side that are currently struggling to pick up victories.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Tottenham Hotspur and Watford at White Hart Lane.

FULL TIME! Southampton take a big step towards European football, with the Saints slipping to within two points of West Ham in the Premier League table. An early goal from Yoshida proved to be just enough, with Koeman's men holding out for the win despite a red card for Wanyama. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Collins claims for a penalty! The West Ham defender tries to flick a close-range shot goalwards, but it is blocked by a hand! Fonte definitely handled, but the Portuguese defender didn't know much about it at all.
(90’) Byram tries to whip in a cross from the right-hand side, but Long makes a timely block. The ex-Leeds man tries another delivery, but Cedric is on hand this time to head clear. Southampton are just hoofing clearances upfield and leaving Austin to chase the loose ball.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Ward-Prowse comes into the game for the dying embers, with the cautioned Clasie taking a well-earned rest. ---
(90’) We're well into the five minutes of stoppage time announced at St. Mary's.
(90’) Anywhere will do for the hosts, with Forster lashing a hurried clearance away from danger following a terribly angled backpass from Cedric! Incredibly risky from the Portugal international, who almost curled a neat finish into the back of his own net! Desperate times call for desperate measures, it seems.
(89’) Big chance missed from Austin! The England international is picked out in the West Ham penalty area, but lashes a powerful effort five yards the wrong side of the far upright! That could have sewn up the three points.
--- 87’ Yellow card Byram gets a booking for throwing his body dangerously into a physical challenge with Bertrand. ---
(87’) Byram is caught offside! The former Leeds youngster is found making a run towards the back post, but sprints off a second too early! The linesman's flag denies him, but Bertrand managed to track the movement of his man anyhow.
(85’) Song takes aim from the edge of the penalty area, before feigning to shoot and finding the feet of Payet. A flick from the Frenchman falls to Valencia, but the Ecuador international can only blaze high and wide from the tightest of angles! What a waste.
--- 83’ Yellow card Clasie picks up a yellow card in the dying stages, with another Saints player now walking the disciplinary tightrope. ---
(83’) Carroll is the subject of a swirling back-post delivery, but Van Dijk gets in ahead to lean on the former Newcastle striker. West Ham aren't allowing Southampton to leave their own penalty box at present, with the final 10 minutes set to feel like 10 hours for the observing home fans.
(81’) Good defending from Van Dijk! The former Celtic defender stands up well to Emenike, ensuring that the substitute is unable to swivel and test Forster. In the aftermath, a secondary cross is lumped into the box, but the Southampton goalkeeper rises above traffic to make a fantastic claim. Moments later, Song fires high and wide after being teed up by Payet.
(79’) West Ham are pushing plenty of bodies forward now, with Austin being left entirely to his own devices up top for the Saints. Song drives down the left-hand side, before cutting infield, but Fonte slides in to make a vital tackle. The turnover in possession leads to a Southampton break, but their lone striker can only win a corner for his side - which comes to nothing.
(77’) Cresswell whips in a wicked cross from the left-hand side, which results in some penalty-box pinball! Carroll challenges for the initial delivery, but fails to make contact, with the rebound falling to Valencia! The Ecuadorian forward jinks onto his left foot, but sees a curling attempt blocked easily.
(75’) What a chance for Emenike! The Nigerian striker is picked out at the near post by a fantastic cross, but the substitute can only guide a header some way wide of the upright! He was relatively unchallenged, with Forster sure to have breathed a sigh of relief there.
--- 73’ Substitution Emenike is thrown in at the deep end for the away side, with the ex-Fenerbahce striker having the chance to win the hearts of his new supporters tonight. ---
--- 72’ Substitution Austin is introduced for the final stages, with the ex-QPR striker freshening up what is a tiring forward line for the Saints. ---
(71’) We're into the final 20 minutes, with the 10 men of Southampton struggling to stem the tide. Song is given the ball on the edge of the penalty area, before the ex-Arsenal man tries an audacious, curling shot from 18 yards out. The ball sails harmlessly over the top and behind for a goal-kick.
(69’) West Ham are seeing more of the ball, but Bilic's men still are struggling to piece together any dangerous moves. The inclusion of Carroll gives a large target to hit, but Forster remains relatively unchallenged in the second half. The England international needs to be tested, especially given the slick and slippery turf at St. Mary's.
--- 67’ Yellow card Valencia now picks up a booking, with the Ecuador international lunging into a laboured and poor tackle. ---
(65’) Cedric tries to make progress down the right-hand side, with Pelle then fed possession. The ex-Feyenoord striker earns his team a free-kick, with Bertrand poised to take. The England international delivers, but Van Dijk can only nod a looping header well wide of the far post! Wasteful stuff from the Saints.
(63’) Long manages to race into the penalty area, with the ex-Hull man having the pace to escape from Collins! The Irishman looks to squeeze a cheeky finish inside the near upright, but fails to hit the target! Adrian looked to be struggling, had his opponent executed his idea properly.
--- 61’ Substitution Tomkins limps off the field, with Byram coming into the game at right-back for the away side. ---
--- 61’ Substitution Moses is hauled off by Bilic, with Carroll coming into the fray as a new focal point for the Hammers attack. Southampton should expect to be bombarded now. ---
(60’) Pelle does well to hold the ball up and outmuscle Tomkins, with the Italy international managing to release Bertrand down the left flank. The former Chelsea left-back curls in a neat cross, but Reid makes a timely headed interception at the near upright! Adrian was caught in two minds as to whether to come out and claim that ball.
(58’) Tomkins and Antonio combine down the right-hand side, but Long tracks back to break up play. The visitors continue to push on, with Cresswell shooting from 30 yards out, but the young full-back can only see an effort clatter into a proximate defender. This could be a long game for the Saints to see out.
--- 56’ Substitution Romeu is introduced for the home side, with the former Chelsea man set to sit in Wanyama's vacated position. Mane is sacrificed by Koeman, with Pelle and Long left up top. ---
--- 54’ Red card! RED CARD! SOUTHAMPTON DOWN TO TEN! Wanyama makes the lonely walk to the dressing room, with the hosts now having to see out their win while a man light. The ex-Celtic midfielder lunged into a terribly timed tackle on Payet, with the referee having little choice but to go straight to his top pocket! ---
(53’) Valencia is picked out making a run into the right channel, with the ex-Emelec striker unafraid to shoot from a very tight angle! Forster makes a comfortable stop, with Van Dijk putting enough pressure on to make life difficult for the West Ham striker.
(52’) Valencia goes down off the ball, with the Ecuador international claiming a push from Yoshida. The Japanese defender is perhaps harshly penalised, with the away side able to load the box with blue shirts as a result. Payet whips in a delivery, but it fails to even beat the first man. Oddly wasteful from the France international.
(50’) Antonio drives into the penalty area brilliantly, with the former Forest winger holding off Bertrand with ease. However, Yoshida is present to then hold up and rob the Englishman of possession. Koeman's side are on the back foot, with the Hammers continuing in the same vein in which they ended the first half.
(48’) Southampton have been uncompromising with their defending in the opening few minutes, with a couple of fouls conceded in unnecessary areas of the field. Tomkins launches a free-kick delivery onto Cedric, but the ex-Sporting right-back manages to deal with Valencia peeling onto him.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! West Ham were looking bright at the end of the previous period, but an equaliser has evaded them thus far. Bilic has some interesting options to call upon on his bench, so the Saints aren't home and dry quite yet.
HALF TIME! Southampton head into the interval with a 1-0 lead, given to them in the early stages by Yoshida. West Ham have since come back into the contest, with Forster kept alert by a few close-range headed efforts from Reid. This clash, which is vital in terms of securing European football, is far from over.
(45’) There is one minute of first-half stoppage time.
(45’) Pelle tees up Mane on the edge of the penalty area, before the latter accidentally bustles into a poor tackle on Noble. Koeman's men just can't seem to maintain any pressure at present, though Pelle has displayed some lovely tecnical ability at times. Long cuts a cross back from the left byline, but Tomkins stands up well to dispossess the Irishman.
(43’) Adrian has been put under pressure after a couple of poor backpasses from his central defenders, with the weather perhaps starting to come into the equation. The rain is pouring down, with the ball skidding off the turf at real pace.
(41’) Noble released Moses down the left-hand side, with the Nigeria international beating Clasie all ends up! Fonte is forced to put a clearance behind for a corner, which comes to nothing. West Ham keep the pressure on, but Reid can only leather a poorly executed long-range effort well wide of the target.
(39’) Narrowly over five minutes remain in the first half, with West Ham creeping their way towards a potential equaliser. Antonio goes on a driving run, before attempting to release Valencia down the right channel, but Van Dijk comes across to deny the Hammers' attack in its tracks. The visitors' deliveries into the penalty box have left something to be desired thus far.
(37’) Reid challenges for a near-post corner delivery once again, with the New Zealand international stretching every sinew in order to guide a flicked header just over the crossbar! Forster hasn't had a great deal to do in this first half of action, but West Ham are gradually narrowing their sights. Koeman will be concerned with how his side have tailed off since taking the lead.
(35’) Song lifts a pass out to Tomkins on the right flank, with Noble then able to take control of possession and win a foul from Wanyama. Payet is the specialist tasked with flighting in the delivery, but Collins can't make the contact required to turn the ball goalwards! Reid scrambles for the second ball, but the Saints clear.
(33’) Southampton open play out to the right-hand side, with Cedric clipping a neat diagonal to the edge of the penalty area. Pelle does brilliantly to bring the ball under his spell, but Song is quickly able to get his body in the way and deny the Italian striker. Chances are drying up at present, with possession spending plenty of time with the West Ham back four.
(31’) The opening half an hour has had a real ebb and flow to it, with Southampton's bright start being met by eventual resistance from the Hammers! Valencia's claim for a penalty and Reid's close-range header remain the visitors best opportunities of the half for Bilic and company.
(29’) Good save from Forster! The former Celtic goalkeeper does brilliantly to deny Reid, after a powerful near-post headed flick from the New Zealand international! The England international did well to parry the ball well beyond the danger zone!
(27’) Antonio is found pressing down the right-hand side, before the ex-Forest man gets to the byline and thunders a low drive into the six-yard box! Fortunately for the hosts, Van Dijk is on hand to hook a clearance away! After a very cagey start from the Hammers, Bilic's men are whirring into action.
(25’) Mane drives forward at pace, with Reid needing to step out and commit a cynical foul on the Saints winger. Southampton are able to loft a free-kick delivery into the box as a result, but the resulting pinball in the penalty area results in nothing more than confusion. The away side clear their lines in hurried fashion, with Adrian caught in no man's land somewhat.
(23’) Valencia drives into the penalty area, but the Ecuador international is well marshalled by Yoshida. The West Ham striker goes down, claiming a push from the Japanese goalscorer, but the referee rightly opts to wave play on. The away outfit are slowly getting into this contest.
(21’) Forster watches a deflected effort from Payet head onto the roof of his net, as the Hammers struggle to generate any kind of danger. Valencia goes down heavily, after a poor challenge from Van Dijk, but West Ham opt to take the free-kick short. Bilic's men just continue to retain possession, probably in an attempt to calm their early nerves.
(19’) Pelle threatens from close range once again, but the Italy international fails to test Adrian once again! Southampton aren't creating as many opportunities at present, but their back three hasn't been tested at all. Valencia has been kept very quiet by Fonte, with Koeman's men all working hard to do their individual jobs well.
(17’) West Ham work their way down the right-hand side, but Moses quickly runs into trouble against Bertrand. Forster finally has something to do moments later, however, with the same ex-Chelsea winger driving towards the edge of the penalty box. The Nigerian forward shoots from range, but a wicked deflection makes it easy for the Saints' goalkeeper to collect.
(15’) West Ham manage to get their foot on the ball, but Southampton have no intention of pressing high at all. The Saints are holding their shape and inviting Bilic's outfit to play the ball into controlling areas of the field. The away side just look a little bit low on ideas and confidence, following a bustling start from Koeman's personnel.
(13’) Cedric clips a cross into the box from deep on the right flank, but Pelle can only guide a terrible header high and wide of the target! The former Feyenoord striker just couldn't rise high enough to get over that attempt. Koeman's men have their tails up, with the Hammers being relentlessly probed in the opening quarter of an hour.
(11’) Southampton are looking in the mood tonight, with Mane, Pelle and Long causing havoc for the visiting defence. Tomkins and Reid are being pulled all over the park, with the hosts even having the pace in behind to keep Adrian on his toes too.
--- 9’ Assist The former Celtic midfielder did well to hold his nerve in the penalty area, keeping his cool and then picking the right pass. ---
--- 9’ Goal! Yet another corner is taken short by the Saints, before Mane feeds Wanyama into the penalty area. The Kenyan midfielder stabs a low cross towards the edge of the six-yard box, allowing for Yoshida to lumber forward and lash a close-range finish past Adrian! ---
(9’) Good save from Adrian! Pelle and Mane combine, before the latter sprays a pass out wide to Bertrand. The Englishman curls in a looping cross, which finds its way onto the head of Long! The former Hull striker powers a well-directed header goalwards, but the West Ham shot-stopper springs to one side to make a solid intervention!
(7’) Southampton win themselves another corner on the left-hand side, with a looping back-post delivery dealt with easily by Song. The ex-Barcelona man tries to feed a run by Valencia, but Wanyama tracks back brilliantly to cut the attack short. Koeman's men are on top and exerting the early pressure.
(5’) West Ham are yet to really break out of their own half and threaten, with Bilic's men happy to take the sting out of the game with a bit of slow possession. Mane tries to slide Long in behind enemy lines, but the Republic of Ireland international hasn't got the legs to get on the end of the pass before Adrian.
(3’) Long is released in behind, courtesy of a lovely flick around the corner from Pelle, but Reid covers across to concede a corner voluntarily. Bertrand takes short, before a secondary delivery into the box is headed clear by Moses. Southampton are on the front foot from the off.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! The hosts need a win here tonight in order to close the points gap between themselves and the Hammers, with Bilic's men able to press into fifth place with victory at St. Mary's.
West Ham substitutes: Randolph, Carroll, Obiang, O'Brien, Byram, Emenike, Oxford.
West Ham starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Adrian; Tomkins, Collins, Reid, Cresswell; Noble, Song; Antonio, Payet, Moses; Valencia.
Southampton substitutes: Tadic, Romeu, Martina, Ward-Prowse, Juanmi, Stekelenburg, Austin.
Southampton starting line-up (3-4-3): Forster; Yoshida, Van Dijk, Fonte; Cedric, Wanyama, Clasie, Bertrand; Long, Pelle, Mane.
TEAM NEWS: James Tomkins continues at right-back, with Sam Byram named on the bench. Alex Song and Mark Noble will provide the basis for the likes of Victor Moses, Dimitri Payet and Michail Antonio to support lone striker Enner Valencia. Andy Carroll and Emmanuel Emenike are including among the substitutes.
TEAM NEWS: Maya Yoshida comes into the starting line-up for the hosts, with Dusan Tadic dropping to the bench as a result. Oriol Romeu also takes a spot among the substitutes, with Jordy Clasie and Victor Wanyama holding in midfield. Graziano Pelle is given the nod to start up top ahead of January signing Charlie Austin. Ronald Koeman has opted to rotate his midfield somewhat this evening.
The hosts are unbeaten during their last four matches, with the Saints able to even hold title challengers Arsenal to a 0-0 stalemate at the Emirates last time out. The Hammers, meanwhile, have only recorded one win on the road in their last eight competitive fixtures away from Upton Park.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of West Ham's away visit to face Southampton, as Slaven Bilic's men look to keep the pace up during their chase towards European football. The Saints need to pick up three points this evening, as they currently sit five points adrift of tonight's opponents in seventh place in the Premier League table.

Arsenal get the response that they needed, taking thee points for the first time in five league games. They move up to third, below Tottenham on goal difference and five points shy of leaders Leicester, who they play next week. Goals from Ozil and Oxlade-Chamberlain a minute apart in the first half did the damage, and in truth, the game never quite lived up to that whirlwind 90 seconds. Still, points are all that matter, and that's something that Bournemouth will have to do without as they fail to advance up the table. That's all the time we have, thanks for joining us!
--- 90’ +3 Substitution The latest of time-wasting changes as Walcott comes on for Giroud. ---
(90’) MAGNIFICENT DOUBLE SAVE FROM CECH! The Arsenal defence froze as Cook puts his foot through a loose ball inside the area, which the keeper saves with his legs. He does even better seconds later as Arter whacks one to the bottom corner on the turn, pushing it around the post!
(90’) RAMSEY SHOULD HAVE WRAPPED IT UP! The Welshman is in the clear and has Giroud in support. He opts to advance all the way to the near post and takes way too long to release the ball, meaning that Boruc is able to make the block.
(88’) PENALTY? King tries to buy a spot-kick off Monreal, but the referee feels that he went down too easily. Moments later, Stanislas has a header, but Cech leaps high to keep a hold of it.
(86’) Ramsey lashes a long ball through the middle for Giroud to chase ,but he's never going to get there ahead of Boruc. Arsenal are closing in on the points as Bournemouth finally seem out of ideas.
(84’) GOOD CHANCE THERE! Stanislas has provided a reliable spark down the right since his introduction, and another delivery puts King in a great position to score, but he fails to make a meaningful connection on the ball.
--- 82’ Substitution An off game once more for Alexis, who is still struggling to find his feet after that long injury layoff. It's strange that his and Coquelin's return coincided with Arsenal's poor run in form, but doubtless they'll be back to their best soon. On comes Gibbs. ---
(81’) As for Arsenal, it's hardly been a vintage performance from them, but they applied the ruthless touch when the opportunities presented themselves, and have generally defended this lead well.
(79’) There's little life left in the game at this point, which suits the Gunners just fine, as they continue to frustrate Bournemouth by shutting the door whenever they enter the final third.
--- 77’ Substitution So there's no scoring statement made today by Afobe against his former club, as he's pulled by Howe. However, he still enjoyed a decent outing, where he asked a few questions of the defence. On comes Grabban. ---
(75’) Finally Arsenal create the right move to launch a counter-attack, as Alexis races into space, before squaring to Ramsey on his left. The Welshman fails to return the ball to the Chilean as he loses his balance though. He's claiming a foul, but the referee isn't interested.
(73’) Decent chance there for the hosts as Stanislas' cross takes a nick off Koscielny, which Cech grabs before Afobe can figure out what's going on. A little more opportunism and Arsenal would have been in trouble.
(71’) Arsenal continue to bide their time off the ball, trying to soak up the pressure from the hosts. They're defending just fine, but are unable to produce the right out-ball to really get going on the counter whenever they regain possession.
(69’) Open period in the game at the moment as both sides work the ball quickly through central areas. To be fair, Arsenal have been pretty comfortable in the second period, with Bournemouth not doing enough to get back into this.
--- 67’ Substitution Wenger follows suit with a change of his own, introducing Coquelin for the goalscorer Oxlade-Chamberlain in a clear defensive alteration intended to shore up his midfield. ---
--- 66’ Substitution Gosling departs after a mediocre game, and is replaced by Joshua King. ---
--- 66’ Substitution That chance was indeed Ritchie's last comtribution of this game. He's been wasteful no doubt, showing no composure when required. On comes Junior Stanislas in his stead. ---
(64’) Ritchie has space and time to drive into the Arsenal half, but once in position at the top of the box, he lashes an effort wildly into the stratosphere for the third time in this match.
(62’) Afobe has held the ball up well here, and his quick feet have also enabled him to evade challenges from retreating Arsenal players whenever his back has been to goal.
(60’) COULD HAVE BEEN BETTER! Alexis takes Smith to the cleaners, beating him to the byline before lashing the ball into the six-yard area. The problem was that Giroud stepped back outside that zone, anticipating a cut-back.
(58’) Bournemouth are trying to take the game to Arsenal, and are committing a lot of players forward. This of course leaves them exposed on the break, but the Gunners seem unable to get out of their own half.
(56’) Giroud loses out in a foot-race with Smith, and in his attempts to win the ball back, steps on the heel of the player with his trailing leg. The referee calls him over, but it's just for a lecture.
(54’) First chance of the second period for the Gunners, as from a corner, Giroud overpowers Cook to get his head to the ball, but it's right down the throat of Boruc. Strong header, but not enough direction.
(52’) INTO THE SIDE NETTING! Bournemouth continue to ask questions of the Arsenal defence. Smith somehow keeps a hold of the ball when trying to turn Koscielny, and he lashes one on goal from inside the area, but it's the wrong side of the post.
(50’) Decent look here for Ritchie, who is the beneficiary of a feed from Smith, but not for the first time in this game, he fails to keep his effort under the crossbar, and the chance is gone.
(48’) No changes to report from the half-time break, and it's Bournemouth who have made the better start to the second period. One more goal puts them right back in this one and gets Arsenal on edge.
(46’) Here we go again.
That will do it for now, as Arsenal hold a two-goal advantage at the break, putting themselves in a great position to end a four-match winless run in the league. A pair of accomplished finishes from Ozil and Oxlade-Chamberlain within a minute of each other burst this game into life. Since then, Bournemouth have had their chances to get on the board, but have been thwarted by Cech and the Arsenal defence. Stay tuned for the second half in just a bit.
(45’) Cech comes to Arsenal's rescue again as he positions himself at the near post to block a shot from Smith, who had escaped into the box behind a ball-watching Monreal down the flank.
(45’) Arsenal try to launch a late attack, but both Oxlade-Chamberlain and Bellerin see the door shut down the right. Ozil then tries to keep things alive with a curler to the back post for Alexis, but it's headed clear.
(44’) Good bit of hold-up play from Giroud, who plucks a pass from Cech out of the sky and puts Arsenal on the attack in the Bournemouth half immediately. However, Daniels covers well to challenge Oxlade-Chamberlain, who was looking to burst forward.
(42’) Arsenal are closing this half on the defensive, as their former player Afobe gets a decent run into the area, but the trajectory of his movement ultimately takes him too far away from goal.
(40’) Daniels marauds down the right channel and gets the ball into the feet of the lively Arter. Koscielny is there to get a challenge in, but it falls for Ritchie instead, who smashes a wild shot over the top.
(38’) Bournemouth have given a good account of themselves since going behind, but they need to start being a little more ruthless in front of goal. One more Arsenal strike would end this as a contest, you feel.
(36’) Surman dictates a decent spell of possession for the hosts, as he spins onto a pass from Daniels, before playing in Smith deep down the right-hand side. However, his second attempt at a through ball to Gosling is intercepted.
(34’) Arsenal are being patient at the moment, keeping the ball, which is worrying the home fans at the moment. They don't like seeing their side camped around their own area, especially against a visiting team that they feel are a little vulnerable, despite the two-goal lead.
(32’) You can tell that the scoring is far from done in this game. That's two great opportunities for Bournemouth to get on the board since Arsenal's double salvo. Giroud is penned in by Smith near the corner flag, but manages to buy a corner off his legs - which comes to nothing.
(30’) BELLERIN BAILS OUT GABRIEL! The Brazilian is caught in possession by Pugh and suddenly the midfielder is through on goal! It appears that the finish in inevitable, but the incredible pace of the Spaniard gets him in position to nip the ball off Pugh's toes.
(28’) STRONG SAVE! Arter advances to the top of the box and lets fly with a stinger of an effort from range, which needs the full flexibility of Cech to tip over the crossbar! Important stop to keep that two-goal lead intact.
(26’) Well, Arsenal needed to win here and make a statement after dropping points in recent weeks, and they've put themselves in an excellent position now. That goal drought is also fading into memory fast.
--- 24’ Goal! ANOTHER ONE FOR ARSENAL! Almost straight from kick-off, the Gunners attack again. Ramsey sprays a pass for the arriving Oxlade-Chamberlain down the left, and he runs onto the ball wide of his man, before driving a tremendous low finish across the keeper and in via the base of the far post! ---
--- 24’ Assist Ramsey spotted the run of his team-mate and played the pass with perfect timing. ---
--- 23’ Goal! GREAT FINISH FROM OZIL! The German arrives late in the area to smash in a flick-on with an accomplished finish on his right foot! Arsenal's long goal drought is broken! ---
--- 23’ Assist A lovely little flick-on at the back post to set up that finish for Ozil. ---
(21’) Not much happening at the moment, with both teams unable to keep a hold of the ball for longer than a beat. We haven't gotten much in the way of chances so far, with neither keeper tested.
(19’) Since awarding that yellow card to Flamini, the referee hasn't given a lot to the home side, despite the feeling in the ground that a few Arsenal challenges deserved to be penalised.
(17’) After a Bournemouth attack breaks down,Arsenal break quickly, and a cross into the area from Bellerin seems primed for Giroud. However, a crucial defensive header from Cook gets rid of the danger.
(15’) A long ball over the top misses Giroud, but is picked up by Alexis instead. He wasn't expecting it though, meaning that he has to rush a shot on the volley and at an angle, and can't get it on target.
(13’) Afobe is shaping up to be a handful for the Gunners, and he wins a free-kick off Monreal, presenting Bournemouth with a decent little chance. However, Ritchie's delivery sails out of play.
(11’) Bournemouth are starting to take control of this game since that booking for Flamini, and the Gunners are struggling to get the ball out of their own half. Good play from the home side.
--- 9’ Yellow card Poor challenge from Flamini, who takes a chunk out of Arter with a two-footed lunge. He gets to the ball first clearly, but his follow-through caught the player and as his studs were showing, the referee was quite right to produce a yellow card. ---
(7’) Good period for the visitors as they carve their way quickly down the left, and Monreal's cutback is cleared only to Ramsey at the top of the area. The Welshman has a crack from there, but it's blocked.
(5’) Oxlade-Chamberlain advances through the middle and slides a pass between the centre-backs for Alexis to chase. However, Cook recovers well to make an important sliding challenge to stop the play.
(3’) A moment of indecision at the back for Arsenal nearly lets Afobe through, meaning that Cech has to race off his line to get to the ball first. He actually goes a fair way up the right flank, before rushing a clearance out of play.

Bournemouth have only played Arsenal twice before, and have lost both times, failing to score in either meeting. They suffered a 2-0 defeat at the Emirates in the reverse fixture earlier in the season, but will fancy their chances against a side deeply lacking in confidence and form.
Leicester's big win at Manchester City has seen the Gunners fall eight points behind the league leaders - albeit with this game in hand. Arsenal have not won in four league matches, and have failed to score in their last three. Another blank, and they will equal their longest-ever Premier League run without a goal set back in February 2009.
Bournemouth have not lost in three games, and are as close to the top half of the table as they are to the relegation zone. Only two defeats in their last 12 league outings have seen them move away from the bottom three. Hello and welcome to our live commentary of the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Arsenal at the Goldsands Stadium. The Gunners are aiming to resurrect a faltering title bid, while the hosts will want to make inroads towards the top half of the table. Stick with us for all the action.

Diego Costa's stoppage-time equaliser ensures the Blues remain unbeaten under Guus Hiddink, cancelling out Jesse Lingard's emphatic opener.
