(90’) FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
--- 90’ +5 Substitution Hoping at this point to just cling on for a draw, United make their final change to milk what little time is left on the clock. Ander Herrera replaces Juan Mata, who didn't have enough of a say in attack. ---
(90’) Celebrations finally cease, and we are poised for a grandstand finish! Chelsea are pouring it on again and Stamford Bridge is absolutely buzzing with anticipation! Surely they can't complete the turnaround?
--- 90’ +1 Goal! CHELSEA HAVE THEIR EQUALISER! They've been persistent, and it has paid off in a big way! Fabregas threads a weak ball into the area, and Blind slips which allows it to go through for Costa. The striker's first attempt is blocked by Borthwick-Jackson, which throws De Gea off, but he's able to stick with it to tap home the follow-up! ---
(90’) The board goes up to indicate SIX minutes of stoppage time, which should serve as a bit of encouragement for the Blues.
(89’) JUST OVER! Costa fights off both Rooney and Blind to get on the end of Willian's free-kick, but he can't direct it on target! De Gea will be in no rush to take the ensuing goal-kick as we get set to enter stoppage time. Can United hold?
--- 87’ Substitution United make their second change of the evening, and there is a loud roar from the away supporters as goalscorer Jesse Lingard is withdrawn. Memphis Depay gets a brief cameo in his stead. ---
(85’) So poor from Willian! His free-kick is dealt with easily, but the Brazilian is afforded another chance to cause some havoc from the ensuing corner - which he flubs even worse. That will do nothing to please Hiddink. Chelsea need to produce a better end product or they're headed for a first defeat under the Dutchman.
--- 83’ Yellow card Smalling is booked for a deliberate handball, which awards Chelsea a glorious opportunity from a free-kick just a yard outside the left of the penalty area. ---
(81’) The tempo has slowed a bit as we enter the final 10 minutes. Chelsea are gearing up for a final push, in an attempt to avoid a first defeat under Hiddink and deny United a possible season-turning victory.
--- 79’ Yellow card A cynical tug of the shirt in midfield sees Lingard into the referee's book. ---
--- 79’ Substitution Van Gaal draws from his bench to make his first change of the match, and it sees Morgan Schneiderlin come on to provide some fresh legs in midfield, with Fellaini giving way. ---
(78’) Groans head throughout the ground as play is forced to be brought to a halt with Carrick down, seemingly suffering from a cramp. He pops back up after a few seconds, which does nothing to settle the rage of these Chelsea supporters.
(76’) STAT: Chelsea are on the current longest unbeaten run in the Premier League, going without a defeat in eight league matches now (W3 D5). Despite this, they still haven't recorded back-to-back wins in the league this season.
(74’) Great effort! Shades of the goal Rooney scored in the Manchester derby a few years back, as a ball comes into the area from Darmian, and the striker meets it with a clever overhead kick! He can't get the contact spot on, however, and it bounces wide of the near post.
(72’) DE GEA STILL AT IT! The Spaniard this time denies his fellow countryman, beating Fabregas' effort away at the near post. United are being pinned back in defence, barely clinging to this lead!
(70’) Chelsea starting to throw caution to the wind and commit bodies forward. This has been a wonderful match of football, contrary to what may have been expected at the start. United are dropping deeper in defence and the bus is starting to be parked - which will make for an unnerving finish.
(68’) THAT IS SPECIAL! Azpilicueta makes a determined run to keep a Chelsea attack alive inside the United penalty area, heading the ball back for Ivanovic. The right-back shows an impressive bit of skill to send a fierce half-volley at goal from close range, but somehow De Gea is able to react and knock it over the bar!
--- 67’ Substitution Chelsea make their final change of the match, and they're going for broke as Pedro comes on to replace Matic. ---
(66’) STAT: Manchester United have won just one of their last 13 Premier League trips to Stamford Bridge, a 3-2 triumph in October 2012 (D4, L8).
(64’) Headed behind! Willian floats a teasing delivery into the area, but Carrick is on hand to usher it behind for a corner. That's a prominent piece of defending from the veteran midfielder.
--- 63’ Yellow card Blind barges into the back of Costa and gives an unnecessary push, just outside the penalty area. He goes into the book, but more importantly is the ensuing free-kick which presents Chelsea the chance for an immediate response. ---
--- 61’ Assist Important touch from Rooney, who gets the assist, but that was all made possible by the cross from Borthwick-Jackson. ---
--- 61’ Goal! UNITED HAVE THEIR BREAKTHROUGH! What a special finish that is from Jese Lingard! Borthwick-Jackson delivers a tremendous cross in from the left, yet again, which Rooney touches into the path of the winger. Lingard takes a touch to turn Azpilicueta, before sending a venomous half-volley into the top corner while falling to ground! That is unstoppable! ---
--- 59’ Substitution Gary Cahill comes on to replace the French centre-half. ---
(59’) Hopefully this is a matter of looking worse than it actually is - but that certainly looked a terrible injury. Who knows how long it could keep him out, but based on the cringe-worthy nature of the landing, and the pain he was in, this is likely the last time we'll see Zouma on the pitch this season.
(57’) OH NO! This appears to be a terrible injury for Zouma, who lands very awkwardly, hyper-extending his right knee, before going down in real pain. He can be heard screaming from a mile away as the training staff rushes on to attend to him. Stamford Bridge collectively holds its breath.
--- 55’ Substitution Hiddink has seen about enough, and on comes Belgian playmaker Eden Hazard. Oscar gives way, and he has not had a match to remember. ---
(54’) DOUBLE SAVE! Martial holds the ball up in the penalty are and tees up Lingard atop the box, but the winger's strike is punched aside by a diving Courtois! Pressure stays on and Rooney tries to power the ball in from a tight angle, but again the Chelsea keeper is up to the task!
(52’) STAT: Wayne Rooney has scored five goals in his last five Premier League appearances; more than he had managed in his previous 25 apps in the competition (4). Rooney has been involved in eight of the Red Devils last 10 league goals (five goals, three assists).
(50’) COURTOIS ALERT! Rooney is starting to come to life, though! The striker makes another tidy turn in attack, this time firing a surprise strike towards the near post, but the Chelsea keeper is able to dive across and get a paw to it! Lovely attacking football from United early on here.
(48’) First chance to the visitors! Manchester United open the second half on the front foot, and it nearly pays dividends as Mata's delightful ball over the top spots the run of Rooney, but it's just a bit too tall for the striker who fails to make clean contact with his header!
(46’) Back underway at Stamford Bridge!
The scoreline is what most would have expected at the interval, but it has been a much more eventful half of football than what we saw over the course of the full 90 minutes at Old Trafford. Both sides enjoyed their prolonged spells in attack, but it is Chelsea who have come closer to breaking the deadlock. Martial and Willian have been the catalysts for either side, who look at their best when the full-backs get forward and provide a bit of width.
(45’) HALF TIME: CHELSEA 0-0 MANCHESTER UNITED.
(45’) PENALTY APPEALS DENIED! Chelsea are refused a strong claim for a spot kick as Blind blocks Terry's effort with his arm! Oliver had a good look and decided not to give it, and there's a case to be made for both sides. The Dutchman's arm clearly got the block in, but it was also tucked close to his body. It was more there for protection, had it been dropped to his side it would have undoubtedly smacked off his neck or face.
(43’) That is a special cross! A delightful delivery from a talented individual, as Darmian launches a diagonal ball into the box from out wide. His delivery is low to the ground and sneaks behind the Chelsea defence and out of reach of Courtois, but neither Rooney or Martial can get on the end of it!
(41’) STAT: Manchester United have lost more often to Chelsea than any other opponent in the Premier League era (16 times).
(39’) Lingard has been a real weak spot for United going forward. The winger has offered no width at all, and is failing to assert his influence on the match. Azpilicueta has had an easy time defending the flank, which has made the Red Devils very one dimensional in attack.
(37’) It has been night and day in this first half from Chelsea. They started out so poorly, walking on egg shells and allowing United to pass their way around them with ease. They have since turned the corner, however, and appear to be inching ever so close to the breakthrough goal with the visitors unable to break out of their own end.
(35’) Needed a touch! An excellent ball forward finds Willian on the right fringe of the penalty area. The Brazilian turns Borthwick-Jackson inside out before whipping an inviting delivery across the face of goal for Oscar - but the ex-Internacional midfielder can't produce the decisive touch with Smalling draped all over him.
(33’) Lifted over! Excellent build-up play from the Blues! They're keeping and moving the ball around much better now. Oscar gets on the end of the latest bit of interplay inside the area, but from in close he's unable to find the top corner and kicks the advertising board in frustration.
(31’) STAT: Guus Hiddink led Real Betis to a 2-1 win over Louis van Gaal’s Barcelona in 2000, and managed three straight victories with AZ over PSV (also coached by the current United boss), before the two met again in December in the return fixture at Old Trafford which ended in a draw.
(29’) SMART SAVE! The Blues are slowly growing into the game, and win another corner. This one is met by the head of Matic at the near post, and he sends a glancing effort towards the far stick, but De Gea does well to get across and not just parry, but make the save and hold on to prevent a rebound from falling to the lurking Terry.
(27’) Chelsea finally win their first corner, with United having already taken nine. Fabregas' delivery is met by Costa, but his header loops over the bar off Blind. It goes unspotted by Michael Oliver and the Spanish striker charges at the referee, enraged with his decision to award a goal kick. He has to keep his cool better than that.
(25’) SPLENDID DELIVERY! Blind floats an excellent corner into the area, which actually lands at the feet of Fellaini. It almost catches the Belgian by surprise, as he fails to sort his footing and Chelsea are able to scramble clear. Back the other way come the Blues, and Willian displays some good hold-up play to win a free-kick.
(23’) Martial continues to give Ivanovic trouble on the flank. The Serbian right-back has been targeted by United in this first half, with the Frenchman and Borthwick-Jackson making strides down the left. They win another corner through Martial, and Blind's delivery is knocked behind for yet another set-piece opportunity.

(17’) Willian makes a darting run through the heart of midfield to advance the ball into the final third, which gets the home fans going. He gets the ball back again near the touchline and plays Matic down the right, but the midfielder is squeezed out capably by Fellaini as it runs behind for a goal kick.
(15’) Chelsea need to find a way to settle themselves down and start stringing together a few passes. It has been quite the unnerving start from the hosts, while Van Gaal will have to be pleased with the sort of confidence his team have showed through the first quarter of an hour.
(13’) Borthwick-Jackson has been lively thus far, and is providing the best attacking threat with his crossing from the left. He wins the visitors another corner, but a few attempts from United to cross the ball in are all dealt with confidently by the hosts.
(11’) United up their corner count to three through the first 10 minutes, but each of which has been dealt with accordingly by Chelsea. (7’) STAT: Chelsea are unbeaten in their last nine matches against Manchester United across all competitions (W5 D4).
(5’) Manchester United enjoyed a large portion of possession in the return fixture as well, but were only able to turn it into a pair of shots on target. They will be buoyed by their performance midweek, and the intent from the Red Devils is already clear with Borthwick-Jackson and Darmian prominent on the overlap.
(3’) Positive start for United, who enjoy a prolonged spell of possession inside the Chelsea half. They will be searching for a victory to act as a springboard for their top four hopes, while the Blues will be hoping for something similar to avoid becoming the first defending champions to finish outside the top seven the following year.

Amidst the many intriguing storylines, one to really keep an eye on is the battle of the two Dutch managers, who add another chapter to their storied 18-year rivalry. They have gone toe-to-toe on opposite touchlines in both La Liga and the Eredivisie. Van Gaal hasn’t beat his counterpart since 1999, while the current Chelsea boss has won four of five since (D1) – though it was Hiddink who derailed the Dutch national team in European qualifying, following their successful third-place finish at the World Cup under the current Manchester United boss.
Manchester United turned on the style in surprising fashion as they dismantled Stoke midweek at Old Trafford, and Louis van Gaal believes it could be the start of a revival of the club’s diminishing title hopes. While that may be a bit ambitious, what it did do is set the standard for what the club and fans should come to expect on a weekly basis. All that remains constant at this point is their need for victories in bunches – not a few impressive performances scattered throughout an accretion of lacklustre outings.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Stamford Bridge to take on Chelsea, with both outfits hoping to replenish their fractured egos. Under Guus Hiddink, Chelsea have been stable – far from the intimidating figure of last season, but a picture of composure when the club needed it most. Confidence is being restored but, as we are coming to see, it is a slow process as the Blues try to piece together the rubble leftover from Jose Mourinho’s tenure.

And that's it! Southampton hold on for a point at the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal undoubtedly had the better of things throughout, but the Gunners came up against an in-form Fraser Forster, whose heroics almost singlehandedly kept the home side at bay. The result ultimately means Wenger's men lose further ground on Premier League pacesetters Leicester City, who beat Liverpool 2-0 in the Midlands today. Jeers greeted the final whistle and no doubt the frustrations of supporters will linger at least until their next home match.

(90’) Forster again proves dependable and takes the sting out of things at the back, as he takes Bellerin's cross out of the air and holds on to it, despite seemingly landing partly on the post. The visitors are almost there.
(90’) Excellent play by Van Dijk, as the defender makes a tackle on the edge of his own area and then surges up the left flank all by himself, before eventually winning a throw-in level with the 18-yard line.

--- 87’ Yellow card And for Coquelin's first involvement, he clatters into Romeu and receives a yellow card. He can have no arguments about that! ---
--- 86’ Substitution Another switch for Saints now. Left-back Matt Target will get a few minutes in place of Mane, as Koeman looks to shore things up. ---

(77’) Fonte is finally up and on his feet again. He has bandages wrapped around his head and will be continuing.

Arsenal have generally edged things, but Southampton certainly look a potent threat going forward, particularly on the counter-attack. There's much more to come from these two sides, but the visitors will be happy at the break.

The only slight disappoint for the Spurs Head Coach will be that his team are not further in front, as they have created plenty of opportunities. You feel the visitors will need one more goal to make this game safe as Norwich have caused a few problems with their long balls over the top.
Where do Norwich go from here? They have found it extremely hard going so far against a rampant Tottenham team. Alex Neil will be very frustrated with the way his team started this match and they found themselves behind after a little over of 100 seconds. The Canaries have been far too passive and have simply allowed Spurs to have it all their own way in the opening 45 minutes. The midfield have been far too narrow and that has caused Ivo Pinto and Martin Olsson all sorts of bother on the flanks.
(45’) Naismith gets in between the Tottenham centre-back pairing and goes to ground after a coming together with Wimmer but nothing doing from the referee. The Norwich fans are far from impressed given that Spurs were awarded a penalty under similiar circumstances.
(45’) That's half-time here at Carrow Road! Norwich City 0-2 Tottenham Hotspur.
(44’) Mbokani has had precious little to go on and is cutting a rather forlorn figure up against Wimmer and Alderweireld. The Norwich centre-forward does well to earn his side a free-kick. Howson chucks it into the box but it is headed away to safety.
(42’) SAVE! Eriksen is the latest Spurs to sting the palms of Rudd in the Norwich goal. The Danish international races onto a Kane flick on and hits a decent right-footed shot but it is straight at the goalkeeper.
(40’) WIDE! Alli has a free header from about ten yards out but glances his header wide. He will be desperately disappointed not to hit the target from there. Rose had whipped in an excellent ball from the left after being set away by Son.
(38’) It is all rather flat from a Norwich perspective at the moment. The home fans don't feel that they are getting much assistance from the officials either which isn't helping their cause. It is crucial that they don't concede again before half-time.
(36’) Norwich are really struggling defensively at the moment. Spurs are cutting through them seemingly at will each time they go forward. The full-backs Olsson and Pinto need a lot more protection than they are getting just now. Far too often they are being left one-on-one.
(34’) OFF THE POST! Kane again finds himself in space on the left-hand side and turns Pinto inside-out before seeing his left foot drive rattle the frame of the goal from an acute angle.
(32’) The size of the task for the Canaries looks sizeable now. There did not seem to be a huge amount of contact between Bassong and Alli for the penalty decision but there were very few complaints from the home side. A moment to forget for the ex-Spurs defender.
--- 30’ Goal! 2-0 to Tottenham! Harry Kane makes no mistake from twelve yards. Sending Rudd the wrong way and slotting the ball away to the bottom right corner of the net. Cool as you like! ---
--- 29’ Yellow card To add insult to injury Sebastien Bassong is booked for his challenge on Dele Alli. The Spurs fans wanted a red card for what they saw as the denial of a goalscoring opportunity. ---
(29’) PENALTY TO SPURS! Kane rolls his man on the edge of the box and unleashes a fierce low left-footed shot that Rudd does well to parry away. Alli again looks to convert the rebound but he is pushed by Bassong and the referee points to the spot.
(27’) Jarvis has been Norwich's best outlet over the last few minutes. This time the former West Ham man takes Eric Dier to the byline and wins his side a corner. But once again Tottenham stand firm from the set-piece delivery.
(25’) Tettey, Howson and Mulumbu are starting to get a foothold in the midfield. This is giving Norwich a platform to try and build some attacking momentum and pressure. The play is still a bit too much infront of Spurs at the moment, they need to try and get in behind through Naismith and Jarvis.
(23’) Olsson tries to get an attack going for the Canaries but is upended by Son which gives Norwich the chance to load the box. It's not the best cross into the area and after a bit of pinball Tottenham manage to clear.
(21’) OVER! Dele Alli sends in a cross from the left-wing but overhits it and the ball curls just over the bar. The way things have been going for the young man recently you wouldn't have been surprised if that had flown in.
(19’) SHOT! The Canaries go a bit more direct in their play and it creates half a chance for the home side. The ball is pumped upfield and the loose ball drops to Matt Jarvis who wastes no time in letting fly with his right foot but can't control his shoot and it sails harmlessly over.
(18’) CLOSE! Harry Kane pops up on the left wing and goes past Pinto like he isn't there, the England striker sends in a low cross to the near post that is met by Son but his left-footed strike only finds the side netting on this occasion.
(16’) The rotation of the Spurs front four is causing the Norwich City defence and midfield all sorts of problems so far this evening. It is very difficult to know who to pick up as they are interchanging positions so frequently. At the end of this passage of play Son cuts inside onto his left foot and fires over the crossbar wildly.
(14’) SAVE! Much better from Norwich, as they string a few passes together for the first time tonight ends up with Mbokani firing in a low shot through the legs of Rose but Lloris is right behind it and holds on comfortably.
(12’) Even at this relatively early stage of this game it is imperative that Norwich don't concede again as then they will have a mountain to climb. At the moment the Canaries are caught between stalls they are not sure whether to press Tottenham higher up the pitch or to drop off and sit deep. The home fans are also getting a little restless with their team for not being combative enough so far.
(10’) Kyle Walker gallops down the right on the overlap and does well to win a corner from Martin Olsson. Eriksen takes the resulting set-piece and picks out Alderweireld at the far post who heads it back across goal but just wide!
(8’) The home side are looking to settle down now and work their way into the match after that shock of going behind so quickly. The absolutely worst possible start to this game for Alex Neil and his players. Norwich have enjoyed a bit more possession in the last couple of minutes or so but Spurs look so threatening on the counter-attack.
(6’) The Canaries try and get their opponents turned and a rather hopeful pass is nearly turned into something through the willing running of Steven Naismith, who looks to scamper in behind. On this occasion Kyle Walker is able to come across and clear the ball on the cover from right-back.
(4’) Kane is released down the right wing and looks to fizz a cross into the danger area but Bassong is able to divert the ball behind for another Tottenham corner. The visitors don't manage to make anything of this set-piece. Norwich just need to hang in there at the moment.
--- 2’ Goal! 1-0 to Spurs! What a blistering start from the visitors. Norwich have hardly touched the ball and they are already behind. Eriksen's corner is punched away by Rudd but only as far as Alderweireld who slices his volley back into the path of Eriksen who volleys at goal - Rudd makes a decent save but it drops perfectly for Alli who can't miss! ---
(1’) Tottenham immediately get into their passing rhythm with Rose, Son and Eriksen exchanging passes down the left. Rose eventually forces a corner which Eriksen will take.
(1’) And we are underway! The away side kick-off. Norwich and Spurs lineup in their traditional colours, yellow and green for the Canaries while the lilywhites are in their famous white and navy strip.
The teams have just emerged from the tunnel and kick off is just a few minutes away. It is a very chilly night here in East Anglia but there is a tremendous atmosphere building inside the stadium.
As for Spurs, well they are absolutely flying at the moment and will be looking for all three points this evening to keep their title and top four ambitions alive. They have not lost away from home in the Premier League since the opening day of the season against Manchester United at Old Trafford in August and they will look at Norwich's recent defensive troubles as a source of encouragement. Tottenham recorded a comfortable 3-0 victory the last time these teams met at White Hart Lane on Boxing Day, Pochettino will be hoping for more of the same.
Norwich have had plenty of time to prepare for this match after their dramatic 4-5 defeat at home against Liverpool, their early FA Cup exit has meant that Alex Neil's side have had ten days to pick themselves up. They have been busy in the transfer market with highly rated teenager James Maddison arriving from Coventry City on deadline day yesterday. The Carrow Road faithful will be hoping some of the new recruits can reinvigorate the team as they battle for Premier League survival.
TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR SUBS: Vorm, Bentaleb, Lamela, Trippier, Chadli, Carroll and Davies.
NORWICH CITY SUBS: Ruddy, Martin, Jerome, Hoolahan, Redmond, Bennett and Odjidja-Ofoe.
TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR XI (4-2-3-1): Lloris (c); Walker, Alderweireld, Wimmer, Rose; Dier, Dembele; Son, Alli, Eriksen; Kane.
NORWICH CITY XI (4-2-3-1): Rudd; Pinto, Klose, Bassong, Olsson; Tettey (c), Mulumbu; Naismith, Howson, Jarvis; Mbokani.
As for Spurs, Mauricio Pochettino reverts to his usual Premier League starting lineup with Kyle Walker, Danny Rose, Dele Alli and Mousa Dembele coming back in after being rested for the FA Cup tie against Colchester United at the weekend.
The team news is in and for Norwich Timm Klose makes his debut at centre-back. There is no place however in the matchday squad for Chelsea loanee Patrick Bamford. Andre Wisdom, who was ineligible for the Canaries last match against his parent club Liverpool is not recalled to the team and Ivo Pinto will continue at right back.
Good evening and welcome along to this live text commentary for the Premier League clash between Norwich City and Tottenham Hotspur here at Carrow Road.

FULL TIME! Man City scramble their way to a narrow 1-0 victory over Sunderland, despite the hosts having a lot of opportunities to get back on level terms. However, it ends with Aguero's solitary goal being the only difference between the two sides, as Pellegrini's men edge towards another potentially vital three points in the Premier League title race. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time!
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card Sagna gets a late yellow, as Man City look to edge their way to a narrow win here tonight. ---
(90’) Silva tries to break down the left-hand side, but the Spaniard doesn't have the legs to do anything other than slide Kolarov in towards the byline. The Serbia international cuts back a pass, but Aguero is caught offside.
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card Yellow card Fernando Luiz Rosa ---
(90’) Allardyce is pacing around his technical area, with the experienced coach desperately trying to frogmarch the Black Cats back into this game. Sunderland are continuing to press on, but yet another corner opportunity is squandered! A goal-line clearance is needed to spare Hart's blushes on this occasion!
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card Aguero picks up a yellow card for a late challenge on M'Vila, but Sunderland are only interested in keeping play moving. ---
(90’) We're into the first of five minutes of stoppage time!
(90’) Sagna makes a towering headed clearance to deny Defoe, with Man City hanging on here! M'Vila is presented with an opportunity on the edge of the penalty box, but the Frenchman can only blaze wildly over from just inside the area! Sunderland can't afford to keep wasting these chances!
(88’) Sunderland win themselves a corner, but Fernando puts his head on the line brilliantly to stop the delivery creeping inside Hart's near post! The second set piece in quick succession causes similar havoc, but N'Doye can't get the ball under his spell! Man City just get rid!
(86’) We're into the final five minutes, with Man City sat rather deep to invite pressure on. The visiting back four are sat on the edge of their box, with Sterling and Clichy prepared to sit in too. Defoe tries to turn on the periphery of the area, but the ex-England international is denied the chance to turn.
(84’) With plenty of changes having been made, the outcome of this match is now left to those currently on the field. Allardyce is urging his players forward, with the Black Cats still in with half a chance due to the narrow difference in scoreline. All it takes is one mistake from the Citizens.
--- 82’ Substitution N'Doye comes into the fray for the final 10 minutes, with Borini trudging off following a fairly anonymous offensive contribution. ---
(82’) Sunderland win a free kick around 30 yards from goal, with Khazri stood over the dead ball once again. The substitute flights in a delivery, but Hart is quick off his line to claim ahead of anyone else. Another wasted set piece for the hosts.
--- 80’ Yellow card Otamendi picks up a caution, with the Argentina international now having to toe a dangerous line during the dying embers of this contest. ---
--- 79’ Substitution We're into the final 10 minutes at the Stadium of Light, with Pellegrini perhaps looking to shut up shop. Kolarov comes into the game in place of Toure, which should lead to the left-hand side being solidified well. ---
(79’) Chance for Jones! The right-back takes aim from the edge of the box, with the Englishman catching a shot sweetly! Hart does well to get up and palm a shot over the crossbar, before the resulting corner is also half cleared by the England international goalkeeper! A second delivery is lumped into the Man City area, but O'Shea lashes over at the back post!
(77’) There's a sense of urgency to Sunderland's play, with the hosts understanding that every point could prove vital in their battle against the drop. Defoe is released on the break, before facing up his man, but the Englshman's eventual cross is headed away by Demichelis.
--- 76’ Substitution Sterling comes into the game for Navas, with the former Liverpool winger offering fresh legs in wide areas. ---
--- 75’ Substitution Caution may be being thrown to the wind by the Black Cats, with Johnson being introduced into the midfield in place of Cattermole. ---
(74’) With narrowly over a quarter of an hour left to play, Navas requires some extensive treatment. The Spaniard went down off the ball, with Man City's physios mustered into action immediately. There's activity on both benches, with both coaches presumably looking to change this clash.
(72’) Man City win themselves a free-kick on the right-hand side, with Khazri bringing down Fernandinho cynically! The delivery is whipped in, but Kirchhoff heads behind for a corner. Silva takes from the left flank, but the Spain international's cross is cushioned back to Mannone by O'Shea.
(70’) The clock is ticking for Sunderland now, but the Black Cats have arguably had the better of the second half. Man City have been restricted to only a couple of half chances, with neither goalkeepers really being tested. But for picking the ball out of his own net, Mannone hasn't had a great deal to do.
(68’) Silva dances his way into the penalty area, before clipping back a cross from the left byline, but Kone heads away from Aguero! The Ivorian defender goes down as a result, after appearing to cramp up. After some extensive treatment, the Sunderland man should be okay to continue.
(66’) Defoe is asked to chance a long throughball, with the Englishman unable to keep the ball in play at the left byline. In the aftermath, there appears to be some kind of clash between the ex-Spurs man, with Otamendi being caught in the face! The referee didn't see anything untoward occur, however.
(64’) Clichy makes a vital clearing header, as Sunderland continue to threaten to nick an equaliser. Man City build a break from deep, with Silva trying to pick apart the hosts, but a neat move only ends in Toure being felled on the periphery of the penalty area. The Citizens just can't seem to put the Black Cats to the sword.
(62’) Aguero lets fly from the edge of the penalty area, but the visiting goalscorer can only bounce a terrible effort straight into Mannone's body! Man City are just leaving the diminutive Argentine up top, with everyone else sat back in organised fashion. Sunderland try their luck through Cattermole, but the Englishman fires horrendously over!
(60’) Sunderland try to stretch things on the break once again, with Jones managing to win a throw-in high upfield. An attempted delivery is thumped into the box, but Otamendi heads clear! As we head into the final half an hour, it appears that Man City will be able to cling onto a much-needed three points.
--- 59’ Yellow card Jones picks up the first booking of the afternoon, with Man City perhaps now being able to focus their efforts down the left-hand side. ---
(58’) Toure tries to feed Aguero in behind the hosts' back four, but O'Shea steps out to deny the Argentine a goal scoring opportunity. This second half is in danger of becoming fairly cagey, given that neither outfit are looking like scoring. Van Aanholt whips a cross in from the left byline, but Clichy has the peace of mind to cushion a pass back to Hart.
(56’) Silva slots a pass to Clichy on the left-hand side, before Toure is picked out in space on the edge of the box. Man City take the sting out of things with some lengthy possession, as Pellegrini's men are certainly in no rush. Aguero spins on the edge of the box, before feeding in Fernandinho, but M'Vila makes a vital interception.
(54’) Sunderland win themselves a free kick around 40 yards from goal, with Khazri poised to take it. Allardyce orders forward a mass of red and white shirts, but the delivery in from the substitute is below par. The hosts maintain their pressure, but Otamendi steps out in commanding fashion to deny Defoe.
(52’) Silva tries to escape down the left-hand side, with the ball eventually fizzed into Aguero. The Argentine forward tries to skip beyond Van Aanholt, but the Dutchman stands up to his man well. Suddenly, it appears that Man City are prepared to sit back, bide their time and hit the Black Cats with some quick counter-attacks.
(50’) Otamendi concedes a corner on the left-hand side, which is cleared easily at the near post. The Black Cats just can't seem to make any dead-ball situations count. Jones goes on a marauding run down the right flank, but Clichy does just enough to ensure that the ex-Baggies defender creates nothing.
(48’) Van Aanholt offers width down the left-hand side, but the former Vitesse defender is caught straying criminally offside. Sunderland are looking confident at the outset of the second period, with Fernando and Fernandinho sitting rather deep in the hope of protecting the visiting back four.
--- 46’ Substitution Iheanacho takes his leave after a quiet first-half performance, with Fernando coming into the fray. That should mean that Toure is pushed into a more advanced area of the field. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Khazri replaces Lens for the home side, with Allardyce making a sole alteration at the break in the hope of inspiring a comeback. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Stadium of Light! The visitors are ahead for now, but the Black Cats have shown that they are more than capable of netting an equaliser before the close of play.
HALF TIME! Man City go into the break with a 1-0 advantage, courtesy of an opportunistic strike from Aguero! Hart has made a couple of smart stops since, however, with the Black Cats certainly not out of this contest yet. Allardyce will be pleased with the hosts' competitive spirit.
(45’) We're into the first of two minutes of stoppage time.
(45’) GREAT DOUBLE SAVE FROM HART! Huge intervention from the England international! With Defoe swivelling about 12 yards out from goal, the ex-Shrewsbury goalkeeper springs to his left-hand side to deny the former Spurs striker! The rebound skids out at a tight angle, before Cattermole follows up! Hart is back to his feet to push another shot away!
(44’) Over from Toure! Iheanacho does well to pick out his captain on the periphery of the penalty area, before the former Barcelona midfielder uses two examples of quick feet to beat two opponents! With Mannone in his sights, the Ivorian balloons over the crossbar from a narrow angle!
(42’) Borini is released down the left-hand side, with the ex-Roma man cutting back a neat pass to the edge of the box. Kirchhoff slides in to try and turn a first-time shot goalwards, but the German midfielder fluffs his lines entirely! Sunderland keep their pressure on, but an eventual cross from Cattermole bounces directly out of play.
(40’) Defoe manages to try his luck with a snapshot, but the former Tottenham striker fails to find the target. Man City still have their one-goal advantage, but Pellegrini will be keen to double Sunderland's deficit before the break. As it stands, the Black Cats will definitely fancy their chances of getting back into this and stealing a point.
(38’) Demichelis comes back onto the field of play, with the ex-Atletico defender not taking long to leave his mark on Defoe! This duel might not be quite over yet. Sunderland win themselves yet another free-kick, but Man City are able to clear their lines yet again. Allardyce's won't be happy with how his outfit have been wasteful with their set pieces.
(36’) Less than 10 minutes remain in the first half, with Sunderland looking as though they can get back into this one. Demichelis and Defoe clash while making an aerial challenge, with the former coming off rather worse for wear. The visiting players surround the referee and ask for a booking, but the match official keeps his cards in his pocket.
(34’) Demichelis makes a timely clearance, with Man City's back four continuing to answer any questions that are asked of them. Looping crosses have been the hosts only source of generating danger, but Hart remains a relative spectator with narrowly over 10 minutes until the interval. Kone rises well to meet a free-kick delivery, but the ex-Lorient man can only head wide of the far upright!
(32’) Kirchhoff tries his luck from the free-kick that he won himself, but the former Bayern man failing to hit the target from 30 yards. Sunderland are starting to put themselves about a little more in the midfield third, but still chances aren't coming. Borini presses high to harass Clichy, but the former Arsenal left-back holds his nerve to hammer a clearance downfield.
(30’) The opening half an hour has seen Man City take charge, with Sunderland sticking to their opening system of coiling up for counter-attacks. Kirchhoff tries to release Defoe in behind enemy lines, but the Englishman is forced back towards his own net by Demichelis. Moments later, Iheanacho is penalised for a foul on the aforementioned German midfielder.
(28’) Aguero is picked out on the left-hand side of the box, before checking back onto his right foot. The Man City forward unleashes a curling shot, which threatens to creep into the top-right corner, but a slight deflection takes it behind for a corner. Silva takes, but a header from Fernandinho is way off target.
(26’) Defoe takes the ball into his chest, but Otamendi gets tight to the ex-Spurs man to dispossess him. The former England international just can't seem to get a touch of the ball without close attention from the visiting central defenders. Lens tries to break to the right byline, but an attempted cross from the Dutchman is skewed behind for a goal kick.
(24’) Toure opens play out to the right-hand side, with the Ivory Coast international then lunging into a poor tackle on M'Vila. Allardyce has a few substitutes warming up already, with the Black Cats clearly not inspiring their coach with the way they've set up shop thus far.
(22’) Aguero manages to bring down a neat lofted pass, with Silva coming up in close support. Man City patiently probe for gaps from right to left, with the aforementioned Spaniard only able to flick a stray ball out of play for a goal kick. Pellegrini's outfit are on top, but the Chilean coach is prowling his technical area menacingly.
(20’) Navas is the subject of a long ball over the top from Toure, but the pass skids off the turf and straight behind for a goal-kick. Aguero is still not moving too well, with the Argentine forward gingerly scampering around. Sunderland aren't managing to escape from their own half on a regular basis, with Defoe not getting any service at all.
(18’) Aguero is back on the field of play for the visitors, but the ex-Atletico man will take a while to move freely. Sunderland win themselves a corner on the right, but a swinging delivery evades Kone on its way behind for a goal kick. Man City have their lead, which should only force the Black Cats to push forward and leave more gaps at the back.
--- 16’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! AGUERO MAKES IT 1-0! Navas drills in a cross from the right, which fizzes through a ruck of bodies and into the path of the Argentina international. With O'Shea at his heels, the Man City striker stabs a powerful finish into the top-right corner! He goes down with a knock in the aftermath, but should be okay to continue. ---
(15’) Demichelis gives away a free kick, which allows for Sunderland to push some red and white shirts into the penalty area, but a delivery from Kirchhoff is very poor indeed. Man City take the chance to break, with Sagna making tracks down the right-hand side, but O'Shea lashes away the Frenchman's eventual cross!
(13’) Silva slots a neat ball down the right channel for Aguero to chase, but the former Atletico striker can't quite bring it under his spell! That's the closest that the away outfit have come thus far, with the former Valencia playmaker struggling to find pockets of space against a congested opposition unit.
(11’) Clichy tries to whip a cross in from the left-hand side, but Van Aanholt flicks a timely defensive header away from the danger area! Quick breaks are the only form of respite for the hosts at the moment, with Man City enjoying the lion's share of possession.
(9’) Important interception from Demichelis! The Argentine centre-back cuts out a ball from Kone on the right flank, as Sunderland look to cause problems on the counter. Allardyce's men finally show some signs of offensive life, with their new defender already deeply embroiled in Premier League action.
(7’) Lens dances infield from the right-hand side, but the Netherlands international is forced into a non threatening area of the field. Van Aanholt is picked out on the far side, but the ex-Chelsea left-back can only win his team a corner. The aforementioned Dutchman takes, but Hart is quick off his line to punch well clear.
(5’) Close for the away outfit! Mannone is forced into action at the near post, following a neat cross from the left-hand side by Clichy! Kone can only divert the ball towards the closest upright, but the former Arsenal goalkeeper makes a simple stop. The visitors are on the front foot immediately.
(3’) Kone gives away an early corner, with the same Sunderland defender rising well at the second time of asking to frustrate the away outfit. Pellegrini's men are immediately on the offensive, with Defoe looking incredibly isolated at the head of the Black Cats' attack.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Stadium of Light! Both of these clubs are playing for different aims, with the hosts looking to take a step towards Premier League safety, while Man City try to hang onto high flying Leicester.
Man City substitutes: Zabaleta, Fernando, Sterling, Kolarov, Caballero, Celina, Barker.
Man City starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Hart; Sagna, Otamendi, Demichelis, Clichy; Toure, Fernandinho; Navas, Iheanacho, Silva; Aguero.
Sunderland substitutes: Brown, N'Doye, Johnson, Pickford, Khazri, Yedlin, Watmore.

TEAM NEWS: Kelechi Iheanacho features up top alongside Sergio Aguero, with the Nigerian youngster impressing with some recent goals. Jesus Navas gets a start on the right-hand side, with Yaya Toure entrusted with a deeper midfield role. Martin Demichelis continues in defence due to Vincent Kompany's absence, with Gael Clichy filling in at left-back.

Man City are still in with a chance of a big silverware haul, with the first step on their road to potential success coming with three points this evening.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Man City's trip to the Stadium of Light in order to face Sunderland. Well, that's all from me for now. It has been a pleasure to bring you all the action from Upton Park this evening, where West Ham have beaten 10-man Aston Villa 2-0 in the Premier League.
As for Villa, it seems as though Remi Garde will need a miracle to keep them up this term. They started sharply and should have had a penalty, but there is no excuse for Jordan Ayew, who has cost his team dearly tonight and may be lucky to get a ride back to Birmingham on the squad bus! However, they showed little fight after that red card, and in truth were never in the game after the interval.
That victory sees West Ham remain within touching distance of Manchester United, who are currently beating Stoke City 3-0 at Old Trafford. Slaven Bilic’s side were poor in the first half, but came out strong after the interval and easily dispatched their lacklustre visitors.
FULL-TIME! That's it from Upton Park, where it has finished West Ham 2, 10-man Aston Villa 0. The visitors started well, but the game turned on the deserved dismissal of Jordan Ayew, and the hosts duly wrapped up the victory with goals from Michail Antonio and Cheikhou Kouyate sealing the victory.
(90’) A final protest from the travelling Villa support now, as they bare banners and scarfs barring slogans such as ‘sack the board’ and ‘Lerner out’. You have to feel for the fans of the 1982 European Cup winners, who have once agains in their side capitulate to a disappointing defeat in the Premier League. They seem destined for the Championship...
--- 90’ +3 Substitution A thrid and final West Ham substitution, as Cheikhou Kouyaté is replaced by Pedro Obiang. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated there will be a minimum of three minutes of added time at the end of this one. Villa will want this game over as soon as possible...
--- 89’ Substitution Another change in quick-succession now, as Antonio, who opened the scoring with a lovely cushioned header, is replaced by Nikica Jelavic. The former Everton and Hull City striker - who is rumoured to be leaving the club for a move to China - has scored in three of his five Premier League appearances against Villa. ---
--- 86’ Substitution And that assist will be the final contribution of the night from Valencia, who makes way for Chelsea-loanee Victor Moses. ---
--- 85’ Assist It was a stunning counter-attack from West Ham, lead by the pacey Enner Valencia, who played in Kouyate with a perfectly-weighted throughball. ---
--- 85’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAALLLL!!!! KOUYATE MAKES IT 2-0! Well, what a counter-attack that was from West Ham! Veretout put in the cross from the corner but the hosts head it clear and Valencia races forward. The Ecuadorian has a plethora of options to aim for, and chooses to tee-up his Senegalese teammate, who makes no mistake with a lofted, powerful finish high into the roof of the net. Game over! ---
(84’) Finally, a slither of hope for Villa, as Sinclair manages to win a corner down the left flank, and the visitors get their big men up from the back… Veretout will take it...
(83’) Patient, easy play for the hosts, who keep possession ticking over in midfield, teasing their opponents - who seem to have all-but given up hope of salvaging anything from this fixture. It’s a real shame for Villa, who were in no doubt the better team early on, and this result, if indeed it does finish this way, may have been very different had Ayew not seen red for a ridiculous foul on Cresswell.
--- 80’ Substitution A second substitution now for Villa, as Agbonlahor makes way for Scott Sinclair. Garde will need his most experienced player fit for the upcoming games now that Ayew is suspended. ---
(79’) Great defending from Noble, who puts his body on the line to prevent Richardson’s driven effort troubling Adrian, as Villa finally manage to forge a foray forward. And the West Ham captain seems to be limping somewhat following that block.
(78’) CUTE EFFORT! Valencia does well to stay on his feet as he jinks his way in from the left, eventually laying it off to Noble. The midfielder goes for goal with an ambitious strike with the outside of his right foot, but it whistles just over the crossbar. West Ham are still searcing for another goal to put this game to bed...
(76’) WHAT A SAVE! Burn does excellently there to somehow tip Cresswell’s strike round the post. The West Ham left-back did brilliantly to take the ball down on his chest before shifting it to his weaker right foot and going for goal, but the Villa shot-stopper was equal to it, though the officials - as they did in the first half - failed to spot that it should have been a corner to the hosts.
(73’) Valencia looks rather bemused now as Jon Moss waives away his claims for a free-kick on the edge of Villa’s area. It did appear that the Ecuadorian had been held back by the retreating Richards, but there was nothing doing for the referee.
--- 71’ Substitution A first change of the game now, for either side, and it is Garde who blinks first. The substitution sees Carles Gil, who looked bright in the opening stages but has been unable to get on the ball since Villa were reduced to 10 men, replaced by Kieran Richardson. ---
--- 69’ Yellow card A yellow card now for Mark Noble, as the West Ham skipper eventually gets himself into the referee's notebook for a late challenge on Cisshoko. ---
(68’) It’s another dreadful ball into the penalty area from the Dutchman, who has failed to test West Ham’s defence all game long from his set-pieces. Poor.
--- 67’ Yellow card Cynical from Collins, who loses possession deep in Villa’s half before tracking back and scything down Richards, who had done well to power forward from right back. Can the visitors take advantage of this set-piece? Bacuna will deliver it... ---
(65’) Cresswell floats in another brilliant cross from the left, which Antonio is beaten to by Okore, at the expense of a corner. Payet delivers to the head of Reid, whose knock-down Kouate attempts to turn goalwards with an acrobatic effort, but the Senegalese midfielder cannot connect and the ball trickles out of play for a goal-kick.
(63’) CLOSE! Villa’s heads are down now, and West Ham are sensing that. The hosts flood forward at pace, with Valencia teeing up Song who, 20 yards from goal, drills his toe-poked effort just wide of the right-hand upright.
(61’) WHAT A BALL! Again, Noble plays in Antonio with an immense pass - this time off the outside of his boot. The winger takes a touch on the edge of the area before attempting to square a cross to Valencia, but Okore is well-placed to hook it away from danger for the time being.
--- 58’ Assist It was a quite sublime pass from Mark Noble, who floated a precise lofted delivery into the path of Antonio, who duly did the rest with a magnificent finish. ---
--- 58’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAALLLLLLLL!!! WEST HAM TAKE THE LEAD! Villa’s resolve is finally broken as Noble picks out Antonio with an inch-perfect pass, and the winger makes no mistake with a great header that finds the bottom-left corner. 1-0 to the hosts! ---
(56’) Burn looks hurt following that Payet free-kick, as it appears the Villa goalkeeper had clattered into the post that the aforementioned West Ham playmaker struck. However, after a moment of stretching-off, the goalkeeper seems to have recovered.
(54’) POST! SO CLOSE! Payet curls a fantastic whipped effort towards goal that has Bunn beaten, but the strike rattles against the woodwork. That’s unlucky!
(53’) Payet is starting to get on the ball now and pick up little pockets of space in central areas. He drifts in-field from the left, taking on both Veretout and Gueye before being brought down by the latter. The France midfielder will take the free-kick...
(51’) WHAT AN EFFORT! Sublime work from West Ham at the resulting corner sees Payet float a cross to the cusp of the Villa area. Noble meets it on the volley and drills a venomous right-footed strike on target, but Bunn gets down sharply to his left to make a quite brilliant save and parry it away from danger. Great play all round!
(50’) SUPERB DEFENDING! What a block from Richards, as the Villa skipper somehow manages to clear the ball off the goal-line with a fantastic bicycle kick to prevent Collin’s header putting the hosts ahead.
--- 49’ Yellow card A first booking of the game now for West Ham, as Song picks up a yellow card for a professional foul on Agbonlahor. There really was not  much difference between that challenge and the one from Noble in the first half. ---
(48’) MISS! Well what a chance that was for the hosts as Antonio latched onto Cresswell’s cross to the back post. The bulky winger goes for goal on the volley, but he skews his effort off target after his teammate Collins had got in his line of vision.
(46’) SECOND-HALF! West Ham, attacking from left to right, get proceedings back under way at Upton Park.
Garde is looking a forlorn figure on the touchline, and it is no real surprise. Villa are still well in this contest, but the odds are heavily stacked in West Ham’s favour…
Since then, it has been a backs-to-the-wall job for Remi Garde's side, but they have done themselves proud so far. West Ham have been lethargic in possession and have struggled to break down Villa's two banks of four, though they did manage to carve out a gilt-edged opportunity that saw Enner Valencia somehow manage to head over from close range after latching onto James Tomkins' cross-cum-shot.
HALF-TIME! Well, that's it for the opening 45 minutes here at Upton Park, where it remains 0-0 between West Ham and Aston Villa. The visitors started well, and in truth should have been awarded a penalty early on following a handball by Michail Antonio. But the game was turned on its head when Jordan Ayew's reckless and un-provoked elbow into the face of Aaron Cresswell saw the visitors' top-scorer receive his marching orders in the 17th minute.
(45’) Appeals for another red card from the referee now, this time from the Villa contingent following a clumsy foul on Agbonlahor by Kouyate, but Jon Moss is having none of it, and rightly so. Bacuna curls in a cross from teh free-kick, but Reid heads it away from danger.
(45’) CLOSE! That’s a great effort from Valencia, who goes for goal from the set-piece with a dipping strike that whistles just wide, though replays show that the hosts should have had a corner, with Bunn having got a hand to it to tip it round the post.
(44’) It’s a free-kick now to West Ham in a central area, around 35 yards out from goal. Valencia and Payet stand over it...
(42’) A bit of wizardry out on the wing there from Tomkins, of all people! The centre back - shoehorned into the team at right back in the absence of injured duo Byram and Jenkinson - jinks his way past Gil with a fantastic bit of skill before drilling in a cross to Antonio, but he is unable to make any real purchase with his header and Villa escape unscathed once more.
(39’) Lucky escape for Noble, there, as the West Ham skipper avoids a booking for a late lunge on Veretout. The midfielder got fortunate earlier in proceedings as well, following a cynical foul on Richards.
(37’) High and wide! Tomkins again latches onto a rebound before striking at goal on the half-volley, but he skies his effort well over the crossbar. West Ham really need to show some improvement here at Upton Park if they are to unlock Villa's stubborn defence!
(35’) Well, despite all of their possession, West Ham have not been zipping the ball around with any pace or tempo so far in this first half, and have not looked to get Payet on the ball anywhere near as much as what you would expect - especially given they are against 10 men! Collins tries his luck with an audacious strike from range, but the defender’s effort is way off target. Bilic is far from happy on the touchline.
(33’) CHANCE! Antonio should have done better there! Gueye manages to win possession on the edge of Villa’s area, but Song gets in a tackle to intercept the visitors’ counter-attack. The former Barcelona man shows his quality with a neat Cruyff-turn that rolls the ball into the path of the aforementioned winger, but the former Nottingham Forest man drags his effort wide.
(31’) WHAT A MISS! How did that not go in!? Cresswell loops in a cross that Bunn flaps at. The rebound falls to the feet of Tomkins, who hammers a first-time strike towards goal. Valencia meets it two yards out from the line, but the Ecuador forward cannot direct his header into the back of the net.
(29’) STAT FLASH: As expected following Ayew’s dismissal, West Ham have seen over 80 per cent of possession in the last five minutes. However, they are yet to create a clear-cut opportunity, and though Payet delivers a dangerous cross from a corner on the left flank, Antonio is unable to connect with his attempted header.
(26’) Based on that one moment of madness from Ayew, this match is now simply a matter of attack and defence for the time being. Villa are sitting deep, camped on the edge of their own area, but at the same time affording no space for Valencia - whose four goals in his last three Premier League games has matched his return for the last 39 outings - to make a run in behind.
(24’) GOOD EFFORT! Easy possession for West Ham sees the play switched out to Payet. The mercurial playmaker ups the tempo by pinging a sharp pass into the path of Noble, who reverses a neat ball to Kouyate. The former Anderlecht man takes the shot on the spin, but his curling strike sails into the arms of Bunn. Better from the hosts!
(22’) Well, Villa’s game-plan that seemed to be working so well in the opening 15 minutes, has gone out of the window now. They have shifted to two solid banks of four, with just Agbonlahor staying in an advanced position. However, despite being a man up, West Ham are still looking lethargic.
(19’) That really is devastating for Villa, and it was the most of ridiculous decisions from Ayew. You have to feel for Remi Garde, whose job has been made even harder now, though many wouldn’t have thought that possible prior to kick-off! Can West Ham, who have been poor so far, make the most of their numerical advantage?
--- 17’ Red card! STRAIGHT RED CARD! Ayew gets sent off! What a terrible decision from Villa’s top-scorer, who receives his marching orders for a ridiculous and un-provoked elbow on Cresswell that leaves Jon Moss with no other option. That really is a ludicrous reaction from the striker, who has put his side - who have so far dominated proceedings - in deep trouble with over 70 minutes remaining! ---
(15’) The free-kick is deflected wide for a corner, but Bacuna’s resulting delivery is a poor one which is headed away by Valencia, but it only results in a corner on the near side. Gil whips in the cross, which almost falls to Richards, but former Villa defender Collins is on hand to clear the danger.
(13’) STAT FLASH: Villa have had 62 per cent of the possession so far, and are beginning to edge ever closer to creating real goal-scoring opportunity, though they have every right to feel aggrieved that they were not awarded a penalty. Gil does well to link his way down the left once more, winning a free-kick after being brought down by Tomkins.
(10’) That should have been a penalty! The visitors are finding some joy down the left and Agbonlahor manages to pick up some pace before attempting to get a cross in to Ayew, but the effort is blocked by the arm of Antonio, which was blatantly in an unnatural position behind his body, but the claims for a spot-kick are waived away by the referee Jon Moss.
(9’) Villa work another patient move down the left flank, which results in Cissokho drilling a low cross into the box. West Ham scramble it clear, but only as far as Gil, who had peeled inside, but his shot does not trouble Adrian.
(7’) Despite the host’s quick start to proceedings, Villa have stamped a semblance of authority of proceedings in recent minutes - knocking the ball about patiently and stifling the normally raucous home crowd. Lescott eventually tries to thread a precise pass into the feet of Ayew, but the Ghanaian’s touch is a poor one and Kouyate intercepts.
(5’) GOOD DEFENDING! That was a fantastic corner from the left flank which evades the grasp of Adrien. Ayew looks set to tap it into an empty net from a yard out, but the former Lorient striker had been tracked terrifically by Reid, who skews a clearance over the crossbar.
(4’) The Hammers have not lost at home in 10 games, and as expected they have made a strong start here. However, Villa finally manage to venture forward, with Ayew doing well to win a corner on the left. Can the visitors make anything of this...
(2’) CLOSE! Almost an opener for West Ham, and it is Payet - so often their talisman - who creates the chance with a brilliant run down the left, taking on Richards before flashing a cross into the six-yard box, but Okore's block deflects it just wide of the upright.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are up and running here at Upton Park, with the visitors, donning their vibrant yellow away strip, getting proceedings under way.
It’s another full house at Upton Park, and the crowd is as loud as ever as the teams make their way out onto the pitch. We should be set for another fascinating Premier League encounter here in east London, between two sides who have definitely headed in opposite directions in recent seasons...

Sam Byram - who made his debut in West Ham’s last home game - is absent with a knock, while Emmanuel Emenike, who joined on loan from Fenerbahce on Sunday, is also missing.

Team news is in from Upton Park, and there are several changes, as expected, for both sides from the line-ups that faced Liverpool and Manchester City respectively in the FA Cup. For the hosts, Victor Moses, Angelo Ogbonna, Pedro Obiang and Darren Randolph make way, with Michail Antonio, James Collins, Mark Noble and Adrian - who celebrated the birth of his son, Enzo, at the weekend - coming in to the fold. Grade, meanwhile, makes five changes, with Jores Okore, Joleon Lesscott, Mark Bunn and Gabriel Agbonlahor all restored to the starting XI.
Despite spending in the January window seeing Premier League sides break a combined figure of £1billion spent on transfers this campaign, there was no business at Villa Park last month - in spite of Remi Garde’s men desperately needing reinforcements in order to try and maintain their Premier League status. They were hammered 4-0 by Manchester City in the FA Cup last time out, having recorded just one win in the top-flight since the first day of the season. However, they are on a three-game unbeaten run, and the reverse fixture on Boxing Day did see Villa manage their highest total of shots on target (eight) this season.
West Ham have been flying this season under Bilic, and have lost just one of their last 10 Premier League fixtures. They drew 2-2 with Manchester City last time out, with Enner Valencia following up his brace at Bournemouth with a double against Manuel Pellegrini’s men. However, if the form guide is anything to go by, then there is unlikely to be many goals tonight - with just five goals having been scored over the previous five league meetings between the two sides.

(76’) Depay is emerging from the touchline now with suggestions that Fellaini is the man who is coming off as he glances towards the dug-out.
(74’) The ball drops back out towards the edge of the box, into the feet of Rooney. He looks to add to his goals tally today but a wild effort is hit high and wide over the bar.
(73’) A sweeping cross from Carrick is played right across goal and could cause danger. Yet United are not there to gamble at the back-post. Muniesa is instead at the scene to read the play and does well to ensure he doesn't inadvertently guide the ball into his own net.
(71’) A chance again for Stoke as they pose a threat to the United defence. This time it is Pieters, on the left, who swings in an early cross towards Crouch. He gets to the ball ahead of his marker and dinks the ball over De Gea, but misses wide of the goal. Play is pulled back for offside against the former Liverpool man, regardless.
(69’) Crouch just...isn't quite tall enough! An odd statement to say, for sure, as the former England man attempts to stretch to reach a cross-cum-shot from Bardsley after the ball drops to the edge of the box from the corner. He just can't quite reach it.
(68’) Decent play from Ireland and Arnautovic at the other end as they combine with a quick one-two in the penalty box, before the latter attempts to swing in a cross from the byline. His effort is blocked and Stoke win the corner.
(66’) United are content with keeping the ball at the minute with Stoke unable to win the ball back. The tempo has dropped off a little bit in these past 10 minutes since the goal.
(64’) Not a happy return to Old Trafford for former Red, Mark Hughes, at the moment. He celebrates his 100th Premier League game in charge of Stoke tonight but is on the brink of his ninth defeat as manager at this ground. Certainly fonder memories as a player then, Mark.
(62’) An inviting cross from Rooney is whipped in towards the left, yet Johnson nips in ahead of a crowd of shirts to clear at the front-post. A fourth goal would really add insult to injury here.
--- 60’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A second change of the game for Stoke now and here is Ireland, having completed his warm-up. He takes the place of Bojan. ---
--- 60’ Yellow card YELLOW! Martial picks up a caution for a foul on Bardsley. ---
(58’) Looks like a change is in the offing for Hughes now with former Manchester City player Stephen Ireland warming up on the touchlines. They certainly need something here.
(56’) Bardsley loses possession of the ball far too easily as United are allowed to counter down the left. Martial is once again the man who is flying down the flank. He has Rooney in the box to aim for but attempts a left-footed shot himself, but cannot stop it from rising over the bar.
--- 55’ Yellow card YELLOW! Darmian becomes the first player to pick up a caution after brushing across Arnautovic to give away a foul in a decent cross position to the left of the area. ---
--- 53’ Assist A goal - and now an assist - for Martial who has really put in quite the performance for his side here today. It is no surprise to see the Frenchman, Mata and Rooney combine for this third goal. The trio have been exceptional in their link-up play in the final third. ---
--- 53’ Goal! GOAAAAL! A third goal and, surely, the three points! Stoke are all over the place as a ball from the back is hit through them towards Mata. He plays it wide to Martial who picks out Rooney with a low cross for a tap-in at the back-post. They've made that look so easy. ---
(50’) A strong challenge from Bardsley on Carrick gives Stoke momentum as they launch a counter attack. Bojan leads it, showing great quick feet to skip past his marker, but as play builds down the right, the eventual cross falls short and is cleared.
(48’) That's wild from Arnautovic as he picks up the ball on the edge of the box, cutting in onto his right foot, only to blaze an effort high and wide over the bar. Still nothing to test De Gea in goal, with his now Stoke's sixth effort off target.
(46’) SECOND HALF! We're back underway for the final 45 minutes of play.
A rather comfortable first half then for the hosts in a display that looks like the United of old. They began the half on the front foot with Martial and Mata causing issues on the left for the Potters defence. A goal from the young France star - and Lingard - have given Van Gaal's side a deserved lead. Not a lot to shout about for Stoke at the moment.
(45’) HALF TIME! And there is the whistle to mark the interval as United are applauded off the pitch, holding a two-goal lead over their Midlands rivals.
(45’) A minute of added time has been given to end this half.
(44’) That is a waste from Stoke as Arnautovic wins a free-kick against Borthwick-Jackson just past the half-way line, only for Pieters' delivery to be swallowed up by De Gea with ease. No threat at all there from that set-play.
(43’) Great play from Mata once more, this time in the defensive half for his side, cutting out a cross-field pass on the half-way line to launch a counter attack. Play builds on the right before it is sent back towards the former Chelsea man on the edge of the area, but his shot is blocked.
(41’) Lovely link-up play on the left between Mata and Martial, who have been terrific for their side today. But as the ball is played in towards the Frenchman near the corner flag, play is pulled back for offside. A relieft for Stoke, who haven't been able to cope with them so far.
(39’) COULD BE THREE! It should perhaps be a third goal for the Red Devils there as Mata misses not one, but two chances to extend his side's lead. The first comes from the left as a ball from Martial finds him free inside the area, only for his effort to be blocked. Yet the ball drops back out, eventually finding Darmian, who swings in a cross for the Spaniard once more but his header drops wide of the goal. Not the man you'd want for that second chance!
(37’) Martial is in acres of space once more on this left-hand side as Mata plays him in on the edge of the box. He looks to take on Bardsley but the former United defender blocks his shot.
(36’) Weak play from Arnautovic as Afellay carries the ball forward to the half-way line before knocking a pass into the feet of his team-mate, but the winger is too weak as he tries to hold up the play and is easily dispossessed, allowing United to break.
(34’) CLOSE! Stoke just starting to edge back into this game now as they cause United problems with crosses into the box once more. It's like ping-pong in the penalty area for Van Gaal's side as they fail to clear with a header, numerous times, allowing Walters to storm in and lash a shot over the bar from close range.
(32’) NEARLY AN INSTANT IMPACT! Could have been an immediate impression from Bardsley there who overlaps from the right and drives in a low cross towards Walters inside the box. He in turn holds up play well, before teeing up Afellay on the edge only to blast an effort high over the bar.
--- 30’ Substitution SUBSTUTUTION! An early change here as Wollscheid is replaced by Bardsley - looks like that's a tactical change as there has been no noticeable injury for the defender here. ---
(28’) Muniesa is nearly caught out at the back for Stoke there as a ball is played towards his own goal, but he manages to just tidy up before Rooney has the momentum to chase him down with just the keeper to beat.
(27’) A real positive change in atmosphere at Old Trafford now, which will please Van Gaal. He said on Tuesday: "I'm not a stupid man. I'm an intelligent man and I cannot predict the atmosphere on Tuesday. I hope that we can give the same level of performance as against Derby." They've certainly done that so far and have been in full control.
(25’) PENALTY!? You've seen them given in the Premier League before, but nothing there for United. And, to be fair, there is no appeal either as a free-kick is hit long towards Fellaini. Crouch challenges with him and appears to lead with his arm, allowing Stoke to clear.
--- 23’ Assist Lovely play from Rooney and Mata to combine in the build-up to this second goal, making space on the edge of the box with some short passes, before the England international spots an unmarked Martial on the left. He has plenty of time to pick his spot, but that is still a super finish from the former Monaco man. ---
--- 23’ Goal! GOAAAAAL! A sublime goal! A stunning counter-attack from United is led by Rooney, who links up well with Mata on the right-hand side, before swinging in a cross towards Martial on the left. He looks up and curls in an effort into the top right-hand corner! Brilliant goal! ---
(21’) A poor delivery from the free-kick is cleared with ease there by Fellaini as United begin to launch a counter-attack of their own at the other end. Yet Arnautovic cuts across Lingard unfairly, leading in with his arm, to give away a foul in his own half.
(19’) Bojan does well for his side just past the half-way line to skips past Carrick with quick feet and draw Blind into a cheap foul to relieve his side of some pressure. They have the chance to swing a cross in from deep here.
(17’) Chances for Stoke at the other end and it is Crouch again who is the danger man, picking up on a loose ball inside the area after a corner, yet his effort central to the goal is blocked by a wall of red shirts.
(15’) NEARLY TWO! Brilliant play from Martial! The youngster skips past the Potters defence with ease, gliding past Johnson inside the penalty area as he drives through on goal. He looks to have beaten the entire defence but then drags his shot into the side-netting!
--- 14’ Assist That is a brilliant assist from Borthwick-Jackson, celebrating his 19th birthday today, as he hits a superb sweeping cross across the box. It causes all sorts of danger, allowing an un-marked Lingard a tap-in. ---
--- 14’ Goal! GOAAAAAL! Lingard gives United the lead! A terrific ball in from the left cuts across the goal with the young academy graduate lurking at the back-post. He pounces to cushion the ball into an empty net with Butland caught out at his near post. A great start for Van Gaal's side! ---
(12’) Stoke press in the final third and win a corner on the left-hand side, which Affelay steps up to take. The former Barcelona man curls in a delivery towards Crouch once more but his is punished for a foul against Smalling inside the area.
(11’) Whelen hits the free-kick towards Crouch on the edge of the box, with the big striker clearly a target man in this game - in this his first league start since March 2015. Smalling rises to challenge him, before the ball drops to Fellaini, who only half clears his lines.
(10’) Unlucky from Martial, who concedes a free-kick just past the half-way line in his own half against Johnson, despite the former Liverpool man catching his foot on the United winger.
(9’) That's strong defending from Stoke City who invite United to press them as Smalling carries the ball forward from the back, before they close down in numbers, first on the England defender, then on Carrick as the ball is played along, before Wollscheid nips in to break up the play.
(7’) Comfortable for Butland! Neat work from United around the edge of the area sees Rooney combine with some short passing play, before working an angle to shoot on the edge of the box. He curls an effort on goal with his left foot, from just outside the box, but the Potters keeper saves easily to his right.
(5’) Martial again making things happen for his side as he floats in a cross from the left, with Fellaini the target in the middle. The big Belgian has bodies to jostles for the ball with and still manages to get his head on the ball, but his effort is blocked and cleared.
(4’) Some smart play from Martial in the opening stages has allowed for some half-chances in the Stoke area. The France international drifts inside from the left and plays a pass towards Mata on the edge of the box, yet his effort is blocked off Wollscheid for a corner.
(2’) Plenty of possession early on for Van Gaal’s side, as expected, with the Potters yet to see the ball. A couple of deliveries into the box have been dealt with by the visitors so far as crosses from the left and a dinked ball from deep by Mata are cleared away from danger.
(1’) KICK OFF! Manchester United get the game underway, shooting from left to right.
We have both sets of players out on the pitch now with handshakes and formalities completed. United are 10 points behind league-leaders Leicester City on 47 and will hope to bounce back from defeat to Southampton with a win. Sitting in ninth, Stoke can move to within a point of their fifth-placed rivals today with victory.
Mark Hughes, on the other hand, makes eight changes from the side that lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace in the FA Cup over the weekend with only Phillipp Wollscheid, Erik Pieters and Bojan Krkic keeping their places in the starting line-up. Marc Muniesa is fit enough to return from injury while top goalscorer Marko Arnautovic returns in attack. Xherdan Shaqiri is on the bench.
Van Gaal makes two alterations from the side that beat Derby 3-1 in the FA Cup fourth round on Friday. Young right-back Guillermo Varela may count himself unlucky to drop to the bench having impressed against the Rams but he sees his place taken by the returning Matteo Darmian. Morgan Schneiderlin is the other change with Michael Carrick fully recovering from a knee injury.
Substitutes: Bardsley, Ireland, Odemwingie, Joselu, Diouf, Shaqiri, Haugaard.
Stoke City XI (4-3-2-1): Butland; Johnson, Wollscheid, Muniesa, Pieters; Whelan, Afellay; Walters, Bojan, Arnautovic; Crouch.
Substitutes: Depay, Romero, Ander Herrera, Schneiderlin, Varela, McNair, Andreas Pereira.
Manchester United  XI (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Darmian, Smalling, Blind, Borthwick-Jackson; Carrick, Fellaini; Lingard, Mata, Martial; Rooney.
Louis van Gaal's men were booed off last time out in the Premier League as they suffered defeat at home to Southampton – and a similar result tonight would only increase speculation over his job security. His side host the Potters tonight looking to avenge a Boxing Day defeat after goals from Bojan Krkic and Marko Arnautovic wrapped up a 2-0 victory at the Britannia Stadium.
