Salomon Rondon was the hero for West Brom as he popped up in the second minute of stoppage time to earn a point for the hosts, who remain three points ahead of the Swans in the table.
FULL TIME: WEST BROMWICH ALBION 1-1 SWANSEA CITY
(90’) The referee blows the final whistle and West Brom have snatched a late point!
--- 90’ +2 Goal! WEST BROM EQUALISE!!! A scramble unfolds from the resulting corner and Fletcher's shot is blocked on the line, but there is no denying Rondon as he slams in the rebound from inside the six-yard box. ---
(90’) WHAT A BLOCK! Anichebe finds Dawson in the area. He is one-on-one with the keeper but, from nowhere, Naughton throws himself in the way to make a terrific interception.
(90’) We are into the first of four additional minutes at the end of this game. Can West Brom find the equaliser?
(90’) WASTED! West Brom build a patient attack but Berahino wastes it, as he shoots with his left foot from 30 yards and sends the ball into the stands.
(88’) OFF THE POST! Some neat play from the Swans releases Naughton down the left. His cross is met by Paloschi after some great movement in the box, but the base of the upright denies him a debut goal.
(87’) Sigurdsson is always looking to make something happen for the Swans. He creates a shooting opportunity out of nothing, but drags his shot well wide of the target.
(86’) It would be three wins in a row if the Swans can hold on and the first time they will have done so since last May.
(84’) West Brom have just over five minutes to find an equaliser in this game. Their general play has been good, but they need to start asking more questions of Fabianski now.
--- 82’ Substitution Swansea make their final change and it is a very conservative one, as Jordi Amat comes on in place of Ayew. ---
(80’) GOOD SAVE! Fabianski shows good alertness again to deny Berahino's goal-bound header. It would not have counted anyway, as the offside flag had been raised.
(79’) Berahino looks for Anichebe with a through ball. It almost breaks kindly for the latter after Swansea clear straight against him but, fortunately for the Swans, it runs through to Fabianski.
(77’) CRACKING SAVE! Rondon helps a high ball forward on for Anichebe. He unleashes a vicious shot from a tight angle and Fabianski shows great reflexes to push it over the bar.
(75’) Swansea continue to push in search of a second goal. They are not willing to rest on their laurels and will look to give themselves some breathing space in this game.
(73’) Paloschi shows just how effective he could be for the Swans, as he shows great strength to hold the ball up and bring his teammates into play. From that, Ayew embarks on a strong run forward but his shot is blocked.
(71’) Fabianski collects a cross from the left and a quick kick out of his hands sets up a counter attack for the Swans. The ball eventually comes to Cork, but his shot is deflected wide and behind for a corner.
--- 69’ Substitution West Brom make their final change as Anichebe is introduced into the action with Sandro making way. ---
(68’) What can West Brom do in response? They do still have Victor Anichebe on the bench should they wish to use him in search of the equaliser.
(66’) Is the Swansea resurgence about to continue? That was a very well-taken goal by Sigurdsson and, judging by the lack of clear-cut chances, it may even be enough for the three points.
--- 64’ Goal! SWANSEA LEAD!!! Sigurdsson breaks the deadlock for Swansea! West Brom just about scramble the ball away but their relief is short-lived, as Britton drives forward before finding Paloschi. The striker is stood up but the ball breaks kindly for Sigurdsson, who guides it beautifully beyond Foster and inside the far post. ---
--- 62’ Substitution West Brom introduce Berahino into the action in place of Sessegnon, who is disappointed to be going off. ---
(61’) CHANCE! At the other end, some crisp link-up play sees Sigurdsson get in behind the defence but he catches his shot all wrong and sends it high and wide of the target.
(60’) Sessegnon receives the ball on the edge of the area and gets his shot away, but there is no power behind it and Fabianski easily gathers.
--- 59’ Substitution A right-back replaces a left-back for Swansea, as Taylor makes way to be replaced by Kyle Naughton. ---
(58’) There is acitivity on both benches and supporters will be hopeful that they can spark the game back into life.
(56’) FLETCHER WASTES ANOTHER CHANCE! McClean whips in a wonderful delivery from the left and the West Brom skipper does well to lose his marker, but cannot keep his header down and sends it over the crossbar.
(55’) There is more activity on the West Brom bench with Berahino getting stripped off ready to come on. He will want to make an impact following the speculation linking him with a move away from the Hawthorns throughout the window.
--- 53’ Substitution Evans is unable to shake off a knock he just picked up and he is replaced by Craig Gardner. ---
(51’) CHANCE! Routledge sits a cross up nicely to the far post where Ayew is waiting. He goes for power, but ends up striking thin air and West Brom clear
(49’) NERVY! McClean whips in a vicious delivery that is spilled but eventually gathered at the second attempt by Fabianski.
(48’) Rondon embarks on a strong run down the right flank and his eventual cross is cleared behind by Williams. West Brom have a corner...
(46’) KICK OFF! The referee blows his whistle and Swansea get the ball rolling once more.
The players are coming back out onto the field and the second half is about to start.
A fairly quiet first half livened up as it drew to a close. Both sides should look to up their performance levels after the break and ask more questions in the final third.
HALF-TIME: WEST BROM 0-0 SWANSEA
(45’) GOOD SAVE! Sessegnon whips the ball dangerously towards goal and Fabianski is forced to push his delivery over the bar. Swansea deal with the subsequent corner and the referee swiftly blows for half-time.
(45’) At the other end, West Brom are awarded a free-kick just outside the penalty area and near the left corner flag. Sessegnon is stood over it...
(45’) CHANCE! What an impact that would have been for Paloschi, who is neatly released on goal by Routledge, but Foster stands his ground to make an important save.
(45’) There are four minutes of stoppage time as a result of that injury to Ki. We are now into the third and this would be a really good time to score just before the break.
--- 45’ +2 Substitution The change is made with Alberto Paloschi coming on for his debut. ---
(45’) There are no surprises as Ki is unable to continue. He eventually leaves the field on a stretcher and it appears that Paloschi is going to come on for his debut.
(44’) Meanwhile, there is a break in play as Ki receives lengthy attention from the medical team after appearing to take a blow to the head.
(42’) FLETCHER SHOULD SCORE! Sessegnon's wayward volley is kept alive by McClean, who whips the ball back into the area. Fletcher is unmarked but fluffs his lines and scuffs the ball wide of the far post.
(40’) NOT FAR AWAY! West Brom are starting to turn up the pressure and Rondon has half a chance, as he stretches to connect with Sandro's cross but sends it wide of the target.
(39’) MUST DO BETTER! West Brom are awarded a free kick that is floated in by Sessegnon. Dawson loses his marker and has a free header on goal, but he can only glance wide of the target from the penalty spot.
(37’) A clever one-two in the middle of the park sends Routledge away on the counter attack. He slides the ball into Ayew, whose shot is deflected behind by McAuley. The subsequent corner is disappointing, as Sigurdsson sends his delivery way over the head of everyone in the area.
(35’) That was very nearly exactly what the game needed. It was a fantastic effort from Sigurdsson and Foster did really well to keep it out.
(33’) WHAT AN EFFORT! Out of nowhere, Sigurdsson unleashes a dipping 35-yard volley and Foster backtracks really well to push the ball to safety.
(31’) This game has gone really flat over the past few minutes. Neither side are particularly pushing forward or asking questions of their opponents' defences.
(29’) Swansea may have won six of their last nine meetings with West Brom, but the Baggies will fancy their chances at home having lost just one of their last six here in the Premier League.
(27’) Nothing comes of the free kick or a subsequent corner for Swansea following a dangerous counter attack. This game needs to be sparked into life from somewhere.
(25’) West Brom have a free kick just inside their own half and Pulis should encourage his side to pump the ball into the box from this.
(23’) That was a very good chance for West Brom and Fletcher should have made a lot more of it. Opportunities like that have been few and far between so far.
(21’) HAVE A GO YOURSELF! Some neat play from West Brom sees McClean deliver a deep cross to the far post that is met by Fletcher who, rather than head for goal, looks to square it for Rondon. The striker is not expecting the ball, however, and Swansea can relax with a goal kick.
(19’) JUST WIDE! West Brom are pressuring Swansea deep inside their own half, but a clever pass from Ki clearly turns defence into attack. Rangel bears down on goal, but sends his effort wide of the target with Sigurdsson screaming for him to square the ball.
(17’) The past meetings suggest Swansea should break the deadlock soon. Nine of their 16 Premier League goals against the Baggies have come inside the opening 25 minutes of matches.
(15’) Both sides are looking good in possession after the opening quarter of an hour, but both need to offer a lot more in the final third and gets shots away.
(13’) Rondon makes a clever run across the defensive line to connect with a neat through ball by Dawson in the box. He drills it across the face of goal, but Swansea are alert and clear.
(11’) History suggests there will be goals this evening, though, as none of the last nine meetings have ended as draws.
(9’) Neither side have been particularly clinical in front of goal this season, with just 22 apiece so far. Only bottom club Aston Villa have scored less.
(7’) That Taylor surge has appeared to get Swansea going. They are now settling into their rhythm have enjoyed more possession over the past couple of minutes.
(5’) Swansea launch their first real attack of the game and Taylor darts into the space down the left flank. However, his eventual cross is deflected away for a corner.
(3’) Sandro looks to make his mark immediately by throwing himself into a strong challenge for the ball. It is a fair challenge and has got the home fans pumped.
(2’) GREAT SAVE: A bright start from the hosts sees Sessegnon produce some good work down the right. He lays the ball off for Dawson to send in a cross that is met by Fletcher, but his header is well turned over the bar by Fabianski.
(1’) KICK-OFF! Referee Neil Swarbrick blows his whistle and West Brom get the match underway kicking from left to right.
HERE THEY COME! The teams are making their way out onto the field and kick-off is just moments away.
SWANSEA SUBS: Nordfeldt, Amat, Naughton, Paloschi, Gomis, Montero, Barrow.
SWANSEA (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Rangel, Fernandez, Williams (c), Taylor; Britton, Ki; Cork, Sigurdsson, Routledge; Ayew.

Tony Pulis made seven changes for the draw with Peterborough United in the FA Cup on Saturday, but there is just one exception to tonight's team from the one that drew with Aston Villa last time out in the Premier League. Good evening and welcome to LIVE text commentary of the Premier League. We're at the Hawthorns tonight as West Bromwich Albion and Swansea City look to move further clear of the relegation zone.

Well, that’s all from me for this evening. It has finished Everton 3-0 Newcastle United at Goodison Park. Until next time, thank you and goodbye!
As for Newcastle, they were not at the races tonight and travel back to Tyneside with their tails between their legs. Three of their four January signings were on show at Goodison, and none of Shelvey, Townsend or Saivet managed to impress. Mitrovic did miss a golden chance to restore parity shortly after his introduction, but that opportunity was all the visitors could muster as they slumped to yet another defeat against Everton.
Everton were by far the better side throughout, and started the first half well and their fast showing was capped off by Aaron Lennon’s well-taken strike mid-way through the opening stanza. The hosts came out strong after the interval, and though they had to withstand a glut of pressure after the hour-mark, the result was put beyond all doubt when  Barkley - superb throughout - converted twice from the spot late on in what were Everton’s first two penalties of the campaign in any competition.
FULL-TIME! That's it from Goodison Park, where it has finished 3-0 to Everton. It was a fine display from Roberto  Martinez's side as they installed some confidence back into their ranks. As for Steve McClaren's men, however, they were desperately disappointing, and if not for their goalkeeper the defeat could have been much heavier.
--- 90’ +4 Goal! WHAT A FINISH!!! That is incredible composure from Barkley, who dinks the spot-kick expertly high into the roof of the net to make it Everton 3-0 Newcastle! ---
--- 90’ +3 Red card! ANOTHER PENALTY TO EVERTON! AND A RED CARD FOR LASCELLES! The former Nottingham Forest defender makes a dreadful mistake which Barkley capitalises on. The England man powers into the area and the Newcastle man can only bring him down, duly receiving a straight red card for his troubles. ---
(90’) WHAT A MISS! That is so poor from Kone! The Ivorian does well initially to combine with Barkley and drive into the area. He is teed up perfectly by his aforementioned team-mate, but with just Elliot to beat, the former Sevilla man blasts his effort high over the crossbar.
(90’) SO CLOSE! Barkley again takes on several Newcastle players before thumping an effort towards goal. It looks destined for the bottom corner, but a deflection off Coloccini sees it edge just wide of the left-hand upright. Unlucky!
--- 88’ Yellow card A stupid yellow card for Jamal Lascelles, who picks up a booking for attempting to put Barkley off in the wait for that penalty to be taken. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!!! BARKLEY HAMMERS HOME FROM THE SPOT! It’s a cool finish from the midfielder, who sent Elliot the wrong way with a powerful penalty into the bottom-left corner. Everton 2-0 Newcastle! ---
(87’) PENALTY TO EVERTON! Lennon does superbly down the right to graft his way into the area before being brought down by Aarons, and Pawson wastes no time in pointing to the spot.
(86’) McCarthy, who has run himself ragged in the second half, wins a free-kick deep in Newcastle territory. Barkley whips it in, but the cross does not beat the first man. That’s disappointing!
(84’) Top defending from Oviedo there! The Costa Rican, so unlucky with injuries so far this season, has played well in place of Leighton Baines this evening and showed his quality there with a fine block to prevent Sissoko getting a cross in, before doing well to steward Townsend off the ball, which gets a well-deserved cheer from the Goodison crowd.
(82’) Wasteful from Townsend there! The former Tottenham winger will have to deliver a better standard of end-product if he is to live up to his potential here at Newcastle. He does well to jink his way to the by-line, but his resulting cross is a poor one and drifts harmlessly wide.
(80’) That was a chance! One does well to tee up Barkley with a cushioned touch, and the youngster as always takes it in his stride. He drives towards the edge of the box, but once again delays his strike, and Lascelles is on hand to make the block.

--- 90’ +2 Assist Jerome is involved in the equaliser, justifying Neil's decision to get the ex-Birmingham man involved off the bench. ---
--- 90’ +2 Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! BASSONG HAS DONE IT! The defender lashes a low finish into the bottom corner from just outside the box! Great effort! Liverpool's players don't get out quickly enough to make the block! ---
(90’) Mignolet is forced to claim a long pass into the box, with the Belgian goalkeeper looking fairly assured of himself this afternoon. Benteke tries to break following a long ball, but the substitute is caught straying offside.
(90’) We're into the first of five minutes of stoppage time at Carrow Road.
--- 90’ Substitution Caulker is thrown into the fray for the dying minutes, with Moreno taking his leave after a rather sluggish second half. ---
(88’) Olsson drives down the left-hand side, but Clyne tracks back well to slide in and deny the substitute. Norwich angle a cross in from the same flank, but Can is present at the near post to guide the ball away from danger.
(86’) Less than five minutes remain at Carrow Road, with Liverpool pressing on again! Firmino chops in onto his right foot, before firing a low drive goalwards, but Rudd merely has to crouch down and make a comfortable save. Nearly a hat trick for the Brazilian.
(84’) Mbokani manages to bring the ball down on the edge of the penalty area, but his attempted shot loops awfully into the air! Moments later, the same striker is subject to a long pass forward, but Mignolet is quick off his line to gobble it up!
--- 82’ Substitution Jerome comes into the game for the home side, with the ex-Stoke striker looking to inject a little more energy into the forward line. Now would be the time to make a big impact! ---
(80’) Only 10 minutes remain for Norwich to fight back, but it'll take a huge physical and psychological effort from Neil's men. Time is running out, but the home fans are starting to get behind their players and urge then towards the finish line.
(78’) Liverpool can now sit back and prey on mistakes from the hosts, with Norwich struggling to get any kind of control in this game. The away outfit are happy to slow things down with slow possession, asking Norwich's tiring players to keep working hard and pressing.
--- 76’ Substitution Benteke comes into the game, with it appearing that Klopp isn't done with pressing on. Firmino will drop back as a result, with the Belgian striker slotting into the attack. ---
--- 75’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! MILNER COMPLETES THE COMEBACK! The England international races into the clear, before sprinting into the penalty area. Rudd comes to close the angle, but the Liverpool midfielder strokes a neat finish inside the near post! Unbelievable stuff! ---
(75’) Can is forced to hook a near-post clearance away, as Norwich remind Liverpool than they're still in this game with a rare break. Martin is unable to catch Milner on the counter moments later, with the ex-Aston Villa man racing into the clear.
(74’) Moreno plays a neat one-two with Firmino, before racing to receive the ball on the periphery of the penalty area. The Spaniard takes aim with his left foot, but can only fizz a low shit into the awaiting gloves of Rudd.
(72’) Bassong makes a timely clearance at his near post, with the former Spurs defender now having to sit on the edge of his own penalty area. The home side are sitting in and inviting plenty of pressure on, which could prove to be a risky approach given that there are still 20 minutes on the clock.
--- 70’ Substitution Olsson comes into the game and will slot in on the left-hand side, in what is something of a consolidatory change from the hosts. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Redmond takes his leave, with the former Birmingham winger struggling to get into the match throughout. ---
(67’) Firmino is the target of a looping delivery into the penalty area, but Pinto tracks his man well to ensure that the danger is cleared well. Lucas then tries to thread a long through ball into the path of Henderson, but Martin steps out to make a vital interception.
(65’) It is the away support that is making all of the noise now, with the Canaries struggling to find their feet. Lallana is slid in behind, before racing into the box and forcing a save out of Rudd, but the linesman's flag was raised for offside anyway.
--- 63’ Assist Lallana whips a sumptous ball in from the left-hand side, with Klopp's first substitute having the desired impact. ---
--- 63’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! FIRMINO STRIKES AGAIN! The Brazilian striker is picked out in the penalty area by a swirling delivery, before having the peace of mind to lift a neat finish over Rudd and into the back of the net! Coolness personified from the ex-Hoffenheim striker. ---
(62’) Norwich are sat in a precarious position at the moment, with the Canaries needing to take the sting and momentum out of the game. Rudd takes a while with a goal kick, which may be a theme of the final half an hour.
(61’) We're into the final half an hour at Carrow Road, with the atmosphere getting a little bit cagey. Norwich are sat deep, with the visitors seeing much more of possession at the minute. Neil's men are happy to concede territory and sit deep.
--- 59’ Substitution Lallana comes into the fray for the Reds, with Ibe struggling to have any real impact since the restart for the second half. Klopp is seeking to make the alterations required to stage a masterful comeback. ---
(57’) Liverpool are suddenly high on confidence once again, with Klopp's men having the belief that they can fight back and get on level terms. Firmino has been vital to the opening two goals, but the introduction of Benteke could pose different questions for Martin and Bassong.
--- 55’ Assist Firmino is involved once again, with the Brazilian proving to be silky customer in the final third. ---
--- 55’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! HENDERSON MAKES IT 3-2! The ex-Sunderland midfielder sweeps home a lovely finish from outside the area, with Rudd unable to extend enough to get a hand to it! ---
--- 54’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! HOOLAHAN CONVERTS! The Irishman slots a neat finish over the sprawling body of Mignolet, with the hosts now having a vital two-goal cushion! ---
(52’) PENALTY FOR THE HOSTS! Norwich have a reasonable handle on the contest, with the potential to counter at real pace. Naismith and Pinto combine, before the former is set on his way into the box! Moreno gets the wrong side of the Scot, who goes down and earns a spot kick!
(50’) The Canaries continue to put on the early pressure, despite it being Liverpool who have all of the catching up to do. Redmond looks to scamper down the right flank, but Moreno stands up to the Englishman brilliantly. Klopp's outfit need to find a foothold in this clash quickly.
(48’) Norwich push on from the off, though Neil's men are clearly conscious of how many yellow shirts that they are pressing forward with. Mbokani holds the ball up brilliantly, before releasing Pinto down the right-hand side, but the former Dinamo Zagreb defender can only loop a swirling effort wide of the far post!
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Klopp's men need to muster up at least two goals to take home three points this afternoon, which looks to be beyond the Reds at present.
HALF TIME! The hosts go in ahead, after a brilliantly competitive first half at Carrow Road! Mbokani and Naismith have got the Canaries sitting pretty, despite the Reds getting the scoring underway through Firmino. Liverpool have some work to do.
(45’) Rudd is forced to lash a hurried clearance away, after a terribly weighted back pass from Brady! Firmino was sniffing about, but the Norwich goalkeeper was quick off his line to deny the Brazilian. There are two minutes of stoppage time.
(43’) Norwich have turned this game on its head, with Naismith pulling all of the strings for his new club. The Canaries sit back from kick off, with the hosts now able to sit back and play on the break. Klopp might have some thinking to do at the half-time interval.
--- 41’ Assist Hoolahan plays an inviting pass down the right channel, with Norwich linking up well on the peripheries of the penalty area yet again. ---
--- 41’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! NAISMITH MAKES IT 2-1! The former Everton makes his mark immediately, after being found overlapping down the right-hand side! He drives into the box, before lashing a low finish across goal and into the far corner! ---
(40’) Less than five minutes remain in the first half for either side to try and get their noses back in front, with Norwich pushing on. Brady drives to the left byline, but the left-back is denied well by Clyne, who is happy to concede a corner. The resulting set piece is easily headed away at the near post.
(39’) The clock is ticking down towards the interval, with Norwich looking to force the issue. Naismith is putting in plenty of hard work, with the Scotland international definitely looking to repay the faith put in him by new coach Alex Neil. The hosts break down the right, with Hoolahan cutting infield, but the Irishman is brought down by a hard tackle.
(37’) Mbokani lifts a lovely ball into the penalty area, with Howson trying to take it down neatly, but Lucas steps in to leather a clearance behind for a corner! The resulting set piece looks for the aforementioned Congolese striker, but Sakho vitally intervenes ahead of the Norwich goalscorer. In the aftermath, Milner is lucky to get away with a shove on Naismith.
(35’) Norwich make progress down the right-hand side, but a delivery into the box comes to nothing. Neil's men work the ball nicely down the other flank moments later, but some intricate play between Naismith and Brady doesn't quite come off. The former Everton midfielder is leading by example at the moment.
(33’) Mbokani comes back onto the field after extended treatment, though Jerome is warming up as a precaution on the sideline. Narrowly over 10 minutes remain in the first half, with both sides enjoying periods of dominance after scoring their respective goals.
(31’) All square again now, with the atmosphere suddenly picking up at Carrow Road! The home fans are making plenty of noise, with that goal from Mbokani sending them into raptures. A set piece proves to be Liverpool's undoing yet again. Play is quickly back underway, before there is a long stoppage for a poor challenge from Lucas on the goalscorer.
--- 29’ Assist Dorrans swung a looping effort into the box, but the ex-West Brom midfielder can only watch as Mbokani does some magic! ---
--- 29’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! WHAT A FINISH FROM MBOKANI! The former Dynamo Kiev striker manages to take the ball down deep inside the opposition penalty area, before backheeling a cheeky effort beyond Mignolet! Pure inspiration and the Canaries are level! ---
(28’) Sakho concedes a free kick on the right-hand side, with Mbokani being sent tumbling to the turf after a push. The hosts have the chance to load the box as a result, but Toure heads the danger away. Norwich keep the pressure on, with Martin whipping in a cross, but Mignolet gets up ahead of Naismith to punch clear!
(26’) Wide from Moreno! The ex-Sevilla left-back is teed up for the resulting free kick, but can only send a swerving shot way beyond the far upright! Since taking the lead, the Reds have definitely been on top, with Norwich having no staying power in the opposition penalty area.
(24’) Liverpool continue to cause problems, with Clyne picked out advancing down the right-hand side. The Englishman slides a pass into Firmino, with Bassong forced into pulling down the Brazil international. Contact was just outside the penalty area, with the Norwich defender fortunate to not give away something a little more serious.
(22’) Milner has a chance of his own! Firmino manages to slid a through ball into the path of the ex-Leeds midfielder, but the Englishman can only force a one-versus-one save out of Rudd! The resulting corner is taken short and then whipped into the box, but Martin clears at the near post.
(20’) Mbokani does brilliant to hold the ball up, before Norwich get some joy down the left-hand side. A swirling delivery is launched into the box by Brady, but no yellow shirts can make contact! Yet again, Toure does just enough to scramble the danger clear.
--- 18’ Assist Milner slid a neat pass in behind enemy lines, with Brazilian doing brilliantly to turn home a finish from a tight angle. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! FIRMINO MAKES IT 1-0! The Brazilian is fed into the penalty area down the left channel, before squeezing home the tightest of finishes! A trickling finish bobbles under Rudd and makes its way into the back of the net after kissing the inside of the far post! ---
(17’) Naismith has the chance to slide a neat pass in behind enemy lines for Mbokani to chase, but the ball from the Scottish midfielder is cut out. Moments later, Firmino is fed over the top by Moreno, but Bassong puts enough pressure on the Brazilian attacker to ensure that the former Hoffenheim man can only hook a looping effort way over the bar!
(15’) Toure and Sakho continue to be dominant in the air, with Norwich only having any luck in the wide areas of the field. After a shaky start, the away outfit are getting their foot on the ball and stringing together a few attacks. Firmino is the target of a long through pass from Henderson, but Rudd sweeps up. Moments later, Hoolahan sees a shot blocked.
(13’) Liverpool work the ball from right to left, before Ibe does well to beat Ivo Pinto to the byline! The Englishman cuts back a neat cross, but it doesn't pick out a red shirt, with the away side finally showing some signs of life. Naismith is picked out and looks to counter, but Sakho fouls the former Everton midfielder.
(11’) Naismith is presented with a chance on the left-hand side, but the Scotland international is unable to swivel and shoot on the edge of the box. Brady is found overlapping as a result, but a cross from the ex-Hull defender is well blocked. Klopp's men are still on the back foot.
(9’) Naismith releases Redmond down the right-hand side, before Ivo Pinto plays a neat one-two with the ex-Birmingham winger. A delivery into the box is hacked away by Toure, with Mignolet glued to his line. Norwich have been bright in the opening stages, with Liverpool struggling to get going.
(7’) Naismith is penalised for a very late challenge on Lucas, with both sides very competitive in the opening minutes. Redmond sprints down the right flank, before attempting to whip a cross in from the byline, but Moreno stands up to his man well. Chances have been few and far between thus far.
(5’) Redmond tries to flick a header towards Mbokani, but the Congolese forward is denied by Moreno easily. Liverpool counter, with Clyne countering down the right-hand side, but the ex-Palace right-back is outmuscled well by Brady while trying to overlap.
(3’) Norwich get the ball out to the left flank, but Henderson does brilliantly to cut a pass out on the edge of the penalty area. Firmino is leading the line for the visitors, but Ibe and Milner are dropping deep to aid their full-backs.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Carrow Road! There's perfect conditions for some football this afternoon, with no excuses for either side as to why they can't get the ball down and play some neat stuff.
Liverpool substitutes: Benteke, Caulker, Lallana, Allen, Flanagan, Ward, Joao Carlos.
Liverpool starting line-up (4-3-3): Mignolet; Clyne, Toure, Sakho, Moreno; Can, Lucas, Henderson; Milner, Firmino, Ibe.
Norwich substitutes: Ruddy, Jerome, Jarvis, Klose, Mulumbu, Olsson, Odjidja-Ofoe.
Norwich starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Rudd; Ivo Pinto, Martin, Bassong, Brady; Dorrans, Howson; Naismith, Hoolahan, Redmond; Mbokani.
TEAM NEWS: Jordan Ibe and James Milner will start in the wide areas, with Roberto Firmino preferred to Christian Benteke up top. Kolo Toure continues in the heart of the back four, with Lucas Leiva holding in midfield. Few changes from Klopp, with Simon Mignolet in goal after recently signing a new contract. John Flanagan is among the substitutes today.
TEAM NEWS: Declan Rudd starts in goal for the hosts, with Ivo Pinto getting a start at right-back after joining from Dinamo Zagreb this month. Wes Hoolahan is inserted into the midfield, with new signing Steven Naismith also starting from the off. Nathan Redmond is deployed out wide, with Dieumerci Mbokani starting alone up top. Gary O'Neil is missing due to suspension.
Liverpool have only won one of their last four competitive games, with that one victory coming against Exeter City in the FA Cup. The Reds should have the potential to turn their form around, with the Canaries scoring merely once during their last three outings. Three points should keep the visitors in the hunt for European football.
Hello and welcome to the Premier League's early kick off, with Liverpool travelling to Carrow Road to face Norwich. The hosts are on a three-game losing run, after falling to consecutive top-flight defeats against both Stoke and Bournemouth. Jurgen Klopp's men, meanwhile, will be looking to recover from an undeserved 1-0 loss at the hands of Man United.

I hope you enjoyed this enthralling game as much as we did! That's all we have time for today I'm afraid. We hope you'll join us again next time. Enjoy the rest of your weekend.
Crystal Palace will hope that today's performance, if not result can be a stepping stone to better things going forward. If they play like this more often then it won't be long before they start climbing back up the table. As for Spurs, it has been a fantastic afternoon for them with Southampton beating Manchester United at Old Trafford to strengthen the North Londoner's grip on fourth spot.
Mauricio Pochettino will be incredibly proud of his squad. They had to hang in there at times and can thank Hugo Lloris for keeping Palace at bay in the second half. But the character and resilience shown will have further convinced the Tottenham Hotspur Head Coach that he has a special group of players at his disposal and that they should have enough to secure a top 4 finish as a minimum this season. On the evidence of this form maybe they can aim even higher?
I'm trying to catch my breath. That was a pulsating encounter. Both teams gave it everything but in the end Tottenham's superior quality was enough to win the day. That was a good, old fashioned - proper London derby. It was feisty, fierce and extremely competitive. Alan Pardew will be bitterly disappointed that his side couldn't hold onto their lead for a bit longer in the second half and will look ruefully on some missed opportunities before Dele Alli's moment of individual brilliance saw Spurs over the line.
(90’) Full time here at Selhurst Park. Crystal Palace 1-3 Tottenham Hotspur.
--- 90’ +5 Assist Dele Alli caps off another impressive display by laying on the third goal for Chadli. Spurs played a corner short before the Belgian attacker added gloss to proceedings from a Tottenham perspective. ---
--- 90’ +5 Goal! And now it is three! Nacer Chadli makes it 3 with an outstanding curling effort from outside the area that Hennessey can do nothing about. The scoreline is perhaps harsh on Palace but this is a massive victory for Tottenham Hotspur. ---
(90’) SAVE! Spurs aren't settling for two they want a third. Chadli plays a lovely sweeping pass into the path of Bentaleb who stings the palms of Hennessey from distance.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Yellow card Harry Kane ---
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Yellow card Mile Jedinak ---
(90’) CHANCE! Alli nearly makes it safe for the visitors by sees his shot come back off the bar. The youngster turned Damien Delaney inside out before lifting the ball over Hennessey.
(90’) Spurs have numbers up in a counter-attack but Kane is rather greedy and goes for goal when he really should have played in Son with a reverse pass.
--- 88’ Substitution Pochettino looks to tighten things up in midfield by bringing on the more defensively minded Nabil Bentaleb for Christian Eriksen. Spurs will be desperate to see this out and claim a precious three points. ---
(88’) Palace are certainly not lying down and nor would you expect them to. Delaney whips in a great cross that is met by a diving header from Zaha but Lloris able to smother it. Can the home side rescue a point?
--- 85’ Substitution Pardew immediately reacts to going behind by throwing on former Tottenham loanee Fraizer Campbell in place of Cabaye. ---
--- 84’ Goal! 2-1 SPURS! Dele Alli - take a bow son! The Tottenham midfielder has just scored a sensational goal. Alli flicked the ball over Jedinak's head before lashing an unstoppable volley into the bottom corner. Breathtaking skill. ---
--- 84’ Assist Eriksen nodded the ball into Alli's path and the England international did the rest. Spurs have turned things around. Can they hold on? ---
(82’) Now it is Tottenham's turn to not just knock but hammer on the Palace door. Kane and then Trippier send cross after cross into the box but Delaney and Dann are up to the task.
(80’) CHANCE! Dann and then Jedinak hit the frame of the Tottenham goal in quick succession. How unlucky can you get?! Puncheon's flighted cross was well met by Dann who looped his header onto the bar. The rebound then fell to Jedinak who crashed the ball off the woodwork. What an escape for Spurs.
(79’) Wickham holds the ball up well before bringing Puncheon into play, the winger steps inside before being bodychecked by Trippier. This could be a big chance for Palace.
--- 79’ Yellow card Yellow card Kieran Trippier ---
--- 79’ Substitution Substitution James McArthur Mile Jedinak ---
(77’) There has been a lovely ebb and flow to this encounter from the get-go and the second half has been end-to-end stuff. Spurs have the chance to use Kieran Trippier on the overlap but Eriksen rather sells him short and Palace are able to clear.
(75’) Into the last 15 minutes here. It really is anyone's guess how this match will finish up. Both sides will fancy their chances of taking all three points.
--- 75’ Substitution Substitution Jan Vertonghen Kevin Wimmer ---
(73’) Jan Vertonghen's afternoon looks to be over. The Belgian defender appeared to be caught with a stray elbow to the face from Wickham moments earlier but it appears to be his knee that is the problem that will force him off. Kevin Wimmer is stripped off and ready to make his Premier League debut.
(71’) Spurs now look to counter and Dele Alli leads the charge forward. He is then unceremoniously fouled by Ledley. Eriksen takes the set-piece but his cross doesn't beat the first man, again.
(69’) SAVE! Lloris not once but twice keeps the score at 1-1 with two excellent reaction stops. Firstly he tips Zaha's curling shot away for a corner and then from the set-piece he gets down quickly to keep out Souare's low drive. Good goalkeeping.
(67’) Rose beats Zaha to the loose bouncing ball on the edge of the penalty area and is then brought down by the Palace wide man. The free-kick is in Eriksen territory but his shot crashes into the wall and the home side can breathe again.
(65’) As you would expect Tottenham have their tails up now and are pouring men forward at every chance they get. This will be a real test of Palace's resolve if they can stand up to the expected onslaught from the visitors. Important for Pardew's men to keep things tight for the next few minutes if they can.
--- 63’ Assist Chadli's cross was a rather looping and hopeful one into the six yard box but Kane made something of it and gave Hennessey no time to react. ---
--- 63’ Goal! 1-1! Spurs are back on level terms. And who else but Tottenham's talismanic striker - Harry Kane! The centre forward rose highest in the penalty area and headed home from close range. Fantastic hunger and desire shown there, he made that ball his. ---
--- 61’ Yellow card Simple call for the referee to make. Eriksen goes for goal from the free-kick and it is well watched by Hennessey as the ball skipped up just in front of him. ---
(60’) Son is dropping deeper and deeper to get on the ball so that he can turn and run at the defence. This time his surge forward is brought to an end by McArthur who crudely hauls him down. Yellow card for the Palace midfielder.
(58’) Eriksen is caught late with a high foot from Jason Puncheon but the referee sees nothing wrong with the challenge and allows play to continue. Unless Palace can see a bit more of the ball it looks like being a rearguard action for the last 30 minutes or so of this match.
--- 56’ Substitution Pochettino makes an early change and it is an attacking one. Dier is replaced by Nacer Chadli. Seems a purely tactical alteration. You would imagine that Alli will drop a bit deeper with Eriksen moving into the no.10 role. ---
(55’) CHANCE! Eric Dier curls in a pinpoint cross from the right hand side and puts the ball onto the forehead of Kane but the Spurs striker can only head the ball straight at Hennessey. It's the sort of chance he usually gobbles up.
(53’) Cabaye gets himself in a tangle with first Kane and then Alli before ending up in a heap just in front of the dugouts. The ex-Newcastle United playmaker came off worse and looked far from impressed with the challenges.
(51’) OVER! Christian Eriksen lets fly from about 25 yards out and almost scores an absolute screamer. The Tottenham midfielder struck a fierce, dipping right footed shot that flew just over the bar. Hennessey was beaten all ends up there.
(49’) Spurs players and fans howl in unison for a handball from Scott Dann inside the penalty area but there is nothing doing from either the referee or the linesman. It looked like the ball struck the Palace defender's face to me, would have been an incredibly harsh decision if it had been given.
(47’) Spurs have begun as they mean to go on. Straight back on the ball and on the front foot. Eriksen lays the ball off to Rose who exchanges passes with Son and looks to burst into the Palace penalty area but Dann comes across and hacks the ball clear.
(45’) Crystal Palace, a goal to the good, get the second half restarted.
The players are just beginning to emerge from the tunnel and the second half will be starting shortly...
Everything is set up for an intriguing conclusion to this contest. The second half is fascinatingly poised. Palace will feel - so far, so good. Their game plan is going to plan at the moment. If Zaha can continue playing the way he has done in this game then the home side will fancy that they can create more opportunities as things wear on. Tottenham on the other hand, will be in no rush to change things just yet personnel wise but they know they have the likes of Lamela, Chadli and Bentaleb to call upon if required.
As for Mauricio Pochettino, a penny for his thoughts at the moment? He has seen his side play pretty well for the vast majority of the first half yet they find themselves behind against a very determined and resolute opponent. You suspect the Spurs manager will be fairly calm at this stage. Surely he will think that if the pattern of the first half continues in the second then a goal is coming for his side?
That has been a thoroughly entertaining first fourty-five minutes. It would be fair to say that Crystal Palace scored rather against the run of play but the home side will not care one bit. Wilfried Zaha has been a real livewire all game and Alan Pardew will want to see him on the ball as much as possible after the break. The England winger has made Danny Rose's afternoon very difficult.
(45’) And that's the half time whistle! Crystal Palace 1-0 Tottenham Hotspur.
(44’) A period of sustained possession for the North London side ends with Alderweireld getting an attempted cross all wrong. Smashing the ball out of play. Alan Pardew will be delighted if his side can go into the half-time interval with their lead in tact.
(42’) This really has been a pulsating London so far. Tottenham go close again but no-one able to connect with Harry Kane's dangerous looking cross flashing across the face of goal. The away side are pushing hard to get back on level terms before the break but Palace are standing firm.
(40’) SAVE! Hennessey shows fantastic reflexes to deny Spurs an equaliser. Eriksen stood the ball up at the far post and Danny Rose meets it with a side footed volley but can only fire his effort straight at the Palace goalkeeper.
(38’) This time it's Tottenham's turn to attack - Dembele picks out the onrushing Trippier down the right wing, who cleverly pulls the ball back to the waiting Son who tries to turn Delaney inside the area but Palace defend well in numbers and smuggle the ball away to safety.
(36’) Puncheon takes a corner from the left hand side and beautifully picks out Cabaye on the top of the box who meets the corner sweetly but his volley is well blocked by Vertonghen. That shot needed stopping as the French international had met that one sweetly.
(34’) SAVE! Spurs launch a quick break with four or five players up in the attack. Eriksen finds Alli, who had drifted onto the left flank, who then cuts inside onto his favoured right foot. The former MK Dons midfielder looks to bend it into the far corner but Hennessey reads it all the way and holds on well.
(32’) WIDE! Good response from Tottenham. Alderweireld takes a pot shot from the edge of the area that whistles past the post with Kane desperately trying to get a toe on it.
--- 30’ Goal! 1-0! Palace take the lead! Jan Vertonghen diverts Zaha's cross into his own net from close range. Just out of the reach of the despairing dive of Hugo Lloris. That is exactly the sort of break the Eagles have been looking for. ---
(28’) As the 28th minute arrives that signals that is now exactly eight hours of Premier League football that have gone by since Crystal Palace last scored.
(26’) Kane, Eriksen and Alli combine on the top of the box which gives the Spurs youngster a chance but Alli can't get enough purchase on his half volley and it is easy for Hennessey to deal with.
(24’) The game has just got a little bit scrappy in the last few minutes with both teams guilty of giving away silly fouls that have spoilt their own forward momentum. As has been a feature of their play this season, the Tottenham full backs are pushing very high up the pitch - trying to provide as much width as possible.
(22’) That half a chance for the home side might just be the spark that the Palace players and supporters require. It would be unfair to say that Pardew's men have been a little flat, as they simply haven't had enough of the ball so far to get themselves a foothold in the game.
(20’) Lloris, not for the first time this afternoon it must be said, hits a poor pass that puts his team under needless pressure. Zaha pounces on the lapse and Palace nearly capitalise on the mistake. The Eagles wide man puts in a teasing low cross that Wickham is almost able to convert but Spurs have just enough men in the box to snuff out the danger.
(18’) Cabaye tries to get the home side going by whipping in a left footed cross from the right but he gets far too much on it and Spurs can clear their lines.
(16’) CHANCE! Free header for Alderweireld but he glances it wide from Eriksen's outswinging corner. The Tottenham centre back will maybe feel he should have hit the target there. The Belgian international has been a threat from set pieces all season. Let off for Palace, far too many players ball watching.
(15’) Tottenham force a corner which is kept alive by Rose at the back post. Alderweireld then pumps the ball back into the Palace penalty area which is cleared but only as far as Eriksen who releases Kane who tests Hennessey low at his near post. Perhaps the England striker could have looked for a teammate there instead of going for goal.
(14’) Alan Pardew will want his midfielders to be a little more careful on the ball than they have been so far. On a few occasions they have been far too sloppy and have simply handed the initiative back to Spurs.

However, Eddie Howe’s side, who now move level on points with champions Chelsea, were pegged back on the stroke of half time by Patrick van Aanholt’s well-taken goal.
FULL-TIME! That's all from the Stadium of Light as the referee sounds the final whistle. It has finished Sunderland 1-1 Bournemouth.
(90’) CHANCE! So nearly a goal for Sunderland! Van Aanholt does excellently to get free down the left and slide a cut-back into the centre of the area. Watmore looks set to tuck it home, but Francis once again puts his body on the line to stem the effort at source.
(90’) We are into the third minute of three minutes stoppage time, now, though referee Roger East will surely add on more following the injury to Stanislas…
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Substitution Junior Stanislas Glenn Murray ---
--- 89’ Yellow card RECKLESS! Billy Jones is a very fortunate boy here, as he escapes with just a booking following a late, hefty lunge in from behind on Stanislas. The Bournemouth winger, who has been impressive today, looks in real pain here. ---
--- 88’ Substitution Another change now for the hosts, as Jack Rodwell comes on in place of Jeremain Lens, who has been rather ineffective in a support-striker role today. ---
(85’) The visitors are upping the ante now as we enter the final moments of this game. Arter plays a wonderful dinked pass into the path of Daniels, who had made a fantastic surging drive into the Sunderland penalty area, but the Bournemouth left-back cannot keep the ball in play following a heavy first touch.
(82’) WHAT A MISS!!! That really was a sitter! Stanislas threads a neat pass through to Grabban, who, with just Mannone to beat, takes a wonderful first touch to bring the ball under his control in the area, but the Bournemouth substitute can only prod his effort well wide from close range.
(79’) CLOSE! A lucky escape there for Sunderland, as Surman’s strike from 20 yards out takes a wicked deflection off Gosling. The Bournemouth man would have been onside thanks to slack defending from Brown, but the knick directs the effort just wide of the target.
(77’) Referee Roger East has brought play to a halt now, as Van Aanholt receives treatment following a collision with Smith. The Dutchman appears to have taken a whack to the side of his head, but after a moment on the deck, the full-back returns to his feet and play will resume with a drop-ball...
(75’) ALMOST! Great play from Bournemouth, as Ritchie and Smith combine crisply down the right before the latter drills in a low cross. Grabban swings his right foot at it, but the former Norwich forward ends up swinging at thin air due to a last-ditch interception from O’Shea.
(73’) SUPERB DEFENDING! Another Sunderland set-piece causes plenty of problems for Bournemouth, who are unable to clear the initial cross, with possession eventually falling to Cattermole on the edge of the area. The midfielder goes for goal with a first-time effort, but Cook charges out to block the shot.
(71’) Compared to the first half, it has been a much less free-flowing encounter since the restart. Johnson flashes a fantastic low ball across the face of goal as Sunderland manage to carve out another opportunity, but Lens cannot get on the end of it.
(68’) Fantastic defending once more from Bournemouth’s Smith, who stands up well to the run of Watmore down the left, timing his tackle perfectly and allowing Howe’s men to drive forward on the counter. The full-back has been excellent today.
--- 66’ Substitution And it is a maiden substitution of the fixture from Allardyce, as he introduces youngster Duncan Watmore in place of Fabio Borini. ---
--- 64’ Substitution A second change then for the visitors, as goal-scorer Benik Afobe is replaced by Lewis Grabban. ---
(62’) A slight lull in play now for the time-being, with both sides engaged in a tussle for dominance in midfield. It seems that changes may be imminent from both managers...
(59’) CHANCE! Almost for Sunderland! Bournemouth have been vulnerable from set-pieces all season, and once more a cross into the box from a dead-ball nearly proves their downfall. Johnson curls a wonderful ball into the box, which Jones connects with, but Boruc is on hand to parry it back out off the goal-line.
--- 57’ Substitution A first substitution of the game now, as Marc Pugh makes way for Matt Ritchie, who missed out last week with an injury. ---
(56’) CLOSE! Finally, Defoe receives the ball in a dangerous area. He latches onto a pass from deep before jinking past Smith and then Francis. With no support, he tries his luck with a dipping effort that looked destined to nestle into the top-right corner, but it sails just a foot wide of the upright.
(55’) That excellent pass from M’Vila seems to have buoyed his teammates somewhat, and it has definitely provided a boost for the Sunderland faithful. The Frenchman does brilliantly again to dispossess Gosling before driving a puncturing ball forward to Lens, but he is unable to find Borini with a disappointing through ball out wide.
(53’) It’s the visitors who have been doing most of the pressing in the opening moments of the second half, with Defoe looking more and more isolated up top for Sunderland. Allardyce’s side finally manage to create a half-chance thanks to M’Vila’s penetrating pass to Borini, who attempts to slip in Lens, but the Netherlands winger cannot keep the ball in play.
(50’) That’s really poor from Stanislas! Sunderland concede possession deep into their own half and Gosling capitalises. He feeds it to the aforementioned winger, who, with Arter in acres of space to his right, elects to go for goal himself, but blazes his effort way over the target. What a waste!
(49’) Stanislas has provided some wicked deliveries into Sunderland’s area this afternoon, but on this occasion the cross from the corner is a poor one, and the hosts clear their lines.
(48’) A sloppy pass from Francis is pounced upon by Van Aanholt, who drives a quick ball to the right but Johnson is not as alert as his full-back was. Bournemouth regain their cool and get forward, with Stanislas finding Afobe, whose strike is deflected wide by O’Shea.
(46’) Back under way! Bournemouth get the second half up and running at the Stadium of Light, with the score locked on level terms. There have been no changes for either side at the interval.
A huge half-time team-talk for both managers now. If Allardyce can mastermind a comeback from his side, then it could well be a real turning-point in Sunderland’s battle to avoid relegation. As for Bournemouth, they controlled the tempo of this game for the opening half an hour, but will rue missed chances from both Afobe and Stanislas that have enabled the hosts to get back into this contest.
HALF-TIME! That's it for the first-half, and what an enthralling encounter it has been so far this afternoon at the Stadium of Light. Benki Afobe gave the visitors the lead early on with his second goal in as many games, but Bournemouth were made to pay for missing several more opportunites when Patrick van Aanholt beat Boruc with a well-placed finish to restore parity heading into the interval.
--- 45’ +1 Assist It was smart play from Fabio Borini, who teed up the Sunderland left-back with a perfectly-weighted through ball. ---
--- 45’ +1 Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLL!!! IT’S ALL SQUARE! What a time to score for Sunderland, as Borini plays a weighted pass into the path of Van Anaholt, who drills in a powerful strike past Boruc at the near-post! ---
(45’) CLOSE! Nervy goalkeeping from Boruc, who is almost deceived by Borini’s deflected strike on goal,but the former Southampton goal-keeper manages to adjust his feet and make the save, fumbling the ball before collecting it in at the second attempt.
(43’) Poor from Lens, who, after latching onto Johnson’s superb pass, takes a heavy touch and allows Daniels to recover, preventing the former PSV attacker getting into the area.
(40’) Wasteful! Bournemouth get forward on the counter attack following sloppy play down Sunderland’s left flank. The visitors work it in-field to Afobe, who tees up Pugh. The winger jaunts onto his right foot and attempts to curl an effort into the far corner, but it sails harmlessly over the crossbar.
(38’) Sunderland have grown into the match somewhat in the last 10 minutes or so, with Bournemouth sitting notably deeper in their own territory than they were in the opening half-an-hour of this fixture. Cattermole drives the hosts forward with a run from midfield before finding Jones with a long pass to the right wing, but Daniels defends the cross expertly.
(36’) CLOSE! Sunderland win another free-kick, this time on the left, which M’Vila curls in excellently. Jones attempts to latch onto it ahead of his marker, but the former West Brom full-back is just unable to leap high enough to make a connection and the ball trickles away for a goal-kick to Bournemouth.
(35’) GREAT SAVE! Sunderland finally manage to muster a chance as Borini floats in a cross which O’Shea - still up from the free-kick a moment previous - meets at the back post. His header is a powerful one, but Boruc dives sharply to his left to parry it away from goal. It falls to the feet of Defoe, but he is flagged offside.
(34’) Poor delivery! Bournemouth have conceded 11 goals from set-pieces so far this term - more than any other Premier League side. But they were never in danger of conceding there, as Johnson’s cross failed to beat the first man.
(33’) An opportunity now for Sunderland as Lens is brought down by Gosling deep in Bournemouth’s half. Johnson stands over the set-piece...
(31’) A bit of pressure now from the hosts, as Johnson - who has already matched his previous record-high tally of assists (six) this season - whips in a corner from the right that Bournemouth fail to clear. The ball falls to the feet of Borini, who twists and turns before eventually being stewarded away from goal by the ever-disciplined Francis.
(28’) Despite their poor start, Sunderland can be confident they will get back into this game if they can just somehow stem the tide of the constant Bournemouth attacks. They have won three of their six Barclays Premier League home games played under Sam Allardyce. They had claimed only three victories from the previous 19 before his arrival.
(26’) UNLUCKY! It’s a good save from Mannone, who does well to prevent Afobe doubling his and Bournemouth’s tally with a powerful strike from the cusp of Sunderland’s area. He had been played in by Stanislas, who then made a fantastic run into the area, but the former Wolves forward elected to take on the chance himself rather than play in his aforementioned teammate.
(24’) Patient build-up play from Bournemouth deep in Sunderland territory almost results in Pugh getting free on the left, but Jones intercepts. The visitors regain possession and work it wide to Stanislas, who tries his luck with a venomous drive at goal, but Mannone is equal to it on this occasion. Sunderland are really under pressure here, and their fans are already starting to make their dis-satisfaction known as the boos ring around the Stadium of Light.
(22’) Sunderland have hardly been out of their own half since the visitors took the lead, and Bournemouth are well in control of proceedings at the moment, and Stanislas - who had combined well with Afobe - would have been in on goal once more then if not for a timely challenge from Van Aanholt.
(20’) Well-worked! A smart corner routine from Bournemouth, as Pugh slides a neat low-cross into the path of Surman on the edge of the area, but the visitors’ No.6 is closed down quickly by his opposite number Cattermole, and Sunderland escape unscathed this time around.
--- 18’ Yellow card A yellow card now for Andrew Surman for a late lunge on Lens. That's the first booking of the game for either side. ---
(15’) SO CLOSE! Bournemouth have scored more goals in the opening 15 minutes of games than any other Premier League side so far this term, and they almost make it 2-0 here with another superbly-worked move, this time on the opposite flank. Pugh once more keeps Jones guessing before poking through a pass into the path of the on-rushing Daniels, who curls in a delightful first-time cross. O’Shea gets a weak header on it at the front post, which falls to Stanislas, but the former West Ham winger is unable to bundle it home into an empty net.
--- 13’ Assist It really was a superb cross from Junior Stanislas, who stood up a brilliant delivery to Afobe, who duly headed home. ---
--- 13’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!!! AFOBE MAKES IT 1-0! No mistake this time from the Bournemouth forward, who latches onto the end of Stanislas’ inch-perfect cross before powering a finish past Mannone, who can only parry it high into the roof of the net. ---
(11’) CHANCE!!! Afobe should have scored there! Gosling shows brilliant skill to weave into the Sunderland box and get to the by-line, before sliding a precise cross into the six-yard box. The aforementioned former Arsenal striker looks set to tap it home past Mannone, but he fails to stretch far enough and the opportunity goes begging.
(9’) It’s been an entreating, albeit lacking in quality, start hear in the north east. Both sides have shown attacking intent from the off, but neither team have been able carve out a clear opportunity as of yet.
(7’) Good work on the left from Pugh, who teases Jones before lofting in a delivery towards the back post. Gosling, who opened the scoring against Norwich last week in similar circumstances, rises to meet it, but the former Everton and Newcastle midfielder is well-marshalled by O’Shea.
(5’) A first opportunity of the game now for the visitors as Stanislas curls in a free-kick from the left wing. The cross fails to find a Bournemouth shirt, but Sunderland fail to clear their lines and the ball falls to Cook who, on the turn, prods a volley goalwards, but the strike does not trouble Mannone.
(3’) Good defending from Smith, who moves over from right back to cover for the exposed Cook, who had been caught out of position and allowed Borini to run in-behind. Johnson curls in the resulting corner, but it is gathered in with ease by Boruc.
(2’) Allardyce has labelled this fixture as a ‘must win’, and his side have made a high-tempo start to proceedings. Lens - starting in a free role behind Defoe - makes a sinking run down the left, eventually cutting inside into the Bournemouth area, but the Dutchman is prevented from getting his shot off by Francis’ solid challenge.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are under way at the Stadium of Light!
Well, despite his manager taking the responsibility for a disastrous Sunderland debut, their is no place in the squad for Jan Kirchoff this afternoon, which perhaps does not bare well for the German, and it means that the visitors’ record-signing Benick Afobe, who grabbed his maiden Cherries goal last time out, will be going up against former Manchester United stalwarts John O’Shea and Wes Brown. At the other end, Jermain Defoe is in fine goalscoring form, with the former Bournemouth loanee having netted more times in the Premier League in 2016 than any other player so far. However, all of the Black Cats’ issues have come at the back, with the north-east outfit having allowed a league-high 140 shots on target against their goal this season - 22 more than any other side.
TEAM NEWS - Bournemouth substitutes: Iturbe, Federici, Distin, Murray, Grabban, Ritchie, O’Kane.
TEAM NEWS - Bournemouth (4-5-1): Boruc; Smith, Francis, Cook, Daniels; Stanislas, Gosling, Surman, Arter, Pugh; Afobe.
TEAM NEWS - Sunderland substitutes: Rodwell, N’Doye, Pickford, Coates, Yedlin, Fletcher, Watmore.
