The teams are in at the Stadium of Light. There are two changes for the hosts, with Fabio Borini replacing Danny Graham - who has left the club to join Blackburn on loan - while young goalkeeper Jordan Pickford drops down to the bench with Vito Mannone returning. There are no changes to the Bournemouth starting XI, though Howe does include Lewis Grabban in his squad after the former Norwich striker missed out last week due to injury. Let’s check on the full line-ups, starting with the hosts.
Howe’s side, meanwhile, returned to winning ways with a comprehensive 3-0 victory over struggling Norwich - goals from Dan Gosling, Charlie Daniels and Benik Afobe wrapping up the three points. They sit in 15th, four places and six points ahead of Sunderland, and could move up into 12th place if they triumph this afternoon and results elsewhere go their way. The Cherries are in great form on the road in recent weeks, having lost just one of their last five Premier League matches on their travels.
Allardyce took all the blame for Sunderland’s disastrous collapse at White Hart Lane last weekend. The Black Cats were level at half-time when the manager chose to switch to a back-three and introduced former Bayern Munich defender Jan Kirchoff, who went on to be at fault for two of Tottenham’s goals on his Premier League debut. The signs are good for the hosts today however, as they have lost just one of the seven meetings with Bournemouth in all competitions (W4 D2 L1), though that defeat came earlier this season on the south coast.
Hello ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to this live coverage of Sunderland’s clash with Bournemouth. Sam Allardyce’s side were on the end of a 4-1 thumping at the hands of Tottenham last time out, while the visitors from the south coast dispatched Norwich City 3-0 at the Vitality Stadium. Stick right here for all the action as it happens from what promises to be another fascinating encounter at the Stadium of Light.

The referee blows his whistle for the final time and the home fans erupt into a chorus of cheers! It's been a difficult few weeks for Watford, who are just about able to hold onto their slender lead to pick up their first league win since December 20th. It's fully deserved as well, as they made Newcastle pay for some sloppy defending at the start of the second half before sitting back and defending resolutely to keep the visitors' determined front line at bay. Quique Sanchez Flores looks mightily relieved, and it's no wonder why!
FULL-TIME: WATFORD 2-1 NEWCASTLE UNITED
(90’) Once again, poor heading lets down Newcastle after they're able to get themselves into a good position inside the Watford penalty area. This time it's Riviere who's the guilty player, as he does well to latch onto the end of a swinging cross from Janmaat but can only send his effort nearer to the corner flag than the goal.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Amrabat receives a loud round of applause from the home fans as he replaces Deeney to make his first appearance for Watford. ---
(90’) Mitrovic goes close! Newcastle are throwing everything they've got at the Watford defence, who are just about managing to hold on to their slender lead. The visitors earn themselves yet another corner on the right wing, which this time is sent towards the far post, but the Serbian striker's bullet header ends up bouncing just past the woodwork after he did well to beat his marker.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be four minutes of added time.
--- 89’ Substitution Meanwhile, Watford have made a more defensive-minded substitution, with Paredes making way for Nyom. ---
--- 88’ Substitution Newcastle have made a late change, and, unsurprisingly, it's an attacking one, with Riviere coming on to replace Coloccini. ---
(87’) What a chance for Capoue to wrap up the win! The Frenchman charges down the left wing on a marauding run that seems to last for an eternity, beating several Newcastle players before breaking into the penalty area. He finally skips past Janmaat before unleashing a rocket of a shot from close range, but he sends up flying over the top of the crossbar. Abdi, Ighalo and Deeney were all in excellent positions in front of goal, and they really should have been picked out by the former Tottenham man.
(85’) A dangerous cross from Janmaat almost finds the head of Sissoko, but Britos is just about able to send it out for another corner on the right flank. Shelvey sends in a similar delivery to the one that resulted in Newcastle's goal, but this time the Watford defence are just about able to deal with it before sending the ball out for a throw-in on the opposite wing.
(83’) Watford work the ball around well on the edge of the penalty area before Deeney cuts onto his right foot and unleashes a thumping shot, but it's overhit and fails to find its intended target. Abdi had a made a good run down the right and, in hindsight, the striker really should have tried to pick out the Swiss midfielder instead.
(81’) Newcastle earn themselves a corner on the left wing, which is curled into a dangerous position inside the penalty area. It's only half dealt with by Gomes, who punches the ball up into the air and kicks off an almighty battle. It bounces around the box with a plethora of players trying to get a shot away, but none are able to do so before Cathcart sends a looping header back into the hands of the Brazilian goalkeeper.
(79’) With little over 10 minutes left to play, Watford now seem to be concentrating solely on holding onto their slender lead. They are now set up in a 4-5-1 formation, and the amount of players that they have camped in the middle of the pitch is making it incredibly difficult for Newcastle to break away quickly every time they try to push forward.
(77’) Great save by Elliot! Ighalo charges into the left-hand side of the Newcastle penalty area and goes one-on-one with Lascelles, who is unable to dispossess the Nigerian. The striker beats the youngster with ease before unleashing a thumping low strike from a tight angle, but the visitors' goalkeeper does well to stick out a foot to send the shot looping over the top of the crossbar and out for a corner.
--- 76’ Substitution Jurado makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Abdi for the final 14 minutes of the game. ---
(75’) Perez flies into the right-hand side of the penalty area after being set up by a well-placed through-ball from Wijnaldum, but his first-time strike is completely mishit and ends up flying well over the top of the crossbar. Watford are starting to push further forward in an attempt to find a third goal that would surely kill off the game, but as a result they are leaving themselves far too open at the back.
(73’) Newcastle have looked far better since the introduction of Perez, who is constantly linking up well with Mitrovic inside the Watford half of the pitch. After spending so long on the front foot it is now the hosts who are having to defend in numbers, meaning that it's going to be a nervy final quarter-of-an-hour.
--- 71’ Assist That was a wonderful cross from Shelvey, who has largely disappointed this afternoon but picked out Lascelles with precision. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOAL! Newcastle are back in the game! Sissoko wins the visitors a corner on the right flank, which is curled towards the penalty spot. The young left-back is left completely unmarked by the Watford defenders, allowing him to fly up into the air before sending an excellent header bouncing past Gomes and into the right-hand corner of the net. Game on! ---
(69’) Mbemba goes close! The resulting free-kick is flung into the middle of the Watford penalty area, where it finds the defender, who rises high and does well to meet the ball. He then flicks a strong header over towards the far post, but it ends up bouncing just a yard or two wide of its intended target.
--- 68’ Yellow card Mitrovic spins round Britos near the halfway line before being dragged to the ground by the centre-back, who is shown a yellow card as a result. ---
(67’) And now Ighalo fails to take advantage of a good chance! Jurado breaks down the right wing before swinging a dangerous cross into the middle of the box, where it finds the aforementioned striker, but his jump towards the ball is mistimed and, as a result, his effort on goal ends up flying away from danger and back out to the right flank, where it can only bounce into the feet of a white shirt.
(66’) A lofted pass forward finds Deeney on the edge of the Newcastle penalty area, and he brings the ball down well before quickly teeing up Capoue. The Frenchman is in a great position 20 yards out and looks set to shoot, but his first touch is far too heavy and sends the ball bouncing into the hands of Elliot.
(64’) And now Perez goes close! Sissoko bursts down the right wing before curling a peach of a cross into the heart of the Watford penalty area. It finds the aforementioned Spaniard, who easily beats Cathcart in the air, but he messes up his header completely and ends up sending his effort well wide of the goal.
(63’) Good defending by Coloccini! Once again, Ighalo tries to fly through the Newcastle back line with a quick dart forward, but this time the Argentine defender is able to stick out a foot and stop him from doing so. If he didn't make that interception then the Nigerian surely would have had the chance to go one-on-one with Elliot.
(61’) What a chance for Gouffran! The Frenchman is immediately presented with a wonderful opportunity to pull a goal back for Newcastle thanks to a great cross from Perez, but his headed effort is far too half-hearted and, as a result, ends up flying well wide of the Watford goal. He really should have done better with that!
--- 59’ Substitution And the second is Perez, who takes the place of Saivet. ---
--- 59’ Substitution Newcastle have decided to make a double substitution. The first player to come on is Gouffran, who replaces Aarons. ---
--- 58’ Goal! GOAL! Watford have doubled their lead! The hosts win themselves a free-kick on the left wing, which is flung into the middle of the Newcastle penalty area. Elliot fails to fully deal with the danger, resulting in an almighty scrap inside the box. Ighalo, with his back to goal, is just about able to poke the ball back to Cathcart, who unleashes an almighty strike that flies past the sea of players in front of him and into the back of the net to make it 2-0. ---
--- 58’ Assist Once again, Ighalo played a vital role in the Watford goal. After a few tough games the Nigerian is looking far better today, and he looks incredibly determined to make up for lost time. ---
--- 56’ Yellow card Behrami goes down inside the Newcastle penalty area, but he's booked for diving! The Swiss midfielder breaks into the left-hand side of the box and immediately goes down whilst battling with Coloccini, but it's a poor dive that leaves the referee with no option but to show the Watford player a yellow card. ---
(55’) Ighalo charges down the left wing on a great run before going one-on-one with Coloccini, but the defender does well to stand tall and out-muscles the goalscorer before denying Deeney the chance to latch onto the loose ball. That was good defending by the Argentine, who has had a slightly mixed game thus far.
(53’) Lovely play by Capoue! The Frenchman twists and turns just outside of the Newcastle penalty area before playing a wonderful one-two with Deeney. He tries to break towards the six-yard box but has his run halted by Coloccini, who then forces the aforementioned Watford striker into sending his attempted cross a few yards over the head of Ighalo.
--- 51’ Yellow card Deeney picks up the ball near the halfway line and immediately has his heel caught by Mbemba, resulting in the defender earning the first yellow card of the afternoon. ---
(50’) Ighalo looks to be playing with far more confidence after getting on the scoresheet, and once again he gets forward well and puts the Newcastle defence under plenty of pressure. He charges down the right wing before cutting a smart pass back to Deeney, who immediately unleashes a thumping strike that ends up bouncing just wide of the near post.
(48’) Great play by Mitrovic! Newcastle quickly push forward from the restart, with the aforementioned Serbian doing well to penetrate the left-hand side of the Watford penalty area. He spins quickly before sending a bouncing cross-cum-shot towards the far post, but there's nobody there to meet it and it ends up rolling just wide of the goal.
--- 46’ Assist That was a great pick out by Deeney, who spotted the forward run of Ighalo before picking out his strike partner with a perfect pass. ---
--- 46’ Goal! GOAL! Watford have taken the lead! The Newcastle back line completely fall asleep, allowing Deeney to chip a lovely pass through the visitors' defence and into the path of Ighalo. The Nigerian latches onto the ball and flies into the penalty area before rounding Elliot, allowing him to easily tap the ball into the back of the net to give the hosts a 1-0 lead. ---
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
After starting well, Newcastle largely had to defend in the first half as Watford saw the vast majority of the ball. However, the hosts have continually failed to make their dominance of possession count, as time and time again they got themselves in good positions only to let themselves down with indecision and poor passes. Paredes and Ake have done well to get forward but have disappointed with their final balls, meaning that Ighalo and Deeney have been spectators thus far. The Hornets will need to increase the intensity if they are to beat a stubborn Newcastle defence.
(45’) Newcastle, who have spent the vast majority of the first half on the back foot, break away quickly through Janmaat, who does well to charge past Ake as the two battle for the ball. He then sends a low cross over towards Mitrovic at the far post, but it bounces through a sea of players inside the box and ends up missing the Serbian striker by two or three yards.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
(44’) Paredes breaks forward on a strong run down the right wing before he sends a bouncing pass into the feet of Ighalo. With his back to goal, the striker tries to spin round Coloccini, but the defender stands tall and easily dispossesses the striker before Newcastle kick-start a counter-attack.
(42’) Sissoko is caught sleeping on the ball, allowing Behrami to cut inside on a quick run from the left wing. He heads towards the edge of the Newcastle penalty area before going down under a block from Shelvey, but he seemed to be looking for a free kick and, as a result, he doesn't get one.
(40’) Jurado, who has arguably been Watford's best player thus far, gets forward well down the left flank before sending a well-placed through-ball into the path of Capoue. The Frenchman tries to hold up the ball near the byline but is easily dispossessed by Lascelles, who is easily able to pick the pocket of the midfielder.
(38’) Great play by Shelvey! The midfielder brings the ball down on the edge of the Watford box before breaking into the left-hand side of the penalty area. He muscles his way to the byline before firing a fantastic low cross towards goal, but there's nobody there to meet it and it misses everyone before Janmaat's follow-up cross from the right flank is defended excellently by Ake.
(36’) Risky defending by Lascelles! A risky back-pass from Janmaat doesn't have enough power behind it and fails to find Elliot, allowing Ighalo to break through on goal as he chances down the ball. He tries to beat the aforementioned youngster but is muscled away, resulting in Watford screaming for a free kick. The referee doesn't agree, however, and once again he waves play on.
(34’) Chance for Jurado! The Spaniard lifts a curling cross over to Deeney, who is left in acres of space on the right-hand side of the Newcastle penalty area. He brings it down well but takes far too long on the ball and misses his opportunity to shot, forcing him into teeing up the aforementioned winger. He then decides to strike after skipping through a sea of white shirts, but his effort on goal is overhit and clears the top of the crossbar by quite some distance.
(32’) A misplaced pass from Shelvey can only find Capoue, and once again Watford are able to throw plenty of bodies forward as they look to put Newcastle under an increasing amount of pressure. They work the ball over to Britos, who then tries to take Janmaat by surprise with a lofted pass towards Ake, but the Newcastle right-back comes out on top and does well to deal with the danger.
(30’) Capoue and Lascelles battle for the ball near the byline on the right wing, and it's the Watford midfielder who comes out on top. He quickly spins before teeing up Paredes, who is waiting patiently in a great position, but the right-back takes too long on the ball and is unable to get a cross away before he's dispossessed.
(28’) It's been a very quiet few minutes for Newcastle, who since Mitrovic's chance - arguably the best of the game thus far - have found it difficult to see much of the ball. The pressing that characterised the early exchanges has now disappeared, making it very easy for Watford to keep hold of possession inside the visitors' half of the pitch.
(26’) Watson and Jurado play a lovely series of passes between themselves in the middle of the pitch before the latter works the ball out to Paredes on the right wing. The Ecuadorian then bursts into a great run and heads straight to the edge of the penalty area before going down under a tackle from Mbemba, but once again the referee ignores the pleas from the Watford players and allows play to continue.
(24’) Excellent save by Gomes! Sissoko charges down the right wing before cutting the ball back to Wijnaldum on the edge of the Watford penalty area. The Dutchman quickly tees up Mitrovic, who latches onto the ball before unleashing a thumping low shot, but the Brazilian goalkeeper does well to stick a foot out to send the shot looping over the top of the crossbar.
(23’) Watford remain on the front foot and come back once again on another bright attacking move. This time it's Paredes who finds himself in a good position far up the pitch, but he brings a promising attack to a disappointing end with a poor long-range strike that clears the top of the crossbar by quite some distance.
(22’) A chipped pass into the right-hand side of the Newcastle box finds Capoue, who brings it down on his chest before quickly going down under a challenge from Aarons. The Frenchman throws his hands in the air and screams for a penalty but once again the referee shakes his head and waves play on, much to the frustration of the home fans.
(20’) Ighalo does well to beat Saivet in the middle of the pitch before sending the ball out to Ake on the left wing. The youngster controls it well before playing a quick one-two with Deeney just outside of the Newcastle penalty area, but Lascelles does well to get back and dispossess the left-back before he can get a cross away.
(18’) Excellent goalkeeping by Elliot! A mistake from Lascelles allows Ighalo to fly down the left wing and into the Newcastle penalty area. The striker holds up the ball well before cutting it back to Deeney, who then unleashes a curled strike from the edge of the box. The goalkeeper pulls off a great diving save to deny the Englishman before he parries away Capoue's follow-up with an even better stop.
(16’) Chance for Deeney! Watford work the ball around wonderfully well on the edge of the Newcastle penalty area before the striker cuts out to the left and unleashes a low shot, but Janmaat throws his body in front of the strike and stops it from testing Elliot.
(14’) After having suffering a tough start to the game, it is now Watford who are on the front foot. However, a terrible pass from Capoue sends the ball straight into the feet of Sissoko, who immediately breaks forward on a quick counter-attack. He charges through a sea of yellow shirts before teeing up Wijnaldum, who is in a great position on the left wing, but the Dutchman's attempted cross is mishit and fails to cause problems for the hosts' disjointed back line.
(12’) Behrami is tripped over by Saivet as the two battle for the ball deep down the left wing, resulting in a free kick for Watford in a dangerous position. Watson sends an excellent cross over to the far post, where it almost finds Ake, but the youngster goes down under a challenge and immediately screams for a penalty. The referee isn't at all convinced, however, and immediately tells the left-back to get back to his feet.
(11’) Newcastle quickly regain possession and come back once again as they look to take advantage of the bodies they still have camped inside the Watford penalty area. The ball finds its way over to Coloccini, who had drifted out to the left, but his attempted cross is poor and ends up sailing harmlessly out of play for a goal kick.
(10’) Once again, Janmaat and Sissoko link up well on the right wing, where Newcastle have been finding joy in the opening period of the game. Shelvey's curled cross from a corner won by the aforementioned Dutchman ends up finding the head of Coloccini, but the defender can't get enough power on the ball to send it near to the Watford goal.
(9’) Watford patiently make their way down the right flank, with Ighalo playing a particularly important role in the attacking move. They win themselves a throw-in near the corner flag but are quickly put under pressure by the Newcastle defence, forcing the hosts into playing the ball back towards the halfway line.
(7’) Janmaat picks up the ball on the right flank and immediately sends a lofted pass over to the opposite wing, where it finds Aarons in acres of space. The youngster brings it down well and quickly tries to take on Paredes, but the right-back stands tall and out-muscles the winger before Capoue clears the danger.
(5’) Deeney battles hard with Mbemba and charges his way towards the byline before winning Watford a corner on the right wing. It's curled into the middle of the box in an attempt to find Cathcart, but it's easily cut out by Mitrovic before it can reach the Northern Irish centre-back.
(3’) Early chance for Newcastle! Janmaat and Sissoko link up well on the right flank before the latter charges towards the byline and cuts a smart pass back to Wijnaldum. The Dutchman's first-time strike is deflected away to the edge of the Watford penalty area, where it finds Aarons, but the youngster's thumping shot ends up sailing a few yards wide of the far post. It's been a good start to the game by the visitors.
(1’) And we're off!
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, Newcastle boss Steve McClaren has made three alterations to the side that featured in the win against West Ham last weekend, with the main talking point being the inclusion of Jamal Lascelles, Henri Saivet and Rolando Aarons, all of whom are set to make their first starts of the season. Meanwhile, there’s a place on the substitutes’ bench for the forgotten figure of Sylvain Marveaux, who hasn’t featured in the Premier League since March 2014.
Quique Sanchez Flores has decided to make just one change to the Watford side that started the aforementioned defeat away to Swansea, with Allan Nyom making way for Juan Paredes at right-back.
Newcastle United substitutes: Darlow, Taylor, Marteaux, Gouffran, Riviere, Thauvin, Perez.
Newcastle United XI (4-2-3-1): Elliot; Janmaat, Mbemba, Coloccini, Lascelles; Saivet, Shelvey; Sissoko, Wijnaldum, Aarons; Mitrovic.
Watford substitutes: Pantilimon, Nyom, Prodl, Anya, Guedioura, Abdi, Amrabat.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
Recent history favours Watford, who have won the last two meetings between the teams. Just two weeks ago they met on this very ground in the third round of the FA Cup, resulting in a 1-0 victory for the Hornets, whilst earlier in the season a first-half Ighalo double guided his side to a 2-1 win at St. James’ Park. However, much has changed since August, meaning that anything could happen over the course of the next 90 minutes.
After going three games unbeaten in the middle of December - a run that saw them pick up impressive victories against both Liverpool and Tottenham - just one win from their following six games means that Newcastle also now find themselves in a difficult situation at the wrong end of the table. Swansea’s win against Watford means that the Magpies currently sit inside the relegation zone, but they will no doubt be quietly confident about their chances of winning today. A hard-fought 3-3 draw against Manchester United was followed by last weekend’s big win at home to West Ham United, and with the Hornets in such poor form, Steve McClaren’s side will feel as if a victory this afternoon is theirs for the taking.
After enjoying a wonderful start to the season that took everybody by surprise, it’s been a tough month for Watford, who head into today’s clash without a league win since Christmas nor a point in any of their last four domestic games. Monday evening’s disappointing defeat against struggling Swansea City would have been particularly hard to swallow, and to make matters worse it was the second time in as many games that the Hornets were unable to find the back of the net. Star striker Odion Ighalo, usually so prolific in the final third of the pitch, now hasn’t scored since December 28th, which has had a big and unwelcome impact on his side. With tough encounters against Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur to contend with in just two weeks’ time, today’s hosts will be desperate to pick up three big points as they aim to stop their slide down the table.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Watford and Newcastle United at Vicarage Road.

Baggies boss Pulis was bold in his changes after the interval, clearly unhappy with his side's performance in the final third from the first half, yet - despite the introduction of Anichebe, Berahino and McManaman - Albion too failed to test Bunn in the Villa goal. A point steadies the ship though after a thumping away to Southampton, and they move onto 28 points.
It finishes 0-0 then between these Midlands rivals and on the balance of play, it is probably a fair result. Villa shaded the first and second half but didn't test Foster enough in the Albion net as their woes in front of goal continue. Garde's side have now taken just three points from a possible 33 in their last 11 away games in the league and, although they now extend their run to five games unbeaten in all competitions, this is perhaps a missed opportunity for the league's bottom side.
(90’) FULL TIME! There is the whistle as West Brom and Aston Villa share the spoils in a scoreless draw at The Hawthorns.
(90’) Anichebe is sloppy in the final third for West Brom as his side look to assert some pressure near the end. His pass is straight into the path of Gil who launches a counter attack for the visitors in what is surely the last attack of the game here.
(90’) Another long-range effort here, this time from Bacuna, but his effort is wild and met by ironic cheers from the home fans. We have three minutes of added time now to end this game.
(88’) Garde's side look to keep the pressure on near the end as Vertetout stands over a free-kick midway through the Albion half. Yet his delivery is cleared by Olsson. Another frustrating set-piece in this game - which has been the story of both sides today.
(87’) Gana is the latest player to try his luck from distance, for the second time in a matter of minutes, but his effort is always rising and nestles high into the stands. A goal-kick for West Brom now.
(86’) Ayew comes up against McAuley as he carries the ball forward inside the Albion penalty area, yet he loses his footing and slips, allowing the hosts to clear. Villa's top goalscorer in the league has worked hard but not had the best of games today.
(84’) A terrific cross from Gil is whipped in low from the right towards the back-post. It zips in across goal and should be causing all sorts of danger, but Villa do not gamble to win the ball and Albion clear. A little too cautious from the visitors.
(83’) Villa are looking the more likely of the two sides to open the scoring but have scored just eight goals in 11 Premier League games under Garde since his arrival. Wil there be late drama here at The Hawthorns?
(82’) CHANCE! A stinging effort from Westwood is hit from distance, forcing Foster into a smart save down low to his left. He palms it away for a corner which Richards meets, but his header is powered over the bar at the back-post.
--- 80’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Gestede comes off for Vertetout for Villa, shortly after coming on. ---
(80’) It looks like that will be the end of the game for Gestede now as he drops to the floor inside Albion's penalty area with what appears to be a hamstring injury.
(79’) CHANCE! A real moment for Villa! The visitors break down the left through Ayew and charge forward with numbers. He has Gestede in the box to aim for but attempts a shot, only to see it blocked. Could that be a costly decision?
(77’) A decent ball from Westwood is knocked long towards Gestede, who cushions the ball down into the path of Bacuna, but the Villa midfielder cannot quite race onto it as it instead rolls into the hands of Foster.
(76’) Gil is caught late by McClean near his own corner flag as the hosts defend. He is caught on his toes by the studs of the West Brom midfielder as Garde's side win the free-kick.
(75’) Positive changes for West Brom in this second half, it has to be said, with Pulis throwing on Berahino, Anichebe and McManaman in the final third. Will his efforts pay off?
--- 74’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A final roll of the dice for Albion as McManaman comes on for Sessegnon. ---
(73’) Cissokho this time attempts an early cross towards the head of Gestede but the former Blackburn man has little space to work in under a sheet of Albion defenders, forcing him to knock his header wide.
(71’) Villa launch a counter attack through Bacuna who commits Dawson into a strong challenge inside the penalty box, forcing a corner. Yet Villa, not for the first time, fail to cause the hosts any problem from the set-play.
(70’) Sessegnon must do better there after working the angle for a cross on the right but, with bodies in the box, drags a delivery to the edge of the area and into the path of claret and blue shirts.
(68’) West Brom are a little shaky at the back as a simple cross from Westwood drops to Olsson inside his own box. He dwells on the ball and it bounces off him, into the path of Ayew, but he is slow to get his shot away and Yacob is given the chance to clear.
(67’) CHANCE! A first sight on goal here for Gestede sees his header drop just wide of the goal. It is Westwood who creates the opportunity with a wonderful half-volley driven across the box. McAuley jostles with the big Villa striker and does just enough to put him off.
(66’) Gil shows a nice pair of quick feet as he runs with the ball at the Albion defence, before playing the ball wide to Westwood. He in turn looks to work a crossing opportunity but is forced back deep.
--- 64’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A first change of the game for Villa, and a straight swap up front, as Gestede replaces Kozak. ---
--- 64’ Substitution SUBSTUTION! Rondon comes off for Anichebe in one of two changes for Pulis' side. ---
--- 64’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! And here is Berahino for Albion as he takes the place of local boy Gardner. ---
(62’) A snap-shot from Westwood is hit from distance but that does little to cause Foster danger in the Baggies goal. He has had a comfortable game so far as he makes his full recovery from injury.
(60’) Just to emphasise how tight the previous meetings between these two sides have been in the Premier League, all seven of Villa's wins against West Brom have been by a one-goal margin. All four of Albion's wins have been by - you guessed it - a one-goal margin.
(58’) Berahino is back out on the touchline, warming up from the substitutes bench. This game, although tight, is here for the taking with just the one goal enough to win this clash you feel. Will Pulis make a change?
(57’) CHANCE! What an opportunity! A rare sight on goal here in this game falls to West Brom after Dawson's cross from the right, near the byline, is knocked in towards Rondon at the near post. He is put under pressure by Villa's defence, forcing him to take it early, but he skies his effort into the stands.
(55’) We're back underway after that short stoppage, with the ball returned to Bunn in the Aston Villa goal.
(53’) Gil drops to the floor with his side in possession of the ball. He appears to have been caught a little late in a challenge with Yacob, although the collision looks fairly innocuous. The referee nevertheless stops the game for treatment.
(51’) A terrific cross from McClean is whipped in towards the back-post but West Brom do not gamble with bodies in the box, allowing Villa to clear at the second attempt. A wasted opportunity from a good delivery there.
(49’) Gardner steps up to take this free-kick and fires in a cross with real pace towards the near-post. Dawson is there to meet it although the ball comes in at such a speed it allows him little time to guide it, instead lifting his header over the bar.
(47’) A rough challenge from Richards gives West Brom the chance to cause danger early in this second half, with a free-kick right on the edge of the penalty area. Rondon wins it from an Evans throw-in after the former Man City defender flew in on the striker from behind. A daft challenge to make, especially with him already on a yellow card.
(46’) SECOND HALF! West Brom get us underway for the second period, at the second attempt, after Kozak closes down in the centre-circle a little too quickly thus ordering a re-take.
Albion have created little in the attacking third themselves and may look to introduce Berahino in the second half to spark this game into life. They could be considered a little fortunate to not have conceded a penalty against Ayew, too, for a mis-timed Olsson challenge midway through the half.
It has been another tight contest between these Midlands rivals in the first half then with the scores still all level. Aston Villa have perhaps been the greater threat in front of goal, but some sturdy Albion defending has restricted them to few real efforts on goal.
(45’) HALF-TIME! A second free-kick from Gardner on the left is sent over the bar, when he had far better options in the centre to aim for, and that marks the end of the first half here at The Hawthorns.
(44’) PANIC FROM BUNN! A shaky moment from the Villa goalkeeper comes from a free-kick as a delivery from Gardner is dropped. A host of bodies from either side scramble for the ball before Okore chases play down on the edge of the area and concedes a free-kick.
(43’) Villa are ending this half the stronger as they get numbers into the box from a cross on the right-hand side. Kozak and Richards are both up there to try and stab the ball towards goal, but Albion defend well to block and clear their lines.
--- 41’ Yellow card YELLOW! And Richards does now pick up a booking for that challenge on Yacob just minutes ago. ---
(41’) A mis-placed pass from Yacob allows Gil to break down the right, yet a cross is blocked. Villa keep the pressure on as play switches to the left and a cross from Cissokho is knocked out for a corner.
(39’) Richards can count himself a little fortunate in the Villa half as he flies into a challenge on Yacob and misses the ball completely, yet a yellow card isn't given by the officials - much to the frustration of the home crowd.
(37’) A real chance for Villa comes through Kozak as he looks to have beaten the offside trap to latch onto a ball from Gil inside the area. He rounds Foster yet, with an empty net, manages to only hit the post! Fortunately for the former Lazio man, the offside flag is raised.
(36’) Kozak does well to win the ball in the air after it is pumped long, holding up play to slide it into the path on Gil in support. The Spaniard tries to dart into a crossing position near the corner flag but he is closed down as Fletcher comes away with the ball.
(34’) McClean wins a free-kick against Gana now at the other end after the duo battle for the ball in the air. The former Sunderland man steps up to curl in a delivery from the set-piece but it drops straight into the hands of a grateful Bunn in the Villa goal.
(32’) The danger is not over yet for Albion though, who fail to clear their lines fully from the free-kick. Play eventually falls back out wide to Bacuna on the right, who cuts inside onto his left foot to fire an effort on goal from distance, only to skew it wide of the goal.
(31’) Evans concedes a cheap foul at the other end as he pushes Richards in the back, midway through his own half. Bacuna steps up to take it but his free-kick fails to beat the first man.
(29’) That's a fine cross from Sessegnon on the right who does well to work an opening on the edge of the area and fire in a low cross with pace. It zips in towards the near-post but Bunn gets down well to smother the ball.
(27’) Despite a slow start to this game, historically the Baggies may well be considered favourites on their own ground. They are unbeaten in their last five Premier League home games against their rivals, winning two and drawing three.
(25’) Berahino has started warming up on the touchline for Albion - could that be a signal that Pulis is unhappy with his side's start in this game? He scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory at Villa Park earlier this season.
(24’) It has been a strong start to this game from the visitors, who has just about edged the opening stages. There have been few clear-cut chances for either side but Villa have looked the more likely to make something happen.
(22’) PENALTY?! That's the call from Aston Villa striker Ayew as he tumbles to the ground under a challenge from Olsson. The pair race for the ball inside the Albion area and the Swedish defender makes a clumsy challenge on the former Lyon man. He appeals for a spot-kick but the officials points for a corner instead. The Baggies defender has got away with one there.
(20’) TERRIFIC DEFENDING! Garde's side build some momentum down the right-hand side as Ayew runs directly at the defence and forces Foster into a save down low. The ball comes back out to Gil who looks to clip in a ball into the path of Kozak but Dawson intercepts with a fantastic header over his own bar.
(18’) A moment of excitement for the hosts here comes from an error from Okore. He charges in on Rondon, looking to beat him to the ball in the air, but misses it completely. That sets up an attack down the left through McClean who cuts a pass to the edge of the box for Sessegnon. The 31-year-old tries a shot from distance but his effort is closed down well by Lescott.
(16’) Another poor delivery there from a set-play, this time from West Brom, as the corner is floated in towards the back-post but over the heads of everyone. It rolls out towards the touchline on the other side as Villa look to push out.
(15’) Dawson does ever so well for West Brom to create a chance out of nothing for his side, from a throw-in near the corner flag. He appears to be crowded out with limited options, but takes on Westwood with a run to the byline and forces Cissokho to block a cross out for a corner. A decent opportunity here for Pulis' side.
(13’) Garde's side have retained the same shape as their previous league clashes, with four at the back, despite suggestions he may have altered to five in defence with the introduction of Richards. The former Man City man slots in at right-back, with Bacuna pushing forward into midfield in the absence of Jordan Veretout - who is on the bench.
(11’) Good width from the hosts sees a tempting ball whipped in towards Rondon inside the six-yard box. He has plenty of bodies to jostle with inside the area but Lescott does well to get in ahead of him to clear the danger. A first real sight of goal for the Baggies.
(10’) Westwood attempts to clip in a cross towards Kozak inside the area as the visitors build pressure from the left, but Evans does well to read the game and intercept in the air. Bacuna attempts to close the ball down quickly as it drops to the left, but concedes a foul.
(8’) Neither side has settled on the ball at the minute with both conceding possession with some sloppy, mis-placed passing. A combination of slow play from Dawson and Fletcher allows Villa to steal the ball on the half-way line, but Ayew loses out on the break.
(6’) Wasted play from the visitors there from the free-kick as an initial delivery from Bacuna is headed away with ease at the back-post, before Gardner fouls Gana on the edge of the box for another foul. A second set-piece is clipped in but Villa fail to pose a threat.
(4’) Ayew does well to win a free-kick midway through the hosts' half after latching onto a pass from Kozak and bursting past McAuley with pace. He knocks the ball around the centre-half and forces the defender to bring him down.
(2’) Jeers for Lescott early on as he is closed down by Rondon in his own half, near the corner flag, and is forced to launch the ball into the stands for an Albion throw-in. He makes his first return to this stadium since leaving the Baggies for boyhood club Villa last summer.
(1’) KICK OFF! We're underway at The Hawthorns!
Of course, this may not be a Premier League fixture next season should Aston Villa succumb to relegation for the first time since 1986-87. A run of four games unbeaten in all competitions has handed the Villans a glimmer of hope, although survival is still a tall order as they remain 10 points from safety.  Albion have a strong recent record at home in this derby and will attempt to complete a league double over their rivals for the first time in 42 years.
Aston Villa make eight changes from their 1-0 win over Wycombe in their third-round replay in midweek and it looks like a change in formation for Remi Garde’s men. Captain Micah Richards keeps his place in defence which looks to unsettle the central-defensive partnership of Joleon Lescott and Jores Okore which has earned four points from their last two league games. He should be one of three central defenders in a 5-3-2 formation.
Tony Pulis makes two changes from the side that overcame Bristol City by just the one goal in their FA Cup replay on Tuesday. Chris Brunt and Victor Anichebe miss out – the former with a calf injury – while Jonas Olsson and Darren Fletcher return despite doubts over their respective hamstring and knee injuries prior to kick-off. Striker Saido Berahino has recovered from a stomach bug to make his way onto the substitutes' bench.

Hello and welcome to our LIVE commentary from the Premier League as West Brom host Aston Villa in a crunch Midlands derby near the bottom of the table. Remi Garde's side are, of course, sitting at the foot of the league and have been for some time - meaning three points is surely a must if they are to have any hope of retaining their top-flight status for next season. The Baggies, on the other hand, have won their last two home games in the league but will look to bounce back from a 3-0 thumping away to Southampton.

In the end, both sides will have to settle for a point each, and under the circumstances neither can have too many complaints. City were far from their best today but were once again saved by a fantastic performance from Aguero, who fought hard all game long and leaves Upton Park with two more well-deserved goals. However, at the back it was a completely different story, as time and time again Demichelis and Otamendi were caught ball watching, resulting in Valencia, Antonio and, in particular, Payet finding far too much joy whenever they broke forward quickly.

(90’) Jelavic goes close again! This time it's Noble who sends a looping lofted pass into the middle of the box, but it's slightly too high for the aforementioned striker, who jumps high but can't get enough power on his header send it past Hart. West Ham are getting closer...
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
--- 90’ Yellow card Toure flies into Kouyate and clumsily challenges the midfielder just outside of the West Ham penalty area, leaving the referee with no choice but to show him a late yellow card. ---
(89’) Chance for Jelavic! The second corner finds the head of the Croatian striker, who does wonderfully well to rise high above his marker, but he's unable to send his header on target and, as a result, it fails to test Hart.

City head to East London on the back of a 4-0 thrashing of out-of-form Crystal Palace, a win that keeps them firmly on the heels of Arsenal and Leicester City, both of whom sit just ahead of today’s visitors. However, away from home it hasn’t been plain sailing for the Citizens, who currently only have the ninth-best away record in the Premier League with 15 points from a possible 30. Manuel Pellegrini’s side have managed to win just two of their last eight games away from the Etihad, with just one of those - against Watford three weeks ago - coming against a team from the top half of the table. West Ham have impressed at home and are now unbeaten in their last nine Premier League encounters, meaning that it could be a difficult afternoon for the title chasers.
It’s been a great season for West Ham, who started the day in an excellent sixth place in the table, just four points away from the top-four that they desperately crave. An impressive eight-game unbeaten run was finally brought to an end by a determined Newcastle United team last weekend, but nonetheless there is still an atmosphere of positivity resonating around Upton Park. As a result, they will be looking to use that feel-good factor to pick up a win against a side that they have beaten twice in their last three meetings, including an impressive 2-1 victory at the Etihad Stadium earlier in the season. The Hammers also boast a solid defensive record after conceding just six times in their last nine Premier League outings, whilst the return of Dimitri Payet could also prove to cause City some real problems.

Since a Robin van Persie hat-trick inspired Arsenal to a 5-3 win at Stamford Bridge, Chelsea have not lost or conceded a goal against the Gunners, with five wins and three draws during that span. The Blues have become something of a bogey team for Arsene Wenger, and he has an unfortunate record when facing Guus Hiddink in the Chelsea dugout. In May 2009, during the Dutchman's first spell as Blues boss,  he dealt Arsenal their heaviest-ever league defeat at the Emirates with a 4-1 result.
Chelsea are currently languishing in 14th place, and even a victory against the Gunners won't move then up more than one spot in the table. Like Arsenal, the Blues have drawn their last two games, and come into this one having only won twice on the road all season. However, since losing to Leicester in December, Chelsea have not been defeated in Premier League action.
A win will take the Gunners back to the top of the Premier League on goal difference over Leicester City. Arsenal have won their last five home games in all competitions, but two consecutive away draws against Liverpool and Stoke have seen them drop four crucial points in what has been an incredibly tight title race.

(60’) DELIGHTFUL FROM HOWARD! The keeper reacts brilliantly to deny the improvised flick from Fabregas following an Azpilicueta cross, before Jagielka comes across to remarkably block the follow up from Pedro!
(58’) Ivanovic is having himself a nightmare in defence, with his flank being ripped to pieces by the likes of Baines and Mirallas. Chelsea have a mountain to climb and their enigmatic striker is starting to lose his temper to make matters worse.
--- 56’ Assist Baines the architect yet again, though this time there was a lot more work to be done when his cross came in. ---
--- 56’ Goal! IT'S AN ABSOLUTE STUNNER! The cross in from Baines was a bit behind Mirallas who takes a terrific first touch, swivels and sends an exquisite half-volley past Courtois and in at the near post! It's turning into a night to remember for Everton! ---
--- 55’ Substitution Long overdue change here from Hiddink. Matic and Mikel both in the team is a bit redundant and the duo were too negative in possession. The Serbian's afternoon is done, replaced by Oscar, which will push Fabregas into a deeper position. ---
(54’) DENIED BY THE WOODWORK! So sloppy from Matic in midfield as he gives the ball away cheaply, allowing Everton to break. Mirallas slides in Barkley who tries to squeeze the ball in at the near post, and has Courtois beaten, but smacks his effort against the frame of the goal!
(52’) STAT: Chelsea are unbeaten in the Premier League since Guus Hiddink took over, but have only won twice (W2, D3, L0). It is their longest unbeaten run of the season.
--- 50’ Goal! EVERTON DRAW FIRST BLOOD! Beautiful passing out of the back from Everton and Barry as they work forward into attack. Barkley holds the ball up before playing Baines through on the left. The wing-back sends in a delightful ball for Lukaku, but Terry flubs it into his own net before the striker can even arrive! ---
(48’) The teams exchange early attacks as the tempo suggests we may be in for a more lively second half. Pedro is the architect for Chelsea's, a rare contribution from him, but his cross into the middle eludes both Costa and Fabregas. At the other end, Terry is able to get a piece of Mirallas' shot to take the sting out and make for a comfortable save for Courtois.
(46’) Back underway at Stamford Bridge!
Scattered jeers rain down at Stamford Bridge as the players head to the tunnel for the break. It hasn't been as stale as the scoreline suggests, but quality has generally been lacking in the final third - especially from Chelsea. The Blues have only once forced Howard into action, through Willian, while the play of Zouma has helped keep Everton out through 45 minutes.
(45’) HALF TIME: CHELSEA 0-0 EVERTON.
(45’) There will be just one minute added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Everton remain in possession as we approach the interval, though there are plenty of Blue shirts back in defence as the hosts try to ensure we head to the break at nil-nil. These home fans don't exactly appreciate how this first half has played out.
(41’) STAT: Chelsea have conceded 31 times in their opening 21 matches this season, their highest ever total in a Premier League season at this stage.
(39’) SENSATIONAL FROM MIRALLAS! The Belgian with an incredible turn in midfield to get beyond his marker and cut onto his right. He darts across with real pace before driving a wonderful strike at goal, but Courtois gets across so quickly to get a hand to it and deny his fellow countryman!
(37’) A rare attack from the hosts results in a corner for them, though Willian's delivery sums up the match as a whole to this point as it runs out of play before swinging back out into the danger area. Boos rain down at Stamford Bridge.
(35’) Everton have been the exact opposite of static in attack, with everyone interchanging positions and offering great runs off the ball to open up space in the final third. The terrific defending of Zouma is all that has prevented Chelsea from falling behind up to this point.
(33’) Pedro has been very poor for Chelsea, unable to offer any sort of outlet down the right flank. As a result it has made Chelsea very one dimensional going forward. They are far too static off the ball as well.
(31’) Barkley is really growing into the game and starting to enjoy himself a great deal in possession. The game has tilted dramatically in Everton's favour and it's reached the point where you could hear a pin drop at Stamford Bridge.
(29’) STAT: Everton have lost just one of their 10 Premier League away games this season (W3, D6, L1). Only Crystal Palace (eight) have conceded fewer than the nine goals allowed by the Toffees on their travels this season.
(27’) One touch too many from Mirallas, who holds onto the ball too long and misses the opportunity to send Barkley through on goal. Everton are starting to send an extra body or two into attack as they sense a real opportunity to jump out ahead at Stamford Bridge.
(25’) Lukaku is winning the battle between the two strikers thus far, seeing more of the ball and proving more of a nuisance for the opposition's back line. Chelsea have been quite underwhelming in attack, with Willian the only bright spot going forward thus far.
(23’) VITAL AGAIN FROM ZOUMA! Lukaku shrugs off Terry far too easily and then works a quick one-two with Mirallas to send him through on goal, but Zouma sprints across to provide just enough cover to force the ball to run to Courtois.
(21’) Everton put together a pair of teasing counters, but neither amount to much. The first of which is sniffed out well by Zouma, before Lennon's final effort drifts wide, while Lukaku scuffs his shot from 20 yards out on the most recent attack. Still, encouraging signs for the Toffees.
(19’) STAT: This is Roberto Martinez’s 250th Premier League match as a manager, and his next defeat with bee his 100th in the top flight (W77, D73, L99).
(17’) CRUCIAL FROM HOWARD! Chelsea break with terrific pace following Everton's squandered free kick. Willian is sprung through in the left channel and has a good effort at goal from in close, but Howard reacts smartly to get his hands up and knock it behind for a corner!
(15’) That's what Everton need more of! Leighton Baines gets forward for the first time on the overlap, and makes a positive contribution as he's tripped up by Fabregas near the touchline. The Toffees can create something from the ensuing free kick.
(13’) Neither side has mustered an attack yet, with both Courtois and Howard hardly having a touch on the ball up to this point. Both sides are being afforded time in midfield to pass the ball around, but are being smothered when they look to transition into attack.
(11’) There hasn't been much tempo adopted by this match through the first 10 minutes. Both sides are putting an emphasis on keeping their shape off the ball and it has really plagued the flow of the game from a neutral standpoint.
(9’) Zouma shows great pace to bail out Ivanovic who had been beat by a long ball over the top. The right-back appears to have no interest getting into a foot race these days and if the early stages are any indication, there could be plenty of space for Mirallas out wide this afternoon.
(7’) STAT: No side has lost more points from leading positions this season than Chelsea (12 - level with Bournemouth and Newcastle). They only dropped 15 throughout the entirety of 2014/15.
(5’) Perhaps not surprisingly it has been a timid start from both teams at Stamford Bridge, with neither side looking particularly keen on taking risks. Willian offers the only piece of direct, attacking play, but his attempted through ball for Fabregas is sniffed out capably by Jagielka.
(3’) Everton keep the bulk of possession inside the first few minutes, but the bulk of it comes at the back. There will be plenty of eyes on John Stones today amidst constant speculation of a move to Chelsea in the summer, after the Blues pursued him heavily this past offseason.
(1’) Chelsea get this game underway on a cold day in west London!
The players make their way out onto the pitch, lead by skipper John Terry who makes his 700th club appearance today. It's not the most energetic atmosphere at Stamford Bridge but that can change should Chelsea get off to a high-flying start.
Three changes to the Toffees side made by Roberto Martinez from their draw at the Etihad midweek. Bryan Oviedo returns to the starting lineup, allowing John Stones to return to his natural position at centre-half, which forces Ramiro Funes Mori to the bench. Aaron Lennon and Kevin Mirallas are also brought back into the team, starting on the flanks at the expense of Gerard Deulofeu and Leon Osman. Tom Cleverley returns to the substitute's bench following a spell in the training room with an ankle injury, though Seamus Coleman and James McCarthy remain out.
With Eden Hazard and Radamel Falcao still injured, boss Guus Hiddink makes just the one change to his starting lineup following their draw with West Brom. Nemanja Matic comes into midfield to partner John Obi Mikel, pushing Cesc Fabregas into a more advanced role and Oscar to the bench. Pedro keeps his place despite speculation he would be dropped after another poor outing against the Baggies.

EVERTON (4-3-3): Howard; Oviedo, Stones, Jagielka, Baines; Barkley, Barry, Besic; Lennon, Mirallas, Lukaku.

Everton showed great resistance in holding Manchester City to a draw on Wednesday, a truly encouraging sign for a Toffees side that had been leaking goals previously. Roberto Martinez will still have his sights set on a place in Europe next season, but their prospects are not looking particularly great at the moment. Consistency has been their biggest issue, but there’s no denying they have the talent at Goodison Park to compete for a top six finish if they can find a way to put all facets of their game together.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Everton’s trip to Stamford Bridge to take on a Chelsea side hoping to maintain their unbeaten run. Things appear to be looking up for the Blues under Guus Hiddink, and although they stumbled in a draw with West Brom midweek, their performance merited more. They still have quite a bit of ground to make up before they can even consider a top six finish, but the goal for them right now will be to continue their upward trend and pick up the pieces following a tumultuous end to Jose Mourinho’s tenure.

As easy as it comes then for City as they grab four goals to temporarily storm into first place in the Premier League. They were quiet for their usual standard in the first half relying on deflected efforts from Delph and Aguero to give them a 2-0 lead at the break. Yet they took full control of the second period and dominated play against a sorry Palace side as the Argentine scored his second - and City's third - before playing in Silva for a tap-in six minutes from time.
(90’) FULL TIME! That's the end of the game as City storm to a comfortable 4-0 win.
(90’) Cabaye is coming close to a second yellow card in a matter of second here as he collides with De Bruyne and gives the City man a shove. The referee simply gives him a talking to, but on another day he could have been off for two yellows.
--- 90’ Yellow card Yellow card Yohan Cabaye ---
(90’) Two minutes of added time have been given.
(87’) Palace just haven't produced any form in recent weeks and this has been a real beating away to City. Four goals conceded, no real threat at the other end, and this is now their fifth league game without a win, or a goal.
--- 85’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Aguero comes off now to a standing ovation as Navas replaces him for the final moments. ---
--- 85’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! An alteration for Palace now sees Zaha come off for Chung-Yong Lee. ---
--- 84’ Goal! GOAAAAL! And there is the fourth goal! Souare gives the ball away in the City half as the visitors attack, allowing Pellegrini's side to break with pace. Aguero drives past the half-way line and past Ward, with just the keeper to beat. He could have his hat-trick but instead squares to Silva for a tap-in. ---
--- 84’ Assist Unselfish play from Aguero there who could have easily burried that to bag his hat-trick. Yet, whereas many strikers would have done just that, he ensured Silva got in on the act for a simple finish. ---
(82’) Silva wins a free-kick after he is tripped up by Ledley, which Toure steps up to take. But his effort on goal, just to the right of the penalty area, is hit into the wall. No fourth goal yet, it seems.
--- 80’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! McArthur is replaced by Mutch in an alteration for Pardew's side, with 10 minutes to play. ---
(79’) A chance for a fourth goal for City from a corner on the left-hand side is wasted by Silva, who steps up to take their fifth of the game, only to curl his delivery straight out of play for a goal-kick.
(77’) City start a counter attack after Palace give the ball away in the opposition half, yet as the action spills out wide to De Bruyne on the right, his cross into the box falls is cleared before the visitors win a foul on the edge of their own area.
(75’) A powerful drive from Cabaye is hit with real venom from distance as the ball is played into him from the left. Hart is forced to cover all angles with that one as it rises just over the bar. Fine hit from the France international.
(73’) Silva looks to pile on the misery for Palace at the back with City now in full control but, inside the area, he cuts a shot across goal which rolls out for a goal-kick. Palace will have to be careful not to concede further here.
--- 71’ Yellow card YELLOW! Chamakh is booked for diving as Palace grow frustrated. ---
(70’) That third goal is undoubtedly the pick of the bunch here today as Aguero finishes off a fine flowing move. They didn't have to work hard for the first two, but they picked Palace off at ease for that one.
--- 68’ Goal! GOAAL! That's three goals and the three points for City! Some lovely play inside the box opens up the Palace defence as Aguero knocks the ball into Toure just on the edge. He could shoot, but plays it once more to De Bruyne. He, too, could shout but he squares is back to the Argentine to tap in from yards out. ---
--- 68’ Assist Unselfish play there from De Bruyne, who has largely been quiet in this clash so far, but choses the right option as he pulls a cross back to Aguero for the simplest of goals. ---
(68’) A rather robust challenge on Silva is made by Cabaye and Ward right under the noses of Pellegrini on the touchline, but the officials wave play on as a throw-in is instead given.
--- 66’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! An alteration for Palace - their first of the game - as Chamakh comes on for WIckham. ---
(63’) Much, much better from Palace in the final third and again the play is developed through Zaha. He links up well with Ward, combining on the edge of the box as he darts into the area looking for the return. But the Eagles full-back has other ideas and tries an effort of his own, which whistles just wide of the post.
(61’) Fernando hacks away at the feet of Wickham in a clever foul on the half-way line as the Eagles look to break on the counter attack. Palace are searching for a yellow card there in what is quite obviously a professional foul, but none is given by the officials.
(59’) Just under an hour gone then and it has been easy for City so far, just as it was in the first half. The Eagles haven't won away to the Manchester club for 26 years since a 2-0 victory in December 1990 - a game in which Alan Pardew played in - and this looks set to continue given the evidence so far.
--- 57’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Iheanacho is replaced by Yaya Toure just before the hour mark. ---
(56’) Zabaleta gets forward in the final third for City after a pass inside from Delph. He looks to play an early cross but it is hit far too close to Hennessey who comes out and claims.
(54’) HANDBALL!? Half-hearted claims from the Palace end for a penalty inside the area there! It would have been harsh, in truth, had it been given as a cross from the left is cleared by Fernando and out for a corner - off the hand of Demichelis. He was unaware of the ball there though with his arms down by his side and his back facing goal.
(53’) A fairly innocuous injury there for Kolarov with no challenge going in on him. City will hope it is not too serious though as he is stretched off the pitch.
--- 52’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! And finally there is the change as Kolarov comes off for Clichy. ---
(51’) A little bit of confusion here now as Kolarov drops to the floor carrying an injury. Pardew is not happy on the sidelines as the physio comes on to offer support to the City defender.

(47’) De Bruyne has been a little quiet in this game so far but is back on the ball on the right-hand side, trying to work his way into the penalty area. He drives with the ball at Souare before trying to knock a cross into the box, but it is deflected out for a thrown-in near the corner flag.
(45’) SECOND-HALF! We're back underway for the final 45 minutes of this clash.
Two goals then for City and they are in full control at the interval. They haven't had to work too hard for the goals with both coming from long-range effort that have deflected into the net. Palace will have to work hard to get themselves back into this one.
(45’) HALF-TIME! That's the whistle for the interval at the Etihad Stadium after one minute of stoppage time.
(45’) A couple of half-chances here for Aguero, looking to add to his tally, as City end this half on top. The first of which sees Dann forced into a smart block inside the box, deflecting the ball out for a corner. It is swung in and eventually finds it's way to the Argentine once more at the back-post. He swivels and strikes on goal but it rises over the bar.
(43’) A perfect time to score for Pellegrini's side, right before the half-time whistle, and they now hold a comfortable two-goal lead. It looks like Palace's terrible run against the hosts will continue today - this will be their seventh defeat in eight in the Premier League.
--- 41’ Assist Iheanacho claims the assist there with Palace again guilty of failing to close down quick enough and leaving a player of Aguero's calibre free, and unmarked, on the edge of the area. Slack defending from Pardew's side. ---
--- 41’ Goal! GOAAAL! City have doubled their lead just before the break! Iheanacho cuts in from the left to slip in an unmarked Aguero on the edge of the box. He isn't closed down and is allowed to shoot from distance yet gets a huge slice of fortune as his shot deflects of Dann and into the bottom corner of the net. ---

Ward tries to keep tight to Silva but the Spaniard skips past him inside the area to knock the ball along to Aguero. He tries to stay on his feet after a challenge from Ledley and just about manages to get his shot away which zips across the goal. Pellegrini's side might have had a penalty shout there though but for the honesty of the City striker.
(35’) A little tight around the edge of the box for City there as they combine down the right-hand side with some close passing. De Bruyne feeds the ball into Aguero on the edge of the box but he is a weak in his hold-up play. Cabaye is there to poke the ball away from behind.

(32’) Strong hands again from Hart with a fine save down to his left. Delph is the man who gives the chance away, fouling Cabaye on the edge of the box. The former PSG man steps up to hit the free-kick and curls it towards the bottom right-hand corner only for the City keeper to palm it out for a corner.
(30’) The City fans have perked up now since taking the lead and have seen their side control most of the play. Palace are certainly not out of this though and have the ability to remain a threat on the counter attack. They haven't, however, scored a league goal since Lee Chung-yong's winner at Stoke before Christmas.
(28’) Zaha concedes a sloppy free-kick for a foul against Kolarov, tripping the City full-back up as he breaks into the visitors' half. A delivery is swung in only for Dann to clear, before a second attempt from Silva is blocked on the re-bound.
(26’) That City goal is a little against the run of play based on the early exchanges here. They hadn't tested Hennessey once prior to the Delph goal and may have got a bit lucky with the finish as the Palace keeper should have had his near-post covered. He cost his side dearly in defeat to Aston Villa in midweek, dropping the ball into the net, and will be unhappy with that one again.
(24’) ALMOST A HOWLER! That could have been much worse for Hart! The City keeper saves a routine header from Dann after a Palace corner but, as he looks to clear long, hits his pass straight into the back of McArthur on the edge of the box. The ball drops to Delaney who tries to lift an effort into the net but his shot, on the slide, is just over!
--- 22’ Goal! GOAAAAL! Finally, a moment of quality from City as they take the lead! Delph is the man who scores it, carrying the ball forward on the edge of the box and unleashing a shot from distance. It may take a slight deflection off Delaney as it squeezes in past Hennessey at his near-post. ---
--- 22’ Assist It is Silva who picks up the assist there with a simple pass to his left to the feet of Delph. Palace were guilty of not closing down the England man quick enough there as he had acres of space and time to think about that shot. ---
(21’) City fans haven't had a lot to shout about in the first 20 or so minutes here and, as Silva attempts a long-range strike from distance, that looks set to continue. His effort floats high and wide over the bar and gives Hennessey no trouble.
(19’) That's a waste again from City in the final third and, not for the first time today, it is Silva who mis-judges the pass. (17’) After that period of passing play for Palace, a long all is pumped forward but there is no runner on the end of it as City regain play with the goal-kick. The hosts need to increase their tempo here, you feel, as both their movement on and off the ball is slow.
(16’) Palace are passing the ball around nicely at the back with City allowing them the time and space to move with the ball. There is very little pressure here from the hosts in the final third with the crowd at the Etihad a little subdued at the minute.

(4’) Delaney should perhaps be scoring there, but he powered his header straight at the City keeper. It would have been a perfect start for Pardew's men, who have only won one in seven meetings with the hosts in the Premier League - losing six.
(3’) FINE SAVE BY HART! That is a fantastic save from the England stopper! City hadn't cleared their lines fully from that corner with Palace keeping the pressure on from outside the box. It is played wide to Wickham who floats a cross in towards Delaney but his header from yards out his palmed away from goal!
(2’) A first corner of the game drops to the visitors, which is floated in towards the edge of the box by Cabaye to Dann, but City head the ball away from danger.
(1’) KICK OFF! Palace get the game underway, playing from right to left.

It’s at City where our attention is focused this afternoon though as Manuel Pellegrini's side look to bounce back from a frustrating 0-0 draw with Everton in midweek with a victory. They face a Crystal Palace side, meanwhile, who are searching for a positive result on the back of defeat at Aston Villa. Full time at St. James' Park. Newcastle  secure a MASSIVE win in the Barclays Premier League as they eventually run out narrow 2-1 winners over West Ham in this fiery Saturday afternoon clash. The home sides were terrific in the first half and went into the break 2-0 thanks to goals from Ayoze Perez and Georginio Wijnaldum, with Jonjo Shelvey really impressing in his debut for the Magpies. Slaven Bilic's men improved after the break and clawed a goal back through Nikica Jelavic, but Steve McLaren can finally breath a sigh of relief as his charges hold on for the three points. Terrific game! Thanks for joining us - see you next time!

--- 90’ +2 Yellow card The referee is perhaps going to add even more time on now as Rob Elliot is booked between the sticks for Newcastle for taking too much time over goal kicks. We can only presume it was incidents like this which is which so much time was added on? ---
(90’) The Newcastle boss is FURIOUS at the moment as the referee has signaled an extremely generous SIX minutes of extra time to be played! Where on earth has the official got that from?! West Ham's tails are up at that news for sure!
(88’) JELAVIC!!! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT?! Steve McLaren's heart is in his mouth in the dugout as the Croatia international collects the ball deep at the back post before sending a lovely half volley spiralling towards goal! Elliot was struggling to get there, but he is let off the hook as the attempt flashes just north of the crossbar! What a grandstand finish we are having here!
(86’) Shelvey has enjoyed a very solid debut for his new side today, particularly in the first half, but has finally succumbed to the perhaps ill-advised urges from the home crowd and went for a long-range shot on goal, despite the pass to the wing being the better option. Up until now, he has made the correct decisions in the final third of the pitch, but not on this occasion!
(84’) The St. James' Park faithful rise out of their seats in expectancy as Wijnaldum strives to get on the end of a loose ball through into space and go on one-on-one with the keeper, but Adrian is proactive in coming off his line and JUST manages to get there before the Dutchman to clear high up the park!
(82’) West Ham are really running out of time to save their afternoon here, but as time goes on, the Newcastle fans will probably get increasingly more nervous. The Hammers just need to take advantage of the nerves of the hosts and keep them camped inside their own half for the last 10 minutes!
--- 80’ Substitution Third and final alteration from Newcastle now as Steve McLaren adds some fresh legs on to the park for the final portion of the match. Coming on is Yoan Gouffran and he will replace Ayoze Perez, who opened the scoring this afternoon with that lovely, curled fnish into the corner! ---
(78’) SITTER FROM MITROVIC! Shelvey sees a rare portion of possession in this second half and takes advantage of the space ahead of him to move into the final third and thread a lovely pass into the feet of the Serbian, who cleverly cuts inside past the defender before moving one-on-one with the keeper, but his final shot on goal is tamely struck into the arms of the grateful Adrian! McLaren is furious on the touchline!

Coming off is Tomkins and he'll be replaced by Carl Jenkinson, who will add a little more penetration down that right wing, so perhaps the West Ham boss is aimed to exploit the wings to try and get some joy. ---
(74’) It is no wonder the Newcastle fans are giving their players pelters at the moment, as they are just taking so many daft decisions at the back! West Ham have enjoyed a superb season this year and are on the brink of potentially qualifying for the Champions League should they put together a good run of form in the second half of the campaign and finish in the top four. Today presents a tough task, though as they have won just one of their last 12 league trips to St James Park , having failed to score in three of their last four.
Newcastle found themselves in a similarly gloom situation this time last season, and are once again battling against returning to the Championship after a few years. They do have fairly fond memories of West Ham travelling to St. James' though, as in the corresponding fixture last year they came out 2-0 winners to avoid going down on the very last game of the season. They have, however, failed to score in five of their last seven Premier League games against the Hammers.
That result may indeed be cause for optimism for the Magpies, but they are still coming off of a fairly tumultuous festive period, in which they were defeated 1-0 in four straight games by Everton, West Brom, Arsenal, and Watford, in a run that stretched from Boxing Day. They are still one point from safety down near the bottom of the table, but will have received another boost this week with the signings of Jonjo Shelvey from Swansea and Henri Saivet from Bordeaux, with the spending seemingly going to continue.
Steve McLaren and Slaven Bilic should be relatively content with the fact that their squads should be heading into today's encounter with some boosted confidence, as they are both coming off very positive results from the midweek round of fixtures a few days ago. Newcastle came back from two goals down to earn a respectable 3-3 draw at home to Manchester United, while West Ham also came from behind to record an impressive 3-1 away victory away at Bournemouth.
In terms of reputation within English football, the two sides featuring today have a fairly similar standing in recent years. However, this season they find themselves at opposite ends of the league table, with Newcastle riding high in 5th – just one point of the last Champions League place, while Newcastle face another battle against the drop down in 19th.

(82’) STAT: Aston Villa have won only four of the 19 Premier League match ups with Leicester (D8, L7), but they have won three of the last four at Villa Park (W3, L1).
(80’) Into the last 10 minutes and it's poised for a grandstand finish at Villa Park. A point doesn't do a whole lot for either teams, so it will be interesting to see how these two sides approach these final stages. Will they go for the win?

--- 76’ Yellow card Huth is booked for protesting, though it's not entirely clear what had the defender so upset in the first place. ---

(73’) STAT: Aston Villa have 11 points through 21 matches, a number no club has ever managed to avoid relegation with. West Brom had 12 at this stage in 2004/05 but managed to survive.
(71’) VITAL FROM BACUNA! Vardy is sprung into space down the right and he picks out a delicious ball for Ulloa in the centre. The substitute's eyes light up as he thinks he has all the time in the world to set himself, but Bacuna sprints back and steps in from behind to break up the move!

(67’) Easy again for Schmeichel! The keeper has been worked in this second half, but again he's not forced into the most difficult save as Ayew's strike is sent straight into the keeper's waiting arms at the near post.
(65’) Villa have really picked up their performance in this second half and are bossing possession over the last 15 minutes. (63’) STAT: Leicester have already claimed two more points this season (43) than they managed throughout the entirety of last season (41).
(61’) PENALTY APPEALS DENIED! Westwood plays an inviting ball into the area, though Huth was always favoured to win it. (58’) EXCELLENT ROUTINE! Straight from the training ground as Leicester play a short corner to Mahrez, who returns it to Fuchs, and the left-back tees up Drinkwater atop the area. The midfielder's first-time shot is a great one, but Bunn is able to tip it over the bar.

(54’) The current predicament plays right into the hands of Leicester. Villa are managing a good period of sustained pressure, but that's exactly the type of situation the Foxes thrive off as it sets them up perfectly for the counter.
(52’) BEATEN AWAY BY SCHMEICHEL! Cissokho has been getting forward consistently down the left flank early in this second half, but his final ball has been lacking up to this point. (50’) STAT: Claudio Ranieri won both games as Monaco manager against Remi Garde and Lyon when the duo were in Ligue 1 in 2013/14.
(48’) Energetic start from Villa who look to send bodies forward. Just a single point doesn't do a whole lot for them, so we should expect to see Remi Garde throw caution to the wind in the hopes of turning this around.
