Shinji Okazaki has Leicester back atop the Premier League table the way things stand, but the Foxes should have a more comfortable lead to take with them into the break if Riyad Mahrez could have converted from the spot. (45’) HALF TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-1 LEICESTER CITY.
(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Fuchs thinks a cross in is going to be dealt with and he turns his back on the play, but it winds up going behind off him for a cheap corner. (41’) STAT: Aston Villa have conceded the first goal in 16 of their 22 Premier League matches this season, the most of any team in the top flight. They have kept just three clean sheets in the league all season.
(39’) STRAIGHT AT SCHMEICHEL! Struck well by Cissokho, who has a sight at goal from 25 yards out and opts to test his luck. The effort it a good one, but it's too close to the keeper to cause him any problems.
(37’) The wave of momentum Villa managed to pick up from that penalty save has been suffocated by Leicester, who are doing an excellent job of taking the sting out of the match. They're passing it around patiently in midfield and hardly affording the hosts a look at goal.
(35’) The Holte End is making plenty of noise now as the tempo starts to pick up. Villa have a spring in their step and Vertout does well to win a free kick with some determined running in midfield before being tripped up by Albrighton.

(33’) BUNN SAVES! It's way too close to the centre from Mahrez, and the keeper guesses the right way to keep it out! There's life in this crowd once again.

(26’) Leicester are the more positive team in possession, but they aren't exactly committing bodies forward. They don't have the same pace and killer instinct we are used to seeing from them in attack, with Villa doing well to keep their shape at the back.
(24’) There is absolutely no pace in this match. It's a slow, tight-knit encounter with very little tempo to speak of. (22’) Well I said the outcome would likely be determined by which team makes fewer mistakes, and both sides come close to conceding first through careless errors. Bunn's intervention on Vardy could have proved costly, while Huth nearly gifted Villa the opener. It remains a cagey affair otherwise.
(20’) SCHMEICHEL TO THE RESCUE! Huth was the hero midweek against Spurs, but he's nearly the villain here as a horrendous back-pass gifts Kozak a clean break, but the striker is denied by the outstretched paw of Schmeichel!
(18’) STAT: Aston Villa have scored just five first half goals this season, a league low. They have not scored earlier than the 40th minute in a Premier League game since September (against Leicester).
(16’) Kante's positioning in midfield has been superb. He covers so much ground, the Frenchman, and leads the Premier League at this stage of the season in tackles (85) and interceptions (83).
--- 14’ Yellow card WHAT WAS HE THINKING?! Vardy was always going to be first to the ball, yet Bunn rushes well out of his area to try and clear the threat and winds up taking the forward to ground. Luckily for him the forward was running away from goal so he escapes with just a yellow. ---

(11’) The stale start continues at Villa Park. Leicester aren't your typical top three team. The Foxes don't want, nor do they need, a ton of possession. They are comfortable with sitting back and waiting for their opportunity to pounce.
(9’) Kozak taken by surprise! Vertout whips an inviting delivery into the area which Ayew flicks on into the path of the striker. The Czech forward tries to control with his chest, but a heavy touch sees the ball run away from him and Leicester clear the threat.
(7’) STAT: Leicester have kept three clean sheets in a row in the league for the first time since May 2015 – they have never kept four consecutively in the Premier League.
(5’) Neither side looking to take many risks in the early going, comfortable sitting deeper in defence and looking to hit back on the counter. If these first five minutes are any indication, we could be in for a tedious match at Villa Park - coming down to which side makes fewer mistakes.
(3’) It has been quite the cagey start to the match with possession changing hands on several occasions in midfield. Villa look a bit edgy early on as they try and work out the nerves. Every game for them is a massive one given their place in the table.
(1’) And we're off at Villa Park!

(90’) FULL TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-1 MANCHESTER UNITED.
(90’) Henderson's delivery has a bit too much behind it, allowing Smalling to win the header and clear United's lines. It's not looking good now for Liverpool!
(90’) Through one of the three minutes of added time now and Liverpool win the free kick they wanted following a Blind handball. They send everyone forward into the area as Henderson stands over to take it.

(89’) WAS THAT THE CHANCE?! Ibe makes a strong run and pulls the ball back for Milner who drives a shot at goal. It deflects straight into the path of Firmino who sends a weak, half-hearted effort at goal as he though he was offside - but the flag stayed down!
(87’) So many white shirts back in defence for United. It has become incredibly congested in the Kop end, making it that much harder on Liverpool to try and negotiate an opening. They have to start playing more direct and sending the ball into the box every chance they get, hoping for a deflection or a lucky bounce.
(85’) United are doing their best to take the sting out of the match, attempting to slow the tempo every time they get in possession. Liverpool need to adopt a greater sense of urgency because they are five minutes plus stoppage time away from walking away empty handed despite a dominating performance.
(83’) Successive corners won by Liverpool as they commit men forward in an attempt to salvage something from the match. Benteke is able to win a header in the area, but neither scramble sees the ball directed towards goal before United finally clear their lines.

(80’) STAT: Liverpool have scored beyond the 90th minute in two of their last three Premier League matches at Anfield to salvage a point (Divock Origi and Joe Allen).

(70’) STAT: Juan Mata has scored three goals and assisted four more in his last six Premier League appearances against Liverpool.
(68’) MAGIC FROM DE GEA! That is absolutely world class from the keeper! Incredibly quick reactions on display as he dives well across to his right and shows his strong wrists as he does just enough to keep out Can's bullet from range after a very poor clearance attempt from Darmian.
--- 66’ Substitution Van Gaal makes the first move, and it's a necessary switch from the Dutchman who brings on Juan Mata with Lingard giving way. ---
--- 65’ Yellow card Smalling is beaten for pace by Firmino and is forced into a cynical tug of the Brazilian's shirt, which sees him into the referee's book. ---
(64’) As we continue to pass through this cagey period, it becomes ever more clear what both teams need off the bench. United could use a creative central figure, with Herrera offering no inventiveness at the moment. They could also use a greater presence out wide with Lingard failing to get the job done. Liverpool need more of a physical presence in attack, someone to hold the ball up and wait for support - a la Christian Benteke.
(62’) Substitutes up and running for both teams as the two managers sense the need to make a change. The match has become increasingly stale, and from Klopp's perspective he will not be happy with the momentum United have generated over the last 10 minutes of so.
(60’) STAT: Manchester United have won six of their last eight Premier League meetings with Liverpool (L2) and two of the last four at Anfield (W2, D1, L1).
(58’) United with a penalty shout this time! Martial is so dangerous with the ball at his feet, able to navigate his way through such tight areas. He again picks up possession inside the box and goes to ground shortly after following a challenge, but Clattenburg was positioned well to make the call. And the replay shows Sakho did get a touch on the ball.
(56’) MUCH BETTER! Borthwick-Jackson sends an inviting ball into the area from the left, but Rooney flubs at it. Martial picks up the loose ball in the area and dribbles straight towards the byline, before driving a shot across the face of goal and just beyond the far post!

(52’) VITAL FROM DE GEA! More great play from Lallana to slide through Can into the area. The German midfielder has a clean sight at goal, but De Gea comes off his line and gets just enough of the final shot to deflect it beyond the far post!
(50’) STAT: Wayne Rooney is looking to score in four successive games for Manchester United for the first time since March 2012.
(48’) Liverpool pile the pressure on early but can't pick out a final ball. He picks out Martial, but the Frenchman is far too indecisive in providing a return pass as the chance goes begging.

Scoreless at Anfield as we head into the break, but Liverpool are well on top based on the run of play. They're asking many more questions of the United defence with their crisp, incisive passing and have come very close to the breakthrough goal on a few occasions. The visitors have struggled to combat the high pressing of the Reds, lacking the quality to pass their way through the spaces in midfield.

(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.

(37’) STAT: Liverpool have lost 11 times at home to Manchester United, more defeats than against any other visitor in the Premier League era.
(35’) United have managed to ride out the latest wave of Liverpool pressure. All it takes is one counter or set piece for the visitors and this stadium could become deflated awfully quick.
(33’) Liverpool are certainly on top at the moment and the crowd is fully behind them. United have done precious little in possession, and have been generally too static in attack. (27’) STAT: Louis van Gaal inflicted Jurgen Klopp’s biggest defeat as Dortmund manager in September 2009 when his Bayern side won 5-1 away at the Signal Iduna Park.

Can is dispossessed in midfield and the ball is sent forward to Rooney, but the striker is blocked off by Lucas who sends the ball back the other way. Milner gets it in a similar position, but he too is lacking in support and fails to keep possession.

(21’) With the exception of the Lallana chance, this match has been sorely lacking in quality thus far. It has been an incredibly tense and scrappy affair, which was to be expected, despite United boss Louis van Gaal suggesting it would be an open contest full of attacking quality.
(19’) The foul count continues to rise, but the ball is being predominately contained in midfield. Lucas' inclusion in the starting lineup has been justified through the opening 20 minutes as he remains responsible in possession but, most importantly, has helped disrupt United's rhythm on the ball.
(17’) STAT: Only Everton v Liverpool (20) has seen more red cards than this fixture in Premier League history (16).
(15’) Tempers boil over! Fellaini gets perhaps a bit over-aggressive with Milner and Lucas right up against the touchline, directly in front of the Liverpool fans. (13’) It is just starting to open up a bit, with Liverpool seeming especially buoyed by their previous chance. Milner is played in along the right and he sends a half-volley at goal, but fails to hit the target. The Reds are starting to press high up the pitch again with United in possession, a favoured tactic of Klopp.
(11’) NEARLY THE OPENER! Lucas sends a delightful ball over the top for Lallana to chase. Firmino arrives on the follow up, but he sends his shot off the outside of the far post and behind for a goal kick!

(77’) Campbell tries to drive at pace through the heart of the hosts' defence, but the Costa Rican is brought down by a cynical challenge. The resulting set-piece deliery is angled towards Giroud, but Butland claims easily. The Stoke goalkeeper tries to release Arnautovic with a long kick out of his hands, but the ball skids right through to Cech at the other end.
(75’) Bellerin tries to break to the byline and whip in a cross, but Diouf tracks back and slides in to deny the Spanish right-back brilliantly. Stoke then look to get down the right-hand side themselves, but attempted link up play between Johnson and Walters is denied simply by Monreal.
(74’) Arsenal win a free kick on the right-hand side, but Shawcross rises highest to clear the looping delivery away from danger. The visitors maintain their pressure, but a long-range strike from Oxlade-Chamberlain is charged down, before a curling cross makes its way in the from left! Campbell threatens to get on the end of it, but Pieters hacks away!
--- 72’ Substitution Walcott takes his leave for the away side, with young Iwobi coming into the mix for the final 20 minutes. ---
(72’) Play is shifted out to the left-hand side, with Walcott the only man who has posed only consistent threat to Stoke throughout this game. Ramsey receives possession in the middle of the park, before attempting to scoop a through ball into Giroud's path, but Wollscheid covers across to punt a clearance away.
(70’) Both coaches continue to stroll around their technical areas, with this game seemingly set to go down to the wire. Bellerin strokes a cross in from the right, but Walcott can't bring it under his spell! Stoke reply with a counter of their own, but Arsenal get enough men behind the ball to slow the hosts down and defuse the situation.
(68’) Ramsey sees a shot blocked on the edge of the Stoke penalty area, with Diouf gobbling up the rebound and immediately driving forward. It isn't difficult to imagine what Hughes' instructions to then ex-Molde man would have been. The Potters win yet another corner, with Pieters' near-post cross being diverted away from Walters by Bellerin. Arsenal have their backs to the wall, but keep scrambling clearances out of harm's way.
(66’) Cech is forced to turn another save around his own post, but the former Chelsea shot-stopper is able to claim the resulting corner delivery. Less than half an hour is left on the clock at the Britannia, with Hughes introducing a forward that has the pace to ask real questions of Koscielny and Mertesacker.
--- 64’ Substitution Diouf is introduced for Bojan, with the ex-Man United striker having the pace to stretch the visiting defence. ---
(64’) Monreal is forced into a defensive header at the back post, following a good cross in from the left flank by Pieters. The resulting corner is cleared at the near upright, with Stoke spurning another good opportunity to do some damage.
(62’) Walcott skips beyond two players at pace, with Whelan forced into making a rather cynical challenge on the England international. Bellerin and Campbell then combine down the right flank, with Pieters doing brilliantly to track back and deny the former. Both outfits continue to cancel each other out.
(60’) We're into the final half an hour at the Britannia, with Stoke still looking likely to take a valuable point on home soil. Clear-cut chances have been very few and far between this evening. A long ball forward from the visitors evades Shawcross, but Wollscheid mops up the scraps ahead of Campbell.
(58’) Shawcross heads just wide! The former Man United defender is picked out at the back post, but looks over to see the linesman's flag raised for offside on the far side. Giroud goes down heavily after a boisterous challenge, but the Frenchman is quickly back to his feet - albeit a little gingerly.
(56’) A cross is lifted into the Arsenal penalty area from deep on the left, but Walters is caught criminally offside at the far post. The linesmen have been very busy when dealing with the Potters' front four in this contest. Both coaches will presumably be looking to make changes sooner rather than later, as there needs to be some kind of catalyst introduced. Stoke threaten through Joselu, but Cech dives to his right to deny the Spaniard and then Bojan from the rebound!
(54’) Koscielny half clears some danger from the right-hand side, before Afellay whips a curling cross in towards the near post! Cech is there is punch the danger away, with chances continuing to be rather elusive to the hosts. Joselu hasn't offered a great deal, with Walters also not being presented with any opportunities.
(53’) Johnson is released down the right-hand side, but an attempted through ball from the ex-Portsmouth defender is cut out with ease. Moments later, Walcott is fed into the penalty area by a low pass, but the Englishman is outmuscled by Wollscheid. The German defender appeared to have hold of his man's arm, but the referee isn't interested in giving a penalty!
(51’) Afellay curls a corner delivery in from the left-hand side, but Shawcross is penalised for putting too much pressure on Cech. Both sides are competing well, with Hughes now off his bench and barking out instructions from within his technical area. Bojan tries to find space on the edge of the box, but Flamini slides in to deny him. Arsenal respond with a counter, but Walcott is dispossessed in the penalty area by Shawcross.
(49’) Arsenal are on the front foot from the outset of the second half, with Stoke seeming to be having problems with Joselu and Arnautovic staying onside. Both forwards have been responsible for moves breaking down. Johnson gallivants down the right flank, before curling in a cross, but Mertesacker heads half clear before mopping up the scraps.
(47’) Good save from Butland! Giroud manages to meet a corner delivery from the right-hand side, with the ex-Birmingham goalkeeper getting down smartly to his left to parry the ball away! Huge chance for the Gunners to take the lead, there.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Hughes' men have perhaps seen more of the ball than Arsenal would have liked, but the Gunners can still go top of the table if they come out with all guns blazing during the next 45 minutes.
HALF TIME! The two sides head in goalless at the break, with Butland making two good saves to ensure that Stoke are still in with a chance of taking three points from Arsenal. The midfield battle has been fairly even, with neither side taking the contest by the scruff of the neck, but there is plenty of time for a breakthrough goal.
(45’) We're into the only minute of first-half stoppage time.
(45’) Whelan and Bojan combine on the edge of the box, but the latter is robbed of possession as he looks to turn. Moments later, Arnautovic drives down the left and shifts the ball inside, but Ramsey makes a timely interception. The midfields are certainly cancelling themselves out at the Britannia.
(43’) Walcott drives down the left flank, before Giroud hangs a cross into the box from the same wing. Wollscheid is present to head the ball into touch, with the German defender coming under no pressure at all. The resulting throw in is taken short, but an errant touch from Ramsey results in the Welshman disappointingly giving away a goal kick.
(41’) We're into the final five minutes of the first half, with Arsenal trying to probe for a rare opportunity. Campbell is fouled by Pieters, as the away side work the ball from right to left, but Stoke have plenty of shirts behind the ball. Possession has been more ponderous than dangerous in this match, it must be said. Walcott tries to cut inside and drive to the edge of the penalty area, but Johnson denies the ex-Southampton man easily.
(39’) Butland is in no rush to take his goal kicks, with the Potters happy to ensure that they stay settled and in control of this game. Walters and Shawcross combine, but Johnson is denied from overlapping beyond the former. The hosts work possession backwards as a result, with Arsenal sitting in and biding their time to counter.
(37’) Narrowly under 10 minutes remain in the first half, with Stoke probably being set to rue missing a few recent chances. Bojan has been bright, while Johnson has whipped in some brilliant deliveries from the right-hand side. All that Hughes needs to see from his personnel is the finishing touch that he provided as a player.
(35’) Cech's penalty area is subject to a lot of pressure at the moment, but the Czech Republic international is yet to make a tough save. Wenger may well be happy to see his side head into the break still level. Bojan breaks down the left, before jinking inside, but the former Barcelona midfielder shoots beyond the far post!
(33’) Arnautovic is caught offside yet again, after another teasing delivery from the right-hand side from Johnson! The Austrian got slightly ahead of his man, but wasn't able to turn home the cross anyway! Cech will be relieved, as the ex-Chelsea goalkeeper was flapping at the ball himself!
(31’) The opening half an hour has been very competitive, with Stoke enjoying a lot of possession after a slow start to proceedings. Arsenal have probably had the better of the chances at the Britannia, but this contest is still delicately poised.
(29’) The Potters look to break down the right-hand side, but Walters cuts back a terrible pass that is easily intercepted. Arsenal respond immediately, with Walcott picking out Oxlade-Chamberlain on the edge of the box. The Englishman tries his luck with a curling, right-footed strike, but Butland tips a save over his crossbar! The resulting corner is half cleared, before a shot from the same Gunners' midfielder is deflected off target by Koscielny.
(27’) Giroud flicks a header to Campbell, before the Arsenal winger looks to release Walcott in behind enemy lines! Fortunately for the hosts, Johnson is alert to the danger and gets ahead of his man to intercept. Stoke continue to try and force the issue, with the Gunners playing off their lone striker before trying to counter at pace.
(25’) Bojan drives down the left-hand side, but the Spaniard loses his footing while attempting to stab a low pass in behind Bellerin for Arnautovic to get on the end of. Stoke are approaching the opposition penalty area well, before running out of ideas in the final third. Afellay tries to part the Gunners' defence on the most recent occasion, but slides the ball straight behind for a goal kick.
(23’) Stoke continue to hold onto the ball nicely, though Butland will feel as though he has importantly kept his side in this match with the save to deny Giroud. Another zipping through ball is fired in the direction of the Frenchman moments later, but he miscontrols entirely. Wollscheid shepherds the ball back to his goalkeeper.
(21’) Afellay's shot is probably the closest that either side have gone thus far, with the Gunners appearing to be stuck for creativity without Ozil. Campbell slides a neat through ball into the path of Giroud, but Butland is extremely quick off his line to make a sprawling one-versus-one stop!
(19’) Ramsey is cynically fouled by Johnson, with a few fouls creeping into this contest already. The free-kick delivery is held up well by Giroud, but the ex-Montpellier striker manages to end up fouling Shawcross in the process. Stoke work their way upfield, with Afellay presented with space at the edge of the penalty box, but the Dutchman shoots wide of the right-hand post!
(17’) Arnautovic is the target of a long pass down the line, but the Austria international's errant touch is gobbled up by Cech. The visitors respond with an attack of their own, with play opened up to the left-hand side. Walcott manages to win a foul from Walters, but the Gunners fail to make anything of the dead-ball situation.
(15’) Johnson drives forward down the right-hand side, before trying to curl a delivery towards the penalty spot, but Mertesacker cuts the ball out well. Stoke have had a strong last five minutes, with the Potters dictating possession and forcing Arsenal to sit in their shape and absorb some extended pressure. Wenger's men aren't looking high on offensive ideas.
(13’) Bojan drifts in from the left and puts the ball on his stronger foot, but a shot from the ex-Ajax man is blocked with ease. The opening stages have been quite even, with both sides taking their turns to go on the offensive. Both Joselu and Giroud have struggled to get themselves into the contest, however.
(11’) Ramsey tries to slice the Stoke defence apart with a pass into Campbell, but the Costa Rica international's first touch lets him down terribly. Moments later, Arnautovic cuts in from the left flank and lets fly, but the Austrian winger can only lash a sliced attempt high and wide of the target!
(9’) Monreal is forced to make a good clerance, with Joselu looking to creep beyond the shoulder of the last defender in order to meet a diagonal pass. This has very much been a midfield battle thus far, with neither side having any stopping power in the opposition half. A long Stoke ball looks for Arnautovic, but Cech is quick off his line to collect.
(7’) Afellay wins a good header in the middle of the park, but the ex-Barcelona midfielder's forward pass is intercepted before Arnautovic can race into a dangerous area. Wenger's men have kept the ball on the ground thus far, with Giroud not getting any service whatsoever. A rather cagey start to proceedings in the Midlands.
(5’) Arsenal enjoy the early possession, with the home fans turning their attentions towards jeering the visiting outfit. Arnautovic tries to race down the left flank, but the ex-Werden Bremen winger is caught quite obviously offside. Hughes is remaining on his bench at the moment, but could be provoked into action should Stoke continue to stutter.
(3’) Walcott is found trying to drive down the left-hand side, with Wollscheid deliberately blocking off the England international. The referee has a word with the German defender, who is already walking on thin ice in terms of going into the book. The resulting free kick is whipped into the box, but the hosts clear.

This clash has got a good amount of history, with the home supporters certainly not the biggest fans of Arsene Wenger and his personnel, with the Gunners able to go back top of the Premier League with a win this afternoon. FULL TIME: SWANSEA 1-0 WATFORD. Skipper Ashley Williams inflicts a fourth-successive league defeat on the Hornets, pulling the Swans out of the relegation zone with new coach Francesco Guidolin watching on.
(90’) WIDE FROM DEENEY AND THAT SHOULD DO IT! He can't direct his shot on target from inside the area, sending it whizzing wide of the near post and behind for a goal kick. Swansea have only a few more seconds to see out!
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card Sigurdsson is shown a yellow card for time wasting. ---
(90’) UNBELIEVABLE! OFF THE WOODWORK! What a terrific bit of running from Gomis inside the area to twist and turn his way into space, somehow getting a shot off, but it smacks off the inside of the far post! Half an inch to the right and Swansea are two goals to the good.
(90’) There will be three minutes added on at the end of the match. Is there a twist in the tale?
(89’) Another Jurado strike drifts just beyond the post with Fabianski struggling to get across. The pressure stays on, however, and Ake's cross is forced behind by Naughton for a corner. Watson delivers, but again Fabianski is wise to it, coming off his line and getting great distance behind his punch.
--- 87’ Substitution Watford use the stoppage to make their second change as well, with forward Obbi Oulare replacing Behrami. ---
--- 87’ Substitution Alan Curtis makes his final personnel decision as interim manager as the Swans use their third substitution. Jordi Amat is introduced as an extra body in defence, at the expense of Ki. ---
(86’) Another Watson set piece is dealt with easily by the Swans. This doesn't seem to be Watford's night. Swansea have not broken their focus since the opening kick and they appear determined to keep all three points - which would be good enough to take them back out of the relegation zone.
(84’) STRAIGHT AT FABIANSKI! A careless bit of defending sees Swansea fail to convincingly clear their lines following a corner, and Jurado latches onto the loose ball. He volleys at goal and makes decent contact, but hits it directly at the keeper.
--- 82’ Substitution Swansea make a second change, with Ayew giving way after putting in a tireless shift up top. He's replaced by Bafetimbi Gomis, who will be hoping to punish Watford on the break as the Hornets start to throw men forward. ---
(80’) DREADFUL EFFORT! Watson is more than capable of sweetly striking a set piece, and he has his chance from 20 yards out, just to the left of goal. Anticipation builds as he gets set to take, but his final effort is a letoff for the Swans as it smacks off the bottom of the wall before being cleared.
(78’) Watford are completely out of ideas and are sorely lacking in creativity as they try and break this Swansea resistance. They have Almen Abdi waiting in the wings and you have to wonder why he hasn't been brought on yet. The Swiss midfielder has created 28 chances for the Hornets this season.
(76’) STAT: Watford have scored exactly one goal in each of their last four visits to the Liberty Stadium across all competitions.
--- 74’ Substitution The first change for Watford isn't really an attacking one as Nyom, who is on a yellow, is replaced by Juan Carlos Paredes in what is a like-for-like swap. ---
(72’) Slowly but surely the tempo is starting to pick up a bit with Watford beginning to throw caution to the wind. They will have little hesitation in sending bodies forward in search of an equaliser, though that won't serve much purpose if they can't start to get their front men some service.
(70’) CRUCIAL BLOCK! Sigurdsson amazes with his skill, dribbling his way beyond a couple of defenders before picking out Ki with a pullback. The midfielder takes the chance first time, but his strike is turned aside smartly by Watson.
(68’) Watford continue to grow into the game, and they seem to have developed more of an idea on how they want to attack. Jurado sprints forward and spots Ighalo, who gifts the midfielder a return pass, but the Spaniard's shot curls beyond the far post.
--- 66’ Substitution Routledge has put in a good shift tonight for the Swans and receives an appropriate ovation as he makes his way off for the final 25 minutes, to be replaced by Modou Barrow. ---
(64’) STAT: The Hornets have lost just one of their last five competitive away games against the Swans (W2 D2 L1).
--- 62’ Yellow card Cynical handball from Britton who knew every bit what he was doing there, taking one for the team to stop what was turning into a promising attack for Watford. He will not escape a booking for that, however. ---
(60’) Speculative effort in the end from Cork as he skews a half-volley wide from 20 yards after Ayew did so well to knock the ball down for him, winning a header inside the area. You get the sense that Swansea may need a second goal if they are to snatch all three points.
(58’) Better from Swansea as they start to pass the ball around a bit better. They had no issue working it around in midfield in the first half but the same has not been true of the second. Sigurdsson is starting to get on the ball a bit more and that's exactly what the hosts need.
(56’) This is exactly what Alan Curtis would have warned his team about at the break. Watford have come out of the interval with a spring in their step, as was to be expected, and Swansea are struggling a bit to keep pace. They need to weather this storm and get back to the form they showed in the first half.
(54’) SPLENDID DELIVERY! Watson whips in a tremendous free kick from the left flank which Britos rises to meet, between Williams and Sigurdsson. He glances a tidy header at goal from close range, but it crashes onto the roof of the net!
(52’) Not a bad effort! Jurado is quickly growing into Watford's best attacking outlet and has been head over heels their most direct midfielder in possession. He works a little one-two with Deeney to line up a shot, but his curled effort drifts a couple yards wide of the top corner from range.
(50’) STAT: Swansea are 11 points worse off after 21 games this season (19) than they were in 2014-15.
(48’) Williams was walking very gingerly at the end of the first half and was especially struggling as he made his way towards the tunnel, but the training staff seems to have worked a miracle on him as he's back out for this second half and moving without any noticeable infringements as Watford ask a few early questions of the Swansea defence.
(46’) Back underway in Wales!
(45’) HALF TIME: SWANSEA 1-0 WATFORD.
(45’) The Swans head into the interval with a slender advantage thanks to a goal from their skipper Ashley Williams, in what has been a rather uneventful 45 minutes of football at the Liberty Stadium with both sides in desperate need of points to halt their respective skids.
(45’) There will be just one minute added on at the end of the first half, as play is brought to a halt with Williams down injured after an innocent coming together with Behrami in midfield. This does appear a bit of a worry for the defender, who remains down as the training staff comes out to have a look.
(43’) Swansea have had close to 70 per cent possession in this first half, but perhaps the most telling stat is that 55 per cent of all possession has been in the midfield third. Neither side have spent a great deal of time in attack, in what has been a relatively uninspiring opening 45 minutes.
(41’) The Hornets are trying to muster a bit of possession, but Swansea are playing with great confidence. They have plenty of energy off the ball and more than enough depth in defence to deal with the movement of Ighalo and Deeney, who have been starved of service in this first half.
(39’) STAT: Watford have not lost four successive Premier League games since May 2000. After winning four games in a row in the Premier League, Watford have now picked up just one point in their four games following this streak (W0, D1, L3).
(37’) Watord are desperately in need of a late push to end this first half. A goal seems to be out of the question, but they have to find a way to tilt the tides a bit or change momentum into the half, or they could be staring a fourth consecutive league defeat in the face.
(35’) It has been all Swansea in this second half and there is no indication of that changing right now. Ake is the latest to commit a foul, in a similar position on the opposite flank. Sigurdsson's last delivery was beaten away by Gomes, so he will be hoping to do a bit better with this one.
--- 33’ Yellow card No question that's a foul as Routledge escapes onto the left flank to get on the end of a pass from Ki and knock the ball beyond Nyom, before the right-back takes him to ground. A yellow is issued to the defender, but the free kick will be more of a worry for the Hornes. ---
(31’) The Swans have not let up since scoring, back on the front foot and looking for more. The club is in a very fragile state right now, so it's important for them to keep their focus and not let Watford grow into the game, because if they concede it could really deal a blow to morale.
(29’) STAT: Ahead of MD22, Swansea had conceded the opening goal 14 times this season, only Villa (15) had done so more often this season.
--- 27’ Assist Ki was instrumental in the buildup, peeling off to the right to get into space before delivering a inviting cross into the area. ---
--- 27’ Goal! THE BIG MAN PRODUCES A BIG GOAL FOR SWANSEA! The Swans send plenty of men into the box for a corner, and although the ball is initially cleared, they manage to keep the pressure on. Ki sends a terrific cross in from the right and there's Ashley Williams to rise and meet it, sending a thumping header in at the near post! ---
(26’) Terrific bit of play from Ayew! A pass is absolutely drilled towards him and somehow he manages to control it, while fending off Cathcart. He keeps play alive and works a tidy one-two with Sigurdsson before forcing Gomes into action with a decent strike from 15 yards out.
(24’) We have entered a bit of a cagey period with the ball largely being contained in midfield. The hosts are still by far the more positive side in possession, but it all seems to be fizzling out for them once they enter the final third.
--- 22’ Yellow card Jurado drags down Routledge in midfield and Michael Oliver brings play to a halt once he realises there is no advantage to be had - and the Spaniard is issued a yellow card. ---
(21’) It's almost as it Watford haven't been told they're playing a game tonight. They have been very poor in every facet of the pitch. A large reason for their success this season can be attributed to how hard they work collectively, but we have not seen that just yet.
(19’) Bravely done by Gomes! There are a lot of eyes on the keeper, despite the fine season he's had to date, with Costel Pantilimon on his way to Vicarage Road from Sunderland. The ex-Tottenham keeper does really well here though in coming off his line to sniff out a through ball intended for Britton, when he knew he would be clattered into if he did.
(17’) STAT: Since beating Manchester United at the end of August, Swansea have won just once at home in the Premier League (W1, D4, L4).
(15’) A mistake from Ake awards the Swans yet another corner as the pressure begins to build on the Watford goal. They have defended capably up to this point, but the rest of the team needs to start doing their part to provide the back four with a bit of respite.
(13’) CLOSE CALL! That's a very tight decision for the linesman who flags Sigurdsson for offside after a clever routine worked by the Swans following a corner. Had the flag stayed down, and it very well could have, the Iceland international could have been into the box with a real opportunity to carve out a scoring chance.
(11’) Watford's main focus seems to be on keeping their shape and remaining disciplined at the back, before trying to break with pace on the counter. Their two strikers are more than willing to put in the work, though the midfield has yet to really produce much for the likes of Deeney or Ighalo to chase.
(9’) The hosts have enjoyed the bulk of possession but they really seem to be lacking ideas in attack, throwing balls aimlessly into the area with the hopes of getting a lucky bounce or a stroke of genius from Ayew or Routledge. They don't have the height in the centre to be throwing balls into the box like this.
(7’) STAT: Watford won 1-0 when the teams met in September - securing their first Premier League victory of the season since returning to the top flight.
(5’) Swansea are not lining up in a 4-3-3 a was originally indicated. They actually have instilled a diamond in midfield, with Sigurdsson at the top of it in the number 10 role, while Cork has been tasked with providing cover for the back line. Routledge and Ayew are roaming freely up top.
(3’) OFFSIDE! The interplay there from Swansea in attack was a real joy to watch, capped off by a delicious back-heel from Sigurdsson to spring Routledge through on goal. The forward just drifted a yard or two offside, however, and it was spotted accordingly by the linesman.

(90’) Daniels accidentally lets the ball run out of play on the left-hand side, which sums up Bournemouth's second-half performance. There are four minutes of stoppage time.
(88’) Collins lifts a long ball out to Antonio on the left-hand side, with the West Ham winger happy to shield a deflected pass out for a throw in. Bilic's men are content to wind down the clock, as this three points will be most welcome indeed.
(86’) Ogbonna hits his own post! The former Juve defender slices a clearance onto the near upright, with Murray lurking dangerously behind him! The resulting corner is punched clear by Adrian, with the Spaniard rising well amidst traffic.
--- 84’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! WHAT A HIT FROM VALENCIA! The Ecuador international tries his luck from the aforementioned free kick, hammering a powerful effort goalwards! It dips and bamboozles Boruc, with the ball arrowing inside the near post! It looked like the Bournemouth goalkeeper could have got there, but that strike was travelling! ---
(83’) Jelavic rises well to flick a header out wide to Antonio, with Gosling sliding into a poor tackle on the ex-Forest winger. West Ham don't have their set-piece taker on the field anymore, however.
(81’) We're into the final 10 minutes at Vitality Stadium, with Bournemouth claiming for a penalty! Stanislas shoots from the edge of the box, with the ex-Burnley winger believing that Ogbonna handled the ball! It did strike the former Juventus defender, but he didn't know much about it!
--- 80’ Substitution The Cherries appear to be throwing caution to the wind, with Murray coming into the game in place of Arter. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Payet is sacrificed by Bilic, with the Frenchman having quite the influence tonight. Song comes into the midfield to help shut up shop. ---
(76’) Bournemouth have to try and fight their way back from one goal behind now, with Howe needing to mastermind quite the comeback. West Ham might have their first away win in quite some time, here, with the Hammers still on course to stay in the top six.
--- 74’ Assist After scoring once, the France international carves out the second! Payet gets to the right byline, before chopping back a lovely delivery from Valencia to turn home. ---
--- 74’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! WEST HAM COMPLETE THE TURNAROUND! The Ecuador international is picked out on the penalty spot, before lashing a first-time finish emphatically into the ceiling of the net! Boruc had no chance and the visitors are 2-1 up! ---
(74’) Arter opens play out to the right-hand side, with Smith trying to slide a pass in behind Antonio for Stanislas to chase. Fortunately for the visitors, the ex-Forest midfielder makes a timely interception. This contest is becoming very stretched indeed, with tired legs definitely on show.
--- 72’ Substitution After running himself into the ground, Afobe is pulled off by Howe. Despite missing two good chances, the ex-Arsenal forward has put in some miles tonight. Grabban is introduced up top. ---
(72’) Jenkinson manages to win a corner from Daniels, but the resulting delivery is lashed away by Afobe. A second delivery is put into the box and flicked on by Antonio, but Jelavic is unabel to meet the flick on. Suddenly, the Cherries are looking rather shaky!
(70’) Suddenly, the ball is back in Bournemouth's court. West Ham have looked dangerous since the restart, with their pressure finally telling. Narrowly under 20 minutes are on the clock for either side to take the much-needed three points.
--- 68’ Yellow card Payet picks up a yellow card for his celebrations, after racing over to the travelling support to mingle with West Ham's fans! ---
--- 67’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! WHAT A HIT FROM PAYET! The France international takes aim from 25 yards out, before curling a dream of a free kick off the underside of the crossbar and into the back of the net! Inspiration from the ex-Marseille midfielder! ---
(66’) Adrian makes an easy save look difficult, after yet another long-range effort from Arter, with the Spaniard choosing not to hold a hammerstrike from the Irishman. West Ham gallivant upfield on the counter, with Smith then giving away a free kick in a dangerous area.
--- 66’ Yellow card Smith picks up a yellow card for the hosts, after making a cynical foul on the periphery of his own box. ---
(65’) Iturbe manages to win the ball back high up the left-hand side, but the Argentina international is let down by Daniels when he attempts to play a neat one-two. The Hammers respond with their own foray down the left, but a delivery from Cresswell is blocked simply.
(63’) West Ham continue to see more of the ball, with Afobe left to chase in an isolated position up top. Bournemouth are sat back in their banks of four, with Boruc being very well protected indeed. A long pass is pumped forward in search of Valencia, but Cook heads the danger clear.
--- 61’ Substitution Jenkinson replaces Tomkins for the away side, with the former Arsenal right-back perhaps offering a little more offensively as the Hammers look to get back on level terms. ---
(61’) Valencia fires over! The former Pachucha striker lets fly from 20 yards out, but can only send the ball arrowing into the stands behind Boruc's goal. Meanwhile, there's some movement on the visiting bench, with it appearing that Bilic is about to ring another change.
(60’) Noble makes an unorthodox challenge on the periphery of the penalty area, with the Englishman able to poke a touch clear of the danger area. Bournemouth maintain their pressure, but a cross in from Stanislas is headed half clear by Collins! The rebound is caught on the half volley by Arter, but his attempt bounces wide of the far upright!
(58’) Payet is released down the left-hand side, but the Frenchman's attempted cross is headed away from danger by Francis! West Ham keep the pressure on, with Bilic's men enjoying the lion's share of possession at the moment. Another delivery into the box looks for Valencia, but this time Cook is on hand to clear.
(56’) Arter unleashes another strike from range, but the opening goalscorer can only fire a low drive into Collins' midriff. Howe's men are looking to play on the break at present, with West Ham trying to impose themselves in this second half. Antonio hasn't seen as much service, but Valencia is still a threat.
(54’) Gosling tries his luck from the left-hand side, but a deflection off Collins takes the ball looping into the arms of Adrian. West Ham counter in an attempt to respond, but the move ends in Boruc claiming the ball easily. The Bournemouth goalkeeper hasn't had a save to make since the restart.
(52’) Arter goes down heavily, after catching an arm to the face from Obiang, but the Republic of Ireland international is quickly back in the fray after brief treatment. West Ham are managing to see more possession at the moment, but can't quite find an equaliser. Valencia is released by a lovely through ball, but Francis intervenes to deny the Ecuador international.
--- 50’ Substitution After suffering from the aforementioned knock, Ritchie is forced off the field of play. Iturbe gets the chance to make his debut, however, with the ex-Roma winger coming into the game as a result. ---
(48’) Ritchie goes down on the edge of his own penalty area, after suffering from a slight knock, but the ex-Swindon man is quickly back to his feet. West Ham whip an early corner delivery in moments later, but the ball sails over the danger zone. Antonio then threatens after jinking infield from the left, but his shot zips wide.
(46’) We are back underway at the Vitality Stadium! Bournemouth have the lead, but West Ham have shown some dangerous signs of fighting back. Payet in particular has looked as though he might have a say this evening.
HALF TIME! Bournemouth head into the break with a 1-0 advantage over West Ham, courtesy of a long-range strike from Arter. The visitors haven't managed to threaten since Carroll went off injured early on, leaving the Cherries to squander the contest's chances. Boruc has made two good saves, with Bilic's men still in with a shout.
(45’) We're into the first of two minutes of stoppage time.
(45’) GREAT SAVE FROM BORUC! The Poland international does well once again! Payet goes on a driving run, after Surman was robbed in the midfield third, but the ex-Marseille midfielder is unable to beat the Bournemouth shot-stopper! A strong right wrist tips the effort over the crossbar!
(44’) Valencia is the target of a long ball from Collins, but Cook rises above the Ecuador international to defuse the situation. Moments later, Payet goes on a driving run, but the Frenchman is dispossessed as he shapes to shoot.
(42’) Afobe is back in the action and moving easily, which is fantastic news for Howe and company. The hosts try and break at pace down the right-hand side, but Smith is unable to take down a lofted pass in his stride. Bournemouth are desperately looking for their second of the night.
(40’) Only five minutes are left for West Ham to see out, with Bilic probably wanting the half-time whistle to come as soon as possible. Gosling goes on a driving run, before trying to slip a pass into Afobe, but the debutant is muscled off the ball by Ogbonna! The Bournemouth striker goes down heavily, but should be okay to continue after some treatment.
(38’) Great save from Boruc! The former Celtic goalkeeper has to be very alert to deny a goal-bound deflection off Cook, following a cross-cum-shot from Jelavic! The resulting corner is whipped in from the right, but Tomkins can only hook a volleyed flick over the crossbar!
(37’) Valencia manages to win a flick on, but Cook steps in ahead of Jelavic to ensure that West Ham continue to be caged in their own half. Howe's men are strutting their stuff, with the visitors having little option but to sit back and weather the storm. Arter tries to scamper down the left flank, but Valencia tracks back well to deny the goalscorer.
(35’) With around 10 minutes remaining until the break, Bournemouth might just end up regretting some missed chances come the end of the game. Afobe has had two great opportunities to double the hosts' lead, with Daniels perhaps able to do better with a chance from the left flank.
(33’) Stanislas manages to break in behind enemy lines, with the Englishman sprinting into the penalty area on the left-hand side. Fortunately for the Hammers, Tomkins recovers brilliantly to outmuscle the Cherries' winger. Moments later, Afobe is slid into the box, but the former Arsenal man is unable to round Adrian due to a terrible first touch!
(31’) The opening half an hour has had a real ebb and flow about it, with both sides having their chance to dominate and force the issue. Stanislas dribbles down the left flank, before cutting back inside and making tracks towards the periphery of the box. Unfortunately for the wide man, against his former club, he can only see a tame shot easily blocked.
(29’) Bournemouth have really had a spring in their step since breaking the deadlock, with Howe's men moving the ball with confidence. Smith and Ritchie combine down the right-hand side, before a cross from the former is blocked well by Noble. Adrian gathers up the scraps.
(27’) Payet tries to slide a cute pass in behind Cook for Jelavic to chase, but the two aren't quite on the same wavelength! The France international's attempted ball instead zips out of play for a goal kick. That's the closest that West Ham have got to equalising since Carroll limped to the treatment table.
(25’) Valencia is released down the right-hand side, but the Ecuadorian forward is once again caught a few yards offside. West Ham have only been able to generate any kind of danger through the ex-Emelec man, especially since Carroll has taken his leave. After five minutes of mayhem, the Hammers have managed to settle back down again.
(23’) West Ham are trying to retain possession and take the sting out of the contest, but Bilic's men are now the team to be making all of the mistakes. An attempted pass back towards Adrian has to be lashed away in hurried fashion, as Afobe continues to lead the line and press high.
(21’) After a terrible first five minutes, suddenly Bournemouth find themselves a goal ahead and well on top! Adrian is forced into his first save of the evening, after Daniels was released brilliantly down the left flank by Afobe! The left-back shoots with power, but West Ham's shot-stopper is equal to it!
(19’) BIG CHANCE FOR AFOBE! Bournemouth work a corner short, with a cross eventually whipped in from the right-hand side with some real swing! The debutant rises well and above Ogbonna, but can only divert his headed attempt up and over the crossbar!
--- 17’ Assist Surman slips a simple pass infield to his midfield teammate, but Arter does the rest! ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! ARTER GIVES THE HOSTS THE LEAD! After receiving the ball around 25 yards from goal, with Irishman jinks onto his right foot and lets fly! His awkward shot bounces just beyond an unsighted Adrian and the crowd goes wild! ---
(16’) Afobe hasn't been given any service in the opening minutes of his debut, with the ex-Wolves striker unable to do anything but chase lost causes. West Ham suddenly need to settle this game back down, with Carroll's injury appearing to have shaken them.
--- 15’ Substitution Jelavic is quickly readied and thrown into the fray, with Carroll limping off and unable to continue due to a muscle problem. That could be another few weeks on the sidelines for the former Liverpool striker. ---
(14’) Arter and Stanislas link up on the edge of the penalty area, but the Iatter's attempted through ball towards Afobe is cut out. Bournemouth are finally looking to be finding their feet in this contest, following a very shaky start indeed.
(13’) Daniels and Stanislas look to combine down the left-hand side, but the Bournemouth duo haven't had any real joy thus far. Carroll heads down the tunnel and will be unable to continue, with the hosts momentarily having the numerical advantage against Bilic's side.
(11’) On second glance, it was Cook who managed to clear from under his own crossbar, there! West Ham are rightly aggrieved that they didn't get a corner. There's a break in play, as Carroll goes down with what appears to be a muscle problem.
(10’) Obiang and Payet link up brilliantly, before the latter slides a lovely pass in behind enemy lines for Valencia to chase! The West Ham forward is caught narrowly offside, before continuing and firing a terrible shot straight at Boruc. The hosts aren't looking in good shape early on. Moments later, Carroll breaks down the right and whips in a dangerous cross from the byline, but Antonio can only lift an attempt over the bar!
(8’) Valencia has seen plenty of the ball in the opening minutes, with the away side looking to try and force the issue. The Ecuador international has been crowded out on the edge of a congested penalty area thus far, but is constantly willing to run at and ask questions of his man.
(6’) West Ham enjoy a calm spell of possession, before a long pass is launched in the direction of Carroll. The former Newcastle striker's flick ons have been inaccurate thus far, but both Francis and Cook are looking to be struggling aerially against their imposing opponent. Bilic will be pleased with how the Hammers have started.
(4’) Stanislas gives the ball away on the edge of his own penalty area, but a quick pass into the feet of Valencia comes to nothing for the visitors. The Cherries don't look particularly settled, with Howe's men making some uncharacteristic mistakes while in possession.
(2’) Noble goes close! West Ham immediately break forward with intent, with Valencia able to chase down a poor pass back from Francis into Boruc! The Bournemouth goalkeeper half clears his lines, with the West Ham captain angling a first-time shot over the bar from the rebound!

Remi Garde picks up his first win as a Premier League manager as Wayne Hennessey's error gifts the Lions three points. It's a 19-match winless skid in the top flight that comes to an end for Villa, who begin what they hope will be the start of a heroic push to safety.
(90’) FULL TIME: ASTON VILLA 1-0 CRYSTAL PALACE.
(90’) DANN LETS IT RUN! Oh what a chance it was for Palace to equalise! It almost seems to catch him by surprise as the ball into the area runs through to him at the far post, but he hesitates and can't get the decisive touch! That might do it.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution Into stoppage time and Villa make their first change. Ciaran Clark comes on as an extra body in defence, with Carles Gil giving way. ---
(90’) Just three minutes to be added on at the end of this match - can Villa hold on for their first victory under Remi Garde?
(88’) Into the final minutes now of what promises to be a tense and nervy conclusion for both teams. Some Villa fans can hardly bare to watch. With the was this season has played out, they won't feel sure of the result until long after the full time whistle sounds.
(86’) MR. HAPPY FEET! Ayew nearly sends the Villa faithful into rapture as he comes inches away from finishing off an exceptional individual effort that would have been a real goal of the month candidate - but in the end his strike drifts an inch over the bar after dribbling his way beyond three Palace defenders inside the area.
(84’) Villa have plenty of space available to them if they can advance the ball up the pitch. A second goal would do so much to relieve the tension in this ground. The last time Crystal Palace conceded twice in a Premier League match on their travels was in a 3-2 victory over Burnley in January 2015.
(82’) SCRAMBLED CLEAR BY OKORE! So calmly done by the defender who blasts the ball away to safety in a vital piece of no nonsense defending following a cross in from the right that Wickham so nearly got on the end of!
--- 80’ Yellow card Idrissa Gueye becomes the second player booked in as many minutes for a cynical tug on the shirt of a Palace player near the halfway line. ---
--- 79’ Yellow card Joel Ward goes into the book after a physical coming together along the touchline. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Final roll of the dice for Pardew who brings on Mile Jedinak at the expense of James McArthur. ---
(78’) OH HOW CLOSE! It wouldn't have counted anyhow, as the flag goes up very late to indicate an offside on Kozak, but that was nearly the second goal for Villa as the striker narrowly misses his strike from close range following an excellent passing move. That would have blown the roof off this place.
(76’) Just under 15 minutes for Palace to try and salvage something. They have adopted a greater sense of urgency, and Puncheon is played through down the right by Cabaye. The forward sends a cross in for Zaha, but the ex-Manchester United winger can do precious little with it.
(74’) STAT: Crystal Palace have lost just one of their last seven Premier League meetings with Aston Villa (W4, D2).
(72’) This looks like anything but a fragile Aston Villa team. They're defending valliantly in an attempt to pick up their first victory under Remi Garde, remaining disciplined and organised at the back. Palace are showing little signs on being able to navigate their way through.
(70’) Into the wall! Anticipation and tension builds as Palace wait to take. Mark Clattenburg moves the wall back and finally gives his go ahead, only for Cabaye to rattle his effort straight into the wall of Villa defenders. Letdown, that, for Palace.
--- 68’ Yellow card Terrific running from Zaha who is tripped up on the very edge of the 18-yard-box by Vertout, who goes into the referee's book. Palace have a real chance from the set piece to follow... ---
(66’) This has been anything but the Palace side we are used to seeing on their travels this season. Bunn has hardly had a save to make and the Eagles simply aren't posing enough of a threat on the counter. They haven't scored in 336 minutes of Premier League action since Bolasie's injury.
(64’) STAT: Aston Villa have conceded the first goal in 15 of their 20 Premier League matches this season, the most of any team in the top flight. They have kept just two clean sheets in the league all season.
--- 62’ Substitution Second change for the visitors who are looking to avoid an embarrassing defeat, as Marouane Chamakh comes on at the expense of Sako. ---
(60’) The crowd is full of belief once again, a rarity this season, and it's put the desire back into the legs of these Villa players. The goal truly was as ugly as you would like, but it couldn't be more fitting as a microcosm of Villa's season to this point.
--- 58’ Assist Good delivery by Vertout from the corner to pick out Lescott. ---
--- 58’ Goal! A LEAD FOR ASTON VILLA! It hasn't happened often this season, but the Villans have the lead! Lescott rises to meet the corner and sends a header straight at Hennessey, but the keeper makes a meal of it and spills the ball across the line by no more than half an inch! ---
(57’) TOO MUCH FROM AYEW! Exquisite interplay from Villa atop the area as they work the ball around and have Palace on their heels. Bacuna threads a pass through to Ayew, but he tries to flick the ball beyond a defender as opposed to getting a shot off, and the chance goes begging.
(56’) Bacuna commits a foul which awards Palace a free kick in a threatening position. Cabaye lifts an inviting delivery behind the defence and right into the danger area, but it's not appropriately attacked and Bunn is able to collect.
(54’) STAT: Aston Villa’s Premier League winless run has reached 19 games (D5, L14), tied for the fourth-worst ever.
(52’) EXCEPTIONAL FROM KOZAK! The striker takes a pass atop the area amidst a real mess of bodies. It looks as though there is absolutely no way through for him, but somehow he manages to force his way beyond two defenders and get a shot off, which forces Hennessey into a sharp save at his near post.
(50’) The three points are there for the taking, it's just a matter of which team wants it more at this point. Which team will take the necessary risks to go forward and get a goal? Which team has the belief and confidence in themselves? That's the area Villa seem to be lacking.
(48’) Slow start to the second half, filled with fouls and other stoppages. The ball is being contained largely in midfield and the crowd is starting to grow a bit restless - they know Villa need three points and nothing less is acceptable at this point.
--- 46’ Substitution On at the break is Connor Wickham, who missed the last few games with injury. Joe Ledley is off in his place. ---
(46’) Back underway at Villa Park!
Wilfred Zaha hit the post and Jordan Ayew the side-netting, the closest either side have come as we head into the break scoreless at Villa Park in what has been a match lacking in attacking quality. Still everything to play for in the second half, with the hosts especially in need of all three points.
(45’) HALF TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 CRYSTAL PALACE.
(45’) There will be one minute added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Approaching the interval now and Villa remain on the front foot, desperate to try and produce a breakthrough before the interval. Their crossing has really lacked conviction in the opening 45 minutes and has taken away from the fact that they are actually finding their way into some excellent areas out wide.
(41’) STAT: Crystal Palace have the best defensive record away from home in the Premier League this season, conceding just seven times in nine games (W5, D2, L2).
(39’) Successive corner for Villa come to nothing as Palace continue to get the best of the aerial duels. Hennessey is also quite confident in commanding his area, as he comes off his line to collect the second delivery and relieve the pressure on his goal.
(37’) CRUCIAL BLOCK! Very impressive, patient play from Ayew atop the area as he twists and turns his way into space for a shot. Anticipation builds in the stands and the Ghana international finally lets fly, but Ledley does so well to get a piece of it to knock the effort behind for a corner.
(35’) The game desperately need a goal to open things up a bit. Both sides are reluctant to take chances and commit bodies forward in fear of leaving themselves exposed at the other end, and it has really prevented there from being too many clear-cut scoring chances outside of the first few minutes.
(33’) Palace are doing a wonderful job of remaining organised in defence, but their transition play has left plenty to be desired. There is far too much individual play within the team on the counter, guys trying to run the length of the pitch themselves, with support lacking.
(31’) The tempo has slowed quite a bit and it's all become quite cagey out on the pitch. Villa still appear in control, but their inability to force Hennessey into action has left the home supporters frustrated.
(29’) STAT: Crystal Palace have not scored in any of their three Premier League matches since Yannick Bolasie went down injured (270 minutes).
(27’) NEARLY THERE! Great movement from Ayew to elude his marker and get behind the defence on the end of a flick on from Kozak. The crowd cheers as they think the Ghanaian has scored, but his half-volley is sent crashing into the side nettiing!
(25’) OFFSIDE! Sako issues a warning to the Villa defence as he creeps behind to get on the end of a ball over the top. He appears to be through on goal, but the hosts are saved as the linesman raises his flag for offside.
(23’) Kozak is making himself a good target man in the centre, but he's really struggling to get the better of Delaney and Dann in the air. He needs more support in the central areas, and more movement off the ball from his teammates to help draw some attention off him.
(21’) SENSATIONAL HIT! That's the sort of threat Sako poses! From out of nothing really, Villa fail to close down on the striker who seizes the opportunity to drive a shot at goal from range. He makes wicked contact, but Bunn will be relieved to see it drift inches over the bar.
(19’) STAT: The eight points Aston Villa have this season is the third lowest any team has managed in the Premier League after 20 games. Sunderland (six in 2005/06) and Derby (seven in 2007/08) were the only who had fewer, and both were relegated.
(17’) It seems as though Villa's best route going forward is through the linkup play of Carles Gil and Bacuna along the right. The Dutchman is very prominent on the overlap and has done an exceptional job of finding space up to this point. He just needs to pick out a better final ball.
(15’) You get a real sense of the tension in the ground with every stray pass or nery predicament the Villa players get themselves into. The crowd is making plenty of noise, but the collective holding of their breath when the ball is played back and Palace press high up the pitch, is quite telling.
(13’) Gueye and Vertout are combining well to pull the string in midfield. They need to be a bit more consistent in producing an end product, however, as another promising move comes to an end as Vertout sends a tame strike straight at Hennessey from range.
(11’) This is a very encouraging start for Villa, who are enjoying plenty of possession in the attacking half. They still seem vulnerable when Palace break on the counter, but there is something to be said for the way they are moving the ball around at the moment.
(9’) STAT: The last seven league meetings between Aston Villa and Crystal Palace have produced just 10 goals.
(7’) Selfish from Bacuna! The Dutchman makes a tidy run into attack and has Westwood screaming out for a pass in all sorts of space to his left, but instead opts to take a shot himself. Ledley blocks it easily, and then Carles Gil fails to pick out Westwood with the follow up as well as another Villa chance goes begging.
(5’) Everything has settled down a bit, but it seems as though Palace hitting the post so early on has shocked Villa into life. They're playing with a bit more urgency, almost as if only now have they realized the predicament they find themselves in.
(3’) WHAT A PACE TO THIS MATCH! Incredible, lively start in Birmingham as the teams exchange attacks. Kozak sprints onto the end of a long pass and tries to get behind the defence, but has to settle for a corner. The ensuing delivery comes to Westwood atop the area, but his strike sails just wide of the top corner!
(2’) OFF THE WOODWORK! Zaha makes strides down the left and works a one-two with Puncheon, with no Villa player sticking with the forward's run. He takes the return pass and curls a shot beyond Bunn, but it rattles square off the woodwork before Villa scramble clear!
