Crystal Palace have evolved into road warriors under Alan Pardew. Defensively they’re a hard team to break down, while they have goals all throughout their side. They can relate to Villa’s current predicament, having been in a relegation battle of their own at this stage last season, but they will have little sympathy. A place in the top five is not out of the question for Pardew’s side who can leapfrog Manchester United with three points tonight.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Crystal Palace’s trip to Birmingham to take on bottom feeders Aston Villa, who are still in search of their first win under Remi Garde. The Villans are staring relegation square in the face and it would require the greatest of all great escapes for them to salvage their place in the Premier League next season. They were poor in their FA Cup game against League Two’s Wycombe on Saturday and the fans seemed to reach a boiling point afterwards. It will be interesting to see how the team responds today, in need of three points. Desperate doesn’t begin to describe it.

And that is the end of one of the best games of the 2015-16 season. Many people, me included, predicted the odd goal deciding this one with both team struggling for goals, but the handbrake was torn off for this game. Three goals apiece, chances galore and a last-ditch equaliser. United will feel a little more aggrieved that they failed to win this game after two terrible misses in the second half, but you can't take anything away from Newcastle. That's all from us, hope you enjoyed this as much as I did. Until next time.
(90’) Toney goes down after tussling with Darmian, but Mike Dean keeps his poker face intact. Good call from the official as it looked fair contact to me. Only moments to go here, and Wijnaldum wastes a late, late counter by selling a teammate short with a pass down the right.
(90’) Deep into injury time now and Memphis has a chance to escape his man, which he does, but can't finish the move by putting through a teammate. Is there time for another twist in this tale?
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Off goes Perez and on comes De Jong in injury time. ---
--- 90’ Goal! NEWCASTLE HAVE DONE IT AGAIN! Dummett goes from joker to prince with a late leveler! United clear the ball right to him at the top of the box, and he smashes it on goal, with a nick of Smalling helping it on its way into the back of the net! ---
(89’) Toney turns the ball over in midfield, and Martial has a chance to orchestrate a killer fourth goal. However, the Magpies survive. It looks like we will have four minutes of added time to finish this game.
(87’) Newcastle are hunting for a third goal, but it appears that if there is to be one, it will most likely be for United. They're playing on the counter and having a lot more space whenever they choose to attack.
--- 85’ Substitution Tiote's night is at an end as he's replaced by Toney. ---
(84’) VITAL STOP FROM ELLIOT! Memphis is the instigator once again, ghosting past his man and finding Fellaini unmarked, but the Belgian's attempt with a header is saved! That should have been that!
(82’) Heartbreak for the Magpies here but there's still time for them to come from behind once again. Credit must go to Rooney and Van Gaal though, one for the goal and the other for the introduction of Menphis, who initiated that goal!
--- 81’ Substitution Gouffran enters for Colback as Newcastle chase another comeback. ---
--- 79’ Goal! ROONEY STUNNER! Memphis started the move by driving at the Newcastle defence. His effort is blocked by Dummett, but it falls kindly to the captain at the top of the box, and he lashes an effort high into the top corner! ---
(78’) Blind tries to hoof away a clearance and misses it completely, leaving the ball for Mitrovic to attack. He glides infield and lets fly on his left, but it's a horrible shot that bobbles wide.
--- 75’ Substitution Herrera departs and on comes Mata. ---
(75’) The visitors are in real trouble as Newcastle are first to every ball and commanding this game at present. There is real belief in the stands that the home side can go on and win this match!
(73’) DRAMA IN THE UNITED BOX! Wijnaldum's shot on the turn is blocked by his own player. Colback picks up the pieces but his effort is also thwarted. United are struggling to clear the ball but eventually get it away!
(71’) GOAL RULED OUT! Darmian sloppily gives the ball away to Sissoko well inside his own half, and the Frenchman slides in Mitrovic for the finish, but the flag is up straight away! It was the right decision - Sissoko was under pressure and had to make the pass, but the Serbian was offside.
(69’) Superb character shown by Newcastle to come back from two goals down, and now the momentum should be on their side! There was a lot of wrestling between Mitrovic and Smalling in that penalty incident, but it appeared that the referee awarded it for Newcastle based on the defender initiating the contact.
--- 67’ Goal! MITROVIC COMPLETES THE COMEBACK! He hits it almost identical to Rooney's earlier in the game, hitting it low to the keeper's left. De Gea dived the wrong way! ---
--- 66’ Yellow card PENALTY TO NEWCASTLE! Smalling and Mitrovic are wrestling for a corner, but the United defender has his arms draped around the striker first, and concedes the spot kick, getting booked in the process! ---
--- 64’ Substitution Memphis has entered the fray for Lingard in the first change of the game from either side. ---
(64’) NO PENALTY! Wijnaldum weights a sumptuous pass into the path of Colback on the right side of the box, and he's got Fellaini on his heels. The Newcastle man goes down under pressure from the Belgian, but the referee rightfully rules it fair contact.
(62’) MASSIVE TACKLE! Rooney is sent away on the counter, and has only Coloccini between him and Elloit in goal. He squares up to the defender, but a crunching sliding challenge on the edge of the box wins the ball cleanly!
(60’) Dangerous cross from Sissoko sails over the head of Fellaini, but it's cleared before Mitrovic can attack it. Newcastle are back on the front foot and looking to complete the comeback.
(58’) No goals yet in the second half, but that's not for a lac of trying from both teams. This is the kind of enterprise that both sets of fans have been begging for all season. They will hope that, whatever the result, the tempo displayed here will be a sign of things to come.
(56’) OVER THE BAR! WHAT A MISS! Martial drives at the heart of the defence, drawing two players before reversing a pass to Herrera. The Spaniard cleverly rolls the ball into the path of Lingard who, unmarked at the back post, lashes the ball over the top! Van Gaal writhes in disbelief!
(54’) We're at the point in this game where almost every attack looks capable of creating a chance to test the keeper. What a superb back-and-forth tempo to this one, and the atmosphere is vocal.
(52’) SISSOKO THWARTED BY DE GEA! The Frenchman twists and turns, leaving two players for dead inside the box. He lets fly from close range, but once again, the Spanish keeper positions himself excellently to block that shot! Two magnificent saves from him today.
(50’) Wijnaldum is looking hungry for more goals here, but Perez fails to capitalise on a solid run from the Dutchman. He's Newcastle's top scorer with eight this season - all of them coming at this ground.
(48’) Lively start to the second half from both teams, as they're being a lot more direct in transitioning from midfield to attack. I get the feeling that the scoring is not quite finished in this match.
(46’) Here we go again.
And that is the end of a thrilling first half from St. James' Park. With both teams in poor attacking form, we expected something along the lines of a stalemate, but it's been anything but. After Rooney's controversial penalty opened the scoring, Newcastle upped the tempo, but conceded again via Lingard. However, Wijnaldum got them back in the game just before the break. A lot to play for still, so do stay tuned.
(45’) WIDE OF THE MARK! Martial provides a good outlet down the right once again, and he collects a long, low pass from Schneiderlin, lashing one on goal after cutting inside, but a deflection off Dummett takes it off target.
(44’) What a game we have on our hand all of a sudden! I'm sure that I'm not the only one a little disappointed that the half-time break is almost upon us. Newcastle have really stepped it up since around the half-hour mark.
--- 42’ Assist Great target man play from Mitrovic, battling hard against the aerially dominant Fellaini to knock it down for Wijnaldum! ---
--- 42’ Goal! WHAT A FINISH! Newcastle are right back in this one. Fellaini loses out to Mitrovic, whose header falls right to Wijnaldum, who doesn't hesitate, sliding in a lovely one-timed effort! ---
(41’) COLOCCINI GOES CLOSE! Well that was unexpected! The Argentine unleashes one from at least 25 yards that has De Gea scrambling, but only succeeds in plucking the rope support behind the goal!
(40’) This is more like it from Manchester United! That was a picture-perfect counterattack, and it's the type of football that their fans have been crying out for. United two up and comfortable.
--- 38’ Assist Excellent execution from Roney there on the break to take three defenders out of the game with a decoy cut inside. Everyone was expecting the shot, but he had other ideas. ---
--- 38’ Goal! BRILLIANT GOAL! Herrera pings the perfect pass towards Rooney on the left side, and the captain strides into the area. He fakes a shot and slips in Lingard instead, who opens up his body and slots it into the bottom corner! ---
(37’) Real signs of motivation now from Newcastle as they've put United under all sorts of pressure in the last few minutes. Van Gaal has a decision to make on Fellaini, who is already on a yellow and looks like a ticking time bomb whenever the hosts attack.
--- 35’ Yellow card The referee pulls play back to book Tiote for a very clumsy challenge on the back of Herrera's calf. It's a deserved booking, and the 51st yellow card for Newcastle this season. ---
(33’) Fellaini needs to calm down. He pulls Colback down during a dangerous Newcastle move but play goes on, and Janmaat skips into the area ahead of Lingard. The United man trips him, but the referee opts against awarding another penalty! Newcastle had a case there as Lingard got nowhere near the ball!
(31’) DE GEA SAVES UNITED! An excellent one-two from Mitrovic and Wijnaldum has Smalling caught in no man's land, leaving the Dutchman with only the Spanish keeper to beat from inside the box. However, a low leg save keeps United's clean sheet intact!
--- 30’ Yellow card Wijnaldum attempts to skip between two players down the left, and just as he's about to wriggle free, herrera comes in with a late leg and trips him up, earning him a booking. ---
(29’) ROONEY FLUFFS HIS LINES! Fellaini nearly sells Blind short with a backpass, but then sticks in an important toe to release Lingard down the right on the break. He then plays in his captain, who takes aim from inside the box but drags it wide!
(27’) A lot of United's attacking threat is coming down the right, and with Fellaini motoring from box to box, the home side have a lot of aerial defending to do thanks to a series of crosses.
--- 25’ Yellow card Fellaini collects a cross inside the area, and tries to shoot on the turn, but three players block him. Instead of giving up on the chance, he barges right into the crowd, upends a Newcastle man and is booked for his clumsiness. ---
(23’) Newcastle try another cross but Fellaini, patrolling at the back post, comes up with another strong header to get rid of the danger. His first instinct this evening has been to drop back in his own area.
(21’) Janmaat has a chance to create an opening with space on the left flank and the ball, but he hooks it well over his teammates and out of play. That sums up what Newcastle have offered in attack.
(19’) United are having it all their own way in terms of possession, with goalscoring chances the only thing lacking from their play. I don't think that Mitrovic has touched the ball yet for Newcastle.
(17’) This is extremely slack from the home side in the midfield, who are turning the ball over like clockwork. Every mistake is greeted by a groan from the frustrated crowd. This is a team bang out of form and it's showing.
(15’) I've just seen the penalty replay again, and you could probably make the case that Mbemba's arm was extended more than normal. Makes it a little less harsh on the Magpies and just highlights the difficulty of the referee's job in the modern game.
(13’) The nerves are starting to spread around the Newcastle ranks as United keep the pressure on. Young's ball into the area is cleared nervously, and possession stays camped around the Magpies penalty area.
(11’) Newcastle are aggrieved, but there's no time for hard feelings as Martial sprints down the right flank to chase a pass from Herrera, but Janmaat gets back in time to make an accomplished sliding challenge to snuff out the danger. Good defensive play.
--- 9’ Goal! ROONEY DOES IT AGAIN! Like he did against Sheffield United in the FA Cup, the captain buries it from the spot, this time hitting it low to the goalkeeper's left. ---
(8’) PENALTY TO MANCHESTER UNITED! Harsh one for Newcastle to swallow as Mbemba is called for a handball while tangling with Fellaini from a high ball. It did hit his hand but there was no way it was deliberate. Up steps the captain...
(7’) Manchester United start to get forward more, and they're looking to get crosses into the area. Fellaini is starting to move forward, and Darmian attempts to pick him out, but it's cleared out for a corner.
(5’) No chances to report yet, but its the home team who have made the more encouraging start to this game. It's been mostly Manchester United defending around their own box, which they've done well so far.
(3’) Slow start to this one, as you might expect. Newcastle win an early corner, but Fellaini deals with the aerial threat with impunity. The first goal is going to be so, so vital in this game.
(1’) Off we go!
Juan Mata's streak of starting every league game this season has ended as he is replaced by Jesse Lingard in the XI. Morgan Schneiderlin mans the middle with Ashley Young, meaning that Bastian Schweinsteiger and Cameron Borthwick-Jackson drop out after their run out in the FA Cup win against Sheffield United.
Fabricio Coloccini shakes off a thigh complaint to start this game, meaning that McClaren makes only one change from his team's loss to Watford. Jack Colback steps into the side, replacing Kevin Mbabu.
Man United subs: Romero, McNair, Borthwick-Jackson, Mata, Depay, Weir, Pereira.
Man United (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Young, Smalling, Blind, Darmian; Fellaini, Schneiderlin; Lingard, Herrera, Martial; Rooney.
Newcastle subs: Sterry, Marveaux, Gouffran, De Jong, Darlow, Lascalles, Toney.
Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Elliot; Janmaat, Mbemba, Coloccini, Dummett; Tiote, Colback; Sissoko, Wijnamdum, Ayoze Perez; Mitrovic.
Newcastle have lost 25 times against Manchester United in the Premier League, with Arsenal the only other top-flight opponent to have beaten them that number of times. The Red Devils' last 12 league trips to this ground have been extremely profitable, with nine wins, two draws and only a solitary defeat.
Fifth place Man United have fast become one of the most uninspiring teams to watch in Europe. While their 17 goals conceded is bettered only by Tottenham in the Premier League, watching the Red Devils has become an exercise in patience, to put it kindly. Goals and general attacking endeavour has been largely absent, and even under-fire manager Louis van Gaal has admitted that he gets bored watching his charges play.
Steve McClaren's Newcastle side are in all sorts of trouble at the moment. They currently sit in the relegation zone, although a win tonight would provisionally move them out of the bottom three. The Magpies haven't scored in their last four games - which they have all lost by a 1-0 scoreline.
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League clash between Newcastle and Manchester United at St. James' Park. Both sides are struggling for goals in the top flight this season, so let's hope that they buck that trend tonight. Stick with us for all the action.

FULL TIME! West Brom strike late to snatch a point at Stamford Bridge, with Hiddink's men being held to a 2-2 draw on home soil. The hosts took the lead through Azpilicueta, with a McAuley own goal also helping their cause, but strikes from Gardner and McClean ensure that the Baggies won't go home empty handed! That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Diego Costa goes down on the edge of the penalty box, claiming that he was brought to ground by McAuley, but the referee isn't interested! Moments later, Azpilicueta goes down due to a supposed arm in the face, but yet again the official has no intention of giving a foul.
(90’) Chelsea need to be careful with their approach to the dying stages of this game, given that West Brom have shown themselves to be a real handful on the break. Berahino and Sessegnon have got plenty of energy between them.
(90’) There are four minutes of stoppage time.
(88’) Suddenly, the complexion of this game has totally changed! Chelsea are now needing to find another goal, with this contest getting very stretched indeed. Diego Costa joins in with hunting for possession, with West Brom happy to launch long passes into wide areas for their substitutes to chase.
--- 86’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! MCCLEAN MAKES IT 2-2! The ex-Sunderland man gets some good fortune, with the ball falling to him on the edge of the box! It only takes a touch for the West Brom man to sweep a strike into the bottom corner and beyond the despairing dive of Courtois! ---
--- 85’ Yellow card Azpilicueta makes a poor challenge on the edge of his own penalty area, as West Brom continue to pile on the pressure. ---
(84’) McClean tries to flick a dangerous header back into the penalty box, but Zouma comes across to defuse the situation. The visitors maintain their pressure, but an eventual opportunity to shoot for Fletcher is charged down! Chelsea have their backs to the wall as we head into the last five minutes at Stamford Bridge.
(82’) Kenedy goes close, with the Brazilian substitute driving towards the edge of the box! When he gets to the 25-yard mark, he fires a low drive towards the right-hand post, but it zips into the advertising hoardings! Chelsea are more than happy to retain possession and slow things down, with only their front three going gallivanting forward.
(80’) Berahino shoots from the right-hand side, but the Englishman can only fire a fairly comfortable effort within Courtois' grasp! West Brom are really trying to force the issue at the moment, with the likes of Kenedy and Willian needing to give their defence a little bit of respite.
--- 78’ Substitution Matic is introduced for the hosts, with ex-Barcelona midfielder Fabregas trudging off after putting in plenty of miles this evening. Hiddink just needs to perk up his midfield slightly. ---
(77’) Diego Costa tries to drive through the heart of the visiting defence, but McAuley makes a cynical tackle to deny the Spain international. Willian takes the resulting free kick, teeing up Zouma, but the former Saint Etienne defender leathers an awful attempt into the stands! He won't want to see a replay of that.
(75’) West Brom have it all to do during the final quarter of an hour, with Pulis' men needing to come up with an equaliser and fast. The Baggies respond with a lengthy spell of possession, but a cross in from the right is headed away by Terry! Chelsea counter, but once again Myhill is on hand to frustrate and deny Diego Costa.
--- 73’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! MCAULEY PUTS THE BALL IN HIS OWN NET! Willian drives down the left-hand side, using two stepovers to wrongfoot Evans! The Brazilian fires a low cross in towards the near post, with McAuley and Kenedy stretching for it! The final touch appears to come off the West Brom defender, but Chelsea don't care! ---
(72’) A red card might not be out of the question as we head into the last 20 minutes, with plenty of players having issues with one another. West Brom threaten, with Berahino racing down the left-hand side, but Zouma comes across to take the ball off the substitute's boot.
--- 70’ Yellow card McClean also sees yellow for his part in the disagreement, as the referee continuing to have to keep the lid on this contest. ---
--- 70’ Yellow card Courtois gets a card for squaring up to McClean, with the Belgium international not really needing to get involved there. ---
--- 68’ Yellow card Myhill gets a yellow card for the away side, with tempers continuing to boil over at Stamford Bridge. The referee is really struggling to keep on top of things. ---
(68’) Berahino tries to curl a right-footed effort towards the top right-hand corner, but McClean gets in the way! The former Sunderland man blocks what could have been a testing attempt for Courtois to deny. Chelsea break down the other end, but Kenedy is forced into fouling Dawson.
--- 67’ Substitution Rondon is withdrawn for the away side, with Sessegnon introduced. The away side are opting for a more mobile front two for the late 20 minutes. ---
(66’) Chelsea are enjoying all of the possession at the moment, but West Brom are continuing to stand firm. Oscar tries to flick a neat through ball into the path of Diego Costa, but McAuley makes a vital intervention. The away side are struggling to break out of their own half for more than a few moments at a time, as it stands.
(64’) We're well into the final half an hour in the capital, with Chelsea desperately trying to push their way towards another favourable result. Willian breaks to the left byline, before cutting back a cross for Diego Costa, but the Spaniard can only hammer a shot into the side netting with the aid of a deflection! Hiddink's men are piling on the pressure.
(62’) Willian tries to curl a teasing cross towards the back post, but Oscar is unable to scamper to the byline in time to keep it in! Chelsea keep the pressure on, with Diego Costa winning a corner on the left flank, but the Blues can't make anything of it. Moments later, Myhill is called into action by Kenedy, but the substitute can't even sting the Welshman's palms.
--- 60’ Substitution Berahino comes into the game for the away side, with Yacob taking his leave, much to the anger of the home support. ---
(59’) Willian tries his luck from the resulting free kick, with the Brazil international only able to curl a terribly weighted effort over the crossbar. On the bench, Berahino is getting ready for the visitors, with Yacob perhaps the man to be replaced - before he gets dismissed.
(58’) Diego Costa is brought down on the edge of the penalty area by Yacob, with the ex-Valladolid forward adamant that the Argentine midfielder should be sent off! The West Brom man has made a couple of poor challenges since picking up a yellow card in the first half, with Pulis perhaps needing to look to his bench before long.
(57’) Myhill is forced into a save at his near post, after Kenedy was teed up unselfishly by Oscar! The Brazilian substitute's attempt took a wicked deflection, but it wasn't enough to put off the Welsh goalkeeper. The atmosphere has gone a little bit flat, despite some fiery scenes on the field.
(55’) Brunt is the target of a back-post cross, but Terry rises well to defuse the situation. West Brom are having their fair share of opportunities in the second half, with Pulis' men certainly not sitting back and waiting to hit the Blues on the counter.
(53’) Tempers continue to flare at Stamford Bridge, with Diego Costa probably needing to watch his step for the final half an hour or so. Chelsea break down the left-hand side, with the visiting goalkeeper able to gather a poor cross from Azpilicueta, but West Brom's players are adamant that Diego Costa followed in unnecessarily on Myhill.
(51’) Dawson breaks down the right-hand side, with the West Brom full-back able to whip in a very dangerous delivery! Rondon tries to meet the ball at the near post with his header, but Zouma gets there first to concede a corner! The resulting set piece is half cleared, but the visitors keep their pressure on, before a tame header from McClean is saved by Courtois.
--- 49’ Yellow card Diego Costa gets a deserved yellow card, after sliding in very late on Gardner. There can be no complaints from the former Atletico man. ---
(48’) Ivanovic is released down the right-hand side, but can only win a corner from Evans. Moments earlier, Willian had wanted a free kick for handball on the edge of the erea, but Gardner didn't appear to know what was going on. The resulting set piece is nodded behind for a second time by Yacob, with the next being claimed by Myhill after a flick on from Diego Costa.
--- 46’ Substitution Kenedy comes into the game at the break, with the very disappointing Pedro taking his leave. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! West Brom have fought valiantly up until this point, with Pulis' side definitely making life difficult for the hosts. For Chelsea's fans, however, anything less than three points will be a disappointment.
HALF TIME! The two sides go in level at the break, with West Brom mustering up a fantastic equaliser against Chelsea due to a wonderful Gardner strike. Azpilicueta opened the scoring, with the hosts having the better of the chances, but Hiddink's men have since struggled to take the game by the scruff of the neck.
(45’) Fletcher manages to win a free kick from Mikel in a good position, with the Nigerian midfielder deliberately blocking off his man. West Brom load the box with red shirts, but the eventual delivery can only result in pinball! Chelsea clear their lines, with Diego Costa streaking away on the counter, but the referee blows for half time! The Spaniard isn't very happy at all!
(45’) There are three minutes of stoppage time.
(45’) Olsson and Diego Costa are calmed down by the referee, with both having plenty to say to each other. Despite apparently making up, the two players continue their conversation immediately and it doesn't appear they're set to be the best of friends.
(43’) Diego Costa is the target of a diagonal ball into the penalty area, but Evans does well to rise up and head clear! West Brom respond with a counter attack, but a cross from McClean is hacked away by Azpilicueta simply. Not long remains for Chelsea to force the issue before the interval.
(41’) Rondon goes close! The Venezuela internatonal lines up a powerful attempt from 20 yards out, after using his body well to evade Terry! The former Rubin Kazan striker can only plant a dipping effort into the stands, after it whistled beyond the angle of post and bar!
(39’) Narrowly over five minutes are left on the clock in the first half, with Chelsea pressing on for a second of the evening. Fabregas slides a pass into Pedro, with the ex-Barca midfielder trying to pick out Diego Costa with his first touch, but again the Spain international gifts possession away. Not the best of halves for the diminutive winger.
(37’) The away side are sitting deep, with Pulis' men happy to invite plenty of pressure on. The former Stoke coach may have to consider a change at the break, however, with the already cautioned Yacob getting into some nervy situations. Myhill is forced into action to deny a powerful header, before a shot from Oscar is charged down by Olsson!
(35’) Dawson lashes a no-nonsense clearance away from danger, with West Brom surely happy to battle their way towards the half-time break at 0-0. A long ball is pumped up into Diego Costa, but the Spaniard is outmuscled by Olsson! Myhill gathers up the scraps.
--- 33’ Assist Fletcher helped to harry Pedro, before sliding a stabbed pass into the onrushing Gardner. The West Brom substitute did the rest! ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! GARDNER WITH A BEAUTY! West Brom win the ball high upfield, due a terrible pass from Pedro, with Gardner able to drive towards the edge of the penalty area as a result! The ex-Sunderland midfielder unleashes a low drive, finding the bottom corner in emphatic fashion! The Baggies are level! ---
(31’) The opening half an hour has been hard fought, with Diego Costa and company causing a few problems for Myhill. West Brom, however, threaten through Gardner, with the ex-Aston Villa man needing to be dispossessed after bursting into the box. Chelsea counter at speed, but their move only results in Diego Costa blazing over the crossbar!
(29’) Fabregas drives into the area, after a neat interchange of play, but the ex-Barcelona midfielder is charged down when attempting to shoot. West Brom respond with a counter, but McClean is unable to burst beyond Ivanovic. The Blues are looking pretty solid defensively, with Terry able to beat Rondon in the air.
(27’) Chelsea may have the lead, but they certainly aren't in total control at Stamford Bridge. The hosts are starting to see a little more of the ball, but West Brom can threaten from the wide areas. Hiddink's men try and work Pedro into a shooting position on the edge of the box, but Olsson clears.
--- 25’ Yellow card Yacob is forced to make a very cynical tackle, after West Brom surrendered possession in a terrible situation. With a few Chelsea players racing into a sparsely populated opposition half, the Argentine midfielder had little choice but to pull play back. ---
(24’) Mikel gives away a foul in a dangerous area, with Courtois needing to assemble a sizeable wall. Brunt looks to be the potential aggressor, with the midfielder hanging up a cross to the back post. Courtois is forced into a near-post save, parrying away a fairly tame header.
(22’) Chelsea look to force their advantage with another break down the left flank, but Oscar opts to shoot from the edge of the box. Instead of seeing the ball curl into the top corner, the Brazilian is forced to painfully watch a terrible effort arrow into the crowd.
--- 20’ Assist Ivanovic is released to the right byline by Willian, before curling a sumptuous delivery towards the far post! Wonderful cross from the Serbia international. ---
--- 20’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! AZPILICUETA OPENS THE SCORING! The left-back is picked out at the back post, after making a storming run to the far upright. All that is left for the Spaniard to do, is to place a cushioned finish over the despairing dive of Myhill. ---
(19’) Diego Costa and McAuley have a war of words off the ball, with the two appearing to not be too enamoured with each other. Chelsea respond with a counter attack, but Olsson slides in brilliantly to deny Pedro on the periphery of the penalty box. Hiddink's men haven't been able force Myhill into a tough save quite yet.
(17’) Good save from Courtois! Dawson is picked out by a free-kick delivery, with the West Brom defender able to power a close-range header towards the near post! Chelsea's shot-stopper gets down smartly to push the ball around his upright. The resulting corner, however, is cleared with ease.
(15’) Gardner shoots over! The substitute takes aim from the very edge of the penalty area, but can only lift a poor attempt well beyond the target. After a shaky first few minutes, West Brom have recovered and now look to be able to legitimately trouble the hosts.
(14’) Fletcher goes close! The ex-Man United midfielder is found in space in the penalty area, but a lunging block from Terry is enough to deny the West Brom man! The resulting corner is whipped in from the right, but heads through a ruck of bodies and clear of the danger zone.
(12’) Terry loses his footing for the home side, but fortunately for Chelsea their captain is able to cushion a header back to Courtois. West Brom launch an attack moments later, with McClean whipping in a cross from the left, but Brunt is unable to beat Azpilicueta in the air. Pulis' men are looking to try and get a foothold in this contest.
(10’) Diego Costa is released down the right-hand side, before attempting to slide a neat pass into the path of Pedro! Brunt tracks back, however, to make a very timely interception. West Brom are struggling to deal with the ex-Atletico Madrid forward's pace and power, it seems.
(9’) Willian jinks in from the right-hand side, before firing a low drive just beyond the far post! Myhill was at full stretch, but did appear to have an on-target strike within his reach. Chelsea continue to threaten while driving forward with intent on the counter.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this evening…
With both sides struggling at the back whilst scoring plenty of goals at the other end of the pitch, tonight’s game has the potential to be a high scoring one. Saturday’s comfortable 3-0 win against Norwich City was only the second time since the start of November that today’s hosts have managed to keep a clean sheet, whilst in the league Everton have managed to achieve that feat just twice since the middle of September. Meanwhile, the Sky Blues have scored 10 times in their last five games, whilst their opponents have netted nine goals during the same period. As a result, this evening’s clash could be decided by which striker is feeling most hungry.
As for City, last Wednesday’s Capital One Cup defeat will have been a blow, but their minds will now be focussed entirely on continuing their push for the Premier League crown. After playing four consecutive games away from home, today’s clash sees them return to the Etihad for the first time since Boxing Day, when they comfortably beat struggling Sunderland 4-1. Manuel Pellegrini’s side have fared far better at home than they have on the road, winning 10 of their last 11 encounters, and they will be hoping to continue that good form today as they aim to keep the pressure on current league leaders Arsenal, who sit three points clear of the Sky Blues but face what could be a difficult clash away to Liverpool this evening.
Today is the second of three times that these two sides will have to meet each other over a two-and-a-half-week period, and it comes just seven days after Everton placed one foot in the Capital One Cup final with a 2-1 win against City at Goodison Park. Whilst they will no doubt be on a high after that victory, domestically things look very different for the Toffees, who have won just one of their last seven Premier League games, with none of their six victories this season coming against teams in the top half of the table. As a result, they currently sit in 11th place, two points behind both ninth-place Watford and 10th-place Stoke City and with a potentially tricky tie to play against Chelsea in just three days’ time.

Mane pounces on another loose ball and surges towards the box but is unable to feed Davis with his attempted backheel. Koeman's side really should have more than just the one goal. (52’) Southampton have continued to develop the momentum they built in the first half since the restart, with Watford being kept back inside their own half and forced to defend. Something needs to change from Flores, because they are largely relying on long balls into Ighalo and he doesn't look very happy about it.
(50’) Play restarts from the corner and Gomes is untroubled, something he'll certainly be pleased with. The ball goes behind and as he takes the goal-kick he offers a little wince. Arlauskis is warming up on the far side just in case Flores is forced to make a change.
(49’) There were claims for a handball against Mane, but they were ignored. Gomes has remained down and is reciving treatment from the medical staff. He's been helped back to his feet and should be able to continue, but he's got a corner to defend instantly and he hasn't looked particularly comfortable dealing with those beforehand.
(47’) OFF THE LINE! A cross from the right by Targett is controlled on the chest by Mane. The ball loops towards goal, drawing Gomes off his line, who punches it onto the head of the Southampton forward. Prodl is alert and gets back to stop the rebound dropping into the back of the net, putting the ball behind for a corner!
(46’) We are back underway!
HALF-TIME - Southampton 1-0 Watford: Koeman's side have completely controlled the first half, penning the visitors back inside their own half for prolonged periods and scoring the game's only goal through Long. They could have had a couple more had Mane proved more clinical in the final third - one of his efforts coming back off the post while he failed to round Gomes late in the period. Flores will need strong words for his players as they've looked off the pace so far tonight.
(45’) There's the half-time whistle!
(45’) We are going to have an additional minute before the interval.
(44’) Mane is presented with another chance to score but he is unable to take it, with Gomes racing off his line and stopping him from getting around him and slotting a simple finish into the back of the net.
(42’) Southampton are unrelenting in their search for a second goal. Cedric loops a cross into the box from the right wing and Long towers over Prodl to connect with a header. The striker fails to generate enough power to trouble Gomes from 15 yards, and the Brazilian is left with a comfortable collection.
(40’) Another corner is attacked unconvincingly by Gomes and Southampton maintain the pressure. Cedric cuts a ball back from the byline which Watson is unable to get away. The ball falls to Fonte and he snatches at it and sends an attempt flying harmlessly over the top.
(38’) Watford have really been let off the hook there but they need to tighten up and concentrate, otherwise this match could well get beyond them.
(36’) MANE HAS TO SCORE! Jurado panics under pressure on the left and decides to play a square ball towards Prodl in the middle. He doesn't spot Mane lurking nearby and the Senegalese gets to the pass first. His touch puts him one-on-one with Gomes and he takes his time before sliding a shot towards the bottom corner. It starts curling away from the target as soon as it leaves his foot and clips the base of the post on its way behind!
(34’) Flores will surely be pleased if his side can get into the interval with just the one goal in the match. They're struggling to get Deeney and Ighalo involved, while Southampton's high press is really troubling them.
(32’) Capoue is caught in possession with Southampton pressing high and causing the visitors all sorts of problems. Davis attempts to release Long but the striker goes too early and is adjudged offside by the official on the far side.
(30’) Targett whips another sensation cross in from the left but Holebas manages to get to it ahead of his man and cushion the ball back to Gomes. The Southampton left-back is having a strong performance tonight.
(28’) Great work from Ighalo! The striker is released down the left by Capoue and squares up Fonte on the edge of the box. He chops inside him but sees his strike at goal deflected behind by Bertrand. That's the first time Watford have really worried the hosts.
(27’) Holebas is back on and looks like he may be fine to continue, but it's certainly something to keep an eye on. Cedric has already been rather adventurous this evening but it could encourage him to increase his attacking forays further.
(26’) Holebas has hobbled off the pitch and didn't look particularly comfortable. Could Flores be forced into an early change? Anya would be the likely replacement.
--- 24’ Yellow card Cedric races into the box to try and pounce on the clearance but he catches Holebas and the referee awards a free-kick to the visitors and shows the Portuguese a yellow card. ---
(24’) GOOD SAVE! Nyom fails to get the ball clear down near the corner flag, with Targett blocking his attempted clearance. The ricochet floats into the box along the byline and Long latches onto it. The Irishman attempts to loop an effort beyond Gomes, but the Brazilian gets a vital hand to it and parries it into the danger area.
(23’) Gomes flaps at a couple of corners, producing unconvincing punches that do not relieve the pressure on his defence. The first one went straight to Targett and his rasping left-footed strike was deflected just wide.
(21’) MANE! The Senegalese picks up the ball on the left and dribbles across the top of the box, working space for a shot. He finally spots a gap in which to pull the trigger and his effort flicks off the leg of Prodl. Gomes reacts well to spring to his left and parry the attempt around the post.
(19’) Southampton certainly do not look like a side that have won just one of their last four home games. They're forcing Watford to defend deep and absorb pressure.
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAL!! SOUTHAMPTON TAKE THE LEAD! They've applied much of the pressure tonight and they now have their reward. Targett whips a fantastic cross into the box from a deep position on the left and Long gets ahead of Britos to steer it into the back of the net and beyond Gomes with his head! ---
--- 17’ Assist M. Targett provided the assist. ---
(15’) Abdi rolls a pass out to the right for Nyom as the visitors finally get out of their own half and apply some pressure to the Southampton defence. The right-back's delivery is aimed at Ighalo but is headed away from the box by Fonte.
(13’) Mane and Long combine in a clever one-two on the left wing but the former is unable to provide a finishing touch from the return pass. Britos did well to get across and apply pressure on the Senegalese forward. It proved to be enough to put the Southampton man off and Watford managed to remove the threat as a result.
(11’) Holebas does well to frustrate Cedric as he tries to twist and turn his way past him near the corner flag. Watford quickly look to clear but it goes straight to a Southampton shirt and the pressure is soon on once more. Flores will no doubt become increasingly alarmed the longer this goes on.
(10’) Long rises up and flicks a pass from deep into the area which Davis attempts to latch onto. Gomes reads it well and comes off his line to claim it, but Watford soon surrender possession and Romeu lashes a wild strike over the top from 25 yards.
(8’) Mane is picked out inside the box on the left-hand side and attempts to cut a pass back for Long. It's too far behind the Irishman, however, and the Watford defence intercepts and clears the danger. That's better from the hosts, though. They're penning Flores' men back inside their own half.
(7’) Southampton have certainly seen more of the possession during the early exchanges. They are also the only side to have threatened in behind up to now. There isn't much urgency from either side at the moment, though.
(5’) Ighalo attempts to make his first run in behind the Southampton defence but he's adjudged offside. The Nigerian was heading away from goal, but he will need to keep a closer eye on the line as the game continues. Southampton move the ball forward well and Davis spreads the play out to Targett on the left with a great pass. The left-back gets to it before it rolls out of play and stands a great cross up in the centre of the area but Long is unable to do anything with it after a great first touch and Watford clear.
(3’) Van Dijk attempts to release Cedric down the right but his pass his intercepted by the nearest marker. Watford show patience on the ball and knock it across the pitch inside their own half before Holebas eventually looks to send a long pass down the left wing. It's closed down by Davis and the visitors have a throw-in inside their own half.

The teams are heading out onto the pitch and kick-off will be upon us in just a few short moments!

FULL TIME: STOKE CITY 3-1 NORWICH CITY
(90’) There goes the final whistle and Stoke move up to seventh in the Premier League!
(90’) Norwich look to force a late consolation as we enter the first of three additional minutes. A nice cross to the back post just evades Jerome, however.
(90’) NEARLY! From the resulting corner, Shawcross meets it with a fierce volley but the defender is in the right position to make an important block.
(89’) ALMOST! Crouch's eyes light up as the ball drops nicely for him. He attempts an audacious scissor kick, but just misses making the vital contact and Norwich clear.
(88’) We are into the last couple of minutes of normal time and Stoke are looking very comfortable in possession. The clock is ticking down for them.
(86’) GOOD SAVE! Stoke are awarded a corner which is met by Crouch on the volley, but Rudd shows good alertness to beat it away to safety.
(84’) Afellay shows he is more suited to heart of midfield this evening as he tries his luck from distance, but sends it high and wide into the stands.
--- 82’ Substitution The final change of the night comes from Hughes, who introduces Peter Crouch in place of the impressive Joselu. ---
(80’) That has surely put the game beyond Norwich now. The visitors are stll battling away, however, and will fight to the death in search of a way back into this game.
--- 78’ Goal! GAME OVER!!! Stoke go 3-1 up after Bennett puts through his own net! A free kick is floated into the area and glances past Rudd off the head of the unfortunate Bennett. ---
--- 77’ Yellow card Tettey is the first player to receive a yellow card this evening following a needless and cynical foul on Joselu. ---
--- 76’ Substitution Stoke clearly looking to shore things up, as Marco van Ginkel comes on in place of the impressive Arnautovic. ---
--- 75’ Substitution The final throw of the dice from Neil sees him withdraw Mbokani in favour of former Stoke player Cameron Jerome, who receives a generous reception from his old fans. ---
(73’) What can Norwich do in response? They showed good character to get themselves back into the game, but now need to do so again if they are to leave the Britannia with at least a point.
(71’) The ball falls for Redmond to strike from the edge of the penalty area. He is unable to direct it towards the target, though, and Butland watches it wide.
(69’) That was a beautiful strike from Joselu to put Stoke back in front. As things stand, they will move up to seventh if they can hold on.
--- 67’ Assist Afellay laid the ball into the path of Joselu. ---
--- 67’ Goal! GREAT STRIKE - STOKE BACK IN FRONT!!! Bassong heads Shawcross' long ball away but only as far as Afellay, who lays it off for Joselu. The striker takes a touch and drills the ball brilliantly into the bottom corner beyond the dive of Rudd. ---
(65’) Pieters did well to beat Redmond along the touchline down the left and delivered a very dangerous cross, which flashed right across the face of goal and out for a throw-in.
--- 63’ Substitution A second change for the Canaries sees Matt Jarvis make his return from injury in place of Hoolahan. ---
--- 62’ Substitution Norwich make their first change of the night, with Odjidja-Ofoe making way to be replaced by Nathan Redmond. ---
(60’) As we hit the hour-mark, Stoke are slowly moving themselves back on top in possession. They are keeping the ball well but need to apply more pressure on the Norwich defence.
(58’) That goal has really thrown the cat amongst the pigeons. What a fantastic strike it was from Howson and all of a sudden, we are all level with everything to play for at the Britannia.
--- 56’ Substitution Stoke immediately make a change, as a disappointing Bojan makes way for Peter Odemwingie. ---
--- 55’ Assist Odjidja-Ofoe brilliantly cushioned the ball into the path of Howson. ---
--- 55’ Goal! WHAT A STRIKE!!! Norwich equalise in emphatic style! Odjidja-Ofoe cushions Hoolahan's cross into the path of Howson, who unleashes a vicious strike into the top corner leaving Butland with no chance. What a fantastic equaliser! ---
(53’) Stoke come forward again with Arnautovic flicking on Johnson's cross. It is just too far away from Joselu, though, and Rudd is able to collect.
(51’) Norwich look to respond immediately as Brady sends the ball in from the left. Wollscheid is in the right place at the right time, though, to make the clearance.
--- 49’ Assist Arnautovic showed great resilience to win the ball back and deliver a very inviting cross. ---
--- 49’ Goal! STOKE TAKE THE LEAD!!! They make the extra man count early in the second half! Arnautovic shows good resilience to win the ball back and deliver a wonderful cross, before Walters peels away at the far post to steer it past Rudd. ---
(48’) Norwich under pressure here as Stoke have the ball deep inside their half. They do well to deal with a corner, before doing the same with the subsequent ball back into the box.
(46’) KICK OFF! Mr Swarbrick blows his whistle and Norwich get the ball rolling once more.
The teams are back on the field and the second half is about to get underway.
Stoke were very much on top towards the end of the first half after Norwich went down to 10 men. They just need a goal to really hammer home their advantage after the break. Gary O'Neil's moment of madness has put the visitors under pressure for the remainder of this game.

(45’) Mr Swarbrick blows his whistle and brings the first half to a close.
(45’) We are now into the first of two additional minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half.
(44’) Norwich have a corner after Shawcross is forced to put the ball behind under pressure from Odjidja-Ofoe. This is a good opportunity for the visitors...
(42’) We are into the final three minutes of the first half at the Britannia. It is still goalless as we approach the break but a goal for Stoke would be crucial now, you feel.
(40’) Joselu wins a long ball forward from Wollscheid and it breaks kindly for Walters. He gets his shot away, but endangers the spectators more than Rudd in the end.
(39’) Stoke will now be keen to make their extra man count before half time. It would be a huge blow for Norwich if they were unable to hold out until the break.
(37’) OUCH! Joselu felt the effects of the slippery surface as he slid into the advertising hoarding. It looked painful but he should be OK to continue.
(35’) Understandably, the red card and subsequent tactical reshuffle from Norwich has taken a lot of sting out of the game. The flow has gone missing for the moment.
(33’) There was absolutely no need for that challenge from O'Neil. He only has himself to blame, but his team mates now have to play nearly an hour with 10 men.
--- 31’ Red card! WHAT WAS HE DOING?! O'Neil goes needlessly sliding into the back of Afellay, who was letting the ball run out of play. Hughes is off the bench incensed by the challenge and the referee is quick to produce the red card. A real moment of madness from the midfielder and completely irresponsible. ---
(30’) CHANCE! Norwich pump the ball into the box and it breaks kindly for Bennett. He puts plenty of venom behind his shot, but hits it straight at Butland who beats the ball away.
(29’) NERVY! Butland's blushes are spared, just! He sends his clearance straight to Hoolahan, who hits the ball straight back first time. It is always drifting, however, and Johnson and Butland watch it all the way past the far post.
(27’) CHANCE! Arnautovic plays a beautifully timed ball in behind the Norwich defence for Joselu to run onto. He looks to chip the advancing Rudd, but catches it wrong and sends it wide of the target.
(26’) Norwich have the ball deep inside their opponents' half. They put another nice move together, but Mkobani is unable to control the final ball and it runs behind for a goal kick.

(22’) Whelan shows good vision to pick out Johnson, who steps inside and lets fly with his left foot. His shot is deflected behind and Stoke have a corner...
(20’) Afellay gives the ball away to Mkobani in the middle of the park, but recovers brilliantly to make a vital interception as the Norwich striker embarks on a dangerous run forward.
(18’) Stoke put a neat move together with crisp passing around the Norwich area. The ball goes out wide to Arnautovic, but his cross is well dealt with by the defence.
(17’) Why not?! Some space opens up in front of Howson as the Stoke defence backs off. He tries his luck from 25 yards, but sends his shot high into the stands.
(15’) Another quickfire counter attack from Stoke sees Arnautovic find some space down the left. Rudd reads his cross very well, however, and comes out to collect.
(13’) Stoke deal with the set piece well and try to put pressure on Norwich at the other end. The ball is worked out to Pieters down the left flank, but his cross is poor and goes behind for a goal kick.

(9’) Arguably, Norwich have settled into their rhythm the quicker of the two sides inside the opening nine minutes here. They are knocking the ball around well and Stoke are struggling to really gain a foothold at the moment.
(7’) GOOD SAVE! Arnautovic chases a long ball forward and gets a clean strike away, but Rudd springs to his right well to tip it wide of the far post.
(6’) This is a tough game to call tonight. Stoke have lost just twice at home in the Premier League since August, while Norwich have won three of their last four matches.
(4’) Norwich come forward and Tettey finds space to whip the ball into the box, but Stoke are alert and able to clear to safety.
(2’) Stoke make a bright start to the game and enjoy time on the ball. Johnson looks to switch it to Pieters on the opposite flank, but the left-back is unable to get it under his control and sees it drift out for a throw-in.

The result leaves Swansea in 17th, just a point above Sunderland and Newcastle, who now sit in 18th and 19th respectively. Next up for Sam Allardyce's side are Tottenham, while Alan Curtis' men host Watford.
Swansea can definitely consider themselves unfortuante this evening. After drawing level through Sigurdsson's spot-kick, the hosts had Kyle Naughton unfairly sent off. Though Ayew did fire them back in front before the interval, Sunderland made their numerical advantage pay in the second half, with Van Aanaholt's goal levelling proceedings before Defoe's second and third goals sealed the victory.
FULL-TIME!!! Sunderland celebrate a hugely significant victory here. It has finished 4-2 to Sam Allardyce's side against 10-man Swansea City. It was a fantastic game at the Liberty Stadium, and certainly has huge implications at the bottom of the table.
(90’) GOOD SAVE!!! Sigurdsson tries his luck with a venomous strike from distance, but Mannone gets across to parry it away.
(90’) Swansea are still searching for a late consolation, here. Barrow finds Gomis in the area with a precise pass, but the former Lyon forward is unable to shirk off O'Shea.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution We're entering added time now at the Liberty Stadium, and there will be one more change for Swansea. Ayew - who has had a fantastic game today - being taken off for Jack Cork. ---
--- 86’ Substitution A final substitution for the visitors, as Jeremain Lens is taken off, with Allardyce introducing Duncan Watmore in his place. ---
--- 85’ Assist Van Aanholt has been superb tonight, and it was a fantastic run capped off with a terrific pass to find Defoe in the six-yard box. ---
--- 85’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAALLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!! DEFOE SEALS THE VICTORY WITH HIS HAT-TRICK! There is no doubt about this one, as Van Aanholt, following clever link-up play with Lens, powers into the area before finding Defoe, who prods home to claim the three points for the visitors. ---
--- 83’ Substitution A substitution with a back-story now, as former Swansea striker Danny Graham comes on for Fabio Borini. He has netted just one goal during his time on Wearside. ---
(82’) Just under 10 minutes left of what is an enthralling affair at the Liberty. Swansea are pressing high - they have little choice but to do so as they search desperately for a leveller. Barrow forges an opportunity down the right, but his cross is cut out at source by Van Aanholt. Sunderland counter, but Johnson is caught offside.
--- 80’ Yellow card A booking now for Patrick van Aanholt, who scythed down Barrow cynically. ---
(79’) Poor! Swansea work a patient, neat move down the left flank. Ki eventually picks it up at an acute angle on the edge of the area, but his cross is directed straight into the side-netting.
--- 77’ Substitution Substitution Wayne Routledge Bafetimbi Gomis ---
(74’) CLOSE! Taylor, yet to score his first Swansea goal, combines with Routledge down the left before driving towards Sunderland's area. He attempts to find the bottom corner with a driven, low effort, but his strike whistles just wide.
--- 73’ Substitution A first change of the game for Sunderland, then, as Jack Rodwell - making his return from a short-spell on the sidelines with a hamstring injury - replaces Lee Cattermole. ---
(70’) DISALLOWED! Defoe thinks he has netted a hat-trick to double Sunderland's one-goal advantage, but this time he is given offside, though it was a typically clever finish from the Sunderland man after latching onto another smart pass from Johnson.
(69’) Sunderland win a free-kick deep in Swansea territory. Johnson whips a cross in, but it is nowhere near any of his teammates and floats harmlessly wide, to the disgust of his manager.

--- 61’ Goal! GOOOOOAAALLLL!!!! DEFOE PUTS SUNDERLAND BACK AHEAD! What a turn-around we have had here! Johnson slides a neat throughball into the path of the aforementioned striker, who makes no mistake in slotting a composed finish past the hapless Fabianski. Swansea 2-3 Sunderland! ---

(56’) Appeals for a penalty from Swansea after Sigurdsson's strike appeared to hit the arm of O'Shea are waived away by the referee, and Sunderland counter at pace but Ki manages to track back and regain possession.

(52’) Curtis will be furious at his side's slack start to the second half. They may have 10 men, but they are putting no pressure on the ball, instead simply sitting deep and inviting Sunderland onto them. It could be a long night now for the hosts...
--- 49’ Assist It was patient and neat build up play from Sunderland. Johnson did well to spot the run of Van Aanholt and find the Dutchman with a smart pass, though the deflection from Fernandez was the major factor in that strike nestling into the back of the net. ---
--- 49’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAALLLLL!!! SUNDERLAND ARE LEVEL! Van Aanholt has been Sunderland’s biggest threat all evening, and he is the one who has restored parity at the Liberty! It's definitley set up for another fascnitating half after the interval. A huge 45 minutes coming up for both of these sides!
HALF-TIME! Well, what a half of football we have had at the Liberty Stadium! It really has had everything, though referee Graham Scott has arguably been the centre of the controversy. After missing a clear-cut offside call for Defoe's opener, the offical then awarded Swansea a dubious penalty, which Sigurdsson duly converted. The teams are in from the Liberty, so without further ado, let’s check on the line-ups, starting with the hosts. Curtis makes two changes to the side that were beaten 2-1 at Old Trafford in their most recent league outing, with Kyle Naughton and Modou Barrow replacing Angel Rangel and Jack Cork, respectively. Andre Ayew is tasked with leading the line for the hosts, with Bafetimbi Gomis, who has been subject of reported interest from the Middle East in recent weeks, on  the bench. There is just the one change for Sunderland, with Jeremain Lens rewarded for his goal-scoring display against Arsenal in the FA Cup with a start on the right wing, Duncan Watmore dropping down to the bench, while former Swansea player Fabio Borini starts on the opposite flank.
The last time these sides met, back in August, they had to settle for a share of the spoils following a 1-1 draw at the Stadium of Light - the same scoreline of the corresponding fixture to tonight’s finished last term, In fact, though Swansea have lost just one of their last 15 league meetings with Sunderland, seven of the last 10 meetings have ended in a draw.
As for Sunderland, they finally brought a five-match losing streak to an end last time out in the league with a comfortable 3-1 victory over lowly Aston Villa. A win tonight would see Sam Allardyce’s side rise up to 18 points - level with their local rivals Newcastle United, who sealed the signing of Swansea midfielder Jonjo Shelvey for a reported £12million fee on Tuesday. However, history does not favour the visitors, who last claimed an away win against Swansea back in November 1963.
Both these sides will be desperate for a victory here. Swansea, who will have caretaker manager Alan Curtis at the helm until at least the end of the season, sit in 17th place heading into this game - one point above the relegation zone and four clear of their visitors tonight. They have managed just two wins in the league since August - though they have taken four points from the two home games that Curtis has been at the helm for. However, they suffered yet another set back last time out, the south Wales club falling victim to an FA Cup giant-killing as they were beaten 3-2 by Oxford United.
