(63’) Kane wins another corner for his side now as the hosts look to keep the pressure on. The England striker attempts a typical long-range effort from distance, which Huth bravely blocks and knocks out for a set-play.
(61’) BRILLIANT SAVE! Two fine pieces of goalkeeping in a matter of minutes! Lamela slips in Kane at the other end, inside the box, at an angle. He gets his shot away but Schmeichel makes himself big and flicks the ball onto the bar with his feet!
(59’) TERRIBLE ERROR! A howler from Walker puts his side in all sorts of trouble! He has Vardy chasing him as he looks to play a short ball back to his keeper. But his pass is underhit, allowing the Foxes striker to latch onto the ball before a quick-thinking Lloris darts out to smother the ball. He had to make that challenge!
(57’) SO CLOSE! That's possibly the closest we have come here! A superb cross from Davies is inviting as it is whipped in low with Kane and Lamela to aim for inside the area. It is the latter who connects with it, hitting an effort on goal which is deflected and drops just wide of the post for a corner! Inches wide there!
(55’) That Spurs free-kick comes to nothing as Leicester eventually break down the attack through Fuchs, who knocks the ball off Lamela near the corner flag to win his side a goal-kick as they restart from the back.
(53’) A succession of corners is eventually averted by the hosts who break on the counter attack with Kane leading the charge, before being knocked to the ground by Morgan who disputes the decision to award a free-kick just to the corner of the penalty area on the right-hand side.
(51’) VITAL BLOCK! That corner is played short again as Albrighton looks to thread in Vardy inside the six-yard box. He holds up the ball and swivels to get his shot away, but Kane sticks tight to his man and deflects his effort over the bar!
(50’) A well-worked short corner from Leicester sees play move out to Drinkwater on the edge of the box, yet his effort is blocked by the Spurs defence and rolls out for another corner on the other side. A good period of play here for the visitors.
(49’) Another set-piece, this time to the Foxes, as Kane commits a clumsy foul, allowing Fuchs to step up and curl a delivery into the box with his left foot. Spurs clear at the first attempt but the visitors retain play on the edge of the box and win a corner after Albrighton's cross is blocked.
(48’) An early corner to Tottenham on the left-hand side is scrambled away rather clumsily by Leicester. It is Morgan who first attempts to clear the danger, miskicking his clearance as the ball rebounds off the underside of his thigh, before Fuchs races off the goal-line to lash the ball away to safety.
(47’) A long ball is pumped forward from the kick-off but it rolls straight into the hands of Schmeichel in the Leicester goal. Spurs will want to make more of their chances in this half, having held 66 per cent of the possession in the first-half, but yet to find the opening goal.
(46’) SECOND HALF! We're back underway for the final 45 minutes of football, still in search for our first goal in this game, as Tottenham restart play kicking from left to right.
Set-pieces could have a part to play in this result as well with both winning their fair share of free-kicks and corners. Alderweireld has come closest in that respect, heading an effort into the ground to force Schmeichel into a finger-tip save over the bar.
We've not been without action then in that first-half, but we have been without any real clear-cut chances. A few long-range effort from Eriksen and Drinkwater for either side have forced both Schmeichel and Lloris into decent saves. But neither have really been tested inside the area.
(45’) HALF-TIME! That's the whistle for the interval as the score remains at 0-0.
(45’) We are going to end this half with just the one added minute, which Spurs start with a free-kick for a foul in their own half.
(44’) Tottenham clear their lines rather easily from that free-kick and are back on the front-foot once more as we enter the final couple of minutes in this half. Vardy and Okazaki have been restricted to little thus far - particularly the former, who is just coming back from minor groin surgery last week and trained with his side on Tuesday.
(42’) Mahrez wins a free-kick for his side now after knocking the ball past Davies, only for the Welsh left-back to collide into him. A chance now for the Foxes to cause some aerial danger with the delivery from Albrighton - who has one of the best crosses in this league.
(41’) Okazaki clears the second corner but only out to Eriksen, in that familiar position on the edge of the box. They look to float the ball back into the danger zone but it is headed away once again, leaving Spurs to try and build once again from the midfield.
(40’) Little for Leicester to shout about in these past 10 minutes with Spurs ending the half as they started - on the front-foot. Alli wins a corner this time on the left, knocking the ball off Simpson inside the area. Lamela steps up to take, which Morgan knocks over to another corner.
(38’) Some patient play from Spurs goes wasted as the ball is worked from left to right, before making its way to Davies on the edge of the box. He looks to lift a cross into a crowded penalty area but puts far too much weight on the delivery, which loops high over everyone.
(36’) A few boos around White Hart Lane now with the home crowd unhappy with the physical nature of those two recent challenges on Alli. The youngster, who has really burst onto the scene in the Premier League this season, is a marked man in this game it seems.
(35’) Simpson gets a little too tight on Alli, who is fouled for the second time in a short space of time, allowing Spurs to start an attack from near the half-way line. Play is slowly built towards the edge of the box but an effort from the England midfielder is blocked by a wall of blue shirts.
(33’) An inviting cross from Lamela as he races towards the byline, but his delivery is perhaps a little too powerful as he lifts it towards the back-post with nobody able to get on the end of it.
(32’) Strong defending from Dier sees him hold off Mahrez, who brings the ball forward midway through the Spurs half, and break up play. That enables a quick ball into the feet of Alli just past the half-way line as the hosts look to counter, but he is brought down by Kante.
(30’) CLOSE! A short corner is played to Kane on the left as Spurs work a move towards the edge of the box, to an unmarked Eriksen. He lets loose with a powerful effort on goal but it matched by his fellow Dane in goal as Schmeichel dives to his left to push the ball away from danger.
(28’) Kane is penalised for a push on Morgan as he races to win a long-ball forward into the Foxes box. The hosts have come under pressure in these past five or so minutes and know - if their earlier meeting wasn't testament to that already - that they are in for a tough game tonight. It's not going all their way at the minute.
(26’) BRILLIANT SAVE! A superb volley from Drinkwater on the edge of the area is hit with real conviction after a Fuchs throw-in finds him on the edge of the box. Lloris is forced into a fine save down low to his right, palming the ball out for a corner! A real open game, here!
(25’) Eriksen this time loses out to Okazaki, allowing Leicester to start another counter attack which is broken down by Spurs' Danish international, who brings down Drinkwater right next to the dug-out. A free-kick is awarded to the Foxes.
(23’) SUPERB COUNTER ATTACK! That is a brilliant bit of play from Leicester! They break quickly as Drinkwater wins the ball back in his own half, threading in Konte to race onto the ball in acres of space in Spurs' left-back position. He drives with the ball inside the area and plays in Okazaki, but he is closed down quickly and his effort is blocked.
(21’) Mahrez uses his experience to draw Davies into a cheap foul midway through the Spurs half, with Albrighton stepping up to curl this set-piece in towards the back-post. Okazaki is the target but Lloris does well to come off his line and claim the ball.
(20’) Leicester are slowly working their way back into this game now after a frantic start. With two up top, they offer a threat to a Spurs defence who have the best defensive record in the Premier League this season, having conceded just 16 goals.
(18’) SPURS IN TROUBLE! That's sloppy play from the hosts as Walker a poor throw-in back to his keeper. Lloris looks to have got himself out of trouble as he is closed down quick, only to give the ball away with pressure from Albrighton. Vardy picks up the ball inside the box who threads in Okazaki, whose snapshot drops just wide of the post from inside the area. A real let-off there!
(16’) Vardy attempts to relieve his defence of this constant, early pressure. He runs into the channels on the left-hand side and is faced by Walker, near the byline. The Foxes man tries to wiggle a way around his marker but, in an attempt to round him, the ball ricochets off his leg and out for a goal kick to the hosts.
(14’) Dier is the latest Spurs man to take a pop on the Leicester goal. The hosts work the ball towards the England man after a pass from Kane. He's in the centre of the pitch from around 25-yards out but his long-range strike whistles harmlessly over the bar.
(13’) The second corner is cleared but Spurs win the ball back in their own half and keep the pressure on. Play is spread out to the left as Davies overlaps, hitting a terrific zipping cross into the box. Lamela, on the back-post, cannot reach it, before a combination of Fuchs and Albrighton scramble the ball away.
(11’) JUST OVER! A right-wing corner is whipped in towards Alderweireld in the centre of the goal, who gets above his marker. He knocks his header into the ground which forces Schmeichel into a finger-tip save over his crossbar for another corner on the other side.
(10’) Ranieri, the Tinkerman, is waving frantically on the side-lines as he urges his side into an organised position at the back. He watches on as Walker, bombing forward from right-back, gets forward to attempt a cross into the box, which is blocked for a corner.
(8’) It has been all Spurs so far as the hosts have penned Leicester back into their own half. Their pressing play is quick, looking to spot the run of colleagues in the final third as this time Kane is sent through, inside the visitors' box, before a vital interception from Simpson knocks the ball back to Schmeichel, who clears.
(6’) Positive play again from Pochettino's men! Spurs break down the right-hand side with Eriksen keeping width. He lifts his head up to find Alli in acres of space on the edge of the box, with Drinkwater not able to get close enough. The former MK Dons man tries to curl a low shot into the corner of the net but it drops just wide of the post.
(5’) A period of sustained pressure from Spurs sees the ball switch from left to right as they attempt to work an opening past a compact Leicester defence. Alli, on the edge of the box, looks to thread an eye of the needle pass into Kane inside the area, but he is pulled back for offside.
(3’) A first shot of the game falls to the hosts through Eriksen as the midfielder carries the ball forward into the Foxes half and drives with it towards the edge of the box. He works an angle to fire a low effort on goal but iIt's easy for Schmeichel to deal with, at a good height.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are underway at White Hart Lane!
A host of changes then for both sides, as expected, from the fixture earlier on Sunday. Spurs make seven changes with only Alderweireld, Dier, Eriksen and Carroll retaining their places as Kane and Alli – fresh from his new contract extension, return to the starting line-up. Leicester make nine changes with Schmeichel and Kante the duo to keep their spot.
Substitutes: King, Gray, Ulloa, Dyer, Wasilewski, Schwarzer, Inler.
Leicester XI (4-4-2): Schmeichel; Simpson, Huth, Morgan, Fuchs; Mahrez, Kante, Drinkwater, Albrighton; Okazaki, Vardy.
Substitutes: Rose, Son, Vorm, Trippier, Dembele, Onomah, Wimmer.
Tottenham XI (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Walker, Alderweireld, Vertonghen, Davies; Dier, Carroll; Eriksen, Alli, Lamela; Kane.
If you're feeling a sense of deja vu with tonight's fixture, there's a very good reason for that. Tottenham and Leicester of course met at this very ground on Sunday in the FA Cup third-round. A late, controversial penalty from Harry Kane earned a replay for Spurs in a 2-2 draw, meaning the two sides face each other three times in just 10 days.
We have a top-four match-up tonight - and who would have expected that come the start of the season? Leicester are riding high in second place as the surprise package of the season, just two points of league leaders Arsenal. A prolific campaign for Jamie Vardy and Riyad Mahrez has propelled the Foxes into lofty heights as they dream of European football next year. Spurs, on the other hand, sit in fourth, with Mauricio Pochettino's young side one of the most exciting in the top-flight right now.
Hello and welcome to our LIVE commentary from the Premier League as Tottenham Hotspur welcome Leicester City to White Hart Lane, with kick-off in around 30 minutes.

As for Liverpool, they will be thoroughly disappointed with their performance today. It's been a topsy turvy season for them and they have failed to find any consistency whatsoever, and today's defeat was another low point for them. They remain in eighth place as a result but could drop to 10th if both Watford and Stoke City are victorious this afternoon.
The referee blows his whistle for the final time and confirms an impressive victory for West Ham. They thoroughly deserve all three points after putting in an excellent performance from start to finish, and they did wonderfully well to nullify Liverpool's front line before hitting them on the counter. The win moves them up to fifth place in the table, for now at least, just three points behind Tottenham Hotspur and, more importantly, a Champions League qualifying spot.
FULL-TIME: WEST HAM UNITED 2-0 LIVERPOOL
(90’) Liverpool push forward on yet another attack, which will surely be their last of the game, but West Ham have every available player back inside the their own half of the pitch to snuff out the danger. That is surely that for the visitors, who simply haven't been good enough today.
(90’) What a chance for Allen to get Liverpool back into the game! Coutinho drifts out to the left-hand side of the penalty area before whipping a lovely cross towards the back post. It meets the substitute, who, under no pressure whatsoever, has a great opportunity to score, but he ends up sending his bullet header just wide of the near post. He really should have done better with that!
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(89’) Great chance for Kouyate! Once again, West Ham pick Liverpool apart on the counter-attack, and this time it's Payet who flies forward. The Frenchman breaks towards the visitors' penalty area before picking out the aforementioned midfielder with a lovely through-ball, but his thumping strike is beaten away by Mignolet.
(88’) After sitting deep to successfully deal with another half-hearted Liverpool attacking move, West Ham try to break away quickly down the right flank as they look to hold onto the ball near the corner flag. Jenkinson battles hard with Smith but ends up fouling the youngster near the byline, resulting in a free kick for the visitors.
--- 86’ Substitution Antonio receives a standing ovation from the West Ham fans as he's replaced by Jenkinson in a defensive change for the hosts. ---
(84’) Carroll goes close to making it 3-0! West Ham break away incredibly quickly, with Antonio flying down the right flank before teeing up Noble. The captain penetrates the penalty area before forcing Mignolet into making a good save, before the aforementioned striker can only send his poked follow-up into the hands of Belgian.
--- 82’ Substitution Liverpool have made their final change of the game, and it's an attacking one, with Allen coming on to replace Sakho for the final 10 minutes. ---
(80’) It's all kicking off inside the penalty area! Yet another Liverpool corner results in a chance on goal for Lucas after Coutinho's thumping effort is blocked by Carroll near the line. The Brazilian defensive midfielder ends up skying his volley over the top of the crossbar before the visitors scream for a penalty, presumably thinking that the aforementioned West Ham striker had handled the ball, before Kouyate and Can are involved in a heated exchange of words.
(78’) Off the line! The resulting corner is nodded onto Lucas, who then unleashes a close-range strike. It looks set to find the bottom left-hand corner of the net but Noble is there to clear the danger with a vital volley.
(77’) Coutinho is fouled on the left wing, resulting in a free kick for Liverpool in a dangerous position. Lallana sends a fabulous ball into the middle of the penalty area, but Collins is there to nod it over the top of the crossbar before it can find Benteke.
(76’) Smith skips past Antonio on the left flank and heads towards the byline before sending a deep cross right onto the boot of Benteke, but once again the Belgian striker ends up skying his effort over the top of the crossbar.
(75’) Coutinho twists and turns on the edge of the West Ham penalty area before going one-on-one with Adrian, but the Brazilian's final touch is poor and, as a result, the Spaniard is able to dart out before dispossessing the attacking midfielder before he's able to unleash a shot.
(74’) Ibe threads a lovely through-ball into the left-hand side of the penalty area, where Smith beats Antonio with ease before breaking into the box. The youngster then looks to send a low cross towards Benteke but the aforementioned winger does well to recover before knocking the ball out for a corner, which Coutinho can only send into the hands of Adrian.
(72’) Liverpool move the ball around quickly just outside of the West Ham penalty area before Clyne whips a dangerous low cross towards the edge of the six-yard box. It looks set to find Benteke, but Ogbonna does wonderfully well to stick out a foot at the vital moment to stop it from doing so.
(70’) West Ham push forward once again before earning themselves a corner on the right flank. It's whipped in by Payet and is only half cleared by the Liverpool defence, resulting in it finding Obiang on the edge of the box, but the midfielder's attempted volley ends up flying safely wide of the near post.
(68’) What a chance for West Ham to make it 3-0! Payet and Cresswell link up wonderfully well on the left wing before the full-back chips a beautiful cross into the middle of the box. It finds Carroll, who forces Mignolet into making a great save with another bullet header. The goalkeeper's clearance can only find Antonio, but the Belgian then does well to save the follow-up strike as well.
(66’) Deep defending from West Ham once again frustrates the Liverpool front line, who are quickly running out of ideas whenever they're able to push into the final third of the pitch. As a result, Ibe decides to unleash a thumping strike from 30 yards out, but it's overhit and clears the top of the crossbar as a result.
--- 64’ Substitution Payet receives a rousing reception from the West Ham fans as he makes his way onto the pitch to replace Valencia. ---
(63’) West Ham are looking increasingly comfortable at both ends of the pitch, with Liverpool failing to cause them too many problems. The visitors are starting to tire and, as a result, the Hammers' defence are finding it easy to protect their two-goal lead.
--- 61’ Substitution And the second is Smith, who takes the place of Moreno. ---
--- 61’ Substitution Liverpool have decided to make a double substitution. The first player to come on is Lallana, who replaces Firmino. ---
(60’) Firmino is dragged to the ground by Obiang, resulting in a free kick for Liverpool in a dangerous position just outside of the West Ham penalty area. Coutinho steps up and unleashes a shot from the set-piece, but it fails to trouble Adrian before the ball bounces out for a goal kick.
(59’) Once again, a cross penetrates the West Ham penalty area and finds Benteke, but the Belgian is unable to fully control the ball before Lucas chests it into the hands of Adrian. It looks as if Liverpool are going to make a change as they desperately try to find a way back into the game.
(57’) Another chance for Benteke flies well wide of the goal! A looping cross finds the Belgian in front of goal, and he initially clips the ball over the head of Tomkins before unleashing a thumping volley, but it's completely mishit and clears the top of the crossbar by quite some distance.
--- 55’ Assist Once again, a West Ham goal is set up by a brilliant cross from the right wing. Moreno stepped up too quickly and left Noble in space down the flank, allowing him to control the ball under no pressure whatsoever before perfectly setting up Carroll. ---
--- 55’ Goal! GOAL! It's 2-0! Noble breaks down the right flank and takes advantage of the space left behind by Moreno, who is nowhere to be seen. The captain then swings a beautiful cross towards the back post, where Carroll rises high above Clyne before beating Mignolet with a bullet of a header that flies into the bottom right-hand corner of the net. West Ham are flying and the crowd are going wild! ---
(53’) After spending the opening seven minutes of the second period on the back foot, West Ham are finally able to break out of their own half of the pitch before earning themselves a throw-in on the left wing. Antonio flings it into the heart of the Liverpool box, where it looks set to find Carroll, but the striker is muscled away from the ball before Can clears the danger.
(52’) What a chance for Benteke! Moreno is left in far too much room on the left wing, allowing him to receive the ball comfortably before sending a bouncing cross into the middle of the box. It finds the big Belgian, but his first-time volley is completely mishit and ends up spinning well wide of the goal.
(50’) Clyne and FIrmino link up well on the right-hand side of the West Ham penalty area, with the latter being put under plenty of pressure from Ogbonna. The aforementioned right-back then fires a low cross into the middle of the box, but it's poorly hit and can only find Noble.
(48’) Ibe holds up the ball well before spinning and teeing up Coutinho, who immediately unleashes a thumping strike from 25 yards out. There's far too much power on the shot, however, and it ends up flying well over the top of the crossbar as a result.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
West Ham have certainly been the better of the two sides thus far, and, as a result, they head into the half-time break with a well-deserved one-goal lead. Early pressure from the hosts, coupled with poor defending from Liverpool, resulted in Antonio finding the back of the net after just 10 minutes, and from then onwards they've done well to sit back and defend against the visitors before attempting to pick them apart with counter-attacks. The Reds started to look better towards the end of the opening period, with Benteke, who has been largely shut out of the game, finding more joy in front of goal, but they still seem to be lacking that cutting edge in the final third of the pitch.
HALF-TIME: WEST HAM UNITED 1-0 LIVERPOOL
(45’) Another determined Liverpool attack, which will surely be their last of the first half, is once again dealt with by West Ham's strong centre-backs before Valencia tries to push forward, but he's clumsily tackled as he tries to break away, resulting in a free kick for the hosts that, unsurprisingly, they take their time with.
(45’) West Ham are unable to break out of their own half of the pitch, allowing Liverpool to flood forward once again. They win themselves a free kick on the left flank, which Moreno flings into the heart of the penalty area, but, as has been the case so many times thus far, Collins is there to clear the danger with a strong header.
(45’) Once again, Ibe and Firmino link up well on the edge of the West Ham penalty area before the Brazilian tries to spin and find a teammate, but this time Noble is there to dispossess him with a poked tackle before Kouyate attempts to break away on a counter-attack.
(45’) Can hits the crossbar! Ibe twists and turns on the right flank before cutting the ball into the feet of Firmino. With his back to goal, the Brazilian tees up the aforementioned German, who immediately unleashes a rocket of a shot that beats Adrian before ricocheting off the crossbar. That was much better from Liverpool!
(45’) West Ham are remaining deep inside their own half of the pitch as they look to take their slender lead into the half-time break. Liverpool work the ball around quickly just outside of the hosts' penalty area before Moreno eventually decides to unleash a strike from 25 yards out, but Obiang does well to cut it down and send it looping into the hands of Adrian.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be five minutes of added time.
(44’) A poor pass from Firmino sends the ball straight into the feet of Valencia, who immediately darts down the left flank. He heads towards the byline before trying to penetrate the penalty area, but the Brazilian does well to get back and atone for his error.
(42’) Cresswell goes close! A poor header from Lovren results in a throw-in for West Ham deep down the right flank. It's flung into the middle of the penalty area, where it's nodded onto the aforementioned left-back at the far post, but his thumping half-volley is deflected off the outstretched foot of Clyne and out for a corner.
(41’) Liverpool flood forward as they look to continue putting pressure on West Ham, but the hosts have almost every player back in their own half of the pitch and camped behind the ball. It eventually bounces out to Moreno on the left flank, but the Spaniard can only send his cross straight to Cresswell, who then chests it into the hands of Adrian.
--- 39’ Substitution Lanzini receives a standing ovation from the home fans as he gingerly makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Obiang. ---
(38’) There are worried looks on the faces of the West Ham fans, as it looks as if Lanzini's day is done. The Argentine drops to the ground off the ball and immediately points to his thigh, indicating that his previous injury has flared up once again.
(37’) Liverpool work the ball around really well just outside of the West Ham penalty area, with Benteke, who has looked sharper over the past few minutes, playing a particularly important role in the attacking move. The Belgian tees up Firmino, who then unleashes a thumping strike from the edge of the box, but he ends up scuffing it completely and it bounces well wide of its intended target.
(35’) Adrian stays down on the ground after being clattered into by Firmino, but after receiving medical treatment for a few moments he's able to continue once again.
(34’) Firmino goes close! Moreno picks up the ball on the left wing and immediately sends a dangerous cross into the heart of the West Ham penalty area. It finds Benteke, whose headed effort bounces off the chest of Carroll and into the path of the Brazilian. He only has Adrian to beat, but his poked, close-range strike ends up finding the safe hands of the Spaniard, who receives a knock on the nose in the aftermath.
(33’) Clyne breaks down the right flank and goes one-on-one with Cresswell, but he's unable to find a way past the West Ham full-back and is forced into firing a cross out for a corner. (31’) A half-hearted West Ham attacking move breaks down deep down the left wing, allowing Liverpool to try and break away quickly. Clyne and Ibe initially do well to skip past several players before the latter cuts inside and tees up Can, but the German takes too long on the ball and is dispossessed by a good tackle from Antonio.

He then tees up Valencia, who skips past Sakho but, off balance, ends up firing his close-range strike well wide of the goal. He really should have done better with that opportunity.
(27’) The ball bounces around the edge of the West Ham penalty area, with neither Coutinho nor Benteke able to beat the sea of defenders camped directly in front of them. The Brazilian is eventually able to tee up Ibe, who tries to beat Cresswell on the right-hand side of the box but, under pressure from the full-back, can only run the ball out of play for a goal kick.
(25’) What a chance for Benteke! A slip from Collins allows a bouncing pass from Firmino to find the Belgian just outside of the West Ham penalty area. He controls the ball well before trying to penetrate the box, but his final touch is poor and takes it away from his feet, allowing Tomkins to dive in and dispossess the striker with an excellent, and vital, sliding tackle.
(24’) After a few moments on the ground receiving medical treatment, Noble makes his way off the pitch, but it looks as if he's going to able to continue after making a quick recovery.

(21’) Great tackle by Moreno! A Liverpool corner quickly turns into a West Ham counter-attack, with Antonio charging down the left flank after a good clearance from Carroll. The winger cuts inside before teeing up Valencia, who then penetrates the penalty area, but just as he's about to shoot the aforementioned Spaniard dives in front of him to send the ball out for a corner.
--- 19’ Yellow card Lanzini cynically tugs on Can's shirt as the German tries to break away quickly, and as a result he ends up receiving the first yellow card of the game. ---
(18’) And now Antonio goes close once again! West Ham quickly win back possession thanks to good play from Cresswell down the left wing. The full-back then sends another dangerous cross into the penalty area, where it finds the aforementioned goalscorer in front of goal, but his poked shot ends up looping over the top of the crossbar.
(17’) Lanzini hits the post! The Argentine finds himself in space just outside of the Liverpool penalty area on the left-hand side of the pitch. After receiving the ball from Valencia he immediately unleashes an excellent 20-yard strike that swerves violently in the air before ricocheting off the woodwork and out of the box. Mignolet was left rooted to the spot and had no chance of stopping that!
(16’) Liverpool are currently bossing possession and working the ball around inside the West Ham half of the pitch, but the hosts are finding it easy to sit deep and defend against the visitors, who are failing to turn their dominance off the ball into chances on goal.
(14’) After weathering a West Ham storm, Liverpool patiently try to work their way towards the hosts' penalty area. Clyne and Ibe initially do well and link up just outside of the box, but just as he's about to unleash a cross the young winger is dispossessed by Noble.
(12’) Great chance for Carroll! Cresswell twists and turns on the left flank before chipping a beautiful cross into the heart of the penalty area. It drops straight onto the head of the aforementioned striker, but his downward header ends up bouncing into the hands of Mignolet.
--- 10’ Assist That was a wonderful cross from Valencia, but questions have to be asked of the Liverpool defence, who failed to close down the Ecuadorian and looked at sixes at sevens inside the penalty area. ---

West Ham head into today’s game with recent history on their side, and they will have fond memories of the 3-0 thumping that they handed Liverpool when the two sides last met back in August. A lot has changed since then, however, and the Hammers’ struggles in front of goal could damage their chances of beating a Reds back line that has looked far more solid in recent weeks. The East London club have scored just six times in their last nine league clashes, and they haven’t scored more than two goals in a game for over two and a half months. However, last weekend saw Andy Carroll come off the substitutes’ bench to hit the back of the net, and Slaven Bilic will be hoping that the former Liverpool striker can do the same today as they aim to record back-to-back wins for the first time since October.
As for Liverpool, they have struggled to find consistency in a season that has exposed the best and the worst of the team. Impressive victories against Chelsea and Manchester City were followed by disappointing defeats against Newcastle United and Watford, but they have started to look far more solid in recent weeks and head to Upton Park with back-to-back victories under their belts after beating both Leicester City and Sunderland over the Christmas period. The Reds now have a tough schedule to contend with, however, as they must play four times in the next week and a half, with all of their clashes coming away from home. As a result, tiredness could play havoc with their chances of reducing the gap between themselves and the top four, particularly with crucial league games against Arsenal and Manchester United to play in the space of just five days later this month.
East London plays host to the first Premier League clash of 2016, and it brings together two sides that are separated by just one place and one point after enjoying very similar seasons thus far. For West Ham, the latter half of 2015 was one that started in such promising fashion before descending into a series of frustrating and lacklustre results. Six of the Hammers’ opening 10 games of the season ended in victories, but since beating Chelsea towards the end of October they have gone on to win just once in nine domestic encounters. That victory came against Southampton on Monday and will no doubt have filled them with much-needed confidence after a string of disappointing draws, but boss Slaven Bilic will be well aware that there is still much work yet to be done if his side are to rediscover their early season form and keep the pressure firmly on the top five.

The referee brings an end to the game and the Chelsea fans and players immediately burst into celebration. They thoroughly deserve all three points after putting in arguably their best performance of the season, and it has resulted in their biggest victory of the league campaign. As for Chelsea, they have looked better in recent weeks but still in sit in an incredibly precarious position in the bottom half of the table. Just three points separate them and the relegation zone, and their record of just two wins from their last 10 Premier League games is a very worrying one. Monday evening saw them hold Manchester United to a goalless draw at Old Trafford, extending their unbeaten run to three games, but it was only their sixth point away from home this season, a record that is only marginally better than Sunderland and Aston Villa, the league’s bottom two sides. Today not only marks the first London derby of 2016 but it is also exactly one year to the day since Alan Pardew was appointed as manager of Palace. An excellent second half of last season has turned into a great first half of this one, and nine wins from 19 games means that they start the day in seventh place, just two points behind fifth-place Manchester United, who have already played this weekend. As a result, another win - which would be their third in five games - would send them above the Red Devils and back into fifth, setting them up wonderfully for back-to-back clashes against struggling Southampton and bottom-of-the-table Aston Villa.

Spurs will fancy their chances this afternoon. They are unbeaten in their last six against Everton - keeping a clean sheet in four of those - and are currently on a three-match winning streak. Meanwhile, the Toffees are looking to improve their recent record of one win in their last six.

But a draw it finishes and a good point for a much-changed Swansea side who now move two points clear of Newcastle United in the final relegation place.
Wilfried Zaha came close to sealing the three points just a minute from time after latching onto a pass from Yohan Cabaye inside the area and curling an effort on goal, only for it to drop agonizingly wide of the post. A Gylfi Sigurdsson free-kick at the other end forced Wayne Hennessey into a smart save at the other end just moments later.
Bamford had the chance to redeem himself later on after finding acres of space inside the area following a storming run from second-half substitute Jordan Mutch, but the midfielder took the effort on himself instead of opting to pass, and - in a game where chances were few and far between - that could have been a costly error.
A point a piece then for both Crystal Palace and Swansea City after a frustrating game. We saw little goal-mouth action in the first-half but the introduction of Patrick Bamford at the interval saw the Chelsea loanee have the best chance, yet squander it from yards out. A smart Lukasz Fabianski save denied him when he really should have scored.
(90’) FULL TIME! It's all over at Selhurst Park as we end as we started, with the score level at 0-0.
(90’) A SUPER SAVE! Sigurdsson steps up for the free-kick and shapes up for the shot from distance. He hits his effort with real venom and forces Hennessey into a stinging save as he palms the ball back out after diving to his left. That was going into the bottom corner of the net!
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card YELLOW! Hangeland earns himself a booking now after he trips Gomis to bring the Swans striker down in the Palace half. ---
(90’) Four minutes of added time have been given by the officials to end this clash.
(89’) JUST WIDE! Oh, so close! That is probably the closest we have come to a goal in this game as Cabaye threads through Zaha inside the area. He still has a lot to do as he drives forward on goal but his shot, at an angle, curls just wide of the corner of the net. Fabianski will be relieved to see that drop wide as he was beaten!
(87’) It is Palace who are ending the game the stronger of the two sides here as they pile on the pressure. Can Swansea hold on to keep their third consecutive Premier League clean sheet
(85’) A Swansea free-kick is played short by Sigurdsson, into the path of Ki, but the midfielder gives the ball away as he tries to float it into the area, allowing Palace to break in numbers!
(83’) GREAT RUN! A storming drive from Mutch - fresh from the bench - carves open the Swansea defence and forces men to commit. Williams is caught out which allows Bamford space inside the area for the pass. Yet the substitute goes for goal himself and lashes a powerful effort wide! He had better options there!
(81’) A fourth corner of the game now for the hosts as Zaha takes on Taylor on the right, near the corner flag, and sees his cross blocked. A delivery comes in but Swansea clear again in an all too familiar story.
(79’) Another chance from the set-piece for Palace as Cork and Cabaye tangle - not for the first time - leading to a free-kick midway into the Swansea half. But the delivery is whipped in by the France international and straight into the hands of Fabianski rushing off his line.
--- 77’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A final change for Swansea as Bartley comes on for Amat in the heart of defence. ---
--- 75’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! McArthur leaves the field now to be replaced by Mutch in a straight swap. ---
(73’) BRILLIANT SAVE! That looked destined for the net! McArthur flicks on the ball inside the area towards Bamford, who breaks free of the Swansea defence, but his shot from little more than 10-yards is saved at point-blank range by Fabianski!
--- 71’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Another change for Palace as Puncheon is brought off to be replaced by Lee. The winger makes his first appearance as a new father, having flew back to England yesterday following the birth of his child. ---
(69’) A little bit of panic at the back there from Palace as a free-kick causes danger in their area. It is Sigurdsson who delivers the cross, which bobbles around inside the box before Ward snatches at the clearance and manages to avert the danger at the second attempt.
(67’) Jedinak has been a real threat in aerial challenges today and has won almost every battle he has contested. If Palace improve their crossing - both from set-pieces and open play - he could prove the difference.
(66’) The free-kick is looped into the area towards Jedinak who once again wins his header, only for Williams to pounce on the loose ball and clear before Ward can latch onto it.
--- 65’ Yellow card YELLOW! A sloppy caution there for Ki who kicks the ball away after Sigurdsson brings down McArthur for a Palace free-kick. ---
(63’) Two of the last three encounters between these two have resulted in draws. We have little under half an hour of play if this one is to go another way.
(61’) CHANCE! That's more like it! A pot-shot from distance has caused all sorts of danger! It is Barrow who picks up the ball on the right, cutting inside and evading the path of Souare. He positions himself for the shot from distance and forces Hennessey to dive and palm the ball over the bar!
(60’) That's poor again from the free-kick as Palace look to dink a ball into the area, yet the delivery lacks any real conviction and Swansea clear once again. Plenty of chances to make the most out of these, but neither side has taken them.
--- 59’ Yellow card YELLOW! Ironic cheers from the home crowd now as Swansea record what they feel is an overdue booking after Taylor brings down Zaha, looking to break. ---
(58’) Another wasted set-piece, this time from Swansea, as Sigurdsson steps up for his first contribution only to float a cross straight onto the head of Hangeland in the Palace defence.
--- 57’ Yellow card YELLOW! A second caution of the game - and once again it is for a Palace player as Souare brings down Barrow near the corner flag in a good crossing position for Swansea. ---
--- 56’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Emnes is withdrawn as Sigurosson takes his place just behind the striker. ---
--- 56’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! Shelvey, who made his first appearance under caretaker manager Curtis in this game, comes off for Ki in the first of two changes for Swansea. ---
(54’) Time for a change? Palace are seeking a third consecutive win at home in the league today - they haven't done that since February 2014.
(52’) A much brighter start to this second half has seen both Palace and Swansea break with pace and urgency. The visitors do so again down the left-hand side as Ward gives chase to Emnes, but wins the throw-in for the hosts near the corner flag after the ball re-bounds of the Swans striker following a challenge.
(50’) Great interception! That could have spelled danger for Swansea there as the ball is curled in from the left, towards the far-post with Bamford the target. Yet Williams reads play well and manages to thrust his body in the way and flick the ball out for a corner. He had to make that, otherwise the Chelsea loanee was in!
(48’) CHANCE! That's the closest we have come! Cabaye whips in a terrific ball from a free-kick on the left which Hangeland meets first. He flicks the ball on with his head, forcing a smart save from Fabianski down low near the post. Dann tries to get to the re-bound but he is flagged for offside.
--- 46’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A first change of the game, and a much-needed one at the interval, as Chamakh comes off for Bamford. ---
(46’) SECOND HALF! We're back underway for the second period!
(1’) A combination of strong defensive work from Williams and Ki sees Palace win yet another corner. It is swung in towards Dann but Bartley is equal to him in the aerial challenge, forcing the former Birmingham defender to guide his header straight up into the air before it is cleared.
Well they've done us all a favour in calling time on that half. There has not been an awful lot to shout about for either side with the scores all level at 0-0. A little more urgency is needed in the final third for both teams as neither keeper has had a single shot to save.
(45’) HALF TIME! And the officials draw an end to the first half.
(44’) Another foul! And they are clocking them up here! Zaha plays the ball short to Cabaye on the left and Amat, eager to close the ball down quickly, flies in on the midfielder right under the feet of the referee. Palace fans want the defender to be booked but nothing is given.
(42’) Palace do this time win the free-kick on the left as Naughton brings down Zaha on the charge. It is swung in towards Jedinak but he cannot control the ball to get his shot away, leaving Palace frustrated again as the Swans clear the danger.
(40’) Another groan from the home crowd as Grimes appears to follow through with his studs in a challenge against McArthur right on the edge of the box, as Swansea look to clear. The Palace midfielder turns around to appeal to the referee but, again, nothing is given.
(38’) Souare does his best to whip in an inviting ball into the box after Puncheon sprays play out wide to him on the overlap, but his delivery fails to cause any danger as Williams clears his lines. We're yet to see one decent cross in this game.
(37’) A free-kick now to Palace midway into their own half, which is met by ironic cheers from the Selhurst Park faithful. They have felt things have not gone their way in this game, both in the decisions from the officials and through chances created.
(35’) That yellow card is a little harsh you could say, and you can understand the frustration of his manager on the sidelines as that has earned Cabaye a suspension - missing the clash with Chelsea.
--- 34’ Yellow card YELLOW! A first caution of the game here and it's a tough one for Pardew to take on the bench as he sees Cabaye disciplined for a high foot against Cork. ---
(31’) Great defending! A tricky run from Barrow on the right spells danger for the hosts, especially as Hangeland is taken out of the game with a drop of the shoulder. He skips into the box but Dann stands strong and takes the ball off his with ease.
(29’) Cabaye hooks in a free-kick from the left, midway through the Swans half after Naughton concedes the foul, but his floated delivery can only be helped on by Jedinak and lifted out for a goal-kick. Very little movement inside the area there.
(27’) A half-chance at the other end for the Swans as Shelvey carries the ball forward from midfield and looks to release Gomis in on goal, but Hennessey rushes out to quell the danger.
(25’) A little bit of confusion down the corner flag as Swansea rush out to close down an attack from the left. Some sections of the crowd are seeking a corner, but referee Neil Swarbrick points for a throw-in instead. Can the Eagles build on this?
(23’) Recent meetings between these two have produced few goals for Palace. They have scored just three times in their last eight league matches, winning just one in the process and drawing another three.
(21’) We have not seen a lot in this game so far but Zaha looks the most likely to turn it on its head. He wins a free-kick after a foul from Taylor, which Cabaye takes, but the header from Hangeland inside the area falls to nobody.
(20’) Cabaye and Cork tangle in the middle of the pitch now after the Swansea man brings his opponent down. Not a lot in that, more of a coming together, but the France international is not happy with that challenge as the two square up.
(18’) The corner is played short from the left and whipped into the area by Zaha, but Fabianski does well to rush off his line and punch the ball clear before Cabaye's follow-up shot on the edge of the box is lashed high and wide.
(17’) Palace press again from the left as Zaha plays in Puncheon, who is hugging the touch-line. He backs away from the ball as it rolls towards him, allowing Amat to jump in with a sliding tackle and it deflects back off the Swansea man for a corner for the hosts.
(16’) Chamakh again is the target man as Dann pumps a long ball forward from the back, which is dummied by Puncheon on the left, although the former Arsenal striker isn't quite on the same wave-length as his teammate as the pass evades his path and rolls out for a throw-in.
(14’) A high defensive line from the Swans catches Chamakh offside as he looks to peel off the shoulder of the back-line and latch onto a long ball forward from Souare. The visitors have a free-kick midway through their own half on the right-hand side.
(12’) Barrow wins a corner for Swansea on the other side and they look to play it short with Shelvey, but they waste it, soon losing possession before Naughton brings down Zaha as the Palace winger looks to break.
(11’) Curtis' side are just starting to settle now as they look to spring a move into life down the right-hand side. It is Naughton who plays an early long ball towards Emnes - a willing runner into the corner. He holds off Hangeland and whips in a cross but Dann clears at the near-post.
(9’) A little better from the Swans there as they keep hold of possession and play the ball around the back in their own half, yet a sloppy pass from Grimes - looking to hook it around the corner of his marker and towards the half-way line - is hit straight out of play.
(7’) Swansea manage to relieve their defence of that early pressure as Emnes does well to win a throw-in near the corner flag after playing the ball off McArthur. They will hope to keep play in the Palace half after a nervy start to this game.
(5’) Puncheon swings in the cross from the free-kick and, after a bit of a scramble inside the area, Swansea clear their lines. There is a half-hearted appeal for a penalty against Shelvey in the process as he challenges for the ball with McArthur, but very little to shout about as play is waved on.
(3’) That's a rash challenge from Shelvey as the former Liverpool man looks to track back and cut out the surging run by Souare, from left-back, only to catch his trailing leg with a sliding tackle. This is a decent crossing position from the free-kick for Palace.
(2’) A nearly-moment there for Zaha early on down the right-hand side. He shows ability on the ball near the corner flag to take on Grimes. The England winger appears to be boxed in but skips past the youngster to race into the area and cut a pass back towards Chamakh, only for Shelvey to intercept and clear.
(1’) KICK-OFF! Swansea get the game underway, shooting from right to left.
It’s a host of changes for caretaker manager Alan Curtis in the visiting corner, with just three players surviving from the victory over West Brom over the weekend. Lukasz Fabianski, Ashley Williams and Neil Taylor are the only ones to keep their place in a side that sees young midfielder Matt Grimes make his first league appearance of the season.
Eagles boss Pardew makes four changes from the side that drew on Boxing Day as Brede Hangeland, Mile Jedinak, Yahan Cabaye and Marouane Chamakh come in for Damien Delaney, Joe Ledley, Jordon Mutch and Fraizer Campbell. Patrick Bamford returns to the bench after recovering from an injury.
Substitutes: Ki, Ayew, Nordfeldt, Montero, Sigurdsson, Bartley, Kingsley.
Swansea City XI (4-2-3-1):  Fabianski; Naughton, Amat, Williams, Taylor; Cork, Shelvey; Grimes, Emnes, Barrow; Gomis.
Substitutes: Speroni, Bamford, Campbell, Lee, Mutch, Ledley, Kelly.

Swansea have seen their fortunes take a turn for the worst this season, just months after Garry Monk guided his side to an eighth place finish and a club record points total in the Premier League. His dismissal leaves caretaker boss Alan Curtis to steady the ship – and quell fears of relegation. Victory over West Brom on Saturday was their first win in seven league games.
Alan Pardew’s high-flying Eagles have been one of the surprise packages of the season so far and find themselves in fifth place on 30 points, occupying the Europa League spot in the process, after a 0-0 draw with Bournemouth on Boxing Day kept them above of Manchester United. That result also helped extend their unbeaten run in the league to five games.
Hello and a very warm welcome to our LIVE commentary from the Premier League as Crystal Palace host Swansea City at Selhurst Park. We are edging near to the end of the calendar year now with just one match to play - and both could do with a win here, for very different reasons.

Well, that's all from me for now. It has finished Everton 3-4 Stoke City at Goodison Park in the Premier League. Until next time, thank you and goodbye!
The win lifts Stoke back into the top-half and there can now be no doubting the quality of Mark Hughes' side. Everton may slip as low as 11th depending on the result of Southampton v Leicester in one of the later kick-offs. After claiming a last-gasp victory themselves last time out, Martinez' side will be truly devasted to have once again thrown away the points and lose ground in their pursuit of European football.
It was a brilliant performance from the visitors, who ran Everton's defence ragged from the off. Xherdan Shaqiri's first goals in English football, either side of another Romelu Lukaku strike, put them 2-1 ahead heading into the interval, though the hosts should have had a penalty themselves for a foul on Seamus Coleman. Lukaku levelled proceedings with a fantastic finish shortly after the hour-mark, before Ross Barkley and Deulofeu combined to put Roberto Martinez' side ahead, only for Joselu's maiden Stoke goal to restore parity, before Arnautovic won and converted a 91st minute penalty.
FULL-TIME! Mark Clattenburg blows the whistle, and this excellent, enthralling clash comes to an end, with Stoke sealing a 4-3 victory thanks to Marko Arnautovic's last-gasp penalty. The hosts - who had taken the lead in teh 71st minute thanks to Gerard Deulofeu - will feel even more aggreived, as it qas quite evident that John Stones had won the ball in the challenge that led to the spot-kick.
(90’) A final throw of the dice now for the hosts, as Stones lofts a throw-in into the area, but Stoke are able to clear their lines.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card PENALTY TO STOKE! IT IS SO UNLCUKY FOR EVERTON! Stones dives in and wins the ball from Arnautovic, but despite initially deciding to wave play on, Mark Clattenburg elects to award the penalty. ---
--- 90’ +1 Goal! GOOOOOAAALLLLLL!!! Terrific penalty from Arnautovic, who despite slipping in his run up, converts the spot-kick down the centre of the net, giving Howard no chance. ---
(90’) WHAT A CHANCE! Coleman combines excellently with Deulofeu. The latter's cross is blocked and rebounds to the aforementioned full-back, who brings it under control, but flashes his strike over.
(89’) Van Ginkel's first involvement is to win a free-kick off Stones. Stoke work a short set-piece before lifting in a cross, but the move is brought back for an offside from Shawcross.
--- 87’ Substitution A final substitution fro Stoke, as two-goal hero Xherdan Shaqiri is replaced by Marco van Ginkel. ---
(86’) Terrific positioning from Johnson, who has been fantastic today, as he heads a deep cross from Deulofeu clear. Stoke counter as Afellay plays it in behind to Walters, but the boyhood Evertonian is flagged for offside.
(85’) Poor from Coleman, as he brings a promising Everton move to an end with a stray run offside. Can eitehr side muster a final chance hear?
(83’) UNLUCKY! Deulofeu whips in a superb delivery from the resulting set-piece, which Butland does brilliantly to claw away from danger.
(82’) Everton should have had a penalty there! Barry drives a volley against Joselu, who handballs it. Mark Clattenburg awards a free-kick to the hosts, but it appeared that the Spaniard was inside the Stoke area.
--- 80’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAALLLLLLLL!!! JOSELU PULLS STOKE LEVEL! A wonderful cross from Arnautovic causes all sorts of problems for Howard, who flaps at it. The rebound falls to the Stoke substitute, who powers a venomous first-time finish into the top-corner. What a game! But that is poor from the Everton goalkeeper! ---
--- 79’ Substitution An attacking substitution now for Stoke, as Huges replaces holding-midfielder Geoff Cameron with the versatile Jonathan Walters. ---
(78’) CLOSE! Fantastic play from Everton once again, as Deulofeu jinks his way past three Stoke defenders after initially blocking Pieters' attempted clearence. The Spanish winger goes for goal with a toe-poked effort, but it creeps wide of the left-hand upright.
(77’) A first poor moment of the game from Lukaku, as he drills a risky pass across field to Funes-Mori, who has to react sharply to prevent Shaqiri latching onto it and having a free-run on Everton's goal.
(76’) Great pressing from Deulofeu, who nips in ahead of Afellay to tee it off to Barry. The veteran midfielder lofts a pass towards Lukaku, but Wollscheid gets across well to stem the danger.
(74’) CHANCE FOR STOKE! Everton maintain possession well, but you still feel their may be another twist in this game. And it almost comes from a sloppy pass from Naismith, who plays it straight into the path of Arnautovic. The forward looks set to tap it home, but Howard is out swiftly to hook it clear. A let off for the hosts!
--- 71’ Assist We have seen five world-class goals at Goodison today, and the fifth is perhaps the best. Lukaku was agian involved as he laid it off to Barkley, who picked out Deulofeu with a precise cross. The Everton midfielder has been excellent today, palying from a deeper position since McCarthy's injury. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAALLLL FOR EVERTON!!! Beutiful football from Martinez' side, as Lukaku slips a wonderful pass into the path of the on-rushing Barkley. The England midfielder gets his head up and squares it perfectly for Deulofeu, who simply taps home into an open goal. Everton 3-2 Stoke! ---
(70’) More scintillating play from Lukaku, who holds it up expertly before laying it off to Kone, but the Ivorian's first touch is too heavy and Pieters intercepts.
(68’) CLOSE! The Goodison crowd are well on side with their team now, as Lukaku leads a fantastic counter attack with a lung-bursting run. Deulofeu drifts in from the right and combines with the aforementioned Belgian, who lays a spuerb first-time pass to Naismith, whose first-time effort is deflected just wide.
--- 65’ Substitution And that will be the last action of the game from Cleverley, as he is replaced by Steven Naismith, despite having only come on as a substitute himself in the first half. Surely that is an injury? ---
--- 64’ Assist It was an absolutely superb assist from Tom Cleverley, who picked up the ball deep down the left before looping a perfect pass into the path of the in-form Lukaku, who never looked likely to miss. ---
--- 64’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLLL!!!! LUKAKU LEVLES IT UP AGAIN! Another fantastic goal, as Cleverley lofts an inch-perfect pass over the top to Lukaku, who takes it down on his chest before poking an expert finish past Butland. ---

(63’) BAD MISS! Everton have had the better of this half, but they are yet to truly forge a clean-cut opening. Stoke work it out from the back superbly once again, only for Coleman to shirk off Bojan. Deulofeu leads the counter and combines with Cleverley to tee up Kone, but the Ivorian's strike is a poor one.
(61’) Stoke concede possession deep in their own half, but Kone cannot capitalise. The ball eventually comes back to Deulofeu, who wriggles his way into the area and attempts a one-two with Lukaku, but the latter's return pass goes astray.
(59’) Barkley again acts the playmaker for the hosts as he kick-starts a flowing move from deep with a pass to Kone, who tees up Deulofeu. The Spaniard again beats his man and finds Barkley on the edge of the area, but his effort is blocked by Wollscheid.
(57’) Neat play from Stoke on the counter, with Bojan weaving his way into the area and causing Coleman to hook it out of play. The resulting throw-in leads to a strike from Cameron, but Howard is equal to it.

(49’) A huge round of applause for Everton fan-favourite Lukaku, as after he concedes possession, the 22-year-old tracks back superbly to win it back off the bombarding Pieters.
(48’) UNLUCKY! A smart move by Everton results in Lukaku feeding Cleverley in the area. The former Manchester United man twists and turns before drilling an effort goalwards, but Johnson stands his ground to get in a good block.

(46’) SECOND-HALF! Mark Clattenburg sounds his whistle and an un-changed Everton get the game back under way. Can they muster a comeback?
Everton are looking extremely vulnerable at the back, mainly down to the link-up play of Arnautovic, Bojan and Shaqiri than any particular individual faults. Kone has offered Galloway little protection, meaning that the Stoke maestro is often finding himself one-on-one with the youngster, and is taking full advantage. Martinez has already been forced into one change due to McCarthy's unfortunate injury, but he may well want to draft in the more experienced Leighton Baines from the bench to try and stem the free-flowing Stoke attacking play. At the other end, the hosts have also looked dangerous, with Barkley at his best and Lukaku grabbing his almost customary goal. We should certainly be in for an enthralling second-half.
HALF-TIME! What a game we have had hear at Goodison, where we have witnessed three fabulous goals from two sides showing plenty of attacking intent. Bojan, Arnautovic and Shaqiri have caused havoc against Everton's back-line, though the hosts' had had the better of the half since their equaliser, and can consider themselves unfortunate to not have been awarded a pentalty for Pieters' challenge on Coleman.

(44’) CLOSE! Aranutovic almost got in-behind Everton's back-line then, as Shaqiri fired in a precise throughball, but the Austrian had already been flagged for offside.

The last clash between Norwich and Aston Villa was back in March of 2014 in the Premier League. Like today's match, it was another relegation battle and on that occasion it was the Villans who ran out 4-1 winners thanks to a double from Christian Benteke, a Leandro Bacuna strike, and an own goal from Sebastian Bassong. How much would Garde like to replicate a similar result this afternoon?!
With the January transfer window approaching later this week, both sides will no doubt take the opportunity to scour the football world for a recognised goalscoring striker, as nobody has stepped up to the plate to rack up a decent tally so far. Villa have netted just 15 times in their 18 games, while Cameron Jerome as Norwich's main centre forward has scored only three times, with winger Nathan Redmond ahead on four.
However, Norwich's current predicament is nowhere near as full of gloom as that of Aston Villa. The Villans have flirted with relegation more often than not in the past few years, but their plight has never appeared as hopeless as this season as they are nine points from safety immediately after Christmas. Tim Sherwood's tenure as manager was halted rather promptly after their poor start to the season, which lead to former Lyon boss Remi Garde being given the role of saviour, but the Frenchman hasn't faired much better despite an encouraging opening draw against Manchester City in his first game in charge.
The Canaries actually started the season in relatively good form, and lost just two of their opening seven games, but have struggled to maintain any kind of performance consistency since then, thus resulting in the threat of relegation still proving a real prospect. The inconsistency of Alex Neil's men can be further highlighted by their results in that they have managed fantastic wins such as defeating Manchester United 2-1 at Old Trafford, only to lose in emphatic fashion around the same time period against Watford, with Tottenham also piling on the misery on Boxing Day with a comfortable 3-0 win.
Today's clash sees two of the relegation candidates in England's top flight do battle for what will likely prove to be a vital three points come the end of the season. Newly promoted Norwich are currently one place out of the dropzone with 17 points taken from their opening 18 matches, while Aston Villa are rock bottom, having notched up just eight points from the same amount of fixtures.

(28’) Alli lets fly from the left-hand side, with the young midfielder cutting inside onto his right foot! Unfortunately for the England international, however, he gets his angles all wrong and sends a low effort skidding into the advertising hoardings.

(90’) THERE IT IS! The referee blows for full time and West Brom have their first win in six.
(90’) West Brom have a corner and that is surely it now...
(90’) We are now into the second of four additional minutes at the end of this game. It is looking like West Brom will hold on, but Newcastle still have time to find the equaliser.
(90’) Newcastle are playing with 10 men for the time being as Sissoko limps to the sidelines. He looked to break away before being stopped in his tracks by a strong challenge from Gardner, and he is clearly still feeling the effects of it.

(87’) GREAT SAVE! West Brom launch another counter attack with Sessegnon finding Berahino, who had peeled away into space. His shot looks destined for the top corner, but Darlow springs across brilliantly to push it away.

(84’) Berahino does really well for his side as he holds off Coloccini and Colback in the corner, before eventually being awarded a free kick by the linesman.
(82’) GREAT SAVE! That would have put the game to bed. West Brom launch the counter attack with Anichebe running at and taking on Coloccini. He only has Darlow to beat, but the keeper does well to deny the striker.

(74’) OOOPS! A sliced clearance from Darlow has presented West Brom with a corner and an unexpected opportunity to capitalise. He caught Mbemba's bouncing back pass all wrong and sent it behind.

(55’) OFF THE BAR! Perez's corner is met by Dummett, who sees his floating header crash against the woodwork, before Coloccini's follow-up effort deflects behind again.

(52’) It has been all West Brom so far in this second half. They have had almost all of the possession and Newcastle are struggling to get hold of the ball.
(50’) STAT ATTACK! Newcastle will upset the history book if they fail to score this afternoon. That has only happened in two of their previous 28 meetings with West Brom.
(48’) West Brom are applying good pressure in these opening minutes of the second half. Newcastle are holding firm at the moment, but can they weather the storm?
(46’) KICK OFF! Mike Jones blows his whistle and Newcastle get the ball rolling in the second half.
The teams are making their way back out onto the field and the second half is about to get underway.
As things stand in the Premier League, a win would be enough to lift Newcastle out of the relegation zone while three points would see West Brom move six clear of the bottom three.
That was a very entertaining opening 45 minutes at The Hawthorns. All that has been missing so far from both sides' performances is a goal.
