Giroud is teed up on the edge of the box by Walcott, with the Frenchman shooting and forcing a save from Boruc! The Polish goalkeeper then spills the ball to the aforementioned Englishman, who can only roll a terrible attempt wide of the post from an offside position!
(69’) Giroud now misses a half chance! Ozil and Ramsey cause problems down the left-hand side with a low cross miscontrolled by the France international! Moments later, Bellerin marauds forward down the right, but Ozil is unable to steer home a volley from a very tight angle at the far post! It's all Arsenal!
(67’) Close for Walcott! The England international is fed into the penalty area by Bellerin, but can only steer a cross-cum-shot across goal! Giroud stretches for the delivery, but can't make contact, with Ramsey calling for a different option at the far upright! It could have been 3-0 and goodnight.
(65’) Ozil curls yet another corner delivery in towards the near post, but Gabriel can only guide a flicked header well wide of the upright! Arsenal are looking confident and Bournemouth might just have to go back into their shells to avoid a comprehensive beating here.
--- 63’ Assist The France international uses the outside of his boot to flick a lovely pass over the top for his German teammate. ---
--- 63’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! THAT IS QUITE BRILLIANT! Ozil pulls the strings yet again, with the German midfielder sweeping a pass into Giroud and making a second run. The ex-Montpellier striker flicks a lovely pass over the top, which the former Real Madrid midfielder takes down with his first touch. His second slides a neat finish beyond Boruc from a tight angle! ---
--- 61’ Substitution Howe looks to freshen things up by bringing O'Kane into the fray in place of Gosling, with the Irish midfielder previously doing well off the bench against Palace. ---
--- 61’ Yellow card The England international dives into a late challenge on Arter, planting his studs into the ankle of his opponent. A deserved booking. ---
(61’) Howe's men only have half an hour to restore parity, with Arsenal continuing to have a firm grip on this fixture. Ozil and Giroud combine nicely on the edge of the box, but Chambers can't get to the rebound first! The ex-Saints man dives into a silly tackle on Arter.
(59’) Gosling drives into the Arsenal penalty area, before going down under pressure from Gibbs and Gabriel. The Brazilian goalscorer miscues his clearance and clips the former Newcastle midfielder, but the referee seems to deem it accidental! Possibly a let off for the hosts.
(57’) Giroud opens play out to the left-hand side, but Walcott is unable to beat Smith after a scrappy tackle from the Bournemouth full-back. Arsenal win back possession and probe down the other flank, but an attempted one-two between Ramsey and Bellerin is cut out. Chances are few and far between at present.
(55’) Daniels manages to win a corner on the left-hand side, which Stanislas takes. The substitute combines with Arter, but an eventual cross is easily cleared. The aforementioned Irishman mops up on the edge of the box, but a first-time shot is charged down by a ruck of red and white shirts.
(53’) Arter works the ball out to the left-hand side, but a looping cross from Daniels is headed half clear by Gibbs! Ritchie picks up the scraps and finds Smith on the overlap, but the right-back's eventual cross is placed far too close to Cech! A brief few signs that Howe's men might be able to find their nerve again at the Emirates.
(51’) Bellerin sprints down the right, before guiding a cross in towards Giroud, but Francis lashes away a half clearance! The start of this half has been very competitive and open, with the Gunners looking to try and put this game beyond Bournemouth with a second goal.
(49’) Oxlade-Chamberlain battles his way to the right byline, before a cut-back takes a deflection off a defender and threatens to creep inside Boruc's near upright! The Polish goalkeeper reacts quickly to prevent a cheap own goal.
(48’) Arsenal look to settle into the second half with some slow possession, which is asking Bournemouth to come forward and press. Moments later, King is released in behind, with the Norway international sprinting his way to the right byline! Gabriel recovers brilliantly, however with the Brazilian defender sliding in to deny a cross! What a chance for the Cherries to equalise.
--- 46’ Substitution Howe makes an offensive change at the interval, with Stanislas coming into the game in place of Pugh. Despite the latter linking up well with Daniels in the first half, the ex-West Ham winger has put in some eye-catching performances of late. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Emirates! Wenger's men will be hoping to carry their momentum into this period of the game, as they pummelled Bournemouth into submission merely 20 minutes ago.
HALF TIME! Arsenal go into the interval with a one-goal lead, courtesy of Gabriel's first ever for the club, in what was a half of two halves. Bournemouth started brilliantly and threatened with the pace of King, before Ozil and company lay siege to the Cherries' penalty area for the final quarter of an hour. Howe's men are lucky to still be in this.
(45’) There is one minute of stoppage time.
(44’) Ozil's corner deliveries are causing absolutely all kinds of issues, with a near-post flick from Gabriel almost being scrambled home at the far upright by Ramsey! Boruc hasn't had many saves to make, but there have been numerous heart-in-mouth moments for the Cherries to endure.
(42’) Only a few minutes are left on the clock, with Arsenal on an onslaught. Bellerin tries to pick out Giroud with a lofted cross, but Cook heads away! Moments later, the Spanish right-back tries to keep the ball in play at the right byline, but isn't quite capable. It's constant pressure for Bournemouth to deal with, as the Gunners lay siege.
(40’) Gibbs angles in a cross from the left byline, but Giroud can't rise high enough to try his luck on goal! Wenger's men are piling on the pressure, with Ozil continuing to wreak havoc. The German midfielder releases Bellerin down the right, but the Gunners' right-back blazes a cross-cum-shot over the crossbar.
(38’) Less than 10 minutes remain until the half-time interval, with Bournemouth probably happy to just hold on to their one-goal deficit at the moment. Howe's men are looking rushed and flustered, with Francis even putting a pass directly out of play for an Arsenal corner.
(36’) Ramsey is fed down the left channel by Ozil, but a cross from the Wales international is headed behind for a corner by Daniels! The ex-Real Madrid midfielder is pulling absolutely all of the strings at the moment. Yet another set-piece delivery causes mayhem, with Gabriel and Giroud unable to make goalscoring contact! Arter hacks clear.
(34’) What a chance for Mertesacker! Ozil whips in the aforementioned corner delivery, with Gabriel getting his head on the ball! Boruc makes a neat save and turns the effort onto the post, with the German defender unable to turn home the rebound from point-blank range! Moments later, Ozil feeds Walcott in behind, but the Bournemouth goalkeeper makes another neat stop!
(33’) Walcott has half a chance! Ozil sweeps a good cross in towards the near post, with the England international making a good run! Cook, however, stands firm to make a block and concede a corner.
(32’) Only a quarter of an hour remain in the first half, with Bournemouth's confidence inevitably taking a hit from conceding that goal from a corner. Arsenal haven't created much at all from open play, with King arguably having had the clearest opportunities this evening.
--- 30’ Yellow card Ramsey gets a caution for a cynical tug on his man's shirt, which the referee remembers and awards after he initially allowed Gosling to play on. ---
(29’) Suddenly, it is Bournemouth's turn to sit back and absorb a little bit of pressure. Howe won't want for his side to concede a quickfire double and consider themselves out of the contest before the interval. The Cherries are still pressing and harrying, but Arsenal have more confidence about themselves now.
--- 27’ Assist It's another assist for the Germany international, who curls in a very inviting corner delivery for Gabriel to nod home. ---
--- 27’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! GABRIEL GETS HIS FIRST FOR ARSENAL! The hosts take an undeserved 1-0 lead, with the ex-Villarreal defender thumping home an Ozil corner delivery! The deadlock is broken and the nerves among the fans appear to have been dispelled. ---
(26’) Chambers manages to find Giroud on the left, with the Frenchman able to play a neat one-two with Gibbs. The ex-Montpellier man, however, is promptly tackled in the penalty area by the no-nonsense presence of Francis. Both goalkeepers haven't had a great deal to do thus far.
(24’) Smith feeds Gosling down the right-hand side, with the Englishman overrunning yet another ball. Bournemouth continue to have an inability to whip in a cross from the bylines. Ozil manages to curl a devilish ball into the box from deep, but Walcott can't quite turn a volleyed finish home! The ex-Southampton man fails to make clean contact, with Boruc gathering up the scraps.
(22’) Pugh and Daniels link up brilliantly yet again down the left-hand side, before the former manages to run the ball out of play at the byline. Arsenal respond with an attack of their own, with Ozil picking out Chambers running down the right flank. The former Southampton utility man, however, blazes an awful cross behind for a goal kick.
(20’) The home crowd continue to be a little restless, as the Gunners continue to stutter in front of newly promoted opposition. Ritchie tries to play a neat ball around the corner for King to chase, but Cech is alive to the danger and races off his line to beat the ex-Man United forward to the pass.
(18’) Smith makes an overlapping run down the right-hand side, but the full-back is penalised for bundling his way into Walcott and pushing the ex-Saints wide man. Wenger's men are looking abject at the moment, with Bournemouth seeming much more comfortable and inventive on the ball.
(16’) Once again, Pugh manages to provide a cross in from the left, which is nodded towards the edge of the penalty area by Ritchie! Arter is there to try his luck with a volleyed effort, but his shot is charged down smartly. Bournemouth are having the better of the play at the minute, with no real bright sparks in the hosts' midfield five at the moment.
(14’) Pugh and Daniels combine down the left-hand side, with the latter managing to fizz a low cross into the near post! King challenges for it, but a few Arsenal players throw themselves desperately into the mix! Somehow, they managed to get the ball away from within a sea of bodies.
(12’) The hosts work their way forward through Bellerin, with the Spaniard testing Daniels for pace. The Bournemouth full-back is forced to concede a corner, with the home fans starting to find their voice now. Ozil delivers the set piece, but Boruc is comfortable enough to wander out of his six-yard box and claim the ball.
(11’) Gosling tries to burst down the right-hand side, but Ramsey slides in brilliantly to deny the ex-Blackpool man. Arsenal expand their play towards Gibbs on the left flank, but a cross from the English left-back is headed away by Daniels. Chances are still at a premium at the Emirates.
(9’) Arsenal now try to find a foothold in the contest themselves, in what is a rather cagey opening 10 minutes. Ozil is constantly looking to find pockets of space, but the ex-Real Madrid man is struggling due to the presence of Surman in between the Bournemouth lines.
(7’) King is released in behind Mertesacker, with the former Blackburn Rovers striker able to use his pace to cause Arsenal's captain come problems. Fortunately for the hosts, the Norway striker can only run the ball straight out of play for a goal kick. Moments later, there is a stoppage in play, as Arter goes down with a head injury.
(5’) Gosling makes a good interception in the middle of the park, but an attempted pass into Pugh is cut out neatly by Chambers. It's the visitors who are getting the ball down and settling themselves, with Arsenal happy to sit back for the moment. Arter feeds a pass into King after robbing Chambers of possession, but the Norwegian forward can only force Cech into a bit of catching practice.
(3’) Walcott leads a charge down the left-hand side, but Oxlade-Chamberlain is easily outmuscled by Francis. Bournemouth look to calm things down with some early possession, with the belief within their ranks evident. That's what good form can do to even the most unfancied of teams.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Emirates! The Gunners can go top of the table, results permitting, should they take three points this evening. Bournemouth, meanwhile, have the threat of relegation to motivate them!
Bournemouth substitutes: Rantie, Stanislas, Federici, Tomlin, Distin, Murray, O'Kane.
Bournemouth starting line-up (4-1-4-1): Boruc; Smith, Cook, Francis, Daniels; Surman; Ritchie, Gosling, Arter, Pugh; King.
Arsenal substitutes: Debuchy, Koscielny, Ospina, Monreal, Campbell, Iwobi, Reine-Adelaide.
Arsenal starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Cech; Bellerin, Mertesacker, Gabriel, Gibbs; Chambers, Ramsey; Oxlade-Chamberlain, Ozil, Walcott; Giroud.
TEAM NEWS: Josh King returns from fitness for the visitors, with the Norway international presumably rushed back in order to trouble the Gunners in behind with his pace. The back four remain unchanged, but Marc Pugh comes into the side on the left in place of Junior Stanislas. The ex-West Ham winger takes a seat among the substitutes.
TEAM NEWS: Wenger makes a couple of changes to his back four, with Kieran Gibbs coming in at left-back in place of Nacho Monreal and Gabriel Paulista replacing the hapless Laurent Koscielny. Calum Chambers will partner Aaron Ramsey in holding midfield, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Theo Walcott in the wide areas. Through the middle, there is the usual partnership of Mesut Ozil and Olivier Giroud.
The visitors are unbeaten in their last six matches in the English top flight, but could only grind out a 0-0 stalemate against Crystal Palace last time out. As it stands, the Cherries are merely three points off safety. Arsenal, meanwhile, could look to go top with a win here today, but they will rely heavily on the contest between Man City and Leicester too.
Hello and welcome to one of the Premier League's later kick offs, as Arsenal look to recover from their horrendous 4-0 Boxing Day meltdown against Southampton. The Gunners host Bournemouth at the Emirates, with Eddie Howe's men turning in some great performance and results recently. Arsene Wenger previously had his men in fantastic form, with today an opportunity to ensure that a blip doesn't turn into a bad run.

The draw is definitely better for Chelsea than it is for United. The Blues were clearly set up to sit deep and hit United on the counter, but as the game wore on it became increasingly obvious that they were always going to struggle to score. As a result, they sat even deeper and did well to frustrate the hosts as they begin to tire.
Despite their dominance, United are unable to leave with three much-needed points and are now without a win in their last eight games. They looked far better today, however, with Rooney impressing in particular, but the result will no doubt keep the pressure firmly on Van Gaal, who will have been pleased by most of what he saw but still frustrated that his side were unable to find the back of the net.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 CHELSEA
(90’) Chelsea are awarded a late free kick after Pedro is fouled by Schneiderlin on the halfway line. Unsurprisingly, the Blues take their time with the set-piece before Mikel launches it forward, where Ivanovic holds up the ball before the referee brings an end to the game.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Oscar slowly makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Loftus-Cheek, who may not be able to get a touch on the ball before the referee blows his whistle for the final time. ---
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card Rooney loses the ball after battling with Mikel and then catches Oscar with a poor high challenge, leaving the Brazilian in a heap on the floor and resulting in a yellow card for the captain. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(89’) The crowd urge United to attack as the hosts try to do exactly that. Depay attempts to burst down the left flank but his final touch is poor and sends the ball out for a throw-in, much to the frustration of the home fans and the winger's manager.
(87’) United are trying their hardest to find a way through the sea of blue shirts in front of them, but Chelsea are set up to protect the draw and are doing well to do so. As a result, the atmosphere has turned slightly nervous as we enter the final few minutes of the game.
(85’) What an opportunity for Rooney to score the winner! Borthwick-Jackson flies down the left flank on an excellent run before curling a phenomenal cross over to the United captain, but his first-time volley is mishit and flies over the top of the crossbar from close range.
(83’) Young skips past Pedro on the right flank before firing a low cross into the penalty area, but it fails to find a red shirt and is cut out at the near post.
--- 82’ Substitution Jones comes on to replace Blind, who looks to limping slightly as he makes his way off the pitch. ---
--- 81’ Yellow card Matic tries to break away down the left wing but is cynically pulled to the ground by Schweinsteiger, who is shown a yellow card as a result. ---
(79’) Ball after ball is flung into the Chelsea penalty area, but each cross is dealt with well by the visitors' back four. They then try to break away quickly through Ramires, but the Brazilian is dispossessed by a great tackle from Schneiderlin on the edge of the box.
(77’) Young charges down the right wing before sending an excellent through-ball into the path of Herrera. The Spaniard sticks out a foot but is unable to make contact with the ball, denying him the opportunity to unleash a shot from the edge of the Chelsea penalty area.
--- 76’ Substitution Mata receives a loud round of applause from the United fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Depay for the final quarter-of-an-hour. ---
(74’) Great chance for Rooney! A lofted pass is flung forward by Mata and bounces into the path of the captain in front of goal, but he's unable to make contact with the ball before the linesman's flag is quickly raised for offside.
--- 72’ Yellow card Hazard sticks out a foot and brings Young crashing to the ground with a poor challenge, resulting in a yellow card for the Belgian. ---
(71’) United quickly break forward from the restart, with Martial doing well to break down the left flank. The Frenchman then tries to take on Ivanovic, but Zouma charges across the pitch and dispossesses the young forward before forcing him into poking the ball out of play for a Chelsea goal kick.
--- 70’ Substitution Meanwhile, Borthwick-Jackson has come on to replace Darmian for United. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Willian slowly makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Ramires in Chelsea's first substitution of the game. ---
(68’) Chelsea initially work the ball around well before sending the ball out to Willian on the right wing, but the Brazilian is unable to keep it in play and ends up bringing a promising attacking move to a disappointing end.
(66’) United are continuing to boss possession inside the Chelsea half of the pitch, but they're failing to turn that dominance into chances on goals. The visitors remain camped deep inside their own half of the pitch and are doing well to keep the hosts at bay.
(64’) Mata screams for a penalty, but nothing is given! United work the ball around quickly before the Spaniard is teed up by Rooney, but he's immediately tripped over by Azpilicueta just inside the Chelsea box. He pleas for the referee to point to the spot, but the man in charge doesn't agree and waves play on.
(62’) What a terrible miss by Matic! Chelsea successfully deal with a United corner before Pedro flies forward on a blisteringly quick dart down the right flank. He then cuts inside before picking out the aforementioned Serbian, who is left in acres of space in the middle of the pitch. He charges into the box before going one-on-one with De Gea, but he somehow ends up skying his effort well over the top of the crossbar from close range. That was the perfect opportunity for him to make it 1-0!
(60’) Young picks up the ball on the right flank and immediately tries to pick out Rooney with a lofted pass forward, but it's slightly overhit and sails over the captain's head before bouncing into the hands of Courtois.
(58’) United revert to patiently moving the ball around inside the Chelsea half of the pitch before Herrera and Martial try to link up with a quick one-two. However, Ivanovic is there to cut out the danger at the vital moment before earning his side a goal kick.
(56’) United scream for a penalty, but it's not given! The resulting corner fails to find a red shirt before bouncing over to the right-hand side of the box, where it's picked up by Willian. Under no pressure whatsoever, the Brazilian collects the ball before it bounces up into his hand, but, despite the pleas from the hosts, the referee allows play to go on.
(55’) What a save by Courtois! Martial skips past Ivanovic and Pedro with ease before whipping a low cross into the penalty area, where it finds Herrera. The Spaniard immediately unleashes a thumping strike from a few yards out, but somehow the Chelsea goalkeeper is able to push it away from danger with an excellent diving stop.
(53’) United initially move the ball around well inside the Chelsea half of the pitch before Schweinsteiger tries to pick out Darmian with a cross-field lofted pass, but it's poorly hit by the German and flies out for a goal kick.
(51’) Darmian and Martial link up wonderfully well on the left wing before the latter sends a dangerous low cross into the middle of the box. It can only find Terry, who thumps the ball away, before the aforementioned Italian sends another pass into the penalty area. However, once again the Chelsea captain is there to deal with the danger before it can find Rooney.
(49’) The resulting set-piece causes problems for De Gea, but he's just about able to punch it out of the box and away from the head of Terry. The ball finds its way to Matic, however, but the midfielder's audacious long-range effort sails safely over the top of the crossbar.
(48’) Fantastic double save by De Gea! Hazard flies through the middle of the pitch before teeing up Pedro. The Spaniard skips past Smalling on the edge of the penalty area before unleashing a thumping strike that the United goalkeeper does well to parry away one handed. His stop can only find Azpilicueta, however, but the follow-up effort is also dealt with well by the United shot-stopper.
(47’) Chelsea push forward on an early attack down the right wing through Ivanovic, who is then tripped over by Schweinsteiger, resulting in a free kick in a good position. Willian sends a good delivery into the box but Martial is there to head the ball away from danger.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
United will certainly be the happier of the two sides after embarking on one of their finest first-half performances of the season thus far. They have spent the vast majority of the opening period all of Chelsea, who, without Costa up front, are lacking any sort of attacking threat in front of goal. As a result, they've been forced to sit deep as they aim to keep at bay the determined Red Devils, who have already hit the woodwork twice through Mata and Martial, both of whom have impressed in the final third of the pitch.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 CHELSEA
(45’) And now United have a late chance to score after a clumsy challenge from Pedro brings Herrera crashing to the ground on the left wing. Mata swings a cross into the middle of the box, but it's easily cut out by Oscar before the referee brings an end to the first half.
(45’) Matic is clipped from behind by Herrera, gifting Chelsea a good chance to score from a free kick 35 yards away from goal. Willian decides to unleash an audacious strike from the set-piece, but it's easily stopped by De Gea at the far post.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
(44’) Once again, Hazard, who has arguably been Chelsea's best player so far, is clattered into by a United player. This time it's Blind who brings down the Belgian, resulting in a free kick for the Blues that they take short but fail to make count.
(43’) Martial cuts inside from the left wing before working the ball over to Herrera. The Spaniard, who is under little pressure from Azpilicueta, quickly curls a cross into the middle of the penalty area, where it's won in the air by Terry. However, the captain can only send his attempted clearance to Schweinsteiger, who immediately unleashes a rocket of a shot that flies well over the top of the crossbar and out for a goal kick.
(42’) A United attack breaks down, allowing Chelsea to break away on a quick counter-attack. It's two on two, with Pedro and Hazard the two blue shirts inside the hosts' half of the pitch. The latter heads to the edge of the box before spinning and trying to tee up Willian, but his attempted pass is too heavy and, as a result, the Brazilian is unable to control it.
(40’) Willian curls the resulting free kick into the heart of the United penalty area, where it finds Zouma, but the defender's attempted volley is poorly hit and ends up clearing the top of the crossbar by quite some distance.
--- 39’ Yellow card Hazard zips down the left wing to get onto the end of a loose ball before being clattered into by Smalling, who receives a yellow card as a result. ---
(38’) Once again, United patiently move the ball around inside the Chelsea half of the pitch as they continue to put the visitors under pressure. Darmian then plays the ball back to Schweinsteiger, but the German is quickly closed down by Oscar, who does well to dispossess the midfielder before turning and kick-starting a counter-attack that fails to result in a chance on goal.
(36’) Mata and Darmian link up well on the left flank before working the ball into the middle of the pitch. With a sea of blue shirts camped in front of them, United are forced into playing it back to the aforementioned Italian on the left wing, but he ends up straying into an offside position and the linesman's flag is quickly raised as a result.
(34’) Willian steps up and curls a dangerous cross from the resulting set-piece that finds Zouma at the back post, but the defender is unable to fully control the ball and can only send it bouncing out for a United goal kick.
(33’) Chelsea work the ball around well midway inside the United half of the pitch before Hazard is clumsily tripped over from behind by Herrera, resulting in a free kick for the visitors in a very dangerous position 30 yards away from goal.
--- 31’ Yellow card Schneiderlin flies into Willian and denies the Brazilian the opportunity to break away quickly with a strong sliding challenge, leaving the referee with no choice but to show him a yellow card. ---
(30’) Fantastic defending by Young! Chelsea do well to deal with the resulting set-piece before breaking away on a quick counter-attack. Azpilicueta flies forward and looks set to penetrate the United penalty area, but the aforementioned right-back is there to dispossess the Spaniard with an excellent sliding tackle.
(29’) Great strike by Rooney! United take the free kick quickly, which takes Chelsea by surprise. The captain then pushes forward before unleashing an absolutely thumping shot from 25 yards out, and Courtois is just about able to parry it away for a corner.
--- 28’ Yellow card United immediately fly forward on a quick attack as they look to take advantage of Chelsea's disjointed back line. Martial sprints into the visitors' half of the pitch before trying to beat Mikel, but the Nigerian sticks out a foot and trips the Frenchman to the ground, resulting in a free kick for the hosts and a yellow card for the defensive midfielder. ---
(27’) Chelsea move the ball around well as they embark on their longest spell of possession so far. Hazard breaks forward in the middle of the pitch before being cynically pulled back by Young, resulting in a free kick for the visitors midway inside the United's half of the pitch. They take it short and the Belgian tries to weave towards the penalty area before teeing up Zouma, who immediately goes down under a challenge from Smalling. However, the player waves play on and allows the hosts the break away on a counter-attack.
(26’) Schneiderlin has his pocket picked in the middle of the pitch, allowing Hazard to try and kick-start a Chelsea counter-attack. The Belgian does well to beat two players before trying to link up with Willian, but the two aren't on the same wavelength and, as a result, his attempted pass can only find a red shirt.
(24’) Almost a terrible mistake by Courtois! An awful goal kick from the goalkeeper sends the ball straight into the feet of Mata, who immediately breaks forward into the space left in front of him. He then tries to curl a cross onto the head of Rooney, who had made a good run into the penalty area, but Terry is there to cut out the danger at the vital moment.
(22’) Martial goes down inside the penalty area, but nothing is given! Once again, the Frenchman twists and turns on the left flank, showing great skill to beat a sea of blue shirts. He then penetrates the box before going down under a challenge from Zouma, but the referee immediately waves away the United pleas.
(21’) After a thoroughly intense opening 20 minutes, the pace of the game has slowed down somewhat, although United are still firmly in control. Chelsea are finding it incredibly hard to get near the ball, and when they do they're failing to find a way past the hosts' determined back line, who are doing well to put plenty of pressure on the reigning champions.
(19’) A poor pass from Smalling sends the ball straight to Oscar, who quickly works the ball out to Willian. The Brazilian sprints towards the byline but is immediately put under pressure by Darmian, which forces him to play a mishit pass into the feet of Schneiderlin on the edge of the United penalty area.
(17’) Martial hits the post! The Frenchman cuts inside from the left wing and beats Ivanovic with ease before unleashing a thumping low shot. It flies past the outstretched arm of Courtois but ends up ricocheting off the crossbar before rolling over to the right flank. United are all over Chelsea at the moment!
(16’) Chelsea, who have spent the entirety of the game thus far camped inside their own half of the pitch, try to break away on a counter-attack after regaining possession. Pedro picks up the ball on the left wing and sends a long lofted pass over to Oscar, who meets it well on the right-hand side of the United box, but the Brazilian's first-time volleyed shot ends up missing the goal by quite some distance.
(15’) Darmian charges down the left flank once again before going one-on-one with Ivanovic. He initially does well to skip past the Serbian before unleashing a deep cross, but it's overhit and ends up flying over everybody inside the box before bouncing out to the opposite wing.
(13’) Another good opportunity for United! Once again, the hosts work the ball out wide to Darmian, who is left in plenty of space by the Chelsea defence. The Italian immediately unleashes a curling cross that almost finds Rooney in front of goal, but it ends up flying just a yard or so over the head of the striker.
(12’) Blind breaks out from the back and charges deep into the Chelsea half of the pitch before linking up well with Darmian on the left flank. The Italian initially does well to beat his marker before heading towards the edge of the penalty area, but his attempted cross is deflected up into the air and into the hands of Courtois before it can find a red shirt.
(10’) Great strike by Schneiderlin! Herrera darts down the left wing before cutting a low cross into the Chelsea box. It meets Rooney, who, with his back to goal, quickly tees up the aforementioned French midfielder, and he immediately unleashes a spinning, 20-yard shot with the outside of his boot that beats Courtois before bouncing just wide of the near post.
(9’) Young battles against Azpilicueta before firing a cross off the Spaniard and out for another United corner. Once again, Blind curls the set-piece towards the near post, but it fails to find a red shirt and is easily dealt with by Chelsea.
(7’) United break forward quickly, with Herrera doing well in the middle of the pitch. He sends the ball out to Martial, who twists and turns on the left wing before beating two Chelsea players. The Frenchman then tries to penetrate the penalty area, but his final touch is slightly heavy and, as a result, he's dispossessed by Mikel before he can reach the edge of the box.

Of the league’s heavy hitters, only Chelsea have struggled more than United. The first game after the departure of Mourinho resulted in a relatively comfortable 3-1 win against Sunderland, whilst their opening clash under the watchful eye of Guus Hiddink ended in a 2-2 draw at home to in-form Watford. However, there is still a lot of work to be done by the interim manager, who will have been quietly pleased with what he has witnessed recently but is nonetheless well aware that today’s game is a huge test for the struggling reigning champions, who desperately need to leave Old Trafford with all three points.
It’s now or never for Louis van Gaal, who heads into today’s clash not knowing whether he will still be in charge of United come the start of 2016. A thoroughly disappointing campaign has quickly turned into a crisis for the Red Devils, who are now without a win in their last seven games as a result of a poor 2-0 defeat away to Stoke City on Boxing Day. The loss against the Potters also means that the Dutchman’s side have lost four consecutive competitive clashes for the first time since 1961, whilst their problems in front of goal have seen them average just 1.22 goals per game, their lowest since the 1989-90 season. The imposing shadow of Jose Mourinho continues to loom large over Old Trafford, and another defeat here today could finally spell the end for the hosts’ desperately struggling boss.

Full time at the King Power Stadium. It wasn't the spectacle that the neutrals were hoping for with the goals flying in, but two of the title contenders in the Barclays Premier League, Leicester and Man City, play out a fairly entertaining 0-0 stalemate in their last fixture of the year. Goals were expected in this Barclays Premier League clash between Leicester and Man City, but it has been proved that we are witnessing two fairly evenly matched teams this season as we head into the break at a 0-0 stalemate. Both sides have enjoyed some chances created in the opposition final thirds, but it is probably Kasper Schmeichel who has been the busier of the two goalkeepers. A very interesting second half to come! Who will be top of the table at the end of 2015?
(45’) Just the one minute of added time signaled by the referee here which sounds about right as we have pretty much saw a free flowing game in the opening 45 minutes. Unlikely we will see someone go into the break with the lead here!

Otamendi, Mangala, and Fernandinho are all involved in the incident, but one of them must have got the ball cleanly as the referee fails to award the foul!

Man City are actually unbeaten in their last five away trips to face the Foxes, winning three and drawing two. However, Leicester seem to enjoy playing in the last match of the year, as they have came out victorious in their last fixture of 2012, 2012, and 2013 – can they continue that run against this talented City side tonight?
The last clash between Leicester and Man City came in March of this year in the league. On that occasion, the Citizens ran out comfortable 2-0 winners thanks to goals James Milner and David Silva. This was preceded by another win in the reverse fixture in December, where they narrowly won 1-0 with Frank Lampard getting on the scoresheet. Leicester have not lost three matches on the bounce against City since all the way back in 1961.
The Foxes themselves haven't endured a particularly happy Christmas, either, as they lost their Boxing Day clash away to Liverpool at Anfield on Saturday 1-0. Claudio Ranieri's charges have been free scoring in the Premier League this campaign, and up until that match a few days ago they had netted in every single league game, mainly thanks to the contributions from star players, Jamie Vardy and Riyad Mahrez. However, the duo were misfiring against the Reds at the weekend, so they will need to get back on form if victory is to be on the cards tonight.
Man City, meanwhile, were always pencilled in to be hovering around the top of the tree around the turn of the year, but perhaps in more emphatic fashion as they are down in fourth place at the moment, with a win tonight taking them into second behind the Gunners. Their pursuit to reclaim the championship from Chelsea has derailed slightly in recent weeks thanks to disappointing losses against Stoke and Arsene Wenger's outfit, but they will be hopeful of getting back to winning ways here.
At the start of the season, not a lot of people would have predicted that the pre-New Year encounter between these two sides would prove to be a top of the table clash. However, Leicester have amazed the Premier League, and indeed the rest of Europe this campaign, with their swashbuckling and entertaining brand of football which has seen them top the division in recent weeks. Indeed, if they can come out as winners this evening, they will go back to the summit of the league ahead of Arsenal, who were victorious against Bournemouth yesterday.

Full time at the Britannia. Stoke claim another massive Premier League scalp this season as they successfully come out well deserved 2-0 winners against Manchester United on Boxing Day. The damage was done for Louis Van Gaal's men in the first half as Bojan and Marko Arnautovic both netted with terrific goals, and even the introduction of the dropped Wayne Rooney couldn't catalyse a comeback for the Red Devils. Mark Hughes' men highly impressive again, and now only three points behind United in the table! Thanks for joining us, and enjoy the rest of the Boxing Day action!

It is fair to say that, while Hiddink is extremely popular with the Chelsea support, the Stamford Bridge faithful are still more than a little torn regarding the sacking of Jose Mourinho. Two of the players who came under much criticism during the last weeks of the Portuguese's tenure are Cesc Fabregas and Nemanja Matic, and they both start in the heart of the midfield today.
It really has been a torrid season so far for the hosts, with that win against Sunderland just their second from their previous eight Premier League fixtures, while, at the opposite end of the spectrum, Watford are searching for a fifth-successive win in the top flight today. The last meeting between these two sides - in the Third Round of last season’s FA Cup - finished 3-0 to Chelsea. Will it be a similar story today, or can Flores’ side maintain their recent winning-streak?
While Hazard may have been one of the first names on the team sheet last term, Hiddink has not chosen to throw the playmaker straight back into action today, and understandably so. The 24-year-old has come under a lot of criticism from both Chelsea supporters and football pundits alike, and he is yet to score in any competition this campaign.

The teams are in at Stamford Bridge, with both sides fielding line ups with just one change a-piece. For Chelsea, Gary Cahill returns to partner John Terry in defence, with Kurt Zouma dropping to the bench. Hiddink is also able to welcome Eden Hazard back to the fold after the Belgium winger recovered from a knock picked up in Jose Mourinho’s last game in charge. As for the visitors, their switch is enforced, with the on-loan Nathan Ake unable to feature against his parent club. He is replaced at left-back by the experienced Jose Holebas.
However, Quique Sanchez Flores’ high-flying Watford present no easy challenge. They sit in seventh place heading into today’s clash - 10 points and eight places above Chelsea - and have already matched their previous points tally in a Premier League campaign. Their fine form is in no small part down to Odion Ighalo, who has netted 12 league goals so far this term, the most recent of which came as a double in the 3-0 win over Liverpool at Vicarage Road last time out. If the Nigeria forward scores today, he will become the clubs’ first ever player to get on the scoresheet in five consecutive Premier League matches.
Hiddink - who lost just once during his previous 22 games in charge of Chelsea as interim manager back in 2009 - took charge of the first team squad this week, and will be looking to build on the 3-1 victory over Sunderland last weekend. The hosts today have won seven of their last eight meetings with Watford, and are unbeaten in the Premier League on Boxing Day since 2003, so the omens are good for the reigning champions.

However, Pulis' starting XI looks rather like he is more concerned about avoiding defeat than necessarily going on to win. James Morrison will likely help them out while also getting forward to support Rickie Lambert, the lone frontman. The former Liverpool man is making only his third start of the season and his first since September, partly down to Rondon's suspension.
West Brom have not been in great form themselves of late either, though their four-match winless run isn't quite as alarming as Swansea's struggles. Nevertheless, the club have not endured a worse run in the Premier League since Tony Pulis took over, so the manager will be eager to ensure that three points are clinched here today.
Swansea have improved slightly in their last two games, with Curtis taking over in a caretaker position. A last gasp goal at Manchester City brought about an unlucky 2-1 defeat and then last time out they held West Ham United to a 0-0 draw at the Liberty Stadium. Goals have been their problem, with Gomis proving rather unreliable in front of goal since September and the Frenchman has to make do with a place on the bench today. Andre Ayew leads the line, with Sigurdsson, Routledge and Montero in support.
Swansea caretaker manager Alan Curtis has been preaching to his team in the build-up to this clash about the need to return to basics. Little has gone to plan in recent months for the Swans and they are currently in the midst of a seven-match run without a win, with five of those games ending in defeat. Garry Monk's dismissal a couple of weeks ago was something of an inevitability after the Welsh club found themselves dropping into the bottom three.

Arsenal have only managed to win one of their last six trips to St. Mary’s, but their impressive away form this year will fill their fans with confidence ahead of today’s clash. The Gunners have picked up 38 points on their travels this calendar year, more than any other team in the Premier League, whilst Southampton have managed to win just one of their last five home games, with that victory coming against Bournemouth almost two months ago.
In stark contrast to their struggling opponents, Arsenal are flying high and enjoying life in the upper echelons of the league table. A record of eight wins from their last 11 domestic games means that they currently sit in second place, just two points behind leaders Leicester City, who were beaten by Liverpool this afternoon. After convincingly beating third-place Manchester City last weekend, today’s clash starts a run of games that the in-form Gunners will be confident about winning. Bournemouth, Newcastle United and Liverpool - all of whom have had their fair share of disappointments recently - await Arsene Wenger’s side in the coming weeks, and they will be aiming to continue their winning run with victories in each of them as they look to overtake the Foxes at the top of the table as we head into the second half of the campaign.
After embarking on a great run of form that saw them lose just once in 10 league games, many thought that Southampton would continue last season’s good work and keep the pressure firmly on the top six. However, a tough and underwhelming few weeks, which started with a lacklustre 1-0 defeat against Stoke City a month ago, means that the Saints now have just one point from their last five clashes, with that draw coming at home to bottom side Aston Villa three weeks ago. As a result, they now sit in 12th place in the table, just four points in front of the relegation zone after positive results for several of the sides lying marginally below them.
Good evening and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Southampton and Arsenal at St. Mary’s Stadium.

(63’) Norwich clear the corner straightaway, but United are attacking up the left instantly once again. Depay finds himself in behind the defence, but his low cross is blocked behind for a corner.

(60’) United at least have a chance from a free-kick now, as Young charges inside and is apparently fouled by Brady. The Irishman appeared to get the ball, but the referee doesn't think so.
(58’) United don't appear to have a specific game plan other than smacking hopeful crosses into the danger zone. It hasn't worked yet today, will it ever? Considering the quality of their crossing, you suspect not.
(56’) Our monitors keep cutting away to Van Gaal and his bench. They look flabbergasted and bereft of ideas. Is this the final straw for the manager?
--- 54’ Assist Jerome holds off his man, charges forward and then picks out the perfect pass. ---

(54’) Mata is again the culprit for United, as the Spaniard looks for a simple pass across to the right flank but sees the ball intercepted by Brady. Surely Van Gaal will haul him off sooner rather than later?

(51’) Great strength from Bassong. The Cameroonian is forced back to deal with Mata chasing a long ball. He gets his body the right side of the ball and then shepherds it back to Rudd. The defender has been very good today.
(50’) The Norwich free-kick comes to nothing and United are swiftly back on the front foot. Mata finds Martial and then continues his run towards the left side of the Norwich area, where the Frenchman finds him again. However, the midfielder's eventual cross is dreadful and goes straight out for a throw-in.
(48’) Good play by Redmond, as the winger picks up possession in his own half, darts up the right flank, taking on two challengers and then charging into the centre of the United half. Eventually the move comes to a halt on the left, as Olsson is fouled by Young.

The referee blows his whistle for the break, and there are plenty jeers and boos audible from the home support, while that pocket of away fans are heard cheering with elation. United have been poor once again. Unsurprisingly they have generally dictated proceedings, but there is little creativity in midfield, the final ball has been poor and Rooney just looks slow. It will get to the point for Van Gaal where the club simply decide such performances are not good enough; could today be the day?
(45’) HALF-TIME!
(45’) There will be a minute added on here.
(45’) Another corner goes to waste, as O'Neil blocks the delivery. It has not been pretty from the hosts in the last 30 minutes or so. How long before the home fans start chanting for Jose Mourinho?
(44’) Better from United. Mata finds space in the middle and stretches the play with a pass in behind the defence for Rooney. The captain has drifted over to the right and finds himself the crosser, but Olsson stands up to him well and concedes a corner.
(42’) This time it is a hopeful lofted ball into the area from Blind on the left, but searching for Rooney instead of Fellaini. Either way, the outcome is rather the same, as the ball takes a nick off a Norwich defender and Rudd is allowed to collect easily.
(40’) There is no instant response for United. Once again they hoist a high ball into the area towards the physical Fellaini, but yet again nothing comes of it. That's about as much creative inspiration that they have shown today. It's not pretty.
--- 38’ Assist Redmond ran at Jones and prodded the ball past him in order for Jerome to collect and subsequently fire home. ---

(38’) United win themselves a corner out of little on the left an it is taken very quickly. Eventually Young hooks it into the area and Fellaini nods it back towards Rooney, but Tettey is on hand to get in the way and clear.
(36’) Brady whips the ball into the area, but due to the lack of pace on the delivery, he gives his team-mates little to work with. Martial is quickest to it and he heads clear unchallenged.

The United captain shimmies the ball on to his left foot and digs a shot out, but his effort is dragged harmlessly wide of the right-han post.
(15’) Good play again from the hosts. Young does well on the right, squeezing a cross past Olsson. Norwich initially clear the danger, only for it to be hooked back into the danger zone. The Irishman has been one of Norwich's best attacking players this season, so the quieter he is, the better.
(5’) That's better from United, as the hosts suddently spring into life down the right thanks to a quick passing move between Mata, Martial and Young. The Frenchman feeds the makeshift right-back up the flank and he crosses, but Rudd deals with it comfortably.
(3’) A low key start at Old Trafford. United are seeing more of the ball at the moment, but they are yet to put together any moves of note, with Norwich so far doing all they need to at the back. One suspects that this could be a pattern that remains for a little while.
(1’) Off we go! Norwich get us under way.
The two teams are out on the pitch with kick-off just a few moments away.
Nevertheless, if there is ever a good time to play Manchester United then it is surely now. Under pressure in terms of their lacklustre performances, rigid and uninspiring tactics implemented by a manager whose apparent stubbornness is seemingly bringing his own job into question, Norwich will be looking to capitalise on the atmosphere surrounding United at the moment and winger Robbie Brady will no doubt be excited about the prospect of potentially getting one over on his former club. Certainly in the Irishman, Nathan Redmond and Wes Hoolahan, City have the ability to at least worry United's defence.
While United will be looking to avoid falling any further behind Premier League pacesetters Leicester City, Norwich have entirely different ambitions on their mind today. Alex Neil's side have won only once in 11 matches, accumulating a total of seven points from a possible 33. That form unsurprisingly has them lurking in the bottom three. A squad some have suggested is too good to be relegated, Neil has a lot of work on his hands, but he will not be able to draw much confidence from City's record at Old Trafford, a place they've not won at in the Premier League era.
Van Gaal has been able to make four changes to the team which lost 2-1 at promoted Bournemouth last weekend, with three of those switches unsurprisingly coming at the back. While Varela and Borthwick-Jackson did little wrong at the Vitality Stadium, they find themselves back on the bench, with Young and Phil Jones taking their places. Paddy McNair endured something of a nightmare and he too drops out, with Chris Smalling one of several to return from injury. Wayne Rooney is the final change and he comes into the side to make his 500th appearance for the club, replacing Jesse Lingard. He will likely slot in behind Martial, who is expected to lead the line. Ander Herrera is also back in contention but has to make do with a place on the bench, despite Michael Carrick's indifferent form of late.
Much of the talk with regards to United in the build-up has been revolving around the combination of their terrible form, growing injury list and the now looming presence of an unemployed Jose Mourinho lurking in the background to put extra pressure on Louis van Gaal. The Red Devils come into this match without a win in their last five in all competitions and playing particularly dull football, certainly according to fans, anyway. Nevertheless, the manager can take some solace in the fact that his injury list is not look quite so catastrophic for today.

The Swans looked far more confident than they have in recent weeks but still looked off the pace in the final third, where they just couldn't beat West Ham's determined back line, no matter how hard they tried. Collins was the standout performer for the Hammers, as he was always on hand to throw his body on the line to help his side pick up their fourth consecutive draw.
FULL-TIME: SWANSEA CITY 0-0 WEST HAM UNITED
(90’) What a chance for Jelavic! West Ham break away incredibly quickly and take Swansea completely by surprise. Jelavic then breaks into the hosts' penalty area before looking to shoot, but Fernandez does well to dart over and cut out the danger before he can do so.
(90’) Swansea push forward on one last attacking move, with Barrow and Naughton linking up well on the right wing. The latter then swings a dangerous cross into the penalty area, where it finds Shelvey, but the substitute's acrobatic overhead kick fails to beat Tomkins, who stays close to him at the far post.

(90’) The fourh official has indicated that there will be four minutes of added time.
(89’) Patient build-up play from Swansea ends with Shelvey 30 yards away from the West Ham goal, and he twists and turns before darting out to the right wing and curling a cross into the box. It's completely overhit, however, and ends up sailing well over the head of Ki and out to the left flank.

(80’) The resulting set-piece is curled into the heart of the penalty area, where it skims off the head of Ayew before falling to Williams, but the Swansea captain can only send his half-volleyed strike flying over the top of the crossbar.

(75’) Swansea quickly work their way down the left flank through Ki, who darts forward before spinning and teeing up Shelvey. The substitute then finds Sigurdsson, who quickly moves the ball onto Naughton, but the right-back's first-time, thumping strike ends up flying well wide of the goal.

(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
It's been an impressive and hard-fought opening 45 minutes, with both sides looking bright at either end of the pitch. Swansea started the better of the two and put the visitors under plenty of early pressure, but West Ham slowly grew into the game and by the end were doing well to hassle the hosts' back line. However, Swansea have held firm to keep the Hammers' front line largely quiet, meaning that it's still all to play for with 45 minutes left to go and with both teams desperate for a victory.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
As for West Ham, they too have struggled in recent weeks and are now in danger of slipping into the wrong half of the table. The East London side sit just one point ahead of both 10th-place Everton and 11th-place Stoke City, and, as a result of last weekend’s goalless draw with the Potters, are now without a win in their last six league games, a far cry from the seven-game unbeaten run that they embarked on earlier in the campaign. The Hammers, who have been hit by a plethora of injuries, the latest of which struck Andy Carroll, are without a win in the Premier League since October 24th, and they, like Swansea, will be desperately looking for three much-needed points to help kick-start their season once again.
A win for Norwich City means that Swansea now sit in the relegation zone in 18th place, making today’s clash even more of a must-win for the South Wales side. After last week’s narrow 2-1 defeat away to Manchester City, the Swans now have just five points from their last 10 Premier League games, a truly terrible run of form that is only worse than bottom side Aston Villa. In truth, they looked far better against the aforementioned Sky Blues than they have in recent weeks and were unlucky not to leave the Etihad Stadium with a point, but they are still struggling at both ends of the pitch, with their defence and attack looking equally poor. However, last weekend saw Bafetimbi Gomis find the back of the net for the first time since the end of August, and caretaker manager Alan Curtis, who will remain in charge for today’s game as the search for Garry Monk’s replacement goes on, will be hoping that the Frenchman can help his side to a much-needed victory here this afternoon.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today’s Premier League game between Swansea City and West Ham United at the Liberty Stadium.

Massive scalp for the Gunners, who nervously edge over the line after a late fightback from City. Two well-taken goals from Giroud and Walcott seemed to give them the points, and they came close to adding a third on a number of occasions. However, an outstanding goal from Toure brought the Citizens back in it, and they laid siege to Cech's goal late on, but could not find another breakthrough. The Gunners open up a four-point gap on the Citizens, and trail leaders Leicester by only two points heading into Christmas. That's all from us, see you next time!
(90’) THAT'S IT! ARSENAL SEE IT OUT!
(90’) Deep into the dying embers of this game, with the last few seconds added on after the delay to tend to the stricken Giroud. Arsenal eat up the clock with a throw-in near the City corner flag. Wenger is out of his dugout telling his side to slow it down!
(90’) Toure has come on in leaps and bounds since his goal, adding another offensive option alongside De Bruyne. This is a gripping finish to this game, with the Arsenal fans trying to roar their team on during the final minutes of added time.
(90’) Into stoppage time now and Giroud is down as he slid in with an important tackle to stop a cross from coming in down the left-hand side. Four minutes have been signaled here to end this game.
(89’) TOURE HITS IT JUST WIDE! Hearts in mouths for the Gunners, who see De Bruyne orchestrate another chance, sliding the Ivorian goalside of his man but at full stretch, he can only poke it the wrong side of the post!
--- 88’ Substitution Walcott puts the end to an accomplished night as Wenger replaces him with Chambers to shore things up in the closing stages. ---
(88’) All the action is down the City right flank now, as Arsenal just want this final whistle to sound. How things have changed - earlier in the half they looked like racking up three or four goals on the Citizens! Bony slashes an effort wide and moment later, glances a header well over!
(86’) Suddenly, this looks like City's point to gain. Sagna gets through down the right-hand side and his cross finds a way through to the near post, but Cech is there to smother it in time.
(84’) ARSENAL WASTE ANOTHER CHANCE! Ramsey was the man on the end of it, as he races onto a ball from Oxlade-Chamberlain, and tries to lob Hart from inside the area. However, his effort misses the top corner when a goal looked inevitable!
--- 82’ Assist Sagna gets credited with the assist, but that goal was all Toure. ---
--- 82’ Goal! WHAT A CASUAL BIT OF BRILLIANCE! There appeard to be no danger when Toure picked up the ball on the edge of the box, but he let Sagna's pass run to his left foot, before lifting a magnificent first-time effort into the far corner, with Cech and everyone else rooted to the spot! ---
(80’) A complaint of Arsenal in previous years was the lack of pace and direct runners in their ranks. How that has changed, with the Gunners always having at least two options on the pitch who can be relied on to beat or out-sprint their man. And that's been without Alexis tonight!
(78’) CITY DENIED! A swift move has Navas racing behind the defence, and he's got the pace to keep the distance between himself and his man. He's got Bony trying to arrive in support, and attempts to pick him out instead of taking the better option of going for goal himself. The ball gets intercepted and the chance is gone.
--- 76’ Substitution Ozil gets a standing ovation and an early rest as he is pulled for the Ox. Two assists - business as usual. ---
(75’) Gibbs leads the Gunners on their umpteenth counter-attack, but his attempt to lift the ball over the top for Walcott is met with a quite superb defensive header from Mangala that guides the ball to Otamendi.
--- 73’ Substitution Substitution David Josué Jiménez Silva Jesús Navas González ---
(73’) Ramsey sails past a challenge and plays the ball to Ozil, who does the same. Monreal is in support on the left as ever, and hoists in a dangerous ball into the six-yard area, but Giroud can't get there in time! Moments before, Ramsey had dribbled pas two players in the box but placed his finish well wide of the mark.
(71’) Bravery or stupidity from Flamini? Certain Arsenal fans might tell you that those lines are often blurred with the Frenchman. He gets right in front of a hammer from Kolarov, blocking the shot without a wince.
--- 70’ Substitution Off goes Campbell and on comes Gibbs to play in front of Monreal, in a defensive substitution that we see fairly regularly from Arsene Wenger. ---
(69’) Giroud does commendably to win the ball back for Arsenal, and he lays it off to Ramsey. The Welshman has Walcott storming down that porous City left flank, but his ball has too much mustard on it and goes through to Hart. Ramsey looks frustrated at his lack of execution.
(67’) Toure has the ball on the corner of the box and tries to give Bony his first sip of the action as he pings a strong cross into the area. However, there's far too much pace behind that cross, and Bony can't contort his neck in time mid-jump to direct his compatriot's delivery on target.
(65’) A long punt forward finds Walcott on the spring with three defenders in front of him. He opts against the headline, holding up the ball to release Bellerin out wide. Giroud motors into the area, but the Spaniard's cross can't pick him out.

(61’) City are temporarily down to 10 men as Aguero jogs off right to the bench. Bony was being prepped to replace him but the Argentine has got his jacket on in the dugout before the Ivorian has entered the pitch.
(59’) HOW ARE ARSENAL NOT THREE UP? Ozil has the ball on the edge of the area and a five-on-three advantage. Arsenal should have scored there - they simply had too many open players around the box. That said - credit to Hart for that stop!

(50’) This is a superb position for Arsenal to be in. They've been defending well so far and can focus all their energies on frustrating City, with the likes of Walcott and Ozil entirely capable of leading a counter-attack whenever those opportunuties present themselves.

Full time at Carrow Road. It has been a game of two halves in the early kick-off between Norwich and Everton as the two Barclays Premier League outfits share the honours in an entertaining 1-1 draw.  The home side were prettty awful in the first half, and went behind, perhaps predictably, to the in-form Romelu Lukaku. Roberto Martinez's men dominated after taking the lead and created plenty of chances, but were unable to tally up more goals, which gave Norwich the confidence to get back into the game after half-time. Alex Neil's men netted shortly after the break through Hoolahan, but couldn't get that elusive second goal for the win. Overall, a missed opportunity for Everton! Thanks for joining us, and enjoy the afternoon fixtures!

(90’) Three minutes of added time signaled by the referee which sounds about right as we have had a relatively free-flowing second period. Should this game finish at 1-1, it will be seen as a horribly missed opportunity for Everton, who seemed poised to grab all three points and indeed tally up a few goals.
(88’) A draw doesn't particularly suit either team here as the victory would see the respective winner catapult a few positions up the table. A point a-piece would certainly be more welcomed by Norwich though, who were arguably lucky not to go into half time three or four goals down. Will we see a winner?!

(82’) Less than 10 minutes to go and there is definitely a winner in this game, but who will it be? Norwich have been by far the better side in the second period but the fact remains that Everton have the more talented players in the final third, even with Lukaku having dropped off the pace slightly. The Belgian did score late on to secure a draw against Crystal Palace on Monday, and his team need him once again, this time for the win.

(78’) SAAAAAAAAAVE FROM RUDD! Kone picks up the ball down the left touchline and quickly shifts inside before sliding a precision pass into the feet of Barry, who rolls the defender in order to turn and lash a strike at goal, but he is foiled by the Norwich keeper, who proactively comes off his line to smother the attempt at the front post!
--- 76’ Substitution Another change from Everton now and it sees the ineffectual Ross Barkley make way for Darron Gibson, who certainly doesn't need to be asked twice to get a shot away if he finds himself in the right position. Hoolahan drifts beyond Mirallas down the right wing and makes it to the byline before managing to reverse a pass into the space on the edge of the six-yard box! The 29-year-old striker meets it, but manages to balloon over the bar with the goal gaping! What a golden chance that was for the Canaries to take a vital lead!
--- 69’ Substitution First change of the match from Roberto Martinez and coming off is Deulofeu, who has not been as effective in the second period, make way for the pacey Belgian, Kevin Mirallas. ---
(67’) Superb block by Olsson! It is all very tight in the home penalty area as Everton try and find a pocket of space! Kone eventually collects the ball and fires a pass into the feet of Lukaku, who returns the favour witha clever flick! The Ivorian shifts possession to his right before smashing a strike at goal, but the left-back is on hand to make the brave tackle!
(65’) What an awful pass from Redmond! The former Birmingham winger takes advantage of the space vacated by Baines at left back and drives forward down the wing with authority! Jerome makes a great run into the middle to be completely unmarked, but the pass into the middle from his team-mate goes straight into the arms of Howard, much to the frustration of the Norwich faithful!

With their position in the table, they probably shouldn't be sacrificing a point to go for the win, but you have to admire their desire to get forward!
(57’) If there is one team who is looking more likely to take the lead here, it is Norwich! Goal kick to the home side and the crowd cheer in anticipation.

There is just a bit more desire, and indeed confidence, in the play of the Canaries now, so at least Everton have something to think about defensively!
(53’) Lukaku receives the ball to feet on the edge of the box and holds off the challenge of Martin with his impressive strength before turning on to his left foot, looking to get the shot away. (51’) The audio microphones at the side of the park pick up a huge scream from Deulofeu as the Everton winger goes down clutching his face after a collision with Olsson down the touchline. He was certainly caught by the stray arm of the left-back, but the contact no where near warranted such a screech!
(49’) Deulofeu attempts to claw Everton back ahead here with yet another driving run down the right wing! He leaves Olsson for dead with a couple of stepovers before chipping a cross to the area around the penalty spot! Norwich clear and Cleverley collects before attempting to strike into the empty net on the half volley, but he was compltely off balance and the attempt sails over the crossbar.
--- 47’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLL FOR NORWICH! WHAT A START TO THE SECOND HALF! Brady whips a deep corner kick to the back post and Bennett rises high to head towards the bottom corner, where Barkley blocks on the line! Hoolahan is on hand to scramble home from a yard out! One-one! GAME ON! ---
(47’) We are back under way at Carrow Road!

Half time at Carrow Road. Everton continue their superb recent form, and indeed Norwich continue their poor recent form, as the Toffees lead 1-0 at the break in this early Barclays Premier League clash. The home side made a decent start and had a nice tempo to their game, but the nerves at the back eventually started to appear again and Roberto Martinez's outfit eventually took the lead after a lovely move and eventual finish from Romelu Lukaku, who nets in his sixth game on the bounce. Everton look good value for more goals, too! Second half to come.
(45’) Well it seems that Stones is made from some tough stuff as he makes his way back on to the pitch after a quick patch up from the Everton physios. It did look potentially damaging, the way he fell off the pitch, but it will take more than that to keep him from seeing out the game by the looks of it!
(43’) Some worrying scenes for Everton at the moment as Stones, who had an injury worry before the game, slips horribly off the side of the pitch after failing to make a decent connection on a header from a corner kick to the front post. The England defender is down at the running track part of the ground, and it doesn't look to promising! He'll probably be assessed at the break!
(41’) Rudd to the rescue again for Norwich! The home side surrender possession far too cheaply in the middle of the park again and this allows Everton to burst forward on the counter, with Kone running through on goal! It is similar to his earlier chance though as he just can't squeeze a strike under the oncoming goalkeeper! The home fans air their discontent at their team's display at the moment!
(39’) BAINES HITS THE POST! Everton come forward with lovely flowing move and Deulofeu eventually clips a teasing cross to the edge of the area! Lukaku doesn't manage to make a connection on it, but the returning left-back takes an assured touch before firing a right-footed half volley at goal, which cannons off the inside of the woodwork! So unlucky, and on his weaker foot too!
(37’) Everton are suffocating Norwich in their own half of the pitch at the moment with their continuous pressing in the final third. Lukaku has been leading the tactic and is not giving the opposition an inch of space, which is making the home fans rather tense at the moment! The Toffees well on top currently!
(35’) Coleman typically opens up his stride down the right with a galloping run and lashes the ball into the feet of Deulofeu, who attempts to return the favour with a one-two in behind the Norwich defence, but the Irishman just went ahead of the play too quickly and is subsequently flagged as offside.
(33’) Just over 10 minutes remaining in this first period and Everton are looking comfortable out there, and also appear to be good value to add more goals to their tally. Lukaku should have scored at least two so far, with another couple of other opportunities having came and gone also!
(31’) AN INCREDIBLE MISS FROM LUKAKU! Cleverley makes his way into the final third and eventually gets himself into a great position just a yard inside the area. You would have put your mortgage on him scoring that considering the form he's in! Norwich survive!
(29’) Brady picks up the ball a few yards in from the left touchline and glides inside before looking to thread a pass through for the darting run of Jerome, but Stones is on hand to clean up with typical composure before playing out of defence. Everton on the counter!
(27’) Jerome looks to take matters into his own hands with a penetrating run down the right-hand side. The former Birmingham attacker makes it to the byline and then stands a lovely, teasing cross to the edge of the box, but before Hoolahan can get the strike away, Deulofeu vigilantly gets back and makes the block! Great defensive work from the young Spaniard!
(25’) Norwich have had their fair share of possession up until now, but it has been their final ball which has disappointed as Jerome hasn't had any good deliveries to work with inside the box. Redmond and Brady, who started the game pretty well, have just lost a bit of quality with their crossing in the past 10 minutes or so.
(23’) Ominously for the home side, Lukaku and Deulofeu are looking hungry to continue their superb recent form today, which has been peppered with goals and assists. Any time the duo link up in the final third, they seem poised to at the very least test the goalkeeper!
(21’) Norwich are shooting themselves in the foot constantly here with their poor possession in defence and midfield! There may not have been an individual error for the conceded goal, but they are looking likely to concede a lot more unless they sort themselves out at the back!
(19’) VITAL SAVE FROM RUDD! Everton are running riot at the moment and Lukaku is at the heart of the action again as he comes deep to receive the ball before sliding a pass through to Kone! --- 15’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLL FOR EVERTON! THE TOFFEES TAKE THE LEAD! The form of each team couldn't really be more in contrast heading into today's match, but over the years it has proved to be a fairly evenly matched fixture. Five of the last seven encounters have ended in a draw, with each team earning a win a-piece. Carrow Road has not been a particularly happy hunting ground for Everton over the years, as they have came out victorious just once in their last seven trips.
Norwich and Everton have already faced each other this season and the clash came back in October in the League Cup. On that occasion, the match ended 1-1 after goals from Leon Osman and Sebastian Bassong for their respective sides, but it would be the Toffees who would prevail and progress to the quarter-finals after winning 4-3 in a dramatic penalty shoot-out.
Norwich, meanwhile, who were promoted from the Championship last campaign, have had a perhaps predictably tough return to the top flight and find themselves only out of the relegation by virtue of goal difference. After a fairly decent start to the season, Alex Neil's outfit have won just once in their last 10 league matches, with the latest defeat coming last week at the hands of Watford, who won 2-0 thanks to goals from Troy Deeney and Odion Ighalo.
This impressive run is in no small part down to star striker, Romelu Lukaku, who has 11 goals in 15 games in the league up until this afternoon. He was once again proved to be the hero of his side in Everton's clash on Monday evening with Crystal Palace, which saw the Belgian equalise with 10 minutes to go after Alan Pardew's outfit took a surprise lead, ending the game at 1-1. Martinez has even went as far to compare his player to the likes of Sergio Aguero in terms of impact and talent in recent weeks.
Roberto Martinez's men have endured a solid start to their domestic campaign this season and are currently situated ninth, with 22 points taken from their opening 15 matches. They have lost just two matches out of their last 16 in all competitions, and it is only due to a fairly high amount of draws that they don't find themselves higher in the table.

(22’) NOT FAR OFF! Zaha is faced by a defender but shifts the ball onto his right foot before shooting. He just got too much on his effort, though, as it just clears the bar.

(15’) Southampton could have expected a close game this afternoon. They are currently on a four-match winless run but, at the same time, have lost just one of their last seven matches on the road.

Late drama at the Etihad as Bafetimbi Gomis and Yaya Toure exchange goals in the final minutes as the Citizens survive an impressive response from the Swans following Monk's departure. Pellegrini's side move top of the table for the time being, with Leicester and Arsenal still to play this weekend.

--- 90’ +2 Goal! Goal Kelechi Promise Iheanacho ---
--- 90’ Assist What an absolutely incredible ball that was from Fernandez to play the striker through! Extraordinary! ---
--- 90’ Goal! SWANSEA INCREDIBLY ARE LEVEL! Fernandez plays a absolutely incredible, searching ball forward to send Gomis through behind the defence and the substitute makes no mistake this time in smashing a ball beyond Hart at the near post! ---
(88’) JUST OVER! More great buildup play from the visitors and Sigurdsson plays a delicious ball in for Gomis. The striker sends a looping header over the keeper, but it rattles off the top of the bar and onto the roof of the goal.

Gomis is played through onside by Sigurdsson, but Hart comes off his line quickly to get enough of a touch to knock it away from the striker before getting absolutely clattered by the Frenchman. (82’) City win the ball back finally and get forward to earn themselves a corner. They will want to keep the ball in the Swansea end as long as they can, but are unsucessful in doing so as Otamendi's header is sent wide and Swansea can start back up again.
(80’) Into the final 10 minutes and it remains Swansea who are on the ball and searching for the decisive second goal of this match. They have committed themselves so well today but you just have to wonder how much they have left in the tank.
(78’) DEFLECTED BEHIND! The ensuing free kick isn't properly dealt with and it comes to Cork. The midfielder does well to get the ball out of his feet and unleash a strike at goal, but Delph is able to get a block to it!

(74’) STAT: Manchester City have fired in more shots on target than any other team in the Premier League so far this season (99 - or 6.6 per match). They have just three so far today.

(64’) STAT: Manuel Pellegrini’s side have won 13 and lost two of their last 15 Premier League home games - not a single draw in that span.
(62’) There is a growing sense of anxiety in the Etihad as Swansea City continue to push back. Sigurdsson's effort from the free kick is punched away smartly by Hart, who has unquestionably been the busier of the two keepers since the opening kick of the match.

So close, yet again!
(54’) STAT: Swansea have suffered through their worst-ever start to a Premier League season with 14 points from 15 matches (W3, D5, L7).
