(48’) City start the second half where they left off in the first, struggling to push the pace in possession, while Swansea have come out rested and eager to win the ball back. The visitors are by no means out of this contest just yet, especially given the sluggish nature of the hosts.
--- 46’ Substitution Fabian Delph replaces Sterling at the break, which will likely prompt a bit of a reshuffling of the formation as City move to more of a 4-3-3 for this second half. ---
(46’) Back underway at the Etihad!
Manchester City in front at the interval with Bony inevitably scoring against his former side, but it was Hart who proved the busier of the two keepers, called into action to deny Routledge inside 10 minutes and then again had a difficult save to make off Sigurdsson's effort with the game still scoreless. Despite the hosts being in front, you would have to say that, considering the run of play in the first half, the points are still there for the taking.

(45’) There will be just one minute added on at the end of this first half.
--- 43’ Yellow card Madley has done well to keep his cards in his pocket during this first half, but Neil Taylor can't escape yellow as a pair of untidy challenges on Navas see him into the referee's book. ---
(42’) DELIGHTFUL BALL! Such clever improvisation from Toure, who spots the run of Sterling and just pokes the ball out of his feet to chip a stunning little ball over the top for the ex-Liverpool forward, but Fabianski is wise to it. The keeper arrives just in time to deny what would have been a killer second goal before the interval.
(40’) STAT: Man City have had the most different scorers in the Premier League this season (13), while Swansea have had the joint-fewest (four, alongside Watford and Stoke).
(38’) Swansea are doing everything they can to push the pace in possession, looking to work the ball up the pitch with great intent. You would figure a quicker pace to the match would favour the hosts, but with the Welsh side in need of a goal they have little choice otherwise.
(36’) Madley has a talk with Sterling as play comes to a halt following a coming together between him and Williams. The winger tried to play on despite spotting the offside flag and the centre-half tossed him aside to get the ball back. Sterling got up and retaliated, which prompted Madley to try and settle things down.
(34’) There isn't a great deal of tempo to this match when City are in possession. Despite being in front, their lethargic approach in possession has elicited a few groans from these fans at the Etihad who are becoming harder and harder to please.

(30’) STAT: Wilfried Bony has now scored four goals in the last three Premier League meetings between Man City and Swansea, three for the Welsh side and two as a Citizen player.

(19’) STAT: Swansea have failed to score in seven of their last 11 Premier League games, including four of their last five.

The Welsh outfit turn over a new leaf today, out to recapture the magic that saw them salvage their season when Monk replaced Michael Laudrup in February 2014. Alan Curtis takes over as caretaker manager for a second time, also filling the role for a brief period in 2004 with the club in the fourth tier of English football. The former striker made close to 350 appearances for Swansea in his playing career while also enjoying stints with Leeds United, Southampton, Stoke, Cardiff and Barry. He was capped 35 times by the Wales national team, scoring six times.
Swansea are starting a new era following the controversial dismissal of manager Garry Monk on Wednesday. The former Swans defender was held in very high regard and considered one of the best up and coming coaches in the UK after taking the club to new heights last season. He set the bar too high in the end, perhaps, as they struggled to rediscover the unsustainable form which they started with under the 36-year-old. What started as a dip in form wound up becoming a landslide down the table and Chairman Huw Jenkins was forced into action.
Hello Premier League fans around the world and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester City and Swansea from the Etihad, with the hosts looking to at least temporarily reclaim first place. Manuel Pellegrini’s men followed a disappointing defeat at Stoke last weekend with a hammering of Bundesliga outfit Monchengladbach midweek, and are hoping to carry that momentum through to today’s clash with their struggling Welsh opponents.

Full time at the Boleyn Ground. West Ham and Stoke share the honours in this Barclays Premier League clash, which ends at a 0-0 stalemate. The scoreline doesn't really tell the story as both sides had plenty of chances to take the lead, with the best opportunites falling to Diouf, Kouyate, and Van Ginkel, but both goalkeepers, Adrian and Butland, were certainly on form to deny the respective attackers in the opposition. A fair result, but one that both managers probably won't be content with! Thanks for joining us folks, see you next time!
(90’) It looks like we are consigned to a 0-0 stalemate in London and if you were to put money on a result before the game, you would probably have said a draw, such as the similar abilities of both outfits. Surely we can't have a winner this late?!
(90’) Four minutes of added time have been signaled by the referee here so there is still time for West Ham or Stoke to grab a win at the death. The home side are enjoying the majority of possession, but Hughes' men have proved they are still a threat on the counterattack!
(88’) DIOUF MUST SCORE!! Stoke counterattack at tremendous pace through Bojan and Arnautovic and the Austrian slides a perfect pass into the box for the substitute, who doesn't look comfortable at all one-on-one with the keeper and ends up firing a strike right at the feet of  Adrian!
(86’) BUTLAND CALLED INTO ACTION! Both sides have had a good bit of joy from set-pieces this afternoon, and the latest threat comes from Valencia who steps up to drive a vicious strike at goal from a 25-yard free kick. The Stoke keeper, ever reliable, manages to get across goal to beat the attempt away, though!
(84’) Five or so minutes remaining now and both West Ham and Stoke are running out of time if they still have aspirations of claiming all three points at the Boleyn Ground! A draw is probably a relatively fair result, both Bilic or Hughes won't care if someone pops up with a winner!
--- 83’ Substitution Another alteration from Bilic here as he brings on another striker in the form of Nikica Jelavic, who will be introduced to replace Antonio. ---
(82’) WEST HAM HIT THE POST! Zarate, who scored a spectacular free kick a couple of weeks ago, looks to be the hero for the Hammers again as he collects the ball around 20 yards out before drilling a lovely strike low towards goal! Stoke survive though as his attempt cannons off the bottom of the woodwork! How is this game still 0-0?!
(80’) Another goalkeeper is called into action as Adrian denies Stoke again! This time, the Potters catch West Ham on the counterattack with some authoritative running into space by Bojan, who picks out Diouf at the back post! The substitute opens up his boot and looks to smash into the bottom corner, but the West Ham keepers makes the save with his feet! That should have been a goal for the visitors!
(78’) WHAT A SAVE FROM BUTLAND! West Ham press forward down the left channel and the ball eventually comes to Cresswell, who hits a cross-cum-shot deep to the far post which actually sees the Stoke goalkeeper scramble to get back! In the end, the England international retreats and manages to tip round the post to prevent a freak goal from the former Birmingham full-back!
(76’) It is a fairly dour period in the match at the moment as both sides can't really muster up any kind of ascendancy in the final third. Attacking changes may have been made, but the respective alterations are yet to really catch fire. Still plenty of time for that to change though!
(74’) Just over 15 minutes to go in this Premier League clash and as it stands, both sides will be going home with a point, but it is not for lack of trying as there is some decent play going forward. It just may be the case that we are witnessing two spectacularly evenly matched teams - which is kind of already proved by their standings in the table!
(72’) JUST WIDE FROM NOBLE! The West Ham makes a late run into the penalty area and takes the ball in with an assured touch before going for the bottom right corner with a low strike, but it is further frustration for the Hammers faithful as the captain's attempt is lashed wide by a yard or so! Not bad, but he probably should have hit the target!
(70’) This game has burst into life in the past 10 minutes or so and we are being treated to some rather entertaining end-to-end football from West Ham and Stoke! The substitutions suggest that neither manager is looking to shut up shop, so there is a real possibility we may actually see some goals this afternoon! Who will strike first, and will it be the winner?
--- 68’ Substitution Third and final change from the Potters and it is another positive one as Cameron makes way for Charlie Adam. ---
(68’) STOKE HIT THE BAR!!! Arnautovic steps up to the 35-yard free kick and smashes his attempt which takes a wicked deflection off the top of the wall before looping ominously towards goal! Adrian struggles to retreat but he is let off the hook as the Austrian's set-piece cannons off the woodwork! Bojan goes for the rebound but sends it way over the bar!
--- 67’ Yellow card Booking for Kouyate as he gives the daft foul away in a useful position for stoke. Arnautovic fancies this one... ---
--- 66’ Substitution The changes are coming thick and fast now and to be fair to both Bilic and Hughes, it looks like they both aren't particularly happy with their attacking play or the proposition of just taking the solitary point. --- 64’ Substitution Positive substitution from Slaven Bilic now as he withdraws a defensive midfielder, Alex Song, in favour of the returning Enner Valencia, who will certainly provide the hosts with a lot more fire power up top. They have missed the Ecuadorian in his injury absence! ---
--- 63’ Yellow card A deserved booking for Afellay here as the Dutchman cynically trips up Kouyate to halt a West Ham counter. ---

Afellay eventually cuts inside and slides a precision pass in between the West Ham defenders for Arnautovic, who lashes a low strike at goal! (60’) SAAAAAAAAAVE FROM BUTLAND! Lovely move from the Hammers, and it nearly paid off!

Great start to the second period from the Hammers!

(25’) Stoke seem relatively content to let West Ham have the ball at the back for a small period of sustained possession at the moment. West Ham feature at home today, but will be in front of their own fans without a plethora of star players due to a recent injury crisis. Currently in the treatment room are Winston Reid, Victor Moses, Dimitri Payet, Diafra Sakho, Manuel Lanzini, and Enner Valencia, so they will need to rely on some fringe players to put in a performance. Mauro Zarate, who has been a bright spark in recent weeks, should be okay to feature, however.
This resurgence in form has seen Stoke bounce back from a poor start to the season, as they currently find themselves in 11th place on 22 points – just one point off sixth. Goalscoring still remains a slight issue, though, as they have the joint-worst record for netting in the league alongside Aston Villa on just 14.
Since being promoted to the top flight, Stoke have been notoriously direct with their attacking play under the tutelage of Tony Pulis, with more of the focus being on defensive solidity than creativity in the final third. However, Hughes is slowly but surely changing the philosophy of the Potters, but without surrendering the stability at the back. They have actually kept six clean sheets out of the last eight games since the return of club captain, Ryan Shawcross, in the heart of the defence.
Last weekend, Mark Hughes' outfit made the whole country stand up and take notice when they successfully, and emphatically, defeated title favourites, Manchester City 2-0 at the Britannia Stadium. Marko Arnautovic was the star of the show as he netted two goals, but it was the Austrian's link-up play with Xherdan Shaqiri and Bojan that proved to be the real highlight, with the trio displaying a spectacular cohesion that City simply couldn't deal with.

(79’) The home fans are making plenty of noise, as they urge their side towards the finish line of what would be one of their biggest results of the season. (77’) Powell releases Borthwick-Jackson down the left flank, but the young full-back's attempted delivery is utterly woeful. The Frenchman dances beyond two challenges, before lashing an awful shot high and wide of the target!
(75’) Only a quarter of an hour remains for the visitors to claw back at least a point, with it looking likely that Van Gaal's side will be dropping points in the race for a top-four finish. Man United are being asked to attack, with Bournemouth biding their time to counter.
--- 74’ Substitution Man United's goalscorer makes way for the remaining minutes, with Powell coming into the fray in an attempt to rejuvenate the midfield. ---

(56’) King manages to loop a chipped effort just wide of the far post, before Man United counter! Fellaini musters up a close-range effort, with the Belgian forcing a hurried parry from Boruc! The rebound is put behind by Cook, with the resulting corner coming to nothing for the away outfit.
--- 54’ Assist Ritchie whips a dangerous corner delivery into the box, which King promptly puts the finishing touches to. ---
--- 54’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! THE EX RED DEVIL STRIKES! The Norway international manages to fire home a neat finish from a corner, after Francis did so well to win the set piece. (46’) We are back underway in the second half! Bournemouth are level with one of the division's Champions League hunting sides, but Howe's men will want anything less than a win! The Cherries have proved that they can contend with some of the top-flight's big boys recently.

(39’) Memphis tries to lift a cross in from the left, with Fellaini the target at the back post! The Belgian midfielder, however, can't get anywhere near what is a poorly weighted delivery. In stark contrast to their opponents, Arsenal are now unbeaten in their last four games in all competitions and will be full of confidence thanks to Wednesday’s spirited and hard-fought 3-0 win against Olympiakos, which confirmed their place in the knockout stage of the Champions League for the 17th year in a row. (61’) That just about sums it up for them, however. They have a throw-in near the far corner flag, but De Jong's return pass to Janmaat is directed straight out of play and the chance is gone.
(59’) The signs are looking a little better for Newcastle over the past couple of minutes. They still need to do a lot more to threaten Spurs but they are making more opportunities for themselves in possession.
(57’) Newcastle are awarded their first corner of the game after good work from De Jong down the left. However, his subsequent delivery is disappointing and Spurs are able to clear without too many difficulties.
(55’) Spurs are back on top in terms of their quality of possession in this second half. There is a lot more flow to their play as opposed to that of Newcastle so far. The visitors will be encouraged by that Cisse chance, though.
(53’) GOOD EFFORT! Some space opens up in front of Kane, who tries his luck from 25 yards, and Elliot has to spring to his right and get a strong palm on the fierce drive.

(50’) Into the wall... There is a lot of anticipation ahead of the delivery, but Eriksen sends it straight into the wall and Newcastle are allowed to relax for a moment.
(48’) Spurs launch a very dangerous counter attack following a Newcastle throw-in near their own penalty area. Alli is tripped by Anita just outside the visitors' box and Eriksen is stood over the free kick...
(46’) KICK OFF! Mr East blows the whistle and Spurs get the ball rolling again in the second half.
The players are back out on the field and the second half is about to commence.
Newcastle need to severely up their performance levels if they are to get anything out of this second half. They must at least gain a foothold in the contest after the break.
Spurs are looking very good value for their lead at the break. They have been very dominant in the first half and will be looking to keep that up after the break.

(45’) Referee Roger East blows his whistle to bring the first half to an end.

(28’) The hosts continue to dominate in possession, but they need to start causing more problems in the final third. Newcastle have looked vulnerable in defence this season, so Spurs should exploit that more.
(26’) Spurs are awarded a free kick near the touchline and send both centre-halves forward as Eriksen stands over the ball. His delivery is very disappointing, however, and Newcastle are able to clear.
(24’) Newcastle need to force their way into this game if they are to make it back-to-back wins. Ironically, the last time they achieved that feat was here last season when they came from 1-0 down to record a 2-1 victory.

(16’) Newcastle just cannot keep hold of the ball at the moment. After being pinned inside their own half for as long as they have been, they need to make more of their possession and try to gain a foothold in the contest.
(14’) There is a slight break in play as Rose receives attention after appearing to overstretch when he tried to retrieve possession. Spurs are looking very dangerous at the moment, but can Newcastle weather the storm?

(10’) Spurs have made the stronger start of the two sides. They are looking a lot quicker and sharper on the ball and getting forward regularly, while Newcastle appear to be quite sluggish at the moment.
(8’) Rose bombs forward down the left flank to latch onto Eriksen's through ball, but puts far too much power into his cross and sees it fly over the defence and out for a throw-in. He appeared to get too excited at the vital moment.
(6’) Those were good signs for the visitors. They will fancy their chances here having won on their last two visits, but it will be difficult against a strong Spurs side.
(4’) GET OUT THE WAY! Newcastle launch a promising counter attack and De Jong gets his shot away. He was in an offside position, too, much to the Dutchman's annoyance.
(2’) Spurs go straight onto the attack with Kane working space for himself to shoot. His effort is creeping inside the near post, but Elliot gets down well to save.
(1’) KICK OFF! The referee blows the whistle and Newcastle get the match underway.

Good afternoon and welcome to LIVE text commentary of the Barclays Premier League. We're at White Hart Lane today as Tottenham Hotspur face Newcastle United.

Meanwhile, the crisis continues for Chelsea, who remain marginally outside of the relegation zone with just four wins from 16 games. They looked off the pace today whilst continually struggling at the back, allowing Leicester to find far too much joy time and time again. They will face Sunderland in their next league game, and that is an absolute must win for Mourinho's struggling Blues.
Leicester manage to hold on and pick up three huge points that send them back to the top of the Premier League table! They fully deserve the victory after putting in such an impressive shift at both ends of the pitch, and they did well to contain Chelsea before punishing them on the counter-attack time and time again. They now travel to Everton in their final game before Christmas, but will have to do so with Huth, who will be suspended after picking up a yellow card today.

(89’) Ball after ball is flung into the Leicester penalty area, but there are so many blue shirts back to deal with the danger. (80’) Kante crashes into the back of Remy and brings the striker down, resulting in a free kick for Chelsea in a dangerous area 30 yards away from goal. (79’) It's all Chelsea as they continue to push forward in search of a late equaliser. Leicester are progressively sitting deeper and deeper and this could cause them problems as the visitors keep pressurising them.
--- 77’ Assist That was a wonderful cross by Pedro, who has been largely anonymous since replacing Hazard but is now starting to come to life as Leicester drop deeper. ---
--- 77’ Goal! GOAL! Chelsea have pulled one back! Pedro drifts out to the left wing to pick up the ball before whipping a beautiful cross into the heart of the penalty area. (75’) Chance for Remy! Willian flies into the left-hand side of the Leicester box before spinning and teeing up the aforementioned Frenchman. He's in a great position to shoot but instead decides to take a touch, allowing Fuchs to easily cut out the danger.
(74’) Costa breaks down the right wing on a marauding run before attempting to cut inside and penetrate the penalty area, but Huth is there to stop the Spaniard's run with a vital interception.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this evening…
Chelsea were handed a boost during the week with a 2-0 win at home to Porto that sent them into the knockout stage of the Champions League, but last weekend saw further domestic misery inflicted on them when they were beaten 1-0 by Bournemouth in a thoroughly disappointing display at Stamford Bridge. The Blues will be hoping that their midweek victory will prove to be the result that finally kickstarts a comeback, and looking at the table they desperately need that to be the case. With only 15 points on the board the reigning champions now sit just one point clear of the relegation zone, and if they are beaten again today it will be their ninth defeat of the campaign, the same amount that they suffered in their last two seasons combined.
This will be a real test for Leicester, however, as they have a difficult few weeks to contend with. Tonight’s game is followed by back-to-back clashes against Everton and Liverpool before they end 2015 with a tough game at home to Manchester City. These four encounters will tell us a lot about the Foxes and whether or not they can be seriously seen as title contenders.
This evening’s encounter not only sees Claudio Ranieri take on the side that he led for four years but also brings together two old foes that have clashed on countless occasions. The Italian is one of many managers to have been on the receiving end of Jose Mourinho’s sharp tongue since the Portuguese took his place in the Chelsea dugout, but in the run-up to this game the Blues boss has been full of praise for the job that his opposite number has done, and rightly so. This game is third versus 16th, but before the start of the season you would have put money on the two teams’ positions being the other way round. Leicester are continuing to enjoy life near the top of the Premier League table and their miraculous run is showing no signs of stopping anytime soon. They are now unbeaten in their last eight league games, six of which have ended in victories, and another win will send them back to the summit, two points clear of nearest challengers Arsenal.

(87’) Navas and Arnautovic have a disagreement off the field, with the latter attempting to block the former Sevilla winger from getting the ball back quickly. Man City continue with their attack, but it only results in Sterling blasting a terrible effort high into the stands - much to the amusement of the home supporters.
--- 85’ Substitution Walters now comes into the front three, with the ex-Ipswich striker being asked to work hard and offer an outlet up top. ---
(84’) Man City are looking lost, with the Citizens set to surrender top spot today as it stands. Stoke, meanwhile, will clamber further away from the relegation-zone mire and hope that this result breathes some confidence into a long run of good form.
(82’) Stoke slow the game down whenever they can, holding onto the ball and finding the spare man providing by Fernando's absence. Joselu is happy to do plenty of running, after only coming on during the last 15 minutes, with Man City unable to wrestle control from the hosts.
(80’) We're into the final 10 minutes on Stoke's stomping ground, with Pellegrini's side looking utterly out of ideas. Despite making a few changes, the Citizens have been unable to do much more than force Butland into relatively easy stops at his near post. Both Bony and Ineanacho have been kept extremely quiet.
(78’) It's end-to-end stuff at the moment, with both teams reluctantly edging their way back and forth. Butland is happy to take his time over his goal kicks now, with Man City running out of time to stage a comeback. The same goes for Pieters, who takes time to applaud the home fans while collecting the ball for a throw in.
--- 77’ Substitution Van Ginkel will look to add some fresh legs into the midfield for the dying minutes at the Britannia. ---
(76’) Stoke look to have the perfect opportunity to secure the three points now, with the away fans watching on in disbelief. Given that the home side can sit back with six or so players, it will be tough for Man City to break their resolve. Kolarov breaks down the left, but can only slam a powerful finish into the side netting!
(74’) Only a quarter of an hour remains at the Britannia, with Fernando now hobbling off with an injury. Due to already making a trio of changes, Pellegrini's side will be forced to play on with merely 10 men.
--- 72’ Substitution After an energetic and dangerous performance, the former Roma forward takes his leave for the fresh legs of compatriot Joselu. ---
(71’) OFF THE LINE FROM DEMICHELIS! Bojan manages to scramble beyond Sagna and go on-one-on with Hart, after teeing himself up from a Shaqiri through ball! The Spaniard stretches, lifting a finish over the goalkeeper, but the recovering ex-Atletico Madrid defender spares his teammate's blushes!
(70’) Sterling is picked out bustling his way into the Stoke penalty box, but the former QPR youngster can only guide a tame shot directly at Butland! Man City have simply not been clinical enough this afternoon, they don't deserve to come away with anything as it stands. There is activity on Hughes' men, with a substitution soon in the offing.
(69’) How has he managed that! Arnautovic is fed into the Man City penalty area by Bojan, before the Austrian sets a fantastic ball across the six-yard line! With Hart out of position and the unguarded net at his mercy, Shaqiri can only pass wide of the target! It would have been easier to make it 3-0!
(68’) Navas and Sagna combine down the right-hand side, but a cross from the former is easily headed clear at the near post! Bojan tries to lead a break as a result, but Fernando lumbers across to outmuscle the former Ajax man. Moments later, Stoke attack again, but Demichelis is on hand to dispossess the ex-Barca forward on this occasion.
(66’) Delph musters up an attempt from range, but the former Leeds midfielder can only send a looping effort high and wide of the target! Butland will be happy to deal with efforts like that all afternoon. There's a definite sense of urgency from the away side now, but Stoke are defending in numbers and congesting the edge of the penalty box.
(64’) Shaqiri lines up a shot from the edge of the area, but Hart makes a comfortable save! Man City respond by heading up the other end, but a low cross from Kolarov is gathered up by Butland before Ineanacho can get there! Solid goalkeeping yet again from the young Englishman.
--- 62’ Substitution Silva is pulled out of the fray for the visitors, with Navas introduced. If the Spain international didn't pick up a knock, that is a very curious change indeed. ---
(61’) Only half an hour is left on the clock at the Britannia, with Hughes' men happy to grind out a fantastic result in limited fashion. The hosts are content to try and retain possession, before spraying passes out to their exciting wide options.
(59’) Navas is now stripping off on the bench too, with Pellegrini seemingly close to making his final change of the afternoon. Given their injury woes of late, the Citizens don't have a wide range of options to call upon in order to turn this fixture around. Yet again, faith has had to be put in Ineanacho.
--- 57’ Substitution Ineanacho comes into the game after netting against Hull during the week, with the disappointing Bony leaving the field of play. ---
--- 56’ Substitution Pellegrini opts to introduce a new midfield option, with Fernandinho taking his leave. Delph comes into the mix. ---
(56’) Sagna plays a pass down the right flank, with Pieters stepping ahead of De Bruyne to concede a corner! Ineanacho and Delph are being readied on the touchline for the away side, with Pellegrini recognising that he needs to change something and fast.
(54’) Man City perhaps had a claim for a penalty, with a cross from the left possibly being blocked by an outstretched arm from Shawcross! Arnautovic and Bojan nearly combine to goalscoring effect on the break, but the Spaniard can only test Hart at his near post, before the Austrian hooks a tame finish wide!
(52’) Stoke are approaching the second half in the same way as they did the first, with six players sat back and four roaming about up top. The Potters are causing problems with their quick transitions upfield, with Otamendi and Demichelis not looking the sturdiest of pairings.
--- 51’ Yellow card Shaqiri manages to turn the Argentina international with ease, with the Swiss winger continuing to cause all kinds of issues with his neat dribbling. A deserved yellow for a cynical foul. ---
(50’) A long ball forward from Sterling is cut out by Butland, with Bony continuing to feed off scraps up top. Moments later, a cross from the left-hand side is gathered up by the England international, who did flap at the delivery slightly! A few early nerves for Stoke, perhaps.
(48’) Whelan is left in a heap by Bony, with the former Swansea striker clattering into the Irishman's head with his hip! That takes any sting or momentum out of the game immediately for Man City, who may have hoped for a high octane start to the second half.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Britannia! Man City need to find at least two goals from somewhere if they are to even take home a share of the spoils this afternoon!
HALF TIME! The hosts go into the break with a 2-0 lead over Man City, but it so easily could have been four! Butland has made some good saves in the Stoke net, but the free-roaming inspiration from Shaqiri, Arnautovic and Bojan has proved to be too much for Otamendi and Demichelis to handle. Pellegrini needs to put together a miraculous comeback in this second half!
(45’) The swirling wind causes mayhem in the Man City box, with both Otamendi and Demichelis unable to get rid of a looping cross! Bojan nearly manages to flick a header into the path of Arnautovic, but the attempted through ball escapes the latter! Stoke really should have put this contest beyond any doubt by now.
(44’) ARNAUTOVIC STRIKES THE WOODWORK! So nearly his hat trick! Yet again, the Austria international is fed into the clear, but perhaps has too much time to think about his finish! The former Bundesliga wide man waits for Hart to go down in a one-on-one situation, before guiding a poor finish onto the top of the right-hand post!
(42’) Another delivery in towards Bony is scrambled away by Stoke, with Hughes' men defending brilliantly in the first half. Cameron and Whelan have sat back in disciplined fashion, with even Afellay dropping in to aid his teammates in the midfield battle.
(41’) Only five minutes remain in the first half, with Man City looking to be very much off the pace at the moment. As it stands, Leicester, Man United and Arsenal could all look to stride ahead of the Citizens in the Premier League standings this weekend. Sterling feeds a pass out wide to an overlapping Kolarov, but the Serbia international is denied at the near post by Butland!
(39’) Johnson sees a ball down the line blocked by Kolarov, but Man City can only counter and see a terrible through ball by De Bruyne cut out. The visitors try to mantain their pressure, but an errant touch from Bony is gobbled up by Whelan. There's a slight stoppage in play, as Afellay receives some treatment after being caught late by Fernandinho.
(37’) Nearly a hat trick for Arnautovic! Whelan is found overlapping down the left-hand side, before lifting a cross towards the Austrian forward! He meets the ball with a deft header, but it bobbles its way just shy of the near post! Hart was worried for a moment there.
(35’) Sterling slides a pass out to the right-hand side, before a cross from Sagna is turned behind for a corner. The resulting set-piece delivery loops its way out of the danger zone, before a second cross from the aforementioned ex-Liverpool winger is headed clear by Shawcross! Bojan leads a one-man break as a result, but loses possession after bundling his way through three tackles.
(33’) Pieters is left in a heap on the turf, following a push from Bony, with Man City conceding a lot of unnecessary fouls during the first half at the Britannia. The Dutchman takes his time to get back to his feet, after appearing to land slightly awkwardly.
(31’) Shaqiri slides yet another dangerous through ball into Arnautovic, before the ex-Werder Bremen winger plays a one-two with Bojan! After getting to the byline and receiving the return pass, the Austrian cuts back a cross to Shaqiri that is cut out easily by Sagna! Man City counter, but Bony can only power a horrendous effort high into the stands.
(29’) Arnautovic is hobbling about, with Stoke's goalscorer clipped by a stray stud from Sagna. The hosts won't want for their counter-attacking threats to slope off the field. Stoke win a corner on the left flank, but Man City clear their lines, before a foray forward from De Bruyne results in a poor delivery into the area from the ex-Wolfsburg man.
(27’) Walters is warming up for the home side, with a couple of Stoke forwards looking to be harbouring minor knocks. Pellegrini is looking rather bemused on the Man City bench, with the Chilean coach perhaps needing to chop and change things slightly. Bojan is moving gingerly, after being caught by a late challenge from Demichelis.
(25’) Despite falling behind, Man City have been unable to muster up anything more than a couple of snapshots from just inside the penalty area. Silva hasn't had much possession, with De Bruyne and Sterling causing more problems while drifting in from the flanks. The ex-Valencia midfielder tries to pick out Bony at the back post with a dipping cross, but Wollscheid lashes a simple clearance away.
(23’) Butland is caught straying off his line by a looping header from Sterling, but the effort from the former Liverpool man is off target. Stoke respond with a counter attack, but a cross in from Cameron is deflected away from the danger zone by Otamendi! Kolarov is not having an easy opening half an hour to contend with.
(21’) Bony has been exceptionally quiet thus far, with the Ivory Coast international simply not being given the service required to have an impact on proceedings. Stoke take the sting out of the game with a lengthy spell of possession, with Man City definitely having a real task on their hands to turn this contest on its head.
(19’) Cameron hasn't been called into question while sat in defensive midfield, with Stoke essentially sat with a permanent defensive six. Bojan, Afellay, Shaqiri and Arnautovic are given all of the offensive responsibility, meanwhile. Sterling tries to break into the penalty area and beyond Johnson, but the England international is penalised for pulling on his ex-Liverpool teammate's shirt.
(17’) Once again, Butland is proving his worth for the home side, with the ex-Birmingham's shot-stopper save to deny De Bruyne looking all the more vital now! Pellegrini's men need to find three goals to take three points now, with Hughes' side certainly not looking like falling apart defensively at the moment.
--- 15’ Assist It's that man again! The Switzerland international manages to turn Fernando inside out, before sliding a neat pass through to Arnautovic! The former Bayern man is pulling all of the strings at the moment in this first half. ---
--- 15’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! ARNAUTOVIC TUCKS HOME A SECOND! It's the same combination on the break yet again for the home side, with the former Werder Bremen forward being released beyond the last man and into the clear! After holding his nerve, the Austrian places a low finish through Hart to double the Potters' advantage! ---
(14’) Butland is forced into another neat stop at his near post, with the Englishman definitely the busier of the two goalkeepers thus far! Stoke are weathering the early pressure, but still find themselves with a one-goal lead over the league leaders.
(13’) Pieters earns plenty of applause from the home fans, with the Netherlands international flying into a brilliant crunching tackle on Sagna! The Frenchman dusts himself down gingerly to take the throw in. The Potters are competitive and fiesty in the opening stages on home soil, all while sitting back and waiting for the chance to lethally counter.
(11’) Butland is forced to parry away a pretty simple save, with the England international pouncing upon the rebound with ease. Whelan gives away a terrible pass in midfield, with the visitors making progress down the left as a result. Silva looks to lift an intricate through ball into the path of Sterling, but the Spaniard gets his angles wrong and the pass skids through to the aforementioned hosts' goalkeeper.
(9’) Man City find themselves behind in the early stages, with the Britannia certainly not an easy place to carve out results in difficult circumstances. The visitors earn themselves a corner on the left flank, but it is well cleared, with Bojan trying to lead a Potters' break. The former Barcelona forward is denied well by Otamendi.
--- 7’ Assist The ex-Inter winger weaves his way to the byline, before curling in an inviting cross that Arnautovic simply couldn't help but polish off! ---
--- 7’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! STOKE TAKE THE LEAD! Shaqiri goes on a great run down the right-hand side, before delivering a ball that Arnautovic can't help but tuck home! The Austrian winger ghosts to the edge of the six-yard box, before thumping a close-range finish beyond Hart and into the back of the net! ---
(5’) Wollscheid comes across well to lash a clearance away from De Bruyne, with the Belgian winger on the left-hand side for the time being. Sterling is playing his trade on the right, which is completely different to how the two figured together against Hull. Stoke try to break upfield at pace through Pieters, but Sagna recovers brilliantly to deny the Dutchman.
(3’) Butland is called off his line quickly, with the ex-Birmingham goalkeeper asked to gather up a deflected through ball! Shawcross managed to get enough on the pass to divert it away from Sterling, with Man City calling the shots with some early possession at the Britannia.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! Stoke are in their customary red and white, with Man City taking a dark strip to offer some contrast.
Man City substitutes: Caballero, Navas, Delph, Clichy, Ineanacho, Manuel Garcia, Humphreys.
Man City starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Hart; Sagna, Demichelis, Otamendi, Kolarov; Fernando, Fernandinho; De Bruyne, Silva, Sterling; Bony.
Stoke substitutes: Joselu, Wilson, Van Ginkel, Adam, Diouf, Walters, Haugaard.
Stoke starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Butland; Johnson, Shawcross, Wollscheid, Pieters; Whelan, Cameron; Shaqiri, Afellay, Arnautovic; Bojan.
TEAM NEWS: Eliaquim Mangala misses out due to suspension for the visiting team, with Vincent Kompany and Pablo Zabaleta also absent from the back four due to injury. Martin Demichelis partners Nicolas Otamendi in central defence, with Joe Hart returning in between the sticks. Fernando and Fernandinho make up a sturdy screen for the Man City defence, with only one selection surprise up top. Sergio Aguero and Yaya Toure are still struggling with injuries, meaning that ex-Valencia midfielder David Silva supports Wilfried Bony through the middle.
TEAM NEWS: After scoring during the week, Ibrahim Afellay gets a start in for the hosts, with Bojan deployed up top as a lone striker as a result. Charlie Adam drops to the bench, with Geoff Cameron slotting into defensive midfield alongside Glenn Whelan. Glen Johnson is preferred to Phil Bardsley at right-back, with Philipp Wollscheid chosen to link up with Ryan Shawcross in the heart of the defence.
Both sides find themselves marching into the League Cup semi finals, after defeating Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday respectively during the week, with Stoke actually in better form of late. The hosts have lost merely once during their last five outings, despite that loss coming at the hands of struggling Sunderland. The visitors, meanwhile, haven't kept a clean sheet in four games.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Premier League table toppers Man City's visit to Staffordshire to face Stoke, in the English top flight's early kick off! Manuel Pellegrini's men find themselves above Leicester on goal difference, with ex-Citizens boss Mark Hughes having the Potters sat safely in mid table for the time being.

Giroud scored an own goal seconds before the half-time interval to cancel out Campbell's opener for Arsenal. But the Frenchman made amends by powering home a header just after the hour mark and Ramsey made the win certain soon after with a late goal in stoppage time.
The Gunners rally past a strong Sunderland side to pick up a massive three points in a 3-1 victory at the Emirates Stadium. Goals from Joel Campbell, Olivier Giroud and Aaron Ramsey see off the Black Cats on the day.
FULL TIME: ARSENAL 3-1 SUNDERLAND
--- 90’ +3 Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!! It's 3-1 to Arsenal! The hosts wrap up the three points as Ramsey latches onto a loose ball inside the penalty area and guides an effort past Pantilimon, who gets a hand to the shot but fails to keep it out. ---
(90’) The fourth official on the touchline indicates that a minimum of five minutes is being added on here at the Emirates as Ramsey drills a shot straight at Pantilimon. Is there time for one last twist in the tale?
(88’) BIG CHANCE MISSED! Johnson sprays a lovely pass in behind Bellerin towards Van Aanholt but the Sunderland full-back fails to keep his shot down as he blasts an effort over the crossbar. The Arsenal defender gets away with a bad piece of defending.
(86’) Both sides have given so much in this game and are therefore starting to feel the effects. The zip in the contest has died down in the last couple of minutes or so, with Arsenal looking to keep possession and run down the clock now.
(84’) Koscielny bursts forward from defence into midfield and plays in Ramsey, but Coates gets tight to the receiver of the ball and clears the danger for Sunderland. The visitors have been terrific at the back today but have just been undone by two moments of cutting edge.
(82’) Ozil receives the ball from Ramsey and looks to set Gibbs marauding down the left with a curling pass, but the former Real Madrid man puts too much on it. Throw-in to Sunderland.
(81’) Ramsey picks up the ball in midfield and tries to find a pass, but Yedlin gets tight to him and makes a good block. It's still really end-to-end here at the Emirates and you can't rule out another goal at the moment.
--- 80’ Substitution Wenger makes his third and final change of the game for Arsenal this afternoon as he brings on Chambers in place of Giroud, who scored for both sides today. ---
--- 80’ Yellow card Yedlin becomes the first Sunderland man to pick up a yellow card today as he makes a silly challenge inside his own half. The right-back has had a mixed afternoon for the Black Cats so far. ---
(78’) Flamini tries to pick out Bellerin with a sweeping pass but he sells the Spaniard short and sends Lens off and running. The Dutchman picks out Watmore down the left but the youngster fails to find anybody with a lofted cross.
--- 76’ Substitution Wenger makes his second change of the game for Arsenal today as he brings on Gibbs in place of Campbell, who played well this afternoon and took his goal really well in the first half. ---
(76’) After a strong spell of dominance from Arsenal after they took the lead again in the second half, Sunderland are now throwing caution to the wind by chucking numbers forward in hope of another equaliser today.
(74’) CHANCE! M'Vila plays a long ball forward over the top of Koscielny towards Watmore, who fails to control the ball inside the box and thus shoots tamely down the throat of Cech from close range.
--- 72’ Substitution Allardyce makes his third and final change of the game for Sunderland this afternoon as he takes off Fletcher, who took a couple of bangs on the ankle today, and replaces him with Lens. ---
(70’) Ozil collects the ball from Ramsey in Sunderland's half and as he plays in Walcott, the striker tries to set up a one-two with the German but Van Aanholt gets to the reverse pass and makes the clearance.
(68’) O'Shea adds urgency into Sunderland's game as he punts a long ball forward towards Fletcher, who peels away from Koscielny slightly but Monreal makes a good headed clearance for Arsenal.
--- 67’ Substitution Allardyce makes his second change of the game as he takes off Borini, who missed a golden chance in the first half to put Sunderland 0-1 up at the time, and replaces him with Johnson just after the hour mark. ---
(66’) It's all Arsenal at the moment as they continue to pile players forward in search of a third. Ozil and Ramsey are lighting up this game for the hosts and it's backs to the wall stuff from Sunderland now.
(65’) OFF THE LINE! Ozil curls in a fantastic corner towards Giroud, who rises highest inside the box and heads towards the far corner but Yedlin hacks away the danger on the line. Great defending from him.
--- 64’ Substitution Wenger makes his first change of the game for Arsenal today as he takes off Oxlade-Chamberlain, who started the match well but faded, and replaces him with Walcott, who returns from injury. ---
--- 63’ Assist Ramsey bags the assist for Arsenal's second this afternoon as he finds Giroud with a good cross. Kaboul fails to track the run of the latter, who heads into the bottom corner with aplomb. ---
--- 62’ Substitution Allardyce makes his first change of the game for Sunderland this afternoon as he takes off Toivonen, who worked really hard in midfield for the visitors today, and replaces him with Rodwell. ---
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!! It's 2-1 to Arsenal! The hosts are back in front as Ramsey gets half a yard on Yedlin and picks out Giroud with a good cross as the Frenchman stoops low to head past Pantilimon. ---
(60’) Ramsey gets Arsenal by the scruff of the neck and drags them forward once again as he slips in Monreal after a good run forward, but O'Shea cuts out the Spaniard's low cross. Fabulous defending again from the visitors.
(58’) SO CLOSE! M'Vila whips in a cracking corner which Toivonen flicks on at the near post towards the back stick, but Fletcher's attempt on goal gets saved by Cech. The former Burnley forward clashes into the post on the way through as well.
(56’) Ramsey bursts forward again for Arsenal and as Monreal offers him support down the left, the former puts too much weight on his pass again as Yedlin mops up for Sunderland with a good clearance.
(54’) OFFSIDE! Ozil glides through Sunderland's midfield with good guile and as he slips in Ramsey down the side of Yedlin, the referee raises his flag for offside to deny the hosts in their tracks. Good defensive line from Allardyce's charges.
(52’) Ozil gives the ball away in midfield as his pass towards Flamini runs too close to M'Vila. The Sunderland man feeds in Borini down the right flank but the forward gets tackled by Campbell on the breakaway.
(50’) Ramsey steams forward through midfield on the attack for Arsenal and as Campbell makes good tracks ahead of him, the Welshman plays a through ball towards his team mate but he overcooks it.
(48’) Watmore curls in a cross from the left towards Fletcher but Koscielny heads away the danger. The ball sits up for Yedlin who chooses to shoot from distance but his effort flies miles wide of the target.
(46’) Welcome back! Arsenal get us under way again here at the Emirates Stadium as neither side makes a personnel change during the half-time break.
Sunderland were the better side for most of the first half and could have took the lead three minutes into the game, but Borini drove a shot straight at Cech from close range. Arsenal will be fuming at how the Black Cats scored, though, after Laurent Koscielny conceded a needless foul on Duncan Watmore, handing the visitors the free-kick to draw level.
Both sets of players head off the pitch and down the tunnel with nothing to split them so far after 45 minutes here at the Emirates. Arsenal took the lead through Joel Campbell, who made the most of some rash defending from DeAndre Yedlin, before Olivier Giroud scored an own goal just a few minutes later.
HALF TIME: ARSENAL 1-1 SUNDERLAND
(45’) JUST WIDE! Monreal gets past Yedlin down the left flank and as Ramsey bursts into the box with a good forward run, the Arsenal full-back picks him out with a driven pass but the Wales midfielder strikes the side netting with a first-time shot. Unlucky.
--- 45’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!! It's 1-1 and Sunderland are level! Giroud stretches out a leg at the near post to deal with M'Vila's lovely low cross, but the Arsenal man ends up sticking the ball into his own net. ---
--- 44’ Yellow card Koscielny picks up the first booking of the game as he slams into the back of Watmore down the flank. The Frenchman hands Sunderland a great chance to draw level here minutes before the interval. ---
(43’) Van Aanholt rolls the ball to Watmore down the left-hand side but the Sunderland winger has little time to react as Koscielny wipes him out with a poor challenge. The referee awards the visitors a free-kick.
(41’) Allardyce cuts a frustrated figure on the touchline as he looks on at Arsenal starting to get into the rhythm in terms of moving possession a lot quicker. Borini's miss just minutes into the game has been a huge blow for the visitors so far.
(39’) NO PENALTY! Giroud appeals for a spot kick as he falls down inside the box under pressure from Kaboul, but the referee waves away the hosts' protests. The replay shows that the Arsenal man hits the deck too easily.
(37’) Arsenal are turning the screw now since going a goal in front. They're finding more gaps in Sunderland's structure as the Black Cats clearly look wounded after conceding not long before the half-time whistle.
(35’) Yedlin got away with a bad piece of defending minutes before Campbell's goal by struggling to clear an Oxlade-Chamberlain cross suitably. And he failed to recover as he let the Arsenal winger get past him to put the hosts in front here.
--- 33’ Assist It's yet another assist for Ozil as he finds Campbell with a clever pass, but it's shoddy defending from Yedlin more than anything. The German midfielder is now up to 12 assists in the Premier League this season. ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLLL!! It's 1-0 to Arsenal! It's poor defending from Yedlin as he gets square on against Campbell and that allows Ozil to slip a ball past him towards the Costa Rican, who finds the back of the net with a good finish. ---
(31’) Kaboul picks up the ball in an unusual left wing position and drives past Bellerin, before he picks out Borini with a good cross but the Italian misses the target with a glancing effort. Excellent play again from the Sunderland defender in the build up to the chance.
(29’) Yedlin collects a pass into him from Kaboul and looks to get at Campbell. He flicks the ball over the top of the Arsenal winger and drives a cross in towards goal, but Ramsey intercepts and hacks the danger away.
(27’) A short suspension in play occurs as Mertesacker takes out Fletcher with the follow-through from a good clearance. The Sunderland man receives some treatment from the physios before he gets back on his feet.
(25’) Flamini nicks possession off Borini and plays in Ozil, but the German soon gives the ball away as well as O'Shea makes a good interception to thwart Giroud. It's still a very even game here at the Emirates.
(23’) Ozil tries to play in Oxlade-Chamberlain but his attempt gets intercepted by Yedlin. Sunderland are making it really difficult for Arsenal to play through them at the moment, getting 10 men behind the ball with Fletcher up top as an outlet to hit.
(21’) Ozil wins a free-kick as Toivonen barges him over in the centre of the pitch. The ball quickly gets transferred across to Campbell down the right but he fails to get a cross in as Kaboul blocks his path towards the byline.
(19’) M'Vila picks up the ball in all sorts of space in the middle of the park and clips a pass looking towards Fletcher, but Koscielny makes a good headed clearance to prevent the Scotland international from testing Cech one-on-one.
(17’) Kaboul keeps Van Aanholt's wayward free-kick in play but sees his cross blocked by Monreal. Arsenal look to counter attack as Ozil plays a pass towards Giroud, but Toivonen steals the ball away from him as O'Shea also gets tight to the striker.
(15’) Ramsey stabs a pass forward looking for Giroud but Toivonen nicks possession off the France international, before the referee pulls play up and awards a free-kick to Sunderland. The Arsenal striker gets penalised for handling the ball.
(13’) Flamini looks to play in Monreal down the left flank but Yedlin gets his body in the way and makes the tackle. Sunderland have made a really good start to this game, getting to every loose ball and they're also enjoying a good spell of possession at the moment.
(11’) Watmore steams forward again for Sunderland down the left and plays a cutback looking for Fletcher. Monreal gets there first but makes a hash of his clearance, before Flamini ushers the ball away from danger and into the arms of Cech with a good tackle. Nervous defending again from the hosts.
(9’) JUST OVER! Yedlin bursts down the right-hand side towards the byline and gets a good cross in towards the back post. Fletcher rises highest and flicks it across the face of goal towards Watmore, who fails to keep his header down from close range.
(7’) Arsenal have, as expected, had the lion's share of the ball in these early stages but the best chance by a country mile so far fell to Borini, who passed up the chance to put Sunderland in front in a good position.
(5’) Ramsey latches onto a neat pass from Ozil inside Sunderland's half but as he looks to play a one-two with Giroud, Kaboul reads the danger well and makes a good block for the visitors.
(3’) HUGE CHANCE! Sunderland break forward on the counter attack through Watmore as Van Aanholt heads away an Oxlade-Chamberlain cross. The Black Cats winger plays Borini in one-on-one with Cech but the Italian drives a shot straight at the Arsenal goalkeeper from close range.

Bilic's side have struggled of late, perhaps linked to the absence of star man Payet. They've not won any of their last four in the Premier League and, although United aren't exactly sparkling themselves at the moment, West Ham have not won at Old Trafford since May 2007. The hosts look set to mix things up a little today and will have the combined threat of Fellaini's physicality and Martial's pace in the final third. There have been few people bemoaning the injury to Rooney in the last few days - can their new-look frontline give Van Gaal a reason to leave his captain out even when he returns?
West Ham have also had to contend with a few injuries, with Payet, Valencia and Sakho not involved today. The latter is one of four to make way in the starting XI, with Lanzini - who picked up a knock in training on Friday - Jenkinson and Obiang coming out of the team. Mark Noble makes a return in midfield, while Andy Carroll, James Tomkins and Song also start, with the Cameroon midfielder fit once again.
Van Gaal has made two changes from the side which drew with Leicester City last weekend. Rooney, Ashley Young and Michael Carrick have made way, with Jess Lingard, Marouane Fellaini and Morgan Schneiderlin take their places. Young and Carrick can at least take up places on the bench, but the pair seem to have been dropped following below-par displays against Leicester, with the midfielder particularly off the pace at the King Power Stadium. Highlighting United's injury problems, Van Gaal has a rather inexperienced bench yet again, with Borthwick-Jackson, Pereira and Varela all present. The Uruguayan right-back would make his Premier League debut if he made an appearance.
Injuries have been the main obstacle for Louis van Gaal and the hosts, with several first-team regulars absent today. Aside from long-term problems for Valencia and Luke Shaw, United now also have Phil Jones, Ander Herrera, Marcos Rojo and Wayne Rooney missing. The latter two picked up their respective shoulder and ankle injuries in training this week, forcing the manager into changes for the visit of West Ham.

If you were to pick a contender for man of the match you would be spoiled for choice as far as Leicester City are concerned but you would struggle to make a case for anyone in the white of Swansea. The home team got off to a dreadful start and never really recovered from that early set back. Only wasteful finishing from the visitors kept the scoreline somewhat respectable. That said, there was a marked improvement after the break but they had given themselves far too much to do.
So Jamie Vardy couldn't keep his remarkable run of goalscoring going but I'm sure he won't mind too much as his side ran out comfortable winners here in South Wales. Riyad Mahrez was the star of the show today walking away with the matchball after a superb hat-trick. In all honesty 3-0 flattered Swansea rather than Leicester it could and perhaps ought to have been a lot worse for the home side, who simply weren't at it today and were outclassed all over the pitch. Pinch yourself Foxes fans, your team are top of the Premier League at the start of December. Fully deserved, particularly on the evidence of today's display.

Well that was a horror show from start to finish for Swansea City. Where do they go from here? You wouldn't be surprised to see some substitutions at the break. Yet a draw it finishes as Spurs equal their best unbeaten run in the top flight since a 14-match streak ended in March 1985. Tottenham remain in fifth place in the Premier League on 26 points, but could be replaced by Liverpool should they beat Newcastle on Sunday. West Brom are also unmoved, sitting in 13th position on 19 points, and four ahead of Chelsea.
Spurs, who ended the first half with a lacklustre performance, improved measurably in the second period - particularly in the opening exchanges. Yet they failed to carve out any real goalscoring opportunities for a quiet Kane in front of goal and were left grateful for a string of superb saves from Lloris. His stop against Olsson from close-range is as good as a goal for Pochettino's side, as the France international had no right to parry his effort over the bar.
A share of the spoils then for both sides and, on the balance of play, it is a fair result. Spurs opened the scoring with a simple goal from Alli after a long ball from Alderweireld in his own half found its way through a sloppy Baggies defence, allowing the England international an easy tap-in inside the area. Pulis' side then recovered to wrestle the remainder of the first half in their favour, before McClean equalised with a bullet header from a Fletcher cross on 37 minutes.
(90’) FULL TIME! The whistle blows as it finishes West Brom 1-1 Tottenham.
(90’) Just a minute left to play now with the scores all level. West Brom have won just three of their last 11 league games at home, having lost six, and their lack of wins in front of their homes fans is set to continue. But this has been a hard-fought point here today should they hold out.
(90’) Three minutes of added time have been given in this second half as both teams try and search for that winning goal.
(90’) A superb cross from McClean is cut back from the left but nobody is in the box to meet it for West Brom! That could have been the chance to win it had they gambled with bodies in the area.
(89’) It is Tottenham who look to end this half the stronger but a poor pass from Walker to Alderweireld is a little shot near the half-way line, allowing Rondon the chance to close in on the Spurs defender. He puts unwanted pressure on the Belgium centre-half, but he hastily clears.
(87’) We are back underway with McClean remaining on the pitch, before McAuley is penalised for a high foot in a challenge against Rose.
(86’) McClean is down on the floor injured and receives treatment from the club physio on the pitch, bringing play momentarily to a halt.
(85’) Pochettino is set to equal a 30-year record if the scores remain the same, with his side on track to extend their unbeaten run to 14 games in the top-flight. A draw is a fair result should it remain this way with just over five minutes of play remaining.
--- 83’ Yellow card YELLOW! It's all hotting up here as McClean picks up a cauton! He flies into a challenge on Dembele that is wreckless as both feet are off the floor. Spurs' players crowd around the referee seeking a reaction, yet it is just a booking for the West Brom goalscorer. ---
--- 81’ Yellow card YELLOW! Dembele concedes a free-kick in another good crossing position for West Brom, picking up a caution in the process. ---
(81’) N'Jie will hope to add extra fire-power here and take the pressure off the defence. Kane, who has led the line on his own, has seen little goalmouth action. He has nine goals in his last seven games for Spurs in all competitions but hasn't had the chance to add to that.
--- 80’ Substitution Alli, who has been a little quiet in these past 10 minutes, comes off with N'Jie coming on in his place. ---
(78’) Lloris is called into action again! Rondon has his back to goal as he picks up a pass on the edge of the area. He is allowed to turn and get his shot on target, but the France international is there to meet it with a save down low to his right.
(76’) PILING ON THE PRESSURE! The hosts are causing real danger here now as another last-ditch interception denies Pulis' side. A ball is played into the box from the right which is left by Alderweireld. Rondon has the chance to head home at the back-post but didn't react quick enough, allowing Walker to hook the ball away with a flick of his boot.
--- 75’ Yellow card YELLOW! Kane becomes the second Spurs player to find his name in the book after sliding in on Dawson unfairly. ---
(74’) SUBLIME STOP! A quite fantastic save from Lloris denies West Brom! Brunt whips in the free-kick from the re-take and Olsson is at the far post to meet it. The ball is loose at the back post before the Baggies defender rifles home a shot from close range but the Spurs keeper somehow stops it - and pushes it over the bar for a corner! Brilliant play!
--- 73’ Yellow card YELLOW! The Baggies have a free-kick on the edge of the area which Gardner looks to play quickly yet, oddly, play is pulled back. Moss was unhappy that he wasn't allowed to finish spraying a foam line on the floor and orders a re-take, booking Gardner in the process. ---
(71’) It has been a real composed defensive display from the Baggies here today who have frustrated Spurs and kept chances down to a minumum. Pulis is just one game away from a century of defeats in the Premier League - and one of only 15 managers to do so - but they have been worthy of this draw here to far.
(69’) Rose and Eriksen combine down the left-hand side with West Brom keeping a close-nit defensive line, which is hard to break down. Yet a ball into the box is played early with Kane the target who breaks free of his marker inside the area, but Myhill reads the play well to intercept and snatch the loose ball.
(67’) Tottenham are patient in their passing play now as they build from the back and look to work an opening. They spread the ball from left to right before attempting to cross into the area, but Morrison gets his foot in to break up any danger and clear away from goal.
--- 65’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! McClean tracks back to steal the ball from the feet of Lamela and force it out for a throw-in near the halfway line and that will be the last action from the Argentine. Heung-Min Son comes on in his place. ---
(64’) ANOTHER WASTE! West Brom have been real poor from their set-piece plays here today. A free-kick is in a good crossing position for Brunt on the right, just outside the penalty area, but he attempts to catch Lloris off guard with a shot from a tight angle but it falls harmlessly wide of the target.
(63’) A good decision from referee Jonathan Moss there as he overrules his linesman, who had initially given offside for a pass from Morrison to Gardner, and instead awards the Baggies a free-kick for a foul on the former by Rose.
(61’) Lloris is again in the thick of the action as he races out of his goal to beat Rondon to a ball over the top, and clear his lines by crashing the ball out of play for a West Brom throw-in midway through the Spurs half.
(59’) A potentially tricky moment there for Lloris as West Brom attempt a long throw-in from near the corner flag. With the wind battering the ground here on a blistery day, aerial balls could be a problem for keepers, yet Dawson's throw is dealt with well by the France international as he beats Rondon to the loose ball.
(58’) This is, of course, a Tottenham side who pride themselves as much on defensive stability as they do flair in attack. Prior to this clash they had conceded just 11 goals in their 14 league games with only Manchester United holding a better record.
--- 57’ Yellow card YELLOW! Morrison picks up the first caution of the game as he brings down Rose, straight after his perfectly timed challenge on Gardner, earning Spurs a free-kick. ---
(56’) ANOTHER SUPERB CHALLENGE! We saw Walker make a crucial interception in the first half and Rose has done the same here in the second. Gardner looks to be clear on goal with Rondon to his right should he lift his head up. But Rose makes a timely tackle to wrap his foot around the ball and break up a dangerous attack. Great play!
(55’) Consecutive corners now for Spurs as they pile on the pressure, this time as Kane crashes an effort off the West Brom defence and out out play. It has been a lively start to this second period and a much-improved performance from Pochettino's side.
(53’) TOWERING HEADER! Lamela, who wins the corner, is the target at the back-post as the delivery comes in and he rises high to meet the ball with his forehead, only for his effort to fall straight into the arms of Myhill. Either side of the keeper, as they say, and that could have been in, but it was otherwise an easy save for the Baggies stopper.
(52’) We have a stretched game here now at the start of this second half with play end-to-end at the minute. West Brom try to attack with a ball into the box but Spurs clear their lines, before launching a threat of their own down the left as Lamela races into the area to see his deflected cross roll out for another corner.
(51’) OFF THE LINE! Last ditch defending saves West Brom! Alli combines well with Kane to lift a ball over the top of the defence and into the area. Dawson tussles with the England striker and does just enough to put him off balance as he shoots. His effort trickles towards goal but McAuley cuts across to whip the ball away from danger and out for a corner!
(49’) Evans is unhappy here after he is penalised for a challenge on Alli. The Baggies defender stretches for the ball as he chases to deny the Spurs man from breaking from midfield, but is deemed to have caught the England man late.
(47’) Rondon thinks he has broken free of Alderweireld as he races through on goal to latch onto a left-wing ball from Brunt, yet the officials pull play back for offside. A warning for Spurs there, perhaps, who are playing a high line early on.
(46’) SECOND HALF! We are back underway for the final 45 minutes of football at The Hawthorns.
Yet a first Baggies goal for McClean has given West Brom a more than a fighting chance in this second half with the scores all level. Pulis will feel confident his side can do exactly what they did against Arsenal last time out at The Hawtorns - come from behind to win. Spurs need to see improvement if they are to secure all three points in this second half.
Tottenham took the early lead through rising England star Alli but, after his 15th minue goal, it has been all West Brom. Pulis will have felt hard-done-by had his side entered the break a goal down, having seen his side on top for much of that half - and defended poorly for the opening goal, too.
(45’) HALF TIME! That's the whistle for the interval with the score here at 1-1.
(45’) Alli combines with a teammate in the final third, just outside the penalty area, but their close passing is broken down by the West Brom defence. Eriksen is lurking just behind to pick up the loose ball and let fire with a first-time shot, yet his effort is sliced high and wide.
(45’) Two minutes of added time have been given as Tottenham end this half in posession of the ball, having conceded just their 12th goal of the league season moments earlier.
--- 44’ Substitution SUBSTITUTION! A blow for the hosts now as Sessegnon makes way for Gardner just before the interval. It looks a precautionary move after a fairly innocuous injury for the West Brom attacker, as he slipped on the wet surface. ---
(42’) Eriksen tries to thread a ball over the top of the West Brom defence for Rose to latch onto, as he breaks free of the Baggies defence on the left, but the ball into the penalty area comes too late as the officials pull play back for offside.
(40’) The Hawthorns is in full voice here now as they roar their side towards the half-time whistle with the scores all level once again at 1-1. McClean's bullet header is more than deserved after dominating the past 20 minutes of play. They might not have seen any quality crossing from set-pieces, but that Fletcher cross is pin-point for his teammate to nod in.
--- 39’ Goal! GOAAAAAL! McClean has levelled the scoring for West Brom! He flies into the box with a terrific header to meet a cross from Fletcher. He shows bravery to get his head to the ball ahead of his marker to nod home for his first goal in Baggies colours. ---
--- 39’ Assist A great assist from Fletcher! He shows real spirit to burst into the box, towards the byline, and cut a delivery back into the area for McClean to meet with a powerful header. A superb time to score a goal here, and certainly deserved on the balance of play! ---
(36’) Alli is not a happy man here as he points to his ripped shirt. He runs through on goal hoping to chase a ball over the top but, as he battles for posession with McAuley, the West Brom defender shield the pass out of play for a goal-kick. He shows the officials his ripped shirt after that encounter but is given nothing.
(34’) West Brom continue their period of dominance and earn another free-kick in a dangerous crossing position after Dembele concedes a foul yet, once again, the delivery is poor and Spurs are able to clear their lines. They have had plenty of chances from set-pieces early on but haven't made the most of them.

(22’) A weak ball is whipped in from the free-kick but the cross fails to beat the first man as Tottenham clear their lines on the edge of the penalty area and launch a counter attack of their own.

(17’) As mentioned prior to kick-off, Tony Pulis' side have earned four points from losing positions in their previous two league matches against Arsenal and West Ham. His side will need to repeat that feat today to avoid defeat in this clash.

Yet the Baggies are hard to beat under Pulis and have developed something of a fighting spirit in recent fixtures. They came from behind to beat Tottenham’s north London rivals Arsenal 2-1 in their last outing here at The Hawthorns, while they also came from a goal down to secure a 1-1 draw with West Ham last weekend.
Spurs are currently in their best run of form in the top flight since March 1985 and can extend their strong run of form into 14 league games unbeaten should they avoid defeat today. Not only is form on their side, but the history books are too, having only lost one of their last 11 Premier League meetings with West Brom.
Visiting manager Mauricio Pochettino makes two changes from the Tottenham line-up that were held to a 0-0 draw with Chelsea last week. Ryan Mason and Heung-Min Son are both out with the former having picked up an ankle injury that is expected to rule him out for around two weeks. Dele Alli makes a timely return from suspension, then, while Erik Lamela also returns. Harry Kanes leads the line - he scored twice in a 3-0 win in this very fixture last season and has only scored more goals against Leicester (4) than against the Baggies (3).

Claudio Yacob drops out due to a one-match suspension paving the way for Chris Brunt to return from his ban in an expected 4-4-1-1 formation. And that will do it from the Bridge! An almighty victory for the newly promoted Bournemouth, who end an eight-game winless run and move out of the relegation zone in the process. Murray's late goal gave them the points, and sends Chelsea lurching into another disaster. Unbelievable scenes! That's all from us, thanks for joining our live commentary!
(90’) Gosling has space in the Chelsea area, but goes for goal himself, and Courtois can grab. Chelsea break from that failed attack with Remy slicing and dicing, but his low cut-back is cleared ahead of Costa!
(90’) SIDE NETTING! Terrific play again from Bournemouth, who pounce on a late slip from Cahill, and Artur steals possession, only to fire into the wrong side of the goal! That was so close to sealing this one.
(90’) Bournemouth continue to attack whenever they get the ball. No corner-flag strategy for them! What a massive result this will be for the newly promoted side. As for Chelsea, it would be right back into crisis after a mini-revival in recent games.
(88’) Ivanovic drills a speculative effort almost out for a throw-in from at least 30 yards, and he hears it from the crowd. Mourinho tries to rally his team with just a few minutes left for them to get back in this game!
(86’) CHELSEA NEARLY HIT AGAIN! Suddenly Bournemouth break with Ritchie on the ball and acres to run into. He decides to go for goal from the top of the box, but hammers it the wrong side of the post!
(84’) Well Bournemouth have barely been a factor offensively in this half, but give Chelsea a lesson in ruthlessness by turning home one of their first attempts of the second period.
--- 83’ Substitution Baba is also brought off for Traore. ---
--- 83’ Substitution Mourinho throws on Remy for Fabregas in the aftermath of that goal. ---
--- 82’ Goal! MURRAY HAS DONE IT FOR BOURNEMOUTH! Chelsea fail to clear a corner, and Cook's attempted rebound falls to the substitute at the back post, who heads it home! He's only been on the pitch for a minute or two! ---
(81’) COSTA COULD HAVE DONE BETTER! Fabregas hoists a long ball into the area for the former Atletico striker to chase, and he makes contact on the ball, slicing it but still drawing a save from Boruc! Imagine if he had caught that cleanly!
--- 80’ Substitution King put in a strong shift up top but his night is at an end as Murray replaces him. ---
(80’) GREAT WORK FROM PEDRO! In the tightest of confines, he wriggles past two players, nutmegs a third and strikes on goal, but it's blocked by the sliding leg of a defender!
(78’) SOMEHOW CHELSEA FAIL TO CONVERT! A scintillating attack sees Hazard stab in Ivanovic down the right, and this time his delivery is spot-on, but somehow missed by both Pedro and Costa in the six-yard area!
(76’) Arter has given away a free-kick here for sticking his leg out to tumble Pedro. He's perhaps lucky to get only a talking-two from the referee and nothing more as it looked reckless.
(74’) The match is stopped as another Bournemouth player is in need of treatment. Stanislas is the lastest to take a knock, and his malaise gives both sides a chance to have a word from their manager.
(72’) Disappointing for Ivanovic, who has not enjoyed a good game. Fabregas slips him through in plenty of space out wide, but his cross is lashed too far ahead of any of his teammates.
(70’) There's a break on from Bournemouth as King charges down the left with Zouma in hot pursuit. He cuts infield, but a crowd of retreating Chelsea players prevent him from releasing the ball to one of his teammates.
(68’) Costa, already on a booking, does something pretty stupid - kicking the ball away after it ran out of play ahead of him. That's almost always a booking in today's game, but the referee errs on the side of leniency.
(66’) Willian's corner, not for the first time in this game, is bent right into the safe arms of Boruc. Too easy for Bournemouth and disappointing from the normally reliable dead-ball specialist Willian.
(64’) Daniels holds off Willian well and makes a purposeful run to the top of the box before being stopped by Zouma right before he could make up his mind. Good defending in the end.
--- 63’ Yellow card Costa has the ball on the left again, and wrestles Ritchie to the turf, leading to a booking for the substitute. ---
