(60’) An hour gone and Chelsea are really stepping up the tempo here in the search for the breakthrough. It's been a commendable improvement from Mourinho's men who are looking a lot more productive.
(58’) DANGEROUS TIMES FOR BOURNEMOUTH! A Willian corner is glanced right into the six-yard area, and there's a nervy moment where it could have gone anywhere with Boruc sprawling, but Gosling hacks it clear!
(56’) GREAT CHANCE! Somehow, Willian manufactures the space for a cross from the right, and his ball into the area takes a nick off the head of a defender, which perhaps surprises Matic at the back post! From point-blank range, the Serbian heads over!
(54’) Pedro collects the ball down the right and angles a cross into the area. Costa is lurking at the back post, but the defence just about get it clear ahead of the Spanish striker.
(52’) It will be interesting to see how the presence of Costa affects Chelsea in this half. Hazard wasn't entirely convincing as the lone striker in the first half, and he will now be attacking from his favoured left-flank position.
(50’) Baba does well to inch down the left flank and hook a cross into the area, but Costa can't contort his body enough to turn a volley on goal. Hazard tries to surprise Boruc with an overhead kick, but it's right down the keeper's throat.
(48’) Ritchie fires one over the bar as Bournemouth look to keep up their impressive first-half form. The level of their play in that opening period certainly deserved a goal. Can they find it here?
--- 46’ Substitution Mourinho recognises that he needs some more thrust up front and introduces Costa for Oscar, with Hazard moving over to the left. ---
(46’) Here we go again.
And that will do it for the first half from Stamford Bridge. It's still goalless, but not for a lack of trying. Bournemouth created the majority of the chances, and tested Courtois multiple times. Chelsea started to loosen up in the latter stages of the half, forcing Boruc into a few saves themselves. I can't imagine this staying 0-0 for long in the second half. Stay tuned for the restart in just a bit.
(45’) Oscar takes a pass with his back to goal and tries to spin away from his man with one touch, but he lost his balance and fell. He appeals for a free-kick but the referee isn't having any of it.
(44’) King is down again after taking a whack to the face from Zouma. It wasn't malicious from the Chelsea defender, but that's the Bournemouth striker battered and bruised once more.

(36’) Ivanovic collects a looping pass down the right and has time to make his mind up, deciding to cut it low to the top of the box for Pedro. The Spaniard's first touch is lead though, and forces him away from goal.

(32’) That wasn't bad from Arter, who once again finds space in the final third to let fly, but a deflection takes it away from Courtois in the Chelsea goal. Good play again from the guests.

(26’) Arter skips past Matic and decides to try a shot, but he drags it wide of the mark. However, the space in front of the defence for Bournemouth must be concerning Mourinho in the first half.

It's all over and Newcastle have picked up a much-needed and memorable victory! In stark contrast to their under-pressure opponents, Liverpool are thoroughly enjoying life under Jurgen Klopp. The German has taken to the demands of the Premier League like a duck to water and has guided his side to seven victories from their last eight games, including Wednesday’s 6-1 thrashing of Southampton and an impressive 4-1 win against Manchester City two weeks ago. With City, Manchester United and Arsenal all finding it difficult to embark on a decent winning runs, it is not outrageous to claim that the Reds, who currently sit six points behind the latter side, can now be seen as being potential title contenders. With just two league wins under their belts and three defeats from their last five Premier League encounters, the Magpies currently sit firmly in the relegation zone in 19th place, three points away from safety and with a difficult run of fixtures to contend with between now and the new year. Leaky at the back and not much better up front, Steve McClaren’s side have shipped a whopping eight goals in their last two games, whilst they have scored just twice since the middle of October. Time is running out for the former England boss, who desperately needs points, and fast, if he is to drag the Toon out of a terrible situation.

(60’) Free-kick to Everton now as Galloway is rewarded for another adventurous run down the left. Barkley stands over it... and it hits the crossbar off of the head of Wickham! So unlcuky!!!!

(56’) GOOD SAVE!! Howard does well to get a flailing leg onto Bolasie's goalbound shot after the winger had burst clear of Stones. Deulofeu attacks for Everton at the other end, taking on Souare before looping a cross onto the roof of the net - though the last touch came off a Palace defender.
--- 53’ Yellow card A booking now for Wickham, who receives the first yellow card of the game for a high-arm into the face of Stones. ---
(52’) CLOSE! Wickham challenges Howard in the air from the resulting set-piece, and is deemed to foul the Everton goalkeeper. The hosts counter through Kone, who plays a one-two with Lukaku before crossing into the box at the second attempt. Barkley latches onto the delivery, but he directs his header just wide.
(51’) VITAL TACKLE! A great challenge from Funes-Mori, who gets across to prevent Ward having a free shot on goal from close range. Pawson awards the visitors with a corner, to Funes-Mori's displeasure...
(50’) Cleverley puts in a strong tackle to dispossess McCarthur before setting Barkley on his way, who finds Kone. He links up with his strike-partner Lukaku, but his resulting shot is fired over the crossbar.
(48’) A positive start from Everton, who win two corners in quick succession, though they are unable to test Hennessey from either set-piece. Palace go long, and Howard hooks it clear, but only as far as Cabaye. The playmaker finds Ward, but his cross is over-hit.
(46’) SECOND-HALF! The home side, attacking the Gwladycs Street end, get us back up and running!
You feel that patience may be the key for both sides in this second-half. Bolasie has presented a real threat to Galloway down Palace's left, while Deulofeu, Lukaku and Barkley are also looking typically dangerous in front of goal.
While Palace have sat deep and looked to play on the counter-attack - which they have done so well - Everton have pressed high in search of an opener, displaying some well-worked attacking moves in the process, though none of which have yet come to fruition, and Martinez will be hoping that his side can re-discover the clinical finishing that has seen them go unbeaten in their last six fixtures.
HALF-TIME! Craig Pawson calls time on the first period at Goodison, where it is still 0-0 between Everton and Crystal Palace. It has been an enthralling encounter so far, with Wickham seeing a shot saved on the goalline by Howard, while Lukaku has rattled the woodwork at the other end.
(45’) Coleman concedes possession to Cabaye in a dangerous area, but the former PSG player's ambitious effort sails well off target as the fourth official indicates a minimum of one minute added time.
(44’) Barry drops a chipped pass into the feet of Lukaku, who twists and turns in the box before getting his shot away, which is well blocked. Barkley delivers the resulting corner, which Barry turns goalwards, but Hennessey is on hand to collect the tame strike.
(42’) A real worry for Everton as Stones goes down momentarily, but the classy defender regains his footing quickly enough. Palace launch an attack through Bolasie down the right, who picks out McCarthur with a cross, but the Scotland international can only volley his effort well wide.
(41’) Great pressure from Lukaku, who shirks off Puncheon and links up with Kone. The Ivorian drives forward and tries to square it to Barkley, but his pass is wayward.
(40’) Fantastic defending from Stones, who stands up Ward before getting in a perfectly-timed sliding challenge to set Barkley away. He finds Deulofeu, who spreads it to Coleman who tries a shot from range, but it is blocked away for a corner.
(38’) Yet another opportunity for Everton goes begging, as Deulofeu delays his final ball just a moment too long and Dann is able to get a tackle in following a swift EVerton counter-charge. The winger can be a real threat, but he is liable to frustrating decisions at times.
(35’) It has been a really entertaining affair so far at Goodison, with both sides showing plenty of attacking intent in the opening half-hour or so. Palace have a spell of possesion for a few moments before Cabaye attempts to pick out Ward, but his pass is nowhere near its intended target. Funes-Mori almost gifts the visitors a chance from the restart, but Stones comes across to see out the danger.
(33’) ALMOST! More truly superb attacking play from Everton, with the two centre-halves nearly combining to put them ahead. Stones jaunts into the box before pirouetting in possession and drifting a cross to his defensive partner Funes-Mori, but the Argentine is unable to prod his effort beyond Hennessey.
(32’) CHANCE! Barkley almost rounds off a superb counter-attack with a goal for the hosts. The England midfielder started the move, with Cleverley then finding Deulofeu, but Barkley is unable to turn the eventual cross goalwards.
(30’) More patient work from Martinez' men, as Barkley drills a pass over to Deulofeu on the right, but the winger - despite fooling Souare with a series of stepovers - overhits his cross and the chance is gone.
(28’) Deulofeu tries to curl a low cross in behind Palace's defence, but Dann is on hand to volley it clear. Bolasie charges upfield, but Funes-Mori is more than equal to the winger's run and Everton restart their attack.
(25’) Puncheon does well to hold off the tackle of Barry and feed Wickham, who, on the half-turn, is brought down by the stand-in Everton skipper. Cabaye loops in the resulting free-kick, which Dann recovers, but the hosts manage to clear the danger this time.
(23’) CHANCE! This time Lukaku turns provider as he slides in a pass to Kone, who charges into the Palace area. The formwer Wigan striker elects to go for power rather than placement, but his strike sails wide of the near-post. Better from Everton...
(21’) POST! SO CLOSE TO AN OPENER FOR EVERTON! After another well-worked move, Lukaku turns in possession on the edge of the area before drilling a curling effort that clatters off of the foot of the left-hand upright and rolls agonisingly across the goal-line and out for a goalkick. So unlucky from Lukaku, who was just a matter of inches away from grabbing his 50th Everton goal in style.
(19’) After a promising start from the hosts, it is Palace who have taken the impetus in the last few moments. Everton have a venture forward themselves, and Deulofeu works his magic with a weaving run past four Palace defenders, but Lukaku is just unable to connect with the Spaniard's pass at the end of the run.
(16’) SAVE! A point-blank stop from Howard as he prevents Wickham's close-range header putting the visitors ahead. The chance came from poor defending from Everton, who failed to clear their lines from Cabaye's corner.
(15’) A wonderfully composed piece of skill from Stones sends the Goodison faifthful into applause, but Palace regain possession and attack down the left flank, with Puncheon delivering a precise cross to the back post which Funes-Mori can only head away for a corner...
(13’) Fantastic play from Bolasie down the right as he takes on Galloway and lofts a cross towards the back-post which Coleman clears for a corner. Palace go short from the set-piece before eventually floating in another delivery, which Barry only-just gets a head on.
(11’) Unlucky again from Everton as Barkley pings a flat pass from the back towards Lukaku. The belgian flicks-it onto Deulofeu, but the former Barcelona youth star is unable to evade the challenge of Dann, who stewards the ball back to his goalkeeper.
(9’) Deulofeu backheels an improvised pass through the legs of a Palace defender and into the path of Lukaku, who lays it off to Barkley. He tries a first-time throughball in-behind to Kone, but his pass is over-hit and trickles out for a goal-kick.
(7’) CHANCE! Brilliant football from Martinez' side as Cleverley finds Barkley on the left. The England midfielder plays a lovely one-two with Lukaku before attempting a first time shot towards the top-right corner, but it sails wide of the upright. It was certainly worth a try from Barkley, who turned 22 at the weekend.
(6’) Another measured build-up by Everton, as they work it down the right to get Coleman into the area, but his strike is skewed wide. Palace race up the other end, but the Republic of Ireland full-back recovers quickly to get a tackle in on Puncheon.
(5’) A bright start from both sides here, and Palace are the next to threaten an opener as, at the second attempt, Bolasie whips in a delightful cross that Funes-Mori does well to hack clear at the near post. Cabaye regains possession, but is deemed to have fouled Cleverley in the process.
(3’) Patient build-up play from the hosts, with Barkley dropping deep in midfield before picking out Galloway, who had made a surging run down the left flank. The youngster attempts to square a cross back to Lukaku in the centre of the area, but Delaney is well-placed to clear the danger.
(2’) An early chance for Crystal Palace as Wickham, who is yet to open his Palace account since his transfer from Sunderland, forces Howard into an early save with a low strike from the edge of the box, though in all truth it never really tested the American goalkeeper.
(1’) KICK-OFF! Palace get us underway at Goodison Park, donning their white and blue away stip as they attack from left to right in this first half.
Romelu Lukaku has been a real star for Martinez' side this term - having netted 13 times in all competitions. The Belgium forward is joint-second in the Premier League scoing charts, four behind Leicester City's Jamie Vardy, and is making his 100th Everton appearance tonight, with his current tally at 49 goals for the Merseyside club.
The teams are coming out nof the tunnel now as Z-Cars blares out over the sound-system. It is another full house at Goodison, where Everton have netted 10 goals in their previous two games.
Like his counterpart, Pardew makes just one change, with captain Mile Jedinak replacing the suspended Wilfried Zaha. Palace have triumphed in four of their six away fixtures in the Premier League so far this term, but will know that they will have to be at their very best tonight to claim the points against a rampant Everton, who will look to capitalise on Liverpool's defeat at Newcastle to leapfrog above their local rivals and into the top six.
Crystal Palace Substitutes: Speroni, Bamford, Campbell, Gayle, Mutch, Chamakh, Kelly.
Crystal Palace (4-2-3-1): Hennessey; Ward, Dann, Delaney, Souare; Jedinak, McCarthur; Puncheon, Cabaye, Bolasie; Wickham.
So just the one change from Roberto Martinez from Everton’s last Premier League fixture, as Tom Cleverley replaces the injured James McCarthy. The former Manchester United man made his first start since August in the win over Middlesbrough, and impressed in a deeper role alongside Gareth Barry. Arouna Kone and Tim Howard sat out that trip to the Riverside Stadium, abut both return to Martinez’ starting XI tonight. Leighton Baines comes back into the matchday squad for the first time this season after recovering from injury.
Everton Substitutes: Robles, Baines, Gibson, Mirallas, Lennon, Naismith, Osman.
Everton (4-2-3-1): Howard; Coleman, Stones, Funes-Mori, Galloway; Cleverley, Barry; Deulofeu, Barkley, Koné; Lukaku.
The teams are in at Goodison, so without further ado, let’s check on the starting line-ups, starting with the hosts…
It is of course the night of the third-round draw for this season’s FA Cup, and Everton have been handed a home tie against either Dagenham & Redbridge or non-league Whitehawk FC. Palace, on the other hand, will travel to Southampton – another of Pardew’s former club. But neither side will be paying much attention to those matches as of yet, with all the focus on tonight’s clash.
Goodison has been a happy hunting ground for Crystal Palace in recent seasons, with the south London club having claimed 3-2 victories in each of their last two visits. After beating Liverpool in their previous game on the road, Alan Pardew’s side were brought down to a earth with a defeat to Sunderland at Selhurst Park. They recovered swiftly with a comprehensive 5-1 thumping of Pardew’s former employers Newcastle United, however, and a win tonight would move them up into sixth.
Everton have been on a sparkling run of form in recent weeks, and are unbeaten in six in all competitions, though they were twice pegged back by AFC Bournemouth in their last Premier League outing. Ross Barkley thought he had given Roberto Martinez’ men the win in stoppage time at the Vitality Stadium, only for Junior Stanislas’ second of the game to cancel that strike out. They bounced back from that disappointing result with a convincing victory at Middlesbrough in the League Cup however, with goals from Gerard Deulofeu and Romelu Lukaku sending them into just their second semi-final in that tournament in over 25 years.
Hello and welcome to our LIVE coverage of this Premier League clash between Everton and Crystal Palace. We'll be bringing you all the action from Goodison Park this evening, with a place in the top six up for grabs for the victors!

Everton will be absolutely kicking themselves for collapsing so spectacularly in the second half. After enjoying such a good opening 45 minutes they really should have put the game to bed but sat back and failed to keep hold of possession well enough, allowing Bournemouth to punish them late on as the visitors began to tire.
My word, what an extraordinary end to the game that was! Bournemouth looked dead and buried after 80 minutes only pull off a great comeback before going behind once again. It looked as if Everton had regained all three points with one of the last kicks of the game, but the hosts never stopped believing and found the back of the net once again to pick up a well-deserved and much-needed point.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 3-3 EVERTON

--- 90’ +8 Assist That was a wonderful cross by Daniels, who picked out Stanislas perfectly. ---
--- 90’ +8 Goal! GOAL! I don't believe it! Bournemouth have equalised yet again! Smith breaks forward before teeing up Daniels, who is in acres of space on the left flank, and the left-back then whips a great cross into the middle of the box. (90’) It's all Everton at the moment as they patiently pass the ball around near the halfway line. They look desperate to keep hold of possession for as long as possible in an attempt to keep the determined hosts at bay.

(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be five minutes of added time.

(84’) And now Lukaku goes down inside the box! It almost identical circumstances, the big Belgian breaks into the penalty area before going down whilst battling with Distin, but, once again, the referee shakes his head and waves play on.

(81’) Smith goes down in the penalty area, but nothing is given! The defender, who has been brilliant since coming on at half-time, flies into the right-hand side of the box before going down under a challenge from behind by Galloway, but the referee immediately waves for play to continue, much to the frustration of the Bournemouth players and fans.

(71’) Everton do well to break down a determined Bournemouth attacking move before trying to embark on one of their own, but Kone's first touch upon receiving the ball is poor and gifts possession straight back to the hosts.

--- 46’ Substitution Federici is still struggling with the injury picked up earlier, so he has made his way off for Allsop, who comes on to make his Premier League debut, ahead of the start of the second half. ---
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half.
Once again, poor defending has proven to be Bournemouth's undoing, and they can have few complaints about heading into the half-time break two goals down. They have impressed when pushing forward, particularly when Stanislas and King link up, but at the back they have looked suspect and have struggled to deal with Deulofeu on the right and Lukaku down the centre, with both of the Everton players finding too much joy whenever they break away quickly.

(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(44’) With a two-goal lead intact, Everton are starting to sit slightly deeper as they look to take this scoreline into the half-time break. (74’) STAT: Manchester City have mustered the most shots of any team in the top flight this season (164, not including blocked).

--- 70’ Substitution Fernando has come on to offer some fresh legs in midfield for the hosts, with Delph giving way. ---

(58’) STAT: Manchester City have allowed fewer shots on target against them than any other team in the Premier League this season (37).

Chelsea’s midweek win in Haifa was the first time in over two months that Jose Mourinho’s men had won away from home, and they will be hoping that the victory there will help them achieve another one today. With that in mind, Chelsea’s task is a huge one, but they will feel as if the tide may be slightly turning in their favour thanks to two positive results in less than a week. The gap between these two London rivals currently stands at 10 points, and, with the hosts in such good form, another will not only send the Lilywhites up to fourth place in the table but will surely destroy Chelsea’s slim chances of achieving a top-four finish come May.

(64’) Norwich starting to spend more time on the front foot as Arsenal appear a bit rattled by how this second half has played out thus far. The three points certainly appear up for grabs right now, with both sides appearing capable of finding a winner as the tempo starts to pick up.
(62’) STAT: The Canaries have won just one of their last eight Premier League games (W1 D2 L5).

Injuries have now started the second half for them once again (Arteta last week, Cazorla this one). The Gunners of course went on to lose that game, so they will be hoping to write a new script this evening.

The players are out on the field as kick-off approaches, but first we will hear the French national anthem as a show of solidarity following the terror attacks in Paris last week.
All eyes will be on Vardy today, however. Janmaat has vowed to do his best to stop the striker making it 12 goal-scoring games in a row, equalling Van Nistelrooy's record, but the Leicester star has looked almost unstoppable so far this season, proving clinical and hard-working. The visitors have plenty of other threats, however, with Mahrez another enjoying a particularly impressive season.
Newcastle have been lingering towards the bottom of the table all season so far, though they went into the international break on the back of two wins in four games, including a 1-0 defeat of Bournemouth last time out. Today as hosts they will have St James' Park right behind them and coach Steve McClaren is confident that the international break has done his side good, rather than upsetting their rhythmn.
Vardy starts up top alongside Ulloa, as Ranieri names two in attack to be flanked by Mahrez and Albrighton, both of whom have impressed in recent weeks. Leicester go into the match in third place so are full of confidence. Their coach is clearly looking to make the most of that by chasing a victory right from the start against a Newcastle side who seem to have steadied the ship in recent games.
Much of the focus today will be on Jamie Vardy, as he chases Ruud van Nistelrooy's record of scoring in 10 consecutive Premier League matches. The England international missed both of his country's games during the international break and he was very much a doubt for the trip to Newcastle. However, Claudio Ranieri has deemed him fit enough to start and he does so in an attack-minded line-up.

Bournemouth have played at a really high tempo and you suspect that they might just be starting to tire. The substitutes for the Jacks, will look to take full advantage of any tired legs or minds at this stage.
(75’) Gomis is on for the final quarter of an hour in place of the largely anonymous Eder. In fairness to the outgoing Swansea forward, he had no service to work with whatsoever.
--- 73’ Substitution B. Gomis comes on for Éder. ---
(73’) OVER! Bartley upends Arter and gives Stanislas the chance to put the ball into the box from a free kick. The Bournemouth winger delivers an decent looking cross into the danger area. It drops to Cook who from about 12 yards out half volleys over the bar. That was a presentable opportunity but it was a case of right place, wrong man - as far as the visitors are concerned.
--- 72’ Yellow card K. Bartley goes into the referee's book. ---
(71’) Sigurdsson and Montero are finally on and are greeted by a rapturous reception from the home faithful. Unsuprisingly, it is the disappointing Britton and Routledge who make way.
--- 70’ Substitution J. Montero comes on for W. Routledge. ---
--- 70’ Substitution G. Sigurðsson enters play, replacing L. Britton. ---
(69’) CHANCE! Routledge seizes upon a loose pass in midfield and sets Swansea away. Eder does well to retain possession and hold it up before bringing Ki into play. The South Korean tees up Andre Ayew on the edge of the box but is shot is deflected through harmlessly to Federici. Much better from the home team, it is the first time they have threatened the Bournemouth goal in the second period.
(67’) Garry Monk really needs to make some changes, as a another Bournemouth goal looks inevitable if the pattern of the game continues like this.
(65’) On this occasion it is Charlie Daniels, the Bournemouth left back, who is bombing forward, playing more as a left winger rather than a defender just now. He takes on Naughton and creates enough space to smash a low cross across goal, Bartley however is well positioned and is able to hack it clear. It is just wave after wave of Bournemouth attacks at this moment in time.
(63’) Yet again Francis get to the byline and pulls the ball back to Matt Ritchie who tries to sidefoot it home from inside the area but his shot is expertly blocked by Leon Britton. Bournemouth continue to turn the screw.
(61’) WIDE! Cook finds himself free at the far post from Stanislas' corner and the centre back strikes his half volley pretty well but the ball flashes across the face of goal and doesn't get the decisive touch it needed. Big let off for Swansea there.
(59’) The first few substitutions of the afternoon don't seem to be too far away with Montero, Sigurdsson and Gomis warming up for Swansea. As for Bournemouth Glenn Murray is doing some rather vigorous stretching and jogging on the touchline.
(57’) Francis has been a great outlet for Bournemouth today and has got forward on the overlap at every opportunity. Ritchie plays him in again but this time the right back's cross is cut out at the near post by Ashley Williams.
(55’) Ki and Taylor look to get Swansea going as an attacking force in the second half with a one-two but Andrew Surman then comes across to make a well timed interception.
(53’) SAVE! Harry Arter takes aim from all of twenty-five yards and the ball bounces up in front of the goalkeeper but Fabianski deals with it comfortably. The rain has been falling continously since kick off, so that save wasn't as easy as the Polish goalkeeper made it look, the surface is very greasy now.
--- 51’ Yellow card J. Stanislas is yellow-carded. ---
(51’) I hope it is not the case but so often it is the way that when there is a really open first half, the second half doesn't continue in the same vein and both teams rather cancel each other out. Stanislas goes into the book and I feel it's a harsh decision on the Bournemouth winger, it was a full blooded challenge on Ayew but he won the ball cleanly.
(49’) Now it is Swansea's turn to enjoy a bit of sustained possession but it comes to nothing as Charlie Daniels snuffs out Ayew attempted forward run. Kyle Naughton has had precious few opportunities to get up the pitch on the overlap so far this afternoon.
(47’) Bournemouth have begun the second half in the same way that they started the first - in calm and composed fashion. Every player is nice and comfortable in possesion and they are prepared to be patient on the ball.
(46’) Bournemouth get the match restarted.
During the half-time interval I have had the benefit of a replay of the penalty decision and have to say that Bournemouth have every right to feel aggrieved. There may have been some contact between Ayew and Francis but on second viewing it looks like the Swansea no.10 trips himself up. But in real time you can understand why Andre Marriner awarded the spot-kick.
Garry Monk might be pleased with the character displayed by his player's, he will be far less happy with the way his team have defended. They have also given the ball away far too easily, which is most unlike them. You wonder how long it will be before Monk considers introducing some of his big hitters into the fray. It has been such an open game so I'm sure the like of Sigurdsson, Montero and Gomis are chomping at the bit to get involved.
Well that is the best first fourty-five minutes of Premier League football I have seen in quite some time! Bournemouth have been excellent in possession and have been very dangerous going forward. Swansea meanwhile deserve a lot of credit for the way have forced their way back into the match. It would have been very easy for the home side to feel sorry for themselves and let their heads drop.
(45’) Half Time. Swansea City 2-2 AFC Bournemouth. What a first half here in South Wales!
(45’) Swansea play themselves into trouble once again and first King and then Ritchie almost make them pay for their sloppiness in possession. Ashley Williams puts in a great block which results in a Bournemouth corner. The away side can't make it count and Fabianski claims the deep cross.
(45’) This has been a pulsating first half and I don't want it to end to be honest. there will be three additional minutes added on. Both manager's will be preparing very important team talks.
(43’) The Cherries look a real threat each and everytime they go forward, which will give them great confidence for the rest of this match. The Swansea defence look decidedly nervous.
(41’) Eddie Howe and his coaching staff are still livid with the decision to award Swansea a penalty. Whatever the rights and wrongs of that incident, Bournemouth will be absolutely kicking themselves for throwing away this two-nil lead. They've struggled to score goals this season and their defensive frailities have come back to haunt them again today.
--- 39’ Goal! Penalty goal scored by J. Shelvey! ---
(39’) GOAL! 2-2 Shelvey makes no mistake from 12 yards. Slotting the ball into the bottom corner. Great penalty from the England international. Federici went the right way but had no chance of getting there. We're all level now.
(37’) PENALTY TO SWANSEA! Britton plays a delicate slide rule pass through to Ayew who appears to have his feet clipped by Francis and the referee points to the spot. I'm not sure there was much the Bournemouth defender could do there as it looked like an accidental tangle of legs but the referee had no hesitation in pointing to the spot.
(34’) I think it would be fair to say that Garry Monk's changes haven't really worked so far this afternoon. Eder, Bartley and Britton have looked like three players who haven't started a game at this level for sometime. Still plenty of time for them to turn things around though...
(32’) It has been a frentic opening half hour to this match. Despite both teams being known for their pretty passing football there have been plenty of crunching tackles going in. It's been pretty fierce and fiesty in the centre of the park.
--- 30’ Yellow card M. Ritchie goes into the referee's book. ---
(30’) The Swans have got their tails up now and want a penalty but there is nothing doing from referee Andre Marriner. Naughton's cross from the right sat up invitingly for Ki, who half volleyed at goal but his shot was blocked by Cook but it was unclear if it was stopped with his chest or his arm. Either way a penalty was not given and Bournemouth breathe a collective sigh of relief.
--- 28’ Assist J. Shelvey gave the assist. ---
--- 28’ Goal! Neil Taylor's deep cross was aimed at Eder at the back post. Distin managed to get something on it to divert it away from the Swansea striker but the ball bounced up for Shelvey to head towards goal. Ayew collected the loose ball and turned it home. The Swansea midfielder looked offside to me but the goal stands. ---
(28’) GOAL! Andre Ayew gets Swansea straight back into it with a cheeky backheel - game on here at the Liberty Stadium!
--- 26’ Assist Assist by M. Ritchie. ---
--- 26’ Goal! Gosling finished off another wonderful counter attack. Stanislas played in Arter who rather got the ball stuck under his feet but he managed to smuggle it to Ritchie who picked out Gosling who showed great composure to side foot the ball into the top corner with some aplomb. ---
(25’) GOAL! Dan Gosling makes it 2-0 with a beautiful finish. Bournemouth are in dreamland here!
(22’) Little stat for you here. Sylvain Distin is making a bit of history today by becoming the first foreign outfield player to rack up 450 Premier League appearances. An outstanding achievement for the French defender.
(20’) Bournemouth's goal had almost settled Swansea down in a strange way and the Welsh side seemed buoyed by those two chances to equalise so soon after falling behind. However, since the King opportunity and the disallowed Stanislas goal the Jacks seem to have lost a little bit of belief. It is vital that they don't allow their heads to drop. The experienced player's need to stand up and be counted during these difficult moments.
(18’) Bournemouth have the ball in the back of the Swansea net again! But this time it won't count as Junior Stanislas is correctly given offside after converting Francis' pinpoint cross. A let off for the home team, who really can't afford to go 2-0 down.
(16’) SAVE! Fabianski makes a decent stop from Josh King, who had raced away from the Swansea defence after capitalising on an unusually sloppy pass from Leon Britton. It looked for all the world that the Bournemouth striker would make it two-nil but the angle rather closed up on him.
(14’) An absolute nightmare start for Garry Monk and his team but they have reacted well to that early setback. What will continue to worry the Swansea manager is the way Bournemouth midfield are dominating central areas. Ki and Britton are being overrun at times.
(12’) Not one but two chances for Swansea to almost hit back immediately but that they can't take either. First Routledge is put through after making a great run from out to in, but his stabbed finish was deflected away to safety by Federici. Then from the resulting corner Eder met Shelvey's dangerous cross but his header was well saved by the Bournemouth 'keeper. Excellent response from the Jacks.
--- 10’ Assist Assist by J. Stanislas. ---
--- 10’ Goal! Stanislas took full advantage of some poor defending and back luck on Swansea's part. Bartley's clearance hit Ki and dropped kindly for the Bournemouth winger. Stanislas wasted no time in squaring the ball for the unmarked King, who couldn't miss! ---
(9’) GOAL! Josh King gives Bournemouth a deserved lead. 1-0 to Bournemouth!
(7’) No lacking in confidence from Bournemouth so far. They don't look like a side that have lost their last four games. They are pressing their opposition so much that Swansea are resorting to long passes towards Eder.
(5’) Swansea are really struggling to win the ball back at the moment and then when they do get hold of it, they aren't able to keep it for very long. Eddie Howe promised Bournemouth would stay true to their footballing philosophy and they are doing exactly that in these early stages.
(3’) OVER! A lovely, flowing move from Bournemouth with Stanislas and King exchanging passes before the onrushing Dan Gosling gets involved but the midfielder rather leans back as he shoots and the ball goes comfortably over the bar.
(2’) Nice positive start from Bournemouth. Straight onto the front foot with some bright passing and movement. No real chances to speak of yet, with Swansea able to clear their lines.
(1’) Both teams are in their traditional strips. The Jacks in all white and the Cherries in black and red.
(1’) Swansea get us underway!
Before every Premier League this weekend 'La Marseillaise' - the French national anthem will be played in memory of the 129 people who tragically lost their lives in the recent terrorist attacks in Paris.
As for the Cherries they will be desperate for a positive result after spurning a hatful of chances last time out against Newcastle United. It may only be November but this look like a bit of a six pointer. Eddie Howe is happy to welcome back Glenn Murray to his matchday squad, the former Crystal Palace striker is named amongst the subsitutes today.
Garry Monk was far from impressed with his side after their 1-0 reverse against Norwich before the international break and has rung the changes. Gomis, Montero, Fernandez and Sigurdsson all drop out while Eder, Routledge, Britton and Bartley are given rare starts in the Premier League. Sigurdsson denied rumours of a fall out between him and Monk, the team selection today will do little quell that speculation. Make no mistake, this is a massive game for the Swansea manager today. Anything less than a win could mean that Huw Jenkins is swinging the managerial axe.

SWANSEA SUBS: Tremmel, Gomis, Montero, Rangel, Sigurdsson, Cork and Fernandez.

The team news is in and we'll start with our hosts Swansea City...
Good afternoon and welcome along to the Liberty Stadium for this Premier League clash between Swansea City and AFC Bournemouth. I'm Chris Baker and I'll be describing all the action for you this afternoon.

I am Alex Moretto and I would like to thank you all for joining me here today. Good bye!
WEST BROM 2-1 ARSENAL. The Gunners lose at the Hawthorns for the first time since 2005 as they take a massive stumble in the title race.
(90’) FULL TIME! INCREDIBLE!
(90’) STRAIGHT AT MYHILL! McClean inexplicably heads a ball back into the danger area, inside his own box, where Koscielny is there to meet it - but the defender sends his shot straight at the keeper!
(90’) West Brom are doing everything they can to see this out. Myhill is shown a yellow for time wasting, but it's a good one to take as more precious seconds wind off the clock. Arsenal can't win the ball back here, let alone find a goal!
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card G. Myhill is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) There will be a minimum of four minutes of stoppage time added on at the end of this match. Can Arsenal find the elusive equaliser?
(88’) Myhill comes out to collect a corner, and now West Brom can look to collect themselves. The fast tempo hardly suits what they are trying to accomplish over these final few minutes, so the keeper will take his time here, give his defenders a breather and let his side regroup.
(86’) EXCELLENT GOALKEEPING! There is an incredible pace to the match now as the teams go end-to-end in search of the decisive fourth goal. A ball is played over the top for Campbell who gets a touch, but Myhill is off his line to collect before he can get a real shot off at goal.
--- 84’ Missed penalty ---
(84’) HE'S SKIED IT! Gardner and Morrison try their best to get in the head of Cazorla in anticipation of the penalty being taken, and it has worked to perfection! The Spaniard can't keep his composure as he lifts a dreadful effort over the bar!
--- 83’ Yellow card PENALTY TO ARSENAL! It's as if someone shut off the music at the party, as the Hawthorns goes deafeningly silent with Clattenburg pointing to the spot. Brunt cannot believe the decision has gone against him! He takes down Sanchez just inside the area as a ball was played in over the top. ---
(81’) Everyone forward for Arsenal as they chase this deficit. This would prove a costly defeat should they fail to find another goal, with Manchester United winning earlier today and Leicester leading 2-0 currently at St. James' Park. They would fall all the way to fourth place with a loss, having entered the day in a tie for first.
(79’) Wenger can't believe his side's luck at the moment. Their approach play has been much better in this second half and they have carved out chances seemingly at will - yet have nothing to show for it. You can sense the tension at the Hawthorns as both sets of fans know not what to expect over these final 10 minutes.
--- 77’ Substitution R. Lambert enters play, replacing J. Morrison. ---
(77’) SO CLOSE! Terrific ball into the area from Bellerin on the right, which picks out Sanchez in stride. It seems to catch the Chilean by surprise, however, as he can't sort out his footing, only able to roll a tame effort straight at Myhill!
(75’) Following the moments of panic, Arsenal are back at the right end of the pitch as far as they are concerned, looking to claw their way back into the game. Sanchez has taken up a central position now with Ozil on the left looking to fire crosses in for Giroud.
(73’) STAT ATTACK: Only 56% of the shots on target faced by Arsenal have been from inside the penalty area - the lowest proportion in the top flight. (Opta)
(71’) OH MY! INCREDIBLE SEQUENCE! All that made possible by the quality of the cross from the corner from Brunt. It creates a whole mess inside the six-yard box and a flurry of activity, but somehow a combination of Cech and Campbell manage to keep the ball out before the offside flag brings play to an end!
(69’) SHOCKING MISS! Cazorla with a clever ball over the top for Campbell, who finds himself all alone after McClean slips, but the substitute scuffs his effort horribly! It looked a sure goal, yet he fails to even hit the target! There's a distinct look of disgust on the face of Wenger following that miss.
--- 68’ Substitution S. Rondón is done for the day. S. Berahino is his replacement. ---
(67’) Wonderful control! If anyone is going to pull Arsenal back into the game, it's going to be Sanchez. He's been so sharp on the ball - his control, his movement and his skill - and West Brom have been unable to slow him. His teammates need to find a way to match the Chilean's intensity.
(65’) Sanchez caught atop the area by Evans after an impressive passing move from the Gunners, but Mark Clattenburg doesn't award a free kick. There didn't appear to be any intent in the challenge but the Chilean's trailing leg was definitely caught there.
--- 63’ Substitution Third and final change for Arsenal as Joel Campbell comes on to replace Gibbs, who didn't excel on the wing like Wenger would have hoped. The Costa Rica international is about the only real attacking option off the bench for the visitors as a result of injuries. ---
(62’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have averaged 0.5 points per game against Arsenal in the Premier League, their joint-lowest return against any side they have met more than twice. (Opta)
--- 61’ Substitution C. Gardner enters the game and replaces S. Sessègnon. ---
(60’) A few nerves are starting to creep in on the touchline and Tony Pulis is frantically getting his side organised. He feels it is time for a substitution, and you hardly blame him following this concentrated period of Arsenal pressure. Craig Gardner is coming on to replace Sessegnon.
(58’) EXCEPTIONAL DEFENDING FROM EVANS! It's surely a goal-saving tackle from the defender who slides in at the vital moment to just touch a ball behind after Ozil appeared to have played Flamini through on goal with a delightful pass.
(56’) They're still chasing a deficit, but Arsenal have enjoyed an incredible start to this second half. They look nothing like the side who struggled to create from open play in the first 45 minutes, and would consider themselves a bit unlucky not to have equalised as of yet.
(54’) CHAOS! Delightful stuff from Sanchez inside the area as he dribbles his way past three defenders before laying off for Gibbs, but the makeshift winger sees his close-range effort blocked! The pressure stays on and it comes to Giroud, but he lifts a shot over the bar!
(52’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal have scored in all 19 of their matches against West Brom in the Premier League, including today, the longest 100 per cent scoring record of any side against one single opponent in the Premier League era. (Opta)
(50’) This is a cursed position for Arsenal this afternoon as Flamini, who came on to replace the injured Coquelin early on, is now forced off himself through injury. Mathieu Flamini is on in his place.
--- 49’ Substitution M. Flamini comes on for Arteta. ---
(48’) OFF THE WOODWORK! What a delightful hit from Ozil, who was moving away from goal as he met the layoff from Sanchez, before dragging a shot off the far post with Myhill cleanly beaten!
(47’) PENALTY APPEALS DENIED! Sanchez remains so sharp in possession, winning a quick free kick off a challenge from Yacob. Ozil floats a terrific delivery in from the ensuing set piece, and Giroud goes to ground in the area - though the referee is having none of it.
(46’) Back underway at the Hawthorns!
WEST BROM 2-1 ARSENAL. Tony Pulis managed sides have a history of frustrating the Gunners, and the trend is continuing as Arsene Wenger finds himself in another dog fight at the Hawthorns. Olivier Giroud provided the breakthrough for the visitors, but the lead was short-lived as tallies from James Morrison and an own goal from Mikel Arteta have provided the Baggies with an unlikely advantage heading into the interval!
(45’) HALF TIME!
(45’) There will be a minimum of two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
--- 43’ Yellow card J. Morrison is cautioned by the referee. ---
(43’) The bookings are starting to accumulate as Giroud and Morrison are both put into the referee's book, no more than a minute apart. The physical nature of the match is starting to pick up, as frustration sets in for Arsenal after a quite shocking end to this first half.
--- 42’ Yellow card O. Giroud is yellow-carded. ---
(42’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom are winless in their last nine meetings with Arsenal in the Premier League, while posting just two victories in the past 19 top-flight clashes with the Gunners (D3, L13).
--- 40’ Goal! WEST BROM COMPLETE THE UNLIKELY TURNAROUND! They go from a goal down to one up in five minutes! This one is as scrappy as you'd like, as McClean bundles his way through the left channel before trying to power a ball into the six-yard box. Cech can't deal with it and Arteta fails to react, as he winds up knocking it into his own net! ---
(39’) Arsenal are looking to dictate the tempo yet again, enjoying the bulk of possession as we approach the final five minutes of the first half. They need to show more desire on the front foot, however, as it has been largely too straightforward for West Brom in defence up to this point.
(37’) To say it is a deserved equaliser for West Brom would be quite a stretch, but Arsenal hardly earned their lead in the first place. Neither side have looked capable of taking control of the game and producing the consistent quality needed to snatch all three points, so a level scoreline is appropriate at this stage.
--- 35’ Assist Assist by C. Brunt. ---
--- 35’ Goal! PARITY RESTORED BY THE BAGGIES! It is an absolutely stunning finish from Morrison who gets inside his marker in the area to get on the end of a free kick and lift a volley over the head of Cech and in at the far post! Terrific control and a rare moment of quality from the hosts in this first half has pulled them level! ---
(33’) West Brom desperately trying to poke and prod their way forward in an attempt to pull level before the break, but they've failed to inspire in possession. Fletcher and Yacob need to be crisper with their passing, while the likes of Morrison and McClean have to offer more width in attack.
--- 31’ Yellow card No protest from Bellerin who is issued the first yellow card of the match as he just catches the trailing leg of Rondon with his tackle. The right-back knew exactly what he was doing there and made sure there was contact to prevent what was looking like a threatening attack for West Brom in its infancy. ---
(30’) STAT ATTACK: Before the weekend, Olivier Giroud had scored in four of his last six Premier League appearances. Arsenal won each of those matches.
--- 28’ Assist The assist came from M. Özil. ---
--- 28’ Goal! A GOAL FOR ARSENAL AND FOR FRANCE! Emotional moments for Olivier Giroud as he blows a kiss to the heavens to celebrate! Ozil floats in the free kick from out wide and West Brom's marking is so poor inside the area that the striker is allowed the simplest of tap-ins from five yards out. ---
(26’) Arsenal have parked themselves firmly in the attacking half, though have little to show for it. Sanchez is the only real bright spot for them in possession, and his sharpness shines through again as he dribbles into a dangerous area before winning a free kick along the right flank.
(24’) The problem with this is that Giroud is dropping too deep to get away from Olsson. He's supposed to be their focal point in attack. Now when Arsenal want to throw balls over the top, Giroud often isn't available as he's dropped in closer to Ozil. The Gunners have been very underwhelming in possession up to this point.
(22’) Giroud is starting to drop deeper to try and get on the ball and help hold play up in attack. Olsson is blanketing the striker, however, tracking his every move. The Frenchman has been left quite frustrated as a result and has had little success escaping the defender's shadow.
(20’) Arsenal have been plagued by a lack of creativity through the opening 20 minutes and you can just see a bit of frustration starting to creep onto the face of Arsene Wenger. They started similarly against Swansea in their last away match before coming flying out of the break and registering three second-half goals.
(18’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have just one victory at the Hawthorns this season in league play, a 1-0 triumph over lowly Sunderland (D1, L4).
(16’) SAFE HANDS! Cleanly-struck free kick from Sanchez, who gets it over the wall and curling back towards the near post. Myhill anticipates it brilliantly to dive across and make the save, however, holding on as well to prevent a rebound.
(15’) Loose ball atop the area and Monreal runs hard to get onto it, before being clattered down by Sessegnon. It's a bit of a careless challenge from the West Brom midfielder, who concedes a free kick in a very threatening position for Arsenal
--- 14’ Substitution F. Coquelin is done for the day. Arteta is his replacement. ---
(13’) The medical team is still out working on Coquelin, while Mikel Arteta is up and running on the touchline. The Frenchman signals over to the bench for a change and it is a shame as his match comes to an end, barely making it 10 minutes.
(11’) Surprisingly it is West Brom who have appeared more dangerous in attack up to this point. Coquelin gives the ball away, but puts in some determined running to atone for his error and win back possession for his side. He seems to have injured himself following the second challenge he put in on Yacob and play is brought to a halt as the training staff is forced to come out and take a closer look at his knee.
(9’) McClean makes an absolutely exceptional run down the left flank, powering his way past two defenders while showing some excellent control in the process. He arrives at the edge of the area and lashes the perfect ball across the face of goal, but none of his teammates are there to attack it as the opportunity is wasted.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal have taken 31 of a possible 36 points from their last 12 Premier League matches on their travels (W10, D1, L1).
(5’) When they do get the ball, West Brom are playing hopeful balls over the top for the likes of Rondon and Sessegnon to chase - but their focus is undoubtedly on improving on the worst home defensive record in the Premier League this season.
(3’) West Brom's intent is evident early on. They will sit back and let Arsenal dominate possession, while focusing their efforts on congesting the midfield third and making it near impossible for them to navigate a passage through on goal.
(1’) Arsenal get us underway, kicking right to left.
The French national anthem sounds throughout the stadium, as it will at every Premier League venue this weekend. It is met by a terrific applause as the two teams gather in the centre-circle in a wonderful, moving showing of solidarity. Of course there is a large contingent of French players and coaches in the Arsenal organisation as well, and they are given the full support of these West Brom fans ahead of kick-off.
Tony Pulis is without defender Gareth McAuley following his red card in stoppage time against Manchester United, but otherwise has a full squad at his disposal. Jonas Olsson gets the nod in his absence. Salomon Rondon keeps his spot in attack as the lone striker, with Saido Berahino relegated again to a spot amongst the substitutes.
With Hector Bellerin returning from injury, it is Mathieu Debuchy who is dropped from the starting lineup. Arsene Wenger has also opted to move Kieran Gibbs into attack, ahead of Joel Campbell. It is a rare opportunity for the natural left-back, who scored his side's lone goal against Tottenham in their last match, to excel in a new position while the Gunners are left shorthanded. Laurent Koscielny and Olivier Giroud have been deemed mentally fit to start, having featured for France during the Paris attacks. It promises to be an emotional return to the pitch for them this afternoon.
SUBS: Chester, Gardner, Anichebe, Lambert, Berahino, McManaman, Lindegaard.
WEST BROM (4-2-3-1): Myhill; Dawson, Olsson, Evans, Brunt; Yacob, Fletcher; Morrison, Sessegnon, McClean; Rondon.
SUBS: Debuchy, Gabriel, Arteta, Ospina, Flamini, Campbell, Reine-Adelaide.
ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Cech; Bellerin, Mertesacker, Koscielny, Monreal; Cazorla, Coquelin; Sanchez, Ozil, Gibbs; Giroud.

West Brom, largely in part to Tony Pulis, have an uncanny ability to make life difficult on their opponents. They fell 2-0 to Manchester United last time out but it was far from straightforward for the Red Devils. The Baggies return home now, but they have actually fared considerably worse at the Hawthorns – something they have to correct to avoid a nervy finish to the season, although they don’t appear in any danger at the moment.
Although their league form has been excellent, Arsenal needed the international break to get healthy. They have an injury list as long as Per Mertesacker’s slacks, but it is shrinking by the week – and they need everyone fit as the fixtures start to pile up approaching the always hectic holiday schedule. The Gunners have put in some terrific performances away from home this season, but now isn’t a time to pat themselves on the back. If they want to keep pace atop the table, these are games they absolutely must win.

Liverpool head over to Manchester in the wake of their first defeat under the watchful eye of Jurgen Klopp, as their last game before the international break ended in a narrow 2-1 victory for Crystal Palace at Anfield. As a result, the Reds start today’s game in the bottom half of the table with 17 points, nine behind their opponents and with only half as many league victories. The Etihad has been a tricky venue for them in recent years, and their last league win came back in October 2008. However, they were victorious the last time these two met at Anfield back in March and will be hoping that they can replicate that win in what is certain to be their biggest test of the season thus far.
As a result of victories for Manchester United and Leicester, City head into this afternoon’s clash in third place, although they will move back to the top once again if they are able to see off a much-improved Liverpool side that have looked far better since Jurgen Klopp took over from Brendan Rodgers at the start of October. The spotlight will surely be on former Red Raheem Sterling, who is set to face his former club for the first time since his summer exit. The youngster has adapted well to life in Manchester, playing an important role in an impressive forward line that has scored 26 league goals so far this season. The hosts will also be boosted by the return of Sergio Aguero, who is available for selection once again after recovering from a hamstring injury that saw him miss seven games.

(88’) Exquisite piece of play from Bolasie to twist and turn his way beyond three Sunderland defenders on the left before Watmore finally takes him down on the edge of the 18-yard-box. The ensuing free kick presents a real chance for Palace to produce an equaliser, but again the Black Cats are up to the task defensively!
--- 86’ Substitution Defoe slowly makes his way off, but is unable to walk under his own power. Two members of the training staff help him limp towards the touchline with Danny Graham set to replace him for the final minutes. ---
(84’) Precious time runs off the clock as Defoe goes down with an injury. The striker did well to hold the ball up and force Ward into a foul, but he came down awkwardly on his ankle and this appears to be a real issue for him as the medical staff comes out to take a look.
(82’) STAT ATTACK: Three of the four Premier League meetings between the two clubs have seen a goal scored in the 90th minute or later (Connor Wickham, Steven Fletcher and Stuart O’Keefe).
--- 80’ Goal! SHOCKING DEFENDING AND SUNDERLAND HAVE THE BREAKTHROUGH! A hopeful, searching ball is played forward for Defoe to chase but he was never favoured to get on the end of it. Dann does well to shield him off but doesn't deal with the threat, anticipating the keeper's arrival. The mixup allows Defoe to poke the ball free and run beyond a stranded Hennessey to roll the opening goal into the gaping net! ---
--- 80’ Assist Billy Jones picks up the assist as he had played the original ball forward, but the blame of the goal can be placed squarely on the shoulders of Dann and Hennessey. ---
(78’) The more Palace press for a winner, the more the tempo has increased. The hosts are slowly committing more men forward in search of the elusive breakthrough, but it has left them a bit stretched at the back and Sunderland have certainly shown they are capable of exploiting the new-found space.
--- 76’ Substitution Having just recovered from a groin injury, Marouane Chamakh is introduced for the final 15 minutes or so at the expense of Wickham - who was unable to punish his former team with a decisive goal. ---
(75’) WHAT A CHANCE THAT WAS! Watmore is the architect, courtesy of a mesmerising run forward. The substitute plays a testing ball into the area which runs to Lens, but his shot from 15-yards out is stopped and held on to by Hennessey!
(73’) Important block from O'Shea! The centre-back played a part in helping Ireland reach the European Championships over the international break and he seems a new player because of it! His defensive work has been top notch today and he's at it again, stepping up to interrupt the run of Cabaye before turning his long-range effort aside.
(71’) STAT ATTACK: The six points picked up by Sunderland after 12 matches is their second-worst start to a Premier League campaign. Their worst was five points in 2005/06, where they eventually went on to finish bottom of the league.
--- 69’ Substitution Well, I've said it before, but at the risk of beating a dead horse... Sako was not healthy leading up to the match and it was considered unlikely he would partake. Pardew took a chance in bringing him on, but it has backfired as he's pulled up injured again and needs to be replaced by Patrick Bamford. That's two substitutions the ex-Wolves forward has been involved in. ---
(68’) Redemption for M'Vila! It's as brave as you would like from the defensive midfielder who fearlessly flings himself in front of Sako's strike to head the ball behind for a corner. That had to hurt!
--- 67’ Yellow card Palace attack with real pace and have numbers going forward on the counter. Zaha is taken down on the edge of the area by M'Vila who goes into the book - but it's a smart free kick to concede because his side were in a bit of trouble there had the ex-Manchester United winger gotten by. ---
--- 66’ Yellow card Watmore makes his presence felt with an encouraging run forward, and that's the sort of dribbling the substitute offers. He forces Dann into a foul, who promptly becomes the first Palace player of the night to be shown a yellow card. ---
(64’) Relentless attacking play from Palace who aren't affording Sunderland passage out from the back. Wickham is starting to spring to life, breaking off the shackles which saw him contained up top for the first hour by the close marking of O'Shea.
(62’) Sunderland are dropping deeper and deeper in defence, inviting Palace to throw bodies forward in search of a breakthrough. These are worrying moments for the Black Cats who desperately need someone to offer a link between defence and attack, helping them keep the ball for more than a few seconds at a time.
--- 60’ Substitution Second change for Sunderland and it's a positive one from Allardyce as young attack-minded Duncan Watmore replaces Seb Larsson. The Swede has struggled to create tonight. ---
--- 59’ Substitution Fletcher has had a bit of a thankless task in attack tonight for Sunderland, asked to cover a lot of ground in dropping deeper to get in possession and hold play up, while pushing up the pitch when Palace are in control. He's seemed to run out of gas and his night comes to an end here with Jeremain Lens on to replace him. ---
(59’) SAKO FROM DISTANCE! Belief is starting to grow in the ground as Palace inch closer to a breakthrough. Cabaye's ball through for Wickham is just broken up by Kaboul, but the pressure stays on and Sako nearly squeezes an effort past a scrambling Pantilimon from 30-yards out.
--- 57’ Yellow card Jermain Defoe finds himself in an argument with Dann about whether or not a Palace free kick should be five yards back. It's a ridiculous discussion as there was no danger to come from it regardless, and the striker is subsequntly booked for time wasting. ---
(55’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace have won just three of their last 10 Premier League matches at Selhurst Park (D1, L6), a shocking drop-off from the seven victories they have managed from their last 10 top flight fixtures away from home (L3).
--- 53’ Yellow card Billy Jones goes into the book for a cynical challenge and it means he will be suspended for their game against Stoke next weekend. He was the only outfield player to start every Premier League match for Sunderland this season - a streak which will end after tonight. ---
(52’) LOVELY HIT! Cabaye lines up a strike from distance as he so often does, and sends an effort destined for the far corner. There isn't enough pace behind it to beat Pantilimon, but the keeper doesn't do enough to knock it away from harm. Luckily for him Van Aanholt is on hand to clear and prevent a follow up.
(50’) OFF THE LINE! Palace keep a defender on each post as Sunderland get set to take a corner, and it's a good thing they do as Cabaye is perfectly positioned to steer a header away from harm and deny the Black Cats a breakthrough!
(48’) Sako has slotted into Puncheon's role, sliding in behind Wickham and playing off the striker. Again Palace start the half well, much like they did in the first, but a couple of searching balls in from out wide are dealt with by Sunderland.
--- 46’ Substitution Once considered a doubt to partake in the match tonight, Bakary Sako has been brought on for the second half. Jason Puncheon, who had been largely anonymous, is the one to give way. ---
(46’) Here we go!
HALF TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-0 SUNDERLAND. Scoreless at the break at Selhurst Park after a first half severely lacking in quality. Chances have been slim to none, and with the exception of the odd strike from range, neither goalkeeper has been called into action. On the bright side, it can only get better in the second half so make sure to stick around and see if there's a twist in the tale!
(45’) CRYING OUT FOR A BETTER TOUCH! Cattermole plays an absolutely incredible ball forward, carving through the heart of the Palace defence. The weight on it is perfect to pick out Van Aanholt in stride, but he doesn't even get a shot off as his heavy first touch off a shin takes him away from goal! What a missed opportunity that was.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated a minimum of two minutes of stoppage time.
(43’) On the other touchline, Allardyce will have to be thrilled with what he's seen. He called this Sunderland side out for playing with fear, though they have been anything but scared over the last half-hour and are nearly halfway towards keeping just a second clean sheet of the season (first on their travels).
(41’) OFFSIDE! Palace let off the hook as they don't convincingly clear their lines following a Sunderland free kick. The ball pings around before coming to Fletcher, but he was standing just an inch or two beyond the last defender. That is one of the luxuries of the Black Cats having three central defenders, in that they can always commit one forward freely for a set piece.
(39’) Just over five minutes until the interval now and Pardew likely will not be pleased with how this half has progressed. They started full of energy and looking to attack, but have since faded, having yet to carve out a clean chance despite all their possession.
(37’) STAT ATTACK: These sides have met twice previously in the Premier League at Selhurst Park, with both matches finishing 3-1. Each side was victorious once, while the losing team in each match finished with 10 men (Mile Jedinak sent off for Crystal Palace, John O’Shea for Sunderland).
(35’) DOUBLE CHANCE! Acrobatic bit of play from Bolasie at the near post to meet a cross with an overhead kick. From up against the touchline he sends the ball back across goal for Wickham, but again the angle is too tight as the striker can't direct his header on target - it actually runs back across to the DR Congo winger who was in an offside position.
(33’) These two teams are very similar in the sense that they boast great pace on the flanks and like to play counter-attacking football. As a result they are both wary of being caught out on the break which has hurt the quality in attack as neither team are willing to commit men forward. The onus has to be put on the likes of Larsson, M'Vila, Cabaye and Puncheon to try and create from a more central role.
(31’) Was that the right decision?! McArthur picks up the ball right at the halfway line and shows good strength to fend off a challenge and sprint into the final third. Cabaye finds a pocket of space and is screaming out for a pass to his left, but the Scottish international opts to try and take the shot himself, though is unable to force Pantilimon into a difficult stop.
(29’) Palace are back on the front foot, but they aren't offering any real threat in attack. It has been a bit too straightforward for the Sunderland back line, who have had plenty of support from the likes of Cattermore and M'Vila as well. The hosts have largely been held to the periphery up to this point.
(27’) STAT ATTACK: Since their victory at Selhurst Park last season, Sunderland have won just two of their last 20 away matches in the Premier League (D8, L10).
(25’) SUPERB FROM DEFOE! What an absolutely extraordinary run from the striker to beat three defenders before finally being tripped up on the very edge of the area, just to the right of goal. The ensuing free kick is played short in an attempt to tee up Fletcher, but it winds up running through to Jones. He tries to power an effort through on goal, but there are too many bodies in the way as it is blocked aside before being cleared to safety.
(23’) Despite seeing less of the ball, Sunderland seem to be growing in confidence with each passing minute. Every failed Palace attack gives the Black Cats an added boost on the counter, and they're starting to feed the ball into some encouraging areas in the final third.
(21’) NASTY CHALLENGE! Puncheon lunges carelessly into the feet of Jones near the touchline, sending the wing-back toppling over. The ensuing free kick presents the visitors with a chance to whip a ball into the area, but the final delivery is a letdown as Palace clear their lines capably.
(19’) The tempo has slowed a bit, with Palace starting to dictate possession. The hosts are taking more of a patient approach in attack as they start to firmly entrench themselves in the Sunderland end - though the Black Cats have remained well-organised to block any passage through on goal.
(17’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace have earned 19 points from their opening 12 matches, setting a new club record for best start to a Premier League campaign.
(15’) Tough collision inside the area! A ball is played in from the right for Bolasie to attack. He runs into the centre with pace where O'Shea is also waiting to head clear. Both players only had eyes for the ball which sees them clatter together quite aggressively - though they should be alright to continue after a moment of respite.
(13’) CRYING OUT FOR A BETTER FINISH! End-to-end action at Selhurst Park! There is a wonderful tempo to the match at the moment, and Sunderland nearly break the deadlock on a sumptuous counter. Cattermole plays a piercing ball through for Defoe, but the striker uncharacteristically scuffs a shot wide from close range.
(11’) FIRST FORAY FORWARD FOR SUNDERLAND! Billy Jones is the architect with a delightful run through the heart of midfield, somewhere you would hardly expect to see him! The wing-back plays a terrific ball to split the two centre-backs and tee up Patrick van Aanholt for a shot, but he drags his first-time effort with his weaker right foot wide of the near post.
(9’) Palace's approach has been to play balls over the top for the likes of their front three to chase. Sunderland are on their heals early on in defence, perhaps echoing Sam Allardyce's sentiments that they are playing with fear. They can ill-afford to concede the first goal of this match, especially not in its infancy.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Sunderland won 3-1 in this fixture last season at Selhurst Park, with Steven Fletcher (two) and Jordi Gomez in amongst the goals. It was their first away victory over Crystal Palace in league play since 1995.
(5’) These fans at Selhurst Park don't take much to get going, but they have every reason to show their support as Palace put Sunderland over waves of early pressure. Yannick Bolasie makes a dazzling diagonal run to break into the area and win the hosts yet another corner - but the Black Cats defend the set piece admirably.
(3’) Encouraging start for the hosts who bring good width into their attack. Pape Souare and Wilfried Zaha issue an early warning sign along the left flank, with the former producing a nifty cross in which John O'Shea is forced to knock behind for a corner.
(1’) And we're underway at Selhurst Park!
Sam Allardyce has reported a clean bill of health for Sunderland, who are boosted by the return of John O'Shea and Lee Cattermole. The duo slot straight into the starting lineup, while Patrick van Aanholt, Seb Larsson and Jermain Defoe are also back into the XI after sitting out against Southampton.
Bakary Sako was a doubt with a knock, and while he has been included in the team, he is forced to start amongst the substitutes. Alan Pardew hands Connor Wickham a start against his former side as a result. Joel Ward is also back in after sitting out against Liverpool, forcing Martin Kelly to the bench.

CONFIRMED TEAM NEWS:
This has the feel of a massive game for Sunderland. They have lost three of four since the appointment of Sam Allardyce, but the new manager has had the last two weeks, uninterrupted, to engrain his system in the team. A victory today would pull them to within a point of safety, and most importantly help restore confidence on Wearside, while a defeat will lead to full-fledged panic at the Stadium of Light – although it’s unclear how much Big Sam can do to help before he has the chance to bring in some new faces in January.
If Crystal Palace could perform at Selhurst Park as they do away from home, they would assuredly find themselves in the top four at the moment and pushing Leicester City as the Premier League’s feel-good story. They have had a tougher fixture list at home thus far, dropping points against Arsenal, West Ham and the two Manchester clubs. In their two home games against weaker opponents (Aston Villa and West Brom) they claimed all three points – a record Alan Pardew will hope to keep intact this evening.

(90’) Tomlin plays the ball sideways to an onrushing Ritchie in the middle of the park, but the winger scuffs his effort and sees his shot trickle out of bounds for a Newcastle goal-kick.
