TEAM NEWS: Steve McClaren has kept the faith by making no alterations to the Newcastle team which started their 0-0 draw with Stoke City last weekend. Kevin Mbabu has made his return from injury and replaces Massadio Haidara on the bench, which is the only change on that front as well for today's visitors.
TEAM NEWS: Howe has made two changes to the side which started Bournemouth's 2-0 defeat against Southampton last time out. Junior Stanislas and Joshua King both get the chance to impress from the get-go this afternoon in place of Marc Pugh and Glenn Murray respectively.
Newcastle, on the other hand, started the new campaign poorly but have been much improved in recent matches. The Magpies have picked up four points in their last two home games and it is on the road where they are suffering at the moment, still looking for their first three points away from St. James' Park.
Bournemouth are looking for their first win since beating Sunderland in September after losing four of their last five Premier League games. Eddie Howe's men, though, have faced some tough opposition in that run such as Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur and therefore they will be hoping to profit against a team in and around them in the table today.
Today's fixture on the south coast sees two teams in the doldrums of the top flight lock horns. Just one point separates 17th-placed Bournemouth from 18th-placed Newcastle prior to kick off and both sides desperately need all three points here this afternoon.
Good afternoon and welcome to our LIVE text commentary on today's Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Newcastle United from the Vitality Stadium. I'm Matthew Judge and I will be your host for the match, which kicks off at 12:45pm.

Watford, meanwhile, did not create enough up front but really can't blame anyone but Gomes for that loss. They didn't play poorly but they gifted the home side with two goals from almost nothing, and failed to recover. Thanks for joining us here today!
Ranieri's men took their chances well and relied on some bad goalkeeping, but full credit to them for making the most of what was presented to them. They're temporarily tied on points with Arsenal and Manchester City and stay ahead of Manchester United!
(90’) AND THAT'S THE GAME! It ends 2-1 here for Leicester after two howlers from Gomes before a late penalty, which didn't bring on the comeback that Watford would've been hoping for!
(90’) A great, late chance here for Leicester, who have a free-kick to the left of Watford's box that's played short to Albrighton, who wiggles back and forth before passing it to Okazaki, who gets taken down for another free-kick!
(90’) Into the second of four extra minutes here and the home side are still pushing for a third goal, but their pressure is cleared. Soon it's Anya, and he goes back to Britos, whose long ball to Ighalo is easily intercepted.
--- 90’ Substitution A late substitution for Ranieri, as Drinkwater comes off - also to a standing ovation! - for King, as he looks to manage the clock and introduce a set of fresh legs to help his side see out this win. ---
(88’) Watford poke and prod as they try to find the equalizer here; Leicester are set up deep and the visitors have to go back to their defence to try and create some space and find an opening.
(86’) Britos has to make two clearances just seconds apart to try and stem a Leicester attack, and Paredes tries to loft it off to Ighalo but his pass is overhit. Time is running out here for Watford!
--- 84’ Substitution It's another substitute for the home side, as Mahrez comes off to a standing ovation for Dyer. The former only lacked a goal to cap off his hardworking display and he's clearly beloved by the fans here! ---
(82’) Vardy tries to send a cross into the box but it's blocked by Ake. As the play develops, Simpson raises his boot high to him a ball and kicks Deeney in the shoulder, winning a free-kick for Watford.
(81’) Paredes dribbles towards the box and gets bundled over but the ball falls kindly for Deeney, who fires his effort but it's right at Schmeichel!
(80’) Fuchs takes a deep throw-in, in his opponents' half, and sends it long into the box. It's cleared and played all the way back to Schmeichel, who hoofs it forward to his side.
(78’) A couple of minutes ago, just after the penalty, Diamanti entered the pitch for Nyom as Watford look to add the enigmatic Italian's spark to their attack up front.
(77’) WHAT AN EFFORT FROM MAHREZ! He got the ball down the right, dribbled fantastically inside of the box and unleashed a furious shot that gets deflected out for a corner!
--- 76’ Substitution A. Diamanti enters play, replacing A. Nyom. ---
(76’) GOOOOOOALLLL DEENEY! The captain slots it down the left, cool as you'd llike, with Schmeichel diving to the right. It's 2-1 now and the game is on!!!
--- 75’ Goal! Penalty goal scored by T. Deeney! ---
(75’) PENALTY TO WATFORD! Kante, the goalscorer, takes down Paredes in the box after a poor touch sends the Watford player through - he stuck out a leg to try and prevent his advance, bundling him over, and now the visitors can reduce the deficit!!!
(73’) Paredes gets the ball and drives forward with energy and guile for his side, looking to spark something from his offence. Watford just cannot make it click up front and soon it takes another Britos clearance to prevent a shot from Leicester!
(72’) Vardy plays it back to his midfield, and his team try to get it wide to Mahrez but the pass is headed out by Britos. Watford soon intercept and look to build from the back, with a nice ball played to Ighalo that he sends wide for Fuchs to send out for a throw-in.
--- 70’ Substitution A change for Watford as Capoue comes off for Paredes, after a middling display where he was effective at times but just not often enough. ---
(68’) Unlike after their first goal, when they let their foot off the gas, the home side continue to keep the ball well. They're just a little more than 20 minutes away from continuing their superb start to the league this season!
(67’) This half has been an absolute disaster for Gomes, who has had a very solid season with Watford up until tonight. But his slippery fingers let the first goal go in and a poorly timed challenge saw him give away a penalty - he's singlehandedly responsible for the deficit here!
(66’) GOOOOOALLL VARDY! He makes absolutely no mistake from the spot, smashing in a superb penalty, and has now scored in a remarkable nine Premier League games in a row - just one away from Van Nistlerooy's record at Manchester United!
--- 65’ Yellow card PENALTY FOR LEICESTER!!! The day goes from bad to worse for Gomes! He enters the book after taking out Vardy just inside the box after running into him while trying to clear the ball! ---
--- 65’ Goal! Penalty goal scored by J. Vardy! ---
(64’) A visitors' free-kick is cleared, then played back in towards Ighalo, but it's overhit and Schmeichel is off his line to schoop it up. Soon after, Capoue wins back possession in midfield and does manage to get the ball to his striker this time, and he's bundled over by Morgan but the referee has deemed that a fair challenge!
(63’) The second corner is nearly headed in by Morgan, who races in front of Britos to get his head on the ball, but the angle is all wrong and he only sends it high over the bar.
(62’) Britos makes a superb tackle in the box to deny Vardy, who was racing towards goal and had just pulled the trigger on a shot that looked destined to go into the net! The home side take a corner, which is played out for another.
(60’) A Leicester free-kick is wafted into the box but headed clear by Ake. The home side try to work it back in on the rebound but end up losing the ball; since the goal, they've struggled quite a bit to string passes together.
(58’) Credit to Watford here, who have actually looked the better side since Leicester scored. Nyom tries to take matters in his own hands after he gets the ball just outside the box, takes a step, and sends a shot towards the far corner, but it drifts over the bar. That was powerfully struck!
(56’) Vardy is up and walks off the pitch but he seems to be holding his right hip gingerly. He's about to come back on, however, and soon re-enters the pitch, jogging carefully.
(55’) After that bizarre mistake, the visitors have it all to do now! Nyom takes a throw-in and tries to work it down the right, but soon afer, Vardy is down and in some pain after landing awkwardly when trying to head the ball. This is a serious concern for the home team, as no one made any contact with the striker.
--- 52’ Goal! GOOOAL LEICESTER! WHAT A HOWLER FROM GOMES!!! And that is utterly shocking goalkeeping - a routine shot from just inside the box from Kante slips between the keeper's hands and rolls into the net! The buildup from the midfielder was fantastic but there's simply no way that should've gone in!!! ---
(51’) After withstanding an early seige here, Watford are seeing more of the ball, but they're not keeping it well. Substitute Okazaki is pushed over by Capoue for a free-kick that the home side plays quickly and close, passing it to the flank.
(49’) Whatever Ranieri said at half-time is clearly working for his team, and not just up front, as his defence steps up just in time to leave Ighalo offside before he could race to the goal with the ball!
(48’) That's a great solo effort from Albrighton, who gets the ball, dribbles past three players, and unleashes a shot - but it's right at Gomes! The home side have begun this half very, very well.
(47’) Vardy contorts his body in the box but can't get his foot around the ball to shoot, and Leicester send another cross in moments after that the defence heads clear.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Okazaki enters the game and replaces J. Schlupp. ---
(46’) We're back underway now, with one substitute for the home side making it onto the pitch, as Schlupp goes off for Okazaki. It's the men in blue who begin with the ball from kick-off, but lose it almost immediately, with a forward chip towards the wring not executed well enough. Drinkwater wins back possession soon after and plays it calmly to his defence.
As for Ranieri's team, they haven't yet incorporated much of Vardy, though they seem to like falling behind before they can spark themselves into scoring!
That first half featured a lot of grit but only intermittent waves where it seemed like scoring was possible. Watford have looked their best when they got Ighalo involved, but that's been far too little so far, with the team certainly needing their forward to see more of the ball after the break.
(45’) Just the one minute of added-time announced by the fourth official here, and the first half ends with Watford trying to get the ball out of their midfield via a throw-in that Leicester are more than happy just to clear to the opposite defence.
(43’) DEENEY JUST MISSES A HEADER! That was utterly superb from Ighalo, who was dynamite to win the ball, run powerfully down the left, and loft in a near-perfect cross that somehow just missed his teammate!
(41’) Francis slides into the back of Anya right around the centre-circle but avoids a caution for his trouble. Soon after, the home side look to counter but the two centre-backs are able to contain the danger, with Cathcart sliding in well to control the ball and clear.
(39’) Mahrez wins a free-kick deep in Watford's half. Fuchs stands over it, delivering a low swooping pass that fails to beat the first man. The visitors try to counter but Schlupp holds up Ighalo well to prevent the danger from growing.
(37’) And that's better from the home side! Vardy gets a simple pass played to him, turns, dribbles around Britos, and fires a low shot that Gomes dives low to catch!
(34’) Ranieri is urging his team to get the ball forward but they're having trouble dealing with the number of men in Watford's midfield, but soon Mahrez has it down the left and is looking for a quick release and return up front.
(32’) Ranieri's men just cannot get out of their own half right now, with Watford in cruise control here. They haven't yet found the cutting edge up front but the ball seems glued to their feet, and it takes a good read from Fuchs to prevent Ighalo receiving the ball in the box!
(30’) This is solid football from the visitors, who use their height to try and work it down the right. They keep it well, but a ball to Ighalo is hit too hard by Abdi and ends up beyond everyone in the home side's box.
(28’) The game has settled now here after a frantic spell, with the visitors looking for Vardy up top but he's well offside when the high lofted ball is played into his path.
(26’) Drinkwater collects an errant pass from the visiting defence in midfield and sprays it wide, sparking a solid atttack that sees Gomes rush off his line to parry the ball and then soon snatch an Albrighton shot out of the air!
(25’) Capoue looks to take matters into his own hands, getting the ball in midfield, driving forward, and unleashing a powerful strike roughly 25 yards away from goal. It ends up a little high and a little wide of the far post, but not by much!
(23’) The home side look to respond now but they're struggling to find a way to get a ball around the duo of Britos and Cathcart, who have been imposing thus far and not given Vardy much space to operate in.
(21’) And out of nowhere this game has exploded to life with chances coming furiously now, with Anya just overrunning the ball ahead of Fuchs in the box as the visitors look to continue to apply pressure at the Leicester defence!
(20’) IGHALO OFF THE POST! It's from one end to another as a dinked pass was played to the forward in the box, who touched it around Morgan before firing and hitting the upright! The rebound fell for Abdi on the volley but he forces Schmeichel into a superb save to deny him a goal!
(19’) AND HOW DID LEICESTER NOT SCORE THERE?! A fantastic free-kick was perfectly lofted into the box by Albrighton but it drifts over everyone before Huth got a touch to it, and Gomes knocked it out of play... oh but the flag is up and it's offside regardless!
(16’) Some nice football from Watford now as they pass the ball quickly, working it from the centre of the pitch out wide to Ighalo, forcing Simpson to make a sliding tackle to send the ball out for a throw-in just outside of his own area.
(14’) The ball pings back and forth with several headers, going this way and that, before Britos can settle it and try to work the ball smoothly up from the back. Watford haven't been at their most clever with that thus far.
(12’) Kante makes a huge tackle in the middle of the pitch on Capoue to stop a counter, with the midfielder taking on one man too many!
(11’) Fuchs makes himself available for a throw-in as Leicester try to work it down the right, but the visitors snatch possession and race towards goal, with Ighalo just a step too slow in the box to collect.
(9’) It's all down the left for Watford, before Watson switches flanks smartly and a ball is cut back to Capoue on the edge of the box. He smashes his effort first time but it's comfortable for Schmeichel to collect!
(8’) Watford finally get a chance to build from the back a bit here, but a long ball up to Deeney is overhit, to the chagrin of their manager on the sidelines. They rushed that opportunity and now it's back with the home side.
(6’) This is a decent if early spell of home side possession, with a well-hit cross entering the box for Gomes to schoop up following solid work down the left flank. Albrighton and Simpson combine well down the right before Ake steps up smartly to clear.
(4’) And from that free-kick comes the first shot of the game, with Kante getting on the end of a loose ball outside the box and whizzing a first-time shot well over the bar!
(3’) It's a tight start to this game in the midfield, with the two sides condensed right in the middle of the pitch. A handball from Cathcart right near Mahrez outside the area gifts the first free-kick of the match to the home side.
(1’) Following a minute's silence for Remembrance Weekend, we have kick-off! The visitors get us started right away, with Deeney urging his side forward before Capoue hofts a long ball up towards Ighalo. The ball is knocked about for a bit before going out of bounds, and Leicester begin in defending mode.
We're just minutes away from kickoff now, with the two teams walking out of the tunnel. The visitors are in their yellow and black alternate kit, with the home side wearing while and blue.
The past three meetings between these two sides have been completely even: one Watford win, one Leicester win, and one 2-2 draw. Today, of course, all expectations will be with the home side, leaving the visitors with the job of pulling off an upset!
The most fascinating part of this match is perhaps the battle between the two men up front for both sides. Should Vardy score today, he'll be jsut one match away from Ruud Van Nistlerooy's record of notching in ten consecutive Premier League matches. His counterpart for the visitors, Ighalo, has scored seven of his team's ten Premier League goals so far.
The visitors, meanwhile, are snuggled in midtable but have struggled for goals this season. They've only allowed 10 goals, which is tied for third-best in the league, but only Aston Villa have scored fewer goals than Quiqie Sanchez Flores' side.
Leicester have been simply soaring in the Premier League this season. In their last five, they've just lost once - at home against Arsenal - beating Norwhich and West Brom away, Crystal Palace at home, and drawing away at Southampton. They've scored the second-most goals in the leagues and have a reputation for being the comeback kings!
Watford (4-4-2): Gomes; Ake, Britos, Cathcart, Nyom; Abdi, Watson, Capoue, Anya; Ighalo, Deeney.
Leicester (4-4-1-1): Schmeichel; Simpson, Morgan, Huth, Fuchs; Albrighton, Kante, Drinkwater, Schlupp; Mahrez; Vardy.
Hello and welcome to our live match coverage of Leicester vs Watford! This should be a thrilling one today, with the third placed side hosting eleventh as Claudio Ranieri's men look to continue their dream start to the league and stay in a Champions' League spot!

Full time at Old Trafford. It wasn't entirely convincing, but Manchester United successfully end their goal and win drought with a 2-0 home victory over West Brom in the Barclays Premier League. It was another day when the deadlock looked like it wouldn't be broken, but the Red Devils eventually managed to claim the win through goals from Jesse Lingard and Juan Mata, who netted with a late penalty. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +1 Red card! G. McAuley is sent off by the referee! ---
--- 90’ +1 Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLL FOR MAN UTD! Juan Mata steps up and confidently dispatches the penalty with a little dinked finish down the middle! Coolness personified! Two-nil! GAME OVER! ---
(90’) PENALTY TO MAN UTD AND MCCAULEY IS SENT OFF! Herrera finds space in midfield and sends a lovely pass over the West Brom defence for Martial, who drives toward goal before being scythed down by the defender, who is given a straight red card!
(88’) It looks like there is going to be four minutes of added time signaled by the referee here which will certainly give West Brom a little bit of a boost going into these latter stages. They just need to get the ball up the other end of the park!
(86’) People may not be too happy about the way United are getting results at the moment, but their defensive stability has to be applauded. Granted, they haven't been tested too much today, but if they can hold out here it will be five clean sheets on the bounce - quite the feat!
--- 85’ Substitution C. Brunt is done for the day. C. McManaman is his replacement. ---
(85’) Third and final change from West Brom as Tony Pulis plays his last throw of the dice. Coming off his Brunt and he'll be replaced by Callum McManaman in what is a positive switch. Plenty of pace and direct running featuring on the left for the Baggies now with McClean also out there.
(83’) Last change of the match from United and it will see Rooney leave the pitch to a warm ovation with Ander Herrera coming on in his place. The England captain, again, just hasn't looked particularly threatening out there.
--- 82’ Substitution W. Rooney is done for the day. Ander Herrera is his replacement. ---
(82’) Just under 10 minutes remaining at Old Trafford and the West Brom onslaught we perhaps expected after the opening goal has not really came, with De Gea possibly being the most bored man in Manchester this afternoon. Still time for a grandstand finish, though!
(80’) United win the ball in midfield and Schweinsteiger moves forward with pace before finding Martial with a lovely pass. The latter finds Lingard at the back post who twists and turns his way into the area before going down under the challenge of Dawson before he can get the shot away. Never a penalty though, and the referee agrees as he waves play on.
(78’) With West Brom chasing the game as they are, the play is becoming much more open which will probably play into the hands of United, who have a lot of pace in their attacking ranks with the likes of Lingard and Martial. There is another goal in this, but for who?
(76’) Another change from United now and it is a senior debut for 18-year-old Cameron Borthwick-Jackson, who comes on at left-back in place of Rojo, who was starting to look a little dodgy after being booked a few minutes ago, and with Sessegnon bombing down the right.
(74’) What a horrible miss from Berahino! The substitute, who has only been on for a couple of minutes, makes an excellent drifting run into the penalty area and latches on to a superb cross from Dawson, but somehow manages to divert his header high and wide over the bar! United let off the hook!
--- 72’ Substitution R. Lambert enters play, replacing S. Rondón. ---
--- 72’ Substitution J. Morrison is replaced with S. Berahino. ---
(72’) JUST WIDE FROM FLETCHER! West Brom get the set-piece on the right wing, which is wickedly curled into the box from Brunt. The Scot rises high and glances a lovely header aimed at he bottom corner, but his attempt flashes the wrong side of the post! Unlucky!
(70’) Just as that is mentioned, West Brom do indeed decide to make changes, and it is with a double substitution. Coming on his two attackers in the form of Ricky Lambert and Saido Berahino, and they'll come on to replace James Morrison and Salomon Rondon. Let's see if the duo can make an impact!
(68’) We are midway through this second half now and it is surprising that Pulis has not delves into his ranks on the substitutes bench to add some fresh legs out there, which the visitors look like they desperately need. United may be a goal ahead but with the scoreline the way it is West Brom always have a chance if they go for it.
(66’) Another booking for West Brom now and it is a deserved one for Brunt who completely takes out Mata a few yards in from the halfway line. The left-back is lucky that the Spaniard jumped over that one or it arguably could have been a straight red.
--- 65’ Yellow card C. Brunt is cautioned by the referee. ---
(64’) McClean picks up the ball down the left wing and looks to test the recently introduced Jones at right-back. The winger goes on a rare venture to the byline and swings a teasing cross to the back post, but Blind is on hand to calmly clear out of the box to Carrick, who looks to move play out of defence.
--- 62’ Substitution P. Jones enters play, replacing A. Young. ---
(62’) First change of the match now and it is a pragmatic one from Man Utd as Van Gaal opts to withdraw Ashley Young in favour of the more defensively minded Phil Jones, who will fill in at right-back. That could be seen as a negative change by the Dutchman, but Young is indeed out of position in defence, so probably an intelligent one.
--- 61’ Yellow card M. Rojo goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 60’ Yellow card S. Rondón is cautioned by the referee. ---
(60’) Another booking for West Brom as Rondon really begins to display his frustration. The Venezuelan has had such little support and service up top that is no wonder that he is losing his head, as he scythes down Smalling near the right touchline to subsequently see yellow. Probably not the best way to deal with the frustration, right enough!
(58’) Now we will see what West Brom are made of as everyone know they can defend brilliantly when required, but they need to come out of their shell and display more of an attacking ambition. Rondon up there on his own just isn't going to cut it, so we should probably expect to see Saido Berahino at some point.
(56’) There is a different feeling to the atmosphere in the stadium at the moment as the Man Utd faithful have got up out of their seats to usher their team forward for more goals. Indeed, it seems to be working as the hosts have a spring in their step after going a goal ahead.
(54’) Had Manchester United failed to score today and West Brom held out for the 0-0 draw, it would have been the first time in 94 years that the Red Devils had went three games with three consecutive goalless draws. Lingard the hero to stop that highly undesired record!
--- 52’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAALLLLLLLLLLL FOR MAN UTD!! THE ROOF BLOWS OFF OLD TRAFFORD! Martial clips a cross into the box which is unconvincingly cleared by Brunt. Lingard picks up the ball and proceeds to curl a fantastic finish into the far corner! One-nil! The drought is over! ---
(50’) So far the second period has more or less followed the same formula as the first as Man United continue to press ahead while West Brom sit extremely deep inside their own third of the pitch. It is going to take something pretty clever for the hosts to open the scoring here!
(48’) Myhill's clearance goes straight to the feet of Rooney outside the box and the United captain takes down with an assured touch before attempting to thread a pass into the feet of Martial. Once again Evans shows an impressive turn of pace to get back and make the vital interception! He is certainly enjoying his return to Old Trafford!
(46’) We are back under way at Old Trafford! Someone give us a goal!
Half time at Old Trafford. Unfortunately for The Red Devils it has been a predictably dull first half as they once again fail to turn their possession dominance into goalscoring chances, as Boaz Myhill in between the sticks for West Brom has only been tested once. Tony Pulis' men have defended very well so far, and deservedly keep a clean sheet at the break as we go in at 0-0. Second half to come; hopefully some goals too!
(45’) SAVE FROM MYHILL! The West Brom goalkeeper is called into action for the first time in the match as Martial collects the ball on the edge of the box before cleverly finding a yard of space and lashing a strike at goal! Unfortunately for the hosts, it is straight at the keeper who makes the solid stop!
--- 43’ Yellow card C. Dawson is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) Dawson, who only a few moments ago almost gifted Man Utd the lead by giving the ball away, compounds a rather awful couple of minutes for himself by being the first player to go into the book with a cynical tug of the shirt on Lingard down the left wing. Free kick to the hosts.
(41’) Fantastic challenge by Evans! Dawson gives the ball away horribly into the centre of the pitch and Martial takes advantage to steal possession before laying into the path of Lingard. The 22-year-old dashes into the box and looks to smash a strike at goal, but is thwarted by the former United defender, who comes in with a superb goal-saving tackle!
(39’) This scoreline is all too familiar for this Manchester United crowd as they are usher their team forward with cheers of 'ATTACK, ATTACK' which has been the chorus of the day in the last few matches at Old Trafford. You can't fault their enthusiasm, but West Brom are defending excellently!
(37’) Rojo picks up the ball to feet and assesses his options before flashing a pass inside into Lingard, who attempts to swiftly turn and make his way into the box. Dawson has other ideas though and proactively gets in front of the ball to make the solid challenge, before popping up top for Rondon.
(35’) West Brom get their first corner kick of the match which is swung dangerously into the box by McClean. The ball comes to Evans who recycles possession back into the danger area, only for De Gea to rush off his line and just manage to clear with an unconvincing punch.
(33’) Van Gaal's outfit have had three-quarters of possession in the game so far but Boaz Myhill is yet to be truly tested in between the sticks for West Brom. Best chance of the match came to Mata, who unluckily strike off target wide of the left-hand post.
(31’) Mata is becoming more and more prominent for United in the past few minutes and this time comes deep to receive the ball to feet and jinks past the defender before sliding a pass down the wing for Rojo. The Argentine then goes to whip a cross into the box, only to be wrongly flagged as offside. Dodgy decision from the linesman there as he was well onside.
(29’) We are well beyond the midway point of this opening half now and the game is yet to catch fire at Old Trafford, and the Man United faithful may get more and more frustrated if chances aren't created in the final third. Two goals in five games is simply not good enough!
(27’) Interestingly, it actually appears that Man United may be employing a 4-4-2 formation this afternoon as Martial has clearly been deployed as a centre-forward alongside Rooney, with Mata attached to the right touchline. It didn't start off this way, but with the possession they have they have switched it slightly.
(25’) Carrick, who has been involved in a lot of the positive action from United so far, moves into space through the centre and dinks a searching pass into the box for Martial. The Frenchman ushers McCauley out of the way but ends up being penalised, with West Brom being awarded the soft free kick. Didn't look too much in that one!
(23’) Some good interplay from United in and around the penalty area at the moment as Rojo steps in from his advanced position at the left wing and fires a pass into Carrick, who attempts to cushion the ball into space to tee up Rooney. It doesn't quite come off for the duo though, and West Brom manage to clear.
(21’) It was probably fairly predictable that the early portion of the match would go by without much incident as West Brom would not have wanted to concede particularly quickly away from home. As the game goes on, we may indeed see a little more attacking ambition from the Baggies.
(19’) Dawson moves play out of defence and plays a diagonal pass deep down the wing for McClean. The Irishman cuts back inside on his left foot before swinging a deep cross to the back post, but it is just behind Rondon who just can't retreat quick enough to get a meaningful connection on his header.
(17’) MATA!!! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT?! The best move of the match ensues as Man Utd move the ball with pace through the middle. Possession eventually comes to Rooney, who cleverly shifts past Evans before teeing up the Spaniard, who curls a beautiful strike aimed at the bottom corner! JUST WIDE! Still 0-0!
(15’) Lingard collects possession down the left touchline and finally has a bit of space to stretch his legs. He does so with a marauding run into the channel but is excellently dispossessed by Dawson, who picks his pocket before sending a lovely ball up the wing for Sessegnon.
(13’) With all the criticism that has been aimed at United in the past few weeks, with their supposed slow build-up play in the middle of the park, it should be interesting to see if Van Gaal deviates from his usually patient game plan. With West Brom defending the way they are, patience will certainly be a virtue this afternoon!
(11’) This game is all-Man Utd at the moment as the hosts attempt to break down this typically sturdy West Brom defence. Martial and Lingard, who look like they have been advised to continually swap positions on the wings, link up down the left but find themselves completely crowded out and are forced back.

West Brom have enjoyed a typically solid beginning to the season under the pragmatic tutorship of Tony Pulis, and currently find themselves in 12th place with 14 points taken from 11 matches. Like United, goalscoring has been an issue for them this season as they have managed to record just 10 goals in the Barclays Premier League. Under the former Crystal Palace boss, the Baggies have been defeated just twice in their last nine top-flight fixtures on the road.
Despite their slight profligacy in front of goal, the Red Devils currently find themselves in the last Champions League qualifying position with 21 points taken from 11 matches – four points behind joint-leaders Arsenal and Manchester City and one point behind high-flying Leicester.
Apart from perhaps Van Gaal himself, the figure that has came under the most pressure due to the recent abject results has been Wayne Rooney, who has had a below-par season up until this point. However, there is cause for optimism for England's top goalscorer as he managed to claim the only goal of the match in Tuesday's vital Champions League victory over CSKA Moscow. The 30-year-old also has a superb record against West Brom in recent years, having been involved in 11 goals via scoring or assisting in his last seven starts against the Baggies.
However, despite a massive improvement at the back, Louis van Gaal and his charges have came under plenty of scrutiny in recent weeks for their lack of prowess at the opposite end of the pitch in the final third, as they have netted just twice in their past five games in all competitions, while also being involved in two consecutive goalless draws in the league against Manchester City and Crystal Palace. This brand of football has been criticised this week by club legends such as Roy Keane and Paul Scholes, who believe a club of United's stature should be implementing more entertaining tactics for the fans.
Today's clash sees two of the sides with the best defensive records in the league come head-to-head. Man Utd have kept more clean sheets than any other team in the division so far this season, while West Brom have not conceded in four out of their first five away matches.

West Ham move up into fifth place above Tottenham Hotspur who play tomorrow. Everton leapfrog their city rivals Liverpool into eighth position, having played a game more.
West Ham fans will be once again cursing the name of Romelu Lukaku who scored his seventh goal in as many games against them this afternoon. They will also be concerned about the injuries sustained by Dimitri Payet and Enner Valencia and hope that they are fit to return in a couple of weeks when the Premier League resumes.
In the end you would have to say that on full reflection of the ninety minutes that a draw was a fair result. Both teams had decent spells during the match but neither did enough to get the victory. A reasonable point for both sides as we head into the international break.
(90’) Full time here at Upton Park. West Ham 1-1 Everton.
(90’) Barry almost sets Mirallas away on goal but his attempted through ball is just overhit and will run through to Adrian. Can either side fashion one last chance?
(90’) The game has got a little bit scrappy towards the end and you get the feeling that both teams would settle for a draw now.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card M. Zárate goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) We will have five minutes of injury time to be added on at the end of this match.
(88’) Former Everton striker Nikica Jelavic does indeed come on for Andy Carroll for the remaining minutes. Can the Croatian striker be the hero?
--- 87’ Substitution N. Jelavić enters play, replacing A. Carroll. ---
(86’) CLOSE! SO CLOSE! Lukaku stabs the ball towards goal from about six or seven yards out but the ball skids past Adrian's near post. Brendan Galloway delivered a decent cross from the left and the big Belgian forward did very well to get across his man.
(84’) SAVE! Jenkinson intercepts the ball and then drives forward from right back. Space opens up in front of him but his shot is straight at Tim Howard.
--- 83’ Substitution A. Lennon enters play, replacing Deulofeu. ---
(83’) Andy Carroll has largely been an observer in the second half and you wonder whether Bilic is brave enough to replace his sides no.9 at this late stage or if he'll throw on someone like Jelavic to join him? It's stick or twist time now.
(81’) Martinez now decides that Deulofeu's race is run and opts to make a rather like-for-like swap by bringing on Aaron Lennon in his place. As an ex-Spurs player Lennon doesn't receive the warmest of welcomes from the West Ham fans.
(79’) It is now Everton who look the more settled of the two teams. If there is to be a winner you would fancy it would be the visitors at this stage. Hammers fans will be mindful that there was a last minute winner from Lukaku in the corresponding fixture last season.
(77’) Those injuries to Payet and Valencia have rather rocked West Ham and they have found hard to get going again since Zarate came on. They have lost all the momentum they had built up at the start of this half.
(75’) Deulofeu looks to take the fight to the opposition by going on the outside rather than cutting inside on the occasion. The young Spaniard forces a corner, that Barkley takes - it is flicked on at the near post but Adrian is alive to the situation and plucks the ball away from Lukaku.
(73’) Everton for the first time in a while string a succession of passes together. Ross Barkley holds up the play before bringing Funes Mori into the game. The centre back then, for reasons unknown, decides to take a shot on from at least thirty yards out that goes comfortably over the bar. Bizarre decision.
(71’) CLOSE! Winston Reid towers above everyone else in the box to meet Mark Noble's corner but the defender's header zips over the crossbar, much to the relief of Tim Howard. Not too far away there.
--- 69’ Substitution M. Zárate enters the game and replaces E. Valencia. ---
(69’) Deulofeu has been a constant bright spark for the visitors today but you have to give Cresswell tremendous credit for sticking manfully to his task all game. The injuries and substitutions have rather disrupted the flow of this match in the last few minutes. Let's hope there can be a grandstand finish to what has been an excellent game so far.
(67’) Valencia is stretched off the pitch and Zarate will look to make a match winning impact from the subs bench.
(65’) Slight delay in proceedings as Enner Valencia receives some treatment after a strong but perfectly fair challenge inside the Everton penalty box by Seamus Coleman. It doesn't look good for the Ecuadorian and I'm not sure he'll be able to continue. Mauro Zarate is preparing himself to enter the fray.
--- 64’ Substitution A. Koné is replaced with K. Mirallas. ---
(63’) SHOT! Lanzini drops his shoulder on the left wing and dips inside onto his favoured right foot. The winger has a crack and the ball flashes past Tim Howard's near post.
(61’) If the pattern of the game continues in this way you can't imagine it will be too long before Martinez freshens things up with a substitution or two. Kone has been very quiet in this second half. Deulofeu has been electric at times this afternoon but needs to see more of the ball.
--- 59’ Yellow card Ramiro Funes Mori is cautioned by the referee. ---
(59’) Moses yet again races down the right wing but it stopped in tracks by a wild tackle from Funes Mori who hacks him down and gives the referee no other option but to produce the yellow card.
(57’) Everton are trying to get a foothold in the game but they are being far too sloppy in possession at the moment. No sooner do they win it back do they give it away again. Martinez will want to see his players take far greater care on the ball.
(55’) West Ham cleverly work a corner short and it gives Victor Moses the chance to cut in onto his left foot from the right wing. Unfortunately, for the Hammers his shot goes out for a throw in. One to forget for Nigerian international there.
(53’) The half time interval seems to have come at the right time for West Ham who have regrouped well since the restart. Everton on the otherhand have rather struggled to regain their rhythm in the opening exchanges of the second half.
(51’) The introduction of Valencia hasn't immediately signalled a change of shape for West Ham, despite the fact that he would probably describe himself as a striker by trade. The Hammers are continuing with their preferred 4-2-3-1 formation and Valencia will play in behind Carroll for the time being at least.
--- 50’ Substitution D. Payet is done for the day. E. Valencia is his replacement. ---
(49’) Payet trudges off the field and goes straight down the tunnel and is replaced by Enner Valencia. The West Ham playmaker seemed to be struggling after being on the receiving end of a heavy tackle from McCarthy. That is a real blow to the home side as Payet has been so instrumental so far this season.
(47’) Concern amongst the West Ham faithful and management as Andy Carroll walks away rather gingerly after a coming together with Gareth Barry. Given his horrendous injury record in recent times, it is no wonder there is genuine worry everytime he goes down.
(45’) Everton get us going again. The Toffees will be kicking towards where their fans are situated in the second half.
It has been refreshing to watch such an open and exciting first half in the Premier League. Many matches these days are tight and tense affairs, particularly in the opening fourty-five minutes and things don't really start to open up until the last twenty minutes or so. Given the end-to-end nature of this encounter so far it is very difficult to call who'll come out on top.
It perhaps says a lot about the progress that has been made in recent years by both these sides, that both teams' substitutes benches look very strong indeed. Slaven Bilic has the likes of Zarate, Valencia, Jelavic and Antonio to call upon. While Roberto Martinez has some decent options of his own with Naismith, Mirallas, Osman and Lennon waiting in the wings.
It has been a thoroughly entertaining first fourty-minutes here in East London. Both teams have looked a lot better with the ball than without it. The attacking flair players for both sides have been at the forefront of this match thus far. More of the same in the second half please!
(45’) Half time here at Upton Park 1-1.
(45’) Now all of a sudden it is Everton who are playing with a swagger. West Ham have clearly been rattled by that equaliser. Kone and Deulofeu are popping up all over the place at the moment.
(45’) OVER! The Hammers look for an immediate response but Lanzini screws his right footed shot over the bar.
--- 43’ Assist The assist came from Deulofeu. ---
--- 43’ Goal! Payet gives it away in midfield and Deulofeu releases Lukaku through on goal with a simply wonderful through ball that splits the defence. Lukaku races onto it before rounding Adrian and tucking it into the back of the net with his trusty left foot. Game on! ---
(43’) 1-1! EVERTON equalise and it is Romelu Lukaku, who always scores against West Ham. Out of nowhere we are all square.
(41’) Almost half a chance for first Barkley and then Kone. The ball sat up invitingly about twenty yards out for the England international but surprisingly the Everton no.20 declined the opportunity to shoot and instead  tried to pick out his teammate.
(39’) The Toffees are looking fairly secure when the ball is in central areas but whenever the Irons get it wide to the likes of Moses and Lanzini they look vulnerable. From an Everton point of view it is imperative that they don't concede again before half time.
(37’) Barkley whips in a devillish delivery from a freekick on the right hand side for Everton. Kone flicks it towards goal but it is deflected out of play for a corner. Barkley also takes this set piece and Funes Mori climbs highest to connect with it but his header is off target.
(35’) McCarthy has become the first player to be cautioned this afternoon and it was a pretty easy decision for the referee. It was an over zealous tackle in  midfield on Payet. The Everton midfielder might argue that he won the ball but he went through the West Ham man to get it.
--- 34’ Yellow card J. McCarthy is yellow-carded. ---
(33’) West Ham tails are now well and truly up as they go in search of another goal. Moses nicks the ball from Galloway and tries to start an attack. The move ends up with Carroll getting his head to a Lanzini cross but he can't direct it on target.
--- 30’ Goal! The young winger opens the scoring with a superb side footed finish from the edge of the area on the half volley. Moses had fired the ball into the Everton area which was blocked by Stones but it fell invitingly for Lanzini who showed great composure to score his first goal at Upton Park. ---
(30’) GOAL 1-0 WEST HAM! Lanzini puts the home side in front!
(27’) It's now the turn of the away side to have a decent spell. Deulofeu shows great trickery to get past Cresswell before smashing the ball across goal. Adrian does very well to get down low and turn it away from danger with his foot.
(25’) SAVE! And it is a fairly straightforward one for Adrian from a Ross Barkley freekick. Victor Moses had rather needlessly handballed it about twenty-five yards from goal. It was a decent enough effort from Barkley but it would need to be something special to beat the West Ham 'keeper from that distance.
(23’) CHANCE! Payet crosses into the area inevitably looking for Carroll but it is overhit and the ball eventually drops to Cresswell who tries to bend a half volley into the top corner with his left foot but can't get quite enough swerve on his shot that curls wide.
(21’) West Ham are applying some sustained pressure at the moment but Everton are standing up to it well. Jenkinson and Cresswell are getting forward at every opportunity and the home side are really pinning their opponents back.
(19’) Moses runs directly at Galloway and is brought down after minimal contact from the Everton defender. Payet takes the resulting set piece which is kept alive at the back post by Tomkins but none of his teammates can react quickly enough to the knockdown and Everton can hack it away.
(17’) First of all Lanzini wriggles away from Coleman before dragging his shot wide. Everton immediately respond by launching a counter attack of their own which culminates in Kone slicing a shot wide when well placed at the top of the box. It's been a pretty open game so far.
(15’) OVER! West Ham work a freekick short before Cresswell whips in a lovely cross which is over the head of Carroll but is met by Moses. The winger on loan from Chelsea makes a good connection but can't keep his header down.
(13’) SAVE! Barkley turns sharply after the ball was fired into him by Galloway and lets fly with a snapshot from the edge of the area. Fortunately for Adrian in the West Ham goal it is straight at him.
(11’) The pace and movement of the Everton front four is giving the West Ham defence a few problems. They seem unsure whether they should get tight or just stand off. In truth they aren't really doing either and it is giving the likes of Kone, Barkley and Lukaku plenty of time and space.
(9’) Slaven Bilic will just want to see a little more patience from his players as Tomkins and Reid have both been guilty of going long a bit too early. With a target man like Andy Carroll to aim at it is always tempting for centre backs who are given too much time on the ball to take the easy option and lump it forward.
(7’) Gareth Barry and James McCarthy are just beginning to get on the ball and dictate proceedings from the middle of the park. Everton have settled down after West Ham looked lively in the opening five minutes or so.
(5’) Now it is Everton's turn to threaten as Kone races down the right wing before putting in a dangerous looking cross into the area that Adrian does well to tip away from Lukaku who was lurking menancingly in the penalty area.
(3’) SHOT! Payet drifts onto the right hand side and dances past a couple of challenges before teeing up Moses who hits a first time shot into the side netting. A bright and positive start for the Hammers.
(2’) West Ham are stroking the ball around confidently in these early moments  looking to give everyone an early touch. Everton are quite content to let the home side have it in their own half.
(1’) And we are underway! West Ham in their traditional claret and blue strip while Everton are in their away kit of white shirts, navy shorts and white socks.
Both sets of players are out on the pitch and kick off is not far away now. On this weekend of remembrance there will be a minute's silence before the start of the match.
Only one change to the Everton team that thrashed Sunderland last Sunday with Bryan Oviedo missing out through injury and he is replaced by Brendan Galloway at left back. As for the Hammers, Winston Reid is back in the fold and replaces the suspended James Collins. Angelo Ogbonna returns to the squad after injury and is named amongst the West Ham substitutes. Diafra Sakho is still unavailable with a thigh strain.
EVERTON SUBS: Joel, Gibson, Mirallas, Lennon, Naismith, Osman, Holgate.
WEST HAM SUBS: Randolph, Zarate, Valencia, Ogbonna, Jelavic, Antonio, Cullen.
EVERTON XI (4-2-3-1): Howard; Coleman, Funes Mori, Stones, Galloway; McCarthy, Barry (c); Deulofeu, Barkley, Kone; Lukaku.
WEST HAM XI (4-2-3-1): Adrian; Jenkinson, Reid, Tomkins, Cresswell; Kouyate, Noble (c); Lanzini, Payet, Moses; Carroll.
The team news is in and we'll start with our hosts West Ham United...
Although he has been trying to play it down in the build up to this match; this fixture must hold special significance to West Ham manager Slaven Bilic, who played for both clubs during his career. Both teams come into this game on the back of very different results last weekend. The Hammers were well short of their best as they suffered a disappointing 2-0 defeat away at Watford. While Everton on the other hand romped to a 6-2 victory at Goodison Park against a hapless Sunderland side.
Good afternoon and welcome along to the Boleyn Ground for this Premier League clash between West Ham United and Everton. I'm Chris Baker and I'll be describing all the action for you today. It promises to be a very exciting encounter here in East London.

FULL TIME! Chelsea fall to another league defeat, with Stoke defeating Mourinho's men by a scoreline of 1-0. Arnautovic's goal snatches three point for the Potters, with plenty more pressure piling onto the Blues. That's all that we have time for from the Britannia, I've been Simon Harrison and I will see you again next time!
(90’) Stoke lead a quick break upfield, with Terry able to step out and deny the Potters. Willian counters, with the Brazilian lining up a low drive! He clatters a terrible shot into a defender.
(90’) We're into four minutes of stoppage time, with Butland forced into another easy stop! The home fans are making plenty of noise, with Hughes' men about to defeat Chelsea once again this season.
--- 90’ Yellow card G. Johnson gets yellow. ---
(89’) Chelsea continue to push on, with Willian facing up Arnautovic down the right-hand side! Matic clips a cross into the penalty area, but Shawcross clears, with Stoke having a lot of red and white shirts in the box.
(87’) Good clearance from Terry! Arnautovic is released down the left, before whipping in a cross! The Englishman gets rid of the ball, allowing for a Chelsea break. Costa is fed into the penalty area, before Butland comes off his line to smother the loose ball.
(85’) Miss from Remy! The Frenchman is found by Costa, before he takes a touch around the advancing Butland! With the goal only guarded by Shawcross, the former Newcastle striker diverts a sliced effort wide of the right-hand post! That could have been given as a penalty, but the Frenchman did well to stay on his feet!
(83’) Butland is happy to take his time with his goal kicks now, with Stoke winding down the clock wherever possible. A win today would keep the Potters in the race for a top-half finish. The hosts work the ball to Walters at the back post, but the former Ipswich striker can only fire a terrible attempt high and wide of the target!
--- 82’ Substitution M. Diouf enters play, replacing X. Shaqiri. ---
(81’) We're into the final 10 minutes at the Britannia. Willian manages to slide a pass into Oscar, who causes havoc with a back-heel flick! Possession finds its way to Hazard at the back post, with the ex-Lille forward only able to guide a curling finish beyond the far upright!
--- 79’ Substitution C. Adam is done for the day. I. Afellay is his replacement. ---
(79’) Afellay is now thrown into the game in place of Adam, who has had a combative evening. The amount of substitutes is breaking up the flow of the contest. Chelsea are running out of time to come back into this fixture, with Mourinho set to be put under even heavier fire.
--- 77’ Substitution Ramires is done for the day. L. Rémy is his replacement. ---
(77’) Ramires combines with Willian, before the Brazilian switches possession inside to Matic. The ex-Benfica man lashes yet another speculative effort goalwards, but it hurtles into the stands. Remy is readied to come into the contest for the away outfit.
(75’) Only a quarter of an hour remains in this contest, with Stoke very close to yet another very positive result against Chelsea. Arnautovic finds Shaqiri on the right-hand side with a good switch of play, but the Swiss winger is unable to keep the heavy pass in play.
(73’) Ramires drives to the right byline, but the Brazil international is unable to keep the ball in play. Chelsea are piling the pressure on, but Stoke are weathering the storm! Diego Costa and Cameron clash in the hosts' penalty area, but the latter wins the free kick. The Spaniard is more bothered about being physical than playing football, at times.
--- 71’ Substitution G. Cameron enters the game and replaces Bojan. ---
(71’) A few changes are made, with Cameron coming into the game in place of Bojan for the hosts. While that may be perceived as a negative switch, Oscar and Fabregas come into the contest for Pedro and Baba for Chelsea. The Blues are searching for at least a share of the spoils at all costs.
--- 70’ Substitution Fàbregas enters play, replacing Pedro. ---
--- 70’ Substitution A. Baba is done for the day. Oscar is his replacement. ---
(69’) Ramires goes down on the edge of the box, but the referee waves play on! Chelsea aren't getting any decisions their way at the moment, with Pieters being very physical against the diminutive likes of Pedro and Hazard. Fabregas is being readied for the visitors, with Mourinho's men needing some inspiration desperately.
(67’) Chelsea are now able to take advantage of a stretched game, with Hazard slid through one-on-one against Adam! The Belgian sets back a pass, before Pedro is picked out on the edge of the penalty area by Willian! The ex-Barca winger sends a dipping shot onto the foot of the left post! So close!
(65’) Stoke counter at pace down the right-hand side, with Shaqiri able to get the wrong side of Baba! The Swiss winger delivers a teasing cross towards the near post, but Arnautovic can only send a glancing header over the bar! Close for the Potters!
(63’) Terrible cross from Pieters! The Dutchman is fed down the left flank, before sending a ball sailing terribly over the danger zone! Stoke are happy to limit themselves to the odd foray forward, with the Blues being asked to push on and attack against two organised banks of players.
(61’) We're into the final half an hour, with Chelsea pushing for an equaliser! Hazard drives towards the edge of the penalty area, before lashing a venomous attempt just over the crossbar! Butland remains relatively untested.
(59’) Willian and Arnautovic are separated after an altercation, with both sides needing to keep their cool. The goalscorer was blocked off by the ex-Shakhtar man, leading to an angry reaction from the Chelsea winger. The referee does well to keep a lid on things.
--- 57’ Yellow card R. Shawcross goes into the referee's book. ---
(57’) Shawcross dumps Costa on the turf, with the England international getting a yellow card for his trouble. The Spaniard is definitely getting as good as he gives this evening. Willian whips in a delivery, but is fails to beat the first man! Disappointing from the Brazilian.
(55’) Chelsea's bench is suddenly very active, with the visitors needing to now come up with two goals from somewhere. Matic unleashes a ferocious effort from around 25 yards out, but the Serbia international can only thump a shot straight at Butland!
--- 53’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! ARNAUTOVIC MAKES IT 1-0! The Austria international puts the hosts in the lead! A cross is swung in from the right-hand side, with the ball sailing towards the back post. Johnson delivers, with the ex-Werder Bremen turning home an acrobatic finish! ---
(52’) Costa drives his way beyond two challenges brilliantly, before throwing himself to the turf! The official waves away his claims of a foul, with the Spain international looking to dramatically win Chelsea a free kick.
(50’) Adam and Walters try to combine with a one-two, but the former is penalised for shoving Matic. The former Blackpool midfielder protests, with the referee giving him a warning. Chelsea press on from the free kick, but a through ball for Costa skids through to Butland!
(48’) Adam whips in a cross from the right-hand side, but Walters fails to get anywhere near it. Hughes is prowling around his penalty area, with the Potters needing to step their game up. Shaqiri goes on yet another dangerous, driving run, but the Swiss international is unable to find a killer pass.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Britannia! This game is very delicately poised, with Mourinho watching on. Chelsea need three points to push themselves up the table, in order to relieve the pressure on their Portuguese coach.
HALF TIME! The hosts hold onto a 0-0 stalemate at the break, with Chelsea unable to find a breakthough! Diego Costa has gone close on a couple of occasions, with Butland making one top save to deny Ramires. The Blues have had plenty of free kicks and corners, but haven't been able to make their pressure count.
(45’) Hazard is picked out on the edge of the penalty area, before Chelsea move the ball from right to left! Matic tries to clip a lofted pass to the back post, but gets his angles entirely wrong. For all of their possession, the visitors have been unable to offer any kind of killer instinct in the final third!
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card A. Baba gets yellow. ---
(45’) We're into the first of four minutes of stoppage time.
--- 44’ Yellow card G. Whelan gets yellow. ---
(44’) Stoke have to put up with yet another free-kick delivery being pinged into the box by Willian, but Matic is caught in an offside position. Chelsea have failed to take advantage of a huge amount of dead-ball opportunities during this first half.
(42’) Bojan leads the charge for the Potters, with the Spaniard able to win a throw in high upfield. Walters tries to combine with Arnautovic, but a flick from the former is woefully inaccurate. The Irishman has offered next to nothing up top for Hughes' men.
(40’) Five minutes remain of the first half, with Chelsea continuing to see much more of the ball. Pedro and Diego Costa combine well yet again, with the latter being found by the former with a neat back-heel flick! The ex-Real Valladolid striker drives into the penalty area, before forcing Butland to make a save with his legs!
(38’) Mourinho's staff are deep in conversation on the bench, with Chelsea certainly not putting in a terrible performance this evening. The Blues are countering with intent, winning plenty of corners from the likes of Pieters and Wollscheid. Costa hasn't necessarily been given enough space to test Butland, but the Spain international is dragging the away outfit constantly upfield.
(36’) Diego Costa drives menacingly forward, with a Chelsea attack resulting in Pedro being tackled well by Shawcross. Moments later, the ex-Atletico Madrid striker allows for Matic to be given possession, but a cut-back from the former Benfica midfielder is intercepted by Adam.
(34’) Ramires is fed down the right channel, but the Brazilian is denied by a sliding tackle from Pieters. The Dutchman's nose looks to be bleeding slightly again, but the Stoke defender won't be put off. Chelsea earn themselves yet another corner as a result, but nothing comes of it. Zouma heads wide.
(32’) Diego Costa manages to win a corner on the right byline, before Terry is warned by the referee for his jostling with Terry. The set piece is taken short, before Hazard sees a powerful shot blocked by a ruck of bodies inside the penalty box!
(30’) Chelsea have had much more of the ball thus far, but Stoke are creating their fair share of opportunities. Only a quarter of an hour remains in the first half, but there will be an extended period of stoppage time due to Pieters' injury.
(28’) Shaqiri beats Baba yet again, before Adam sees a shot charged down on the edge of the box! The rebound falls back to the Swiss international, who whips a dangerous cross to the back post! Arnautovic rises well, but the Austrian can only send a bullet header above the crossbar! Stoke are getting closer.
(26’) Shaqiri is picked out on the periphery of the penalty area by a hopeful cross, but the Swiss winger can only nod a tame header well wide of the target! Half chances galore at the Britannia, but both defences and goalkeepers are equal to the test. Costa is found at the back post by a low delivery from Hazard, but the Spaniard can't quite make contact!
(24’) Zouma goes close! Willian whips a free-kick delivery in from the left flank, with the ex-St Etienne defender stretching to make goalscoring contact at the back post! Fortunately for Stoke, the France international both misses the target and is caught narrowly offside by the linesman's flag!
(22’) Chelsea look to break down the left, before Ramires is picked out on the edge of the box! The ball sits up nicely for the ex-Benfica midfielder, who managed to dip a dangerous half volley goalwards! Butland gets up excellently to tip a strong save over the crossbar! The resulting corner is well cleared.
(20’) Pieters is expected to be continuing here with a broken nose, but the Dutchman hasn't been tested at all by Pedro. The Netherlands defender heads clear yet another clearance, with Chelsea's front three being kept extremely quiet. Butland has had nothing to do as of yet.
(18’) Begovic is forced into a neat save, before Stoke threaten again through Bojan. The ex-Barcelona midfielder shifts a pass inside to Johnson, but the right-back can only wriggle into a pocket of space before losing out to Zouma! The home fans respond to a good spell of pressure from the Potters.
(16’) Hazard is found making tracks down the left-hand side, but the ex-Lille man can't turn a first-time finish home at the back post! Chelsea are starting to retain possession well, with Stoke dropping back in numbers. A long ball forward in search of Diego Costa is gathered up with ease by Butland!
(14’) Shaqiri manages to win a free kick on the right-hand side, with the eventual dead-ball delivery being headed behind by Zouma. Stoke win a corner as a result, but the cross into the box doesn't even beat the first man. The Blues counter, but the move ends in Ramires firing a long way wide of the target from just inside the area!
(12’) Play finally gets back underway, after extensive treatment for Pieters. The Netherlands international looks to be fine to continue, but will need to change his shirt after bleeding heavily from his face. Not an ideal start at the Britannia, with the game failing to get the chance to get flowing.
(10’) Pieters appears to have a heavy nosebleed, with Wilson being forced to warm up immediately. The Dutchman was caught square in the face by Pedro, with the aforementioned Irishman looking to be the replacement should a change need to be made.
(8’) Shaqiri manages to wriggle around from Baba down the right-hand side, with the ex-Augsburg defender getting caught out! The former Bayern winger whips a cross in from out wide, but the delivery loops over Walters and to safety. There's a brief break in play, as Pieters is treated for catching a boot to the face from Pedro.
(6’) Diego Costa lashes out slightly at Shawcross, with the Spain international already doing his fair share of messing around. That battle could prove key throughout the fixture. Chelsea win themselves a corner on the right flank, but Butland and the aforementioned English defender combine to clear the Potters' lines.
(4’) Over the bar from Pedro! The Spaniard is found out on the right-hand side, before lashing an awful attempt high and wide from a very tight angle. Both goalkeepers are yet to be tested, with nerves evident at the start of this contest. Chelsea are in real need of a positive result.
(2’) Over from Shaqiri! The Switzerland international tries his luck with an over-head kick effort from 15 yards out, but can't hit the target! Moments later, Walters goes down while jostling with Zouma, but the Stoke forward is penalised for bumping into the physical Frenchman.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! The hosts are wearing their customary red and white, with Chelsea in their own home strip of blue. After a minute's Remembrance silence, the football begins.
Chelsea substitutes: Fabregas, Oscar, Mikel, Kenedy, Remy, Cahill, Amelia.
Chelsea starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Begovic; Azpilicueta, Zouma, Terry, Baba; Ramires, Matic; Pedro, Willian, Hazard; Diego Costa.
Stoke substitutes: Ireland, Wilson, Afellay, Diouf, Cameron, Crouch, Haugaard.
Stoke starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Butland; Johnson, Shawcross, Wollscheid, Pieters; Adam, Whelan; Shaqiri, Bojan, Arnautovic; Walters.
TEAM NEWS: Asmir Begovic starts in between the sticks against his former club, with Kurt Zouma chosen to partner John Terry in the heart of the defence. Spurs have won just once in their last 22 visits to play Arsenal, with 13 defeats in that stretch. That match was a 3-2 win in 2010, where the Gunners threw away the game by surrendering a two-goal advantage. However, Tottenham lost only two of their last 10 matches away from White Hart Lane in the league - but face a team that have taken 13 W's from their previous 18 outings at tonight's venue.
Spurs themselves are on a fine run of form in the league. After losing their opening-day fixture against Manchester United, they have gone unbeaten in the top flight, including winning five of their last seven games. They also sit atop their Europa League group after the opening four matchdays, with seven points, one ahead of second-place Monaco. Both teams are flying high in the Premier League, making this one even more of a must-see than usual.

But whatever their form elsewhere, in the Premier League, the Gunners have been on fire. They sit level with league-leading Manchester City on 25 points and, along with Manchester United, boast the division's best defence with only eight goals conceded from 11 games.

Stoke, meanwhile, showed flashes of promise but not enough consistency, and need a better gameplan up front to make use of their pacey, tricky wingers. Thank you for joining us here!
Newcastle played very well but will be angry that they didn't score, with Butland utterly superb in the second half. --- 90’ Substitution P. Crouch enters the game and replaces X. Shaqiri. ---

(84’) Butland with another great save! Sissoko gets the ball on the edge of the box, fakes a shot, dribbles in, and then fires a rifle onto the net that the goalie parries out for a corner!
--- 83’ Substitution D. Janmaat is replaced with J. Lascelles. ---

(81’) It's all Stoke right now, with Shaqiri beautifully lifting the ball over the defence for Walters, who fires his shot far too high from a close range, yet a poor angle!
(80’) Shaqiri slips the ball to the onrushing Arnautovic in the box, with the latter trying to cut it back for a shot on goal but the ball is cleared!
(79’) Mitrovic swings it into the box but Butland rises high to punch it clear. Elliot thinks he's cleared the danger on the other end but Stoke soon pounce and have the ball outside of the box, losing it after a very foolish pass across field from Johnson to no one in particular.
(77’) Arnautovic goes in very hard on Janmaat on the sideline outside of Stoke's box and the flag goes up almost immediately. The former Inter man avoids a booking, but his team now has to defend a set-piece in a great area.

(73’) Peiters holds onto Mitrovic, conceding a free-kick, which the striker tries to get on the end of. Shawcross has his arm out to prevent the Newcastle player from getting forward, and he goes down in the box, but no call is made!
(72’) NEARLY FOR MITROVIC... HE WAS OFFSIDE ANYWAY! Wijnaldum gets from box to box to send a cross towards the striker; not realizing he's offside, he rounds Butland and tries a deft finish, but Pieters slides to make the stop anyway!
--- 71’ Substitution Tiote comes off after a decent showing in the midfield for De Jong, but it's Newcastle who are on the backfoot after the substitute, with Stoke captalizing on a poor ball and it takes Wijnaldum tracking back to stop that! ---
(70’) Stoke keep trying to play a similar kind of ball into the box, looking for an incisive cross that swings past the defence but finds Walters, and so far it has not paid dividends. With 20 minutes left here, there's all to play for!

(65’) Tiote loses the ball in midfield, finally giving Stoke a chance to maintain the ball. Afellay works it wide, going out to Shaqiri, who dinks a ball into Arnautovic that Coloccini stretches to clear!
(64’) It's Perez again who is just uncontainable this half, getting to the byline and slipping a cross into the box that Stoke struggle to clear. Mitrovic is soon in the middle of another tussle, pushing Johnson down, but avoids a second booking - though he certainly needs to be careful now!
--- 63’ Yellow card A. Mitrović receives a yellow card. ---
--- 63’ Yellow card Wollscheid and Mitrovic are both booked! He went face-to-face with Mitrovic after the ball went out, with both players wanting it. The Newcastle man made a meal of it, after pushing the centre-back, and Wollscheid retaliated by pushing him with his chest! ---

(61’) Newcastle now are estabishing themselves more as a calmer, dominant side. They've gone close a few times now through Perez and are building up from the back confidently.

(58’) Adam gets his pocket picked and Newcastle counter ferociously, which ends with yet another Perez shot that Butland powerfully pushes out for a corner!
(57’) The half looks to finally be settling into a tighter kind of affair, with the midfields now getting packed and busy. Neither side is holding onto the ball well, with some errant passes and over-eager through balls up to strikers.
(55’) A corner for Newcastle comes to nothing, though a few strikers and centre-backs were flirting to scoring a goal. Unlike the first half, when both sides weren't really testing the keepers, both keepers have been very busy thus far here!
(53’) Another great counter from Stoke but Elliot is once again equal to the task, launching a great counter that Sissoko breaks free down the middle to get to an nearly slides it into the net! This game has really come alive and both sides are so, so close to scoring!
(51’) Walters leads a counter superbly for Stoke, crossing it wide for a delivery to be returned to him and his header forces Elliot into a low save! That was a powerful header and equal to Wijnaldum's effort just moments before!
(49’) Wijnaldum wins a free-kick just outside of Stoke's box and then takes it, delivering an excellent strike that nearly dips in under the upright but drawing a superb save out of Butland!
(48’) Ayoze gets the ball just outside the box, dribbles into it, and then unleashes a curling shot that goes just wide of the far post! That was very, very good and nearly broke the deadlock here!

McClaren will want a little more from his men; though they've hit the crossbar, they've conceded a lot of the intitiative to the visitors, and they despreately need the points to rise out of the relegation zone.
(45’) And not a second of extra-time is given: that's the half! It's been fairly entertaining, with lots of half chances but nothing that's truly tested the keepers.
(44’) Anita runs through the back of Bojan and suddenly Stoke have a free-kick on the left wing, that Shaqiri whips into the box. It's cleared, but only to Johnson, who tries another cross that Wollscheid can't get to!
(42’) After a while of being pegged back in their own half, Newcastle have the ball and try to build something here. Tiote tries a cross into the box that's blocked, and soon it's back with Stoke, who are doing everything with more ease than the homeside are now.

(37’) Perez and Mitrovic combine well on the edge of the box, with the former trying to dribble and juke his way inside - he goes down, and the fans are angry, but once again Referee East does not blow the whistle.
(35’) Frustrated with the sea of black and white in front of him, Adam tries a long range effort from distance - and why not, given his track record with those, as evidenced by his stirke against Chelsea last season - but it sails harmlessly over the bar.
(34’) Mitrovic has the ball deep in Stoke's box following a counter but his attempt to cut it back across the face of goal is cleared by Wollscheid!
(33’) Newcastle have a corner now, which is played by Ayoze into the middle of the box, taking a bounce before being cleared. Stoke try to counter, but Shaqiri has to go deeper in his half before playing it back out wide. Bojan runs into Dummett in the box and loses his footing, but doesn't appeal for a penalty.
(32’) Still the visitors on the ball here at the moment. They really aren't playing like the stereotypical away team; this Stoke side are not set up to defend and counter, but seem to like playing on the front foot and building up their goals well.
(30’) Stoke don't let that moment rattle them and are keeping the ball well now. The wide forwards are tucking inside to help the midfield gain some width as needed when Newcastle are flooding the middle of the pitch.
(28’) MITROVIC OFF THE UPRIGHT! An excellent cross from Tiote is played in perfectly for the stirker, who nods it onto upright. It bounces around Butland a few times before he can gather it!
(27’) Stoke on the ball now, with Walters fighting the centre-backs to get on the end of the ball and spray it wide. (25’) Mitrovic is offside again as another high ball is played in, with Johnson stepping up just at the right time to ensure that the striker wasn't clear through on net.
(23’) Stoke's turn to be offside now, with Adam playing a great ball over the top of the Newcastle defence, but Walters is too eager to get there and the flag is soon up.

(4’) Stoke's gameplan here looks to be to counter quickly as Newcastle stranglehold the ball, but when the home side lose the ball, it's all too easy for the Potters to work their way down the flank.
(2’) After a frantic minute, Newcastle are settling the ball, before Janmaat sends a high ball down the flank which Sissoko can't get to. Stoke are in no rush to take the ensuing throw-in, which is played to the Newcastle backline. Coloccini heads it clear.

We're just moments away from the kick-off now!

(78’) Leicester under real pressure here, with Palace lumping cross after cross into the box. Sako puts in another inviting delivery, but it sails just over Dann’s head and goes out for a goal kick.

The end of a jam-packed first half at Upton Park. Even with Zarate's opener, it seemed like a fairly low-key London derby, but that all changed in the last 10 minutes of the half. Great chances at either end, a narrowly disallowed goal for Chelsea and Matic's sending off for a second bookable offence has sent the home fans into delirium and Mourinho into further strife. Can the champs recover in the second half? Stay tuned to find out.
(45’) Fabregas and Terry led the complaints for Chelsea, and have been booked for their protests. What's more, a member of the Blues backroom staff has been sent off for complaining! Mourinho has something of a resigned look on his face.
--- 45’ Yellow card Diego Costa gets yellow. ---
