(86’) AND SUNDERLAND MAKE IT 3-0!!! It's definitely all over now as Steven Fletcher wraps things up with an excellent volley from M'Vila's left-wing cross at the end of a Sunderland counter.
(85’) Newcastle commit a foul at the subsequent corner. It's been a day of frustration for those on Tyneside.
(84’) Dangerous low ball from Janmaat but Sunderland survive again as Younes Kaboul clears the danger.
--- 82’ Substitution J. Lens is replaced with S. Larsson. ---
(82’) Sunderland make their final change as Sebastian Larsson replaces Jeremain Lens.
(81’) Newcastle, despite being a man down, have not lacked ambition. However, their efforts remain fruitless as Thauvin shoots wide from the edge of the area.
(79’) Newcastle have thrown on Florian Thauvin in a late bid to claw their way back into the game. Can he make a decisive impact?
--- 78’ Substitution F. Thauvin enters play, replacing P. Dummett. ---
(77’) And as I say that Mitrovic heads wide after good work from Janmaat down the right. Aside from the red card, a lack of cutting edge has been Newcastle's main issue.
(76’) Only 14 minutes for Newcastle to salvage something from this game. It's looking very, very unlikely.
(74’) Newcastle win a corner, it isn't properly cleared but Anita's effort is miles over the top.
(72’) JOHNSON RATTLES THE CROSSBAR!! The former Manchester City winger cuts in from the right and launches an effort with his left foot than cannons off the woodwork.
(70’) Excellent save from Pantilimon. Wijnaldum lashes one towards goal at the near post but Pantilimon produces a fine low save to prevent Newcastle from halving the deficit.
(69’) Anita misplaces a pass to predictable ironic cheers from the Sunderland fans. It's turning into a miserable day for Newcastle.
(67’) It's a long, long way back for Newcastle now. The Sunderland fans are understandably delirious, their team is on course for a sixth derby win in a row.
--- 65’ Assist Assist by Y. M'Vila. ---
--- 65’ Goal! AND THEY TAKE IT! Newcastle fail to deal with the corner, which is volleyed into the path of Billy Jones by Yann M'Vila, with the former West Brom defender making it 2-0 from point-blank range. ---
(64’) FLETCHER HITS ONE and it's deflected over. Sunderland win a corner and have an opportunity to put themselves in command.
(62’) Free-kick for Sunderland as Janmaat is penalised for handball, a touch of irony in that one after the referee's earlier decision not to give Newcastle a penalty for the same infraction.
(60’) We've reached the hour mark and Newcastle have 30 minutes plus any stoppages to avoid another derby defeat to their arch rivals. To their credit, they've conducted themselves well with 10 men.
(58’) Cattermole fouls Perez on the edge of the area, the midfielder receives a final warning from referee Madley, who has quickly become the story in this game.
(56’) Now Perez surges through the heart of the Sunderland midfield and hits one from range, this time it's more comfortable for Pantilimon, but this game is far from over.
(54’) GREAT SAVE FROM PANTILIMON! Newcastle work the ball to Mitrovic at the far post, he cuts inside onto his right foot but Pantilimon makes himself big and pulls off an excellent close-range stop.
(53’) Sunderland pushing for a second but Defoe's effort from the edge of the area. Newcastle, save for Coloccini's shoulder barge of Fletcher, have defended well today.
(51’) Steven Fletcher attempts to make hay down the left but Chancel Mbemba is having none of it and muscles him off the ball and wins a goal-kick for Newcastle.
(50’) Sunderland unsurprisingly moving the ball about with more and zip and confidence now. They have an excellent opportunity to put this game to bed.
--- 49’ Substitution J. Colback is replaced with V. Anita. ---
(49’) Colback's race is run and Vurnon Anita comes on in his place.
(48’) Colback is helped off the field so Newcastle are temporarily down to nine men.
(47’) Now more problems for Newcastle as Colback is down following a heavy challenge from Cattermole.
--- 46’ Substitution J. Lascelles enters play, replacing C. Tioté. ---
(46’) Newcastle make a change at half-time, with Jamaal Lascelles taking the place of Coloccini, with Tiote - who had been booked - making way.
Replays suggest Newcastle have a case that a penalty should have been given at the other end as Lee Cattermole looked to handle in the area moments before the decision that has turned the game on its head, can Newcastle mount a recovery in the second half?
Half-time, Steve McClaren is absolutely apoplectic with rage at referee Madley. Newcastle have been by far the better team and now have to play the second 45 minutes a goal down and a man down.
--- 45’ +3 Yellow card J. Colback receives a yellow card. ---
--- 45’ +3 Goal! Adam Johnson steps up... AND SCORES! Rob Elliot goes the right way but the winger's effort is powerful enough to nestle in the bottom right-corner. Euphoria at the Stadium of the Light and Johnson runs all the way to the other end of the pitch to celebrate in front of the Newcastle fans. ---
--- 45’ +1 Red card! After being on the back foot for all of the first half, Sunderland now have a chance to take the lead and will play a man up for the rest of the game after Coloccini barges over Fletcher in the box. ---
(45’) PENALTY TO SUNDERLAND! AND COLOCCINI SENT OFF!
(45’) Sunderland clear the resulting corner and the one that follows. Newcastle still piling the pressure on, though.
(44’) Tipped over by Pantilimon! Wijnaldum's curling effort is a good one, but the Romanian goalkeeper is equal to it.
(43’) And now a free-kick right on the edge of the area following a bad foul from Coates on Wijnaldum. Big opportunity for Newcastle here..
(41’) Free-kick for Newcastle in a dangerous area after Lee Cattermole fouls Perez.
(39’) Sunderland doing a bit of pressing here late in the half. Can they make Newcastle pay for their profligacy?
(38’) Superb build-up play from Perez but Mitrovic cannot latch on to his cross as the Serbian is well marshaled by Coates.
--- 37’ Substitution S. Coates enters the game and replaces J. O'Shea. ---
--- 36’ Substitution J. Defoe enters play, replacing O. Toivonen. ---
(36’) Jermain Defoe, the hero of last season's corresponding fixture, is on for the injured Toivonen. Now John O'Shea looks to be in some distress and is replaced by Sebastian Coates.
(34’) Toivonen looks to be struggling significantly. Worrying times for a Sunderland team that has looked second best by some margin.
(33’) PEREZ! The Spaniard can't quite find a telling touch from Sissoko's near-post cross and Sunderland eventually clear their lines. Big chance for Newcastle. Meanwhile, Ola Toivonen is down for Sunderland.
(31’) Sunderland getting some respite as the game is just calming down a touch in the final 15 minutes of the half. Can Newcastle get their reward for an impressive start?
(29’) Sunderland really struggling to keep possession whenever they get the ball near the Newcastle half. It has been one-way traffic so far and Newcastle need to make their dominance count.
(27’) Excellent play from Newcastle. First Janmaat lofts a perfectly weighted pass into the path of Colback, whose shot is turned behind by Pantilimon, before Mitrovic shoots wide from the resulting corner.
(25’) Dangerous cross into the Newcastle box, but Paul Dummett does very well to win the header and clear.
(24’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have had 70 per cent of the possession so far, but Coloccini's early effort remains the best chance of the game.
(22’) Lens receives a cautionary word from referee Robert Madley after catching Colback late, Newcastle free-kick in their own half.
(21’) Jeremain Lens' whips in a cross to the far post but it is much too strong for Johnson, who fails to keep the ball in play.
(20’) Sunderland win a throw-in deep in the Newcastle half, it's thrown long into the box but the visitors clear and manage to break again.
(18’) COLBACK GOES CLOSE! The midfielder almost scores against his former club but his low effort from the edge of the area is deflected wide by team-mate Mitrovic.
(16’) Neat link-up play from Mitrovic and Georginio Wijnaldum, whose tame effort from the edge of the area is comfortably saved by Pantilimon.
--- 14’ Yellow card C. Tioté is cautioned by the referee. ---
(14’) Tiote then fouls Yann M'Vila and is promptly booked.
(13’) Cheick Tiote is getting a bit of a talking to from the referee for a late challenge on Johnson, a tackle fitting of the occasion.
(12’) A first real bit of pressure from Sunderland but Newcastle easily clear Adam Johnson's cross and are able to break quickly, with Aleksandar Mitrovic heading wide from Daryl Janmaat's right-wing cross.
(10’) Steve McClaren's men have the ball in the Sunderland half again but Colback misplaces a pass and the ball goes out of play.
(8’) Newcastle having all of the ball and seem just happy to keep it at the minute. The Sunderland fans are beginning to get a bit restless.
(6’) Sunderland clear back-to-back corners with little difficulty, but the hosts have yet to really get a grip on the game.
(5’) An excellent surging run from Moussa Sissoko wins a corner for Newcastle. Good start from the visitors.
(3’) First chance for Newcastle! Jack Colback's free-kick is a good one and find its way to Fabricio Coloccini, whose acrobatic bicycle kick is turned away by Costel Pantilimon.
(2’) Newcastle start on the front foot and win a free-kick in a good area on the right.
(1’) Pre-match formalities completed and we are underway!
The teams emerge from the tunnel to a predictable cacophony of noise.
We're just five minutes away from kick-off at the Stadium of Light, who will take the bragging rights this time around?

Newcastle: Elliot; Janmaat, Mbemba, Coloccini, Dummett; Sissoko, Tiote, Colback, Wijnaldum; Perez, Mitrovic.

Meanwhile Sunderland were beaten 1-0 by West Brom in their last game but once again go into a derby match with a new manager, Sam Allardyce, in their second game in charge for the fourth time. The Wearsiders have won all three of the previous matches where that has been the case.
The two teams meet at the Stadium of Light with both mired in the relegation zone, although Newcastle are coming off a 6-2 victory over Norwich City last weekend.

Matt Ritchie got Bournemouth off to the perfect start with a goal inside the opening minute but it all went downhill from there for the struggling south coast outfit, who haven't won in their last four Premier League games now.
Harry Kane scores a hat-trick as Spurs hit Bournemouth for five in a comfortable win at the Vitality Stadium. Mousa Dembele and Erik Lamela were also on the scoresheet for Tottenham as Artur Boruc has a nightmare between the sticks for the hosts.
FULL TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-5 TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR
(89’) Bournemouth are having their best spell of possession for the last 20 minutes or so at the moment as Francis looks for passing options from the right-hand side for the struggling hosts.
(87’) Rose plays a clipped ball over the top of Cook towards an onrushing Alli but the as the Spurs midfielder tries to get the ball down from the air, Distin makes a clearance for the hosts.
--- 85’ Substitution Pochettino makes his third and final change of the match as he takes of man of the match Kane for N'Jie late on. The former has been absolutely excellent from the first minute today. ---
(85’) N'Jie runs through on goal but gets held up slightly as Cook recovers. The former Lyon striker cuts inside and then powers a shot towards the bottom corner, but Boruc makes a good save.
(83’) Howe cuts a frustrated figure on the touchline as Spurs continue to have the lion's share of the ball at the moment. The hosts have woeful at the back this afternoon and have barely had a kick in the last 10 minutes or so.
--- 82’ Substitution Pochettino makes his second change of the match for Tottenham as he takes off Trippier and brings on Walker in a right-back swap for the visitors, as we approach the final minutes of normal time. ---
(81’) Spurs have gone about their business in the second half really well and are seeing the game out now. They don't appear to have any desire to go on and score a sixth at the moment.
(79’) It looks as though Pochettino is about to make his second change of the game as Tripper gets stripped and ready to come on in the next couple of minutes for Tottenham.
(77’) Spurs substitute Mason receives the ball in the centre of the pitch and tries to feed it through to Kane, but the pass carries too much weight as it runs all the way back to Boruc.
--- 75’ Substitution Howe makes his third and final change for Bournemouth as he takes off Smith and brings on Pugh in the dying minutes here at the Vitality Stadium. The former played okay but his influence faded for the hosts. ---
(75’) Daniels drives forward for Bournemouth late on but Alderweireld gets in the way and clears the danger. The hosts' left-back, alongside Ritchie, has played well today but their contributions may get ignored in tomorrow's newspapers.
(73’) Ritchie tries to play a one-two with O'Kane but as the Bournemouth winger attempts to get on the end of the reverse pass, Rose gets his body in the way and falls down under the slightest of touches for a free-kick.
(71’) NO PENALTY! Boruc yet again drops the ball inside the six-yard box towards Kane and as he hopelessly tries to reclaim it, the Spurs man falls down inside the box. The referee waves away his appeals for another spot-kick, though.
(69’) Tottenham are conserving energy by knocking the ball around amongst themselves now. They haven't had to work hard to score five goals this afternoon, though. It's becoming awful to watch as a Bournemouth fan.
--- 68’ Substitution Howe makes his second change of the game as he takes off Murray and hands Kermorgant some playing time. You feel they need defenders on, if anything, as damage limitation. ---
--- 68’ Substitution Pochettino makes his first change of the game for Spurs as Dembele comes off for Mason in a like-for-like swap. The points are in the bag for the visitors now and it's a case of giving others a chance to impress in the closing stages. ---
(67’) OFF THE WOODWORK! Alli carries the ball forward superbly and slips it back to Eriksen, who hits a dipping effort towards goal and it strikes the post from distance. So unlucky.
(65’) CLOSE! Ritchie, perhaps the only Bournemouth player who will come away from today pleased with his display, drives a shot towards goal which Lloris saves brillianty, as it takes a slight nick off Alli on the way towards him.
--- 63’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAAAALLL!! It's a hat-trick for Kane! Boruc spills Eriksen's corner right into the path of Kane, who taps home with aplomb. The Bournemouth goalkeeper has had a nightmare between the posts this afternoon. ---
(62’) SAVE! Dier receives a good pass from Walker and touches the ball into the path of Kane who strikes the ball powerfully towards Boruc, who parries behind for a corner to Tottenham.
--- 61’ Substitution Howe makes his first change of the game as he takes off King, who hit the post in the first half, as O'Kane runs onto the field of play as his replacement. Murray will be pushed further forward now. ---
(60’) 'You're going down with the Chelsea' sounds around the Vitality Stadium as the Spurs supporters continue to enjoy their afternoon in the sunshine. Tottenham are totally in cruise control at the moment.
(58’) Cook clears a Rose cross to Daniels and the Bournemouth left-back, who has been his side's best defender by a country mile today, feeds a pass towards King but Alderweireld quashes the danger.
--- 56’ Assist The assist came from C. Eriksen. ---
--- 56’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!! It's 1-4 to Spurs! Eriksen gets given too much space inside Bournemouth's half as he spins a delightful pass in behind Distin towards Kane, who guides the ball past Boruc superbly. ---
(54’) Ritchie sees his cross towards Murray take a slight deflection on the way through and that leads to the ball flying up into the air towards Pugh, but Walker gets above him and clears well.
(52’) OH DEAR! Boruc almost makes his third mistake leading to a goal this afternoon as he drives his clearance straight into Dembele, and the ball just about trickles away from going into the back of the net.
(50’) Walker bursts down the right-hand side towards Distin but the Bournemouth centre-back keeps up with him excellently, and gets a foot in to push the ball behind for a throw-in.
(48’) Pugh gets forced back away from goal by Walker but the referee awards the Bournemouth man a free-kick. The ball curls in towards Murray but Alli heads away the danger for Spurs.
(46’) Welcome back! Tottenham get us back under way here at the Vitality Stadium with neither side making a personnel change during the half-time interval on the south coast.
Boruc has been so poor between the sticks for Bournemouth so far. After bringing down Kane for Spurs' first goal from the penalty spot, he dropped the ball straight into the path of Lamela to tap home for the visitors' third. Dembele scored in between those two strikes after the ball kindly fell into his path from a long-range drive by Rose.
What a turnaround in the first half. Bournemouth started the opening period amazingly well, scoring just minutes into the game through Ritchie, and Spurs couldn't cope with their intensity. But Spurs have since got on top after Kane got them up and running from the spot.
HALF TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-3 TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR
(45’) ALMOST A SECOND! Pugh sees his effort from a great cross by Ritchie get cleared off the line by Alderweireld, before King strikes the post seconds later from Daniels' low ball in.
(45’) The fourth official indicates that two minutes are being added on to the second half. Bournemouth are in possession and are pushing for another goal before the break.
(43’) Lamela receives the ball centrally deep inside Bournemouth's half and sprays a pass over the top towards an onrushing Eriksen, but it takes a slight nick off a defender and goes out for a corner to the visitors.
(41’) Kane works hard for the team as he tracks back to nick the ball away from Ritchie down the flank. The Spurs striker gets back up gingerly, though, which might be something for Pochettino to look at during the half-time interval.
(39’) Tottenham are popping the ball around with an apparent ease at the moment as they're clearly in the ascendancy in the first half. Bournemouth have been forced to try and counter-attack now.
(37’) King puts heaps of pressure on Lloris as the Frenchman receives a back pass from Alderweireld and shifts the ball from right to left before clearing, to the nervousness of his team-mates.
(35’) Much talk before this afternoon's game was about Bournemouth's injuries costing them, but that hasn't been the problem today. Going forward they look sharp but they simply cannot defend well enough. Like Federici last weekend against Manchester City, Boruc has undone all of their good work at the beginning of the match.
(33’) It's more defensive hesitation again from Bournemouth as the ball spins away from Kane to Cook inside the Cherries' penalty area, but the centre-back panics as the crowd get on his back before smashing it clear into the stands.
--- 31’ Yellow card Rose becomes the first man to get his name taken by the referee this afternoon for a silly lunge down the left-hand side of the pitch. He's been very shaky defensively so far today. ---
(31’) A good chance to get a second comes for Bournemouth through a free-kick but Ritchie passes up the opportunity as he fails to beat the first man, driving it straight at the head of Alli as the chance goes begging.
--- 29’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAALLLLL!! It's 1-3 to Spurs! Kane shifts the ball from right to left inside Bournemouth's box and sees his cross deflect off Francis towards goal, but Boruc spills the ball right into the path of Lamela who taps home. ---
(27’) Distin reacts angrily to the linesman on his side of the pitch as he gets forced to clear the ball under pressure from Dembele. The Bournemouth defender feels he should have had a free-kick as the Belgian grabs his shirt slightly.
(25’) Pugh switches the ball out wide to Daniels and the Bournemouth man drives a low cross towards Murray, but as Alderweireld blocks the ball, it gets caught underneath him slightly as he eventually digs it away under pressure from King.
(23’) BIG SAVE! Spurs come so close to making it 1-3 as Alderweireld flies past Cook too easily and heads towards goal at the near post, but Boruc beats the ball excellently with solid reactions between the sticks.
(21’) Lamela dances past Gosling between Bournemouth's midfield lines and plays a lovely threaded through ball to Kane, who ghosts beyond Cook but the official on that side of the pitch denies the Spurs man with his raised flag for offside.
(19’) Bournemouth show a good response to falling behind as Ritchie picks up the baton from Murray and swings in a good cross towards King, who fails to make contact with the ball as Walker heads behind for a corner.
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!! It's 2-1 to Spurs who are now in front for the first time today! Rose drives a shot towards goal which hits Cook and falls into Dembele's path, who runs through unmarked and slots the ball past Boruc. ---
(15’) Alderweireld plays a cracking lofted ball towards Eriksen down the left wing but as the Dane tries to cut inside onto his stronger right foot, Francis gets his body in the way well and snuffs out the danger.
(13’) CLOSE! Ritchie latches onto the ball down the right flank as Rose again fails to get tight enough to him and as the Bournemouth man curls in a dangerous cross towards the box, King heads wide.
(11’) Kane wins a flick-on above Cook and that sets Alli off and running, but as Distin gets there first, he smashes the ball back to Boruc who just about gets enough contact on it to clear it away. Good goalkeeping.
--- 9’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!! It's 1-1 and Spurs are back level. Kane restores parity here at the Vitality Stadium as he calmly slots the ball past Boruc, who dives the wrong way after giving away the spot-kick. Game on! ---
(7’) PENALTY TO TOTTENHAM! Eriksen slips the ball down the side of Cook to Kane, who touches the ball around Boruc and gets wiped out in the process by the Bournemouth goalkeeper.
(5’) Bournemouth combine excellently down the left-hand side once again as Pugh plays in Daniels, who gets given far too much time and space to curl in a cross past Walker but Rose heads away at the back stick.
(3’) Pugh tumbles to the floor as he nicks the ball away Dembele in the middle of the park and wins a free-kick for the hosts. Spurs are really struggling to keep hold of possession at the moment. Bournemouth are all over them with massive intensity.
--- 1’ Assist Assist by C. Daniels. ---
--- 1’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAAAAALLL!! What a start for Bournemouth! Daniels whips in a dangerous cross which goes all the way to the back post past Rose, who fails to shut down Ritchie as the winger smashes it home from close range. ---
(1’) Bournemouth get us under way here in the glorious sunshine on the south coast. The man in charge of the cards for today's encounter is Roger East.

FULL TIME: UNITED 0-0 CITY. Far from a classic as the Red Devils are held to a point at Old Trafford, despite a lifeless showing from Manuel Pellegrini's side. City were mere spectators for much of the match, offering next to nothing going forward. The hosts grew into the game well in the second half but a lack of inventiveness, coupled with some smart goalkeeping from Joe Hart, proves enough to keep them out.
(90’) PARITY IN MANCHESTER!
(90’) Into the first of three minutes of stoppage time and United are being urged forward by their supports following the defence of a City corner. A hopeful ball over the top for Rooney runs harmlessly to Hart, and the cheers quickly turn into a mix of boos and groans.
--- 89’ Yellow card M. Schneiderlin is cautioned by the referee. ---
(89’) BRILLIANT GOALKEEPING! There's the impact on Fellaini, winning an aerial duel and heading a ball down into the path of Smalling inside the area. The defender takes the chance first-time and forces Hart into a tremendous reactionary stop to keep the effort out at the near post!
(87’) EXCELLENT DEFENDING! De Bruyne sends an inviting delivery in from the left, following a set piece. Otamendi gets behind the defence and looks sure to meet it, but Rooney provides just enough pressure on the defender to prevent him from turning it in!
(85’) OFF THE BAR! Well that's got the Old Trafford faithful making noise again! Exceptional run from Lingard who is played through by a delightful ball over the top from Martial. The substitute volleys at goal first-time, chipping Hart, but his effort rattles off the frame of the goal!
--- 83’ Substitution Final change for City as Iheanacho is introduced for Bony. The striker had a tough night in attack, but service was poor and he did what was asked of him - the rest of the blame has to be put elsewhere. Perhaps the youngster can provide them with a late spark. ---
--- 81’ Substitution Valencia is down again and in a bit of discomfort as he clutches his foot. This is the same injury that plagued him in the first half and it may see his day cut short once and for all as the medical staff comes out to attend to him. ---
(79’) Tired legs appear to have taken over. It's been as far as you can get from an instant classic, but these players have put in a lot of running today to take away space from their opponents and ensure they are never caught out of position. As a result, fatigue has set in and we appear to be in store for a sluggish final 10 minutes.
--- 77’ Substitution A really disappointing night for Yaya Toure comes to an end and it's a shockingly-negative change from Pellegrini as he brings on Martin Demichelis to replace him. It's clear they're playing for the point now, which should provide United with more desire to push forward and snatch a winner. ---
--- 75’ Substitution It is Schweinsteiger who gives way for Fellaini, and the German international has been nothing short of superb today. Both on and off the ball his contributions have been crucial. The Belgian will likely play in a more advanced role however. ---
(74’) STAT ATTACK: There has not been a draw in any of the last 12 Manchester derbies, with the last scoreless tie between the two teams coming in November 2010.
(72’) Marouane Fellaini, who was a star in United's 4-2 victory in this match last season, is preparing to come on. The hosts desperately need someone to hold the ball up and distribute in attack, while offering a threat that has been desperately lacking in the air.
(70’) Lingard provides a nice injection of pace, perhaps the reasoning behind his introduction ahead of Memphis, as he makes his first impact with a good run and pass to pick out Rooney. The striker tries to square for Herrera, but Otamendi is wise to it.
(68’) Well for the time being it appears as though the hosts are the only side capable of breaking the deadlock, with City showing absolutely nothing going forward. Part of it can be attributed to the organised play of United at the back, but for the most part that's just a cop-out for these visiting players who have to be held accountable.
--- 67’ Substitution J. Lingard comes on for Mata. ---
(66’) United's first change is imminent and it's Jese Lingard who is introduced ahead of Memphis Depay! The England Under-21 international returned to Premier League action against Everton last week before starting in Russia on Wednesday, and comes on here at the expense of Juan Mata.
(64’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester City have scored in 18-consecutive Premier League matches since a 1-0 defeat at Burnley in March (W14, L4). It is the longest active streak in the top flight, with Leicester a distant second (11).
(62’) TERRIFIC GOALKEEPING! City concede possession as they try and break out of their own half, and a ball is played over the top for Mata. The Spaniard appears to be clean through, but Hart is so alert, quick to react and sprint off his line to clear the danger just ahead of the Spaniard's impending arrival.

The Belgian has taken the league by storm since arriving and will be hoping to etch his name in Manchester City folklore as he takes part in his first Premier League derby.

Daley Blind and Memphis Depay have also become regulars on the substitute bench following the disappointing end to their European Championship qualifying campaign with the Netherlands. MANCHESTER CITY TEAM NEWS: The big question surrounding the Sky Blues was regarding Vincent Kompany and whether or not the defender would return to action for the first time in six weeks. Well the news is good for City fans as the skipper is back in the team and starting in defence alongside Nicolas Otamendi. David Silva and Sergio Aguero remain injured, however. Aleksandar Kolarov is brought back into the team, along with Fernando, after the duo sat out against Sevilla. Pablo Zabaleta and Jesus Navas are dropped to the bench as a result.
MANCHESTER UNITED TEAM NEWS: Louis van Gaal makes just one change following their midweek Champions League draw in Russia, with Juan Mata replacing Jesse Lingard. Memphis Depay is again relegated to a spot among the substitutes, while Wayne Rooney gets the start up top. Anthony Martial will provide support, along with the two Spaniards, Ander Herrera and Mata.
Enough rambling, though. This is a football match not a benefit concert – and an important one at that. Louis van Gaal's side will have the crowd behind them, but there has been no way to know which United team will show up match to match. City have been the more consistent side, but have their share of injury woes and will have the embarrassment they suffered at Old Trafford last season in the back of their minds. With the timing of the match and the detriment that a loss would cause either side, you have to wonder whether both managers would sleep well tonight knowing they walked away with a point.
Manchester purists – Mancunians, if you will – have just one qualm with the current state of the derby: a lack of homebred talent. For a second year running, neither side line up with an academy graduate in their starting XI. The borders have been torn down in Manchester as the two clubs boast top talent from around the world, as has become the norm in today’s game. This is not a reason for Manchester to lament, but to instead share their local tradition with supporters across the globe.
As far as one-city rivalries come, this may be the biggest. On the global scale of world football, only Real Madrid v Atletico comes close in terms of the current stature of the two teams involved. The size, financial power and compete level of the clubs has brought the Manchester derby to a new level in recent years – building to the global event it has now become.

All eyes will be on the visitors’ dugout, however, as Klopp aims to become the first Liverpool manager since Kenny Dalglish in 1985 to win his first game in charge of Liverpool. Whilst it is difficult to know just how his players will initially perform under the watchful eye of the exciting German, one thing is for certain: he has joined the Merseyside club at a time in which they are in the middle of a poor run of form. They have managed to pick up just one victory from their last six Premier League games, whilst away from home they have looked even worse, managing only one win from nine, their worst run since the start of 2011.

(70’) Cresswell goes wide to Moses, who jinxes past Puncheon before the Palace player recovers to knock the ball out for a visitors' corner. Sakho keeps it alive but it's cleared by Hangelaand!
--- 69’ Yellow card M. Jedinak gets yellow. ---
(68’) Payet has the ball deeper in his half, and scans upfield to see who's free. Unhappy with his players' movement, he sends it lateral, and it's slowly worked up the pitch. Soon Payet lifts it smartly over the defence to Lanzini down the right, who wins a corner when his cross is deflected out.
(66’) Poor from Bolasie, who had Puncheon free down his right on the counter, and instead tried to do it all himself. Collins read the play very well and stepped up smartly to win the ball back for the visitors.
(65’) Carroll's first real involvement is to pull down a Palace defender, allowing the home side to take a free-kick just when West Ham looked threatening in the box.
--- 63’ Substitution M. Jedinak enters play, replacing J. McArthur. ---
(63’) Jenkinson sends a super cross in that Sakho heads, rising above Hangelaand, into the ground and off the post! That was so nearly the second for the visitors!!
--- 62’ Substitution This has been a period of sustained possession from Palace, with West Ham surely wondering how they've let the home side have so much of the  ball thus far. Carroll comes on for Noble as Bilic looks to ensure his side wrap this one up! ---
(60’) Kelly takes a throw-in down his flank that's worked back to him and passed to McARrthur, who goes wide to Puncheon. Bolasie flicks a cross into the box and Sako can't get his shot off as he dribbles past two defenders!
(58’) Moses out on the left, cuts it to Noble in the middle... and it's intercepted. Palace are very compact at the back and breaking quickly with width when hey can, which has frustrated West Ham thus far.
(57’) Payet now sends a cross across the pitch, and the visitors work it around the mouth of the area trying to find an opening, but the defence for the home side holds firm!
(55’) Bolasie winds down the right and races into acres of space, cutting smartly inside. Puncheon gets it soon after and curls a shot towards the far post, but it goes wide!
(53’) West Ham are pressing ferociously to try to win the ball back in midfield. They're exploiting the wings and working the ball side-to-side to try and find the gaps at the back. It always ends up back at Payet to play that final pass.
(51’) Payet chips a smart pass into the path of Sakho but he uses his hand to take it down in the box, giving the home side a free-kick. Palace are doing well early in this second half to ensure that they give a fight to the visitors despite their numerical disadvantage.
(49’) This is good possessio from Palace, who win the ball down the left, take a throw-in and keep the ball around the box, before Bolasie can't get on the edge of the pass and watches the ball go out of play.
(48’) Sako tries to turn around Hangelaand but the centre-back is smart to the trick and shepards the ball in his own box.
(47’) Bilic, meanwhile, will be relishing the chance to win today despite Jenkinson giving away a penalty moments after scoring. They have the entire second half with a man advantage and plenty of attacking options on the bench to bring on! Join us in 15 for the second half.
--- 46’ Substitution W. Zaha is done for the day. B. Sako is his replacement. ---
(46’) One substitution to begin this half, with Zaha off for Sako. West Ham begin with the ball, under no real pressing from Palace. They're lurking around the area but can't get the final ball into the box.
(46’) For Palace, it was a nightmare start after conceding Jenkinson's goal but they got back into it immediately and were every bit as into the game as West Ham until Gayle's sending off. Now they'll have to figure out a way to keep the league's best away team from doing what they've done so well this season.
(45’) Jenkinson, the man of the half in many ways, gets through the defence and sends a smart, incisive ball towards the back post but no one can meet it! That's the last meaningful action of the half as it ends 1-1.
(45’) It's all West Ham here, to no real surprise, as Bilic's team now have a man advantage. Palace are clinging on in their own half, desperate to get to halftime without conceding, and do well to clear a cross that Sakho rose high to try and meet.
--- 44’ Red card! D. Gayle gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(44’) GAYLE SENT OFF!!! PALACE DOWN TO TEN MEN! That's an absolute moment of madness for Gayle, who was already on a yellow, and lunges in late on Kouyate deep in West Ham's half. Clattenburg did not hesitate there for a second and now Pardew and his men have it all to do!
(42’) HOW DIDN'T PALACE DO MORE THERE!? Collins makes a complete hash of the offside line and lets Bolasie fly into the area, but he sends an easy pass to Zaha just behind the winger, letting West Ham recover to knock the ball out of play!
--- 40’ Yellow card Payet enters the book for petulance, kicking the ball away after he knocked over Bolasie trying to win the ball back. It's a silly way to be booked and surely Bilic will be furious his star player couldn't control his emotions in that moment! ---
(39’) A sizzling counter from the home side finds Zaha in space down the left, and he beats Jenkinson but fires a very weak effort towards Adrian far too close to the near post. The West Ham keeper has no trouble collecting that!
(37’) The free-kick comes to nothing and Noble and Moses try a quick passing exchange to get in behind the defence, but Zaha races back and knocks the ball out of play off the former Chelsea player to win his side a goal-kick.
(36’) Excellent defending deep in his own half by Zaha, who cuts out a deep pass intended for Jenkinson. The full-back takes revenge a few seconds later when he pushes over the pacey winger, but only gives West Ham a free-kick,
(34’) This match is simply breakneck, with the two sides changing possession every few seconds, always racing towards the opposition's box trying to make something happen. Cabaye and Payet are running the show in the midfield.
--- 32’ Yellow card Gayle enters the book after a late, sliding tackle on Payet. Clattenburg gave him a talking-to before showing him the yellow and putting him in the book. ---
(30’) Payet wins a corner off of Kelly and he sends in a fast ball to the heart of the box, that's cleared but played back to Payet. Moses races down the wing and squares it to Sakho, who shoots from the centre of the box and sees his shot deflected with by Hangelaand!
(28’) Palace are building from the back, though Tomkins heads a thrown-in back towards their defence that Souare sends further down the pitch. Sakho does brilliantly to break passt Hangelaand on the counter and Payet shoots in the box but it's blocked by Kelly!
(26’) What an absolutey furious few minutes this game has seen. Cabaye now has 3 penalties scored in his last 3 matches for his side and the two teams can thank Jenkinson for allowing each of them to score!
--- 25’ Goal! Cabaye scores but it has to be retaken! Gayle had run into the box right in front of Clattenburg before the ball was struck, forcing the referee to blow his whistle. No matter, though - Cabaye sinks the second one with aplomb, as Adrian gets a finger to it but can't keep it out of the top left corner! 1-1 in this game of madness! Gayle goes after Payet in the midfield with a very late challenge, and the whistle is blown and Clattenburg gives him a talking-to before booking him. That was a bit of a nasty challenge! ---
(24’) PALACE HAVE A PENALTY MERE SECONDS AFTER THE GOAL! And it's Jenkinson who concees it! He takes down Gayle just as he stepped into the box, leaving Adrian with a huge task against Cabaye...
--- 22’ Assist V. Moses provided the assist. ---
--- 22’ Goal! AND THE GOAL DOES COME! IT'S WEST HAM VIA JENKINSON! A fantastic play created that; Lanzini took the ball, cut inside, and a beautiful pass is played in from Moses to slice the defence wide open and let Jenkinson race into the box to place underneath Hennessey! 1-0 to the away team! ---
(21’) Puncheon sends a great cross into the box but Adrian rises high to parry it well! The chances are coming fast and furious now and it certainly seems only a matter of time before one of these sides can break the deadlock!
--- 20’ Yellow card Tomkins gets down the other end and pulls down Gayle as he was racing into the area, earning himself a yellow and Palace a free-kick that should be floated into the box. ---
(19’) Payet sends a superb ball into the box from a corner and Tomkins heads it towards goal but it somehow goes just wide of the near post! A goal-kick is awarded to Palace even though it seems Hangelaand may have had the last touch!
(18’) Gayle races onto a loose ball in the box and collides with Adrian, who had come off his line to claim it. The referee judges the challenge to have been fair but the striker is furious that he didn't receive a penalty!
(17’) Unfortunately for the visitors, the set piece is wasted. Cresswell races up to take it but leans back as he strikes the ball, sending it ever higher, away from the crossbar.
(16’) Hangelaand jumps into Sakho's path outside of the box and there's no doubt that the ensuing free-kick is fairly awarded to the visitors, who now have a fantastic chance at goal!
(15’) Zaha and Puncheon team up down the left as they try to overload Jenkinson, but they're forced inside and West Ham soon counterr with aplomb via Kouyate.
(13’) Palace, currently dominating possession, draw cheers from the crowd when they pass the ball laterally to avoid a few high-pressing visiting players. Payet gets fouled further down the pitch to win his side a spell with the ball.
(12’) The teams are very congested in the middle of the pitch but both are trying to use quick-passing to exploit the space left behind by both defences. It'll be interesting to see if either manager adjusts his team's formation to allow for more space to open up in midfield.
(10’) Choas in the West Ham box! Bolasie surges into the area and beats one defender with a pass, and the rest of the backline make a meal of the clearance before Puncheon tries a shot that gets deflected out!
(9’) Puncheon gets the ball without much space to run into down his flank but does well to win a throw-in off Collins.
(8’) Payet is doing all he can on the edge of the box to poke and prod his way through the defence, and he eventually fires a shot at the near post that Hennessey dives low and with some ease to smother.
(6’) Ah almost something! Bolasie tries to slip the ball through the defence for Puncheon but Adrian is off his line quickly to smother. A few seconds later, Puncheon gets another chance after a free-kick is hoofed into the box but he smashes his shot wide of the far post from inside of the box!
(5’) The home side now send a side out of bounds when Hangelaand sends it up for Bolasie, but the centre-back's pass is overhit. This is a bit of a muted start after that near goal in the very first minute.
(4’) Another slick move from Lanzini shields the ball and sends it wide to Payet, who tries a clever give-and-go to sneak the Argentine in behind the defence, but the ball is sheparded out of play.
(2’) In just a few seconds there, West Ham showed how dangerously they can counter. Zaha loses the ball to Cresswell as he came back into his own midfield, and the ball is now mired in the centre of the pitch.
(1’) AND WE HAVE KICK-OFF! It's Palace who begin with the ball, in their blue and red striped kit, and Zaga immediately zips forward. It's a high ball played towards Gayle that's cut out easily, and the Hammers counter... PAYET NEARLY SCORES! His shot from Lanzini's cutback goes just wide! Nearly a dream start!
We're just minutes away from kick-off now. Stay tuned to see which of these sides can continue to defy expectations and stay in the hunt for a Champions' League spot!
Recent history has been very kind to the home side, who have only lost one of their last seven league meetings with West Ham. The visitors, however, took the three points on their most recent match-up and are the second-highest scoring team in the league, behind only Manchester City!
Both sides are missing key players due to injury today. The home side will have to do without Wickham, Chamakh, and Appiah, while the visitors will be without Carroll, Valencia, and Song.
West Ham (4-2-3-1): Adrian; Cresswell, Collins, Tomkins, Jenkinson; Noble, Kouyate; Moses, Payet, Lanzini; Sakho.
Palace (4-2-3-1): Hennessey; Kelly, Hangeland, Dann, Souare; McArthur, Cabaye; Bolasie, Zaha, Puncheon; Gayle.
The visitors are another side bouyed by a smart summer signing: Dimitri Payet. They've scored in all of their matches this season and have already taken major, major scalps on the road, including Arsenal, Manchester City, and Liverpool. They oddly have a worse record at home than on their travels, but they're yet to lose away, and they'll be hopeful that they can extend that streak to five games today.
The home side have done as well as could be expected in the last five weeks in the Premier League. They've defeated West Brom, Watford, and Chelsea while losing by narrow margins against Manchester City at home and Tottenham Hotspur away. Anchored by the brilliant Yohan Cabaye in midfield, they're showing just how transformational money well spent in the league can be.
Hello and welcome to our live match coverage of Crystal Palace vs West Ham! It's matchday 9 in the Premier League and these two teams have defied all expectations, sitting in 4th and 6th respectively. At least one of the sides will drop points today - but who will it be? Alan Pardew and Salven Bilic will be hoping it's each other, but both deserve plaudits for fantastic starts to the season.

FULL TIME! Man United turn in a comprehensive 3-0 victory over Everton on their Premier League travels, with goals from Schneiderlin, Herrera and Rooney wrapping up a vital three points for Van Gaal's men. The Toffees didn't really get going, with Martinez's men firing blanks up top. That's all that we have time for on Merseyside, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Jones scrambles away yet another clearance, with Man United edging towards a deserved clean sheet. Martial drives to the left byline, before setting another dangerous cross into the six-yard box, but both Fellaini and Lingard can't make contact.
(90’) There are three minutes of stoppage time at Goodison Park.
(88’) Coleman does well to head a dangerous cross away, after a neat break down the right by Herrera. Moments later, Martial breaks into the box and rifles in a low cross, but nobody in red can get on the end of it! Despite being three goals to the good, the Red Devils are still looking the more dangerous of the two outfits.
(86’) Fellaini tries to drive down the left flank and break, but McCarthy recovers brilliantly to deny the ex-Everton midfielder. The Red Devils are trying to slow this contest down and hold onto the ball, with the hosts only pressing very reluctantly at this point.
(84’) Martial is released in behind enemy lines down the right flank, but the Frenchman is denied by the linesman's flag. Everton respond by breaking forward at pace, but Deulofeu's eventual cross is lashed away from the danger zone by Jones. Man United have defended solidly.
(82’) We're into the final 10 minutes at Goodison Park, as Everton look to salvage some of their pride if possible. Carrick drives his way forward and wins a free kick from McCarthy, but Man United are happy to set possession back and see this game out.
--- 81’ Substitution M. Fellaini enters play, replacing Ander Herrera. ---
(80’) Barkley wrongfoots Schneiderlin and wins a dangerous free kick on the edge of the penalty area. The England international sends a dipping strike goalwards, but the ball zips over the crossbar and behind for a goal kick. Nothing is quite going to plan for the hosts.
(78’) Good defensive header from Stones! The ex-Barnsley man denies Herrera brilliantly, following a teasing cross from the right-hand side! The former Athletic Club midfielder was inches away from grabbing his second goal of the evening, but the Everton centre-back denies him. Moments later, Martial jinks his way into the box, but has a near-post strike saved by Howard!
(76’) Deulofeu is trying to inject a sense of urgency into the hosts' play, with the Spaniard having the creativity and flair to make an impact this afternoon. Martial dances into the box, before feeding a pass into Rooney, but the Englishman's touch escapes him. Lingard picks up the rebound, but lashes a terrible shot well wide.
--- 74’ Substitution M. Carrick comes on for B. Schweinsteiger. ---
(74’) Carrick replaces Schweinsteiger, with the Germany international's yellow card making him easily replaceable. Barkley is denied by the aforementioned ex-Spurs midfielder, but an eventual through ball from Rooney is gobbled up by Howard.
--- 73’ Substitution Deulofeu enters play, replacing A. Lennon. ---
(72’) Time is running out for the home side, who are coming up against an immovable object in Man United's defence. Van Gaal's side are allowing the Toffees to have the lion's share of possession, safe in the knowledge that Everton have looked rather toothless all afternoon. Coleman loops in a cross from the right, but Darmian clears easily.
--- 70’ Yellow card R. Lukaku is yellow-carded. ---
(70’) Lukaku is stood up well by Schneiderlin, with the Everton striker booked for fouling the Frenchman and then hurling the ball at the turf in frustration. That sums up the hosts' afternoon, as they certainly haven't had things all their own way. Lingard rifles in a cross from the right, but Jagielka slides in to make a timely clearance that denies Rooney.
(68’) Coleman sees a shot charged down from a very narrow angle, with Everton winning themselves a corner as a result. Barkley and Lennon combine and take the set piece short, but an eventual shot from the former is parried clear of the danger zone by De Gea. Man United break upfield, but a stabbed finish from Rooney is well saved by Howard.
(66’) Martial is fouled in the midfield third, with Everton giving away some free kicks due to their overzealous attitude towards trying to get back into this game. Martinez still has two changes to make, but the hosts have to totally transform if they are to cause Man United any kind of concern.
(64’) Schweinsteiger breaks down the left flank, but Coleman stands his man up easily. Everton's bright start to the second half has all fallen apart, courtesy of a quick counter from the visitors. Three goals are the minimum that the Toffees have to come up with, all within the next 25 minutes of play.
--- 62’ Assist Ander Herrera gave the assist. ---
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! ROONEY MAKES IT 3-0! Jagielka gives possession away to Schneiderlin in midfield, with Herrera released down the right. The Basque midfielder sets a pass into his teammate's path, with the ex-Toffees forward slotting a neat finish over the sprawling body of Howard! Game over! ---
(61’) Less than half an hour remains for Everton to try and get back on level terms, but Man United have sensibly looked to sit back and weather the storm from Martinez's men. Van Gaal's side are pressing well.
(59’) Rojo and Schweinsteiger have found themselves dragged into some awful situations, with Van Gaal perhaps needing to think about making some changes if the Red Devils are to end this game with 11 men on the field. Barkley wins a free kick from Schneiderlin, but the England international is denied by a save from De Gea!
(57’) Man United are having to stem the tide in the early stages of the second half, with the Toffees needing to respond quickly with a goal. Martial dribbles into the penalty area from the left, but his second touch escapes him somewhat. A third from Man United would put this contest beyond doubt.
(55’) Rojo stands up well to deny Lukaku, with the former Chelsea forward currently unable to evade the intentions of Smalling. The England international is having an excellent game at the heart of the Red Devils' defence. Barkley whips a free-kick delivery in from the right yet again, but it is headed away easily. Moments later, Lukaku sees a close-range shot courageously blocked on the line!
(53’) Lukaku goes down on the edge of the penalty area, with Rojo picking up a yellow card for a cynical bodycheck on the Belgium international. A few bookings might just unsettle the away outfit. Barkley lines up the free kick, but Martial is able to head away as first man.
--- 52’ Yellow card M. Rojo gets yellow. ---
(51’) Lukaku and Kone play a neat one-two on the edge of the penalty area, but a shot from the latter is blocked well by Jones! Everton keep the pressure on, with Coleman setting a cross up to the back post, but Lingard denies Barkley with a good recovering interception!
--- 50’ Yellow card B. Schweinsteiger is cautioned by the referee. ---
(49’) Herrera manages to combine with Schneiderlin, but an eventual cross from Darmian is lashed to safety by Galloway. This second half is yet to settle down at all, with Everton feverishly trying to get themselves back into this game. Deulofeu and Mirallas lie in wait on the bench.
(47’) Mata is replaced by Lingard at the break, with Kone coming into the game for Naismith too. Both coaches have shuffled their pack slightly, with the Toffees needing to make serious improvement. Barkley whips in a free-kick delivery from the right, but Lukaku fires wide of the back post due to pressure from Smalling.
--- 46’ Substitution A. Koné enters play, replacing S. Naismith. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Mata is done for the day. J. Lingard is his replacement. ---
(46’) We are underway in the second half! The hosts have it all to do if they are to take any spoils from this afternoon's clash, as Everton need to score at least two goals in the next 45 minutes at Goodison.
HALF TIME! The visitors have a comfortable 2-0 lead at the interval, with goals from Schneiderlin and Herrera putting Man United in a solid position. The Toffees just haven't been at the races, with two quick-fire goals leaving Martinez's men with a lot to do after the restart.
(45’) There is one minute of stoppage time.
(45’) Good save from De Gea! Barkley tries his luck from a narrow angle on the left flank, with the Spaniard able to palm a smart save away from the danger zone! That's the closest that the hosts have gone.
(44’) Darmian whips a cross in from the right-hand side, but his delivery is cut out simply. Man United are happy to put their foot on the ball and slow down play for the dying minutes on Merseyside. Everton need to go back to the drawing board if they want to take any spoils from this contest.
(42’) Huge chance for Man United! Rooney breaks down the right-hand side, with the Englishman cutting back a neat pass due to a narrow angle! Martial meets the ball with a first-time attempt, but a combination of Stones and Howard denies the young France international!
(40’) Martial does well to turn away from Stones, with the Monaco forward able to make occasional dangerous forays forward. Naismith goes on a mazy dribble forward, with Lukaku being picked out well. The Belgian keeps play moving out to the right flank, but an eventual cross from out wide is cut out. Everton's spell of pressure ends with Jagielka curling a 20-yard effort hopelessly wide.
(38’) Naismith is picked out by a ball over the top, with Smalling unable to keep pace with the Everton striker. De Gea, however, is quick off his line to gobble up the danger. Martinez is looking extremely concerned on the sideline, as the Toffees have wandered their way through the first half.
(36’) Good clearance from Smalling! Galloway whips a cross in from the left flank, with the ex-Fulham man lashing a dangerous cross away. The resulting corner is met by Naismith, but the Scottish forward is penalised for leaning into De Gea, however.
(34’) Narrowly over 10 minutes remain in the first half, with Everton still being caught on the break. Man United are setting up camp with a nice spell of possession, as the Toffees struggle to piece together meaningful attacks. The home supporters are grumbling.
(32’) McCarthy comes across to slide in and deny Martial, with the ex-Monaco striker unable to force himself into the equation thus far. Man United haven't created many chances since doubling their lead, but Van Gaal will be very pleased with how his side have kicked on from the international break.
(30’) Everton work the ball from left to right, but a forward pass from Coleman is easily cut out. The Toffees maintain their pressure, with the Irishman then able to whip a delivery in from out wide. Lukaku and De Gea challenge for the cross, with the goalkeeper taking a stray arm to the face from the former Chelsea striker. Jones is still receiving treatment on the touchline.
(28’) Galloway and Naismith combine down the left, but a flick from Barkley is easily intercepted. Everton just aren't getting a foothold in the midfield battle, with Martinez perhaps needing to think about re-setting his stall for the second half. Jones is forced to remove himself from the field, with the Englishman picking up a rather fierce nosebleed.
(26’) Lukaku is picked out by a lofted pass upfield, with the Belgian striker able to flick a nice header towards Naismith. Smalling recovers well to hook a last-ditch clearance away from the Scottish forward, with the England international having a very solid start to this contest at the heart of the visitors' defence.
(24’) Lukaku goes down in the opposition penalty area, but the Belgium international doesn't get anything from the referee! He has been dealt with physically by Smalling and Jones, with the Toffees' target man failing to have a real impact on proceedings.
--- 22’ Yellow card S. Coleman receives a yellow card. ---
--- 22’ Assist Assist by M. Rojo. ---
--- 22’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! HERRERA DOUBLES THE VISITORS' LEAD! Rojo is released down the left-hand side, with the ex-Sporting defender able to curl a delightful cross in from out wide! The ex-Athletic Club midfielder is on hand to guide a delicate header inside the right-hand post! Howard had no chance! ---
(20’) Everton now have to try and fight their way back into this contest, with Man United able to sit back and perhaps try their luck at breaking at pace instead. Martinez will not be too pleased with his side's start at Goodison Park, as Barry and McCarthy are yet to take control of the game in the centre of the park.
--- 18’ Assist C. Smalling provided the assist. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! SCHNEIDERLIN OPENS THE SCORING! The French midfielder is on hand at the back post to guide a great finish inside the far post! Smalling picks out the ex-Saints man, who slots beyond Howard to give the Red Devils an early lead! ---
(17’) Stones does well to lash a dangerous cross away, with Lukaku chasing the long ball upfield. Smalling shifts a pass back to De Gea, with the ex-Chelsea striker continuing to have to race around feeding off scraps. Herrera unleashes a good strike from around 25 yards out, but Howard does well to palm a save over his crossbar!
(16’) Smalling manages to Lukaku to a ball forward yet again, with the former Fulham defender doing well to contend with the ex-Anderlecht striker. Man United are having more of the possession, but Everton's quick breaks forward are keeping De Gea on his toes.
(14’) Barkley bursts into a dangerous area on the edge of the penalty area, but the Englishman sees a shot charged down easily. Moments later, Naismith is felled by Schneiderlin, with the visitors surrendering a free kick to the Toffees. Lukaku shoots, with a deflection off the wall wrongfooting De Gea - but the ball skips the wrong side of the upright!
(12’) Lukaku is fed into a dangerous area, but Smalling does well to jostle with the lone striker and pressure him into taking a poor touch. Jones mops up the scraps, with the former Blackburn Rovers defender able to cushion a header back to De Gea. The Belgian forward is being fed in behind enemy lines regularly now.
(10’) Darmian plays a neat one-two with Herrera, before the former Torino defender's cross is missed by Rooney! The Italy international put in a lovely ball, right in between the hosts' defensive line and Howard. The Red Devils are playing much of the better football thus far, with Martinez gesturing wildly.
(8’) Martial goes on a good run down the left channel, but Coleman matches the Frenchman for pace! The Irishman shields the ball back to Howard, who kickstarts an immediate counter. Lukaku is fed in behind enemy lines, but De Gea is alert to the danger and quick off his line to deny the Belgium international. Mata then whips a cross in towards Rooney, but Jagielka clears.
(6’) Schweinsteiger lifts a ball over the top for Rooney to chase, but both Stones and Jagielka are across quickly to deny the England international. Van Gaal's men are leading the early charge, with Everton being forced onto the back foot. Lukaku hasn't been able to do anything other than chase lost causes thus far.
(4’) Herrera is felled by a cynical tackle from Galloway, with Man United having a chance to load the box with red shirts. Mata's free-kick delivery is half cleared by a header from Jagielka, with Schweinsteiger lashing the rebound well wide.
(3’) Martial is pushed out to the left flank, with Rooney playing through the middle as it stands. Galloway is released down the left-hand side, before feeding Naismith into an dangerous area, but the Scotland international sees a shot charged down well.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Goodison Park! The hosts are looking to extend their current unbeaten run, with Man United aiming to forget their horrendous performance against Arsenal last time out. There is a minute of silence before kick off for ex-Toffees boss Howard Kendall.
Man United substitutes: Depay, Carrick, Blind, Fellaini, Lingard, Pereira, Johnstone.
Man United starting line-up (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Darmian, Smalling, Jones, Rojo; Schneiderlin, Schweinsteiger; Mata, Herrera, Rooney; Martial.
Everton substitutes: Robles, Kone, Mirallas, Deulofeu, Osman, Funes Mori, Browning.
Everton starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Howard; Coleman, Stones, Jagielka, Galloway; McCarthy, Barry; Lennon, Barkley, Naismith; Lukaku.
TEAM NEWS: Phil Jones starts alongside Chris Smalling in the heart of the hosts' defence, with Marcos Rojo being deployed at left-back in the long-term absence of Luke Shaw. Bastian Schweinsteiger and Morgan Schneiderlin will be asked to sit in midfield, with the likes of Wayne Rooney, Ander Herrera and Juan Mata set to fluidly support Anthony Martial. Memphis Depay and Daley Blind drop to the bench, after having a disappointing international break for the Netherlands in recent weeks.
TEAM NEWS: Leighton Baines, Tom Cleverley and Steven Pienaar are the high-profile absentees for the hosts, with John Stones and Seamus Coleman shaking off recent injury problems to start. Brendon Galloway starts at left-back, with Steven Naismith and Aaron Lennon starting in wide areas. Ross Barkley will look to carry some good form for England into his domestic performances. There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
As for West Brom, they too have struggled in recent weeks and will be desperate for a win as they aim to move away from the relegation zone. Just one victory from their last four league games has seen them drop to 17th place in the table, and after today they will have to face Leicester City, Manchester United and Arsenal in three of their next four Premier League encounters. Tony Pulis’ men have looked good at the back, which has resulted in them picking up four clean sheets, but it is at the other end of the pitch where they struggled, scoring just six goals, the lowest of any side in the division.
After suffering a terrible start to the new season, it was only a matter of time before a clearly jaded and frustrated Dick Advocaat would finally decide to leave the Stadium of Light. In his place comes Sam Allardyce, whose absence from the Premier League lasted just four months and 20 days. The aforementioned Dutchman’s final game in charge of the Black Cats ended in a 2-2 draw at home to, ironically, the new boss’ former club West Ham United, and it was the first time in over a month that they had managed to avoid losing. However, the clash saw them surrender a 2-0 lead and was further evidence of the problems that are quickly mounting at the club.

Full time at the Vitality Stadium. This has been a game of two halves and a tale of two goalkeepers this afternoon as Bournemouth and Watford play out an entertaining 1-1 draw in the Premier League. The home side started the match excellently and eventually took the lead through Murray after bossing the first half, only for goalkeeper Artur Boruc to gift Quique Sanchez Flores' men a way back into the match after playing the ball straight to the feet of Odion Ighalo for the Nigerian to pass into the empty net. The Hornets had the better of the play for the large portion of the second half, but in the end had to rely on their man between the sticks, Gomes, who saved wonderfully from Cook and also kept out a Murray penalty. Fair result in the end at 1-1! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!

(87’) This game has definitely been a tale of two goalkeepers! Boruc has contributed to Bournemouth potentially not picking up three points, while Gomes has certainly contributed to potentially earning a point for his side! Two fantastic saves in two minutes from Cook and Murray!
--- 85’ Missed penalty MISSED PENALTY FROM MURRAY! The new Bournemouth recruit, who scored the opening goal of the game with a brilliant header, passes up the opportunity to give them the lead late on as Gomes makes an outstanding save down to his left! Still one-one! ---
(85’) Penalty saved by Gomes!

(82’) What a fantastic attempt from Cook! The Bournemouth captain latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box and, with his back to goal, sends a brilliant overhead kick hurtling towards the top corner, only for Gomes to break Bournemouth hearts with an outstanding save!
(80’) This is end-to-end stuff here as, rather strangely, both sides are having plenty of joy on the counterattack! Watford have been the better team in the second half, but overall it has been pretty even, which is reflected in the scoreline.

Bournemouth take it short though as Ritchie steps up to smash the lay-off towards goal, only to see his attempt brilliantly charged down by Deeney. A disappointed groan comes from the home fans for that one.

The Bournemouth stopper does much better this time than his efforts in the first half though, and solidly palms the strike behind for a corner!

Disappointing in the end.

(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!

It all seemed like Eddie Howe would have a fairly pleasant team-talk after the first half as Glenn Murray gave Bournemouth the lead with an excellent header, with the home side also looking pretty comfortable at the back. (90’) Lukaku and Sakho square up in the penalty area with both players looking absolutely incensed at one another. Their team mates are quickly in to diffuse the situation, though.
(88’) SHOOT!!! Everton push forward and the ball runs kindly for Lennon. It is begging to be hit at goal but he opts to take the ball out wide and look for a cross, but Liverpool deal with it.
(86’) There have been some famous last-gasp winners in the history of this fixture. Who could forget Gary McAllister's 40-yard free kick in 2001? Someone must stand up and be counted in these final four minutes.
(83’) It is looking likely that both sides are resting on their laurels and happy to take a point from this game. A lot of the pace has gone out of it and there have been no real pushes for that winning goal.
(81’) As things stand, this point would lift Everton up to sixth in the table while Liverpool would remain in 10th. Can either side find a winner inside the last nine minutes? All will be revealed!
--- 79’ Substitution J. Allen enters the game and replaces Lucas Leiva. ---
--- 79’ Substitution S. Naismith is done for the day. A. Koné is his replacement. ---
(79’) And that is Lucas' last action of the game as he is wisely brought off by Rodgers with Joe Allen taking his place. Everton also make a change with Arouna Kone replacing Naismith.
(77’) THE REFEREE HAS BOTTLED THAT! Lucas produces a professional foul to stop McCarthy from advancing forward with the ball. For some reason, Mr Atkinson opts not to show the Brazilian a second yellow card when he should have done without any hesitation.
--- 76’ Substitution A. Lallana comes on for D. Ings. ---
(75’) Adam Lallana is going to come on for the final quarter of an hour and he has the quality to produce something out of nothing. Ings is the player to make way for his introduction.
(72’) GOOD SAVE! Coutinho comes to life by driving at Browning before shooting early with a powerful effort that is well pushed away by strong hands from Howard. That is the most dangerous the Brazilian has looked all afternoon.
(70’) STRONG HANDS! A nice move from Everton sees Lennon deftly help the ball into the path of Lukaku, who unleashes a vicious right-footed drive that is well beaten away by Mignolet.
--- 69’ Yellow card Lucas Leiva receives a yellow card. ---
(68’) It is looking likely that we are heading for a fourth straight draw here, unless either side can find a winner. It is still a very evenly-matched game, but both could do with offering more in the final third.
(66’) GREAT EFFORT! Barkley latches onto the ball just inside Liverpool's half and drives at the defence before looking to bend an effort into the far corner, but it goes just wide of the post with Mignolet struggling to get across.
--- 65’ Yellow card J. McCarthy is cautioned by the referee. ---
(64’) At the other end, Jagielka maintains his solidarity by being in the right place to head Clyne's dangerous deep cross away before Sturridge can head home.
(62’) Lennon gets involved immediately as he takes on Moreno and drills a dangerous ball across the area, but Skrtel is well positioned to make a vital clearance for his side.
(61’) Coutinho has had a very quiet game by his standards this afternoon and that is mainly down to the persistence of Everton. This is the case once again as McCarthy nudges him off the ball near the left corner flag.
--- 60’ Substitution A. Lennon comes on for Deulofeu. ---
(59’) Everton make the first change of the game and it is a like-for-like swap as Aaron Lennon comes on in place of the quiet Deulofeu, although the former will offer a lot more pace down the right flank.
(57’) Barkley gets to the byline down the left and flashes a low cross into the area looking for Lukaku, but Mignolet reads the ball well and comes out of goal to gather well.
(55’) Everton are awarded a free kick following an interesting tussle between Lukaku and Skrtel. Barkley's subsequent delivery is ultimately disappointing, though, as it goes straight through to Mignolet.
(53’) Once again, a fairly even balance has developed in early stages of the half. It is really difficult to pick a winner from this game and will be interesting to see who comes out on top.
(51’) Coutinho looks to play a neat one-two with Milner in the Everton area, but the hosts read the situation very well on this occasion and are able to intercept and clear to safety.
(49’) The Toffees may have failed to win in the last 10 meetings and won just one of the last eight here, but they certainly fancy their chances of ending that record if they can keep up this start.
(47’) CLOSE! Barkley's corner is well met by Browning at the near post, but his header takes a deflection which just about carries the ball over the bar. Everton have made a bright start to this second half.
(46’) KICK OFF! The referee blows his whistle and Everton get the ball rolling once again.
The players are coming back out onto the pitch and the second half is fast approaching.
Mignolet made some vital saves during that first half so Everton will be keen to keep testing him during the second, while Liverpool need to get more shots away at the other end.
Following a pulsating half, the two goals both came in the final five minutes. Ings was left completely unmarked to head in the opener, while Lukaku showed fantastic instincts to control and volley home the equaliser in stoppage time.
HALF TIME: EVERTON 1-1 LIVERPOOL
(45’) Mr Atkinson blows his whistle and brings an exciting first half to a close.
--- 45’ +1 Goal! WHAT A TIME TO EQUALISE!!! Can fails to clear Deulofeu's deep cross into the area and Lukaku instinctively reacts to control, before sweetly volleying the ball into the bottom corner to send Goodison Park into raptures. ---
(44’) What a week Ings has had! After receiving his first call-up to the England senior squad following a strong start to his Liverpool career, he is now off the mark in this famous fixture.
--- 41’ Assist J. Milner gave the assist. ---
--- 41’ Goal! LIVERPOOL LEAD!!! Ings scores his first goal in a Merseyside derby as he is left completely unmarked from Milner's corner to nod past the helpless Howard, who will be furious with his defence. ---

(37’) CAN NEEDS TO BE CAREFUL! He goes for the spectacular overhead kick as Barry literally puts his head in where it hurts. There was no malice involved but had Mr Atkinson seen that as dangerous play, he would have been walking.

--- 35’ Yellow card R. Barkley is cautioned by the referee. ---
--- 35’ Yellow card E. Can receives a yellow card. ---
(34’) Barkley squares up to Can after the Liverpool player refuses to give him the ball back. Players quickly step in to calm the situation and both men are booked for their troubles.
(32’) It will be interesting to see how important those saves prove to be in the context of this Merseyside derby. Both strikes looked destined for the back of the net but for Mignolet's intervention.
(30’) GREAT STOP! Everton put a crisp move together around the Liverpool area before McCarthy unleashes a powerful effort, which is brilliantly turned away by Mignolet who did well to spring across to his right.

(20’) We have a slight break in play here as Skrtel goes down near his own penalty area. He appears to be nursing his hand and is now receiving attention from the medical team.
(17’) There has been a fairly even balance to this game inside the opening 17 minutes. Both sides are enjoying decent spells of possession, but are yet to really trouble either keeper. That should change soon.

Arsenal move above United into second place on goal difference after today's result in North London, with both sides locked level on 16 points behind leaders Manchester City. Next up for the Gunners is a trip to Watford while Van Gaal's men face Everton at Goodison Park, with each tie coming after the international break.
Wenger's men completely outclassed United in the first half and some of their football was scintillating. They defended well without possession, with Cech making a couple of big saves, in a complete performance from the Gunners.
The Gunners pick up their first Premier League win over United since 2011 as a brace from Alexis Sanchez and a solitary strike from Mesut Ozil sees off the Red Devils at the Emirates.

(88’) Martial runs to the left of Gabriel inside the penalty area and tumbles to the floor under pressure from Arsenal man, who runs away with the ball. There was no real protests from the visitors for a penalty there.

(78’) There's no real desire for a fourth from Arsenal as the Gunners have set out to protect their three-goal swing in this second half. They've done a good job at it as time continues to run out for United to turn things on its head.

(74’) Carrick feeds through a decent pass towards Martial who holds off Gabriel and drives a ball across the face of Arsenal's goal towards Rooney, but Mertesacker clears at the back post brilliantly.

So far they've worked hard as a unit off the ball and ensured United have created next to nothing, in a much more improved display.
Arsenal's front three of Ozil, Walcott and Sanchez have been excellent in the final third, causing so much mayhem in the United backline from the first whistle. The Gunners surged forward numerous times before taking the lead and Van Gaal's charges didn't know what him them.
Both groups of players head towards the tunnel for the half-time interval with United all set up for an ear-bashing from Van Gaal in the dressing room. Although Arsenal deserve huge credit for their oustanding, glorious football, the Red Devils were so off the pace in the first half it was unbelievable at times.

Their impressive start to the new season has largely gone unnoticed but has left them just one victory away from a top-three spot that would see them sit just three points behind current leaders City heading into the international break. The North Londoners certainly have history on their side, too, as they have won the last seven meetings between the two sides, whilst Swansea haven’t tasted victory against the Lilywhites since October 1982.

In recent weeks, things looked to be slowly on the up for the hosts, who suffered a lacklustre start to the new season before picking up their first victory of the campaign with a narrow 1-0 win against struggling Sunderland two weeks ago. That was followed by three more points against Crystal Palace in a game that saw new signing Heung-Min Son impress with his first goal since joining the club from Bayer Leverkusen, but Wednesday’s defeat against bitter rivals Arsenal will have hurt them dearly. This afternoon is guaranteed to be a tough test, as City have a tendency to bounce back strongly after being defeated domestically. In fact, they have only suffered back-to-back Premier League defeats on one occasion in almost five years.

That defeat brought an end to an 11-game domestic winning run that stretched back to the middle of April, and with it the reigning champions' 100% record. However, they bounced back during the week with a 4-1 thumping of Sunderland in the Capital One Cup and they will be looking to do the same today as they take on a Tottenham side in erratic form.
