--- 71’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAALLLL!! It's 3-2 and it's raining goals here at Anfield! Amavi surges forward down the left-hand side and Gestede towers above Skrtel at the back post to guide his cross home with a trademark header. ---
--- 69’ Substitution Traore comes on for Villa as Sherwood makes his second change of the match. It was quiet game for Grealish, in truth, and it's a fair call from the former Spurs boss. ---
(69’) And breathe! Two goals in a matter of minutes at Anfield sees this game spring into life. You can't rule out more goals as it's so end-to-end at the moment.
--- 67’ Assist Assist by Philippe Coutinho. ---
--- 67’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAALLL!! It's 3-1 and it's Sturridge again! Just as Villa think they're back in this game, Sturridge plays a beautiful one-two with Coutinho inside the penalty area and sweeps the ball past Guzan. ---
--- 66’ Assist A. Hutton gave the assist. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAALLL!! It's 2-1 and Villa have a lifeline! Hutton bursts down the right flank past Lucas and sends a cross towards the back post, which Gestede meets and guides home with aplomb. Game on at Anfield! ---
(65’) Liverpool are still continuing to have the lion's share of the ball at the moment but Villa are standing firm defensively and are looking to make a couple of more substitutions in order to try and get back into things.
(63’) Clyne comes in field from the right-hand side and plays in Sturridge, who just about does enough to dig the ball out from his feet under pressure from Lescott but the effort lacks power as it flies into Guzan's arms.
(61’) Wow! That was outstanding from Sturridge but the role of Lucas in that goal musn't be understated. He's picked his passes well all game today and he cleverly played in Milner, which brought about the assist.
--- 60’ Substitution Sherwood rolls the dice for the first time in this match as he takes off Sanchez, who has played well today. It's clear he wants more attacking, creative options on the pitch and Veretout enters the pitch as a result. ---
--- 59’ Assist J. Milner gave the assist. ---
--- 59’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAALLL!! It's 2-0 to Liverpool! Milner chests the ball down under pressure from Gueye and plays a perfect pass over the top to Sturridge, who strikes it first time past Guzan magnificently. What a finish. ---
(56’) Coutinho picks up the ball in the middle of the park and sprays a fabulous pass forward towards Ings, but Lescott comes across and bravely sticks his head out to divert the ball away towards Guzan. Top defending from the former Everton man.
(54’) Coutinho steps up to take a free-kick and cleverly sweeps it low around the Villa wall but Guzan remains equal to it, as he dives low to his left and gobbles up the ball. It was an excellent idea from the Liverpool man.
(52’) CLOSE! Milner collects from a Sturridge knockdown and forces a brilliant save from Guzan with a left-footed effort. The Villa goalkeeper tips it out wide to an onrushing Clyne, but Amavi gets his body in the way in the nick of time and prevents Liverpool extending their lead.
(50’) Grealish drives forward through midfield but Sakho does enough as he slides in and sees the ball slide out wide. Hutton collects the spillage from the Frenchman and finds Sinclair, who heads wide of Mignolet between the Liverpool sticks.
(48’) WIDE! Grealish loses the ball under a challenge by Milner and Clyne plays a lovely low cross towards Ings, which Coutinho collects but it diverts out for a corner as Richards blocks his shot from close range.
(46’) Welcome back! Villa get us underway again for the second half, with neither side making a personnel change to their starting lineups during the half-time interval.
Coutinho has been in inspired form alongside the likes of Moreno and Milner but Gestede passed up a great chance to restore parity after lashing the ball wide of Mignolet's goal from a poor Can back pass. Westwood also had a shot deflected narrowly wide of the post and therefore Rodgers' men still have their work cut out despite their slender lead.
Milner's first goal for Liverpool against his former club is the difference at the break as the Reds lead Villa by one goal to nil. The hosts were the better for long spells in the first half but their opponents got stronger towards the back end of the opening 45 minutes.
HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-0 ASTON VILLA
(45’) Sanchez takes a blow to the head and hits the deck immediately and the referee therefore blows his whistle for a suspension in play, as the Villa man receives treatment from the physios.
(43’) Clyne's header back towards Skrtel flies beyond the Liverpool centre-back and the lack of communication almost benefits Villa as Sinclair rushes onto the loose ball, but his curling effort from distance flies easily into the arms of Mignolet. The visitors are getting stronger as time ticks on in the first half.
(41’) SAVE! Hutton curls in a delightful cross past Sakho and towards Gestede, but Mignolet rushes off his line and punches clear. From the rebound, Westwood powers in a low effort which gets diverted out for a Villa corner.
(39’) Gueye screams in frustration as the referee ignores his protests for a free-kick as Lucas nips his break forward in the bud, before the man in charge of the cards issues one seconds later as Richards closes down Sturridge from behind.
(37’) Milner plays in two consecutive corners but neither set play comes to anything. As Amavi tries to make a breakaway following the spillage from the second, Lucas steps in quickly and snuffs out the danger with a solid challenge.
(35’) Hutton moans to the referee as he tumbles to the floor under a challenge by Moreno near the right-hand side of the pitch. Villa have been much better defensively in the last 10 minutes or so.
(33’) Milner gets a telling off from the referee as he barges into Grealish but minutes later, the Reds goalscorer has to be quick off his feet as Amavi almost catches him with a high boot towards his right leg. Free-kick to the Reds.
(31’) Coutinho finds half a yard of space inside Villa's half and coolly tries to play in Ings with a good pass but the Liverpool striker hands the visitors a free-kick for pulling on Hutton's shirt as he tries to reach the ball.
(29’) Sturridge latches onto Milner's pass to him inside the box and as the Liverpool forward flicks it around to an onrushing Clyne, the ball strikes off Lescott and out for a corner. The crowd appeals for handball but the replay shows that it came off the Villa defender's chest.
(27’) Milner fizzes in a corner towards a queue of players inside the penalty area but Guzan gets a hand to the ball and clears the danger. Sinclair puts the pressure on and forces Moreno to play it back to Mignolet as the attack goes.
(25’) Ings touches down Can's pass towards Milner but it runs away from the Reds captain, who chases down Amavi to retrieve the ball but the former Nice left-back does enough to see it out of bounds for a Villa goal-kick.
(23’) Villa go back to being all over the place at the back as Richards puts too much pace on his back pass to Guzan, who touches it out wide for Moreno to run onto. The cross from the Spaniard comes to nothing but it was woeful play at the back again from the Villans.
(21’) BIG MISS! Hutton plays a misplaced cross to Can and the Liverpool man poorly squares the ball to Gestede, who slices an effort wide of the goal from close range unmarked. What a chance that was for the former Blackburn Rovers man to draw the visitors level.
(20’) Liverpool press forward looking to add to their solitary goal but Sanchez wins several tackles in a row down the right-hand side of the field to stem the flow of attacks from the hosts. Fabulous defending from the Villa midfield anchorman.
(18’) Ings plays a cute lofted pass over the top of Hutton to Sturridge and as the Liverpool striker lays the ball off to an onrushing Milner, Richards prevents the midfielder from getting a shot away from inside the box as it trickles out for a goal-kick to Villa.
(16’) Coutinho causes Hutton a few problems again down the left and wins another corner for Liverpool. Milner plays in the set piece towards Sturridge but Gestede snuffs out the danger for Villa. The hosts are still on the front foot and are looking for more goals.
(14’) Clyne marauds forward down the right and feeds in Milner, who forces a great tackle from Amavi for a Liverpool corner. Moreno curls in the resulting set play but Richards clears for the visitors at the back stick.
(12’) CLOSE! Can pumps a long ball forward towards Ings but as the pass bypasses the Liverpool man, Sinclair relaxes with Moreno on his case and lets the Spaniard in. The ex-Sevilla man drives a low cross towards the face of goal but Guzan collects well.
(10’) Sinclair gets the better of Can down the left-hand side and after a few twists and turns, he tests Mignolet's resolve with a powerful left-footed effort towards the near post but the Belgian shot-stopper manages to save comfortably.
(8’) In similar fashion to how Liverpool's goal was engineered, Can breaks through the Villa midfield lines and plays in Ings, who forces a decent save from Guzan with a low effort just outside the penalty area. The visitors need to close space much quicker if they're to come away from Anfield with positive result today.
(6’) Sturridge plays in Milner making tracks further forward and the former Villa man ghosts past Sanchez and sends in a high cross towards the back post, which Guzan collects with Sturridge lurking. Straight up the other end, Gestede towers above Sakho but sends his header just wide of Mignolet between the Liverpool sticks.
(4’) Rodgers needed an early goal to lift the confidence amongst the Liverpool faithful inside Anfield today and Milner showed exactly why he has the captain's armband by stepping up to the plate when needed. Villa boss Sherwood will be massively disappointed nobody got out to prevent the Reds skipper from getting a shot off.
--- 2’ Assist The assist came from Philippe Coutinho. ---
--- 2’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAALLLLL!! It's 1-0 to Liverpool! Coutinho spins away from Westwood and plays in Milner, who picks up the ball deep into Villa's half unmarked and drives it into the bottom corner past Guzan. What a start by the Reds! ---
(1’) Liverpool get us underway here at Anfield. The man in charge of the cards for today's encounter is Jonathan Moss.
Both sets of players are stripped and raring to go as they leave the tunnel and enter the field here at Anfield. We are just moments away from seeing the action unfold.
In this fixture last season, Agbonlahor scored after just nine minutes in what proved to be the winner as Aston Villa won 1-0 against Liverpool. In fact, the Midlands outfit are unbeaten in their last four visits to Anfield.
ASTON VILLA substitutes: Bunn, Clark, Veretout, Clark, Bacuna, Ayew, Gil, Traore.
ASTON VILLA (4-3-3): Guzan; Hutton, Richards (c), Lescott, Amavi; Sanchez, Westwood, Gueye; Sinclair, Gestede, Grealish.
LIVERPOOL substitutes: Bogdan, Toure, Gomez, Lallana, Allen, Origi, Ibe.

TEAM NEWS: Sherwood has made two changes to the Villa side which started their 1-0 defeat against West Bromwich Albion last weekend. Idrissa Gueye comes in to replace Carles Gil, while midweek hero Rudy Gestede starts up front in place of Gabriel Agbonlahor, who is absent through injury.
TEAM NEWS: Rodgers has made just one change to the Liverpool side which started their last league outing against Norwich City, with Danny Ings being given the chance to continue his goalscoring form of late in place of the injured Christian Benteke. The Belgian misses out on the chance to play against his former paymasters.
Liverpool have conceded seven goals in their last three games and aren't scoring enough at the other end either, while Aston Villa currently sit 17th in the league table with four points to their name. The Villans haven't tasted victory in the top flight since beating Bournemouth 1-0 on the opening day of the campaign.
Both Brendan Rodgers and Tim Sherwood picked up vital wins in the League Cup in midweek to keep their heads above water, as speculation mounts over their respective futures. It's the Premier League that is becoming an obstacle for them, though, and the three points on offer on Merseyside today is much-needed for the two managers.
Good afternoon and welcome to our LIVE text commentary of today's match between Liverpool and Aston Villa from Anfield. I'm Matthew Judge and I will be your host for the match, which kicks off at 3pm.

I'm afraid that's all I've got time for today. Thanks very much for joining me and enjoy the rest of you weekend. Until next time I've been Chris Baker.
United were some way of their best but Van Gaal will be delighted with the professional manner that his players went about their business. An easy win with plenty of gas left in the tank for the bigger challenges that are yet to come. The Red Devils seem to be gelling nicely and took full advantage of Manchester City's defeat at Tottenham. Can they keep it up and sustain a real title tilt? Only time will tell...
As for Sunderland - well where do they go from here? The players appear to still be trying for their manager and while that remains the case there seems little point in sacking Dick Advocaat. Unfortunately for the Mackems they don't look like scoring many goals or keeping many cleansheets. And as any football fan will tell you that combination is a recipe for disaster. They look certainities for relegation on the basis of today.
This match had home banker written all over it and so it proved as United run out comfortable winners. This final score hadn't looked likely after 44 minutes but two goals either side of half time ended this game as a contest. The understanding of the attacking trio of Rooney, Martial and Memphis is improving with each game. Van Gaal will be confident of a successful season if they can maintain this type of form.
(90’) FULL TIME 3-0. United see the game out with no alarms. Knocking the ball around amongst themselves under little pressure. Sunderland know that they are beaten and it will be another disappointing journey home for them and their fans.
--- 90’ Goal! GOAL! MATA makes it three! A typically calm and composed finish from the Spanish international. Ashley Young tormented Billy Jones before smashing the ball across goal, it lands at the feet of Mata who finishes with some aplomb into the top corner. Game, set and match. ---
(90’) We are going into three minutes of added time at the end of this game with the home side easing to another win that will put them top of the pile. It has not been vintage Manchester United but it hasn't needed to be to beat a distinctly average Sunderland side.
(87’) Rooney nearly fashions a goalscoring opportunity all of his own making after making the sort of swashbuckling run that we were so used to seeing from him in his younger days. The United striker picked up the ball just inside the Sunderland half and took the fight to the heart of the opposition. Kaboul eventually denies him.
--- 85’ Yellow card L. Cattermole gets yellow. ---
(85’) Almost another individual error from O'Shea costs Sunderland a goal as the former United defender is caught in possession on the edge of the penalty area but Rooney can't make the most of it and Van Aanholt gets his teammate out of jail.
(83’) Sunderland are by no means throwing the towel in but there is a desperate lack of quality about their play at times. United on the other hand are being very professional and are taking no chances on the ball.
(81’) United are rather toying with Sunderland at the moment and are perhaps guilty of overplaying at times. Schneiderlin is the culprit on this occasion as he looks to play in Martial rather than having a shot from the top of the box.
(79’) It appears that Jermain Defoe can't be as near match fit as Dick Advocaat would have us believe. Otherwise it seems very odd that he has not been introduced with Sunderland chasing the game. There has definitely been an improvement from the Black Cats but not enough to seriously trouble their hosts.
--- 77’ Substitution A. Young comes on for M. Depay. ---
(77’) SAVE! Mata stings the palms of Pantilimon with a swerving low shot from the edge of the box. The giant Sunderland goalkeeper got down very quickly there to keep it out. When it left his foot Mata must have thought it was destined for the bottom corner.
(75’) The match is just going through a little bit of a lull at present which is probably down to the raft of changes that both sides have made. The life and fight seems to be draining out of Sunderland and a third goal for the home team looks far more likely.
--- 74’ Substitution P. Jones enters the game and replaces D. Blind. ---
(73’) Memphis yet again races down the left wing and looks to stand the ball up at the back post for Martial but the United winger slices his cross and it goes out of play. The front three of the Reds looks very promising and the Old Trafford supporters will be excited to see them progress as the season develops.
(71’) As expected World Cup winner Schweinsteiger has come on in place of Michael Carrick as United look to see this game out. There is a real swagger about the play of the home side at the moment and Van Gaal will want another goal to end this as a contest once and for all.
--- 70’ Substitution O. Toivonen is done for the day. S. Larsson is his replacement. ---
(69’) OVER! Martial's performance probably deserves a goal and he is a whisker away from making it 3-0 with a looping header that just creeps over the crossbar. Sunderland are having to take risks now but it is leaving them very exposed at the back.
--- 68’ Substitution B. Schweinsteiger enters the game and replaces M. Carrick. ---
(67’) CHANCE! Unbelievable opportunity for Memphis to put this game to bed but he can only shoot straight at Pantilimon with the entire goal at his mercy. Martial turned over possession and raced clear before unselfishly laying the ball onto his teammate. That really should be match over.
(65’) The game is beginning to get a little stretched and Dick Advocaat will hope that if his side can get a goal back then it could be game on again. It is vital that they don't go further behind.
(63’) Almost some champagne football from the Red Devils as Memphis is inches away from heading in Mata's cross. The United attacker then does well to recover possession and find Rooney who backheels it to Martial, who is proving himself to be a real handful. The ball eventually gets fired across the six yard box but Sunderland have enough men back to snuff out the threat.
(61’) SAVE! Not for the first time today, De Gea's legs come to United's rescue. Van Aanholt made a lung busting run from left back and was played in by Borini. It was a difficult angle for the defender and he did well to hit the target.
(59’) It is usually around this time in a game that Van Gaal switches Carrick for Schweinsteiger. With a Champions League fixture in mind, that substitution can't be far away.
(57’) Rooney absolutely loves that long diagonal ball out wide to Valencia and has tried to play that pass whenever possible. The United right back has given Van Aanholt a very difficult game so far.
(55’) That opportunity seems to have sparked Sunderland into life and they are now enjoying their first real spell of sustained pressure on the United goal. Lens and then Fletcher throw the ball into the penalty area but Smalling and Blind are unmoved at the heart of the home defence.
(53’) CHANCE! M'Vila's free-kick is a good one and the ball falls to Toivonen who stabs the ball goalwards but his effort is cleared away by De Gea with his feet. There can't be another goalkeeper in the Premier League that uses their feet to save the ball more than the United stopper.
(52’) United are really starting to get on top here and enjoy themselves. In saying that, Fletcher does well to nick the ball and launch a counter attack which is then abruptly halted by Schneiderlin who goes into the book. Positive play there from the Sunderland substitute.
--- 50’ Yellow card B. Jones is cautioned by the referee. ---
(50’) Yellow card for Billy Jones, with a cynical tackle on Memphis who had turned away from the Sunderland full back. That was a very easy decision for the referee there. It might feel like a very long second half at this rate for the away side.
(48’) United are heading towards the summit of the Premier League at the present time. If it was mission difficult at one-nil down for Sunderland, is it now mission impossible for the Black Cats? They've got an absolute mountain to climb now. Dick Advocaat must be absolutely furious, it was far too easy for United to double their advantage.
--- 46’ Assist A. Martial provided the assist. ---
--- 46’ Goal! GOAL! And almost instanteously United are 2-0 up. Wayne Rooney is off the mark in the Premier League after some brilliant work in the build up from Anthony Martial. England's record goalscorer knees the ball into the net from close range. Dreadful start to the second half. It took United just 38 seconds to add to their lead. Incredible. ---
--- 46’ Substitution A. Johnson is done for the day. S. Fletcher is his replacement. ---
(46’) And Advocaat hasn't wasted any time in making a change. Steven Fletcher is preparing to enter the fray in place of the hapless Adam Johnson, who had a first half to forget. United then get the second period going.
The United bench looks incredibly strong with the likes of Fellaini, Young, Schweinsteiger and Herrera waiting in the wings - ready to rub salt into the Sunderland wounds. You can't imagine it will be long before Advocaat considers introducing Fletcher and/or Defoe into the action to give Fabio Borini some much needed help. Jermain Lens has looked lively at times but hasn't seen enough of the ball to be a consistent threat.
Louis Van Gaal on the other hand will be feeling a whole lot happier after seeing his team struggle to find their usual fluency against the side that are rock bottom of the Premier League. United have been way below their best but have crucially got their noses in front. The Red Devils will feel confident that they can add to their lead in the second half with Sunderland forced to abandon their totally defensive mindset.
Goals change games as the cliche goes and Advocaat will be sick to his stomach at the break. Sunderland were so close to going in level but they were totally undone by a rare moment of genuine quality. His half time teamtalk will have changed dramatically with his side conceding such a late goal. Can they turn it around in the second half? It's going to be a very big ask of his team who must be feeling deflated in the dressing room.
--- 45’ +4 Assist Mata gave the assist. ---
--- 45’ +4 Goal! GOAL! MEMPHIS BREAKS THE DEADLOCK ON THE STROKE OF HALF TIME! A simply brilliant pass from Daley Blind finds Mata who lays it on a plate for the Manchester United number seven. Horrible timing for Sunderland. ---
(45’) And that is half-time here at Old Trafford 1-0 to United. A bitter blow for Sunderland who had worked so hard during that first period.
(45’) It's no surprise, given the amount of stoppages in this first half that there will be a minimum of four minutes of injury time to be added on. Can Sunderland hold on?
(44’) This is as well as O'Shea and Kaboul have played together this season, which might not being saying much on recent form but the Sunderland centre backs have very solid so far. If they can get through to half-time at 0-0 they will be delighted with the first fourty-five minutes.
(42’) Valencia and Darmian are giving the home side great width on the overlap with Mata and Memphis tucking in on the flanks. You get the feeling that it will be one of the full backs that unlocks this stubborn Sunderland rearguard action.
(40’) Manchester United are certainly huffing and puffing but they can't find that killer pass at the moment to blow the Sunderland house down. On this occasion Carrick tries to fire the ball into the feet of Rooney but his pass is not on the money and Sunderland clear their lines once again.
--- 38’ Yellow card A. Johnson is yellow-carded. ---
(38’) Martial is absolutely fearless on the ball and looks to beat his man at every opportunity. This time he squares up Billy Jones on the left wing and then goes past him like he isn't there. His cross isn't a bad one but Cattermole is in the right place at the right time to hack it away.
(36’) Adam Johnson isn't having the best of games so far and inexplicably handles the ball on the edge of his own box. It gives Memphis the chance to work the Sunderland goalkeeper from the resulting free-kick, which he duly does but the shot is weak and is easily saved. So far, so good for the Black Cats.
(34’) Anthony Martial feels the full force of a typically robust challenge from Lee  Cattermole. The Sunderland stalwart had to get the tackle right as he was the last man. After a bit of attention from the physio the world's most expensive teenager is fine to carry on.
(32’) Borini is lucky to not to be be seriously injured after a clumsy and potentially dangerous challenge by Antonio Valencia. In fairness to the United right back he did slip as he went into the tackle but it wasn't pretty and the Sunderland striker is far from impressed.
(30’) The Old Trafford faithful are just starting to get a little frustrated with what they perceive to be deliberate time wasting from the visitors as well as the slow build up play from their team. Rooney finds some space to turn into and looks to get Martial in on goal but his pass can't find his strike partner.
(28’) Schneiderlin and Carrick are beginning to pull the strings here and are dictating proceedings from the middle of the park. Rooney then picks out Valencia with an excellent cross field pass. The right back wriggles past Van Aanholt but his low centre is well cleared by Kaboul.
(26’) SAVE! Memphis is given far too much room about 25 yards from goal and curls the ball towards the top corner but it is straightforward enough for Pantilimon to tip over the crossbar.
(25’) CHANCE! Out of absolutely nothing Jermain Lens smashes the ball into the legs of David De Gea and so nearly gives the Mackems an unlikely lead. It was a decent strike by the Sunderland winger.
(23’) Memphis goes through the gears and simply glides past a posse of Sunderland player's but tries to do too much and is crowded out by Kaboul. The loose ball breaks to Darmian but his cross is too strong and drifts out of play for a goal kick.
(21’) Sunderland will be reasonably pleased to have got through the first twenty minutes without conceding. The break in play for Cattermole's injury was probably a welcome bit of respite for the away side. It has just disrupted United's rhythm at the moment.
(19’) Slight delay to proceedings as Lee Cattermole is down in the centre circle and is in need of some treatment. The midfielder looks to be in some discomfort but will be able to continue after some work from the magic sponge.
(17’) A mix-up in the Sunderland defence almost leads to a goal or even a red card for the goalkeeper. A hopeful punt forward was chased down by Martial who was sandwiched in between O'Shea and Pantilimon, who was also close to handling it outside the area. The upshot is a Manchester United free-kick that Juan Mata crashes into the wall. Let off for the away side there.
(15’) SHOT! Mata works half a yard on the edge of the box and his low left-footed shot is deflected just wide of the post for a United corner. Depay whips the ball in but Sunderland deal with the set piece well. Pressure building on the visitors goal.
(13’) The pattern of this game is what you would have anticipated pre-match. The home side are seeing a lot of the ball and are being very patient in possession while the Black Cats are quite happy to let United have the ball in non-threatening areas.
(11’) Save by De Gea but the United goalkeeper was never troubled by John O'Shea's weak header. Sunderland had done well to keep the ball alive after a deep freekick was thrown into the area. Much better from the visitors.
(9’) The Red Devils are already knocking on the door here and this time it is Carrick who picks out Depay with a lovely reverse pass but the Dutchman's first touch is poor and will run through to Pantilimon.
(7’) Freekick in a dangerous position for United, just to the right hand side of the Sunderland penalty area. Mata takes it but he can't beat the head of Yann M'Vila who clears it away to safety.
(5’) Darmian this time flies down the flank on the overlap and clips in a decent ball towards Martial but the cross is just too heavy for the French striker. The ball does find its way to Juan Mata who curls it back into the danger area but it is overhit and goes harmlessly out of play.
(3’) Almost half a chance for United as Mata plays a wonderful ball over the head of van Aanholt and Valencia races onto it but can't quite keep the ball in and it will be a Sunderland goal kick. Good signal of intent from the home side.
(2’) Manchester United as you might expect have started off this match in confident fashion. Quite content to knock the ball around and try to get Sunderland out of their defensive shape.
(1’) Sunderland, in their change strip of all green will get us underway here. Manchester United are off course in their famous red, white and black kit. The away side will attack the Stretford End in this first half.
Sunderland will not want to give anything away, particularly early on in this match but you suspect that if they simply attempt to park the bus at Old Trafford there will only be one winner. With the likes of Adam Johnson, Jermain Lens and Fabio Borini in their side there is enough to keep the Manchester United defence busy.
Will new boy Anthony Martial be able to continue his sensational start to life in a Manchester United shirt? He'll certainly fancy his chances against a Sunderland back four that has looked decidedly shaky so far this season. Another man that will be desperate to get on the scoresheet will be a certain Wayne Rooney, who is yet to get off the mark in the Premier League despite netting in the cup competitions.
SUNDERLAND SUBS: Mannone, Larsson, Gomez, Defoe, Coates, Yedlin and Fletcher.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Romero, Jones, Young, Herrera, Fellaini, Pereira and Schweinsteiger.
Former City midfielder Jack Rodwell is injured and is replaced in the starting lineup by Lee Cattermole. Kaboul, Jones and Pantilimon are restored to the eleven that were on the end of another hammering from Manchester City in the Capital One cup in midweek. The Black Cats are desperately out of form and sit bottom of the Premier League which makes the always difficult task of coming to Old Trafford all the more daunting.
SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Pantilimon; Jones, Kaboul, O'Shea, van Aanholt;  M'Vila, Cattermole; Johnson, Toivonen, Lens; Borini.
Unsuprisingly, Louis Van Gaal makes a number of changes to the United side that defeated Ipswich in the League Cup during the week. Carrick, Memphis Depay, Martial and Schneiderlin come in while Darmian starts at left back in place of Ashley Young. With Manchester City being soundly beaten at White Hart Lane, the Red Devils have the chance to go top of the table with a wn this afternoon.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Valencia, Smalling, Blind, Darmian; Carrick, Schneiderlin; Mata, Rooney (c), Depay; Martial.

FULL TIME - Southampton 3-1 Swansea: Saints took the lead through Van Dijk early on and added to their lead with strikes from Tadic and Mane after the interval, showing a far more clinical edge than their opponents. SWANSEA (4-3-3): Fabianski; Naughton, Fernandez, Williams, Taylor; Ki, Shelvey, Cork; Ayew, Gomis, Sigurdsson.

SWANSEA TEAM NEWS: Despite a bright start to the season, Jefferson Montero finds himself dropped to the bench with Ki Sung-Yueng taking his spot in order to tighten up the midfield. Monk's much-changed side suffered a disappointing elimination from the League Cup at the hands of Hull City in midweek, but it's a far more familiar line-up today.
SOUTHAMPTON TEAM NEWS: Jay Rodriguez, Shane Long and Sadio Mane all scored two goals apiece in the 6-0 League Cup victory over MK Dons in midweek, but only the Senegalese features in the starting line-up today. Graziano Pelle returns after missing that trip with a foot injury as Koeman makes three changes from last weekend's defeat to Manchester United with Oriol Romeu, Matthew Targett and Maya Yoshida replaced by Steven Davis, Ryan Bertrand and Cedric.
Swansea began the campaign with a draw at Chelsea, which they followed up with an impressive victory over Manchester United at the end of August. Despite the defeat to Watford and the goalless draw with Everton that have followed, Garry Monk's men remain eighth and will be eager to get back to winning ways.
Southampton's impressive start to the previous season eventually tailed off as they finished seventh in the Premier League. But this time around, after failing to secure a place in the Europa League group stage, they have picked up just six points in their opening six games. Drastic improvements are needed if Ronald Koeman's men are to dart up the table, and these are the sort of games that they'll need to be winning if they are to do so.

Bournemouth will feel hard done by after putting in such an impressive performance during the second half, but they only have themselves to blame after it took them almost 70 minutes to get going. Up until then it was largely comfortable for Stoke, but the hosts dropped far too deep in the second half, allowing the visitors to hit them hard as they tired. However, Diouf was there to save the day with a lovely header that results in the Potters' first league victory of the season.

Games between Watford and Palace have a tendency to be exciting and goal-filled encounters, and this afternoon’s is likely to be no different. Hornets’ fans will have painful memories of the last time that these two sides met, as a narrow Eagles victory, made possible by an extra-time Kevin Phillips penalty, resulted in a 1-0 defeat for today’s hosts in the 2013 Championship play-off final. As a result, they will want nothing more than to inflict a defeat on the side that forced them to wait for their Premier League return.
However, seeing off an impressive Palace side won’t be an easy task, as the South Londoners have looked full of attacking flair and capability in their opening six games of the season. Thanks to impressive wins against Norwich City, Aston Villa and Chelsea, the Eagles currently sit in 10th place in the table with nine points, although their last two league encounters ended in narrow defeats against Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur. However, they will be quietly confident about their chances of picking up a positive result from today’s clash, which will be the first Premier League meeting between these two sides.
After a patient yet solid start to life back in the Premier League, Watford have been absolutely flying over the past two weeks, and they head into this afternoon’s encounter looking to secure their third successive top-flight victory for the first time since 1987. They certainly have recent history on their side, as the Hornets have looked excellent at home so far this season, failing to lose a single game or concede any goals. They have also impressed going forward, and in-form Odion Ighalo will no doubt play an important role in today’s clash. The Nigerian striker, who has hit the back of the net three times in their last two games, has scored 20 goals in 24 league appearances in 2015, more than any other player in the top four English divisions.

Everton remain unbeaten on their travels this season and much of that has to do with the adjustments made by Roberto Martinez. There are no new faces in defence, but the Toffees are organising themselves much better at the back and it has paid great dividends early in the season. They have been a bit inconsistent in front of goal, but have too much talent in attack for that to be an issue. Their forward line will be put to the test this evening, however, against a Baggies side who haven’t conceded since the third week of the season.

You can see how much they improve week-to-week by simply looking at the results – the progress under Pulis has been staggering. They face a tough test this evening but the atmosphere should be great at the Hawthorns and, with everything starting to click for the Baggies, there could be an upset on the cards.

(90’) Murray got on the end of the ball and cut inside in the box, unleashing a very solid shot that Pantilimon had to react quickly to parry! That was so nearly the third for the home side.
--- 90’ Substitution Ritchie, scorer of tonight's wonder goal, comes off for Smith, to massive applause around the ground. He gave the fans something to celebrate today! ---
(88’) Sunderland have a very late free-kick here, which M'Vila plays into the box from roughly 20 yards out. Jones gets behind the defence and tries to head it in but he misses the chance, to Boruc's delight.
(86’) The initial effort hits the wall and bounced kindly for Ritchie, who tries an acrobatic shot that is cleared! It comes back for the player who crosses it to a teammate, who thumps it off the crossbar, before Ritchie fires another shot that Pantilimon saves! The entire play is soon annulled, however, with the flag up for offside.
--- 85’ Yellow card O. Toivonen is yellow-carded. ---
(84’) Toivonen concedes a free-kick right on the edge of his own box as Gosling raced into the area with speed and purpose and drew several players over to him to stop his run. It's yet another booking for the Sunderland, who have endured an afternoon they'll want to forget as soon as possible.
(83’) Good pressing down the left from the visitors who are desperately trying to create something - anything, really - here, but they lose it too easily and Bournemouth counter in numbers. Francis tries a cross but it's overhit and sails harmlessly out for a throw-in.
(82’) Free-kick for Bournemouth now deep in their own half, which is rolled across the pitch and pressed forward, though eventually cleared by the visitors.
--- 80’ Yellow card D. Gosling receives a yellow card. ---
(80’) Ohhh close from Toivonen! He's in a great position in the box and rises tall to challenge for a header but the ball is played just a whisker too high and he can't connect.
(79’) Bournemouth have a foothold on the ball and are trying to use the numerical advantage but Gosling bundles over Johnson and becomes the first player on the home side to be booked this afternoon.
(77’) This is all but over now for Sunderland, who are doing well to keep the ball but have a mountain to climb in front of them and just cannot breach the home side's backline.
--- 76’ Substitution Wilson comes off to raptorous applause for Murray as Bournemouth now make a change. The ensuing free-kick from Kaboul's clumsy challenge is played right into the arms of Pantilimon. ---
--- 74’ Red card! KABOUL IS SENT OFF! He gets a second yellow for kicking Wilson in the leg while trying to clear the ball. In all honesty, that's been coming all night, and now Sunderland have to cope being down to ten men while down two goals! ---
--- 72’ Substitution Advocaat is showing his disdain for his strikers' performance as Borini comes off not long after Defoe for Johnson, who will be asked to have maximum impact in a very short amount of time. ---
(71’) Pugh's shot gets deflected out for a corner and this could all but wrap the match up if they can get their third now! It's played short, however, before hoofed up towards Gosling, who lays it off for Daniels. This is all down the left flank and the home side are doing very well not to lose the ball.
(69’) Bournemouth play with fire a little bit when Francis is closed down by Lens deep in his own box, but to his credit, he does enough to get it to Boruc who clears it out.
--- 68’ Substitution Surman again involved in a solid play for the home side, playing quick passes to keep the ball circulating. Defoe is substituted off for Fletcher, and he comes out to applause from fans who fondly remember his time at the club. ---
(67’) A nice touch from Surman to keep the ball away from Sunderland's attack after Cook's header away from the box was a little too close to the opposition.
(66’) The momentum looks to be shifting back to Bournemouth, with O'Kane getting the ball in a great central area with his first touch. His team are unable to build off of it and Sunderland work it to Pantilimon before distributing it safely around their defenders.
--- 65’ Substitution Tomlin comes off to raptorous applause from the crowd, and he turns to clap his hand at the supporters in return. On comes O'Kane - a pair of fresh legs to run at this wobbly Sunderland defence. ---
--- 63’ Yellow card Ritchie cuts out a Rodwell pass out high, and on the counter-attack, Francis pulls wide ahead of Borini, causing the Italian to clip his foot to bring him down. He's duly cautioned for that challenge, joining three of his teammates in the referee's book. ---
(62’) Van Aanholt races forward and plays a cleverly weighted pass towards the back post, but it's cleared by Distin, who has not had much to do today. Rodwell picks up the ball soon after but slots it directly out of play.
(61’) Borini takes the ball down with his chest and first times a volley from roughly 30 yards out that nearly dips in under the bar but goes just over - had that been a goal, it surely would have been a contender for goal of the season just far. In a match with Ritchie's goal, that's saying something!
(60’) Now that's some excellent defending on Wilson, who Coates slides the ball off of just inside of the box! The striker has clearly done some damage today, with three of the four visiting defenders booked.
(59’) Bournemouth's pressing eventually forces the visitors to play it all the way back to their goalkeeper, who clears it, causing a series of headers back and forth around the middle of the pitch.
(58’) Van Aanholt plays a throw-in short in a very crowded area but his side work well with it, getting it to the other flank and working it deeper towards the goal.
(56’) Deep throw-in for the home side who have not let the past few minutes rattle them too much. It is cleared out quickly but only results in another, before Pantilimon can take a free-kick. M'Vila is having a chat with the referee before the ball can be played.
(55’) At the very least, that call seems to have given Sunderland a little bit of life, but the players are furious about it being annulled. The home side now are working their way down the right, with Toivonen holding on to it as he seeks options.
(53’) GOOOOAALL SUNDERLAND! NO... IT'S OFFSIDE! That was perhaps their best spell of the game, with Borini influential in winning a corner, and it's played short before being looped into the box. Lens gets a thumping header onto it but it's ruled out for offside! That's a dubious call at best!
(52’) Ah, that's more like it for Sunderland! Off of a corner, a deep delivery finds its way over to Toivonen, who tries to head it towards goal but it's deflected and cleared.
(50’) A high ball comes into the Sunderland box and Wilson and Tomlin look up hopefully, but the tall Pantilimon can collect that without much of a problem. The latter home side player tries to make a run through the defence seconds later but is pick-pocketed from behind.
(48’) More of the same here, despite the substitution, early in this half: Sunderland are still on the backfoot and struggling to make much of an impact, while the home side remain lively and buzzing.
--- 46’ Substitution The second half is now underway! Jordi Gomez, who had a quiet evening, has come off for Rodwell as Advocaat looks to try to change things up in the midfield for his side. ---
Sunderland, meanwhile, need quite a bit more. They need much more from their captain, who is being torn apart at the back; they need more from the midfield, to hold the ball and control the match; and they need more chances being created by their strikers.
No doubt about that: Bournemouth have thoroughly deserved their win, with several players in particular having a great half, including Pugh, Cook, and Wilson. They've been full of energy and thrust this afternoon.
(45’) Into the second of three minutes of extra time here, and Borini has raced forward to win his side a deep throw-in. As soon as the clock hits 48 minutes, however, the whistle is blown and thus ends the half!
(45’) Tomlin performs a Zidane esque flick of the ball in the air, whipping it over Kaboul - as if the centre-back hasn't endured enough humiliation thus far - but the visitors are spared further blushes when a teammate rushes over to clear.
(44’) Francis touches the free-kick off to the onrushing Ritchie, but his shot is deflected by the wall. Cook and Wilson keep possession down the left flank, before Pugh centers it, and the home side are just irrepressible at the moment.
--- 43’ Yellow card Kaboul takes down Wilson on a counter-attack and the home side now have a great free-kick just outside the box. The captain is having a nightmare, sticking far too close to the striker and allowing him to use his acceleration and turning to drag him every which way! ---
(41’) Ritchie goes down in a central position in Sunderland's half and his team want a free-kick but the referee refuses to award one. Tomlin takes the ball and nearly dribbles half the opposition but can't get a shot off!
(40’) BORUC SAVE! Defoe was sent clear-though with a clever turn - not unlike Wilson's in the opening goal- but the goalie came off his line, made himself big, and stopped the shot with his body! What a save!
(39’) Jones twists back and forth down the flank and tries to get a good cross in, but it's out for a goal-kick. Kaboul had defended that well.
(38’) M'Vila tries an ambitious pass over the top, but it goes over the top of everyone, and right into the foot of Boruc. Sunderland will need much better than that in order to try to claw their way back into this.
(35’) For a team that has only tested Boruc once, on a free-kick that headed towards the near post, this is a golden chance for Sunderland. Kaboul's free kick is a rocket and hits Wilson, standing in the wall, square in the chest. The medical team is out to evaluate but it looks like he'll be able to continue.
(34’) The woefully quiet Borini slots a pass wide to Gomez, who interchanges back-and-forth passes with Van Aanholt. The possession eventually ends in a free-kick in a good position when Cook knocks over Defoe, roughly 10 yards outside of the box.
(32’) On a quick attack, Pugh launches the ball deep into the box for Wilson, but Kaboul rises high to nod it out for a corner. On the ground, the English striker has the former Tottenham man beat, but the centre-back has done well in the air to keep the service to a minimum.
(31’) In the first third of the match this has not been much of a contest at all. The good news for the visitors is that it's only been one third, and with so much left to play for, a single goal can change everything.
(30’) Bournemouth's style under Howe is finally bearing fruit for them (at least thus far): they're an exciting side to watch, looking incisive and potentially like scoring on every attack. With a confident Wilson as a focal point, this team believe they can win this - and they're well on their way to just that.
(28’) Absolutely excellent dribbling from Pugh who leaves Jones in his wake to motor down the left and allow his side two chances to shoot, but in both cases, the away side's defence closed down the attacks just before the shots could be released.
(27’) Nearly a superb play from Bournemouth, who had some quick passing and even a dummy on the edge of the box as Tomlin looked to wind up a shot, but for once, the Sunderland centre-backs were not fooled and cleared the danger.
(26’) Sunderland look like they have a better foothold of this now; they're not quite threatening Boruc but they're at least not pinned back in their own box anymore, either. Their midfield has compacted towards the center and made it more difficult for Wilson to get service.
--- 24’ Yellow card B. Jones gets yellow. ---

(23’) Lens, who's also been quiet so far, cuts inside and whips in a cross that Boruc gathers before releasing quickly. On the counter-attack, Jones is booked for a foul just outside of the box.
(22’) The game's become a little niggly now, with cheap fouls and free-kicks coming left and right in the midfield. Defoe is urging his side forward, clapping them on, though he's had very little service or activity thus far.
(20’) Kaboul absolutely cannot handle Wilson at the moment, pulling him down yet again on a long pass from Cook that wins Howe's men a free-kick. Francis tries to send it to Distin in the box but it's cleared, and Gosling loses possession on the follow-up.
(19’) Now this is far better from Sunderland, who are putting the Bournemouth defence under pressure with sustained possession near their box. The home side are able to whip away a clearance and win a throw-in but they're finding it a little bit harder to make forays forward.
(17’) Jones takes a throw-in deep in Bournemouth's half, and he gets the pass back before Daniels tackles him. It looks as though he's won the ball cleanly but the referee awards a free kick that Gomez tries to play into the near post, drawing Boruc into a solid diving save!
--- 14’ Yellow card Coates pulls down Wilson and earns a booking as well as giving away a free-kick about halfway through the visitor's half. Daniels takes the free-kick that Pantilimon has to rise high to gather, but he misses and watches it luckily go over the line for a goal-kick. The visitors are just a mess at the back. ---
(13’) Sunderland have one foray forward but it comes to naught, and soon it's back with the home side, who comfortably corral it deep in their own half. M'Vila in particularly is struggling to pass to teammates not under pressure, and his distribution has proven risky for his team early this game.
(11’) This is all unraveling so quickly for Advocaat. He was hesitant to stay with the club this summer and given their nightmare start to the season - nevertheless this match - surely many will be wondering if he should have walked away!
--- 9’ Goal! RITCHIE GOLAZO! OH MY WORD! THAT WAS ABSOLUTELY SENSATIONAL! The ball is cleared from the corner and falls for Ritchie, who volleys it from outside of the box with his first touch and finds the top left corner of the net, leaving Pantilimon with no chance! That was his first ever Premier League goal and the home side are 2-0 up in the first ten minutes!! ---
(8’) M'Vila nudges over Pugh to gift a free-kick to the Howe's men, who play it quickly and earn a corner when the ball is knocked over the line by Coates. Sunderland are all over the place at the moment and they simply cannot get the ball with any kind of consistency.
(6’) The home side now are full of confidence and Wilson is roaming into the box, looking for a midfield to make a run forward but none come. He's forced to play it wide and now his team are keeping it well, to the left of the Sunderland area.
--- 4’ Assist Assist by D. Gosling. ---
--- 4’ Goal! GGOOOOAAAAALLLLLLL WILSON! And that was a superb finish from one of the Premier League's newest danger man. Gosling slipped it to him just outside of the box and he turns right around Kaboul as if he were not even there before slotting it past Pantilimon! 1-0 to the home side! ---
(3’) Daniels leads the charge in the home side's first foray forward to Sunderland's box, sending in a low, incisive cross that Pantilimon scoops up easily.
(2’) M'Vila wins it in the heart of his midfield and slots it over to Jones, who can't find an outlet and has to switch flanks under pressure. The visitors win a free-kick in Bournemouth's half and look to play it short.

We're just moments away from the kick-off now!

Hello all and welcome to our live match covereage of Bournemouth vs Sunderland! It's gameweek 6 in the Premier League and these are already two sides desperate for points. Full time at Villa Park and West Brom win the Midland derby! Sherwood will be disappointed with the lack of creativity today, whereas Pulis will be more than delighted his side executed his tactics to perfection. Thanks for joining us for this Premier League clash.

(47’) Scott Sinclair, who has largely been a spectaor in this game, has been taken off for Gestede as it seems like Villa switch to a 4-4-2.

(45’) Only one minute added time at the end of the first half. Berahino's free-kick is the last of the action from the starting 45 minutes and draws it to a close.

Neither Sherwood or Pulis will be unhappy with their respective sides performances so far, but still the goalkeepers are yet to be tested. However, Watford have kept a clean sheet in three of their last four league matches, while the Tyneside club have not scored in four games.
Watford finished second in the Championship last term, only a point off winners Bournemouth, to advance back to the top flight. They tied their first three games against Everton, Southampton and West Brom, and also drew a blank as they fell at Manchester City. A goalless draw at Manchester United in August has been their brightest moment in the league so far.

West Ham will travel to the Etihad beaming with confidence having already registered rare away victories over Arsenal and Liverpool. Slaven Bilic has the Hammers playing responsible, disciplined and attractive football away from home and they have a real opportunity to build on this dream start with the table toppers appearing a bit vulnerable at the moment. To snatch a third consecutive road victory to start the season would have been almost unimaginable upon the schedule release, but don’t tell them that.
Manchester City began yet another European campaign with defeat on Tuesday and you have to wonder when it starts taking a toll on their confidence. It came at a cost as well, losing skipper Vincent Kompany to injury. Last year they did really well to combat the surplus of matches, losing just once in the league between their first and last group stage match. That being said, the quality of some of the middling Premier League clubs has increased drastically over the summer and with there being very few guaranteed victories, they will have to be careful not to linger on the Juventus loss or it could jeopardize their position atop the table.

Palace will feel hard done by having twice rattled the woodwork on either side of half time, but in the end it simply wasn't enough as Tottenham pull level with them on points.

Crystal Palace’s road form is the envy of the Premier League at the moment – except perhaps for that of West Ham. They’ve enjoyed a lovely start to the season – boosted by some superb dealings in the transfer window – and could jump into a three-way tie for second place by picking up three points today. The belief in their team has to be sky-high at the moment and they will surely come into White Hart Lane with the intention of going for it, setting the stage for what promises to be an entertaining contest.
Tottenham’s subsequent victories over Sunderland and Qarabag will have done them a world of good, but goals continue to be a problem for them. It remains to be seen if Harry Kane is simply in a slump or crashing back down to earth following an unsustainable breakout season. Regardless of the answer, it is doing nothing to help Spurs’ cause. With the Premier League as deep as it has been in years, every dropped point is so costly. Without goals there are no wins and another lengthy run of draws could prove to be the difference between fourth and 10th place.

Milner hangs a cross up to the far post, but Whittaker heads half clear, before winning a free kick from Moreno.

As for Chelsea, their chances of returning to winning ways were given a huge blow on Wednesday when goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was ruled out for three months with a knee injury, whilst Oscar, who hasn’t featured for the Blues since the opening day of the season, is still out after picking up a knock in training before the 3-0 defeat against Manchester City. However, Jose Mourinho will once again be able to call on captain John Terry, who is available for selection following a one-match suspension.
After a lengthy and, at times, heated transfer saga involving John Stones, the focus will surely be on the young centre-back as he comes up against the side that were so desperate to sign him. After struggling last season, Everton have started this campaign in a far more positive manner thanks to a comfortable win away to Southampton and a hard-earned goalless draw against Tottenham Hotspur. They will be aiming to take advantage of Chelsea’s lack of confidence by picking up all three points today, particularly as they have a tough month and a half coming up in which they must face Swansea City, Liverpool, Manchester United and Arsenal in four of their next five games.
For one of the first times in his managerial career, last week’s international break will have been welcomed by Jose Mourinho as a chance for his struggling side to regroup and refocus after suffering a disappointing start to the new season. A narrow and nervy victory away to West Bromwich Albion three weeks ago looked as if it might finally kick-start their campaign, but they were then sent crashing back down to earth by an impressive Crystal Palace team, who handed the Blues their second defeat in three games with a 2-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

FULL TIME - Watford 1-0 Swansea: The Hornets pick up their first three points of the season thanks to Ighalo's second-half strike, downing Garry Monk's previously unbeaten side. Their task was made all the more difficult following the dismissal of Behrami, but the hosts held on for the victory.
(90’) There is the final whistle! Watford have their first win of the season!
(90’) Eder is penalised for a high foot in a challenge with Anya, and that could be it!
(90’) Watford have the ball near the corner of the pitch in Swansea's half. Can they see the game out down there? No, they've given away a throw in. One last chance for the visitors, then, possibly.
(90’) A cross from Montero is attacked by Gomis and Eder at the back post. They help the ball into the middle but Gomes parries it away. Possession is worked back to the Ecuadorian who picks out Fernandez in space. However, the Argentine fails to get his header on target, instead looping it high and wide of the opposite corner!
(90’) Gomis lifts a pass into the box for Eder and the Portuguese goes down under pressure from Cathcart as he tries to spin onto it. The officials see nothing in it, though, and play continues.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card E. Capoue goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) IT SHOULD BE TWO! Watford hit Swansea on the counter-attack after a cleared corner with Jurado finding Berghuis in space at the back post. The Dutchman releases a weak shot which Fabianski keeps out, and the follow-up shot is held by the former Arsenal man too!
(90’) We are going to have a minimum of seven (yes, seven) added minutes!
(89’) Shelvey rifles a shot on goal from 30 yards which bounces just ahead of Gomes, making it hard for the keeper to hold it. He is forced to rush forward and claim the second ball, only just beating Eder to it!
(88’) The final third in Watford's half is becoming extremely congested now. Montero is again the man Swansea look to to make something happen, but his latest cross is sent straight out for a goal kick!
(86’) With Swansea pushing for the equaliser they are starting to leave themselves more and more exposed at the back. Montero twists and turns away from Nyom and Capoue to try and get a cross in but the final touch comes off him before going behind. Can Watford hang on for their first win of the season?
--- 84’ Substitution T. Deeney is replaced with A. Diamanti. ---
(84’) Deeney hands the captain's armband over to Cathcart and makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Diamanti.
(82’) Eder rolls a pass out to Montero on the left before darting straight into the box. The Ecuadorian attempts to pick him out with his cross but Gomes races out to punch it away. Watford then counter-attack with Capoue racing down the left. He tries to poke a pass across to Deeney on the far side but Taylor blocks it!
(80’) Ki attempts to work some space at the top of the box and get a shot away but his touch ends up running into the path of Montero. The former Real Betis man fails to keep his strike down, though, and the ball flies over the top.
(78’) The time-wasting tactics are creeping in for the hosts now, with Nyom staying down after a clash with Montero by the touchline. He managed to knock his clearance off the Ecuadorian for a throw in, but he's encouraged to get back to his feet by the official and that he does.
(76’) Fernandez steps forward and decides to pull the trigger from 30 yards. He gets it all wrong, though, and lashes a woeful effort high into the stands!
(75’) Shelvey spots Montero making a diagonal run into the box from the left and he slides a pass into his path. The Ecuadorian tries to return the favour but Capoue gets a touch on the ball before Watson hoofs it clear. This could be a sign of things to come as Watford try to hold on to their lead.
(74’) Gomes will indeed be fine to continue, and he gets play back underway with a long kick out to Jurado. The Spaniard looks to make his way beyond Naughton but the right-back puts in a good challenge. There are claims for a free-kick but the referee ignores them.
(72’) Gomes is down and receiving attention from the medical staff after a collision with Gomis inside the box. He looks to be in some pain, but this could just be a way of taking the sting out of the game.
--- 71’ Substitution Éder comes on for G. Sigurðsson. ---
--- 71’ Substitution S. Berghuis enters the game and replaces O. Ighalo. ---
(71’) Changes from both sides now. Sigurdsson makes way for Eder for the vistiors while Berghuis replaces Igalo for the hosts.
(70’) Swansea are caught on the break, with Anya driving to the byline and seeing his cross deflect off Fabianski and loop to the top of the box. Capoue strikes it on the volley but his effort is blocked and Jurado's follow-up dribbles wide of the target.
(69’) Monk has Eder readied on the touchline, with the Swans boss clearly not wanting to hang around while his team have the chance to get back into this with momentum on their side.
--- 67’ Yellow card Sung-Yong Ki is cautioned by the referee. ---
(67’) After a prolonged spell on the sidelines receiving treatment from the medical staff, Ayew is invited back onto the pitch to continue. Things are in danger of boiling over as Ki sends Ighalo tumbling in front of the dugouts, but the South Korean is only shown a yellow card.
--- 66’ Substitution A. Abdi is replaced with B. Watson. ---
--- 66’ Substitution J. Cork is done for the day. Sung-Yong Ki is his replacement. ---
(66’) Before play resumes Monk makes another substitution, introducing Ki in Cork's place to add some more invention. There is also a change from Watford, with Abdi making way for Watson.
--- 64’ Red card! V. Behrami is sent for an early shower! ---
(64’) RED CARD! WATFORD ARE DOWN TO 10 MEN! Ayew goes to win the ball with a sliding challenge and Behrami tries to step over it, but ends up standing on the Ghanaian's leg! It was a poor decision from the Swiss and that will put his team under a lot of pressure in the remaining 25 minutes.
(62’) Montero instantly tests Nyom, slowing it down before racing for the byline. However, the right-back manages to keep up with the Ecuadorian and steps in the way to shepherd the ball out of play for a goal kick.
--- 60’ Substitution J. Montero comes on for W. Routledge. ---
(60’) Monk immediately makes a change, replacing Routledge with Montero.
--- 59’ Assist T. Deeney gave the assist. ---
--- 59’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAL!! WATFORD BREAK THE DEADLOCK! It's the Hornets' first Premier League goal of the season at Vicarage Road and it comes from a route one move! A long pass is nodded inside by Deeney, picking out Ighalo who fires beyond Fabianski! ---
(57’) Nyom squeezes a great cross in from the right that bounces towards Deeney. However, the striker fails to connect adequately and fails to divert it on target. He is involved in Watford's next attack, too, flicking a header on for Ighalo who slices wide of the near post after bursting into the box!
(56’) Jurado is wrestled to the ground by Jurado as the Spaniard attempts to spin off him and latch onto a pass down the left. Abdi takes the set-piece but, yet again, it is headed away by Gomis as the chance is not capitalised upon.
(54’) Abdi pulls the trigger once again after finding space 25 yards from goal, but this time his effort is poor and bobbles into the grasp of Fabianski.
(53’) Cork is caught in possession by Ighalo and the former Granada man bursts forward. He has little support and is forced to turn back, with Deeney eventually joining the charge. The momentum is lost, though, and they reset from the halfway line.
(51’) The set-pieces have been sub-par from both sides this afternoon, with Shelvey the most recent guilty party. His corner is sent low along the floor to the near post where it is cleared immediately.
(50’) Prodl lofts a long ball forward for Ighalo to chase, but Williams nods it back to his keeper so that Swansea can build from the back. They are moving the ball between the flanks impressively, attempting to stretch the hosts as much as possible.
(48’) Swansea have started this half positively, breaking forward down the right only to have a cross cleared behind by Prodl. Chances from inside the box have been limited so far this afternoon.
(46’) We are back underway!
The teams are returning to the field so the second half will begin momentarily.
HALF TIME - Watford 0-0 Swansea: It remains goalless at the interval but there have been plenty of chances at either end that could have resulted in a goal. Gomis called Gomes into action with a quality strike, while Abdi, Deeney and Ighalo have all gone close for the hosts up the other end. The Hornets have often looked dangerous but failed to find the net, and Flores will be desperate for them to put that right after the interval. Stay tuned for the second half!
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) Gomis gets in behind and produces a stunning, acrobatic volley that pulls a save from Gomes. However, he had once again strayed into an offside position! We will have one minute of added time.
(43’) Taylor is perhaps lucky to get away without conceding a penalty as he impedes Deeney's attempt to attack a cross by backing into the striker. The referee sees nothing in it, though, and allows play to continue with a goal kick.
(42’) Ighalo does well to shake off Fernandez down the left and then race around the outside of Williams and into the box. He dribbles in along the byline but, rather than cut it back into the centre, he goes for the shot from an acute angle which Fabianski keeps out with his legs.
(41’) Watford are awarded a free kick just outside the box on the right wing. Abdi, this time, clips it into the middle but the Swansea defence manage to get it clear. Nyom then loses possession and invites the visitors to break, though they fail to create anything meaningful.
(39’) WHAT A CHANCE! Anya hesitates in possession by the corner flag and has his pocket picked by Ayew. The Ghanaian dribbles into the box but his target, Gomis, runs straight into Prodl and the pair go to ground. Regardless, he sends a pass to the Frenchman who sweeps an improvised shot from the deck straight into Gomes' arms.
(37’) After such a promising spell midway through the half, Watford are surrendering the momentum to the visitors. They are sitting deeper and deeper, allowing the Swans more time on the ball. Williams makes another erroneous pass, conceding possession to the hosts inside his own half.
(35’) Jurado dirfts in from the left before attempting a reverse pass to the byline for Anya. However, even the speedy Scotsman is unable to get on the end of it as it rolls out of play for a goal kick.
(33’) Naughton rolls a short pass inside from the right for Sigurdsson but the Iceland international shows great awareness and dummies it, letting the ball run for Shelvey. The former Liverpool man hits it first time but produces a tame effort which is never going to trouble Gomes.
(31’) Gomis has already been caught offside a number of times this afternoon and the flag goes up against him once more here, as he controls a pass from Shelvey on his chest 20 yards out.
(30’) When Swansea have the ball Watford have everybody back behind it, closing the opposition quickly and forcing them into action. Ayew has been watched extremely close and, as a result, has struggled to get involved so far.
(28’) Watford certainly look the more dangerous of the two sides, but failing to turn that into goals has already become a theme of their season. They need someone to step up and grab that goal, and they need it quickly because Gomis has already shown just how sharp he is.
(26’) Jurado darts into the box and has the chance to shoot but instead opts to cut inside. Cork is tight to him and sticks a foot in, dispossessing the Spaniard and removing the threat. The Watford man has not looked at his best so far today.
(25’) STAT: Swansea have kept just one clean sheet in their last six Premier League away games.
(23’) WATFORD GO CLOSE AGAIN! Deeney comes out to the right and dribbles across the top of the box before playing a neat one-two with Capoue. The captain beats Fabianski with his strike but he also sends it wide of the target! The opening goal could come at any moment if we continue like this!
(22’) ABDI AGAIN! The Swiss catches the ball on the volley after Fernandez's headed clearance drops kindly to him. His connection comes with a bit of slice that sends it swerving and looping beyond the far post!
(21’) GREAT SAVE! Swansea's star duo of the season so far combine, with Ayew feeding Gomis at the top of the box. The Frenchman spins away from Cathcart and releases a powerful strike towards the bottom corner that Gomes keeps out with a strong hand!
(20’) Fernandez loses out to Deeney on the right following a poor pass from Williams, and the striker pings a cross towards Ighalo in the box. Fabianski sees it all the way and comes off his line to claim it at the first time of asking. The hosts are in the ascendancy.
(18’) JUST WIDE! Watford come within inches of taking the lead. A nice move sees Ighalo tee Deeney's pass up for Abdi, but the Swiss' strike from just outside the box is deflected narrowly outside of the upright following a deflection!
(17’) Jurado and Ighalo try to unlock the visitors' defence with a one-two through the middle but Fernandez steps up and intercepts. He cannot do anything with it and Watford are soon back on the attack, this time down their right. Nyom picks out Deeney 20 yards from goal and he has his effort blocked. Promising signs from Flores' men.
(16’) Naughton lifts a delightful pass down the right wing for Ayew to chase, but the bounce takes it away from the Ghanaian and into the arms of the onrushing Gomes. The keeper judged that one well.
(15’) Monk's men are beginning to look more confident in possession despite the Hornets actively looking to restrict their time and space. Shelvey surges forward on the right but fires an attempted centre for Gomis into the stand behind the goal!
(13’) Swansea finally manage to ease the pressure that they have been coming under in the last few minutes, winning a free kick just inside the Watford half. Shelvey opts to take it short but the hosts press quickly to try and stop the Swans from opening them up with their short, passing style.
(11’) Jurado has another chance to pop a free-kick into the box from the left, but he fails to achieve anything better with Gomis again the man to head it back out to the Spaniard. He flicks a clever pass down the line for Anya, whose lofted delivery is knocked down for Prodl. The centre-back thumps a shot towards goal from the top of the box which is always rising and sails over the top!
(9’) Jurado fails to make the most of the set-piece as his dreadful delivery is cleared away by Gomis, the first man. Watford had packed the box and that will come as a disappointment for them.
(8’) Anya shows brilliant feet and a rapid turn of pace to get away from two white shirts and race into the Swansea half from the halfway line. He offloads to Jurado on the left wing but the Spaniards cross is cleared comfortably. Possession is soon back with the Scottish left-back and he earns a free kick in a great position with more tricky play.
(7’) Capoue is hobbling after a collision in midfield but the referee lets play continue as Watford have the advantage. The hosts, however, feel the midfielder needs treatment and knock the ball out of play. The Frenchman is soon back to his feet at Taylor sportingly sends possession back to Gomes.
(5’) Taylor stretches his legs for the first time this afternoon but Abdi comes across to cover and assist Nyom, who hooks it out for a throw-in. The Hornets regain possession once play resumes and Capoue attempts to release Deeney with a long pass which is overhit.
(3’) Swansea are looking to get a quick stranglehold on possession. A stray pass from Cathcart is pounced upon by Ayew and the Ghanaian instantly looks to race forward. He attempts to slide a pass in behind the defence for Gomis but the former Manchester United centre-back recovers to intercept.
(1’) We are underway!
Watford have lost both of their previous two league meetings with Swansea at Vicarage Road and are without a win in four, home and away, against the Welsh outfit.
Swansea bench: Nordfeldt, Rangel, Bartley, Ki, Montero, Emnes, Eder.
Swansea (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Naughton, Fernandez, Williams, Taylor; Shelvey, Cork; Ayew, Sigurdsson, Routledge; Gomis.
Watford bench: Arlauskis, Holebas, Watson, Berghuis, Diamanti, Dyer, Ibarbo.
Watford (4-2-3-1): Gomes; Nyom, Prodl, Cathcart, Anya; Capoue, Behrami; Abdi, Ighalo, Jurado; Deeney.
SWANSEA TEAM NEWS: Jefferson Montero did not travel with the Ecuador squad for their friendly against Honduras and has subsequently recovered from a thigh injury, but he is only fit enough to start as a substitute. Therefore, Monk names the same XI that began the 2-1 win over Man United before the international break.
WATFORD TEAM NEWS: There is one change for the Hornets and it comes at left-back, with Jose Holebas dropping to the bench with Ikechi Anya favoured. New signing Victor Ibrabo has overcome work permit issues to feature on the bench while Miguel Britos suspended.
Quique Sanchez Flores would love such a prolific player in his side. His team have failed to get a single shot on target in each their last two outings and have scored just twice in all competitions this season. With the international break behind them, the Spaniard will be looking for his team to really get their campaign going with a victory as soon as possible.
My name is Tom Webber and I will be guiding you through all the action today, with Swansea striker Bafetimbi Gomis looking to become just the third player in Premier League history to score in the first five games of the season. The Frenchman has been in fine form this term and, alongside team-mate Andre Ayew, is a nominee for the Player of the Month award. The Swans' coach, Garry Monk, is also up for the Manager of the Month accolade, something which proves how impressively his side have started the campaign.
