Nothing could separate West Bromwich Albion and Southampton, who played out a goalless draw at the Hawthorns. The Saints looked the more threatening in the second half, but neither side did enough to stake a claim for all three points.
FULL TIME: WEST BROMWICH ALBION 0-0 SOUTHAMPTON
(90’) There goes the final whistle and Mr. Attwell brings a fairly disappointing afternoon to an end.
(90’) Fantastic defending from Fonte - stayed on his feet and didn't dive in. He is facing McClean who looks to take him on, but produces a wonderful stab tackle to deny the winger from hurting his side.
(90’) FOUR MINUTES! That's how long both sides have to try and find a winner from this game.
(88’) Given Pelle's obvious quality for club and country, he has been very poor today. He has looked lethargic and he has just sent a tame effort from 18 yards into the grateful arms of Myhill.
--- 86’ Substitution J. Evans is done for the day. J. Olsson is his replacement. ---
(86’) West Brom make their final change and Evans limps off after failing to recover from a knock he just picked up. Jonas Olsson comes on for the last four minutes.
(84’) As we approach the final stages of this game, can either side find a winner? The work of both teams in the final third has been disappointing on the whole today. Neutrals will be hoping that changes.
(82’) FIRST TIME?! Southampton work the ball nicely to the edge of the box and it is laid off for Mane. He takes too long in shaping up to shoot, though, and Brunt is able to block. Why didn't he just shoot straight away? Only he knows...
(80’) Brunt is shown the first yellow card of the game for a heavy challenge on Mane. Southampton should look to attack him at every opportunity now in these last 10 mintes - one false move and he's off.
--- 79’ Yellow card C. Brunt gets yellow. ---
(78’) Berahino leads the counter attack for West Brom and lays the ball into the path of Rondon, who steps inside rather than letting it run across him and shooting and Southampton eventually clear.
(76’) Koeman may be looking for the win but he makes sure that things remain tight at the back, as he brings on the fresh legs of Maya Yoshida in place of Soares.
--- 75’ Substitution M. Yoshida comes on for Cédric Soares. ---
(74’) Mane is found with a neat through ball, but his first touch takes him away from goal and his shot flies just wide of the target. Southampton are getting closer.
(71’) Davis looks for Pelle with a beautiful lofted ball with the outside of his boot. The striker is unable to stretch far enough to flick it over the onrushing Myhill.
(70’) We have a slight break in play here, as Pelle receives attention following a heavy knock to his foot. It looked like it stung a bit but he should be able to continue.
(68’) The Saints' intentions are increasingly clear as Koeman now throws on Mane in search of a winner. He is a tricky little player capable of moments of magic.
--- 67’ Substitution S. Mané enters play, replacing J. Rodriguez. ---
(66’) Southampton are turning up the pressure here. They have looked a lot more lively since the break and are seeming the most likely to grab a winner of the two sides.
(64’) OVER THE BAR! Davis leads the charge for the Saints by finding Pelle, whose cross runs for Tadic. Rather than shoot, though, he cuts inside and lays the ball back for Ward-Prowse to fire into the stands.
(63’) Van Dijk does well to dig his fellow centre half Fonte out of trouble. The Saints skipper's header is loose and Rondon looks to latch onto it, but his partner is quickly across to clear the danger.
--- 61’ Substitution C. McManaman is done for the day. J. McClean is his replacement. ---
(61’) That was one of McManaman's last actions of the game as he is replaced by James McClean in a like-for-like swap by Pulis. The Irishman has a very dangerous left foot.
(59’) McManaman works his way into the box but is quickly closed down by three Southampton defenders, who are able to block and deflect the ball behind for a corner.
(57’) OOPS! A West Brom free kick deflects high into the air and is spilled by Stekelenburg. Fortunately for him, he is able to recover and spare his blushes before McAuley can pounce.
--- 55’ Substitution R. Lambert is replaced with S. Berahino. ---
(55’) HERE HE COMES! The moment everyone had been waiting for has arrived at the Hawthorns, as Berahino makes his return for the Baggies. Lambert is the player to make way.
(54’) WHAT A CHANCE! Rondon controls a cross brilliantly from the right hand side and holds off his marker, but just lifts the ball over the crossbar. West Brom should be in front.
(52’) Berahino receives a fairly generous reception from the home fans as he is sent to warm up by his manager. This will be his opportunity to put the transfer saga behind him once and for all.
(50’) Koeman's half-time team talk appears to be having the desired effect. The Saints are playing with a lot more urgency and enjoyed the vast majority of possession.
(48’) Tadic's decision making lets him down again in the space of a couple of minutes. He leaves Brunt for dead once more and only needs to fire the ball across goal, but puts too much loft on his cross and it evades everybody.
(46’) WHY DIDN'T TADIC SHOOT?! He gets the better of Brunt and has the opportunity to get his shot away, but looks to do too much and the danger is eventually cleared.
(46’) KICK OFF! Southampton get us going once again.
The teams are coming back out onto the field and the second half is fast approaching.
Southampton will be looking to get on top after the break. Tadic has looked dangerous but they haven't tested Myhill and Pelle doesn't look to be at the races. Koeman does have the likes of Sadio Mane and Shane Long on the bench should he wish to freshen things up.
West Brom will be pleased so far. They have enjoyed good spells of possession, but need to create more goalscoring opportunities. Lambert and Rondon have been passengers during that first half, so it may well be 'cue Berahino'.
HALF TIME: WEST BROM 0-0 SOUTHAMPTON
(45’) The referee blows his whistle for half time.
(45’) The fourth official raises his board to indicate that there will be two minutes of added time at the end of this first half.
(43’) The Serbian is involved again as he partners up with Soares against Brunt. The latter delivers a dangerous cross which evades Myhill, but Dawson is on hand to clear the danger.
(41’) Tadic is carrying a huge threat down the right flank like he always does. He is very unpredictable on the ball and his left foot causes havoc with his range of crossing and shooting.
(39’) It is great to see Rodriguez back playing again. He missed the whole of last season following the injury he picked up at the end of the 2013/14 campaign, and will be keen to make a statement to Roy Hodgson ahead of Euro 2016.
(37’) BEST CHANCE SO FAR! Tadic sends in a sweet left-footed delivery from the right and Rodriguez shows great movement to meet it, but steers his header just wide of the post. Southampton should be in front.
(35’) Rodriguez tries to make something happen for the visitors as he wriggles away from a couple of challenges and gets his shot away. It is quite disappointing in the end, however, as there is no power and Myhill easily collects.
(34’) You would have thought there would be a lot more attacking threat from both sides, giving the undoubted quality they have at their disposal. We are still awaiting a meaningful attack, though.
(32’) The Saints may have struggled here in recent years, but West Brom haven't fared much better. They have lost four of their last six matches, conceding at least three in each of those.
(30’) West Brom are looking the better of the two sides on the whole. They seem the more dangerous in possession and going forward, but just need to make the most of it now.
(28’) Southampton will have been favourites for this clash, but their form at the Hawthorns does not make for pleasant reading. They have won once in their last nine visits, which came on the opening day of the 2013/14 campaign when Lambert scored the winner.
(26’) Brunt sends in a trademark textbook delivery with his left foot which is attacked by Dawson, but he finds himself underneath the ball and can only direct it over the crossbar.
(25’) McManaman embarks on a strong run down the right flank and his cross is eventually deflected behind by Targett. West Brom have another corner and decent opportunity.
(23’) Boos ring around the Hawthorns as Southampton play a short free kick in a good position. Tadic does eventually deliver a dangerous cross, which is headed away by Rondon.
(21’) That McManaman run into the area was the most dangerous attacking threat we have seen so far. Both sides are enjoying lots of possession but there have been no shots on goal.
(19’) Southampton are renowned for bringing players through the youth ranks and Targett is the next one to be handed an opportunity in the first team. The likes of Luke Shaw have notably prospered from left-back for the Saints in the recent past.
(17’) It looked like there was definite contact on first glance, but replays show that the West Brom winger was already on his way down and should have been booked for diving instead.
(16’) NO PENALTY! McManaman goes down in the area under a challenge from Targett, but referee Stuart Attwell is not interested in his appeal and a goal kick is awarded.
(13’) It has been a fairly open 13 minutes at the start of this game. Both sides are getting the opportunity to go forward, but without any real penetration as of yet.
(11’) Yet again, the Baggies have failed to take advantage of a set piece as a corner is fired in too low and Southampton easily clear. With the threat in their ranks, they need to make the most of those situations.
(9’) West Brom waste a free kick by opting to play it short when they have both centre halves forward and the likes of Lambert ready to attack. In the end, they are quite fortunate that the Saints concede a throw near the corner flag.
(7’) We should expect a fairly tight contest here. In fact, at least one of the teams has kept a clean sheet in each of their last five meetings. Of course, there is still plenty of time for that to change.
(5’) Southampton respond with some promising attacking play of their own. Tadic whips a cross towards goal, but Pelle is unable to quite stretch far enough to connect with it.
(3’) The hosts have made a strong start to this game. They have put their opponents under pressure from the start and we have a slight break in play, as Soares receives attention after taking a knock in a strong challenge with Gardner.
(1’) KICK OFF! West Brom get us underway kicking from left to right.
The teams are out and kick off is just moments away!
Both sides picked up their first victories of the new season last time out, so will keen to build on that momentum this afternoon and propel themselves up the table.
SOUTHAMPTON SUBS: K. Davis, Yoshida, Long, Mane, Romeu, Juanmi, Caulker.
SOUTHAMPTON (4-2-3-1): Stekelenburg; Soares, Fonte, Van Dijk, Targett; Wanyama, S. Davis; Ward-Prowse, Tadic, Rodriguez; Pelle.
Southampton have been boosted by manager Ronald Koeman ruling himself out of the running for the Netherlands job. Maya Yoshida, Sadio Mane and Oriel Romeu drop to the bench.
WEST BROM SUBS: Lindegaard, Olsson, Chester, Morrison, McClean, Berahino, Gnabry.
WEST BROM (4-1-4-1): Myhill; Dawson, McAuley, Evans, Brunt; Yacob; Rondon, Gardner, Fletcher, McManaman; Lambert.

FULL TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 3-1 LIVERPOOL. Daley Blind opened the scoring to spring the game into life after a mundane first half, and Ander Herrera doubled their tally with 20 minutes to play. Christian Benteke seemed to give Liverpool life with the goal of the night - and there were quite a few to chose from - before Anthony Martial put the final nail in the coffin with an exquisite debut goal.
(90’) There's no one these United fans love to beat more, and they've done it again tonight! The final whistle sounds but it's only the start of the part at Old Trafford where they will be partying long into the night.
(90’) United dictate possession in the final minutes here as the Old Trafford faithful serenade them through to the final whistle. They jump ahead of Arsenal now on goal differential, into second place, trailing only their Manchester rivals.
(90’) Liverpool are dejected and even the indication of four minutes of stoppage time isn't enough to give them a glimmer of hope. They finally got back into the game after scraping and clawing for much of the second half, but Martial has done his part to ensure three points for the Red Devils.
--- 88’ Substitution Alberto Moreno comes on for Lucas Leiva. ---
(88’) Well what a finish this turned out to be! It may not rank among the great derby games of all-time, but it will be remembered for years to come. Blind's belter, Benteke's worldly and Martial's debut goal have made this second half very easy on the eyes.
--- 86’ Assist A. Young provided the assist. ---
--- 86’ Goal! MARTIAL WRITES HIS NAME IN UNITED FOLKLORE! Whatever you can do, I can do better says Martial to Benteke! It's a goal for the ages, on his debut nonetheless! Martial dribbles his way past three defenders en route into the area from the left, including a nutmeg on Skrtel, before curling a shot past Mignolet and in at the far post! ---
--- 84’ Goal! Goal to Liverpool, scored by C. Benteke! ---
(84’) OH MY WORD! GAME ON! It's an absolute wonder-strike from Christian Benteke! A goal of the season candidate and we're only in September! Clyne's cross is deflected high into the air by Blind. Benteke shields his marker and meets it with the most incredible overhead volley Old Trafford has seen since Rooney did it against City!
(83’) DE GEA IS BACK! That's what we're used to seeing from the United shot-stopper. He's got a new contract and seems to have put the whole transfer saga behind him. Ibe sprints in from the left and curls a strike destined for the far corner, but the Spaniard soars through the air to keep it out.
(82’) Defensively this has been a better showing from Liverpool. Conceding from a set piece and a penalty, but otherwise they have limited United's chances from open play. Going forward has to be the real worry for Rodgers as his side have created next to nothing in attack, still stuck on two goals for the season - one a belter and another offside.
(80’) Liverpool are left chasing the game and trying to mount an improbable comeback, yet they're unable to win the ball back. It's the Red Devils who continue to enjoy the bulk of possession and are doing brilliantly to limit the Reds when they try and break out of their own end.
(78’) Another poor clearance from Mignolet, though this time he was put under pressure from Martial, sees him give the ball away. Fellaini is picked out in the centre and sprays a good ball out wide for Shaw, but a nice recovery from Skrtel denies the left-back's cross from getting through.
(76’) STAT ATTACK: The last time Manchester United and Liverpool played to a draw at Old Trafford was in March 2000. They have played 17 times since then across all competitions without ending in a stalemate.
--- 75’ Yellow card J. Milner receives a yellow card. ---
--- 74’ Substitution D. Origi enters the game and replaces D. Ings. ---
(74’) Two more changes now, one from each side. The final for United sees Carrick - who has been wonderful on the day - replaced by Morgan Schneiderlin. For Liverpool it's Divock Origi who makes his first appearance of the season in place on Ings.
--- 73’ Yellow card M. Darmian gets yellow. ---
--- 72’ Substitution M. Schneiderlin enters play, replacing M. Carrick. ---
(72’) Well it's all or nothing now for Liverpool. They have to start taking chances and really have a go at it. Two goals may prove too daunting a task, but even one could provide them with a bit of confidence moving forward - which they seem to be sorely lacking at the moment.
--- 70’ Goal! HERRERA SCORES IT! Exquisite penalty from the Spaniard who crashes an unstoppable strike into the ceiling of the net! And what a massive goal that is... ---
(69’) PENALTY TO MANCHESTER UNITED! Carrick plays Herrera through into the area and an inexperienced Gomez slides in to try and break it up, but gets too much of the man. He gets up and glances straight at the referee with a look of guilt in his face, making the decision that much easier for Michael Oliver.
(68’) United have settled things down once again, turning to the likes of Schweinsteiger and Carrick to help them keep possession. Darmian has also played a vital role with the hosts on the ball, posing a constant threat on the overlap.
(66’) Changes for both sides here, and with it brings the debut of Martial for Manchester United, replacing Mata. He's the first Red Devils player to debut against Liverpool since 1936 (John Thompson). For the Reds we see Jordon Ibe finally brought on, and it's Roberto Firmino who gives way. A like-for-like swap there for the visitors.
--- 65’ Substitution Roberto Firmino is done for the day. J. Ibe is his replacement. ---
--- 65’ Substitution A. Martial comes on for Mata. ---
(65’) CLEARED OFF THE LINE! Skrtel meets a corner and heads an effort at goal, but Blind manages to stretch his leg out to save a goal! He's scored at one end and now denied a clear chance at the other!
(63’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool have won just one of their last seven away matches in the Premier League dating back to last season (D3, L3). They recorded just one point last campaign against the top four teams on their travels, in a 1-1 draw with Chelsea who had the league wrapped up at the time, being outscored 11-3 in those matches.
(61’) Lovren's foul on Fellaini awards United another glorious chance from a dead ball situation. Young and Mata stand over it from 25-yards out and it's the substitute who takes, but his strike never does dip, sailing a few metres over the bar.
(59’) De Gea forced into action! The best spell we've see all evening from Liverpool and it has United scrambling at the back. Ings collects a pass following a poor clearance from De Gea and gets a good shot off, but the Spaniard redeems himself by keeping the effort out at the near post.
(57’) VITAL FROM SMALLING! Lovely one-two between Firmino and Clyne. The latter plays a return pass to send the Brazilian through on goal, but from a tight angle he tries to feed a pass across for Benteke that Smalling is able to knock away from goal! Much better there from the Reds.
(55’) Now this sounds more like a derby! Old Trafford has been resurrected by the left foot of Daley Blind. The noise level inside the stadium is higher than it was at any point in the first half and it's provided United with a spring in their step. Liverpool are entering a dangerous period here where they have to find a way to keep possession and quiet this crowd.
(53’) STAT ATTACK: David de Gea has not kept a clean sheet in any of his last seven appearances in the Premier League in which he played a full 90 minutes.
(51’) Just needed a touch! Another free kick causes problems for Liverpool. This one bounces around before coming to Schweinsteiger, but it catches the midfielder by surprise. All it needed was a good first touch and United very well could have doubled there lead.
--- 49’ Assist Mata provided the assist. ---
--- 49’ Goal! DALEY BLIND STAMPS HIS NAME ON THE DERBY! Straight from the training ground, Mata squares the free kick for Blind who meets it atop the area with a thunderous left-footed drive into the top corner. From nothing there is life at Old Trafford! ---
--- 48’ Yellow card Much better from United! Threatening build-up play there with Young on the end of it. The winger nutmegs Clyne who is forced to shied his passage into the area, which awards the hosts a free kick in a very dangerous position. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Back underway at Old Trafford! Interesting switch from Van Gaal as Memphis is replaced at the break by Ashley Young. Surely the Dutchman must be injured or fatigued, because he was their most direct and exciting player going forward in the opening 45 minutes. ---
Brendan Rodgers should also be pondering a switch. Lucas has broken up play nicely a few times but he's also been very poor in possession. He could also look into replacing Ings, with Jordon Ibe likely to pose more of a threat on the flanks and run at those Manchester United full-backs.
You have to wonder how long it will be until Van Gaal decides to bring on their new 37-million-pound striker Anthony Martial. Fellaini has had little room to operate and his touch has been poor when the ball is played into his feet.
HALF TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-0 LIVERPOOL. Lifeless. Timid. Lackluster. Call it what you want, but this has been anything but a classic at Old Trafford after 45 minutes. Neither side have looked capable of creating anything and as a result those in attendance have been left unsatisfied. Here's to hoping - against all odds - the second half springs to life.
(45’) The assistant referee is quite clearly a glutton for punishment as he indicates there will be one more minute added on to the end of this first half, though with the pace it's moving at one can hardly see the point.
(43’) Van Gaal might be wise in allowing Memphis to drift into a more central role. The Dutchman could do with escaping the close marking of Clyne, while his desire to run at defenders could also open up plenty of space and make for some nervy moments for the likes of Lovren and Skrtel.
(41’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 16 red cards in the Premier League matches between Manchester United and Liverpool, the second highest total after the Merseyside Derby (20).
(39’) Well this certainly hasn't been a classic. We knew coming in it was going to be a tense affair as opposed to an open, end-to-end contest. Both teams have struggled to find goals and the lack of creativity has been apparent today. What is surprising is the feel this match has about it - with the intensity nowhere near what you would expect from a derby of this stature.
(37’) Can has been the lone bright spot in midfield for Liverpool, the only one who looks willing to put the required work in to help his side transition into attack. He's been the link between the back line and Benteke, but with such little movement off the ball in midfield he's often having to go at it alone.
(35’) Carrick and Schweinsteiger are absolutely dominating the midfield battle. They're dictating the tempo and direction of the match, and it hasn't been much of an ask for them either with Liverpool dropping deep, affording them far too much space to operate.
(33’) Another good period of possession from United, but crosses from Shaw and Mata are unable to pick out their desired targets. It gets back with Liverpool and Skrtel lobs a ball 50 yards up the pitch for Benteke to chase. Again it's a tough ask of the striker and possession is given right back to the hosts.
(31’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool have been held without a goal in each of their last two Premier League fixtures. They haven’t failed to score in three consecutive league matches since February to March 2005.
(29’) Confident goalkeeping from Mignolet! Mata stands over a free kick along the right and whips a flat, inviting delivery towards the far post. Fellaini times his run well to attack it, but the keeper reads it brilliantly to sprint off his line and collect with sure hands.
(27’) Firmino and Benteke link-up atop the area, with the latter chesting down a pass and looking to send a half-volley at goal. He telegraphs his intentions, however, and Blind is able to interject. Firmino buries his head in his hands as he was shouting out for a return pass that could well have sent him clean through on goal.
(25’) There's been a few half-chances but neither side has possessed much potency in attack. Memphis looks up for the occasion, another lovely take to control a pass sprayed out wide by Carrick, but he's going to have a hard time beating Clyne for pace this evening as the right-back is again able to break up the move.
(23’) DEFLECTED WIDE! Extremely poor from Lucas as he gives the ball away in his own end, allowing the hosts to break. Memphis surges into the area via the left channel and plays a pacey ball in at goal from a tight angle, but a deflection sends it crashing into the side netting.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United have kept a clean sheet in three of their four Premier League matches this campaign. Their two goals allowed is bested only by their inner-city rivals (none).
(19’) Good defending from Darmian as he prevents Can from finding his way through. The German showed a nice bit of trickery there to dart along the edge of the area, but his attempted cutback is halted. Pressure stays on and Gomez whips an inviting cross in, but Benteke is unable to make clean contact under pressure from Shaw.
(17’) You wonder how long it will be until Benteke grows frustrated up top. Ings is having to track back often with Darmain eager to provide support on the overlap, and Liverpool have been relegated to sending hopeful balls over the top for the Belgian striker to chase.
(15’) United win a cheap corner as an attempted one-two comes to nothing as Memphis halts his run, but there's more miscommunication at the back from Liverpool as Clyne sends the ball needlessly behind. He has to be given warning there by a teammate.
(13’) Teasing delivery! Ings gets caught as he tries to track the run of Darmian, allowing him to find a bit of space on the right. The defender pulls back an inviting cross but Herrera can't make clean contact and then the follow up from Fellaini is poor as he fails to control as a result of a heavy first touch.
(11’) United have held the majority of possession with Liverpool unable to pass their way out from the back. It's been an underwhelming start from the Reds who have yet to show any signs of life on the ball. Memphis gets the crowd going with a darting run down the left, but no foul is given as he's clattered over by Lovren.
(9’) STAT ATTACK: This is the 193rd meeting between these two teams across all competitions. Manchester United have the edge with 77 wins to Liverpool’s 64. The other 51 ended in a stalemate.
(7’) Careless from Mignolet! The keeper tries to roll a pass out of his area but it's straight at Mata who knocks it into the path of Fellaini, but the Belgian is unable to hit the target with the keeper miles off his line.
(5’) Good play from Christian Benteke, who is no longer stranded up top with the inclusion of Ings. The Belgian striker takes a pass as Liverpool look to break out of there end, holding possession well before forcing Chris Smalling into a foul near the halfway line.
(3’) Slow start to the match, as can be expected, with the two teams feeling each other out. Manchester United manage a good period of possession in the attacking half, though fail to ask much of the Liverpool defence before Nathaniel Clyne halts the run of Memphis to bring their spell to an end.
(1’) And we're off! Liverpool get us underway, wearing all white and kicking towards the Stretford End.
The anticipation is palpable as the players take the pitch, not just inside the stadium but across the whole of England. Manchester United versus Liverpool. Oasis versus the Beatles. Hate them or love them, this is arguably the biggest rivalry in the Premier League with under 40 miles separating the two historic clubs and the latest edition kicks off in just a few moments.
Just one change for Brendan Rodgers as the suspended Philippe Coutinho is replaced by Danny Ings in attack. Jordan Henderson and Adam Lallana remain out with foot and thigh problems respectively, while the real surprise comes in defence where Dejan Lovren keeps his place in the starting lineup despite a shocking performance against West Ham in the final match before the international break.
David De Gea can finally put the Real Madrid saga behind him. The goalkeeper penned a new deal yesterday and has been reinstated in the starting lineup at the expense of Sergio Romero. Michael Carrick has recovered from a calf injury and thus replaces Morgan Schneiderlin in the first XI.
The big news is the absence of Wayne Rooney, whom Louis van Gaal said suffered a minor injury in training and cannot be risked this evening. It's a big blow for the Red Devils, with Marouane Fellaini starting as the lone striker up top ahead of new recruit Anthony Martial who starts on the bench.

Today marks the 193rd meeting between Manchester United and Liverpool, and the derbies are starting to take on a very different feel than the days of old. For the second time running, the Reds visit Old Trafford with plenty of pressure on the two managers. Louis van Gaal and Brendan Rodgers have come under plenty of scrutiny for their teams’ respective slow starts to the season – and a pair of defeats before the international break did nothing to help their cause.

Sunderland will feel hard done by after putting in arguably one of their best performances of the season, but they fell asleep at the vital moment and were made to pay for their mistake. They now go on to face Bournemouth in their next league game, whilst Tottenham are in action against Crystal Palace after hosting Qarabag in the Europa League.
Tottenham are just about able to hold on to their slender lead to claim all three points and, most importantly, their first Premier League win of the season. After a lacklustre first half they looked far better in the second, particularly as Sunderland tired and failed to find much joy in the final third of the pitch. Townsend, who was superb, completely changed the game after coming on for Alli, as did Lamela, who set up his side's winning goal with a lovely through-ball.
FULL-TIME: SUNDERLAND 0-1 TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR
(90’) Kaboul keeps the move alive and sends a looping cross towards the back post, but Lens can only send his headed effort several yards wide of the near post and out for a goal kick. That should be that for Tottenham, who are now almost certain to pick up all three points.
(90’) Lens shows great skill to break into the penalty area before fizzing a pass across the face of goal, but there's nobody there to meet it and it ends up bouncing over to the right flank, where M'Vila then wins his side a throw-in near the corner flag.
(90’) Chadli misses again! This time the Belgian picks up the ball on the right-hand side of the penalty area but holds onto possession for far too long before firing a wild strike wide of its intended target.

(31’) Davies, who seems to have recovered from a poke in the eye, returns to the pitch and play resumes with Sunderland giving the ball back to Lloris.
(30’) Davies seems to have picked up an injury and is currently on the ground receiving medical treatment, resulting in a break in play that allows the players a chance to have a drink and receive instructions from the two managers.
(28’) It's all Sunderland at the moment! Borini dispossesses Walker with ease before teeing up Van Aanholt, who flies into the left-hand side of the penalty area and tries to tee up Defoe. Off-balance, he is unable to find the striker and instead sees his pass cut out by Vertonghen.
(26’) Defoe hits the post! The former Tottenham striker breaks through the visitors' disjointed back line and charges towards goal before going one-on-one with Lloris. His swerving low strike beats the goalkeeper but  ricochets off the far post and away from danger.
(25’) Alderweireld is left in too much space in the middle of the pitch, allowing him to charge forward before unleashing a strike from just outside of the penalty area. O'Shea sticks out a foot and sends the ball looping up into the air, but Pantilimon is able to deal with it before it can find Kane.
(24’) Sunderland work the ball around well before teeing up Lens, who cuts inside from the left flank and fires a curling strike from 30 yards out that flies comfortably wide of the near post.
(22’) Walker picks up the ball in space on the right wing and immediately curls a dangerous cross into the middle of the penalty area, but Kaboul is there to deal with the danger with a strong header.

(19’) The resulting set-piece is sent deep towards the back post but it's dealt with by Davies before Alli clears the danger with ease.

Tottenham are still searching for their first victory of the season as well, although they head to the Stadium of Light marginally in front of Sunderland in 17th place with three points from four games. After losing away to Manchester United in their opening game their next three encounters all ended in draws, highlighting the fact that the balance in the team still doesn’t seem to be quite right. Mauricio Pochettino will be hoping that the recent acquisition of Heung-Min Son will help to kick-start their season, and the South Korean, who signed from Bayer Leverkusen at the end of last month, has been thrown straight into the line-up for this afternoon’s clash.

Nonetheless, today’s game represents arguably their toughest test so far, despite their opponents also suffering a stuttering start to the new season.

(83’) Payet clips a pass out to the left for Moses as the Hammers look to hit the visitors on another counterattack. The winger attempts to cut inside of Janmaat but lacks conviction this time around and the attack comes to an end. He produces a moment of sublime skill to get away from the Dutchman moments later, leaving the home fans in awe for a moment.
(81’) GOOD SAVE! Perez finds De Jong at the top of the box and the Dutchman produces a good touch to turn quickly. His shot takes a deflection which sends it looping towards the target. However, Randolph reacts well to touch it over the bar.
--- 79’ Substitution R. Aarons comes on for G. Wijnaldum. ---
(79’) McClaren makes his final change, withdrawing the industrious Wijnaldum for Aarons.
(78’) Colback adds some intensity to Newcastle's play, rolling a vertical pass into De Jong who then knocks it out to Haidara. The left-back's delivery finds Cisse, but the striker's touch lets him down at the vital moment! That is the problem that has been endemic in the Magpies' current campaign.
(76’) Moses races in from the right and offloads to Payet, who then slides a first-time pass to Kouyate. He twists and turns away from Janmaat but runs into Mbemba, still managing to win his side a corner.
(74’) Janmaat again proves to be Newcastle's most dangerous player, arriving late to the ball 25 yards out. He has to stretch in order to get a shot away and subsequently can only loop it into Randolph's arms.
(73’) Kouyate sets Sakho on his way with a lovely pass and the striker carries the ball into the box before checking back. It gets him away from Colback but Mbemba quickly arrives to get his body in the way of the West Ham man's shot.
(71’) Jenkinson gets away from Colback on the right and drills a cross towards Sakho with plenty of venom. The striker gets his head to it but doesn't make enough contact to divert it on target.
(70’) Sakho's backheel for Moses is intercepted by Colback, with the midfielder sliding it out of play for a corner. Payet pings it towards Reid but it is too high for the centre-back and Mbemba nods it clear. Obiang dribbles into the box from the right and has a shot blocked by Coloccini.
(69’) Cresswell decides to go for goal despite the fairly acute angle. He hits it with plenty of pace but can only guide it into the side netting of Krul's goal.
(68’) West Ham are awarded a free kick in a dangerous position, just outside the box on the right, after Perez fouls Noble from behind. This will be a great chance for the hosts to add to their tally.
(66’) De Jong initiates a one-two with Sissoko 30 yards from the West Ham goal but the return pass is intercepted by Tomkins. The Magpies then attack down the left, but Haidara sees his delivery blocked by Jenkinson. They do finally get the ball into the box from the resultant throw-in, with Janmaat pulling a strong save from Randolph once more.
(64’) Perez wins a free kick from Noble in midfield which Colback takes short. Newcastle probe down the right but again hit a dead end, with Reid clearing the ball into touch. They've seen 58 per cent of possession in the second half but, once more, have done nothing with it.
(62’) STAT: West Ham have won just one of their last five Premier League meetings with Newcastle and only two of their last nine at home to the Magpies.
--- 60’ Substitution Ayoze Pérez comes on for F. Thauvin. ---
--- 60’ Substitution S. de Jong enters the game and replaces V. Anita. ---
(60’) Anita tries his luck with an ambitious effort from 25 yards out that is always going over the top. It proves to be his final action of the match, as he is replaced by De Jong. Thauvin is also withdrawn as Ayoze comes on.
--- 59’ Substitution Pedro Obiang enters play, replacing M. Lanzini. ---
(59’) Well, Obiang does indeed enter the fray but it is Lanzini who makes way. A slightly defensive switch from the Croatian coach.
(58’) Kouyate takes a heavy knock during a tackle and takes a while getting back to his feet. Bilic has Obiang preparing for action in the dugout, so we could see a change in a few moments.
--- 57’ Yellow card D. Janmaat gets yellow. ---
(56’) A mistake from Coloccini sees him pass the ball straight to Payet just outside the box on the right. The Frenchman darts to the byline and sees his cutback blocked behind for a corner. He swings it himself, only to see Mbemba head it out for another set-piece. The former Marseille man jogs over to take the next one from the opposite flank. This time it is short and comes to nothing.
(54’) Moses shows his effectiveness at the other end now, tracking back and nullifying the threat of Janmaat. The ball is cleared up field and Newcastle have possession once more. Sissoko whips a cross in from the right that comes at an awkward height for Cisse, who shins an effort off target.
(52’) Janmaat earns a corner for the visitors which Thauvin leaves to Wijnaldum. The Frenchman ends up controlling the set-piece inside the box but it's knocked away as far as Janmaat, who slices an effort wide from 25 yards.
(50’) That will be a big blow for Newcastle, who have enjoyed plenty of possession and would have been hoping to work their way back into this game following the restart. Instead, they find themselves two down and the search for an elusive goal continues.
--- 48’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAL! WEST HAM SCORE ON THE BREAK! Thauvin's free-kick is cleared up the pitch and Moses races in behind, shaking off Anita before cutting inside of Anita. His strike cannons back off the bar but Payet is perfectly placed to fire home his second of the night! ---
(47’) Reid concedes a free-kick following a foul on Janmaat, but the defender quickly tells the Dutchman to get back to his feet as he feels he made too much of it. The set-piece is fired in by Thauvin but once more it's not good enough.
(46’) We are back underway!
HALF TIME - West Ham 1-0 Newcastle: Payet's super strike in the ninth minute gives Bilic's men the advantage at the interval, but it is the visitors that have enjoyed the majority of possession. They've done little with it in truth, though, and, when their best chance to Janmaat, Randolph responded with a quality save. The hosts have been potent on the break, so there are plenty of reasons to stay tuned!
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) Lanzini lifts another lovely pass into the box for Sakho, who juggles it before looping a cross to the back post. Payet manages to keep it in play and picks out Noble at the top of the area. The captain goes for goal with a volley that is always bending away from the goal.
(43’) MOSES! It's another rapid counter-attack for the hosts, breaking at pace following a Newcastle corner. Payet rolls a brilliant pass into the path of the Chelsea loanee as he races beyond him to the right. He fails to get a good connection with the ball, though, slicing his effort wide of the near post.
--- 42’ Substitution A. Ogbonna is done for the day. C. Jenkinson is his replacement. ---
(42’) It is indeed the end of Ogbonna's night and his replacement is Jenkinson. Tomkins will likely move into the centre of defence now.
(41’) Janmaat sets Wijnaldum away down the right and Ogbonna comes across to force him back. The right-back chases up to offer support to his compatriot, earning a corner off the aforementioned Italian. He's now down in the box and clutching his hamstring, receiving medical attention.
(39’) Newcastle continue to see more of the ball, with West Ham only really threatening on the break. Bilic will be pleased by the fact that his team have looked much harder to penetrate tonight.
(37’) Anita does well to dispossess Payet in the centre circle and clip a pass out to Cisse on the left. The striker turns back and feeds Thauvin, who floats a cross towards Wijnaldum in the box. Randolph watches it the whole way and is able to collect it unchallenged.
(36’) Noble is penalised for a handball after tackling Sissoko in the middle. The West Ham captain has really struggled this evening despite playing an important role in the opener. His passing has been uncharacteristically sloppy.
(34’) West Ham break through the centre, with Lanzini releasing Kouyate who dribbles towards the top of the box. Sakho tries to make a run off his team-mate but the former Anderlecht midfielder holds onto possession for too long. Coloccini takes full advantage and makes an important intervention.
(32’) Lanzini rolls what looks to be a short pass back to Randolph, but the keeper races out and launches it long. It almost proves to be the perfect ball for Sakho, however, the striker is unable to control it as it drops from the sky.
--- 30’ Yellow card J. Colback gets yellow. ---
(30’) Colback is the first player to go into the book for a blatant, cynical trip on Kouyate as the midfielder looked to break forward. He can have no complaints about that.
(29’) Sakho does well to eke a pass out to Payet on the right, and the Frenchman then looks for the striker's run into the box. His delivery is too close to Krul, who barely has to move to claim it. There's plenty of fluidity in the three players operating behind West Ham's striker.
(28’) Haidara is not closed down 25 yards out and opts to use the space to pull the trigger. His attempt isn't the best, though, swerving off target as soon as it leaves his boot.
(27’) Another poor pass from Noble is seized upon by Colback. He loops a header on to Cisse but the striker cannot get the better of Ogbonna, who positions himself perfectly to clear the threat.
(26’) Kouyate looks to run onto Lanzini's lofted pass down the right but he bundles Coloccini in his desperation to stop the ball from running out of play. The referee awards the visitors a free-kick as a result.
(25’) Kouyate seems to be the first player to every loose ball at the moment. He nods one out to Payet who produces some fantastic footwork to get away from Sissoko and drive inside. He slides a pass inside for Lanzini, but the Argentine rifles his shot high over the bar.
(23’) Sakho controls a long ball on his chest at the top of the box before attempting an audacious strike on the spin. He gets under it, though, and ends up sending a looping shot beyond the far post. That was never going to worry Krul.
(22’) STAT: Newcastle have only picked up two points from their last nine games on the road, though they’ve shown improvement under McClaren with a 0-0 draw at Manchester United last month.
(20’) WHAT A CHANCE! Janmaat goes on a marauding run down the right before having his pass knocked into the feet of Wijnaldum. The former PSV man's first touch looks heavy but ends up falling kindly for the right-back, who shoots straight at Randolph!
(18’) Newcastle have had the majority of possession so far tonight but they haven't done anything with it. Much of their time on the ball has been around their own halfway line. They almost get exposed at the back, though, with Moses spinning away from Janmaat and centring for Payet who stabs wide.
(17’) Payet's delivery isn't great and Cisse, back to help defend, heads it away. The hosts probe down the right and fail to forge an opening, with Noble then knocking a clearance from Krul out for a throw-in on the far side.
(16’) Noble and Lanzini have both given the ball away cheaply in the past few minutes, but neither error came in a potentially destructive area. Cresswell initiates a one-two with Payet on the left and the defender is blocked off by Sissoko, and the referee blows for a free-kick.
(14’) Janmaat's driven cross is helped into the feet of Colback by Cisse. The midfielder has to take an extra touch to get it out from under him and that sees the angles narrow, resulting in his shot being blocked. Newcastle quickly send the ball back into the centre but the aforementioned Senegalese striker is offside.
(13’) Newcastle get West Ham penned back inside their own half and recycle the ball from right to left after failing to find a route through the defence. Haidara and Thauvin try to create something but Tomkins is alert and steps in to nullify the threat.
(11’) Bilic couldn't have asked for a better start. Anita had been breathing down Payet's neck throughout the early exchanges but he was nowhere to be seen as the Frenchman opened the scoring there.
--- 9’ Assist Assist by M. Noble. ---
--- 9’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAL!! WEST HAM LEAD! It's a brilliant finish from Payet! Sakho's backheel finds Noble at the top of the box and the captain cuts inside and tees up the Frenchman. He strikes the ball first time, curling a delightful finish out of the reach of Krul and into the top corner! ---
(8’) Newcastle build slowly from the back before Janmaat provides an attacking injection by rolling the ball down the right for Sissoko. The Frenchman's attempted cross is deflected behind for a corner, which Thauvin delivers. The set-piece is disappointing and is headed away by the first West Ham body in the box.
(6’) Payet pokes a pass to his left for Moses and the Chelsea loanee twists and turn before releasing the ball. His attempt to find Cresswell goes out off a Newcastle shirt and the hosts have a throw-in in an advanced position. Possession is soon back with Moses but, under pressure from Sissoko, he inadvertently knocks the ball out.
(4’) Reid's long clearance is chased by Sakho but Coloccini clears it into touch. It's been a rather low-key start to proceedings, with neither side settling into an early rhythm.
(2’) West Ham break with Sakho feeding Payet in down the left. The Frenchman cuts inside of Anita and attempts to return the favour by sliding a through-ball into the box. He doesn't quite get it right, though, and ends up sending it straight out for a goal kick.
(1’) We're off at the Boleyn Ground!
The teams have made their way out onto the pitch and the game will begin in just a few moments. An interesting aside to this game; should Newcastle win then reigning Premier League champions would find themselves in the bottom three!
There were concerns that kick off would be delayed tonight, with traffic prolonging Newcastle's journey to the stadium. However, the team coach has been escorted to the ground and we will be underway in 15 minutes, as expected.
NEWCASTLE BENCH: Darlow, Lascelles, Aarons, De Jong, Obertan, Gouffran, Ayoze.
NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Krul; Janmaat, Mbemba, Coloccini, Haidara; Anita, Colback; Sissoko, Wijnaldum, Thauvin; Cisse.
WEST HAM BENCH: Spiegel, Collins, Jenkinson, Obiang, Antonio, Jelavic, Carroll.
WEST HAM (4-2-3-1): Randolph; Reid, Tomkins, Ogbonna, Cresswell; Noble, Kouyate; Moses, Lanzini, Payet; Sakho.
NEWCASTLE TEAM NEWS: The Magpies have scored just twice in their opening four Premier League games and are without Aleksandar Mitrovic due to suspension, so the burden falls on Papiss Cisse this evening. Elsewhere, McClaren’s team is unchanged from their 1-0 defeat to Arsenal last time out.
WEST HAM TEAM NEWS: Andy Carroll returns to the squad after seven months out and features on the bench alongside new signings Michail Antonio and Nikica Jelavic. One deadline day signing does start, though, with Victor Moses coming in for Pedro Obiang. Darren Randolph continues in goal as Adrian serves the last match of his three-game suspension. However, Mark Noble, who was dismissed in the previous match against Liverpool, is available after having his red card rescinded.
The starting line-ups for tonight have been confirmed, so let's take a look at how the two teams will be shaping up.
Tonight's fixture sees the Slaven Bilic and Steve McClaren face off once more. Almost eight years ago, Bilic's Croatia defeated McClaren's England side 3-2 at Wembley, denying the Three Lions a place at Euro 2008 and ending the former Middlesbrough coach's time with the national team. The memory of that defeat still follows the current Newcastle boss around, and he would surely take some pleasure from getting one over his counterpart tonight.
Hello and welcome to this evening's LIVE coverage of the Premier League clash between West Ham United and Newcastle United at the Boleyn Ground. The Hammers have suffered defeat in both of their opening home fixtures this season, while the Magpies are winless on the road this term. Will something give this evening? My name is Tom Webber, and I will be guiding you through all the action as we find that out!

My name is Ben Cullimore and it's been an absolute pleasure describing all of the action to you this afternoon. Until next time, goodbye!
The victory moves Arsenal up to fifth place - for now at least - ahead of the international break, whilst Newcastle remain marginally outside of the relegation zone with just two points from their opening four games. They could end up falling into the drop zone if Southampton, Sunderland and West Bromwich Albion all enjoy success this weekend.
In the end, it was a relatively comfortable afternoon for Arsenal, who leave St. James' Park with a well-deserved three points thanks to a solid, if slightly unspectacular, display. They could have done more going forward but did enough to get the win, with Newcastle constantly finding it incredibly difficult to break out of their own half of the pitch. It was always going to be difficult for the hosts after Mitrovic's red card, and no matter how many attacking players Steve McClaren threw on his side just couldn't seem to cause the visitors' back four any problems whatsoever.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-1 ARSENAL
(90’) What an opportunity for Giroud! The Frenchman breaks through the disjointed Newcastle defence before, one-on-one with Krul, he fails to beat the Dutch goalkeeper with a poorly-hit chipped shot. He should have done better but with no time left on the clock, it doesn't look as if it's going to make any difference to Arsenal, who are now just a few seconds away from victory.
(90’) It's all Arsenal at the moment, but they are, unsurprisingly, holding onto possession deep inside the Newcastle half of the pitch as they look to see off the hosts, who can't get anywhere near the ball.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card A crunching challenge from Coloccini on Coquelin, who has been on the receiving end of some hefty tackles today, results in yet another yellow card for a Newcastle player. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(89’) Sanchez is left in acres of space on the left flank, allowing him to pick up the ball before cutting inside and firing a thumping strike that deflects out for a corner. The resulting set-piece bounces through the Newcastle defence before reaching Monreal, and the Spaniard's half-volley from the edge of the penalty area is easily stopped by Krul.
--- 87’ Substitution De Jong comes on to replace Thauvin in Newcastle's final substitution of the afternoon. ---
(87’) Cazorla fires a curling strike from the resulting set-piece that beats the wall of Newcastle players before flying towards the left-hand corner of the goal, but Krul does well to get across and keep out the effort with a strong diving save.
(86’) Coquelin skips through a group of Newcastle players before being clumsily tripped over, resulting in a free kick for Arsenal in a very dangerous position 30 yards away from goal.
(85’) Arsenal patiently pass the ball around inside the Newcastle half of the pitch as they look to hold onto possession for as long as possible. With a one-goal lead intact and the hosts' down to 10 men, they have taken their foot off the gas somewhat as we enter the final five minutees of the game.
(83’) After a period of pressure from Newcastle, Arsenal are back on the front foot once again. Monreal and Cazorla link up well before the latter tries to muscle his way towards goal, but he's unable to find a way past Haidara before Krul sends the ball out of play for a corner.
--- 81’ Substitution Oxlade-Chamberlain makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Arteta for the final 10 minutes. ---
(80’) Newcastle break away on a dangerous attack through Colback, who then tees up Thauvin on the right wing. The Frenchman finds Perez with a great cross-field pass but the Spaniard's first touch is poor and takes it away from him and into the feet of Monreal.
--- 78’ Substitution Newcastle have made their second change of the game, with Sissoko making way for Cisse. ---
(78’) Great goalkeeping by Krul! Oxlade-Chamberlain sends a lovely through-ball into the path of Sanchez, who sprints towards goal only to be beaten to the ball by the aforementioned Newcastle goalkeeper, who darts out of his box before unleashing a thumping clearance.
(77’) Ramsey flies down the left flank before cutting a lovely pass back to Giroud, who is left completely unmarked by the Newcastle defence, but the Frenchman ends up sending his first-time strike straight into the hands of Krul.
(76’) Oxlade-Chamberlain tries to skip past Haidara but the left-back dispossesses the winger with a great sliding tackle at the vital moment. The ball goes out for a corner, which Cazorla sends towards Giroud, who immediately nods it down into the path of Sanchez. The Chilean unleashes a shot from a tight angle but it's deflected out of play once again.
(74’) Newcastle do well to get forward once more - again down the right wing - but the attacking move is brought to a disappointing end by Janmaat, who carelessly strays into an offside position near the corner flag.
--- 72’ Substitution Perez makes his way onto the pitch to replace Anita in Newcastle's first change of the afternoon. ---
(72’) Newcastle embark on a rare foray forward through Janmaat on the right flank, but he's quickly outnumbered by Arsenal players and is eventually dispossessed by Sanchez before he can get a cross away.
(71’) Giroud is immediately involved in the action, but he slightly mistimes his run into the Newcastle box and, as a result, the linesman's flag is quickly raised for offside.
--- 70’ Substitution Arsenal have decided to make their first substitution of the game, and it's Walcott who makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Giroud. ---
(68’) Chance for Sanchez! Arsenal quickly regain possession before lovely play down the right wing results in a chance for the Chilean. He then unleashes a thumping strike from just inside the penalty area but it's straight at Krul, who does well to stop the shot.
(66’) Oxlade-Chamberlain battles with Sissoko on the right-hand side of the penalty area before firing a low cross off the Frenchman and out for a corner. Cazorla swings the set-piece into the middle of the box but once again the aforementioned Newcastle midfielder is there to clear the ball.
(65’) It's all Arsenal at the moment as they put Newcastle under an incredible amount of pressure, but they hold onto the ball for far too long and fail to penetrate the hosts' back line before Colback once again deals with the danger.
(63’) Monreal breaks into the left-hand side of the penalty area before cutting a lovely pass back to Oxlade-Chamberlain, but the winger's first touch is poor and it bounces off his leg before going out of play for a goal kick.
(62’) Cazorla tries to thread a quick through-ball into the path of Walcott, but Haidara does extremely well to cut out the danger before Colback picks up the ball on the edge of the Newcastle penalty area.
(60’) Monreal shoves Thauvin to the ground, resulting in a free kick for Newcastle midway inside the Arsenal half of the pitch. It's swung towards the edge of the penalty but is completely mishit and is easily dealt with by Oxlade-Chamberlain.
(58’) Another great save by Krul! Cazorla sends a lovely pass down the left wing and into the path of Ramsey, who immediately cuts the ball back to Sanchez. The Chilean takes a quick touch before unleashing a close-range strike, but the Newcastle goalkeeper does well to push it away from the goal with a strong stop.
(56’) After dealing with another patient Arsenal attack, Newcastle break away on an incredibly fast counter attack through Thauvin once again. They push forward quickly but are unable to beat Bellerin, who darts across the pitch to clear the danger at the vital moment.
(54’) Chance for Thauvin, but he's offside! Janmaat breaks down the right flank before sending a lovely pass through the middle of the Arsenal defence and into the path of the aforementioned Frenchman, but his run is slightly mistimed and the lineman's flag is immediately raised as a result.
--- 52’ Goal! GOAL! Arsenal have finally found the back of the net! Ramsey picks up the ball in acres of space just outside of the penalty area and immediately fires a thumping strike. It's pushed away by Krul but only as far as Oxlade-Chamberlain, who unleashes a follow-up shot from the right-hand side of the box that deflects off the heel of Coloccini and into the back of the net. ---
(51’) Arsenal patiently work the ball around midway inside the Newcastle half of the pitch as they try to find a way though the hosts' defence, who are just about managing to keep them bay.
--- 49’ Yellow card But Wijnaldum ruins the joyous atmosphere by picking up a yellow card for himself, presumably for something he said to the referee in the wake of Cazorla's challenge. ---
--- 49’ Yellow card Cheers of joy emanate from the Newcastle fans as the referee shows a yellow card to Cazorla for a clumsy trip from behind as Wijnaldum was breaking away quickly. ---
--- 48’ Yellow card A poor challenge from behind on Sanchez results in yet another yellow card for a Newcastle player, and this time it's Anita who enters the referee's book. ---
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
A raucous mixture of boos and claps ring around St. James' Park as the players make their way off the pitch. Boos for referee Andre Marriner, with whom the Newcastle fans are angry for his dismissal of Mitrovic, and claps for the remaining 10 players, who have defended wonderfully well since losing the Serbian striker. Arsenal have dominated from the start but head into the half-time break frustrated at their inability to find a way through the hosts' determined defence, who have shut them out brilliantly to keep alive their chances of salvaging at least a point.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 ARSENAL
(45’) Monreal charges down the left wing before curling a dangerous cross into the penalty area. It finds Oxlade-Chamberlain, who tries to pull off a spectacular overhead kick, but he ends up missing the ball completely, much to the relief and amusement of the Newcastle fans.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be two minutes of added time.
(44’) Pass after pass is exchanged on the edge of the Newcastle penalty area as Arsenal desperately try to find a way towards goal, but they're shut out by the determined Newcastle defence before a Sanchez shot is deflected away.
(43’) The hosts revert to having almost every available body behind the ball, and, once again, Arsenal are unable to find a way through the sea of black and white shirts, who are putting in an excellent defensive display as they look to keep their clean sheet intact as we near the end of the first half.
(41’) Newcastle push forward on an excellent attack, with Thauvin twisting and turning on the right flank before sending a dangerous low cross into the middle of the box. It almost finds Wijnaldum in front of goal but Gabriel is just about able to get a foot in to cut out the danger at the vital moment.
(39’) More Arsenal pressure results in yet another corner for the visitors. This time it's taken short and sent towards the near post before coming back to Oxlade-Chamberlain, who immediately fires a cross back towards Walcott, but Mbemba does well to get in front of the aforementioned forward before he can get a shot away from close range.
(38’) The Newcastle defence are at sixes and sevens at the back, allowing Ramsey to get a shot away from just inside the penalty area that is deflected out for a corner. The resulting set-piece is flung into the heart of the penalty area and almost finds Gabriel but ends up flying just over the head of the Brazilian.
(36’) Janmaat launches a lovely pass up the pitch and towards Sissoko, but Koscielny does well to dart across the Arsenal penalty area before heading the ball away from the midfielder and towards Monreal on the left flank.
(34’) Arsenal move the ball around nicely before Sanchez chips a pass over the top of the Newcastle defence and into the path of Ramsey, who darts into the penalty area to meet it, but the attempted ball forward is slightly overhit and bounces out of play for a goal kick.
(32’) What a miss by Walcott! Sanchez unleashes a great strike from 25 yards out that Krul can only push into the path of the aforementioned Englishman, but somehow he ends up dinking his follow-up shot wide of the goal from close range. He really should have scored from there!
(30’) Janmaat does well to get down the right wing once again before sending a better cross into the penalty area, but it's hooked away by Bellerin before it can find Thauvin.
(28’) For the first time this game, Janmaat is able to get forward down the right flank. He battles with Monreal on the edge of the penalty area and tries to find a way past the Spaniard before trying to curl a low cross into the middle of the box, but he's unable to send it far enough past the aforementioned left-back and, as a result, it ends up flying into the side-netting.
--- 26’ Yellow card Another poor sliding challenge, this time from Thauvin, results in a fourth card. The Newcastle players are being far too reckless with their tackles and it's already proving to cause them a huge amount of problems. ---
(25’) The visitors patiently pass the ball around deep inside the Newcastle half of the pitch before Coquelin tries to find Cazorla with a lofted pass forward, but it's cut out by Janmaat, who rises high to meet the ball.
(23’) Arsenal keep putting the Newcastle defence under an incredible amount of pressure before earning themselves a free kick on the left wing. It's flung into the box by Sanchez but fails to find a red and white shirt before Krul comfortably cuts out the danger.
(21’) Sanchez decides to shoot from the resulting set-piece, but the strike is poor and fails to beat the wall in front of him. He then tries to sprint round to the right flank but Colback is there to dispossess him with a good tackle from behind.
(20’) Frustration is growing around St. James' Park! Colback flies into Ramsey and brings the Chilean crashing to the ground with a poor sliding challenge, resulting in a free kick 30 yards away from goal, and the Newcastle midfielder is very lucky not to receive a yellow card.
--- 19’ Yellow card The referee's card is out again! This time it's Mbemba who receives a yellow card for a cynical shoulder-barge on Sanchez as the Chilean attempted to fly down the left flank. ---
(18’) Despite being down to 10 men, Newcastle push forward on a patient attack down the left flank, but they lack the instensity and movement to beat the Arsenal back line and the visitors are easily able to deal with the danger.
--- 16’ Red card! RED CARD! Newcastle are down to 10 men! Mitrovic chests the ball down before sticking his foot out and catching Coquelin on the shin with a terrible challenge, leaving the referee with no choice but to give him his marching orders. It's gone from bad to worse for Steve McClaren... ---
(15’) Sanchez darts down the left flank, taking advantage of the space left by Sissoko, before cutting inside and looking to unleash a cross, but he's pushed to the ground by Mbemba before he can do so, resulting in a free kick for Arsenal midway inside the Newcastle half of the pitch.
(13’) Arsenal scream for a penalty, but it's not given! Oxlade-Chamberlain knocks a lovely pass into the path of Bellerin, who sprints into the right-hand side of the penalty area before being clipped from behind by Thauvin. The Spaniard tumbles to the ground immediately before turning to the referee, but he shakes his head and awards a goal kick instead.
(11’) Lovely play again by Arsenal! Cazorla skips through the centre of the pitch before sending a wonderful pass into the feet of Ramsey, who immediately fires a shot from just inside the penalty area. Krul pulls off a strong save to deny the Welshman before the linesman's flag is raised for offside. The visitors are all over Newcastle at the moment.
(10’) Fantastic opportunity for Walcott! Bellerin dinks a lovely volleyed pass towards the edge of the six-yard box, where it finds the aforementioned Englishman, but he's unable to beat Krul, who rushes out to smother the shot with a good save.
(8’) Newcastle immediately break away on a dangerous counter attack down the left wing before Thauvin tries to swing a cross towards Mitrovic. It takes a slight deflection off Bellerin, however, and as a result it can only find the hands of Cech at the near post.
(7’) Sanchez is left in acres of space in the middle of the pitch, allowing him to patiently push forward before sending a lovely pass out to Oxlade-Chamberlain. (5’) Sanchez skips past Janmaat and towards the byline before chipping a dangerous cross into the heart of the penalty area that is half dealt with by the Newcastle defence before Colback finally thumps the ball away from danger and up towards the halfway line.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
Last season’s corresponding fixture resulted in a 2-1 victory for Arsenal, although Olivier Giroud, who scored both goals that day, has been controversially left out of the starting line-up for today’s clash. In his place will be Theo Walcott, and it’s going to be a big day for the Englishman, who will be desperate to prove to Arsene Wenger that he is capable of leading the line on a more regular basis.
As for Arsenal, they too have suffered a slow start to the season, although, in stark contrast to their opponents, they head to St. James’ Park in the top half of the table with four points. Poor defending caused them problems in the first two games but seemed to be a thing of the past on Monday evening when they defended resolutely to hold Liverpool to a goalless draw at the Emirates. Tough clashes against Chelsea and Manchester United lie ahead for them in the coming weeks, so they will be desperately looking for a second win of the campaign against a side that they have found great joy against in recent years, as the Gunners have failed to lose any of their last nine league games against the Magpies.
It’s been a slow start to the season for Newcastle, who head into today’s game with two points from their opening three games. A 2-2 draw with Southampton on the opening day of the campaign was followed by a disappointing defeat away to Swansea City, but they will have taken confidence from last weekend’s performance against Manchester United, in which they pulled off a great defensive display to earn themselves a well-deserved draw. They looked significantly better up front as well, with Aleksandar Mitrovic coming close to scoring his first goal for the club, whilst Georginio Wijnaldum, another of Steve McClaren’s recent acquisitions, was a constant threat in front of goal. The pair are expected to be joined by Florian Thauvin, and the trio could end up causing problems for Arsenal's injury-ridden back four.

FULL TIME - Bournemouth 1-1 Leicester: The Cherries dominated for long periods and took the lead through Wilson's acrobatic strike in the first half. However, the eased off after the interval and the Foxes stepped up their efforts to win, eventually equalising as Vardy converted from the penalty spot with four minutes of normal time remaining. It was a thoroughly entertaining game on the south coast, but Howe may be disappointed that his side couldn't take all three points.
(90’) There is the final whistle!
(90’) There are claims for a penalty as Wilson goes down in the box under the challenge of Benalouane but the referee is unmoved!
(90’) Leicester manage to keep the ball in the Bournemouth half but they cannot create space for a shot. The clock keeps on ticking down!
(90’) Kante releases Vardy down the left and the striker holds it up before feeding Schlupp. The left-back again darts to the byline and earns his side a corner. It's fired deep to Morgan but he cannot loop it back into the middle with his head.
(90’) It's a short set-piece routine for the Cherries which culminates in Francis' shot being deflected behind for a corner. It doesn't fall for a Bournemouth shirt and the visitors break.
(90’) Benalouane gives away a cheap free kick 20 yards out on the left-hand side, with Pugh dropping to the deck fairly easily under contact from the Tunisian. Can the hosts produce anything from this?
(90’) BORUC JUST GETS IT CLEAR! Kante releases Schlupp down the left and the Ghanaian gets to the byline before standing a cross up at the back post. The keeper can only get a hand to it but he is first to the second ball, punching it out of his box.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card J. Schlupp is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Schlupp becomes the latest player to enter the referee's notebook, and he is shown the yellow card for dissent. The pressure is certainly rising in stoppage time!
--- 90’ +1 Substitution Y. Benalouane enters play, replacing R. De Laet. ---
(90’) Ranieri decides to make his final change now, replacing De Laet with Benalouane. A strange choice, perhaps, when he could have brought Ulloa on and really gone for the win.
(90’) We are going to have eight minutes of added time now.
(88’) Leicester feel like they can win this now! Don't forget that we are probably going to have plenty of added time given the injury to Mings earlier in this half. It's going to be a grandstand finish!
--- 86’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAL!! THERE IS THE EQUALISER! The Foxes have reaped the rewards for turning up the pressure in the late stages as Vardy thumps the spot-kick to Boruc's left. The keeper gets his hands to it but is unable to do anything but divert it into the roof of the net! ---
(85’) PENALTY TO LEICESTER! O'Kane loses possession and Leicester feed Vardy on the left. He turns Elphick inside out so Cook comes across and sends the England international tumbling!
(83’) SCHLUPP! The left-back is playing extremely high up the pitch now and he finds plenty of space to bring down a cross-field ball. He plays a one-two with Okazaki before drilling a shot towards the far corner which drifts wide of the target.
(82’) Some great link-up play down Leicester's left results in Vardy sending a cross towards the right-hand side of the box for Dodoo. The headlines are there for the youngster to grab but he produces an air-shot!
(81’) What a challenge from Elphick! The centre-back makes a perfectly timed tackle to dispossess Okazaki in the area as the Japan international looks to spin and get a shot away from Schlupp's cutback! He simply had to get that right.
(80’) Pugh dribbles forward on the left, relieving the pressure on his defence. He turns inside and out but ends up stumbling and can only fluff a cross straight into De Laet.
(79’) The Cherries look like they are beginning to lose their composure, with the ball being hoofed long by the defence as quickly as possible. Leicester are growing in confidence and still have a substitution spare.
(77’) The Foxes are pushing for an equaliser now, with the tension rising in the Vitality Stadium. Bournemouth are getting plenty of men back and looking to threaten on the break, but it's a risky tactic to start employing after controlling the match for so long.
--- 75’ Yellow card E. O'Kane is yellow-carded. ---
(75’) O'Kane is booked for pulling on Drinkwater's shirt as the Leicester man dispossesses him in the Bournemouth half. He had to stop the break, there, but now the visitors have a great chance to test Boruc from the set-piece. Drinkwater's delivery bounces behind the defence and the keeper dives to his right and punches it clear under pressure from Morgan.
(74’) Ritchie's set-piece is disappointing once more, and the Leicester defence clear it for a thow in. The home crowd are making plenty of noise and urging their team forward in search of another goal.
(73’) Kante is caught on the ball and Bournemouth look to break. Tomlin's pass is poor but as Leicester try to play out from the back, Dodoo commits a foul on Smith.
--- 71’ Substitution M. Albrighton is replaced with J. Dodoo. ---
(71’) Ranieri makes another change, now, with Dodoo coming on for his Premier League debut with Albrighton the man to make way. Can the teenager have the same impact that he did against Bury in midweek?
(69’) Kante does well to hold up the ball 25 yards from goal before spinning and rolling a pass down the channel for Schlupp. The left-back drills a cross into the centre but the hosts' defence deal with it. Pugh gives possession away cheaply and Leicester's Frenchman puts another delivery into the box which comes to nothing.
--- 67’ Substitution M. Gradel is replaced with M. Pugh. ---
(67’) Gradel hobbles off the pitch with the aid of the medical staff and Pugh comes on in his place.
(66’) The signal for the substitution comes from the physio, so Howe is going to be forced into using his final substitution.
(65’) This is worrying for Bournemouth as Gradel is down, beating the turf after a challenge from De Laet. The Ivorian may have got his studs caught and twisted his knee. The hosts try and play on but Ritchie is dispossessed on the right and the medical staff make their way onto the pitch.
(63’) Tomlin produces a lovely backheel 20 yards out that almost puts Wilson clean through, however, a superb sliding tackle from Morgan takes the ball off his toe. Schlupp cannot get it clear, though, and Bournemouth come again. Surman tries to play a penetrating vertical pass but it doesn't quite come off for the hosts.
(61’) Ritchie rolls a lovely pass down the right for the run of Francis, and the former Southend United man angles a brilliant cross into the middle. Morgan gets up ahead of Wilson to head it away, but Bournemouth look to be getting back on the front foot now.
(59’) Vardy does well to earn the visitors a corner which Albrighton fires towards Morgan in the centre. He is unable to get his head to it and Gradel launches the ball clear. The Cherries have eased off in the last few minutes, allowing Leicester to take more of an active role in possession.

(57’) After going for a few sprints up and down the touchline to keep warm while Mings was tended to, Smith is finally introduced and the play gets back underway.
(56’) Mings is carried off the pitch with his head in his hands, suggesting that could be a bad one for the defender. The fact that the medical staff have been so delicate with him suggests there could be some ligament damage, which would be a huge blow for the Cherries.
(54’) Well, Smith is now stripped and ready on the touchline and it looks like he is going to enter the fray as Mings is loaded onto a stretcher.
(52’) Mings has dropped to the deck after coming off worse in a 50-50 challenge with Drinkwater. It looks like he may have done some damage to his knee and the medical staff are on to give him some treatment. It looks like the full-back's debut may be coming to an early end here.
(50’) Bournemouth have maintained the positive momentum that they built up in the latter stages of the first half. Ritchie floats a cross into the middle which Schmeichel is able to claim unchallenged.
--- 48’ Yellow card R. Huth is cautioned by the referee. ---
