The referee blows his whistle and the centre-back kicks the ball at the prone strike in the aftermath. Fortunately for him the connection isn't particularly strong, but Mings takes objection and the German stretches an arm his direction. Somehow, though, he only gets away with a booking.
--- 46’ Substitution T. Mings enters the game and replaces C. Daniels. ---
--- 46’ Substitution S. Okazaki enters play, replacing R. Mahrez. ---
(46’) The second half is underway! Both sides have made a change, with Mahrez making way for Okazaki for the visitors, while Mings has replaced Daniels for the Cherries.
HALF TIME - Bournemouth 1-0 Leicester: The Cherries take a one-goal lead into the interval courtesy of a sublime, acrobatic finish from Wilson. The hosts deserve their advantage having played far more adventurous football in the first half, with Daniels particularly impressive on the left. The Foxes need to make some changes soon as they've not imposed themselves at all thus far. Stay tuned for the second half.
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) Mahrez is penalised for pulling Tomlin's shirt and the hosts get another free kick wide on the left. Gradel dinks it down the line for the former Middlesbrough man but he's unable to do anything with it and Huth sends the ball upfield.
(45’) We are going to have a minimum of two added minutes at the Vitality Stadium.
(43’) Mings is out of his tracksuit and ready for action on the near side but Daniels has trotted back onto the pitch. Maybe he'll try and make it to half time so they can reassess the situation in the changing room.
(42’) There is a concern for Howe now as Daniels knocks the ball out of play 20 yards from goal and then drops to the deck, raising an arm towards the bench. It would be a big loss for the hosts if her were forced off through injury as he's been an influential figure so far.
(40’) Leicester are struggling to get out of their own half now. As Bournemouth keep pushing forward in waves the visitors are resulting to kicking the ball long to try and relieve the pressure. They clearly want to get to the break with one goal between them.
(38’) Surman drives forward from midfield and initiates a one-two with Tomlin. The forward, however, has other ideas and tries to use his team-mate's run as a decoy in order to turn inside and shoot himself. His touch isn't tight enough, though, and he is soon dispossessed.
--- 36’ Yellow card A. King receives a yellow card. ---
(36’) King receives a yellow card for a tackle on Tomlin near the halfway line. It looked like a clean challenge in which he took some of the ball, but the referee clearly wasn't happy with it.
(34’) Gradel curls the resultant free kick round the wall and on target but sends his delivery too close to Schmeichel. The keeper opts to punch it away, though, and the Ivorian collects possession and draws another foul from the Leicester defence.
(33’) The Cherries have a free kick in a great area now as Kante catches Tomlin on the edge of the box. The referee tries to play the advantage but puls the play back as nothing arises. However, the challenge was made right on the line and could well have been a penalty on another day!
(32’) Francis plays a one-two with Ritchie to get in behind on the right, only to have Morgan comes across and knock the ball out for a corner. It's taken short by the hosts but the eventual cutback towards the penalty spot is cut out by Drinkwater.
(30’) Bournemouth's left flank continues to be their greatest threat, with Gradel and Daniels linking up to great effect. This time around, though, the Ivorian's return pass to the left-back goes through his legs and brings the move to an early end.
(27’) Ranieri, with his hands on his hips, looks utterly nonplussed by what he has witnessed so far. His team have looked aimless so far, with Vardy struggling to make a mark up top on his own.
(26’) Gradel tries his luck down the left wing again and once more De Laet is unable to get close to him. However, his end product at the byline is poor and he fires his cross straight into the side netting of Schmeichel's goal.

Daniels plays a one-two with Tomlin before driving a cross into the box. Gradel manages to keep it alive and his touch falls kindly for Wilson, who fires an overhead kick into the back of the net for his fourth Premier League goal this season! ---
(22’) STAT: All eight league meetings between Leicester and Bournemouth have been won by a single-goal margin.
(20’) SO CLOSE FROM DANIELS! The left-back has been fairly adventurous this afternoon and he is left in too much space by the ball-watching Mahrez. Schmeichel is forced to scurry across his line and will be relived to see it drift narrowly wide of the upright!
(18’) Neither team has really settled yet, with the action still fairly open and possession changing hands frequently. Huth steps up from the back to bring down and aerial ball and drive his team forward but an awkward bounce sees it hit his arm.

(1’) Leicester get the ball rolling on the south coast!

Mark Noble beautifully picked out the left back who turned Nathaniel Clyne absolutely inside out. Perhaps he would've been better off looking for one of his teammates but you can't blame him for taking the shot on after doing so well to open up the chance for himself.
(74’) Silly free-kick given away by Cresswell gives Milner the opportunity to swing a cross into the box. The set piece is rather lofty and Benteke is penalised for a foul on Winston Reid. Time is running out for Liverpool and it is all beginning to look rather desperate.
(72’) Sakho, who has been pretty quiet today but going into the last twenty minutes or so, he clearly fancies having a run at Lovren and Skrtel now. If the pattern of the match continues in this vein it seems much more likely that West Ham will add a third rather than Liverpool getting one back.
--- 70’ Yellow card Lucas Leiva receives a yellow card. ---
(70’) SHOT! Sakho and Lanzini combine nicely on the edge of the area but the ball ends up popping out to the onrushing Kouyate who tries to place his shot into the bottom corner but it doesn't have sufficient power to significantly trouble Mignolet.
(68’) Liverpool can simply not keep hold of the ball at the moment. They are giving the ball away as quickly as they can win it back. West Ham look very comfortable at the present time and it is hard to see the home side getting back into it as things stand. Ings has made a positive difference since coming on it must be said.
(66’) The West Ham travelling supporters are chanting 'Ole' with each successful pass. The move ends with Lovren clearing Cresswell's dangerous low cross at the near post. Everything has gone right for the visitors today and the away fans are clearly enjoying their day out.
(63’) WIDE! Milner drags his shot just wide of the post but he has to hit the target there. Ings had done well to divert Moreno's cross into the path of the former Manchester City midfielder but the England stalwart can't work Randolph in the West Ham goal. Big, big opportunity missed there.
--- 61’ Substitution D. Ings enters the game and replaces Roberto Firmino. ---
(61’) West Ham get a bit of relief by forcing a corner from Joe Gomez. Once again though, like Liverpool did at the end of the first half, they opt to take it short rather than trying to make use of their numerical advantage in the box. The ball works its way out to Cresswell who overhits his cross and it is easily claimed by Mignolet.
(59’) Danny Ings will now make his Anfield debut coming on in place of Roberto Firmino. Brendan Rodgers will hope that the former Burnley striker can feed off of Benteke's knock-downs as Liverpool look to claw their way back into contention.
(57’) The West Ham midfield trio of Kouyate, Noble and Obiang have been nothing short of exceptional this afternoon. They have not given Liverpool a moments peace. Pressing and dropping off at the right times, giving brilliant protection to the back four and keeping a consistent shape.
(55’) Ogbonna not for the first time this afternoon has a handful of Christian Benteke's shirt as the Liverpool centre forward tries to hold the ball up for his team. The West Ham defender is playing a very dangerous game, absolutely no need for the away side to take any risks whatsoever at this stage of the game.
(53’) SHOT! From a very, very long way out Dejan Lovren has a crack at goal and certainly gets hold of his shot. Randolph however, is right behind it and comfortably holds on to it. That is the first piece of meaningful action for the West Ham.
--- 52’ Red card! RED CARD! Coutinho's unhappy afternoon comes to a premature end after a rash tackle on Payet. The Brazilian picks up his second yellow card and has to go. The Liverpool number 10 was cautioned late in the first half and then put in an unnecessary and reckless challenge that leaves his team in all sorts of trouble. ---
(49’) OVER! Coutinho fires the ball over the crossbar from about 30 yards out. It was certainly well within his range but he just couldn't keep his shot down. West Ham will be reasonably happy to let Liverpool have speculative efforts from that sort of distance.
(47’) Moreno is already seeing plenty of the ball since coming on as Liverpool look to stretch the game. Benteke is looking increasingly isolated as the service into is becoming more and more hopeful. Reid and Ogbonna are marshalling the big Belgian well and are successfully crowding him out.
--- 46’ Substitution Alberto Moreno enters play, replacing E. Can. ---
(46’) Liverpool have switched to a 3-5-2 with Moreno and Clyne as the wing backs with Joe Gomez dropping into a back three. Will it have the desired effect? We'll soon see...
(45’) West Ham get the game restarted. One change for the homeside with Emre Can being replaced by Alberto Moreno.
Liverpool must be contemplating changes at this stage in an attempt to get back into the match. Rodgers has plenty of options with Origi, Ings, Ibe and Moreno waiting in the wings. The danger for the Reds is that they will leave themselves open on the counter attack as they push for a goal back.
I'm sure that the first 45 minutes is has exceeded even the wildest expectations of anyone of a West Ham persuasion. Bilic's gameplan has been implemented perfectly. If anything, the Hammers boss might be disappointed that they have not taken some more of the good chances. The game could concievably be three or four up at the break.
What a story we have unfolding here at Anfield. West Ham are on course for a famous victory at a traditionally unhappy hunting ground for the East Londoners. Brendan Rodgers will be far from pleased with his side's first half performance. The first 15 minutes of the second half will be crucial for both teams.
--- 45’ +4 Yellow card Philippe Coutinho is cautioned by the referee. ---
(45’) That's half time! Liverpool 0-2 West Ham United.
(45’) The mood of the Liverpool fans has not been improved by the decision of James Milner to take a short corner which then breaks down. Why wouldn't you throw the ball into the penalty area just before the half time interval. A bizarre choice that backfired horribly.
(45’) We're into four minutes of added time at the end of this first half and West Ham are taking every opportunity to run the clock down. Liverpool on the other hand have looked far too narrow, especially down the left side. it wouldn't be a great surprise to see Moreno come on to provide some more natural width.
(45’) Lanzini really has been a revelation for the visitors in this first half. He has been incredibly positive on and off the ball, giving his side a real outlet. Liverpool have been rather stifled by West Ham's tactics thus far.
(43’) It has been a really disjointed first half performance from Liverpool. They have looked shaky at the back and have lacked fluency going forward. Lovren, not for the first time in his Anfield career has not covered himself in glory so far. Big team talk coming up for Brendan Rodgers, in truth it could be worse for the home side.
(41’) West Ham are just beginning to drop a little bit too deep and this is inviting pressure. From Slaven Bilic's point of view it is vital that they go into the break at 2-0 up.
(39’) Firmino just about keeps the ball in play in the inside left position and picks out his compatriot Coutinho, who looks to work half a yard on the top of the box but his low shot is superbly blocked. The West Ham defenders are really putting their bodies on the line when required today.
--- 38’ Yellow card M. Noble is yellow-carded. ---
(37’) The Anfield crowd are becoming more and more agitated which is being reflected by the players on the pitch. Mark Noble becomes the first player to be yellow carded and it appears to be a bit of a harsh decision. it was a full blooded challenge with Emre Can but the West Ham skipper seemed to win the ball.
(35’) Cresswell and the rest of the West Ham player's have reacted very well to the disappointment of last Saturday. The Hammers left back is having a great afternoon so far. The away side continue to create chances. Mark Noble this time half volleys the ball over Mignolet's goal.
(33’) This time it is the left back Joe Gomez who gallops down the wing on the overlap but he can't control his attempted cross which is sliced over Randolph's cross bar.
(31’) Slight delay in proceedings as first Sakho and then Kouyate need to receive treatment from the West Ham medical team. Kouyate landed awkwardly after a strong tackle from Liverpool captain James Milner.
--- 29’ Goal! Lovren made a horrible mess of things in the left back position and the lively Lanzini took full advantage surging into the box squaring the ball to Sakho who's effort was snuffed out but the ball dropped to Mark Noble, who was the calmest man in the stadium as he slotted the ball in the bottom corner. Superb composure. That goal has really put th cat amongst the pigeons here at Anfield the visitors two up inside half an hour! ---
(28’) GOAL! WEST HAM HAVE DONE IT AGAIN! 0-2! Skipper Mark Noble with the finish.
(26’) CHANCE! West Ham could and possibly should be two-nil up here. Kouyate burst into the Liverpool penalty area, his shot was blocked but it fell kindly for the marauding Aaron Cresswell who really should have done better with his weaker right foot blazing it high over the bar.
(24’) West Ham on occasion are pressing Liverpool high up the pitch which is frustrating the home faithful. Clyne then forces another corner after is deflected cross was put behind by Randolph. The set piece comes to nothing but Benteke appeared was being held there, the Hammers will need to be careful with that in future.
(22’) Liverpool, as you would expect have had plenty of the ball, particularly since going behind but they are finding it hard to get in behind this resolute West Ham defence. The Reds are being probing and patient in possession but are lacking that penetrating final pass at the moment.
(20’) So far, so good for Slaven Bilic's side who needed a positive reaction after that shock defeat at home to Bournemouth last weekend. The West Ham back four have been dominant in the air and have been well supported by a disciplined and organised midfield and attack in front of them.
(18’) As they did on Monday night Brendan Rodgers' side are looking to hit Christian Benteke at every opportunity and have put in plenty of crosses and long balls into the box. Clyne is providing great width on the right-hand side.
(16’) WIDE! Lanzini fires a shot wide after being given acres of room in the Liverpool midfield. The youngster is full of confidence after his goal and might be a little disappointed that he did not work Mignolet there.
(14’) Payet whips in a devillish delivery from a free-kick on the right wing which Tomkins does well to control before Liverpool smuggle the ball away for a corner. West Ham are looking a real threat whenever they go forward. The Liverpool backline looks distinctly fragile at the moment.
(12’) The travelling West Ham fans are in terrific voice as you would expect after making such a dream start to this match. The Liverpool fans still seem to be in a bit of shock after going behind so early on.
(10’) There was a coming together in the West Ham penalty area between Reid and Benteke but nothing doing from the referee. The big Liverpool no.9 went down a bit too easily there. Good, strong defending from the New Zealand international.
(9’) OFF THE POST! Firmino is oh so close to scoring his first Liverpool goal and it would have been a wonderstrike. The Brazilian unleashed a left foot shot from 25 yards out that rattled the woodwork with Randolph well beaten. Unlucky.
(7’) Coutinho immediately tries to get the Reds back on level terms by working some room for himself on the edge of the area but this time he can't produce a moment of magic and the ball sails harmlessly over the bar.
(5’) Would you believe that Lanzini's goal is the first to be scored by a West Ham player at Anfield in nine years! Bobby Zamora was the last Hammer to get on the scoresheet away against Liverpool in August 2006.
--- 3’ Assist The assist came from A. Cresswell. ---
--- 3’ Goal! GOAL! 0-1 WEST HAM! Lanzini has scored on his debut in front of the Kop. What a start for the youngster! Cresswell picked the ball up on the top of the penalty area, he stabbed the ball across the face of the goal and Lanzini was on hand to tap in from close range. That was far too easy for the Hammers, poor defending from Liverpool. ---
(2’) Liverpool have made a bright start to this match and are looking to take the game to the opposition. Clyne sends in a deep cross which Tomkins calmly chests back to West Ham goalkeeper Randolph.
(1’) Liverpool get us underway and they will kick towards the Anfield Road end in this first half. The home side are in their traditional all red strip while West Ham are in their away kit of all sky blue.
West Ham's record at Anfield is not good to say the least and if they defend in the same way as they did at home to Bournemouth last weekend it will be a very long afternoon for the visitors. Aaron Cresswell  had a torrid time last Saturday and will want to put that right. He will need to be near his best to contain the likes of Coutinho and Firmino.
Slaven Bilic keeps faith in Diafra Sakho despite the striker being in the news for the wrong reasons this week. Meanwhile, Kevin Nolan left the club by mutual consent this week and Manuel Lanzini takes his place in the starting lineup. James Tomkins comes in for the suspended Carl Jenkinson.
Brendan Rodgers sticks with the same eleven that put in a pretty impressive performance, particularly in the first half, away at the Emirates. This means Danny Ings still has to wait for his first start for the club. Jordan Henderson and Adam Lallana are not fit enough yet to return to the squad.
WEST HAM SUBS: Spiegel, Jarvis, Oxford, Cullen, Samuelson, Lee and Knoyle.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Bogdan, Sakho, Moreno, Origi, Ings, Ibe and Rossiter.
WEST HAM UNITED (4-3-3): Randolph; Tomkins, Reid, Ogbonna, Cresswell; Kouyate, Noble (c), Obiang; Lanzini, Sakho, Payet.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Mignolet; Clyne, Lovren, Skrtel, Gomez; Milner (c), Lucas, Can; Firmino, Benteke, Coutinho.

Next up for Man City after the international break is an away clash against Crystal Palace, while Watford play hosts to high-flying Swansea City, with the Hornets still looking for their first win of the new season.
Watford defended superbly in the first half but you always wondered how long they could hang on for without a striker up top, with Deeney playing in an unconventional right-wing role in a 4-2-4 system. It was designed purely to shutout Man City but the hosts had too much quality in the end.
Second half goals from Raheem Sterling and Fernandinho have handed Man City a 2-0 win over Watford at the Etihad Stadium today. The victory means the Citizens have made a 100% start to the new campaign, winning all four games and conceding none.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 WATFORD
(90’) Iheanacho gets his first touch of the ball on his Premier League debut with the home fans cheering in the background. Watford have been off the pace for a while now but they will learn from today and can build on a solid first half showing.
(90’) The officials have announced that a minimum of two added minutes are being added on to this first half, as Man City continue to keep possession and run down the clock.
--- 89’ Substitution Sterling comes off pleased with his competitive Man City goal as young striker Kelechi Iheanacho runs onto the pitch in his place. The Citizens have big hopes for the academy graduate and it will be interesting to see if he can make an impact. ---
(88’) Nasri plays a lovely one-two with Sterling and stings the palms of Gomes with a powerful long-range effort. The Watford 'keeper prevents Aguero getting a tap-in with a good parry.
(86’) Anya drives towards Sagna but the Frenchman is equal to him and forces the ball out for a Watford throw-in. He's making it very difficult for Pablo Zabaleta to come back into the starting lineup when he's fit again after starting the new Premier League campaign brilliantly.
(84’) And today just keeps getting even better for Man City as the news comes through that title rivals Chelsea are losing 2-1 against Crystal Palace at Stamford Bridge.
(82’) Man City are keeping possession ticking over at the moment as opposed to thrusting bodies forward in search for a third. It seems as though they're happy with a 2-0 win and they've been made to work for it by Watford.
(80’) Nasri has come on and made a real difference for Man City today. With it looking like De Bruyne will join the club in the coming days, the Frenchman may fall down the pecking order even further but - just like he was against Everton last weekend - he has been brilliant as a second half substitute.
(78’) It will be interesting to see if Watford look to strengthen their striking department before the window closes, should they fail to score for the fourth consecutive game in these closing stages. Deeney, to be fair, hasn't even been given the opportunity to play up top today and can't be blamed for their lack of goals.
--- 76’ Substitution Quique Flores makes his final substitution of the game as Capoue comes off for Watson in the middle of the park. The Frenchman was his usual combative self and his partnership with Behrami will cause teams problems all season long. ---
(76’) It's all Man City at the moment as time ticks on in the second half. Watford were banking on keeping them out for a 0-0 draw and you knew their heads would drop if they were to concede today.
--- 75’ Substitution Silva, who had a big hand in both of Man City's goals so far today, comes off to a usual standing ovation at the Etihad. Delph comes off the bench to make his competitive home debut for the hosts. ---
(74’) SO CLOSE! It's more fluid football from Man City as Kolarov drives a low cross towards Toure, who swings his left foot at the ball first time and sees his effort fly just wide of the post.
--- 72’ Substitution Mexico international Layun comes on for Ighalo as Watford look to add even more pace to hit Man City with. The former played well in spells today but couldn't get forward enough. ---
(72’) Aguero goes down under a Behrami challenge but the referee waves away the City striker's protests as Watford launch a counter-attack. Deeney tries to create half a yard for himself but Kompany does enough to prevent him testing Hart from outside the box.
(70’) Watford are having a good spell of possession at the moment and it looks as though they're about to make a double change, with Layun and Diamanti both stripped on the touchline.
(68’) Watford's good defending in the first half mustn't be forgotten come the full-time whistle if the score stays the same, but Man City are in cruise control at the moment and are looking a good bet to add to their two-goal lead.
(66’) CHANCE! Deeney runs over the ball as Anya comes in from the left-hand side and tries to test Hart from close range, but Sagna makes a superb block in the nick of time. Corner for Watford.
(64’) Silva steps up and curls the ball over the crossbar as Gomes breathes a sight of relief between the sticks. The angle was always against the former Valencia man there.
--- 63’ Yellow card Prodl catches Aguero high on his left leg just outside the penalty area and picks up a deserved yellow card as a result. Watford now have two of their defenders' names in the referee's book. ---
--- 63’ Substitution Abdi comes off after the hour mark for Anya, with the real notable difference between them being the latter has more pace to inject into this game for the visitors. ---
(62’) Man City have a free-kick in a dangerous position as Prodl hacks down Aguero just outside the box on the breakaway. Silva is standing over it for the hosts.
(60’) Sterling locks onto Toure's pass on the counter-attack but as he looks to slip in Sagna on the overlap, Holebas gets back in time and snuffs out the danger for Watford. There is a lot more space for the hosts to operate in now and they're making the most of it.
(58’) BIG MISS! Silva, Toure and Sterling link up excellently as the first Man City goalscorer today slips the ball to Aguero on the penalty spot, but the Argentine fails to make the net bulge for a third time as he messes up his kick from close range.
(57’) You always felt that Watford couldn't keep Man City out with every man behind the ball for the whole game and you have to worry for them that the floodgates could open now. Silva makes the difference yet again for the hosts with his 50th Premier League assist.
--- 56’ Assist Assist by David Silva. ---
--- 56’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAALLL!! It's 2-0 to Man City! Toure's free-kick gets blocked by the Watford wall but only to Silva, who cleverly plays in Fernandinho and the midfielder slams home his second goal of the season superbly. ---
(54’) Behrami pulls Nasri to the ground after the Frenchman flew inside from the left. This is a great goalscoring chance for Man City just outside the penalty area, with Toure standing over it.
(53’) Sterling spins away from Prodl down the left and although he stays on his feet, the winger wins a free-kick after the Watford man rushes in on him. Nasri curls in the resulting set-play, which flies straight into Gomes' arms.
(51’) Sterling's opener has meant Watford now have to open up a bit more, with Deeney moving away from the right to the striker's position. This could play into Man City's hands further but we shall see.
(49’) All of Watford's hard work is undone 90 seconds after the restart. Silva creates the space wonderfully for Sagna to set up Sterling, who has moved up front after Navas went off during the half-time break.
--- 47’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAALLL!! It's 1-0 to Man City and it's Sterling's first goal for the club! Sagna whips in a delightful cross towards the six-yard box and the summer signing was on hand to tap home unmarked with aplomb. ---
--- 47’ Assist B. Sagna gave the assist. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Navas comes off during the interval for Nasri. The Spaniard was rather quiet in the first half but it appears it's more a tactical change for the hosts, with Sterling moving more centrally and Silva heading out onto the right. ---
(46’) Welcome back! Man City get us underway for the second half here at the Etihad Stadium, with Samir Nasri coming on for Jesus Navas during the interval.
Watford are playing their way out of trouble, with no striker to launch balls towards, but while that has been brave in one sense, they've also caused themselves a few problems as well as City have caught them cold a couple of times. They'll need to quash those errors down if they're to remain unbeaten come full-time.
Pellegrini won't be disappointed with his players but he'll definitely want them to add more pace to their play in order to break Watford down. The Hornets are lacking a striker, with Deeney sitting on the right in a 4-2-4, and therefore pressing them in their own half would be another route that could produce goals for the Citizens.
Well, well, well. It's been a first half that has lacked in excitement in terms of goalscoring chances at the Etihad but fans of defensive football will be pleased with the way Watford have so far managed to shutout Man City. It's been backs to the wall stuff from the visitors but it's done the job and it's been quite admirable to watch.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 0-0 WATFORD
(44’) There is just the one minute being added on to this first half, with Watford currently in possession with plenty of neat and tidy passes being played in the middle of the park.
--- 43’ Yellow card Nyom dives in on Sterling down the flank and gets absolutely nowhere near the ball. The right-back deservedly picks up Watford's first caution of the game. ---
(42’) Pellegrini will certainly be telling his players to increase the speed in their game after the interval as Man City have been too slow for large spells of this first half. Watford to deserve a large slice of credit for that, though.
--- 40’ Yellow card Kompany receives the first yellow card of the game from Mark Clattenburg as he dives in needlessly on Jurado inside his own half. The Man City defender has rarely had a challenge to make after 40 minutes. ---
(39’) CLOSE! Abdi, with no Watford striker to hit, gives the ball away in his own half and allows Aguero the chance to shift the ball from left to right, but the City stiker sends his effort just wide of the post.
(37’) Man City win a free-kick as Behrami gets too tight to Aguero in the middle of the park. The set play is much-needed by the hosts, who could do with another alternative to try and break Watford down.
(35’) With just 10 minutes to go in the first half, Watford are continuing for frustrate the hosts by getting every man behind the ball. They've protected Gomes between the sticks admirably and Quique Flores will be delighted with what he has seen from his players so far.
(33’) Watford enjoy their best spell of possession as they try to build their way up the pitch through neat triangle passing methods. That's been their plan from the get-go, with so many bodies getting behind the ball when Man City are on it.
(31’) Sterling picks up the balll just outside the box from Silva and tries to set up Toure for a trademark long-range drive, but Behrami steps in quickly and clears the danger for Watford.
(29’) Fernandinho plays in Sterling and as the ex-Liverpool man looks to send in a cross, he is surrounded by several Watford jerseys, with Nyom crashing the ball out for a throw-in.
(27’) GREAT SAVE! Watford give the ball away to Sterling in their own half and the winger drives past Nyom, with his low effort just about getting tipped around the post and out for a corner by Gomes. Superb goalkeeping from the Brazilian.
(26’) Navas drives at Holebas and wins yet another corner for Man City. The former Sevilla man curls the resulting set-play in which falls to Sagna, who drives a shot straight into the arms of Gomes.
(24’) Watford have defended really well in the opening spells of this first half but they're risking getting caught cold in their own half with no striker up front to hit from deep areas with long balls.
(23’) Navas drives a pass straight into the feet of Capoue but the Frenchman gives the ball away as they have no outlet up front, with Deeney operating as almost a second right-back to stop Kolarov and Sterling with Nyom.
(22’) It was always going to be important for Watford to keep solid and compact in the first 20 minutes of this game and they have done exactly that so far. The tempo of the match has slowed down in their favour, as have the noise levels.
(20’) Aguero wins a free-kick for Man City and gifts Kolarov a great chance to make it two goals in two for him, but the Serbian powers his effort well over the crossbar from just outside the box.
(18’) Silva tries to spin away into a pocket of space down the left but Behrami tracks him every step of the way and wins a throw-in off the Spaniard with a tough-looking slide tackle. Excellent defending.
(16’) Silva plays in the Man City corner but Deeney rises the highest in the midst of a queue of bodies and clears the danger for Watford. Jurado tries to launch a counter-attack but Sterling tracks back brilliantly and prevents the breakaway.
(14’) Watford play in two consecutive corners aimed at Prodl but Man City are able to just about deal with both and win one of their own on the counter-attack through Kolarov.
(12’) Aguero spins away from Catchcart and plays in Toure, only for the official on that far side of the pitch to raise his flag for offside. Man City are looking towards the Argentine to be the man to spring attacks off.
(11’) Man City continue to dominate possession but are needing to be patient in order to break down this sturdy Watford structure. Deeney is lining up on the right without the ball in a 4-2-4 formation, with every man behind the ball for the Hornets at the moment.
(9’) After the first few minutes we can see that it is Ighalo who is lining up on the left-hand side for Watford, while Jurado is the man chosen to operate the position just behind Deeney. The Spaniard has made a good start to this first half.
(7’) Aguero collects the ball from Silva and tries to weave his way into the penalty area, but Capoue drops back and snuffs out the danger with an important interception in the nick of time. Great defending from him.
(6’) Jurado breaks away through the middle of the park and tries to feed in Ighalo on the counter-attack but the Nigerian fails to latch onto the ball as Fernandinho intercepts brilliantly.
(5’) Abdi wins a free-kick for Watford after Toure pulls him down on the breakaway, with the Ivory Coast international perhaps a tad fortunate to not receive a yellow card for that.
(3’) Sterling cuts inside from the left and attempts a lovely give-and-go with Silva, but the Spaniard overcooks his pass and sees it run through to Gomes between the Watford sticks.
(2’) Silva wins an early corner for City off a Prodl challenge and aims his delivery towards Mangala, but the Frenchman fails to get on the end of it as the ball runs away from Watford's box.
(1’) Watford get us underway here at the Etihad Stadium. The man in charge of the cards for today's affair is Mark Clattenburg.
Both sets of players are stripped and raring to go as they leave the tunnel and head out onto the turf here at the Etihad Stadium. We are just minutes away from seeing the action get underway.
Both sides have dropped in and out of the top flight in the last decade or two but they have faced off recently. Man City claimed two home wins over Watford in the 2013 and 2014 FA Cup tournaments, with the Citizens having to come back from two goals down to be victorious in the latter.
Pellegrini's men are looking to achieve a club record 10th consecutive top-flight win today, while Watford are in search of their first victory of the new season. The last time the latter beat Man City in a top-flight game was back in April 1987 at Maine Road.
Man City have been the early pace-setters at the top of the Premier League summit after three games but they face a tough test, on paper, against Watford today. Today's visitors to the Etihad are unbeaten in their last five top-flight games and haven't conceded in their last two.

FULL TIME! Southampton defeat Norwich by a comfortable 3-0 scoreline, earning the home side their first Premier League win of the season. Goals from Pelle and Tadic were enough, after Whittaker saw red for the Canaries just after the half-hour mark. That's all that we have time for from St. Mary's, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again!
(90’) Johnson tests the Saints' goalkeeper! The former Leeds man sees a shot from 30 yards parried out, with Hooper only able to drag a close-range effort way wide of the far post!
(90’) Juanmi tries to slide a through ball straight into Rodriguez, but the ball fizzes off Howson and behind! The referee, however, points for a goal kick. If the scoreline had been a little different, perhaps the England international would have complained a little more.
(90’) We're into the first of three minutes of stoppage time!
--- 89’ Substitution G. Hooper enters the game and replaces C. Jerome. ---
(89’) Brady curls in a cross-cum-shot from the right-hand side, with the ball zipping narrowly over Stekelenburg's crossbar! The resulting goal kick allows for a break in play, with Hooper able to replace Jerome for the dying embers of the contest.
(87’) Southampton win themselves a corner on the right-hand side, but Ruddy is yet again able to command his area well. Only a few minutes are left on the clock, with Koeman's men set to pick up a much-needed first three points of the Premier League season.
(85’) Juanmi hangs a cross up towards the edge of the six-yard box, but Ruddy claims ahead of Pelle. Norwich try to break forward for a consolation goal, with Johnson teeing up Tettey, but the Norwegian midfielder blasts a horrific effort high and wide of the target.
(83’) Both sides would probably want the final whistle to come as soon as possible. Norwich haven't been in this contest at all, especially since the half-hour mark when Whittaker saw red. They will just hope that they can keep things tight at the back until the very end. Bassong comes across neatly to deny an attempted through ball from Tadic.
--- 81’ Substitution Juanmi enters the game and replaces S. Mané. ---
(81’) Juanmi comes into the game for the final 10 minutes. Ward-Prowse takes the aforementioned free kick, but the young Englishman can only guide his effort over the wall and wide of the target. That was a poor attempt from the Saints' youngster, with Ruddy not needing to move an inch.
(79’) Play is opened out to the Saints' right-hand side, but Brady does well to outmuscle Tadic. Norwich attempt to break through Wisdom, but the Liverpool loanee is promptly dispossessed and the home side can counter. Mane dances around Tettey, with the Norway international bringing down the Senegalese forward, earning his side a free kick in a dangerous area.
(77’) Southampton link up with some lovely one-touch passages of play, with the mood in the stadium extremely positive now. This comfortable win could be exactly the confidence boost that everyone involved with the club needed. Redmond beats Martina down the left, but Fonte is present to block the Englishman's eventual cross!
(75’) Important clearing header from Bassong! The ex-Spurs defender rises well at the near post to deny a dangerous cross in from Tadic, given that Rodriguez and Pelle were queuing up behind him. Rodriguez chops in from the left-hand side, before curling an effort just over the crossbar! Moments earlier, Howson and Jerome were getting themselves into a heated argument - things aren't quite going according to plan for the Canaries.
(73’) Martina comes into the game in place of Cedric, with Koeman opting to give the former Sporting man a rest after terrorising the right-hand side throughout. Brady tries to curl a cross in towards Jerome and Redmond, but Stekelenburg claims with ease.
--- 72’ Substitution R. Martina enters play, replacing Cédric Soares. ---
(71’) Southampton are continuing to look down the right-hand side, with Brady really struggling when trying to deal with the partnership of Mane and Cedric. Norwich are sitting deep, with Jerome still offering nothing up front due to a lack of the ball. Rodriguez then lashes a volleyed effort just wide of the near post!
--- 70’ Substitution G. Dorrans is replaced with B. Johnson. ---
(69’) The home side are totally in control, with their fans now jubilant at St. Mary's. Mane and Pelle attempt to combine with a one-two, but the return pass from the latter is placed too close to Ruddy. Only around 20 minutes remain for the Canaries to suffer through, before what will feel like a long journey home.
--- 67’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! GAME OVER! 3-0! Tadic taps home! A cross from the right-hand side is headed towards goal by Pelle, with Ruddy able to make a reasonable save! The rebound falls to the Serbian midfielder, who doubles his tally for the afternoon! ---
(66’) Norwich have to decide whether to stick or twist at the moment, as the Canaries are simply sitting back and absorbing pressure, which will surely result in further Saints goals. Whittaker's red card has been vital in this game, with the Scotland international largely to blame for the home team's domination.
--- 64’ Assist Assist by S. Mané. ---
--- 64’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! TADIC MAKES IT 2-0! Mane drives his way down the right-hand side brilliantly, before cutting back a neat low cross to the back post! The former Groningen midfielder is on hand to guide a first-touch finish across goal and into the top corner! Brilliant stuff! ---
(63’) Just over from Pelle! The Italy international can't keep his header down from a corner, though the Southampton goalscorer is furious that the referee didn't spot Bassong tugging on his shirt. Crosses continue to be the main theme of the Saints' approach play, but they aren't proving to be fruitful at the moment.
(61’) Brady is able to take a corner, as a result of some suspect defending from Cedric, but Bassong is beaten to the delivery at the expense of another Norwich set piece. The second is hoofed immediately clear by Ward-Prowse. That is probably the closest that the Canaries have come to threatening Stekelenburg's net in about 40 minutes of play.
(59’) Just wide from Pelle! The Italy international is found on the periphery of the box once again by Mane, with the former Feyenoord man sweeping a low strike just beyond the right upright with his first touch! It makes the side netting quiver on its way behind for a goal kick!
(57’) Ruddy gives away a terrible pass, which allows for Mane to pick up the loose ball on the edge of the penalty area! The ex-Salzburg man cuts in from the right-hand side, before forcing the visiting goalkeeper into a great save! Moments later, Rodriguez is picked out by Pelle on the break, but the former Burnley striker is again denied by Ruddy!
(55’) Redmond tries to break down the right, but Targett does excellently again to hold up the wide man. Dorrans eventually whips in a cross from the right, but Yoshida heads to safety. Norwich just aren't able tot create anything here this afternoon.
(53’) Rodriguez lines up a shot on the edge of the box, but Bassong stretches to make a timely block. Moments later, Jerome is penalised for catching Yoshida in the hip with his knee, with the Englishman looking at the referee with disbelief. The hosts break down the right through Cedric as a result, but the Portuguese full-back's cross is claimed confidently by Ruddy.
(51’) A rare delivery into the Southampton penalty area is easily caught by Stekelenburg, with Neil's men struggling to get firing offensively. Moments later, Brady attempts to dip in a cross, but it bounces straight out of play on the far side for a throw in. His coach does not look impressed.
(49’) Rodriguez manages to whip a cross in from the left-hand side, but Pelle can only send a looping header into Ruddy's grasp! Southampton have started the second half as they ended the first period, with plenty of red and white shirts piling forward in an attempt to double the hosts' advantage.
(47’) Tadic and Pelle combine well down the left-hand side, before the latter angles a neat pass forward in search of Rodriguez. The England international attempts to take the ball in his stride, but Brady covers across well to deny him. Moments later, Ruddy makes a good save to frustrate Rodriguez, but the linesman's flag was already raised for offside.
--- 46’ Substitution J. Rodriguez comes on for S. Davis. ---
(46’) We are underway in the second half at St. Mary's! Jay Rodriguez has been introduced into the fray in place of Davis, with it apparent that Koeman wants his side to take the game to the ten men of Norwich.
HALF TIME! Southampton go into the break with a 1-0 lead, courtesy of a stoppage-time strike from Pelle! Koeman's men have been on top throughout, with a red card for Whittaker only making the hosts' lives easier. Norwich have struggled to get forward and will need to come up with something special to turn this contest around.
(45’) It was nearly two! Mane drives down the right-hand side, before flighting in a good cross! Pelle turns another shot towards goal, but Ruddy makes a neat save before gathering up the loose ball!
--- 45’ +1 Assist S. Mané gave the assist. ---
--- 45’ +1 Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! PELLE MAKES IT 1-0! The Italy international manages to poke a near-post finish home right on the brink of half time! Southampton win the ball high upfied, before Mane slides a pass into the ex-Feyenoord striker. Ruddy doesn't anticipate that the Saints' man will get to the ball, but he does! ---
(45’) Romeu sees a shot blocked on the edge of the penalty area, with the home fans getting a little bit restless. Brady goes down briefly, with the former Hull wide man appearing to come off worse in a clash with Pelle. The physio comes on, meaning that the visitors will be down to nine men.
(43’) Tadic opens play out to Davis on the left-hand side, but a quick cross from the Northern Ireland international is headed clear by Martin. Norwich are managing to weather the storm, with deliveries from wide areas probably suiting the stature of the Norwich captain and Bassong. Not long left for Southampton to grab an important first-half goal.
(41’) Pelle claims for another penalty, but the referee isn't interested! Mane tries to slide the Italian forward in behind Bassong, but the former Spurs defender doesn't even make a move. The Saints' man goes down claiming contact, but Bassong quite simply just stood there. A strange incident.
(39’) Cedric breaks down the right, before feeding Mane, but a cross from the latter is easily charged down. Jerome then goes on a marauding run down the left, but is unable to keep the ball in play under pressure from Fonte. The Englishman has looked incredibly isolated up top and hasn't received much service to speak of.
(37’) Wisdom covers across brilliantly to deny Mane, after the ex-Salzburg forward gallopped diagonally into the penalty area. The visitors are struggling to get out of their own half for any given period of time, with Neil presumably wanting the Canaries to hold on until the interval when they can regroup.
(35’) Southampton are dominating possession, with Norwich looking to have a long afternoon ahead of them. Davis and Mane both challenge for a cross in from the right, but the former is eased off the ball by Bassong! Ruddy races out to gather it up.
(33’) Crosses keep raining into the Norwich penalty area, with Hoolahan being sacrificed for Andre Wisdom. Jerome might just look a little bit isolated now, with the Canaries having a long time to fight with 10 men. A back-post delivery is whipped in by Cedric, but Ruddy is able to claim yet again. Wasteful delivery after wasteful delivery from the Portuguese.
--- 32’ Substitution W. Hoolahan is replaced with A. Wisdom. ---
--- 31’ Red card! RED CARD! Ward-Prowse tries to lift a long ball in behind Whittaker for Tadic to chase, with the right-back grabbing hold of his man's shirt! The ex-Twente man goes to ground and the referee has no option but to brandish another yellow in the direction of the Norwich full-back! ---
(30’) Romeu spreads play out to the right-hand side, but a cross from Cedric is cleared simply by Bassong. Moments later, Tadic is found at the back post by a cross in from Mane, following a flicked header from Pelle. The Serbian midfielder drags a shot just wide of the far post, but Ruddy had to get down to make sure it wasn't nestling inside the upright!
(28’) Yellow card for Whittaker, with the Norwich right-back grabbing hold of Targett to prevent the full-back from taking a quick throw. Tadic can look to attack his marker a little more, now. Immediately, he wriggles away from the Scotland international and whips in a cross from the right, but neither Pelle nor Mane can rise high enough to meet it! Dangerous stuff!
--- 27’ Yellow card S. Whittaker goes into the referee's book. ---
(26’) Hoolahan curls a cross in from the left, but it evades everyone and falls to Whittaker on the right-hand side. The Scotland international feeds Redmond, who tries to beat Targett with some step overs, but the young full-back isn't having any of it and easily dispossesses his opponent. Moments later, Tadic tries to curl a cross in from the left, but Pelle can only guide a glancing header wide of the far upright!
(24’) Mane tries to thread a pass through the eye of a needle, with Tettey able to step out and make a simple interception. This contest has been fairly untidy, though Redmond attempts to kick start a performance from the Canaries. The former Birmingham winger shoots on his stronger right foot, but a deflection off Fonte sends the ball looping up comfortably into Stekelenburg's arms!
(22’) Those two chances have mustered a little bit more life out of the crowd, in what has been a very quite opening 20 minutes or so. Mane drives inside from the right-hand side once again, before appearing to be impeded, but the referee decides that the wide man was making the most of minimal contact. The Senegalese forward has been the main threat.
(20’) Wide from Jerome! Dorrans is picked out on the far side by a dipping cross, with the former West Brom man able to cushion a brilliant square ball back into the danger area. The ex-Stoke striker stretches to meet it with his head, but misjudges the delivery entirely! Stekelenburg is fortunate, as contact could have meant a goal from that range!
(19’) Speculative effort from Pelle! Mane races down the right after benefitting from some nice combination play between Davis and Cedric, before whipping a cross towards the edge of the penalty area. It bounces up kindly for the Italian forward, who attempts an overhead kick from 16 yards out, but Ruddy is happy to watch it wide!
(17’) Southampton are moving the ball far better than their opponents, with the away side struggling to piece together any kind of move in the opposition half. That said, chances have been at a premium thus far. Ruddy has been the busier of the two goalkeepers, but both defences are coming out on top at the moment.
(15’) Jerome tries to stroke a pass into Howson's path, but the former Leeds man miscontrols. Southampton break, with a long ball aimed in behind Norwich's back four in search of Pelle, but Whittaker covers across to cushion back to his own goalkeeper. Quality in the final third has been decidedly low thus far. Mane also tries to race away on the counter, but Bassong makes a timely tackle.
(13’) Tadic takes a quick throw to feed Targett, with the ball then switched out to Mane on the right-hand side. The former Salzburg man jinks inside Brady, before unleashing a shot from the edge of the box, but can only find Ruddy with his effort!
(11’) Norwich finally enjoy a spell of possession of their own, but Martin then passes a terrible ball directly out of play under minor pressure from Pelle. Neil is not looking very happy in his technical area, as he thinks that his side should be a little more composed. The Saints are immediately back in control.
(9’) Wide from Pelle! The Italy international is picked out by a corner delivery, with Bassong sticking very tightly to his man. The ball appears to come off the striker's shoulder on its way beyond the left-hand post, with Ruddy happy to watch it head behind for a goal kick.
(8’) Tadic wins a free kick from Whittaker, despite the Scotland international claiming that he managed to get something on the ball. Ward-Prowse delivers again, but Ruddy is quick off his line to claim amongst a few bodies. Aside from the early free-kick effort, the Norwich goalkeeper has been untested. The hosts are still dominating, mind you!
(6’) Tettey has been combative in midfield in the opening minutes, with the visitors wanting to keep things nice and simple in front of an early Saints onslaught. Koeman's men have been camped in the opposition half for the duration. Jerome manages to rob Yoshida of possession and bring the Canaries upfield, however, before a pass out to Redmond on the far side flashes the ball straight out of play.
(4’) Targett looks down the line towards Tadic, but Martin covers across neatly to clear the ball into touch. Southampton have started very positively, with their fans responding. Tettey gives a corner away on the right flank, but Tadic takes it short. The Serbian manages to pick out Fonte at the back post, but the former Benfica man cushions a volley high of the target.
(2’) Great save from Ruddy! Bassong immediately climbs all over Pelle to give away a very early free kick. Ward-Prowse shoots from 30 yards out, but Ruddy dives across to his right to acrobatically tip the ball around the post! The resulting corner is blazed over the crossbar by Romeu!
(1’) We are underway in the first half! The hosts are wearing their customary red and white stripes, which affords Norwich the opportunity to wear their own home strip of green and yellow.
Norwich substitutes: Wisdom, Johnson, Hooper, Rudd, Bennett, O'Neil, Van Wolfswinkel.
Norwich starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Ruddy; Whittaker, Martin, Bassong, Brady; Tettey, Dorrans; Redmond, Hoolahan, Howson; Jerome.
Southampton substitutes: K. Davis, Long, Rodriguez, Martina, Reed, Juanmi, Caulker.
Southampton starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Stekelenburg; Cedric, Fonte, Yoshida, Targett; Romeu, Ward-Prowse; Mane, Davis, Tadic; Pelle.
TEAM NEWS: No surprises from Neil, with the Canaries lining up exactly as expected. Robbie Brady continues at left-back, with Nathan Redmond and Jonny Howson maintaining their places as forward-thinking wider options. Wes Hoolahan will look to pull all of the strings in behind lone striker Cameron Jerome. Lewis Grabban is left out after indiscipline, with Ricky van Wolfswinkel taking a seat on the bench, despite the Dutchman being linked heavily to a move away from the club.
TEAM NEWS: Maya Yoshida partners Jose Fonte at centre-back, with Cedric preferred to Martina at right full-back. Oriol Romeu gets another start since joining from Chelsea, with Steven Davis providing an industrious partner for the Spaniard in midfield. Sadio Mane and Dusan Tadic should offer a threat from wide areas, with Graziano Pelle hoping to add to his early season trickle of goals.

For the second match running, Swansea have come from behind to beat Man United at the Liberty. Juan Mata put the visitors in front, but goals from Andre Ayew and Bafetimbi Gomis turned the game on his head and gave Swansea the win.
FULL TIME: SWANSEA CITY 2-1 MANCHESTER UNITED
(90’) NO, THEY CAN'T! Swansea have held on for the victory!
(90’) Still no sign of United finding an equaliser. Can they pull it out the bag? They have two minutes to do so...
(90’) FOUR MINUTES! That's how many minutes of stoppage time that United have to find an equaliser. They need to be more creative in the final third than they have been.
--- 89’ Substitution K. Bartley enters the game and replaces J. Shelvey. ---
(88’) FANTASTIC DEFENDING! Rooney opens a chance for himself by nipping the ball away from Fernandez, but Williams recovers brilliantly to make a vital interception.
(86’) Fellaini wins the header in the penalty area from Shaw's deep cross but, once again, Swansea are equal to it and quite comfortably clear the danger for now.
(85’) As we enter the last five minutes at the Liberty Stadium, can Swansea hold on for a third consecutive 2-1 victory over United? It would also be their fourth in the last five meetings.
(83’) Swansea are looking like they will see out this game at the moment. They are keeping the ball very well and getting plenty of bodies behind the ball whenever United go forward.
--- 81’ Substitution Éder enters the game and replaces B. Gomis. ---
(81’) Monk looks to shore the game up as he replaces a tired Gomes with fresh legs in Eder. He is a similar player and will hold the ball up well for the Swans.
--- 80’ Yellow card J. Shelvey is yellow-carded. ---
(80’) Swansea keep the ball absolutely beautifully, as they evade tight situations and maintain possession. Their spell comes to an end, though, when Shelvey is wrongly ruled offside by the linesman.
(78’) Fellaini is straight into the action with some neat control before playing the ball out wide to Young, whose cross doesn't clear the first man at the near post as Swansea deal with it very well.
--- 77’ Substitution M. Fellaini enters play, replacing Ander Herrera. ---
(76’) The last throw of the dice from Van Gaal sees Marouane Fellaini thrown on in place of Herrera. He will play as a second striker and his height will certainly be beneficial to his team.
(74’) Young looks to make something happen for United as he sits a cross up to the far post for Depay, who cannot get enough on the header and Fabianski easily gathers.
(72’) There is rightly a lot of urgency about United all of a sudden. They are seeing plenty of the ball but really need to find some more ideas up front if they are to rescue a point.
--- 70’ Substitution M. Carrick enters the game and replaces M. Schneiderlin. ---
--- 70’ Substitution A. Young enters the game and replaces Mata. ---
(70’) A double substitution is made by Van Gaal as he now looks to salvage a point from this game. Ashley Young and Michael Carrick have been thrown on in place of Mata and Schneiderlin.
(69’) Some neat link-up play from United around the area involving Rooney and Mata sees the ball go out wide to Darmian, whose cross goes over everyone and out for a throw-in.
(68’) What an amazing few minutes for Swansea. From struggling to find a way back into the match at 1-0 down, they now lead 2-1 and are closing in on a third straight victory over United.
--- 66’ Assist The assist came from A. Ayew. ---
--- 66’ Goal! SWANSEA LEAD AND IT'S GOMIS!!! Four goals in four games for the Frenchman who latches onto a wonderful through ball from Ayew, before neatly sliding it underneath the body of a helpless Romero. What a turnaround! ---
(65’) Depay looks for Rooney with a chipped through ball but Williams is alert to the danger and quickly steps in to head away. Solid defending from the skipper and Rooney has had no change yet.
(63’) Pick a winner now! That was a wonderful equaliser from Swansea, who came from behind here to win last season's clash. Can they do the same again today? The Liberty Stadium is in full voice now.
--- 61’ Assist G. Sigurðsson gave the assist. ---
--- 61’ Goal! AYEW EQUALISES!!! Swansea hit United on the counter with Williams finding Sigurdsson in space on the right hand side. His cross is perfect for Ayew to run onto and powerfully head beyond Romero. ---
(60’) GOOD SAVE! Herrera plays a clever through ball for Mata to run onto in the penalty area, but his powerful low shot is well kept out by quick reactions from Fabianski.
--- 58’ Substitution Sung-Yong Ki enters play, replacing W. Routledge. ---
(58’) Routledge is the man to make way for the South Korean and Monk has opted for two strikers, as he pushes Ayew forward to support a so far isolated Gomis.
(57’) Ki Sung-Yeung is being geared up to come on for the Swans. He scored in both matches between the sides last season and will be looking to make it third time lucky today.
(55’) Depay looks to get in behind the Swansea defence as he tussles for the ball with Naughton, who goes down and is given the benefit of the doubt by Mr. Atkinson.
(53’) If Swansea are to come from behind in this game, they must do what no other team has done so far in the Premier League this season - score against United.
(51’) ALMOST AN OWN GOAL! Depay's cross loops towards goal after deflecting off Williams, but Fabianski does brilliantly to spare his captain's blushes by scrambling back and clawing the ball away.
(50’) OUCH! Ayew is receiving attention from the Swansea physio following a challenge from Shaw. Replays show that the United left-back accidentally stamped on his opponent's shin. Ayew should be able to run it off, though.
--- 48’ Assist Assist by L. Shaw. ---
--- 48’ Goal! MATA PUTS UNITED IN FRONT!!! Shaw embarks on a strong run down the left and his cross evades Rooney, but Mata comes steaming in and the far post to fire into the roof of the net. That's his 50th Premier League goal. ---
(47’) Sloppy play from United at the back sees Blind put pressure on Darmian, who brings down Routledge and concedes a free kick in a decent position for the Swans.
(46’) KICK OFF! Swansea get us back underway.
The teams are back out and the second half is imminent.
Van Gaal's main cause for concern will be the lack of creativity in and around the box for United. Their overall play has been decent, but they need to get more shots away at least.
Monk should look to encourage the Swans here. They looked so dangerous during their period of dominance and need to do more of the same after the break.
HALF TIME: SWANSEA 0-0 MAN UNITED
(45’) The referee swiftly blows his whistle for half time.
(45’) ONE MINUTE! We are going to have just a single minute of stoppage time at the end of this first half.
--- 43’ Yellow card W. Routledge is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) It will be interesting to see who is the happier of the two managers at the break. Other than their surge around the 20-minute mark, Garry Monk will feel Swansea can offer a lot more. Van Gaal, meanwhile, will want United to be more creative in the final third.
--- 41’ Yellow card M. Depay gets yellow. ---
(41’) With continued speculation surrounding the future of David De Gea, Romero really needs to focus and concentrate on making the number one jersey his own. You feel he would be first choice should De Gea depart.
(39’) Another slightly nervy moment for Romero sees him fumble Shelvey's deep free kick in the area, but he is able to quickly make amends and gather at the second attempt.
--- 38’ Yellow card M. Schneiderlin gets yellow. ---
(37’) Good defending from Shaw. Swansea come forward with Sigurdsson running at the United back line before finding Routledge, who is quickly closed down and dispossessed brilliantly by the left-back.
(36’) Schneiderlin bursts forward into the space and lays the ball off for Herrera, who tries his luck from the edge of the area but cannot hit the target with a drilled effort.
(35’) There is no doubt in the quality that Schweinsteiger possesses, that is evident by what he has achieved in the game. He does seem to be struggling a little, though, with the pace of the Premier League.
(33’) HALF A CHANCE FOR ROONEY! Herrera finds some space to receive the ball, turn and find Rooney who looks for a cheeky dink over Fabianski but doesn't get the required execution.
(31’) United seem a little stunned by Swansea's recent surge. They have struggled to really get back in their rhythm since and small mistakes have crept into their game.
(29’) This is more like what Swansea are capable of. They have just decided to go for it and very nearly hit the jackpot there. They must take their chances, though, or United will surely punish them.
(27’) OFF THE POST! Shelvey finds Gomis who neatly steps away from Blind and Shaw, but sees a shot with the outside of his boot just clip the post and go wide.
(26’) NERVY FROM ROMERO! A loose kick from the United keeper goes straight to Shelvey who fires the ball straight back towards goal, but Romero recovers in time to gather.
(25’) INCHES AWAY! Shelvey catches United off-guard with a quick free kick that is helped on by Gomis, before Sigurdsson pulls his effort just wide of the far post.
(23’) CHANCE FOR GOMIS! Schweinsteiger dallies on the ball and is strongly dispossessed by Shelvey, before Ayew looks to Gomis with a neat ball forward. The in-form striker takes it in his stride but shoots high and wide of the target.
(21’) CHANCE FOR MATA! United work the ball nicely into the box with Herrera laying it off for his fellow Spaniard, who fires his shot just wide of the near post.
(20’) There is a bit more urgency about United now. They are moving the ball around a lot quicker and Swansea are struggling to gain a foothold at the moment.
(18’) Shaw looks for Rooney with a beautifully weighted through ball. The United captain tries to cut inside Williams, but is denied by solid defending from the Swansea skipper.
(16’) The good times appear to have returned for United. They qualified for the Champions League with flying colours in midweek and are hoping to mount a genuine title challenge this year.

History is not on Newcastle’s side ahead of what is sure to be a tough afternoon. They have won just once at Old Trafford since 1972, with that victory coming during the middle of David Moyes’ stint in charge of the Red Devils. Both home and away, the Magpies have continually struggled against the 20-time league championships; they have lost 25 Premier League games against Manchester United, more than they have against any other side.
As for Newcastle, they have suffered a slow start to the new campaign, picking up just one point from their opening two games. An already tough clash away to Swansea last weekend was made even more difficult by Daryl Janmaat, who needlessly picked up two bookings in the first half to leave the Magpies with a mountain to climb in a game that they eventually lost. After making a plethora signings during the summer - the last of whom was French forward Florian Thauvin, who could end up featuring today - Steve McClaren’s new-look side will no doubt take some time to gel as they learn how to operate with one another, but, as the former England coach will be well aware, time is not always on your side in the Premier League, and they will have to get going quickly if they are to have any hope of improving on last season’s dreadful end to the campaign.
It’s been a solid yet unspectacular start to the season for this afternoon’s hosts, who head into their second home game with two 1-0 wins under their belts, meaning that they are one of just four clubs to boast a 100% record thus far. Tuesday evening also saw them mark their return to the Champions League with a 3-1 victory against Club Brugge, leaving them with one foot firmly in the group stage of the competition ahead of next week’s second-leg clash in Belgium. With potentially tough clashes against Swansea City, Liverpool and Southampton all coming up over the course of the next month, Louis van Gaal and his Manchester United team will be looking to keep that good momentum going today as they aim to put last season’s disappointments behind them.

Palace have won three and lost only one of their last six encounters with Villa, but their last four meetings in the English top flight have produced only three goals total. If Villa win here, it would be the second straight time that they've started a Premier League season with back-to-back away wins. With Palace losing four of their last five at home, it's not that far-fetched of a possibility.
Aston Villa also began their season with a victory, sending newly promoted Bournemouth 1-0. However, that would be the scoreline by which Manchester United would overcome them last Friday. Still, it's a mark of the improving strength of the Premier League that clubs like Palace and Villa are able to give heavy hitters like Arsenal and Man Utd so much trouble. Like Pardew, Tim Sherwood also took over at Villa earlier in 2015, but he barely avoided the drop, finishing 17th.
Palace took full points off Norwich in the opening game of the season courtesy of a 3-1 victory, and came close to snatching a result against Arsenal last week, but were ultimately denied by a 2-1 scoreline to the Gunners. The Eagles finished a club-record 10th last campaign and did so with only six games won at Selhurst Park. Still Alan Pardew, who took over in January, did a commendable job to guide the once relegation-threatened club into mid-table.

Bournemouth are quickly coming to learn how vital it is to capitalize on your chances in the Premier League. They played well in their opener against Villa, and gave it the old-college-try at Liverpool – though both times left empty handed. They had good periods of play in each match, but failing to convert chances proved to be their undoing. Scoring in the Premier League isn’t the same as the Championship, as they are quickly coming to find. Matches are tighter, defences are better and chances are harder to come by. They have a great team dynamic and chemistry is high in the room, but Eddie Howe could really do with bringing in a proven top flight goalscorer to increase their chances of survival.
West Ham were brilliant in the season-opening victory over Arsenal, playing tight and compact, while being clinical in converting their chances. Then came week two, where they were placed in Arsenal’s shoes, tasked with forcing the game – and it didn’t go nearly as well. These aren’t the days of old at the Boelyn. Teams will come here and play smart, defensive football, forcing Bilic’s side to push the issue and create chances. Sitting back and hitting teams on the counter will no longer work for them in these kinds of matches, and the sooner they realize that the better their chances of finishing inside the top six.

The defeat sends West Brom to the bottom of the table ahead of next weekend's trip to Stoke City, whilst Chelsea, who are next in action against Crystal Palace, move up into the top half of the table.
Chelsea are finally able to pick up their first victory of the season at their third attempt, but my word were they made to work hard for it! After bossing the first half, disaster struck in the second, with Terry receiving a red card early on, forcing the reigning champions into play on the back foot for the rest of the game. West Brom pushed as hard as they could but could only find their way past Courtois once, with McManaman and Morrison linking up for what was one of the best goals of the game, and, as a result, their search for a win goes on.

(42’) A poor pass from Richards sends the ball straight to Memphis, who immediately tries to tee up Rooney. However, the youngster's attempted through-ball is rushed and, as a result, poorly hit, and it ends up flying past the captain and into the feet of Guzan.
(40’) Villa are back on the front foot once again, as United seem to have tired and are now finding it difficult to string together a decent series of passes. A poor ball from Romero almost gifts possession straight to Agbonlahor, but Carrick is there to cut out the danger with a vital sliding interception.
(38’) Mata holds onto the ball for far too long, allowing Amavi to dispossess him on the left flank before firing a cross off Smalling and out for a corner. The resulting set-piece finds Richards in the heart of the United penalty area, but, off balance after wrestling with Darmian, he ends up sending his header well over the top of the crossbar. The Villa captain screams for a penalty but the referee shakes his head and signals for a goal kick.
(36’) A poor pass across the pitch from Smalling ends in the feet of Veretout, who immediately turns and tees up Westwood. The midfielder tries to send a quick through-ball towards Agbonlahor but the rushed pass is poor and misses the striker by several yards.
(35’) The hosts are finally able to regain possession, but a misplaced pass from Clarke can only find Darmian, who beats Agbonlahor to the ball before sending it back to Smalling, allowing the centre-back to kick-start another counter attack.
(33’) Villa just can't seem to get anywhere near the ball, with United absolutely dominating possession inside the hosts' half of the pitch. A series of quick passes ends with Januzaj on the edge of the penalty area, but he ends up holding onto the ball for too long and is eventually dispossessed by Richards.
(31’) With a goal under their belts, United look determined to find another before the end of the first half. They patiently work the ball around well before Rooney tries to flick a pass into the path of Januzaj, but it's slightly misplaced and hands possession to the hosts.
--- 29’ Assist Mata provided the assist. ---
--- 29’ Goal! GOAL! United have taken the lead! Mata links up with Shaw before sending an absolutely excellent through-ball straight into the feet of Januzaj. The youngster immediately spins past Richards at the near post before side-footing a low shot off the leg of Clark and into the bottom right-hand corner of the net to make it 1-0 with his first league goal since April 2014. ---
(28’) United up the tempo slightly, allowing Januzaj to break forward before sending a looping cross towards the back post. It finds the head of Memphis, but, slightly off balance, he can only direct his effort on goal well wide of the near post.
(26’) United are controlling possession at the moment but are finding it increasingly difficult to find a way past the sea of Villa shirts camped in front of them. As a result, the visitors are having to keep hold of the ball around the halfway line.
(24’) Rooney scoops a deft chip over the top of the Villa defence and into the feet of Memphis, who then sees his low strike deflected wide of the near post and out for a corner. It's taken short and sent towards the aforementioned winger, who then curls a deep cross towards the back post, but it's completely overhit and flies out of play for a goal kick.
(22’) Gueye twists and turns on the edge of the United penalty area before spinning past Carrick and attempting to send a through-ball towards Agbonlahor, but Smalling is there to cut out the pass.
(20’) The Villa defence are unable to deal with the danger, resulting in an attempted clearance bouncing off the head of Carrick and into the path of Memphis. He sprints forward and attempts to make contact with the ball on the edge of the penalty area but Guzan does extremely well to charge out and dispossess the Dutchman at the vital moment with a great sliding tackle.
(19’) Januzaj initially holds up the ball well before going down under a shove from Richards, but the referee ignores the youngster's pleas for a free kick and instead waves play on.
(17’) Great chance for Schneiderlin! Memphis curls the free kick towards the back post, where it finds the aforementioned Frenchman, but his diving header ends up flying well wide of the goal.
(16’) Richards dives into Schneiderlin and brings the Frenchman crashing to the ground, resulting in a free kick for United in a very dangerous position on the left flank.
(14’) Amavi wins the ball back well from Januzaj before Clark sends a lofted pass over the top of the United defence and into the path of Sinclair. It's slightly overhit, however, and ends up bouncing safely into the hands of Romero.
(12’) After a lengthy period of Villa possession, the hosts earn themselves a free kick just inside the visitors' half of the pitch after a clumsy challenge by Shaw on Ayew. They take it short but are unable to make it count due to the pressure being exerted on them by the United midfield.
(10’) United patiently work their way down the left flank before Memphis swings a low cross into the heart of the Villa box, but it's poorly hit by the Dutchman and is easily cut out by Richards.
(9’) Veretout breaks into the right-hand side of the United penalty area before attempting to cut inside and beat Shaw, but his final touch is poor and sends it straight into the feet of the aforementioned youngster, who then comfortably clears the danger.
(8’) Memphis is muscled off the ball by Veretout, allowing Villa to break away on yet another fast counter attack. Again, Westwood sends an impressive pass forward that this time finds Sinclair just outside of the United penalty area, but the former Manchester City man is offside and the linesman's flag is immediately raised as a result.
(6’) A lovely lofted pass from Westwood finds Amavi, who takes on Darmian only to come off second best. Villa keep hold of the ball, however, and come back at United once again, but a promising attacking move is brought to a disappointing end by Bacuna, who strays slightly offside down the right wing.
(4’) Villa push forward on a determined attack, taking advantage of the space left behind by Darmian on the left flank. They earn themselves a throw-in, which is quickly sent towards Agbonlahor, but Smalling is able to shepherd the ball out of play for a goal kick.
(2’) After a patient start to the game, United try to break through the middle of the Villa defence through Januzaj, but Richards is there to dispossess the youngster before being fouled on the halfway line.
(1’) And we're off! United get us underway, attacking from right to left.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off. The atmosphere inside the stadium is electric, with both sets of fans in fine voice.
Meanwhile, United coach Louis van Gaal has made just one alteration to the side that started at home to Spurs, with Adnan Januzaj coming in to the starting line-up to make his first league start since February. As a result, Ashley Young drops to the bench.
Tim Sherwood has decided to name an unchanged Villa side to the one that started against Bournemouth, with the only change coming on the substitutes’ bench, where Czech striker Libor Kozak returns to the first team after 18 months out due to a nasty leg break.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this evening…
As for Villa, they, too, kick off their first home game of the new season on the back of a 1-0 win thanks to last weekend’s narrow victory against new boys Bournemouth, with newly-signed Beninese striker Rudy Gestede bagging the winner midway through the second half with his first goal for the club. He is expected to feature again tonight, as are fellow new recruits Micah Richards, Jordan Amavi, Jordan Veretout, Idrissa Gueye and Jordan Ayew, all of whom played a part in their opening day success.
United head to Birmingham with three points under their belts thanks to a narrow 1-0 victory at home to Tottenham Hotspur on the opening day of the season. The Red Devils also have history on their side, as they have not lost a Premier League game at Villa Park in almost exactly 20 years, winning 12 out of the 19 meetings between the two sides since then. However, uncertainty and hearsay still hang around the club like a bad smell, and once again David De Gea is scheduled to play no part tonight as the speculation surrounding the Spaniard's possible exit to Real Madrid continue to rumble on.
Tonight’s clash is the first and only Friday night Premier League game of the season and one that has been brought about purely due to exceptional circumstances. An English Defence League march in Walsall scheduled for tomorrow means that the West Midlands Police force would be unable to be present for a Saturday afternoon kick-off, when the fixture was originally planned to be played, whilst United’s Champions League qualifier against Club Brugge on Tuesday evening means that a Sunday meeting would also be unsuitable. As a result, tonight is the night, giving the fans a glimpse into the future as from next year onwards Friday evening matches will become a regular occurrence as a result of a new £5.14 billion TV deal.
