FULL TIME - Southampton 0-3 Everton: The Toffees end a run of six games without a win at Saints with a comprehensive victory on the south coast. Two counterattacking goals from Lukaku in the first half punished Koeman's men and Barkley wrapped up the three points with a sumptuous strike late on.
(90’) There is the final whistle!
(90’) Everton are letting Southampton have the ball while they sit deep now. They've been brilliant at the back all afternoon and will be confident of seeing this out with a clean sheet.
(90’) We are going to have four minutes of added time here.
--- 89’ Substitution Deulofeu enters play, replacing R. Lukaku. ---

(86’) That should wrap up the three points for Everton and they've thoroughly deserved it given their display this afternoon. Koeman looks extremely frustrated and disappointed on the touchline.
--- 84’ Assist The assist came from S. Coleman. ---
--- 84’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAL!! BARKLEY GRABS THE THIRD! The Toffees complete a fantastic afternoon on the south coast with the midfielder taking a great first touch from Coleman's pass, committing Cedric, before bending a sublime effort into the opposite corner! ---
(82’) Everton again push the ball forward on the break and Barkley fires a cross towards Cleverley on the far side of the box. (80’) Martinez also makes a substitution, introducing some fresh legs up top with Naismith taking the place of Kone.

(77’) Rodriguez is playing just in behind Pelle now, but for the time being the Toffee's back four are managing to keep them at bay. A goal soon would set up a very entetaining close to this match.
--- 75’ Yellow card J. McCarthy goes into the referee's book. ---
(75’) Mane swings a lovely cross towards Rodriguez at the back post but he is beaten to the header by Coleman. Everton's defence have been superb in this second half.
(74’) McCarthy is the latest player to go into the book after catching Pelle inside the centre circle. He took one for the team there, ensuring that Saints didn't break on an exposed defence.
--- 72’ Substitution J. Rodriguez enters play, replacing S. Long. ---
(72’) A second change of the day from Koeman now, with Rodriguez coming on for Long.
(71’) Time is running out for the hosts now. They need to get back up the other end and work some openings. That's easier said than done, though, with Everton's defence proving fairly rigid so far this afternoon.
(69’) A good spell of pressure from the Toffees! Lukaku chases a lost cause and manages to win his side a corner. The ball is sent back out to Barkley who drives in along the byline and sees his cross go behind with a touch from a Saints shirt.

(66’) Another chance for Everton on the break as Lukaku is released down the right. He holds up the play well and has Kone and Barkley breaking into the box in support. His pass goes between the pair, though, and when the England international goes to recover it he is unable to produce anything.
(64’) We get back underway with a free kick and Cedric returns to the pitch after having his head bandaged up. The set-piece is sent straight to Howard and Everton have possession once again. They are unable to get forward and relieve the pressure they have been under since the restart.
(62’) We have another break in the play now as Cedric requires attention from the medical staff. He appears to be struggling so it will be interesting to see whether he remains on the pitch or not.
(60’) Cedric floats a diagonal ball into the box which Pelle brings down on his chest while holding off Stones. He attempts to get the shot away with his second touch but is unable to make a clean connection. He claims for a penalty but is ignored by the referee.

(54’) Wanyama breaks forward from deep to provide an additional option for Mane. The Senegalese dinks a pass towards the former Celtic man but Everton's regimented defence are able to shepherd it out of play.

(48’) Long has now come out to the right with Mane moving out to the left and Davis pushing forward into a more advanced position. The Northern Ireland international tees up Romeu at the top of the box and he flicks a great pass to Pelle who has his shot blocked.
(47’) The hosts win an early corner which is sent towards the back post for Fonte. It is actually Wanyama who gets to the delivery, though, and he again puts his header off target.

Another counterattacking move saw the Belgian add his second just before the interval in what has been a positive showing from the visitors. Koeman will be looking for much improvement from his side in the second half, so be sure to stay tuned for it!
--- 45’ +4 Yellow card R. Barkley gets yellow. ---
(45’) Tadic flights it into the middle but Howard punches it clear and the half-time whistle is sounded!
(45’) There's going to be one last chance for Southampton here as Barkley dives in on Mane 20 yards from the Everton goal and earns himself a yellow card.
(45’) We are going to have a minimum of three additional minutes at the end of this half.
--- 45’ Assist R. Barkley gave the assist. ---

(44’) Koeman shakes his head in the dugout following a poor cross from Tadic that sails out of play without finding a team-mate. He will surely have some strong words for his charges at the interval.
(43’) Pelle makes a run to the near post and looks to get in front of Jagielka as he attacks Tadic's delivery from the right. He gets a stud to the ball but cannot make enough of a connection to test Howard.

He runs straight in to try and recover the ball but knocks it out for a goal kick with his tackle on the Irishman.

--- 38’ Yellow card G. Pellè gets yellow. ---
(38’) It's another yellow card for Southampton as Pelle tugs back Coleman as he looks to race away down the right. He knew what he was doing and cannot have any complaints about that.

(32’) Play gets underway with Saints sending the ball all the way up to Howard as a show of sportsmanship. Targett walks off the pitch following his treatment and quickly returns to the action.
(30’) We've got a break in play now as Targett is down and receiving reatment following a coming together with Kone.

(20’) STAT: Lukaku has scored just four goals in his last 23 Premier League appearances.

Advocaat's men remain without any points, after a 3-1 defeat at the hands of newly promoted Norwich. Watmore tries to break down the flank and whip in a cross, but the debutant can only win a corner from Whittaker.
(74’) Johnson concedes a corner for the home side, which Lens whips in again. Norwich clear with ease, before Redmond collects the loose ball and looks to engineer a break. Grabban, however, is dispossessed before he can get within shooting range. Sunderland just are not pressing enough.
(72’) Jones hits Lens, but an attempted through ball from the latter is allowed to head through to Ruddy by Bassong. The Norwich goalkeeper has still not had a save to make, even though there are only 20 minutes left on the clock in the North East.
--- 70’ Substitution D. Watmore enters the game and replaces S. Fletcher. ---
(70’) Despite Sunderland needing to at least save some of their pride with a consolation goal, it is still Norwich who are in control and on top. Play is halted, with young Watmore coming into the fray. The crowd respond, roaring on a player that they clearly identify with. Some positive energy in the air!
--- 68’ Substitution L. Grabban comes on for C. Jerome. ---
(68’) Jerome drags a shot wide, with the Englishman given too much space by Kaboul. Norwich are able to piece together moves with ease. Sunderland just aren't combative or intense enough to deny the Canaries. That will be his last contribution, however, with Grabban introduced.
(67’) Graham is desperately trying to work hard while leading the line, but a lack of follow up from his teammates making his pressing rather pointless. Dorrans lines up a shot from the edge of the penalty area, but the former West Brom man is denied by a sliding tackle from Van Aanholt.
(65’) Less than half an hour remains for the Black Cats to put together a response, but nothing is looking like changing. Sunderland are pressing or defending as a unit, with the defeat against Leicester not looking like a flash in the pan from the Foxes. Norwich have been comfortable throughout.
(63’) Sunderland are once again being allowed the ball in defence by Norwich, with Neil's men looking to be responsible at the back, given the current scoreline. Whittaker and Redmond combine down the right once again, but Kaboul comes across well to aid Van Aanholt and put the ball into touch.
--- 62’ Substitution B. Johnson enters the game and replaces W. Hoolahan. ---
(61’) Hoolahan goes on a mazy run beyond several Sunderland players, but the Irishman is robbed of possession just as he shaped to shoot with his left foot! He already has two assists to his name this afternoon and Norwich continue to look lethal on the break.
(59’) Sunderland claim for a penalty, but the referee waves away the protests from the home fans and players alike! Jones wanted a foul, after a lunging challenge from a visitor, but nothing is doing. The Stadium of Light wants a response now, but Norwich are sitting back and looking to keep things tight.
--- 57’ Assist W. Hoolahan gave the assist. ---
--- 57’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! 3-0 TO NORWICH! REDMOND! Howson almost manages to burst through and get on the end of a through ball, but Pantilimon smothers ahead of the midfielder. Norwich then win possession back deep in enemy territory, courtesy of Jerome. Redmond is picked out on the right, plays a one-two with Hoolahan and slots a finish inside the near post! ---
(56’) Sunderland are trying to be positive and take the game to the Canaries, but they are heavily reliant on Lens' quality in forward areas. The Dutchman has been the only real ray of hope for the Black Cats on a disappointing afternoon. They still have over half an hour to buck their ideas up, but Advocaat has no more offensive changes at the ready.
(55’) Jones manages to win a corner from Bassong on the right-hand side, with the former West Brom man doing brilliantly to get something out of nothing. Sunderland load the box, with Lens delivering, but Kaboul sends a diabolical header well wide of the right post.
(53’) Cattermole bypasses one player, before feeding Graham into the penalty area, but the former Swansea striker is caught just offside! Not that it mattered, as Ruddy came out and narrowed the angle well, before making a solid one-on-one save.
(51’) Dorrans plays a neat backheel into the path of the overlapping Redmond, with Sunderland's defence unable to deal with the former Birmingham wide man. Kaboul concedes a throw in, which is taken quickly and results in a cross towards the back post from Whittaker. The right-back's delivery soars above everyone and to safety.
(49’) Norwich sportingly put the ball out of play, with Fletcher struggling in the centre of the park. The former Burnley striker is clutching his shin and looks to be in considerable pain, but makes his way off the field under his own steam. It looks as though he can continue.
--- 48’ Yellow card A. Tettey goes into the referee's book. ---
(47’) Lens tries his luck from the best part of 25 yards, but the Dutchman fires his effort straight down the throat of Ruddy! Norwich immediately counter, with Coates beaten down the left, but a cross into the box evades Jerome. A frenetic start to the second period, with Tettey also picking up a card for a tackle on M'Vila.
--- 46’ Substitution D. Graham comes on for S. Larsson. ---
(46’) We are underway in the second half at the Stadium of Light! Sunderland need to improve, but it won't be tough to turn in a better performance than they did in the opening 45 minutes. Norwich, meanwhile, have a solid two-goal lead to defend.
HALF TIME! Good starts don't seem to be Sunderland's speciality, with the Black Cats struggling their way to an uninspiring 2-0 deficit at the interval. Norwich have created chances, with Martin and Whittaker contributing goals from the back line. The home fans boo their team off and they are rightfully horrified with their first-half viewing.
(45’) Norwich have plenty of man back behind the ball, but as soon as they win possession they attack! Redmond runs at pace at the Sunderland defence, but quickly miscontrols, with Coates able to punt a clearance down the line.
(45’) Pantilimon lifts a long free-kick delivery upfield, but Martin sends the ball straight back where it came from. Norwich are easing off and looking to keep things tight ahead of the break. There are three minutes of stoppage time.
(43’) Some running repairs are made on Brady, with the left-back having his hand quickly strapped up on the sideline. Sunderland look for Fletcher with a long ball upfield, but Bassong rises highest to deny his man. Big hoofs upfield from Kaboul are all that Advocaat's build-up play is really offering. Lens has been the only dangerman.
(41’) With less than five minutes until the interval, Norwich can smell blood. Neil's men are racing forward, but they have to be careful at the back. Lens is found on the left-hand side, before jinking onto his right foot and whipping a nice delivery towards the back post! Fletcher meets it, but can only place his header the wrong side of the post! Close!
(39’) Jerome fires just over! Sunderland's fans are heading for a half-time break already, with more terrible defending not aiding their side's cause! The former Stoke striker is presented with the ball around 12 yards out, but leans back too much and lifts a shot high of the target.
--- 37’ Assist W. Hoolahan gave the assist. ---
--- 37’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! GREAT GOAL FROM WHITTAKER! The right-back plays a neat one-two with Hoolahan, before using his strength to break into the penalty area! With the goal in his sights, the Scotland international blazes a powerful effort beyond Pantilimon and into the far corner! The goalkeeper will be very disappointed with that. ---
(36’) Redmond rattles the resulting free kick into the wall, with a second delivery back into the penalty area claimed with ease by the tall frame of Pantilimon. Sunderland are struggling to break out of their own half, with the Canaries pressing very well. Jerome has been a real handful.
(35’) Coates now gives away a free kick in a dangerous area, with the former Liverpool defender diving into a sliding tackle when Redmond was heading away from goal. A nonsensical decision from the Uruguayan, with Norwich now having another chance to test Pantilimon.
(34’) There are only 10 minutes until the break, but Ruddy hasn't been asked any question by the Black Cats. Norwich are allowing the home side to hold the ball in their own half, but as soon as Sunderland press upfield, they lose possession very quickly. Jerome leads a quick break, but Coates does well to rob his man of the ball just inside the box.
(32’) Whittaker tries to set Redmond away down the right flank yet again, but his lofted pass is slightly too heavy. Both sides have some pace in wide areas, but the Canaries are definitely going about using it in a better manner. Sunderland certainly don't look like the home side on the balance of the opening half an hour.
(30’) Redmond breaks down the right, before placing a wonderful delivery across the face of goal! Nobody is present at the back post to apply a finishing touch, however. Norwich are continuing to create all of the chances, with Advocaat looked on in rather unimpressed fashion from his technical area.
(28’) Norwich deserve their lead, with Sunderland being caught in possession far too regularly. The hosts try to respond immediately, with Lens shooting from the best part of 30 yards, but the Netherlands international drags his effort some way wide of the left-hand post. Ruddy hasn't been worried yet.
--- 26’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOOAL! MARTIN MAKES IT 1-0 TO NORWICH! The captain is present at the back post to tap the ball home, after a shot from range proved to be too hot for Pantilimon to handle! The short corner isn't pressed well by Sunderland, with their goalkeeper parrying Brady's shot into traffic. The opposition defender does the rest! ---
(26’) Cattermole is caught on the ball in the centre of the park, with Jerome able to start a counter. Hoolahan finds Howson on the edge of the box, before the former Leeds midfielder lets fly from 25 yards out! Pantilimon has to get down to his left-hand side very quickly to push the strike around the post!
(24’) The hosts are still on the back foot, with Advocaat's men only able to string together a maximum of six passes. Defoe does break to the edge of the penalty area, however, before attempting to poke a though ball into the path of Fletcher! The Scottish striker doesn't quite take it in his stride, with Ruddy off his line in a flash to gather the scraps.
(22’) Sunderland look to respond immediately, with a long ball down the line from Larsson attempting to find Defoe in behind. The England international battles with Whittaker, before noticing that the linesman's flag is raised for offside.
(21’) The resulting free kick is thumped into the wall, with Neil most likely going absolutely spare on the sidelines. Norwich do retain possession, however, with Brady able to curl a delivery in from on the left. Howson turns the cross towards goal with an unorthodox flick, but Pantilimon collects.
(20’) Redmond does well to win possession back high on the right-hand side! The Englishman feeds the ball to Dorrans, who attempts to whip in a cross, but Coates is on hand to concede a corner. Brady takes it, but the curse of the near-post delivery rears its head once again. Fortunately for the Canaries, Jerome manages to win a free kick from Kaboul moments later.
(18’) Good defending from Martin! Fletcher is played down the left-hand channel nicely by M'Vila, but the Scotland international's eventual cross from the byline is denied by his compatriot. Larsson whips in the resulting corner, but again the Swede is unable to beat the first man. Wasteful set pieces from the Black Cats during the opening 20 minutes.
(17’) Cattermole looks for Lens on the left-hand side, but the former Dynamo Kiev wide man somehow doesn't manage to pull the pass out of the sky. Sunderland do look to be able to do some damage with their pace down that flank, but only if the two Dutchmen can get the ball under control first.
(15’) Van Aanholt is subject to a crossfield ball from Larsson, but the former Chelsea full-back is unable to bring the pass under control. Lens then commits another poor tackle, with the Dutch winger needing to be careful after picking up an early booking. The referee has had to be quite busy thus far!
(13’) After a nervy opening few minutes, Sunderland looked to have stepped up their game, but Norwich are back on top. Brady pings a cross in from the left, which is narrowly avoided by everyone in the box, before the Irishman is allowed the chance to shoot during the next move. He can only blast high and wide of the target.
(11’) Another dead-ball situation materialises, with Norwich getting a corner on the left-hand side, but the delivery can't be turned goalwards by Jerome. Sunderland try and break immediately as a result, but Tettey tracks back and recovers brilliantly to halt the attack.
--- 9’ Yellow card J. Lens is yellow-carded. ---
(9’) Lens breaks down the left-hand side at pace, with Bassong coming across and scything down the Dutchman. The referee is straight over and brandishes a yellow card, with Larsson able to whip in the resulting free kick - but his delivery doesn't even make it over the first man. Moments later, the hosts win themselves a corner, but the aforementioned Norwich defender heads clear.
--- 7’ Yellow card S. Bassong gets yellow. ---
(7’) Brady and Hoolahan try to combine down the left-hand side, but a pass from the former runs narrowly out of play. Neil appears to be a little irritated on the sideline already, despite the Canaries being able to grab this game by the scruff of the neck immediately. Sunderland look nervous.
(5’) Coates is forced to poke away an early cross from the left by Brady, with Sunderland coming under pressure early on. The Black Cats look rushed in possession and very limited at the back. Advocaat appears to have a side set up to battle, rather than keep hold of the ball. Kaboul appears to be deliberately hiding behind his man rather than asking for a touch.
(3’) Norwich are immediately looking to get on the front foot and dominate the ball, but Dorrans is penalised for a tug on Lens' shirt. Kaboul rattles a terrible clearance into Hoolahan, before the Frenchman shows his nerves again to try and hoof the ball down the line. Not a composed start, by any stretch.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Stadium of Light! The home side are donning their usual red and white stripes, with Norwich also turning out in their home kit. The visitors got into a huddle before kick off, let's see if that togetherness comes out in how they play!
Both teams are out on the field of play and we are only a few minutes from the action at the Stadium of Light! The conditions are perfect, with neither side having any excuses to not be able to move the ball around on this pitch.
Norwich substitutes: Hooper, Bennett, Wisdom, Grabban, Johnson, O'Neil, Rudd.
Norwich starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Ruddy; Whittaker, Martin, Bassong, Brady; Tettey, Dorrans; Howson, Hoolahan, Redmond; Jerome.
Sunderland substitutes: Graham, O'Shea, Mannone, Bridcutt, Watmore, Matthews, Rodwell.
Sunderland starting line-up (4-4-2): Pantilimon; Jones, Coates, Kaboul, Van Aanholt; Larsson, Cattermole, M'Vila, Lens; Defoe, Fletcher.
TEAM NEWS: Nathan Redmond and Cameron Jerome come into the side, with Bradley Johnson and Lewis Grabban dropping out. Wes Hoolahan will look to play in the hole behind the lone striker, with Redmond and Jonny Howson playing out wide. The back four is unchanged, with Norwich having a rather rare all-English substitutes bench. Neil has reacted to his side's improvement as the game progressed against Palace, that much is evident.
TEAM NEWS: Summer signing Yann M'Vila is set to make his debut for the hosts, with the Frenchman slotting into central midfield alongside Lee Cattermole. Seb Larsson and Jeremain Lens are occupying the wings, with a forward two of Jermain Defoe and Steven Fletcher. Despite conceding four goals last time out, Advocaat opts to keep the exact same back four as the one which faced the Foxes. Danny Graham is the Black Cats only real offensive option on the bench.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action from the North East, as both of these teams look to pick up their first points of the campaign. There are a few new signings dotted around in both team selections, with Dick Advocaat definitely needing to inspire a better start from his personnel than the one they offered last week. The nightmare against Leicester saw the Black Cats go 3-0 down inside 26 minutes, something that their fans won't want to see again.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League's second matchday, with newly promoted Norwich City heading up north to face Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. The hosts fell to a 4-2 defeat in their opening fixture, with the Black Cats needing to try and steady the ship before they come under further scrutiny. The Canaries, meanwhile, have chopped and changed their starting 11, given that Cameron Jerome and Nathan Redmond helped Alex Neil's side improve and score after racking up a two-goal deficit against Crystal Palace.

I am Alex Moretto and I would like to thank you all for joining me here today. Good bye!
FULL TIME: SWANSEA 2-0 NEWCASTLE. Gomis gave the hosts the lead inside 10 minutes and they never looked back. Janmaat's sending off made for a comfortable second half for the Swans who doubled their lead through Andre Ayew - the Ghanaian's second goal in as many Premier League games.
(90’) These fans are soaking up every second left, cheering on their side who have started the season brilliantly. Four points from two games against Chelsea and Newcastle will have to please Monk, who sees his side take on struggling Sunderland in a week's time. Newcastle remain on the road for a date with Manchester United.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on at the end of this match, though it's little more than a formality at this point.
(88’) Swansea are back in possession, largely keeping the ball in their own end amongst the defence. A testing ball from Williams starts them forward, however, catching Newcastle sleeping and it allows Routledge to have a go at goal, but his effort deflects behind for a corner.
--- 86’ Substitution G. Sigurðsson is replaced with L. Britton. ---
(86’) STAT ATTACK: Steve McClaren’s Derby County scored 37 goals away from home in the Championship last season, more than all but three clubs over the course of the campaign – Bournemouth, Watford and Norwich City.
--- 84’ Yellow card A. Mitrović receives a yellow card. ---
(84’) And Mitrovic promptly picks up a yellow card just a minute after coming on - exactly the same story as last week. He's clattered into by a late challenge from Neil Taylor. The striker doesn't take kindly to it, getting right up and in his face before shoving him away. He certainly isn't a stranger to confrontation.
(83’) Mitrovic is introduced, too little too late by McClaren, but he has an immediate impact showing great determination to win his first aerial duel, just seconds after coming on. They've been lacking that determination throughout. Obertan is the man replaced.
--- 82’ Substitution G. Obertan is done for the day. A. Mitrović is his replacement. ---
(81’) Lovely first-touch pass from Gomis to roll the ball into the path of Dyer inside the area, but the substitute tries to play a cross back in. He scuffs his contact horribly and taps the ball feebly behind for a goal kick.
(79’) The body language of these Newcastle players is eerily similar to what it was down the stretch last season. They have to adopt a greater resiliency to their game, because this just doesn't cut it. Regardless of the scoreline, they have to show some fighting spirit and battle through to the final whistle.
--- 77’ Substitution Montero is the second Swans player to bring the fans to their feet as he makes his way off. He departs without scoring, but he's been their top attacker on the afternoon. Wayne Routledge is set to replace him. ---
(75’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle used just one English player against Southampton, Jack Colback – the same team they used this afternoon. That's fewer than any other team in the Premier League over opening weekend.
(73’) The result has settled in it would seem now. Swansea are well on their way to three points, while Newcastle will have to wait another week for their first victory under Steve McClaren.
--- 72’ Substitution N. Dyer enters the game and replaces A. Ayew. ---
(71’) There's a rowdy applause throughout the Liberty Stadium, with the fans jumping to their feet to applaud Ayew as he makes his way off the pitch. Nathan Dyer comes on, and his pace will have to worry these tiring Newcastle defenders.
(69’) Newcastle play themselves into trouble deep in their own end with some nonchalant passing. Taylor eventually gives it away and Swansea settle into attack yet again, patiently working the ball around in the final third, probing for an opening.
(67’) Mbemba has played right-back before, but not against the same quality in the Belgian league as Montero. The winger continues to prove a menace on the flank, negating the defender's physical style with blinding pace.
(65’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea have never lost consecutive home matches in the league under Garry Monk – they lost their last of the 2014/15 campaign against Manchester City.
(63’) If he were an inch taller! Ayew again does brilliantly to escape his marker and get on the end of another cross from Montero, but he just can't get enough on his header to direct it past Krul at the far stick.
--- 61’ Yellow card Naughton commits late to a slide, taking out Haidara in the process. Mike Jones comes over to have a word, and just when it looked like the defender would escape a booking, out comes the yellow card. ---
(60’) Newcastle look dejected as Swansea continue to dominate possession and dictate the tempo. Wijnaldum has had a thankless task in the middle of the pitch, tasked with dropping deep to defend and feeding the ball forward for the likes of Obertan and Aarons - who are doing little to make themselves available.
(58’) Important block there as Cork lines up a strike from 25-yards out after a well-worked move to gift him the ball in space. It was Coloccini who got the block in, but play has come to a halt as Haidara has gone down after a coming together with Gomis.
(56’) This Swansea side is so sound top to bottom. Garry Monk has them buying into the system and it's working wonders. They play such an attractive brand of football going forward, while remaining compact and organized off the ball.
--- 54’ Substitution Newcastle make their second change, but it's not the impending arrival of Mitrovic like fans would have hoped. Instead teenager Rolando Aarons has come on to replace Cisse, who doesn't look very disappointed to see his afternoon come to an end. ---
--- 52’ Assist J. Montero provided the assist. ---
--- 52’ Goal! WHAT A START TO HIS BPL CAMPAIGN! A second goal in as many Premier League matches for Andre Ayew as he makes a great run towards the near post to get on the end of Montero's cross and direct a brilliant header into the far corner. Spectacular stuff from the Ghanaian! ---
(51’) STAT ATTACK: Gylfi Sigurdsson registered a goal and three assists in two matches against Newcastle last season, his first in Wales.
--- 49’ Yellow card Ayew picks up a yellow card for a challenge right beside the corner flag on Haidara. Wijnaldum whips a very inviting ball in from the ensuing set piece, but again Fabianski is first to claim it amidst the mess of bodies. ---
(48’) Tremendous hit! Sigurdsson lines up a strike and lets fly from range, smacking the underside of the bar. It bounces off the line before Krul collects. Mike Jones looks straight at his wrist but the goal-line technology says it stayed out!
(47’) The sending off of Janmaat forces McClaren's hand, as their most creative player has now been forced off. Taylor will slot in at centre-half with what looks like Mbemba shifting over to the vacant spot on the right.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Taylor enters the game and replaces M. Sissoko. ---
(46’) Underway in the second half. Sissoko, who picked up a knock in the first half, is off with Steven Taylor taking his place.
HALF TIME: SWANSEA 1-0 NEWCASTLE. The hosts started wonderfully and were rewarded through Gomis. The Tyneside club started to grow into the game and just when it looked as though we were poised for an exciting second half, Janmaat gets himself sent off. It's an uphill battle now for Newcastle, a goal and a man down after 45 minutes.
(45’) Speculative effort! Newcastle win a free kick a bit off to the left, about 30-yards out from goal. They pack the penalty area with bodies, but Wijnaldum goes for goal himself and his ambitious strike sails over the bar.
(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
(44’) HOW UNLUCKY?! Montero practically jogs past two defenders who get nowhere near him, en route to the top of the area. The attacker drives a low strike in and has Krul beaten, but it rattles off the woodwork!
(43’) Just as Newcastle were growing into the game, including Janmaat, the right-back goes and kicks his team's legs out from under them. What a massive blow that is, as Swansea are given another boost before the break.
--- 41’ Red card! Janmaat is off! What a dreadful decision from the defender! Already on a yellow card, he gives the ball away in attack and inexcusably pulls back the shirt of Montero, 70-yards from his own goal, which will end his afternoon! ---
(40’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea picked up just a point against Newcastle in their Premier League debut season in 2011/12, but have since gone unbeaten against the Toons (W5, D1).
(38’) Newcastle would love themselves a goal before the break, but they can take solace in the fact that they've really taken over in the last 15 minutes or so. They're transitioning so well into attack and it's now Janmaat who finds himself escaping the marking of Montero.
(36’) Wonderful defending! More good play from Newcastle and Sissoko is again at the heart of it. He picks out a nifty pass for Obertan, who plays a low ball in for Cisse, but Fernandez tracks the run and gets a block in. He's clattered into on the follow-up and the medical staff will have to come out to attend to him.
(34’) Fantastic ball movement from the visitors, imitating Swansea with a series of one-touch passes to break their way into the final third. Janmaat's final delivery was always going to be tough considering the height of the ball played across to him. He does well to volley a cross into the centre, but Fabianski is able to sniff it out.
(32’) BRILLIANT DRIBBLING! Absolutely splendid work from Montero down the left flank, driving at Janmaat with pace and skipping past him wonderfully at the byline all while eluding a challenge and keeping the ball in play. He could have gone down and won a free kick, but instead carries on, though can't pick out a teammate with his cutback pass.
(30’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have lost six consecutive Premier League matches away from home, scoring just a single goal over that span.
(28’) One of the big differences for Swansea has been that of Shelvey. He was superb early on, proving the catalyst in midfield. Since assisting the opener, however, he's been careless in possession, unable to push forward and ask any questions of the Newcastle defence.
(26’) You can feel the tide starting to shift ever so slightly. Swansea aren't playing with the same sense of urgency they adopted in the opening 15 minutes, and it's allowed Newcastle to have a bit of a breather and start to grow in confidence.
(24’) The delivery is encouraging but it's not attacked with any conviction by Newcastle allowing Fabianski to collect with relative ease.
(23’) Bit of a senseless challenge from Shelvey as he fouls Colback, whose back was turned to goal, near the corner flag, awarding Newcastle a good opportunity from the ensuing free kick.
(21’) Swansea fans up in arms as Mbemba commits another hard challenge, this time on Montero. They clamor for a foul, but nothing is given by referee Mike Jones and rightfully so. The DR Congo centre-half plays with plenty of physicality and it's been on display through these opening 20 minutes.
(19’) Newcastle have started to get into a bit of rhythm, no longer being contained in their own half. Possession is starting to even out a bit, though it's still Swansea who hold the sizable advantage overall. Colback and Anita haven't had the same impact thus far than they did against Southampton.
--- 17’ Yellow card Janmaat goes into the referee's book for his second hard foul on Montero, clashing into the back of the winger. It appears something of a warning sign from the Dutchman, who has been marking him like white on rice. ---
(16’) Much better from the Magpies! Papiss Cisse plays a lovely ball out wide for Gabriel Obertan. The winger picks up a full head of steam before cutting his way into the centre and driving a shot in at the near post which Lukasz Fabianski is forced to knock behind for a corner.
(15’) This is a clinic being put on by Swansea, with Newcastle unable to break out of their own half or win back possession. Their work rate needs to improve in the midfield third - they aren't closing down gaps nearly quick enough.
(13’) STAT ATTACK: Bafetimbi Gomis has scored six goals in his last seven Premier League matches for Swansea City, having registered just two in his first 25 league games with the club.
(11’) There was absolutely no stopping that move from Swansea. Gomis timed his run well, just kept onside by Janmaat across the pitch and Shelvey did so well to pick out that peach of a pass. It's nothing less than they deserve after such a positive start to this match - and season, if you will.
--- 9’ Assist J. Shelvey provided the assist. ---
--- 9’ Goal! DREAM START FOR SWANSEA! Bafetimbi Gomis is on target once again! Shelvey is the architect, carving out space in midfield before picking out a absolutely brilliant pass to play the striker through. He rounds the keeper and slots home his second goal of the season! ---
(7’) You can see the emphasis Steve McClaren has put on slowing Montero. The winger ripped through the very capable Branislav Ivanovic on opening weekend, but Newcastle have come out today looking to take any and all space away from the tricky winger. Janmaat is marking him closely, which should be an intriguing battle to keep an eye on throughout.
(5’) Great defending at both ends. Newcastle look to get forward on a quick counter and commit bodies forward in numbers. Mossa Sissoko has options to his left, but Ashley Williams lunges in with a committed tackle to sniff out the attack and start Swansea on the break. Jefferson Montero finds himself in a similar position, but Chancel Mbemba this time replicates the defending of his counterpart.
(3’) Fantastic start for Swansea! They keep Newcastle pinned in their own end and launch a few efforts toward goal, though they can't find a way through. Pressure stays on and Jonjo Shelvey shows a lovely bit of skill to escape his marker and drive a strike on target, but it's straight at Tim Krul.
(1’) And we're off! Swansea in their all-white home strip, with Newcastle supporting their snazzy new dark blue away kits, with a subtle pink and white stripe across the front.
The Liberty Stadium is ROCKING as they welcome their home team back after holding the defending champions to a draw a week ago. Swansea are home, and they'll feel the same way in the Premier League, though Newcastle do what they can to spoil the party.
Vurnon Anita gets the start once again, despite being stretchered off with a back injury last weekend. As a result, Steve McClaren has made no changes to his starting lineup. Remy Cabella and Paul Dummett have returned to training, though neither are ready for first-team action. Meanwhile, Siem de Jong has been left off the 18-man squad.
Garry Monk has been forced into making an swap in midfield with Ki Sung-Yeung absent after suffering a hamstring injury against Chelsea. He's replaced in midfield by Jack Cork, the lone change for the Swans. Bafetimbi Gomis continues to hold down the fort in attack, flanked by the enigmatic Jefferson Montero and Andre Ayew, with Gylfi Sigurdsson pulling the strings as the number 10.

The Swansea manager said he wanted to set a standard of performance against the Blues for his side to live up to the rest of the season – and boy did they ever. Stoke not only picked up their first point today but also their first goals of the new campaign and their fightback today will give them huge confidence going into their next match against Norwich City, who also won today against Sunderland.
And Spurs will need to lick their wounds quickly as next up for them is a trip to high-flying Leicester City, who have today beaten West Ham United 2-1 away from home to make it back-to-back victories for Claudio Ranieri's side.
Diouf had several opportunities in either half before coming up with the last-gasp equaliser, but a crucial turning point in the game - besides Ireland's introduction - was the penalty. Stoke were huffing and puffing but it was Alderweireld's rash decision inside the box which led to the fightback from the visitors.
Spurs headed into the interval with a two-goal lead thanks to Dier and Chadli, with Stoke producing one of their worst displays on the road in a long, long time. However, Hughes made a couple of inspired changes in the second half which worked a treat and handed them a deserved point on the balance of play.
Boos ring around White Hart Lane as Tottenham throw away a two-goal lead to draw 2-2 with Stoke City. The Potters were excellent as soon as Stephen Ireland came off the bench just before the hour mark.

Chadli finds the back of the net via a Pieters deflection right at the end of the first half to put Spurs 2-0 to the good against Stoke. What an end to an incredibly exciting game! West Ham’s visitors are also under new management, with Claudio Ranieri kick-starting his tenure in charge of Leicester with a great win in front of a packed home crowd. The victory means that last season’s 14th-place finishers have now won seven of their last 10 Premier League games, an absolutely fantastic run that shows just how impressive they can be when they’re in form. The Foxes have struggled when playing in London, however, and are now without a win in their last 20 Premier League games in the capital. Only three of those have ended in draws, the last of which came back in May 2004.
This afternoon’s game brings together two sides that enjoyed brilliant starts to the new season, with both bagging themselves excellent opening-day victories. West Ham stunned everybody with a 2-0 win against Arsenal at the Emirates, whilst Leicester thrashed Sunderland 4-2 in an action-packed encounter at the King Power Stadium. The Hammers will be looking to continue their good form and pick up three more points this afternoon in a game that is not only their first home clash of the campaign but also one that marks Slaven Bilic’s return to Upton Park 18 years after leaving East London for Everton.

FULL TIME - Palace 1-2 Arsenal: The Gunners pick up their first win of the new Premier League campaign, getting their season up and running. Giroud opened the scoring with an acrobatic finish before Ward pegged the Gunners back with another impressive strike. The visitors pushed on after the interval and secured the three points after Delaney put through his own goal.

Puncheon's delivery flies into a swarm of players and Cech comes off his line but doesn't reach it. Mutch somehow gets his head to the ball but can only help it over the top.

Of all this season’s title contenders, City certainly looked the most impressive on the opening day of the campaign. Their 3-0 win against West Brom showed just how up for the fight they are ahead of a season in which they are almost guaranteed to be constantly fighting alongside current holders Chelsea. Yaya Toure was excellent last weekend and is sure to play another vital role in today’s clash, whilst Sergio Aguero’s return to the starting line-up will no doubt galvanise an already extremely confident team.
Whilst Chelsea played some lovely football at times against Swansea, on the whole they looked off the pace and far from the dominating and exciting championship-winning side that we became used to last season. However, it would be foolish to read too much into one disappointing game, particularly so early in the campaign, and today’s clash gives them a good opportunity to prove themselves against an opponent that will more than likely be battling with them at the top of the table come May.
After a convincing opening-day performance at the Hawthorns that saw them come away with a comfortable 3-0 victory against West Bromwich Albion, City return home to take on a Chelsea side that not only struggled at times in last weekend’s game against Swansea City - resulting in a 2-2 draw for the reigning champions - but also find themselves with off-field problems to contend with so early in the season. The build-up to today’s clash has been almost entirely dominated by Jose Mourinho’s row with medical staff members Eva Carneiro and Jon Fearn in the wake of last Saturday’s draw, and it will be interesting to see if the negativity surrounding the club will have any affect on the pitch this afternoon.

(86’) TOP OF THE NET! The corner is swung in from the right-hand side and meets the head of Tomlin, but the ball is always rising and goes over the bar.
(84’) Bournemouth are pushing to try and level the game. They are throwing everything at Liverpool in these final few minutes, but to no avail as of yet.
(82’) Liverpool have just made their final change of the night with Coutinho going off to a wonderful reception from the Kop. Alberto Moreno comes on in his place.
--- 81’ Substitution Alberto Moreno comes on for Philippe Coutinho. ---
--- 81’ Substitution A. Smith enters play, replacing M. Gradel. ---
(80’) Cook meets a corner with a glancing header but cannot direct it towards goal. Bournemouth have 10 minutes to find an equaliser or they will be leaving empty-handed.
(78’) Tomlin receives the fourth yellow card of the night after bringing down Lallana. Interestingly, Mr. Pawson dished out six in his first appointment of the season in Newcastle's 2-2 draw with Southampton.
--- 77’ Yellow card L. Tomlin receives a yellow card. ---
--- 76’ Yellow card M. Ritchie is yellow-carded. ---
(76’) We're into the final quarter of an hour and Bournemouth are not out of this yet by any means. They do need to threaten a lot more going forward and get the ball to the likes of Ritchie and Wilson.
--- 75’ Yellow card J. Gomez goes into the referee's book. ---
(74’) STUNNING BLOCK BY DANIELS! A mistake in the Bournemouth midfield allows Benteke to race away before squaring the ball to Coutinho, whose volley is quickly charged down by the left-back.
(72’) GREAT BLOCK BY SURMAN! Milner's cross for Benteke is only half-cleared by Bournemouth and Coutinho shapes up for the volley, but Surman is quickly out to stop him getting a shot on goal.
--- 70’ Substitution J. Ibe is done for the day. Roberto Firmino is his replacement. ---
(70’) With 20 minutes to go, the noise levels raise at Anfield as Roberto Firmino is introduced for his debut. Jordan Ibe is the man to make way for the Brazilian.
(69’) Fortunately for Bournemouth, Coutinho hits it straight into the wall. They would have been cursing their luck had anymore been made of that free kick.
(67’) INTERESTING DECISION! Daniels smashes the ball straight against his team mate who has his arms by his side, but the referee penalises the visitors and awards Liverpool a free kick right on the edge of the area.
(65’) You cannot fault Bournemouth's effort again tonight. The question is whether they can turn it into points. Granted they are up against superior opposition, but they don't want to be playing catch-up too early on in the season.
(63’) SIDE NETTING FROM O'KANE! Some nice football around the edge of the area sees Wilson find O'Kane who is forced wide but gets his shot away, only to see it go the wrong side of the post.
(62’) The Bournemouth winger had more assists than anybody during his side's promotion season. It is always going to be tough to repeat at the higher level, but moments like that suggest that he can be just as dangerous a threat in the top flight.
--- 61’ Substitution J. King is done for the day. L. Tomlin is his replacement. ---
(60’) WHAT AN EFFORT BY RITCHIE! The ball breaks kindly for the winger and his sizzling first-time strike crashes against the post with Mignolet beaten.
(58’) Things have quietened down slightly as we approach the hour mark. Neither side are looking particularly adventurous going forward but are keeping possession nicely.
(56’) Milner has the chance to establish himself in the first team with Liverpool after being named their vice-captain. Chances never fell too freely for him at Manchester City, although he was arguably one of their better performers during their disappointing 2014/15 campaign.
(54’) Benteke wins the ball back from Elphick and lays it off for Ibe, who takes on a couple of players before his cross is dragged just wide of the target by Milner.
--- 52’ Substitution J. Henderson is replaced with E. Can. ---
(52’) Liverpool are being forced into an early change in this second half and Henderson is the man to come off. He looked over to the bench a couple of minutes ago and is replaced by Emre Can.
(51’) Milner finds Coutinho in space to drive forward at the Bournemouth defence. The Brazilian's shot takes a deflection and skids just wide of the far post.
(49’) RITCHIE TRIES AGAIN! He receives the ball on the right from Wilson and cuts inside a challenge, but he gets too much on his shot and sends it way over the bar.
(47’) GOOD STRIKE FROM RITCHIE! The Bournemouth winger works the ball onto his left foot and puts his foot right through it. It is right down Mignolet's throat but he has to show good hands to hold.
(46’) KICK OFF! Bournemouth get the second half rolling.
The teams are back out after the break and the second half is imminent.
Bournemouth can be pleased with the way they started the game, but allowed Liverpool to get on top too easily. This will be a big team talk from Howe.
Liverpool recovered from a slow start and eventually made their superiority tell as the half wore on. Benteke's first goal for the club will settle him down.
HALF TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-0 BOURNEMOUTH
(45’) Mr. Pawson blows his whistle for half time!
(45’) ONE MINUTE! The fourth official holds up his board to indicate that there will be a single minute of additional time at the end of this first half.
(44’) CHANCE FOR COUTINHO! Some neat play around the edge of the area sees a Bournemouth intervention put the ball on a plate for him, but he cannot find the target as his shot passes the far post.
(43’) What a waste from Gradel! Bournemouth have a great opportunity to get players forward and attack Liverpool, but he plays his pass behind his team mate and Gomez clears.
(41’) Bournemouth could do with the half-time whistle now in all fairness. Howe needs to get their minds back on the gameplan and start playing their own game again.
(39’) That was very good sportsmanship from Henderson. Too often nowadays, you see players going down looking for penalties with the slightest touch. He was clearly not trying to con the referee on this occasion, though.
(37’) PENALTY?! Henderson goes down under a challenge from Gradel in the area, but is quickly back to his feet and looks to pick out a cross which is well cleared. It would have been harsh in all fairness.
(35’) Liverpool are very much in control now. They haven't necessarily threatened as much in the last couple of minutes, but Bournemouth are struggling to get the ball back.
--- 34’ Yellow card E. O'Kane is yellow-carded. ---
(33’) If the visitors are to to find an equaliser, they will have to do it against Mignolet who has kept more clean sheets than any other Premier League keeper in 2015 with 10.
(31’) It will be interesting to see how Bournemouth respond to going behind. They cannot afford to let their heads drop, they have done well so far but need to keep things tighter at the back.
(29’) OFF THE BAR! A free kick is taken short to Henderson, who tries his luck first time with a looping 35-yard effort that grazes the top of the crossbar.
(28’) That was a marvellous cross from Henderson. There were suspicions of offside in the Bournemouth defence, but they were too slow reacting and Benteke punished them.
--- 26’ Assist J. Henderson provided the assist. ---
--- 26’ Goal! LIVERPOOL TAKE THE LEAD AND BENTEKE GETS HIS FIRST GOAL IN A LIVERPOOL SHIRT!!! Henderson delivers a cross after his corner is cleared, Coutinho misses it but Benteke arrives at the far post to steer home. That's his 50th goal in English football. ---
(24’) Space opens up for Benteke as the ball breaks into his stride. His effort isn't the greatest, though, and it swerves away from goal not troubling Boruc.
(22’) Bournemouth press forward and the ball almost falls kindly for King on the corner of the six-yard area, but he is under pressure from the Liverpool defence and it bounces behind for a goal kick.
(21’) The stage is set for the little Brazilian to become Liverpool's talisman following the departure of Steven Gerrard. He will be hoping his stunning strike against Stoke was a sign of things to come this season.
(19’) Coutinho picks out Ibe with an inch-perfect diagonal pass from the centre of the pitch, but the winger cannot get the ball under control and it goes out for a goal kick.
(17’) Benteke comes to life as he looks to latch onto a lofted ball over the top of the Bournemouth defence, but it is just too far ahead of him and he cannot stretch enough to control.
(15’) Bournemouth's last two visits to Anfield have resulted in 4-1 defeats. On the balance of play so far, they should avoid that happening for a third straight meeting.
(13’) There is pressure on Liverpool to perform this season. Fans will have been disappointed with their sixth-placed finish a year after finishing second, and they will have high expectations for the campaign.
(11’) Just looking at the disallowed goal again, Bournemouth have been pretty hard done by. Elphick did have his hands on Lovren, but you see that sort of thing go unpunished every week in the Premier League.
(9’) So far so good as far as Howe will be concerned. His side do not look intimidated by the hosts and have taken the game to them if anything. More of the same needed for the Cherries.
(7’) Francis delivers a dangerous ball into the box looking for King and Skrtel has to make a very important header to clear at the expense of a corner.
(5’) BOURNEMOUTH SCORE! But it won't count... Elphich rises in the area to head a corner beyond Mignolet. His joy is short-lived, though, as he is penalised for pushing Lovren.
(4’) GOOD TRY FROM IBE! Henderson's corner is cushioned to the youngster by Skrtel, but he cuts across the shot and sends it high and wide of the target.
(3’) The Bournemouth supporters raise the roof at Anfield as they are awarded a corner. It comes to nothing, though, and Liverpool are able to clear.
(1’) KICK OFF! Liverpool get us underway kicking towards the Kop end.
Anfield is rocking as the teams are out and kick off is just moments away! Craig Pawson is the referee. Both sides have won their last two matches that he has officiated - one of those records will go tonight.

Full time at Old Trafford. Manchester United start as they mean to go on in the Barclays Premier League with an opening win over Tottenham in the first fixture of the season. One-nil is the scoreline on the day in what was a tense, tight affair from start to finish. The only goal of the match came in the first period as Kyle Walker put the ball into his own net whilst attempting to stop Wayne Rooney from getting a shot away. Neither team particularly convincing, but still time for some tinkering before the end of the transfer window. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card D. Alli is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Four minutes of added time have been signalled by the referee which is met with musings of disdain from the Old Trafford faithful. Tottenham should be buoyed by the extra time given to find an equaliser, so we should be in for an interesting finish.
--- 90’ Yellow card Mata gets yellow. ---
(89’) ANOTHER STOP FROM ROMERO!!! Spurs are really knocking at the door here and keep the ball in and around the opposition penalty area. Eriksen eventually latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box and whips a lovely strike aimed at the bottom corner, but again the newly recruited goalkeeper makes the save!
(87’) SAVE FROM ROMERO! A dangerous ball is floated into the area and cannons off the head of Smalling before squeezing towards the bottom corner, but the Argentina international gets across goal to beat the clearance away!
(85’) United have Spurs just where they want them at the moment in terms of position on the pitch as Pochettino's men are pinned back at the top left corner flag with the hosts keeping the ball through little triangles. The equaliser won't come unless the visitors can penetrate their way out of there.
(83’) Fantastic defending from Smalling here as Chadli gets into a brilliant position inside the United box. The Belgian hits the byline and attempts to dance his way back into the danger area, but is foiled by the tall defender, who wonderfully times his tackle to win possession. Any miscue there and that was a penalty.
--- 81’ Substitution A. Valencia enters the game and replaces M. Darmian. ---
(81’) Last substitution of the match now as Van Gaal introduces Antonio Valencia in place of the newly recruited Darmian. The Italian seems to have nailed down the right-back position in the Italy national team and has been very impressive in his debut today, so it looks like United have found the solution to their right-back problems.
(79’) Spurs are just enjoying a nice little period of possession in the final third at the moment as they pin United back into their own defensive area. The home side are looking solid despite the pressure though so it might take something special, or a mistake, to break them down.
--- 77’ Substitution E. Dier is replaced with D. Alli. ---
(77’) Third and final change from Tottenham now and it is a clever one from Pochettino as he withdraws the recently booked Dier, who is looking more and more frustrated, for 19-year-old Dele Alli, who signed for the North London club from MK Dons last campaign.
--- 76’ Yellow card E. Dier is cautioned by the referee. ---
(75’) Young picks up possession whilst hugging the touchline and then ignores the overlapping run of Ander before cutting inside and looking to exchange a pacey one-two with Rooney, but not before being taken out by the challenge of Dier, who earns a yellow card for his trouble. Rooney takes the resulting free kick, but it is an awful attempt.
(73’) Schweinsteiger collects possession 25 yards out and is prompted to shoot by plenty of cheers from the home crowd, but ever intelligent on the ball, the World Cup winner reverts back and then neatly passes inside to Mata. Nothing comes of the eventual attack, though, and Spurs clear.
(71’) Spurs just haven't managed to muster up any kind of ascendancy or tempo to this game in the second period and are looking pretty much out of ideas in the final third. Definite signs of fatigue there for all to see as their pressing and passing is sluggish.
(70’) Another substitution from Pochettino now as Dembele makes way for Erik Lamela, who is another player who will be looking to make a much bigger impact on the league this season.
--- 69’ Yellow card B. Schweinsteiger gets yellow. ---
(69’) Schweinsteiger quickly makes his mark in the Barclays Premier League by committing a rather cynical foul on Chadli inside the centre circle, earning his first yellow card for his new club in the process.
--- 68’ Substitution M. Dembélé is replaced with E. Lamela. ---
--- 68’ Substitution Ander Herrera enters the game and replaces M. Depay. ---
(67’) Another change coming from Man Utd now and it is summer signing, Memphis Depay, who is coming off and he'll be replaced by Ander Herrera, who was in fantastic form at the end of the last campaign. With all the new transfers coming in, the young Spaniard certainly has a point to prove.
(65’) Schweinsteiger has already made a positive impact on the match through his sheer class when in possession in those central areas. There hasn't been anything glitzy about his cameo so far, but the patience and calm nature on the ball is already evident on this Old Trafford pitch.
(63’) We have just past the hour mark in the match now and we have seen a distinct lack of goalscoring chances throughout, even with that own goal from Walker, which can barely be considered as a real opportunity. Both keepers haven't had much to do, but still time for more goals to flow in.
(61’) First change of the match from Van Gaal now and it is a popular one among the United faithful as Schweinstsiger comes on to make his debut in the middle of midfield, replacing Michael Carrick in the process. Over the course of the season, we may see that duo swap places in the XI quite often.
--- 60’ Substitution B. Schweinsteiger enters the game and replaces M. Carrick. ---
(59’) In a much similar incident to the one previously, Vertonghen comes through the back of Rooney with a high foot, only this time the connection is a lot more serious as the United captain is caught on the back of a head with a knee. Strangely, no free kick this time though.
(57’) Spurs are awarded a free kick in a decent position down the right wing as Blind goes in with a high foot on Eriksen. The Denmark international dusts himself off to take the set-piece and floats it into the danger area, but Romero comes off his line confidently to claim. Wasted opportunity there.
(55’) Young and Walker, who have had an extremely entertaining duel down the flank up until now, get involved in a mini scuffle near the touchline which results in a free kick to Spurs, much to the chagrin of the former Aston Villa winger.
--- 53’ Substitution R. Mason comes on for N. Bentaleb. ---
(53’) First change of the match now and it comes from Pochettino as he introduces Ryan Mason in place of the disappointing Bentaleb, whose work on the ball in the middle of the park hasn't been great this afternoon. Some more energy provided in there for Spurs now.
(51’) Walker gets himself into a great position inside the United box and Shaw shies away from making the challenge in such an area, which allows the full-back to find Chadli. The Belgian then looks for Kane near the penalty spot, but Darmian covers his central defenders well to make the clearance.
(49’) Blind gives the ball away poorly in a very dangerous position at the back and Kane collects before assessing his options 25 yards out. He attempts to lay the ball into the feet of Chadli inside the area but the Dutchman recovers fairly well to make the important interception.
(47’) So far, although very early, the second period has followed much the same formula as the opening 45 minutes. Spurs are enjoying a relatively decent amount of possession at the back but are finding themselves under massive pressure from the United attackers.
(46’) We are back under way at Old Trafford!
Half time at Old Trafford. It has been a relatively tight game so far between Manchester United and Tottenham as Van Gaal's men enter the break with a narrow 1-0 lead. The vital moment of the match so far came midway through the half when Kyle Walker netted an own goal whilst trying to dispossess Wayne Rooney inside the box. Spurs looked encouraging in the early stages, but looked fatigued as the game went on. Interesting second period in store!
(45’) Indeed, just one minute of injury time has been signalled and we are coming up to half-time. Eriksen stands over a free kick on the right wing and swings to dangerously to the back post, which allows Alderweireld to whip a strike towards the top bag, but Romero is on hand to make the stop.
(43’) Shouldn't be too many added minutes allocated by the referee here as we have more or less had a free-flowing game. Spurs will be grateful of the rest but will be hoping they can create one clear-cut chance on goal before the break.
(41’) Spurs are just cleverly curbing the ascendancy of Van Gaal's men here as they take the tempo out of the game with some patient passing in defence. Considering their shaky nature on the ball up until now, it may not be the best policy, but they are certainly in need of a little respite.
(39’) Memphis latches on to a mistake from Alderweireld and then moves forward with pace before smashing a strike at goal. The Belgian recovers to make the important block on the edge of the area but Darmian picks up possession again as United continue to press forward and attack.
(37’) Mata ignores the overlap from Darmian and typically glides inside once again before flashing a pass into the feet of Schneiderlin. The Frenchman attempts to clip a first-time pass over the Tottenham defence but there is just too much on it and Vorm comes off his line to make the catch. Slick stuff from United.
(35’) Mataaaa! Unlucky! The Spaniard picks up the ball in the inside right channel and drifts inside before lashing a strike at goal, which is blocked. He collects the rebound 12 yards out and then squeezes out an awkward volley towards the bottom corner, but Vorm sees it comfortably wide.
(33’) Walker does well to collect a slightly dodgy clearance from Vorm and then moves down the wing with authority before pinging a lovely ball over the top of the United defence for Kane, but Romero proactively comes off his line to snatch it out of the air before the Englishman can get a shot away.
(31’) Man United are going for the jugular here as Tottenham can barely get out of their defensive third at the moment. There are just too many poor clearances and a lack of composure at the back from Pochettino's men, but up until now the home side have only managed to create one real goalscoring chance, which they netted from, so cause for slight encouragement.
(29’) I did mention previously that Spurs were looking pretty lively even with their midweek friendly exploits, but as this match goes on it is pretty likely that two 90 minute matches only a few days ago will catch up on them. Remains to be seen whether this will be the case, but United will be ready to pounce if they see any signs of fatigue.
--- 27’ Yellow card J. Vertonghen receives a yellow card. ---
(27’) Mata steps up and whips the free kick towards goal but it cannons off the top of the Spurs wall. The visitors don't clear the ball effectively though and United collect possession near the touchline, in what has been a very promising period for Van Gaal's outfit.
(26’) Free kick to Man United on the edge of the box here as Mata collects the ball to feet before being unceremoniously scythed to the ground by Vertonghen. Now, there are plenty of candidates for this set-piece, with Mata and Memphis taking a particular interest.
(24’) A terribly unfortunate goal for Spurs to concede having started the match so confidently. The only negative that United can take from that opener is that Rooney looked extremely slow on the ball inside the box and should have grabbed his first goal of the season.
--- 22’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR MANCHESTER UNITED! THE HOSTS TAKE THE LEAD! Bentaleb gives the ball away in the middle of the park and United pounce. Young drives down the right wing and plays into the box for Rooney, who languishes in possession too long, but Walker comes in and plays into his own net while attempting to make the tackle! One-nil! First goal of the new season! ---
(20’) It hasn't been a particularly encouraging start for Blind, who has been deployed as a centre-back alongside Smalling for this afternoon's game. The Dutchman's distribution from defence has been poor and he has lost the physical battle against Dembele and Kane up until this point.
(18’) Shaw opens up his stride down the left flank and then lays back inside to Young. The former Aston Villa winger is forced into the middle by Walker but then manages to find Mata with a beautiful diagonal pass to the opposite wing.
(16’) Spurs are fresh off two midweek games in the Audi Cup against Real Madrid and Milan, and it must be said that the toils of that pre-season tournament don't seem to have fazed Pochettino's outfit up until this point. Indeed, it is United who are looking the more sluggish of the two teams.
(14’) Both sides are just showing each other too much respect in these opening stages, in what has largely been a midfield battle. The creative players in either side, such as Eriksen, Mata, and Memphis, haven't really managed to find the space required to hurt the opposition in the final third.
(12’) Kane is certainly aiming to put himself about up top physically as he attempts to ruffle the feathers of this untested Manchester United defence. Not a lot of sights on goal for the Englishman as of yet, but a fairly bright start regardless.
(10’) Spurs have just moved their defensive line 10 yards or so further back which is allowing Schneiderlin and Carrick to boss those central areas with the space awarded to them. Pochettino's men do possess plenty of pace in attack though, so perhaps they are looking to reel United in before breaking forward.
(8’) Young, who recently signed a new contract with the Red Devils, takes on Walker down the left wing before standing a teasing cross to the front post, but Alderweireld is on hand to make the commanding clearance. United eventually recycle possession and gain the throw-in deep in the opposition half.
(6’) United appear to have been jolted into sorting themselves out after that Eriksen chance as they only now seem to look confident on the ball, especially in the middle of the park. We are yet to see much from Rooney or Memphis as of yet, but early doors, of course.
(4’) What a chance for Tottenham! Kane collects the ball up top and delightfully lifts the ball over the oncoming United defence for Eriksen, who controls on his head before looking to dink a strike into the top corner, but his attempt just goes north of the crossbar!
(2’) A decent start to the match from Spurs as they look to gain dominance in these early stages through short passing in the middle of the pitch. A confident beginning from Dier, who has been deployed out of position as the defensive midfielder. Will be interesting to see how he does today.
(1’) The Barclays Premier League is back under way with Manchester United versus Tottenham!
The teams have made their way to the pitch at Old Trafford and we are almost ready for kick-off!
There is plenty of cause for optimism in both camps before the season starts this afternoon. Man Utd will be looking to build on their Champions League qualification of last campaign and mount a serious assault on the championship. Tottenham, meanwhile, have aspirations of making it into Europe's premier club competition themselves.
Some interesting selections from Van Gaal and Mauricio Pochettino for this opening day of the season, then. As expected, Romero starts in goal for United, with De Gea not even making the first team squad. Darmian is given a debut at right-back, while Schneiderlin and Memphis make their first league starts also. For Spurs, Alderweireld starts alongside his compatriot, Jan Vertonghen, while Eric Dier is deployed in the middle of midfield. Kane starts as the lone striker and Hugo Lloris is still struggling with a wrist injury, meaning Michel Vorm is in between the sticks.
Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Vorm; Walker, Alderweireld, Vertonghen, Davies; Dier, Bentaleb; Dembele, Eriksen, Chadli; Kane.
Man Utd (4-2-3-1): Romero; Darmian, Smalling, Blind, Shaw; Schneiderlin, Carrick; Mata, Memphis, Young; Rooney.
TEAM NEWS...
The last time this fixture took place was back in March, and Manchester United ran out comfortable 3-0 winners thanks to goals from Marouane Fellaini, Michael Carrick, and Wayne Rooney. Spurs did, however, managed to claim a victory the season before that at Old Trafford, when Emmanuel Adebayor and Christian Eriksen sealed the 2-1 win.
The Red Devils will be hoping to avoid a repeat of the opening day in the last campaign when they went down to an impressive Swansea side 2-1 at Old Trafford. Over the course of the season, though, United managed to recover to earn a coveted fourth-placed finish in the lague, which has seen them matched up against Club Brugge in the Champions League play-off, which was drawn yesterday.
Over in North London, it has been an uncharacteristically low-key summer for Spurs, who have refrained from the spending seen in previous seasons. They have, however, bought well in Toby Alderweireld, and perhaps most importantly, managed to keep hold of star striker, Harry Kane.
Louis van Gaal has overseen another transitional summer at United, with plenty of comings and goings in terms of transfers. The exciting batch of recruits includes Memphis Depay, Morgan Schneiderlin, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Matteo Darmian. However, it is perhaps another signing that will make the headlines today as Sergio Romero starts in goal, with David de Gea seemingly on his way to Santiago Bernabeu with Real Madrid.

(90’) ...but Sanchez heads it away from danger. It looks like the points are going back to the Midlands tonight!
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card A. Westwood gets yellow. ---
(90’) Both managers are waving their charges forward here as the tension starts to build here. Bournemouth win a corner so late in the game...
(90’) There will be a minimum of FIVE minutes of added on time.
(89’) It's been the epitome of a smash and grab performance so far from the Villans but it might be enough to see them pick up all three points. We are about to head into stoppage time...
(87’) The visitors are finding it much easier to break now as the Cherries continue to pile the men forward, but Agbonlahor's cut back to Gestede is too close to Elphick.

(81’) WILSON GOES DOWN! Clark flattens the Bournemouth man on the edge of the penalty area and the majority of the crowd cry foul but the referee is having none of it. The South Coast side are starting to look a little desperate now.
--- 80’ Yellow card D. Gosling is yellow-carded. ---

TEN MINUTES TO KICK OFF! How are your nerves, Cherries fans? You have finally reached the promised land - the zenith of what could be argued as the best league in the world.
