All square then in a very exciting opening game of the 2015/16 Barclays Premier League season. Watford took a 14th-minute lead through Miguel Layun, before Ross Barkley equalised 14 minutes from time. Substitute Odion Ighalo looked to have won it for the new boys in the 83rd minute, only for fellow late arrival Arouna Kone to snatch Everton a share of the points.
FULL TIME: EVERTON 2-2 WATFORD
(90’) HONOURS EVEN!!! The referee blows his final whistle.
(90’) ONE MINUTE TO GO!...
(90’) NEARLY FOR EVERTON! Kone looks to thread the ball through for Naismith but Cathcart spots the danger and is quickly across to clear to safety.
(90’) This will be the second straight season that Everton have started a campaign with a 2-2 draw against a promoted club. They did the same against Leicester City 12 months ago.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution R. Lukaku is replaced with S. Naismith. ---
(90’) FIVE MINUTES! Steven Naismith is sent on by Martinez in search of a winner in place of Lukaku and, straight after that, the fourth official indicates that we will have five minutes of additional time.
(88’) Fantastic drama in the closing stages here at Goodison! Both sides really going for it here as they look to get three points on the board on this opening weekend. We've got an exciting final two minutes plus stoppage time to come...
--- 86’ Assist The assist came from R. Lukaku. ---
--- 86’ Goal! WHAT A RESPONSE FROM EVERTON!!! We're all level once again as an attack sees Lukaku find Kone, who races onto the ball and drills it into the far corner. Pick a winner from this one!... ---
(85’) WOW! That really wasn't in Everton's script! It was a beautifully taken goal by Ighalo, who left Stones for dead with that dummy before finishing with aplomb.
--- 83’ Assist Assist by T. Deeney. ---
--- 83’ Goal! WHAT AN IMPACT FROM THE SUBSTITUTE!!! IS THAT THE WINNER?! A long kick down the field breaks Ighalo's way and he cleverly cuts inside Stones, before drilling the ball past Howard to regain his side's advantage. ---
(82’) Everton won the repeat of this fixture 2-1 back in August 2006. Mikel Arteta and Andy Johnson scored the goals. That same scoreline would do very nicely for them here.
(80’) Watford have made their final change and introduced Ben Watson, who gave Martinez his greatest moment as a manager with the winning goal in the 2013 FA Cup final for Wigan. Behrami makes way.
--- 79’ Substitution V. Behrami is done for the day. B. Watson is his replacement. ---
(78’) Everton have plenty of momentum with them now going into the final 12 minutes of this game. They will fancy themselves to go on and get a winner, but need to be wary of Watford on the counter attack.
--- 77’ Substitution K. Mirallas is done for the day. B. Oviedo is his replacement. ---
--- 76’ Assist A. Koné gave the assist. ---
--- 76’ Goal! WHAT AN EQUALISER FROM BARKLEY!!! EVERTON ARE LEVEL! Coleman's cross is controlled and laid off by Kone into the path of Barkley, who fires a thumping strike into the top corner. No chance for Gomes - game on! ---
--- 74’ Substitution O. Ighalo enters play, replacing Jurado. ---
(74’) Watford are making another change and Jurado is given a rest by Flores. He has worked hard for his team today and is replaced by Odion Ighalo, who netted 17 goals in 18 games at the back end of last season.
(72’) It is Coleman's turn to deliver a delicious ball into the area but, again, nobody in blue really attacks the cross and Gomes is able to rise unchallenged to punch clear.
(70’) OUCH! Mirallas is receiving attention from the physios after Behrami mistimes his tackle and accidentally stands on the ankle of the Everton winger. Martinez will want him to continue.
(68’) KONE SHOULD DO BETTER! Cleverley delivers a marvellous cross from out deep on the right hand side. Kone is unmarked in the area but can only direct his header wide with Gomes flat-footed.
(67’) GOOD EFFORT! The Watford left-back then tries his luck with a fierce drive from distance and Howard has to get strong hands on the ball to beat it away.
--- 66’ Yellow card J. Holebas gets yellow. ---
(66’) Watford show the first real sign that they are already hanging on to this lead, as Holebas is booked for time-wasting for not taking a throw-in when he should have.
(65’) Barry is no stranger to that position, of course, but you have to go back to his younger days at Aston Villa for the last time he regularly played there.
--- 63’ Substitution B. Galloway is replaced with A. Koné. ---
(63’) Kone is called upon by Martinez and it is an interesting move. Galloway is the man to make way and the striker takes his place up front with Barry moving to left-back.
(61’) Everton have some good options on the bench if they wish to use them. The likes of Arouna Kone and Steven Naismith have the ability to make things happen.
--- 59’ Substitution J. Paredes enters play, replacing M. Layún. ---
(59’) The visitors are now going to make the first change of the afternoon and it is the goalscorer Layun making way, with Juan Carlos Paredes taking his place.
(57’) Should they go on to hold out for the win, it would be their first on the opening weekend of a Premier League season. They have lost their previous two against Everton in 2006/07 and Wimbledon in 1999/2000.
(55’) Watford are hanging on here. Granted they are now protecting a lead, but they have began this second half completely the opposite to how they did the first when they were flowing forward with attacks.
--- 54’ Yellow card S. Coleman is cautioned by the referee. ---
(53’) RIGHT PLACE, RIGHT TIME! Lukaku and Barkley find McCarthy darting into the penalty area. He pulls the ball back across the box, but Cathcart takes up a good position and is able to prevent an almost certain tap-in.
(52’) There is a lot of purpose about the hosts' play since half time. They are looking so much more dangerous and Watford cannot get out of their own half.
(50’) HE SHOULD DO BETTER! Barkley a dangerously deep cross with his left foot to the far post where Lukaku is unmarked, but cannot direct a header towards goal.
(49’) IMPORTANT TOUCH FROM GOMES! Mirallas delivers a cross from the right hand side. It really isn't the best but it swings towards goal and the Watford keeper has to tip it over the bar.
(47’) Everton start the second half well with some very neat link-up play and Behrami has to make a vital interception to stop Coleman from delivering the cross.
(46’) KICK OFF! And away we go, Everton gets things going once more.
The teams are coming back out onto the field and the second half is about to commence.
As for Everton, there is plenty for them to think about at the break. They started off well but have looked short of ideas going forward since. Martinez needs to encourage them now, they've got quality but must use it well.
Watford will be very pleased with themselves after that first-half performance, they just need to be careful not to sit back too much in the second and rest on their laurels.
HALF TIME: EVERTON 0-1 WATFORD
(45’) Boos rings around Goodison Park as Mr Jones blows his whistle to bring the first half to a close.
(45’) OOH SO CLOSE! A cross is cleared by Everton straight to Layun 25 yards from goal. The goalscorer drills back a vicious effort that fizzes just wide of the far post.
(44’) Well read by Gomes! Lukaku chases a long ball over the Watford defence but the Watford keeper is quickly out to claw the ball away from his path.
--- 42’ Yellow card T. Deeney goes into the referee's book. ---

(41’) Capoue links up nicely with Jurado 35 yards from goal before adavancing and trying his luck with a drilled effort which is straight at Howard. Nevertheless, it's all positive signs for the Hornets.
(39’) Everton's all-round play hasn't been to bad so far on the whole. They just seem a little short of ideas in the final third. Mind you, Watford have been exceptional at the back in this first half.
(37’) They could find things difficult this campaign as, before the end of October, they are scheduled to play each of the teams who finished in the top seven last season.
(35’) Everton do tend to be rusty in the early stages of any season. In fact, they have won just one of their last seven opening Premier League fixtures. That came against Manchester United in 2012.

(26’) Barkley can be so dangerous when he finds the small pokcets of space in the middle of the pitch. He looks to do so again but is quickly dispossessed by a wonderful sliding challenge from Behrami.

(21’) It is not only Watford who have got off to the perfect start this season. Over at the King Power Stadium, Leicester have already raced into a 2-0 lead over Sunderland!
(19’) NO CHANCES FROM GOMES! A corner is swung in from the right and met by Barry who looks to guide the ball into the top corner, but the Watford keeper gets across well and tips it over the bar.
(18’) Incredibly, that is the 36th goal that Everton have conceded in their opening game of a Premier League season - that's more than any other side.
(16’) That is exactly what Flores will have wanted. It has been a very confident start from his side and he will be hoping they can keep this going throughout the season.

(12’) Watford are playing a very patient game here. They are happy to just sit back and let their opponents have possession, providing they hold themselves together.
(10’) Both sides will be looking to follow in the footsteps of Manchester United and get their seasons off to a perfect start. United overcame Tottenham Hotspur by a goal to nil in today's earlier kick-off.
(8’) Galloway shows that he is capable of deputising for Baines straight away, as he covers his centre-half well by coming across to make a decent interception from Deeney.
(7’) It has been a fairly open start to the game. Both sides are looking assured and confident on the ball. Everton have probably just shaded things inside the opening seven minutes.
(5’) It will be interesting to see how this new-look Watford gel today. Three of the back four have been signed over the summer and Flores will be hoping they can consolidate as a unit fairly quickly.
(3’) As just mentioned, our referee today is Mike Jones. The 47-year-old from Cheshire brandished 117 yellow cards and 10 red during his 34 games last season.
(1’) KICK OFF! Mike Jones blows his whistle and Watford get us underway!
The teams are out and kick off is just moments away!

FULL TIME: LEICESTER 4-2 SUNDERLAND. Claudio Ranieri's tenure gets off to a dream start as the Foxes run riot over a defensively frail Black Cats outfit. Riyad Mahrez scored a brace while Marc Albrighton provided a goal and two assists as Younes Kaboul and company are exposed at the back. Sunderland put up a fight in the second half, but it wasn't nearly enough.
(90’) That will do it!

(86’) Kante to Okazaki! The new boys link up for what nearly produces the fifth Leicester goal! Penetrating run from the midfielder who darts through the centre before picking out Okazaki, but the striker sees his shot deflected behind for a corner.

(81’) Dreadful tackle from Rodwell who doesn't even attempt to play the ball before taking out the legs of Okazaki. He's incredibly lucky not to be given a yellow card, which would have seen him sent off.

--- 77’ Substitution R. Mahrez is done for the day. C. Fuchs is his replacement. ---

--- 73’ Yellow card Y. Kaboul is cautioned by the referee. ---

Schlupp drives it back into the area and Kaboul gives it straight to Albrighton who turns and nestles a shot into the bottom corner. ---

The atmosphere is absolutely superb inside the King Power Stadium, and nothing less should be expected on opening day. These fans are thrilled to be back in the Premier League when their prospects looked so bleak a few months ago, and they'll try to prove they belong yet again this season.
There's few surprises surrounding the Black Cats team, though John O'Shea has been dropped meaning Lee Cattermole will serve as captain. Jeremain Lens and Younes Kaboul make their competitive debuts for the club, while Adam Matthews starts on the bench. Yann M'Vila has hardly had the chance to train with his new teammates so he'll have to wait another week to feature.
The main question surrounding the Foxes was whether they would play with three or four in defence under Claudio Ranieri. The Italian has indeed swayed from what worked so well for Pearson last season, instead opting for a traditional four at the back. Wes Morgan is a surprise inclusion having been a part of a hectic international schedule this summer, while Shinji Okazaki makes his competitive debut for the club, partnering Jamie Vardy up top. No starts for N'Golo Kante or Yohan Benalouane who just arrived this week, with the duo beginning the match on the substitute's bench.

Sunderland on the other hand are at least a bit familiar with their new permanent manager, Dick Advocaat. Leicester City picked up the reputation as loveable underdogs a season ago when they achieved the impossible, avoiding relegation after being bottom of the table for the greater part of seven months. It was a heartfelt story orchestrated by Nigel Pearson, but he's no longer the man in charge. It's often said that life is harder for promoted teams in their second Premier League season, should they get there – and that's the daunting task facing new manager Claudio Ranieri, who kicks off his first season back in England since 2004.
IT'S OPENING DAY! There's buzz aplenty around the world as the Premier League kicks off another wonderful season. The King Power Stadium is our venue today as Leicester City and Sunderland celebrate their involvement in the festivities after a couple of close calls in the previous campaign. Norwich meanwhile will feel very hard done by, having a hat-trick of chances to equalize going against them: a penalty not called, a goal chalked off, and a ball cleared off the line. Thank you for joining us here today!

(69’) Obertan surges forward on the counter-attack for Newcastle but plays the ball back to Colback, as a result of a lack of options ahead of him. The Toon midfielder drives forward and wins a corner superbly down the left.
--- 68’ Substitution Anita is taken off on a stretcher as Newcastle are forced into making their first change of the game, with Tiote coming on to replace the former Ajax midfielder. ---
(67’) Tadic steps in-field from the right and drives a shot towards goal, which Coloccini diverts behind for a corner; a good chance for Southampton to try and find a leveller.
--- 65’ Substitution Rodriguez returns from a lengthy injury lay-off and gets just over an hour of Premier League football for the Saints, before being replaced by Shane Long who is the last player tiring defenders want to see coming on. ---
(65’) Anita is currently down for Newcastle and it looks as though he is struggling while receiving medical attention. Tiote looks set to come on for the hosts, in what would be a like-for-like swap in midfield.
(63’) Mane wins a corner from a saved shot by Krul and from the resulting set-piece, Tadic finds Fonte but the Portuguese defender heads over from the penalty spot.
(62’) Haidara bombs forward in search of setting up a third Newcastle goal and almost plays in Cisse but Fonte comes across and clears the danger brilliantly for Southampton.
(61’) Colback steals possession down the left and creates a lovely give-and-go with Cisse before winning Newcastle a corner. The ex-Sunderland midfielder has been brilliant today.
--- 60’ Yellow card José Fonte receives a yellow card. ---
(59’) Southampton are getting a foothold in this game now as Pelle flicks on Tadic's ball forward towards Rodriguez, before Janmaat steps across the Englishman and heads back to Krul.
(57’) Wijnaldum gives away a silly free-kick as pushes Mane, who had nowhere to go, to the floor and gives Southampton the chance to put pressure on the hosts' defence.
--- 55’ Yellow card Colback pushes and pulls Mane several times before bringing down the Southampton man, cancelling out a breakaway from the visitors in the process but he receives a yellow card for doing so. ---
(55’) Davis clips in a free-kick towards Fonte lurking at the back post but Coloccini clears the danger for Newcastle, who are looking to hit the Saints on the break now.
(53’) Mbemba, who has become a favourite amongst many on social media today after rocking up to St. James' Park in a tuxedo pre-match, looks to have overcome his nerves in the first half and is looking confident on the ball at the moment.
(51’) Southampton look to hit back with an equaliser of their own as Davis cleverly plays in Pelle, but the Italian moves into an offside position just before the ball was played.
(50’) Wijnaldum has been brought in by Newcastle to be the shining light of the McClaren era and he's certainly made the perfect start to life on Tyneside with that header. Excellent technique from the ex-PSV man.
--- 48’ Assist The assist came from G. Obertan. ---
--- 48’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAALLLL!! It's 2-1 to Newcastle! Obertan surges down the right on the counter-attack and makes the most of Sissoko's lofted pass by hanging the ball up for Wijnaldum, who superbly heads home past Stekelenburg. ---
(47’) BIG MISS! Southampton almost break the deadlock as Davis curls in a delightful free-kick towards the six-yard box and Yoshida, just a few yards out, brings out a good save from Krul but he really should have done better.
--- 46’ Substitution R. Martina enters play, replacing Cédric Soares. ---
(46’) Welcome back! Newcastle get us underway for the second half here at St. James' Park, with Southampton bringing on Cuco Martina for Cedric during the break.
Cisse's goal allowed Newcastle to deservedly get back into this game as McClaren's men shaded the first half, but Southampton look dangerous every time they win possession and surge forward.
The referee blows up for half time here at St. James' Park as Newcastle and Southampton are locked level on the scoreboard 1-1. Pelle's superb header put the Saints in front before Cisse managed to nick a goal back for the hosts minutes before the break.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-1 SOUTHAMPTON
(45’) CHANCE! Cedric gets on the end of a difficult pass towards the byline and flicks in a cross towards Tadic, who really should have done better as he guides the ball over the crossbar from close range.
(45’) Cisse drifts out wide and drives in a cross towards Sissoko at the back post but Fonte raises a leg and manages to deflect the ball away from the danger zone, and out for a Newcastle throw-in. As time ticks on in this first half, it's all Newcastle.
(44’) Cisse's first strike of the season has given the St. James' Park crowd a real lift heading into the interval and the officials have just indicated that two minutes will be added on to this first half.
--- 42’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAALLLLL!! It's 1-1 as Cisse draws Newcastle level! Wijnaldum plays a short corner towards Haidara, whose deflected cross off Mane goes right over the top of Stekelenburg and gifts Cisse the easiest of tap-ins inside the six-yard box. ---
(40’) Anita collects the ball from Colback and plays a woeful pass straight to Davis, who quickly clips it forward towards Mane's direction but the linesman on that side raises his flag for offside.
(38’) Newcastle are starting to get more bodies forward in support of Cisse now but that is playing into Southampton's hands, as Mane has almost been in on the counter-attack on a couple of occasions now.
(36’) Obertan makes a positive break down the left-hand side and surges past Cedric but his cross lacks in quality as it flies straight into the arms of Stekelenburg. Cisse has really struggled to get enough service in the first half.
(34’) Newcastle are enjoying a lot of possession at the moment but McClaren's men are just struggling to create many openings due to their lack of options inside the penalty area, making it all too easy for Southampton's defenders.
(32’) Southampton are continuing to find joy when crossing the ball into the box as Rodriguez and Pelle are having the better of Mbemba and Coloccini respectively when the likes of Cedric and Tadic were providing the ammunition from wide areas.
(30’) Newcastle have been the better of the two sides for large parts of this first half but the double blow of Southampton scoring and the referee not awarding them a penalty seems to have rocked them a little bit.
(28’) NO PENALTY! The referee again waves away Newcastle's appeals for a penalty as Sissoko flicks the ball up at the back post with his head and it appears to strike Rodriguez's chest, thus the officials were not interested in the hosts' claims.
(26’) Cedric initially appeared to be on thin ice at one point after a succession of fouls but his wonderful overlap to set up Pelle has put the Saints 1-0 up and are going in search for a second now.
--- 24’ Assist Assist by Cédric Soares. ---
--- 24’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAALLL!! It's 1-0 to Southampton! Despite Newcastle looking the brighter in this first half, Pelle rises above the two Toon defenders and finds the back of the net against the run of play to grab his third goal of the season, and his first in the Premier League. ---
(22’) Wijnaldum again chucks in a poor cross from the resulting set-play but Coloccini manages to keep the ball alive inside the box and clips it towards Yoshida's arm. The referee waves away Newcastle's appeals for a penalty, to the anger of the Toon skipper.
(20’) Cedric, already on a yellow card, surely picks up his last warning from the referee as he brings down Haidara and gifts Newcastle a free-kick in a dangerous position down the left.
(18’) Southampton pick up a corner after some poor defending from Newcastle as Tadic bends in a decent cross towards the back post, but Coloccini superbly prevents Rodriguez connecting with the ball which trickles out for a goal-kick.
(16’) Sissoko again surges down the right unmarked and powers a low cross towards an onrushing Colback, but Davis steps in and just about manages to clear the danger after slicing the ball.
(14’) WHAT A SAVE! Cedric latches onto a cute pass from Tadic over the top of Haidara inside the box and drives a low shot towards Krul, who parries the ball away from goal excellently. The former Sporting CP full-back thought he'd scored there!
--- 12’ Yellow card The Southampton right-back picks up the first caution of the game as he cynically pulls down Wijnaldum, just when the Newcastle number five was looking to break away at speed down the left-hand side. ---
(11’) Southampton are really struggling to get into their rhythm at the moment as Newcastle are sitting deep, making it really difficult for the visitors to find space, and are counter-attacking with immense pace going forward.
(9’) Sissoko again gets the beating of Yoshida down the right-hand side but his neither Cisse nor Obertan attempt to latch onto the end of his cross, before Cedric snuffs out the danger for the visitors.
(7’) BIG CHANCE! Wijnaldum almost breaks the deadlock for Newcastle but Davis makes a superb block inside his own penalty area. Sissoko makes a brilliant break down the right and bypasses Yoshida with ease, before he cuts it back to the Magpies new boy, who drives a shot straight at the Southampton midfielder. Stunning defending.
(5’) Newcastle give the ball away cheaply and that allows Rodriguez to break away down the left, but his cross flies past Pelle and out for a throw to McClaren's men. An early let-off for the Toon.
(3’) Wijnaldum collects the ball down the left-hand side and whips in a poor cross which Obertan does his best to flick towards the Southampton goal, but Stekelenburg gobbles the ball up comfortably. The hosts have made a good start to this game.
(1’) Southampton get us underway here at St. James' Park. The man in charge of the cards for today's game is Craig Pawson.
The players are stripped and raring to go as they leave the tunnel and enter onto the St. James' Park turf this afternoon. We are just moments away from seeing the action get underway.
Southampton, on the other hand, will be hoping to repeat their efforts at today's venue from last season as their 2-1 win at St. James' Park during the 2014/15 campaign is their only victory on Tyneside since 1997.
So despite spending £13m on Mitrovic from Anderlecht this summer, McClaren has decided to go with Papiss Cisse from the get-go and Newcastle fans will be hoping the Senegal forward can help put to bed their recent opening day misery of late. Before today, the Toon have failed to score in their opening day fixture in four of their last five seasons.
TEAM NEWS: Southampton have handed a Premier League debut to Cedric Soares, while Maarten Stekelenburg - formerly of Fulham - makes his first league start for the Saints. Jay Rodriguez makes his top-flight return after a lengthy injury lay-off, while new boys Cuco Martina and Juanmi are on the bench for Ronald Koeman's side.
TEAM NEWS: Newcastle boss McClaren has handed debuts to Chancel Mbemba and Georginio Wijnaldum, in what is a strong-looking starting eleven to kick their campaign off on home soil. SOUTHAMPTON substitutes: Gazzaniga, Martina, Caulker, Reed, Ward-Prowse, Long, Juanmi.
SOUTHAMPTON (4-2-3-1): Stekelenburg; Cedric, Fonte, Yoshida, Targett; Davis, Wanyama; Tadic, Mane, Rodriguez; Pelle.
NEWCASTLE UNITED substitutes: Darlow, Taylor, Tiote, De Jong, Aarons, Perez, Mitrovic.

A host of new players have been brought in by the Magpies this summer as Newcastle look to bounce back from a disappointing campaign last season, while Southampton will once again be hoping to secure a high league standing alongside juggling Europa League football.
After an interesting start to the 2015/16 season on Saturday, all eyes now turn to Sunday's action and today's fixture between Newcastle United and Southampton certainly is an intriguing match-up.

FULL TIME! Liverpool edge their way to a 1-0 win at the Britannia against Stoke, courtesy of a 86th-minute screamer from Coutinho. It was a hard-fought game with plenty of half chances, but a bit of magic from an individual settles it. Plenty of positives for Hughes' men, with the Reds very fortunate to come away with three points. That's all that we have time for, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Mignolet is very quick off his line to rush out and deny Diouf and Walters the chance to bustle into the penalty area and poke home a well-weighted ball into the box! The Belgian pushes the ball to safety with his hands.
(90’) A curling free-kick delivery from Odemwingie curls behind for a goal kick once again, after evading everyone who tried to attack it. Stoke are running out of time to make a comeback. There are three minutes of stoppage time.
(88’) Well, this game needed something out of nothing to get it started - and that was certainly something. The away fans are now making plenty of noise, with Stoke only having a few minutes left to try and claw back a point.
--- 86’ Assist Assist by J. Gomez. ---
--- 86’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! COUTINHO FIRES HOME A SCREAMER! The Brazil international takes aim from range and clatters a long-range thunderbolt into the back of Butland's net! After some neat play from the away side, he bends a dipping and swerving effort just above the glove of the goalkeeper! ---
(84’) Diouf is fouled yet again, with Stoke getting another chance to load the penalty area with bodies. Odemwingie dips a swirling effort in towards the back post, but is hurtles beyond the woodwork and into the advertising hoardings with Mignolet easily having his angles covered. Moments later, Johnson picks out Diouf with a cross, but his header is deflected narrowly over.
(82’) Big chance for Stoke! A block prevents Mignolet from needing to get involved, with Van Ginkel the man frustrated. Liverpool head down the other end, with Coutinho trying to get in behind the hosts' back four, but Cameron recovers brilliantly to hook the ball into touch.
(80’) Firmino immediately shows a bit of skill, before trying to permit Milner to overlap - but the Englishman is tackled easily. Moments later, the ex-Man City midfielder lifts a back-post cross up to Benteke, but Sidwell drops back well to help win an aerial battle for Stoke.
--- 78’ Substitution S. Sidwell enters the game and replaces C. Adam. ---
--- 78’ Substitution P. Odemwingie enters play, replacing I. Afellay. ---
--- 78’ Substitution J. Ibe is replaced with Roberto Firmino. ---
(78’) Milner lifts a long ball up towards Benteke, but Cameron does well to beat the Liverpool striker in the air. Rodgers opts to make a change, with summer signing Roberto Firmino coming into the action in place of Ibe. The young Englishman really hasn't managed to make a big impact this afternoon. Pieters and then Muniesa have both done well thus far. Afellay is replaced by Odemwingie and Sidwell comes in for Adam.
(76’) Long balls are coming to nothing for both sides, with the goalkeepers needing to come out and collect plenty of loose through passes. Benteke is released towards the edge of the Stoke penalty area, but Cameron keeps tabs on his run and ensures that the Belgium international can't take control.
(74’) This game might just get a little bit more nervy as we edge into the dying embers, with Rodgers in particular under pressure to start the season well. A cross is curled in towards the back post by Muniesa, but Mignolet is light on his feet to come out and claim the ball in plenty of traffic.
--- 73’ Yellow card C. Adam is cautioned by the referee. ---
(72’) Liverpool manage to win possession back in midfield, before a long ball is clipped up towards Benteke. Substitute Wollscheid uses all of his height to beat the Belgian in the air, before play is stopped due to Ibe taking a blow to the face. Adam picks up a yellow card for his troubles.
(70’) Only 20 minutes are left at the Britannia, with no sign of the seven goals that were mustered up the last time this fixture took place. Both teams are starting to throw more men forward and put the result on the line, now. Liverpool play some great football, with Henderson released down the right by Milner! The Englishman lifts a cross towards the back post, but Benteke isn't there to nod home!
(68’) Great save from Butland! The resulting corner is headed goalwards by Skrtel, but the English goalkeeper gets across well to his right-hand side to make a clean save. With otehr players lurking, the former Birmingham shot-stopper does brilliantly to not spill or parry the effort.
(67’) Coutinho manages to dance around a couple of challenges, before seeing a shot blocked inside the penalty area! The loose ball falls to Benteke, who jinks onto his stronger right foot, but the Belgian's eventual effort is charged down and then hacked away! There's been a real ebb and flow to this second half. Moments later, Coutinho is involved again after good work down the right from Milner, but Liverpool can only win a corner.
(66’) Stoke have started to put on some considerable pressure of late, but still no goals are forthcoming. Ibe tries to break down the right again and bypass Muniesa, but the former Barcelona defender manages to cleverly play the ball back off the Liverpool man and behind for a goal kick. The crowd applauds.
(64’) Good save from Mignolet! Adam whips in a tantalising free-kick delivery from the right flank, which floats beyond Diouf and towards the bottom corner! The Liverpool goalkeeper gets down well to push the ball clear of danger.
--- 63’ Yellow card J. Gomez is cautioned by the referee. ---
--- 63’ Substitution E. Can comes on for A. Lallana. ---
(63’) Can replaces Lallana for the Reds, with the German definitely offering a bit more mettle in compared to the technically gifted man he replaced. In the aftermath of a set piece, Lovren manages to dig out a shot, but Butland makes a simple save at his near post. Stoke try to break, but their counter is halted by Gomez, with the young left-back booked as a result. Slightly harsh, perhaps, as Walters backed into him in the first place.
(61’) Less than half an hour remains for either side to break the deadlock, with Afellay shifting the ball out to Johnson well. The English defender tries to break beyond Lallana and Gomez, but the latter is able to shield the ball behind for a goal kick. The Stoke man thinks that the last touch came off a scrappy sliding tackle by Lallana, however.
(59’) Walters is caught offside yet again! The Irishman is picked out bending a run in behind Gomez, but goes slightly too early! A few Stoke attacks have been halted by the linesman's flag this side of half time, with Hughes presumably growing a little bit tired of it.
(57’) A dangerous cross into the Liverpool penalty area is a brief cause for concern for the visitors, but nobody managed to take the ball under their spell - with Diouf caught offside moments later. Emre Can is being given instructions by Rodgers, with the German looking to be the away side's first change of the afternoon.
(55’) Henderson whips in a corner from the right-hand side, which Butland palms away rather unconvincingly. Another long ball is pumped into the Stoke box, but Johnson has the peace of mind to nod a cushioned header back to his goalkeeper. Liverpool are already going for an alternative plan of hitting Benteke with more direct balls.
(53’) A long ball looks to release Benteke in behind the slightly sluggish Wollscheid, but the pass skids straight through to Butland. Moments later, Ibe races down the right flank and bursts into the box, but Muniesa times a challenge brilliantly to dispossess the youngster. He had to get that right, otherwise it was a certain penalty.
(51’) Diouf goes down in a heap holding his face, with Lovren quickly being booked by the referee. The former Southampton defender clearly raised his arm in his opponent's face, but the referee deems it to only be worth a yellow card. With another official, that could have had a different outcome.
--- 50’ Yellow card D. Lovren receives a yellow card. ---
(49’) Benteke has half a chance, but the former Aston Villa striker can only poke an effort on the stretch towards goal. Butland gobbles it up with consummate ease. The second half has started at a fairly slow and cagey pace. Stoke will want to allow Wollscheid to settle into the rhythm of proceedings, before leaving him too exposed. Coutinho rounds Johnson and bursts into space, but can only loop a terrible effort towards the goalkeeper.
(47’) Pieters looks to have picked up an injury at the end of that first half, meaning that Muniesa has been pushed out to left-back for the hosts. Van Ginkel tests Mignolet from the very off, firing a low drive towards the near post that the Belgian gets down well to.
--- 46’ Substitution E. Pieters is replaced with P. Wollscheid. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! The opening 45 minutes were tight and low on opportunities, with both coaches probably pleased to get into the interval to freshen things up in terms of ideas and instructions. Wollscheid is brought on at the break by Hughes.
HALF TIME! The two sides head into the break with a goalless scoreline at the Britannia, with the hosts not doing too badly at all. Johnson and Diouf have had half chance for Stoke, while Coutinho has seen a couple of shots in dangerous areas well blocked. This is very finely balanced, with everything still to play for in the second half.
(45’) There are two minutes of stoppage time at the end of the first half. Ibe battles to get beyond Pieters, but struggles, with Butland racing out of his goal to smother the ball and aid his left-back. That should be about that for the first half, aside from Van Ginkel clashing with Lallana.
(45’) Diouf is released in behind the visiting back four, before chopping back inside Clyne and onto his stronger foot. He picks out the onrushing Van Ginkel with the pass, but the Dutchman can only drag a terrible effort wide of the target and straight at Gomez. The young defender controls before clearing upfield.
(44’) Afellay falls awkwardly, after landing on his back, with the Dutchman appearing to be a little bit winded as a result. He needs a moment before being helped back to his feet by the physios, with the referee having to add a couple of minutes of stoppage time onto the first half for this.
(42’) Ibe tries to break down the right flank, but he is quickly mobbed and dispossessed by four red and white shirts. The youngster hasn't been able to get beyond Pieters too often, with the Dutchman well protected despite having the lightweight Afellay ahead of him.
(40’) Milner throws himself into a tackle on Adam, with the Scotland international looking to be in some discomfort from the challenge! The referee is quick to brandish a card at the former Leeds midfielder, but he doesn't look at all happy with the decision. Five minutes remain in the first half for an opener.
--- 39’ Yellow card J. Milner is yellow-carded. ---
(38’) Benteke is nearly found by a lifted ball into the penalty area, but the bounce beats the Belgian striker! It skips up off the turf and into the arms of Butland, who had to be very quick off his line to gobble up the pass ahead of his opponent! Liverpool's marquee signing has been quiet, but one chance could change all that.
(36’) Johnson fires over! Walters breaks down the left, with Van Ginkel able to send a cross in from the byline! It is deflected over Mignolet, but Skrtel makes a good clearance! The danger stays alive, with the former Liverpool right-back picked out merely eight yards from goal, but he scoops a rushed shot beyond the crossbar!
(35’) A few fouls break up the flow of play, with only 10 minutes remaining until the end of the first half. Stoke can be pleased with how they've created more dangerous opportunities, but it doesn't quite compare to their last first-half performance against Liverpool. Rodgers continues to note down points on his pad and paper feverishly.
(33’) Diouf is penalised for following through on Mignolet, after the Belgian goalkeeper had already hacked a clearance upfield. Pieters requieres some treatment for the home side, with the Dutchman going down off the ball. Hughes takes the opportunity to bark some instructions at Walters.
(31’) Benteke tries to jink around Cameron and in behind the hosts' defence, but the former Genk striker doesn't have the legs to beat Butland to the ball. The opening half an hour hasn't seen the English goalkeeper tested at all, with Liverpool still needing to get Coutinho and Ibe on the ball in more dangerous areas.
(29’) Walters guides a header just wide of the back post from the resulting free kick, but the Stoke forward was narrowly offside anyhow. Moments later, Gomez tries to lay a pass back into Mignolet, but the Belgian goalkeeper is put under a lot of pressure by Diouf. Fortunately for the visitors, their shot-stopper can clear.
--- 28’ Yellow card M. Škrtel is yellow-carded. ---
(28’) Stoke are keeping the ball fairly well inside their own half, but are struggling to create any ideas higher up the field. After a neat pass around the corner from Afellay, Skrtel comes through the back of Diouf horribly. Deserved yellow card for the Slovakian defender.
(26’) Henderson whips in the resulting free kick, but it fails to make it over the first man. Moments later, Lallana tries to ghost in behind the Stoke back four, but the England international is caught narrowly offside following a pass from Gomez. Not much in terms of offensive quality on show, thus far, with moves breaking down upon arriving at the edge of the penalty box.
(24’) Walters is picked out making a run in behind by a long ball, but the Republic of Ireland international can't angle a header goalwards due to some pressure. Ibe then break down the right-hand side and nips beyond Pieters, with the linesman's waving for a free kick due to how the Dutchman jumped in on the winger.
(22’) Coutinho sees a shot blocked on the edge of the penalty area, with Benteke continuing to struggle to find space against a Stoke back four that become very compact. Chances continue to be at a real premium, with Liverpool surely still very aware of their 6-1 defeat here only a few months ago. They're looking more solid in defence this afternoon, however.
(20’) Lallana jinks in from the left-hand side, before trying his luck with his right foot, but the former Southampton midfielder sees his shot deflected behind for a corner. Milner drives into the box after receiving the set piece short, but can only win a second one. The next comes to nothing, too, with Johnson heading away at the near post.
(18’) Afellay continues to drift in pockets of space down the left-hand side, but Clyne is standing up to the early interrogation on his debut well. Benteke is yet to really be brought into play, with Rodgers' side not getting any bodies around their new striker. Diouf fires a tame effort directly at Mignolet.
(16’) The opening quarter of an hour hasn't seen much in the way of chances, but Liverpool will be pleased that they aren't looking flimsy enough at the back to concede six goals. Van Ginkel finds Afellay, who spreads play out to Johnson, but the former Portsmouth right-back's cross is far too heavy.
(14’) Shaqiri will probably be impressed with what he has seen so far in terms of tenacity from Stoke, but Hughes' men haven't created anything for 10 minutes or so. A long ball is lofted in towards Van Ginkel, but Skrtel rises highest to head clear. Moments later, Diouf is fed down the left by a backheel from Afellay, but the former Manchester United striker is dispossessed easily.
(12’) Henderson lifts a cross in towards Benteke, but the ball loops straight out of play for a throw in on the far side. Liverpool are settling into the contest in terms of having more possession, but Butland is yet to be given anything to worry about at all.
(10’) Liverpool look to break down the right, but Afellay tracks back to intercept a loose pass and stroke possession back to Butland. Stoke's fans are spending the vast majority of their time clapping appreciatively, which shows how their side have started. Ibe is again the target of a searching pass, but Pieters slides in ahead of the Englishman.
(8’) Half chance for Stoke! Adam is presented with the ball on the edge of the penalty area, but the awkward height of it prevents the Scot from striking a clean half volley. The home team are seeing more of the ball and Liverpool are struggling to make any real inroads going forward. Ibe is picked out on the right-hand side, but found a yard offside.
(7’) Afellay is already looking quite lively for the hosts, with the former Barcelona wide man able to drift inside and look for the ball. Stoke break down the right-hand side, but Lovren covers across well to deny Adam the chance to whip in a cross. Plenty for the home fans to be excited about thus far, with Hughes' men moving the ball neatly.
(5’) Stoke are pressing very high upfield during the opening minutes, with Afellay picking up an early yellow card as a result. The Dutchman shows a high foot in a challenge with Clyne, which forces the referee to go to his book very prematurely in this clash. A sign of things to come?
--- 4’ Yellow card I. Afellay goes into the referee's book. ---
(3’) Xherdan Shaqiri is in the stands for this clash, but it remains to be seen as to which club the Switzerland international might be signing for. Let's give Stoke home advantage and presume that the Bayern man could be looking to join Hughes' Spanish-infused revolution.
(2’) Coutinho immediately tries to dance around a couple of challenges, before attempting to poke a through ball into Benteke, but Johnson cuts out the danger well. Moments later, Lovren drops back well to hook away a bouncing pass, with Diouf lurking over his shoulder.
(1’) We are underway in the first half! Stoke have a few different faces on show, compared to when they last played Liverpool, while the Reds' sole goalscorer in the 6-1 defeat is now plying his trade in the MLS. Big names have departed from both of these squads.
Both sides are out on the field of play and we are moments away from kick off at the Britannia Stadium! Unsurprisingly, the atmosphere is feeling rather optimistic, which is probably down to the result at the tail end of last season.
STOKE SUBS: Ireland, Odemwingie, Joselu, Sidwell, Given, Crouch, Wollscheid.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Toure, Firmino, Moreno, Can, Origi, Ings, Bogdan.
STOKE (4-2-3-1): Butland; Johnson, Cameron, Muniesa, Pieters; Adam, Whelan; Walters, van Ginkel, Afellay; Diouf.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Mignolet; Clyne, Lovren, Skrtel, Gomez; Henderson, Milner, Coutinho; Ibe, Lallana, Benteke.
STOKE TEAM NEWS: Glen Johnson sure didn't have to wait long to be reunited with his Liverpool teammates, as he gets the start today with his new club against his former. There are two other making their competitive debuts for the Potters this afternoon as Dutch duo Marco van Ginkel and Ibrahim Afellay anchor a three-man line behind preferred striker Mame Diouf. Captain Ryan Shawcross is sidelined with a back problem, meaning that US international Geoff Cameron is pushed into centre-back alongside Marc Muniesa.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of Liverpool's opening game of the Premier League season against Stoke. Brendan Rodgers will hope that lightning won't strike twice for his away side this afternoon.

City subsequently sit top of the table after one game, while West Brom prop everyone else up from the bottom. That's all we have time for tonight. Thanks for joining me, Tom Webber, and have a great night!
FULL TIME - West Brom 0-3 Man City: The Citizens get their season off to the perfect start, beating the Baggies thanks to a pair of goals from Toure and a header from Kompany. Pellegrini's men have managed something neither Chelsea nor Arsenal could - win their opening fixture of the 2015-16 Premier League campaign! They produced a formidable display and fully deserved the three points.
(90’) There is the final whistle!
(90’) MYHILL MAKES THE SAVE! Kolarov attempts to whip the free kick into the bottom corner but the Welshman gets across to parry it away! He may have conceded three tonight but he can be pleased with some aspects of his performance.
(90’) Yacob is once more guilty of bringing Silva to ground wide on the left. The Spaniard has been extremely impressive tonight. Could this set-piece provide the Citizens with a fourth?
(90’) Silva is felled inside the box but the referee does not award the visitors with a penalty. There will be a minimum of three added minutes now.
(89’) ANOTHER GOOD SAVE FROM MYHILL! Silva controls a cross exquisitely but has his shot blocked by Dawson. The ball falls kindly for Aguero but his effort is kept out by the keeper at his near post! The Welshman has made some impressive stops in this half.
(88’) Aguero comes in off the left, pulling defenders along with him before teeing up Nasri with a backheel. The Frenchman's shot is deflected out of play and the resultant corner is taken short by Navas.
(87’) Anichebe has been bright since coming on. Again he does well to hold off Kompany and use his pace to get away from him before slamming a shot towards the corner which Hart is able to hold.
(85’) City are just calmly knocking the ball around in the West Brom half now. Sagna and Navas combine on the right in a move that releases the Spaniard but his cross is poor and ends up with Kolarov all the way out by the sideline on the opposite flank.
(83’) Anichebe holds off Kompany at the top of the box, using his chest to control the ball before looking to spin in behind. The Belgian gets a toes to it but Brunt is on hand to pounce on the loose ball. However, Sagna slides in and does enough to put the left-back off it!
(82’) Yacob concedes another free kick following an overzealous challenge on Silva, though the referee lets him off without a second yellow card. The Spaniard flights it deep into the box and Kompany fails to connect, leaving the ball to roll out on the far side.
--- 80’ Substitution C. McManaman comes on for S. Berahino. ---
--- 80’ Substitution M. Demichelis enters the game and replaces Y. Touré. ---
(80’) Both coaches use their final changes, with McManaman replacing Berahino for the hosts and Demichelis taking Toure's spot for the remainder.
(79’) STAT: Silva has scored in three of his last four appearances against the Baggies. That may improve if he is awarded the night's first goal, which he is surely going to claim.
(77’) STRAIGHT AT HART! Anichebe plays Brunt in with a delightful backheel and the left-back picks out Morrison with his delivery. The midfielder gets his head to the cross but fails to put it to either side of the keeper, who collects it at the second attempt.
(76’) The hosts continue to look for a consolation goal, but if they overcommit they could well be caught on the counterattack. None of the substitutes have had much of an impact this evening, with Aguero receiving very little service since coming on.
--- 74’ Substitution V. Anichebe comes on for R. Lambert. ---
--- 74’ Substitution S. Nasri enters the game and replaces R. Sterling. ---
(74’) Lambert's debut comes to an end as he makes way for Anichebe. City also make a change with Sterling going off to a chorus of boos with Nasri taking his place.
(73’) Brunt's deliveries from set-pieces have been brilliant and his latest forces Hart to come from his line and punch it clear. The hosts get it back into the box but this time Mangala heads it behind. Another corner follows and again the City keeper gets his fists to it. The relief doesn't last long, though, as West Brom win yet another set-piece that Lescott ends up heading wide. A good spell of pressure nonetheless.
(71’) STAT: City have been victorious in four of their last five visits to the Hawthorns in the Premier League.
(69’) Brunt launches a throw into the box, aiming for Lambert. It is flicked on and the bounce almost catches Kompany out but he manages to get it clear at the last.
(67’) Gardner pings in a great corner from the left that Dawson attacks in the centre. The defender connects with a header but it goes wide of the target following a slight touch from Kolarov. Regardless, it didn't look to be worrying Hart.
(65’) Aguero gets his first shot of the night away but it is blocked at the top of the box by Dawson. City aren't settling for the three goals that they already have.
(64’) Morrison dribbles towards the top of the box and attempts to take on Mangala but the Frenchman keeps him at bay with a strong tackle. His clearance is gathered by the hosts and Gardner uses it to fire a cross in for Lambert. The striker was in an offside position even though Hart denied him.
--- 63’ Substitution S. Agüero enters play, replacing W. Bony. ---
(63’) Yacob becomes the fourth Baggies player to go into the book for a challenge on Silva. Kolarov decides to go for goal directly from the free kick but produces a poor effort which sails over the top! Following that effort Pellegrini withdraws Bony for Aguero.
--- 62’ Yellow card C. Yacob goes into the referee's book. ---
(61’) It's hard to begrudge City this lead. West Brom have been vastly improved since the restart but the individual quality in the Citizens' ranks is seeing them through this one at the moment.
--- 59’ Assist David Silva provided the assist. ---
--- 59’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAAL!! CITY GRAB A THIRD THROUGH KOMPANY! More fantastic play from Silva sees him somehow work the space next to the byline and get a cross into the centre which is nodded behind. The Spaniard takes the set-piece himself and finds the captain who loops a brilliant effort into the far corner from the near post! It may have come off his shoulder, but he won't mind! ---
--- 58’ Yellow card J. Chester gets yellow. ---
(58’) Silva gets away with a tackle out on the far side but moments later Chester clips the heels of Sterling after being caught in possession. The crowd aren't happy as the referee again decides to pull out his yellow card for the Baggies player, despite letting the Spaniard off!
--- 57’ Yellow card C. Gardner receives a yellow card. ---
(57’) Gardner becomes the latest player to be shown a yellow card for a lunging tackle that cleans out Navas. He prevented a counterattack but it has cost him a booking.
(56’) Silva has been superb this evening and he continues his fantastic showing by getting away from Yacob and Lescott to attack along the byline on the right. He stabs the ball across the face of goal but no one makes a run to get on the end of it!
(54’) Silva loops a pass out to Sterling and this time the forward looks to come inside and get a shot away with his right foot. He overruns the ball, though, and is dispossessed by Yacob who brings it away to the adulation of the crowd.
(52’) Fernandinho now joins Fletcher in the book for persistent fouling no doubt. The resultant free kick is sent into the box by Gardner but is cleared for a corner from which the hosts fail to create anything.
--- 51’ Yellow card Fernandinho is cautioned by the referee. ---
(51’) ANOTHER GREAT CHANCE! Morrison dinks a lovely pass over the top of the defence for Berahino to latch onto. The striker may have been slightly offside but the flag stays down. Despite that he fails to take advantage, micuing a shot straight into the arms of Hart!
(49’) JUST OVER! Another foul from Fernandinho results in a free kick to West Brom in a great area. Lambert again takes on the responsibility and this time his effort is much better! Hart is forced to dive across his goal but the striker's attempt hits the roof of the net on its way behind!
(47’) Myhill to the rescue once more! Silva sets Sterling away down the left and he carries the ball into the box from the wing. Dawson forces him to go around the outside and the England international does just that, driving to the byline and poking a shot towards goal. From such an acute angle it is difficult for him to squeeze his effort beyond the keeper, who makes the block.
--- 46’ Substitution C. Yacob enters the game and replaces J. McClean. ---
(46’) We are back underway!
The teams are back out on the pitch and there is to be a change from Pulis with Yacob coming on for McClean.
HALF TIME - West Brom 0-2 Man City: The visitors lead thanks to two goals from Toure in a completely dominant half of football. It's been a difficult evening for the Baggies as they've been unable to contain the positivity of Pellegrini's men. A change of shape has helped but they will need to vastly improve after the interval to avoid this turning into a rout. Be sure to stay tuned for the second half!
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) There will be one minute of added time here.
(43’) That move has raised spirits inside the Hawthorns, though! Berahino whips a cracking ball in from the rigth wing but it bounces up at too difficult of a height for McClean to do anything with it. Another chance is created for the visitors moments later, though, with Kolarov having a shot deflected over after a surging run from left-back.
(41’) WHAT A CHANCE! Sterling passes up a fantastic chance to score a debut goal after being set free behind the West Brom defence. He produces a poor shot which is close enough to Myhill for the keeper to block! He really ought to be scoring there! The hosts attack and have a goal correctly ruled out for an offside decision against Berahino.
--- 39’ Yellow card D. Fletcher is yellow-carded. ---
(39’) The game's first yellow card is shown to Fletcher following a late tackle on Silva. The Spaniard had skipped away from him and the former Manchester United man made sure he didn't progress any further!
(37’) STAT: Pellegrini’s men finished the 2014-15 season with six successive wins. As things stand they look set to continue that run into the new campaign, unless, of course, West Brom can begin a comeback as soon as possible.
(35’) Lambert draws a foul from Mangala as he looks to bring down a long pass and the referee awards him a free kick. It is clipped into the box by the hosts but City are quick to repel the delivery.
(33’) The Baggies are beginning to look long for Lambert now, with the striker yet to really get involved in the action. After a disappointing spell at Liverpool he will be eager for a good start to his career at the Hawthorns.
(31’) JUST WIDE! Fernandinho releases Kolarov with an excellent pass out to the left and the Serbian races onto it. He spots Bony hanging back at the top of the box and rolls the ball to him. The Ivorian shoots first time but his effort deflects off Dawson and narrowly misses the target!
(30’) Berahino has pulled out onto the right now and he picks up the ball in a deep area. He pushes inside and Morrison overlaps him, so he rolls a pass for him to the byline. The subsequent cross is poor, though, and flies straight into the side netting. The Baggies clearly looking for more control in that midfield area now.
(28’) West Brom have a free kick in a decent area as Fernandinho sends Gardner tumbling in a central area 30 yards from goal. Lambert is the man to strike it but he fails to hit the target, curling his effort high of the bar. Hart was scrambling across his goal but knew that was going to worry him!
(26’) Pulis looks forlorn on the touchline. Their plan to withstand the Citizens for as long as possible has crumbled and now they need to become a bit more adventurous and take an active, positive role in this fixture.
--- 24’ Assist Assist by W. Bony. ---
--- 24’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAL!! TOURE MAKES IT TWO! The Ivorian picks up the ball just outside the centre circle and drives forward. He plays a one-two around Morrison with his compatriot Bony before curling a sublime effort past Myhill and into the top corner! A super strike from the midfielder! ---
(23’) With the visitors enjoying so much of the possession you sense that it won't be too long until they get another. West Brom kept 10 clean sheets in 18 league games under Pulis last season, but they look vulnerable here.
(21’) Pulis' men instantly go on the counterattack and Gardner whips a cross in from the right flank. Hart comes from his line to claim it but can only get it under control at the second attempt.
(20’) Almost another for City! Sterling initiates a one-two with Silva on the left-hand side of the box and the Spaniard's return pass sends him to the byline. He fires it into the centre and West Brom fail to deal with it. The ball eventually falls to Bony but his sliding strike is deflected away from goal.
(18’) Sterling is again involved for the visitors but his attempt to play a first-time pass into Bony is poor and loops over the Ivorian. Lescott is hand to nod the ball back to Myhill and West Brom reset the play. It doesn't take long for Pellegrini's men to regain the ball, though.
(16’) Silva picks out Sterling at the top of the box and the forward tries to turn Lescott and get a shot away. He loses his footing as he attempts to spin, though, and the Baggies get it clear. The ball is quickly sent to McClean who is felled by Fernandinho as the Brazilian decides to halt a potential counterattack.
(15’) McClean gets involved in an attacking sense for the first time this evening, pushing up on the left and driving a low cross into the middle. He is unable to find a team-mate, though, and the City defence get it clear at the first attempt. The home fans let out a roar of encouragement, though.
(13’) STAT: The Citizens have won five of their last six matches on the opening day of the Premier League, drawing one.
(11’) City continue to control possession and will be full of confidence following that early strike. West Brom are proving very passive in these opening stages with the visitors dictating the play.
--- 9’ Assist Jesús Navas gave the assist. ---
--- 9’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAL!! CITY LEAD! It hasn't taken long for Pellegrini's men to break the deadlock, but it's a fairly fortuitous goal that does it! Navas cuts the ball back to Toure at the top of the box and he mishits a shot towards the far corner. It rolls along the deck but seemingly takes a nick off Silva and then Dawson before trickling into the net beyond a flat-footed Myhill! ---
(7’) The hosts are affording City plenty of time in possession and at the moment they are using it fairly well, knocking it around and probing for an opening. Sagna is released at the byline but his delivery into the box is too deep for Bony to attack.
(5’) Gardner gets a talking to from the referee following his tug back on Sterling as the forward looked to charge into the Baggies' half on the break. The official clearly feels it is a little too early for a card, as it could well have warranted one on another night.
(4’) Silva drifts in off the right before pulling the trigger only to have his effort on goal blocked by Morrison. He picks up the rebound and moves it on to Sterling, but his pass out to the left is poor and West Brom come away with possession. The former Liverpool man is coming in for some rough treatment from the home fans.
(3’) The Citizens are applying all of the early pressure, with the Baggies defending with two lines of four. Sterling has started from the left wing with Navas on the right and Silva playing in behind Bony.
(1’) City get us underway at the Hawthorns!
The teams are out on the pitch so kick off will be upon us in a few short moments.
West Brom's last win against Man City on their own turf came back in December 2008, when a late Roman Bednar goal sank the Citizens, then coached by Mark Hughes. The Baggies beat Chelsea here late last season and would love to kick off the new campaign with a similar result.
This will be a huge night for Sterling following his big-money move from Liverpool. The forward will be expected to take his game to another level in Manchester in order to warrant the fee that brought him in from Anfield. Bony, too, will want to make a mark tonight to try and stake his claim for a regular starting spot.
Man City bench: Caballero, Zabaleta, Denayer, Demichelis, Nasri, Iheanacho, Aguero.
Man City (4-4-2): Hart; Sagna, Kompany, Mangala, Kolarov; Navas, Toure, Fernandinho, Silva; Sterling, Bony.
West Brom bench: Rose, Olsson, Jacob, McManaman, Sessegnon, Anichebe, Ideye.
West Brom (4-4-2): Myhill, Chester, Dawson, Lescott, Brunt; Morrison, Gardner, Fletcher, McClean; Lambert, Berahino.
MAN CITY TEAM NEWS: David Silva is declared fit enough for a place in the starting line-up following illness but Samir Nasri and Sergio Aguero both begin among the substitutes. Raheem Sterling debuts from the start alongside Wilfried Bony in attack, while Pablo Zabaleta is held back after his Copa America exploits with Argentina as Bacary Sagna is picked at right-back.
WEST BROM TEAM NEWS: The signing of Salomon Rondon from Zenit St Petersburg has been completed by the Baggies today but he is unavailable for tonight’s clash. Rickie Lambert, another new signing, therefore starts in attack alongside Saido Berahino and Boaz Myhill begins between the posts with Ben Foster still sidelined due to a knee ligament injury.
The title winners from the past five season have all started their season on a Monday night. A win tonight could encourage some West Brom fans to start dreaming about a maiden Premier League trophy lift, but City are no doubt considered more realistic contenders!
